abstract: Accurate prediction of wave attenuation by coastal vegetation remains a critical challenge in coastal engineering, with no generally accepted empirical formulas currently available. Existing theoretical or numerical models rely on the drag coefficient Cd as an intermediate variable when calculating wave attenuation, but the available empirical formulas for this coefficient lack universality, and have limited prediction accuracy. abstract: Prognostication is important in personalising oncological care for breast cancer patients. Although conventional approaches, such as Cox regression, may be used to predict breast cancer outcomes, they may have limitations in capturing the complex interactions among multiple variables. abstract: In this paper, two novel data-driven models based on Kriging and neural networks (NN) are proposed to predict pressure losses across perforated plates with circular perforations in turbulent flows. abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) represents a relevant framework for integrating ecosystem services (ES) into planning and decision-making processes. abstract: Abstract Cross-domain intrusion detection is essential for securing heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. abstract: Accurate bathymetry estimation is fundamental for applications in marine navigation, coastal hazard forecasting, and geophysical research. Conventional approaches, including shipborne sonar and satellite remote sensing, while effective, remain expensive, data-intensive, and limited in regions with sparse or noisy measurements. abstract: The Meghna River in Bangladesh receives increasing amounts of industrial and domestic effluents. title: Salud financiera y gestión estratégica en empresas inmobiliarias: Una revisión de enfoques y tendencias
abstract: La volatilidad del mercado, las nuevas regulaciones y las demandas de sostenibilidad, convierten la salud financiera en un factor clave para la permanencia y la competitividad de las empresas inmobiliarias. Sin embargo, la literatura actual presenta enfoques dispersos y una escasa integración entre los indicadores financieros tradicionales y las variables estratégicas a largo plazo. abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting marine biodiversity, particularly for monitoring elusive or endangered species. This study develops a framework for evaluating landslide risk in the Uttarkashi District of Uttarakhand, India, using GIS and machine learning. abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are extensively employed in environmental monitoring, healthcare, industrial automation, military surveillance, and security applications. abstract: Fish diseases pose a serious obstacle to the economic stability of aquaculture. abstract: This text analyzes the differences between a text written by a human and one produced by AI. abstract: Traffic incidents reported on social media, especially Twitter, can provide valuable real-time information for managing urban transportation. abstract: ABSTRACT Here, we develop and validate a machine‐learning (ML) framework for rapid screening and prediction of hydrogen‐storage performance in perovskite hydrides (ABH 3 ), using 17 physicochemical descriptors derived from 1000 DFT‐calculated compounds. title: A survey of routing protocols for internet of underwater things from a performance evaluation perspective
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a review of IoUT routing protocols, categorizing them into four groups: geographic, opportunistic, void-handling, and clustering routing protocols. We compare and evaluate these routing categories using various performance metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the strengths, limitations, applications, and performance trade-offs of existing IoUT routing protocols across the evaluation scenarios considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future research directions for the development of IoUT routing protocols.

title: Enhancing weather radar data by removing non-meteorological echoes, using neural networks trained on synthetic weather data
abstract: Abstract. Meteorological weather radars are essential for atmospheric research, weather forecasting and aviation safety, but they often detect non-meteorological echoes from scatterers such as insects, birds, and ground clutter. These non-meteorological echoes can then lead to misinterpretations in quantitative precipitation estimation and hydrometeor classification, which cause difficulties for atmospheric research and weather forecasting. This paper introduces a novel AI-based approach to identify such non-meteorological echoes in polarimetric radar data using a convolutional neural network.

title: Welcoming generation alpha through the lens of connectivism: Featuring AI's rhetorical agency
abstract: As students pack for college do they leave space in their carry on for agency—self-empowerment through the strategic use of artificial intelligence? And in what ways do educators address the need to define and shape their learning experience? Preparing to welcome the first wave of Generation Alpha (Gen Alpha) by endowing them with agency, this theoretical framework draws upon the eight principles of connectivism. abstract: Urban expansion and industrial concentration in Central Europe’s historic Black Triangle zone-encompassing Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic-continue to drive elevated carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, posing significant challenges to regional climate goals and the downstream ecological stability of the Baltic and North Sea basins. abstract: Green finance is a key mechanism for alleviating agricultural financing constraints and achieving a green transition in agriculture. abstract: Abstract Nutrient enrichment and warming cause widespread costal deoxygenation, leading to hypoxia or even anoxia in bottom waters. The benthic-water-column-feedbacks that develop under persistent seasonal oxygen depletion and amplify hypoxia remain poorly constrained. Through constant interaction with their aquatic environment, fish secrete a natural supramolecular protective mucus hydrogel, rich in gel‐forming glycoproteins (mucins), multiple antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), and ultraviolet‐protective mycosporine‐like amino acids (MAAs). abstract: Abstract The increasing availability of pretrained Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) models has accelerated the operational adoption of deep learning within geographic information systems. abstract: Aim: Breast cancer recurrence (BCR) remains a major determinant of poor outcomes in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where context-specific predictive tools are limited. We aimed to evaluate Boruta-based feature selection for identifying relevant predictors and compare multiple machine learning (ML) classifiers for predicting two-year postoperative BCR in a Tanzanian cohort. abstract: The Sea Lamprey Control Program (SLCP) suppresses invasive sea lamprey populations to protect valuable fish and fisheries in the Laurentian Great Lakes. Integrated pest management has been a longstanding, aspirational policy directive for the SLCP. However, multi-objective decision support tools (DST) capable of evaluating integrated control portfolios are lacking. abstract: Abstract Understanding the implicit regularization imposed by neural network architectures and gradient based optimization methods is a key challenge in deep learning and AI. In this work we provide sharp results for the implicit regularization imposed by the gradient flow of Diagonal Linear Networks (DLNs) in the over-parameterized regression setting and link this to the phenomenon of phase transitions in generalized hardness of approximation (GHA). title: A shared vision: regional data harmonization for resilient small-scale fisheries in the Western Indian Ocean
abstract: Effective fisheries management in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) is currently hindered by a lack of timely, harmonized data, which undermines the formulation of evidence-based policies. To address this gap, this study utilizes the Integrated Data Harmonization Framework (IDHF) to: (1) examine gaps and limitations in existing digital data collection systems in the region; (2) identify challenges and solutions for harmonizing small-scale fisheries (SSF) data; and (3) develop a strategic roadmap for national and regional data integration. abstract: Este trabajo analiza el drenaje horizontal en mezclas bituminosas porosas (PA) diseñadas para Sistemas de Drenaje Sostenible (SUDS). Video-based facial modeling is therefore a complementary way to estimate apparent personality, rather than a substitute for psychological assessment. This study evaluates continuous prediction of the Big Five dimensions (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism) using ArcFace transfer learning and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Understanding these relationships is essential for developing effective corrosion monitoring and maintenance strategies for marine infrastructure. title: From human hearing to machine diagnostics: Incipient fault diagnosis of rotating machines using multi-bioscale attention entropy and acoustic signals
abstract: Fault diagnosis in rotating machinery is traditionally performed using vibration signals; however, acoustic signals captured by non-contact sensors provide a promising alternative for early fault detection. Although entropy-based methods have been widely applied for signal complexity analysis, existing multi-scale entropy approaches are not specifically designed for acoustic signals and may not fully exploit their perceptual frequency characteristics. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel bio-inspired feature extraction method called multi-bioscale attention entropy (MBSAE).

abstract: This study investigates the perceptions of meat quality among urban consumers in three West African capital cities: Dakar, Abidjan, and Abuja, with the goal of assessing the market potential for meat from extensive Sahelian livestock systems. To complement large-scale quantitative assessments of West African urban meat demand (e.g., ILRI/CIRAD household surveys), this qualitative study applies Convention Theory to unpack the underlying social, cultural, and quality-evaluation logics of consumers. abstract: Abstract Coastal cities are highly urbanized regions where ecological sensitivity and the continuous expansion of urban space pose significant challenges to the sustainable development of ecosystems. This study assessed ecosystem services (ESs) from an integrated past–future perspective and elucidated spatiotemporal evolution patterns, as well as trade-offs and synergies among multiple ESs in Tianjin over the past two decades and under three future scenarios. abstract: This study develops an artificial intelligence–driven credibility analytics artifact for English–Chinese information systems. It evaluates whether subsequent observable actions support narrative commitments and transforms bilingual disclosures into transparent, comparable, and traceable credibility signals. abstract: Abstract Carbon partitioning between organic and carbonate‐associated forms remains poorly constrained in arid to semiarid coastal soils, where geomorphic position, salinity, and carbonate accumulation jointly structure surface‐soil carbon patterns. abstract: Phenol is a highly toxic pollutant frequently detected in industrial wastewater. abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has promoted the advancement of data-driven AI medical models, bringing transformative changes to the field of traditional cancer imaging by significantly improving diagnostic accuracy. title: Skillful subseasonal-to-seasonal ensemble forecasting with a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic model
abstract: Accurate subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction is critical for disaster mitigation under accelerating climate change, yet remains challenging due to complex multi-sphere interactions and intrinsic atmospheric uncertainty. Here we present TianXing-S2S, a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic deep learning model for global S2S ensemble forecasting. TianXing-S2S first encodes diverse multi-sphere predictors into a compact latent space, then employs a diffusion model to generate daily ensemble forecasts. abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we systematically benchmark AI's ability to imitate humans in three language tasks (image captioning, word association and conversation) and three vision tasks (colour estimation, object detection and attention prediction), collecting data from n = 636 humans and 37 AI agents. abstract: As generative artificial intelligence continues to iterate, mainstream models such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Copilot are entering the teaching spaces of universities, and teaching processes, teacher–student relations and assessment practices are changing with them. abstract: China’s dual-carbon agenda has elevated blue carbon from a broad ecological aspiration to an actionable policy domain requiring accounting standards, measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), and institutional implementation pathways. abstract: The rapid development and advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly influenced learning, information retrieval, and academic research in higher education sector. abstract: Probabilistic machine learning models estimate total dissolved solids (TDS) levels and exceedance probabilities, enabling risk-based regulation and safeguarding public health. abstract: In biomass estimation of in-water fish, a primary challenge is accurately estimating depth to reconstruct the physical dimensions of detected specimens. abstract: A basic premise of standard machine learning is that the training set and the test set come from the same distribution, but this premise is often broken in practice. Text classification is one of the most fundamental tasks in natural language processing (NLP). The poor robustness of its models to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become an important research topic. This study reviews the latest research on OOD generalization in text classification. abstract: This article examines how university students in southern Mexico articulate academic uses of ChatGPT, TikTok, and other generative artificial intelligence tools. abstract: Accurately predicting battery life is vital for next-generation energy storage. abstract: Illegal fishing gear (IFG) may remain in the marine environment when administrative procedures, field capacity, and downstream handling do not operate on the timescale required for fisheries enforcement. This study examines rapid IFG removal in South Korea as an operational link between fisheries enforcement and downstream handling. abstract: Small-scale fishing communities along Somalia’s Banadir coast face compounding climate-related pressures, yet remain almost entirely absent from the peer-reviewed literature on climate change perceptions and livelihood vulnerability. This study addresses that gap through a cross-sectional survey of 125 artisanal fishers at two Mogadishu landing sites, Abdiaziz and Hamarweyne. title: Modelado numérico y clasificación del riesgo ecológico por transporte de contaminantes en cuerpos de aguas superficiales
abstract: This paper examines water pollution and its health risks. The primary goal is to identify ecological risk zones using a hybrid approach that combines numerical solutions and machine learning. The two-dimensional advection-diffusion equation is used to model pollutant dispersion, creating a dataset for training a supervised classification model. The results demonstrate high accuracy, surpassing 95%, in predicting risk zones (low, medium, or high). It is concluded that this method is an effective tool for water quality management thus having the potential to adapt to real conditions.

title: Climate‐Driven Straightening of Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclone Trajectories
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) trajectory shifts remain a critical uncertainty in climate risk assessment. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and health implications of air pollution in Nigeria
abstract: Air pollution is a major environmental and public health challenge in Nigeria, driven by urbanization, industrialization, transportation, biomass combustion, gas flaring, waste burning, and increasing energy demand. However, evidence on its sources, spatial and temporal patterns, health effects, and emerging monitoring approaches remains fragmented. This study conducted a systematic review of evidence on air pollution in Nigeria using the PRISMA 2020 framework. abstract: Expedition scientists on the JOIDES Resolution ( JR ) during the Ocean Drilling Program (ODP), Integrated Ocean Drilling Program, and International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) carried out visual descriptions of hundreds of kilometers of cores to characterize the sequences drilled for subsequent subsampling and analysis. abstract: Solar flares are violent energy-release events in the solar atmosphere, accompanied by intense electromagnetic radiation and energetic particles that threaten satellites, radio communications, and power infrastructure, making accurate flare prediction essential for space weather early warning. abstract: Abstract Accurate simulation of river discharge underpins hydrological research, climate‐impact assessment, and flood forecasting. abstract: Rapid urban growth transforms land cover and alters surface thermal conditions, especially in fast-changing tropical coastal cities. abstract: A new species of the Tapinoma nigerrimum complex, T. elongatum sp. nov ., is described from SW Spain. abstract: Abstract Saline-alkaline soils severely constrain wheat production and have become a major threat to food security, especially in regions experiencing secondary salinization and climate change. As a glycophytic crop, wheat is highly sensitive to excessive salt and alkaline stresses, which disrupt ion balance, osmotic homeostasis, nutrient uptake, photosynthesis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) metabolism, ultimately reducing plant growth, yield, and grain quality. title: Microplastics and bisphenol A in the edible mussel Perna perna from southeastern Brazil: occurrence and dietary exposure assessment
abstract: Abstract Edible bivalves are an important route of human exposure to environmental contaminants because they are consumed whole and accumulate particulate and chemical hazards from coastal waters. This study assessed microplastics (MPs) and bisphenol A (BPA) in the brown mussel Perna perna from Espírito Santo Bay, southeastern Brazil, and estimated dietary exposure under average- and high-consumption scenarios. abstract: Abstract Snow water equivalent (SWE), which quantifies the amount of water in a snowpack, is critical for water supply forecasting. abstract: One of the core technologies for water transportation safety is the intelligent anti-collision technology for vessels. Although significant progress has been made in the research of intelligent anti-collision for vessels, the problem of multi-vessel adaptive anti-collision in complex waters has not been fully explored. title: GIS-Based Maritime Traffic Risk Identification and Assessment
abstract: Maritime traffic risk shows significant spatial and temporal differences among vessel activities, navigation conditions, and environments. The further development of Automatic Identification System (AIS) and Geographic Information System (GIS) provides useful tools to analyze vessel trajectories, accident hotspots and environmental risks. title: An Introduction to Methods to Quantify Carbon Dynamics in Rangeland Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Rangeland ecosystems store substantial terrestrial carbon and contribute to climate mitigation, yet their spatial heterogeneity, dynamic disturbance regimes, and multiple carbon pools make accurate quantification challenging. This introduction outlines and compares methodological approaches for measuring aboveground biomass, soil organic carbon, and fire-derived pyrogenic carbon across rangelands, with emphasis on how sampling design, sensor platforms, modeling frameworks, and accounting tools scale across ecological gradients. abstract: Introduction Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment. title: West Nile virus in Greece: One Health surveillance for early warning
abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) has emerged as a significant public health threat in Greece since 2010. Central Macedonia was the epicentre of the 2010 and 2022 outbreaks, whereas Attica, Eastern Macedonia and Thrace, and Thessaly predominated in other seasons. abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into educational feedback offers opportunities to expand personalisation and accessibility, but it also raises risks of bias, opacity and the erosion of teacher mediation. The objective of this theoretical-conceptual article was to propose a framework to guide the use of generative AI in feedback from the standpoint of inclusive assessment and Universal Design for Learning (UDL). abstract: Abstract This viewpoint article argues that South African teacher education requires a distinctly decolonial agenda for generative artificial intelligence (AI), developed in critical dialogue with scholarship from Aotearoa New Zealand and wider international contexts. AI is not a neutral efficiency tool: its infrastructures, training data, evaluation standards, and platform logics can intensify linguistic hierarchy, data extraction, epistemic marginalisation, and pedagogical standardisation. abstract: The development of information technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shifted the paradigm of state resilience away from protection oriented toward territorial areas and toward the protection of a borderless digital space. title: An improved CNN-Transformer network for seismic denoising with local–global feature modeling
abstract: In seismic exploration, field data are always affected by noise, reducing the quality of subsequent analysis. Striking a balance between signal preservation and noise attenuation effectively is a major challenge. This study adopts a dual-branch framework with convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformer architecture that integrates blind-spot convolution (BS-Conv) for local detail capture, rank-augmented linear attention (RALA) for global feature extraction, and the gated CNN block (GCB) for adaptive feature selection to achieve high-fidelity signal reconstruction and noise suppression.

abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. abstract: Time-series analysis often suffers from missing data, a common problem across several fields, including healthcare and environmental monitoring. abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid industrialization produces massive oily wastewater and frequent marine oil spills, severely damaging ecosystems and human health. abstract: Phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N) concentrations in surface waters are substantially affected by droughts and warm months. abstract: The identification of individuals from their vocalisations offers a non-invasive approach to population monitoring, but only if individual vocal signatures are distinct and stay stable over time. abstract: Hongshan culture in northeastern China offers a critical case for understanding prehistoric social complexity. abstract: Digital transformation has become essential for improving maritime safety and operational efficiency in archipelagic countries. This study examines the opportunities, challenges, and implementation strategies for Unmanned Lighthouse Systems in the Class II Type A Navigation District of Banjarmasin, Indonesia. abstract: Abstract Seismic data obtained after stacking or migration typically exhibit low dominant frequency, sparse spatial and temporal sampling, and may retain a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) even after stacking. abstract: Ecological risk assessment (ERA) is moving toward greater ecological realism, where population-level responses across focal species are evaluated. abstract: Sentiment analysis has become increasingly important for interpreting customer-generated content across social media and digital technologies. abstract: Malaria continues to pose a major public health threat in the Peruvian Amazon, where climate variability influences transmission patterns. This study assessed whether watershed-based spatial units (hydrobasins) outperform traditional administrative boundaries in predicting P. vivax and P. falciparum cases in Loreto, Peru. The Galápagos Archipelago, with its high endemism and limited industrial activity, provides a unique setting where natural and anthropogenic sources may interact. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the presence, distribution, sources, and effects of heavy metals in environmental matrices and wildlife in the Galápagos. abstract: Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. abstract: Abstract* Background Digital technologies offer new opportunities to support climate change education, yet the intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and relationships between technological approaches, pedagogies, and educational objectives remain insufficiently characterized. title: Beyond total arsenic: rethinking seafood-related arsenic risk assessments
abstract: Seafood is an important component of human nutrition worldwide but also represents a major dietary pathway of arsenic (As) exposure. Assessing seafood-related health risks remains challenging because As toxicity depends strongly on chemical speciation rather than total concentration alone. Although seafood often contains high total arsenic (tAs), most occurs as organic compounds such as arsenobetaine, generally regarded as low in toxicity and rapidly excreted in humans. abstract: Abstract. Europe is a global leader in mitigating methane emissions through comprehensive policies, including the EU Methane Strategy and commitments under the Global Methane Pledge. National bottom-up inventories are widely regarded as high quality; however, atmospheric observations remain essential for independent verification and tracking emission reductions. abstract: To keep pace with the rapid development of modern biotechnologies, including gene sequencing and synthetic biology, the BBNJ Agreement has established a mechanism for the fair and equitable sharing of both non-monetary and monetary benefits arising from the utilization of digital sequence information (DSI) on marine genetic resources. abstract: The exploration and discovery of lunar water reservoirs, particularly in sunlit regions, remain challenging due to an incomplete understanding of water formation mechanisms via hydrogen retention. abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Curcuma longa L. (turmeric) is an important medicinal and culinary plant and a major source of curcuminoids and volatile oils with diverse pharmacological activities. However, its phytochemical composition varies according to cultivar, genotype × environment interactions, climate, soil characteristics, cultivation practices, and post-harvest processing, creating challenges for reproducibility and standardization of turmeric-derived preparations. title: Unveiling organic aerosol sources through combined offline and online measurements at two French urban sites
abstract: Abstract Carbonaceous aerosols play a key role in urban air quality. However, their sources, particularly those contributing to secondary organic aerosol (OA), remain difficult to disentangle using conventional measurements. abstract: Accurate, scalable mapping of anthropogenic geomorphic features from high spatial resolution terrain data remains challenging. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) characterize local texture well but have limited receptive fields, whereas transformer-based architectures such as SegFormer model longer-range dependencies; their value for geomorphic mapping has not been systematically tested. abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid increase in electronic waste (e‐waste) and the growing demand for rare metals underline the urgent need for effective technologies to recover valuable elements such as gold from waste, a process known as urban mining. title: Pasture potential estimation for dairy farms: A hybrid modelled approach using integrated industry and spatial data
abstract: Pasture eaten (t DM/ha) is known to be a primary driver of profitability in New Zealand pastoral dairy farm systems. However, locally relevant estimates of achievable home-grown feed eaten (the “pasture potential”) are difficult to derive at industry scale. This study used a multi-stage hybrid methodology to estimate farm-specific pasture potential across a large industry dataset. abstract: In recent decades, natural gas hydrate has emerged as a promising alternative energy resource, attracting worldwide attention in the petroleum and natural gas industry. Hydrate-based technologies have demonstrated considerable potential in various engineering applications, including natural gas exploitation, transportation, gas sequestration, and seawater desalination. title: Uncovering diversity and bioactivity of mangrove Actinomycetia through systematic analysis
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems, between the terrestrial and marine domain, harbor a diverse and specialized microbial community, including Actinomycetia members, which produce a variety of functionally distinct bioactive metabolites. Molecular and genomic approaches have enabled the investigation of Actinomycetial diversity and identification of new strains and secondary metabolites. abstract: ABSTRACT Natural fiber‐reinforced polymer composites (NFRPCs) have emerged as sustainable alternatives to conventional synthetic fiber composites, owing to their low density, renewability, biodegradability, and favorable specific mechanical properties. In the past 5 years, they have demonstrated considerable promise in numerous applications spanning aerospace, automotive, wind energy, rail transit, marine engineering, and sports equipment. title: Reconstruction of Rock Uplift in South‐Central Germany Since Late Mesozoic Times
abstract: Abstract Rock uplift and denudation act as first‐order controls on geological processes that influence atmospheric and ocean composition, and landscape‐forming processes. However, estimating rock uplift rates remains challenging due to the temporal averaging of rates calculated from individual thermo‐ or geochronologic systems. abstract: Multi-bolted flange (MBF) connections are essential components of piping systems, pressure vessels, offshore structures, renewable energy infrastructure, and process plants. title: AnnelidaDB: a comprehensive platform of taxonomic and multi-omic resources across annelids
abstract: Annelids inhabit marine, freshwater, and terrestrial ecosystems and are important models for studying animal evolution, regeneration, and host-microbe interactions, yet their rapidly growing omics resources remain dispersed across repositories and publications. abstract: Monthly streamflow information supports seasonal water-resource planning in tropical highland basins, where dry-season scarcity and wet-season runoff require different management responses. title: Host-country media discourse and China’s economic presence in Africa
abstract: China’s economic engagement in Africa takes place in changing host-country discourse environments, yet the consequences of adverse media reporting for China’s overseas presence remain unclear. We argue that worsening media tone can signal rising operating risk and may therefore trigger adjustment across different margins of presence. title: Anticipating street-flooding complaints through rainfall data: a Value-at-Risk approach for urban operations
abstract: Urban street-flooding is a growing concern in coastal cities, where intense rainfall and aging drainage systems often combine to disrupt daily life. This study introduces a value-at-risk (VaR) framework for anticipating resident-reported street-flooding complaints in New York City from antecedent rainfall. It draws on 15 years of publicly available 311 and weather-station data, with more than 75% of complaints occurred within two days of measurable rain. This finding motivates a rainfall-based approach to understanding complaint activity in three boroughs: Manhattan, Queens, and Staten Island.

abstract: Palm oil fuel ash (POFA) and palm-biomass biochar have attracted interest as lower-carbon concrete constituents, yet material variability continues to impede confident engineering adoption. This critical qualitative literature review shifts attention from cement-replacement feasibility to the causal relationships among residue origin, processing, cement microstructure, exposure-dependent durability and qualification. abstract: Societal Impact Statement Pollen allergies are a primary cause of seasonal allergic rhinitis, which affects over 500 million people globally, damaging quality of life and incurring significant costs in medical treatment and reduced work productivity. Many countries monitor pollen to inform allergy sufferers about seasonal pollen levels. In Norway, airborne pollen has been monitored for 45 years. title: Projected Global Mortality and Economic Burden from Wildfire Smoke under Climate Change

abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) plays a central role in biological carbon pump (BCP) and global carbon cycling, but NPP estimates in high-latitude regions remain highly uncertain despite their disproportional contribution to the global carbon sink. abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis assistance, lesion detection, and computer-aided medicine. abstract: Hastelloy is a nickel-based superalloy widely used in demanding marine, nuclear, energy, and aerospace applications because of its high strength and excellent corrosion resistance. abstract: ABSTRACT Transparent self‐powered photodetectors are attractive for smart windows, environmental monitoring, and underwater optoelectronics, yet using the surrounding medium remains largely unexplored. abstract: Immersive virtual reality has entered universities with promises of deeper learning, yet the available evidence shows heterogeneous results that depend heavily on the conditions under which it is used. abstract: The emergence and spread of Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistant parasites remain a significant hurdle to malaria control and elimination. title: High resolution spatiotemporal modelling of outdoor temperature for assessment of heat-related health inequalities in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Abstract Urban heat exposure is unevenly distributed within cities, often disproportionately affecting socially and environmentally vulnerable populations. abstract: Early successional species like piping plovers ( Charadrius melodus ) rely on storms and other natural disturbances to create and maintain habitat on coastal landscapes, but anticipating year-to-year habitat availability for management purposes is difficult where dynamic conditions persist. abstract: Against the backdrop of rising global economic uncertainty and increasingly frequent multidimensional shocks, enhancing urban resilience (UR) has become critical to ensuring the stable functioning of cities and promoting high-quality development. abstract: Ethiopia is facing a soil pH problem that has not yet been accurately measured due to limited research on this issue. Soil samples were taken using stratified random sampling over six kebeles of the Gozamen District. Soil pH was analyzed based on the standard procedure of FAO (2020) and GLOSOLAN (2019). title: An explainable swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer framework with wavelet-based spatial–temporal feature modeling and activation function analysis for rainfall classification across Pakistan’s climatic regimes
abstract: Abstract Accurate rainfall occurrence prediction is essential for climate risk management, flood preparedness, and water resource planning, particularly in climatically diverse regions such as Pakistan. This paper develops and compares a multi-phase classification of rainfall based on daily IMERG precipitation data over six representative Pakistani cities spanning very low-, moderate-, and high-rainfall regimes, i.e., Gharo, Gilgit, Islamabad, Karachi, Swat, and Turbat. title: A decade after the implementation of primary healthcare under one roof: policy evaluation and recommendations for integrated quality healthcare delivery in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract This study sought to evaluate the progress made over a decade of implementing the Primary Healthcare Under One Roof (PHCUOR) policy in Nigeria. A longitudinal study design using predefined scorecard was used. The scorecards are Scorecard 2 (2014) to Scorecard 6 (2022); Scorecard 1 (2012), corresponding to the programme’s inaugural year, was unavailable and therefore excluded. title: RDAR biofilm formation and in silico analysis of putative amyloid proteins in Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245
abstract: Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245 is a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium (PGPR) whose ability to benefit host crops depends on robust root colonization, a process driven by the transition from a planktonic state to a sessile, biofilm-associated lifestyle. This study investigated the capacity of A. baldaniorum Sp245 to form Red, Dry, and Rough (RDAR) morphotype biofilms. title: Optimizing Multi‐Fuel Operations for Green Container Shipping: Models, Analysis, and Solution Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the optimization of multi‐fuel operations for container shipping in the context of evolving environmental regulations. Faced with increasing pressure to reduce emissions, particularly of sulfur oxides and carbon dioxide, the maritime industry must navigate a complex regulatory landscape in terms of energy use. Key policies include Sulfur Emission Control Areas, the European Union's (EU) Maritime Emissions Trading System, and the FuelEU Maritime Regulation. title: Detección de intrusiones en redes IoT mediante modelos ligeros de aprendizaje automático: revisión técnico-aplicada y propuesta de validación experimental para Esmeraldas, Ecuador
abstract: El crecimiento del Internet de las Cosas (IoT) amplía la superficie de ataque de redes formadas por dispositivos con recursos limitados, heterogeneidad de protocolos y ciclos de actualización reducidos. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar enfoques de detección de intrusiones basados en aprendizaje automático y formular una arquitectura ligera, reproducible y evaluable para entornos IoT con conectividad y capacidad computacional restringidas. title: Biofilm Formation and Antibiotic Resistance in Pathogenic Bacteria: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Significance, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies; A Review Article
abstract: Bacterial biofilms are highly structured microbial communities that contain bacterial cells that bind to biotic or abiotic surfaces and are enclosed in a matrix of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secreted by the bacteria themselves. The ability of pathogenic bacteria to form biofilms is one of the most crucial strategies that allow these bacteria to survive and is strongly linked to persistent, recurring, and difficult-to-treat infections. title: Energy-efficient reverse osmosis desalination through GA-PSO motor control and hydraulic energy recovery
abstract: Improving the energy performance of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) requires coordinated consideration of the electric drive, hydraulic subsystem, membrane transport, and energy recovery. This study develops a numerical framework integrating a field-oriented-controlled permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), a high-pressure pump, hybrid genetic algorithm-particle swarm optimization (GA-PSO), and a solution-diffusion reverse osmosis model applied to nine commercial thin-film composite membranes. title: Characterizing Climate-Driven Shifts in Chilean Rainfall Regimes with a Hybrid Hidden Markov–Copula Framework
abstract: Abstract Understanding and forecasting changes in rainfall regimes is critical for climate adaptation in regions facing increasing hydroclimatic variability. We develop a hybrid modeling framework combining non-homogeneous Hidden Markov Models (nHMMs) and multivariate copulas to detect and simulate climate-driven shifts in precipitation patterns. Applied to daily rainfall data from 462 stations in Chile (1980--2021) during austral winter (May--August). title: The Cost of Being Green: Sustainability‐Linked Eco‐Friction, Trade‐Off Tolerance, and Tourist Satisfaction in Island Reviews
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability is often assumed to enhance tourism value, yet tourists do not always evaluate green practices positively in lived service encounters. This study examines sustainability‐linked evaluation in island and coastal tourism by distinguishing eco‐delight from eco‐friction, defined as environmentally anchored inconvenience rather than generic dissatisfaction. title: Frogs and toads in the holes: Late Miocene amphibians from the Gargano Terre Rosse fissures (Southern Italy)
abstract: Nowadays, Mediterranean islands are home to several, often endemic, amphibians. Knowledge is limited, however, about amphibian palaeocommunities in the islands and palaeoislands of the Mediterranean Sea, despite the certain presence of fossils in such areas. One case with known but understudied insular amphibian fossils are the Gargano Terre Rosse, a complex of fissures in Southern Italy representing the remaining evidence of a Late Miocene (palaeo)insular fauna. title: The Mediating Effects of Trust in an Institution on the Relationship between Perceived Transparency and Student Satisfaction in Higher Learning Institutions: Evidence from Tanzania
abstract: Higher learning institutions (HLIs) are essential bases for a knowledge economy by developing human capital and technology. The HLIs fuel developing countries such as Tanzania to remain competitive in the current global economy. This paper explores the relationship between perceived transparency, trust in an HLI and student satisfaction. The quantitative data were collected from respondents in the coastal zone of Tanzania using a clustering approach with multi-stage sampling methods (N = 398). title: STEAM and educational robotics in the development of statistical literacy
abstract: In primary school, the teaching of mathematics and natural sciences should promote meaningful, context-based learning that enables students to apply knowledge in real-life situations. Interdisciplinary approaches such as STEAM foster 21st century competences through active and collaborative methodologies, while educational robotics (ER) supports the development of computational thinking and social skills. title: A hybrid meta-heuristic optimisation and unsupervised learning framework for predictive stability enhancement of single-machine infinite-bus power systems
abstract: Accelerating renewable penetration into modern interconnected grids has amplified low-frequency electromechanical oscillations, eroding the dynamic stability margins of synchronous generators. A unified two-phase framework is proposed to address Power System Stabiliser (PSS) parameter optimisation and real-time stability estimation for the Single-Machine Infinite-Bus (SMIB) benchmark. title: Fucoidan attenuates metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in mice and is associated with gut microbiota remodeling and AMPK/PPARγ signaling
abstract: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a growing metabolic disorder closely linked to gut micro biota dysbiosis and impaired gut–liver communication. Dietary interventions targeting the gut micro biota represent a promising strategy for MAFLD management. Fucoidan (FUC), a marine-derived bioactive polysaccharide with limited host digestibility, is primarily metabolized by intestinal microorganisms. abstract: Abstract Firefly squid ( Watasenia scintillans ) possess distinct blue and green bioluminescent photophores. Owing to their possession of three visually active pigments (a highly uncommon trait in the deep sea, where monochromatic visual systems dominate), it has been postulated that firefly squid may utilise two distinct photophore colours for private, intraspecific communication. abstract: Many New England salt marshes are rapidly degrading due to the combined effects of accelerating sea-level rise (SLR) and other anthropogenic stressors, resulting in loss of high-marsh vegetation and threatening marsh-dependent wildlife such as the Saltmarsh Sparrow ( Ammospiza caudacuta ). abstract: Environmental degradation in ecologically significant regions often becomes not only an environmental crisis but also a discursive struggle over meaning, responsibility and legitimacy. This study investigated how environmental degradation in Raja Ampat, Indonesia, one of the world’s most biodiverse marine ecosystems, was linguistically framed in Indonesian online news media. abstract: The advent of large-scale spectroscopic surveys will deliver tens of thousands of spectra of blue massive stars spanning a wide range of spectral types (SpTs) and luminosity classes (LCs). This data volume renders traditional spectral classification techniques increasingly impractical and motivates the development of automated classification tools. abstract: Rapid urban growth in Sub-Saharan Africa poses significant challenges to sustainable land management, food security, and environmental quality. Kano Metropolis, Nigeria's second-largest city and the primary commercial hub of the Sahel belt north, has experienced accelerated spatial expansion driven by population growth, rural-urban migration, and inadequate planning and regulation. abstract: Building on research linking personality to financial behavior and market participation (Brown & Taylor, 2014; Conlin et al., 2015), this study examines whether personality traits influence simulated trading performance and whether this influence operates through trading intensity. abstract: Background Rodent eradication on oceanic islands is essential for the conservation of endemic species. abstract: Background: PANoptosis contributes to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) pathogenesis. We aimed to identify PANoptosis-related gene signatures as candidate biomarkers and evaluate their genetic associations with COPD risk. Methods: Three transcriptomic data sets were integrated to identify differentially expressed PANoptosis-related genes in COPD, followed by enrichment analyses and immune infiltration profiling using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. abstract: Agricultural drought threatens food security in irrigated and rainfed regions worldwide, and early warning is especially difficult in large irrigated basins, where canal water partly decouples crop condition from local climate. abstract: To improve the detection accuracy of SAR ship targets under complex background clutter, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 detection method for SAR ship detection tasks. Three optimization strategies are adopted, including CA attention module, improved DSConv convolution module, and Shape-IoU loss function. abstract: Tourism ecological security (TES) is essential for sustaining destination resilience, ecological quality, and long-term tourism development. The digital economy (DE) plays a crucial role in improving TES by enabling smart monitoring, efficient resource allocation, and precision governance. abstract: Abstract Depth–duration–frequency (DDF) curves are essential tools in hydrologic and hydraulic engineering, used to estimate the magnitude and frequency of extreme precipitation events across varying durations. abstract: La correcta administración de inventarios influye en la productividad y competitividad de una empresa y la aplicación de los sistemas ABC y FSN permite optimizar el almacenamiento, la entrega de materiales y la toma de decisiones. abstract: Cities depend on infrastructural lifelines that extend far beyond their territorial boundaries, yet urban resilience is often conceptualized through capacities located within cities themselves. This Perspective uses disruptions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz to reconsider how urban resilience is shaped by geographically dispersed infrastructure networks operating across multiple spatial and institutional scales. abstract: Numerous global initiatives and policy frameworks, including blue carbon strategies, biodiversity targets, and ecosystem restoration commitments, highlight the need to conserve and restore seagrasses, yet losses continue to accelerate across many regions. abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire-weather activity globally, yet the extent to which ecosystem structure modulates fire-weather regimes in complex mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate contrasting responses of forested and non-forested landscapes to climate-driven fire weather in the Alborz Mountains (1980–2025). abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted health service utilisation worldwide. abstract: Introduction The restoration of heavy metal-contaminated urban waste-dumping sites requires sustainable approaches that improve soil functionality while supporting contaminant attenuation, biomass production, and resource recovery. abstract: La atención sanitaria basada en valor (ASBV) incentiva un modelo asistencial que se centra en la participación de las personas trabajadoras, los profesionales de la salud laboral y los proveedores con el fin de alcanzar el mejor resultado de salud al menor coste posible. abstract: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. abstract: Background Malawi’s water security depends on the Lake Malawi-Shire River system, which receives approximately 60% of its inflows from transboundary catchments in Tanzania and Mozambique. abstract: Fine-scale wetland mapping is challenged by fragmented patch shapes, spectral confusion between wet and dry surfaces, and the scarcity of annotated high-resolution training samples. abstract: ABSTRACT The need for more holistic and context‐aware approaches to flood‐risk assessment has become increasingly urgent with extreme climate change events faced globally. abstract: Abstract. This study presents a semi-systematic synthesis of scientific literature published between 2015 and 2025 on climate risk in African cities. From an initial set of 1,832 records identified through broad climate- and urban-related keywords, 273 articles were selected through title and abstract screening. abstract: Rapidly escalating heat extremes, characterized by abrupt onset and limited preparation time, pose disproportionate risks to public health, agriculture, and regional economies, yet their governing mechanisms and subseasonal predictability remain poorly understood. Here we identify 107 such events over North China during the summers of 1940–2024 and classify them into four spatial types. abstract: Abstract The Turkey Lake Watershed (TLW), located in Northern Ontario, forms a cascading lake system that ultimately drains into Lake Superior. Historically, the TLW has served as a key research site for studies on acid rain and climate change. abstract: Abstract Estuaries are under threat globally from a wide range of stressors, with rates of ecosystem metabolism – respiration (R), gross primary production (GPP), and net ecosystem metabolism (NEM) – representing a way for resource managers to quantify their impacts. In this study, we assessed how natural and anthropogenic stressors have altered metabolism within the extensively modified Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (“Delta”) in California, USA. abstract: Abstract Accurate weld type recognition and stable keypoint localization are essential for automated weld seam inspection, yet real-time deployment is still challenged by the high computational cost of dense prediction models and visual disturbances such as arc glare and spatter. This paper presents LDCNet, a lightweight compression framework for DenseNet-CenterNet. title: Data Driven Model Development to Predict Soil Temperature and Freeze-Thaw Cycles in Pavement Foundation Systems
abstract: Abstract Road infrastructure is central to economic development of the United States. However, particularly in cold climates, the soil temperature and annual freeze-thaw cycles significantly impact road conditions, therefore it is important to accurately predict the number of freeze-thaw cycles and their duration. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate long-horizon streamflow forecasting is crucial for water resource management, but existing models often face efficiency and interpretability challenges. This study comprehensively evaluates the Mamba architecture, which utilizes state-space models (SSMs) for efficient sequence processing, for 120-h hourly generalized streamflow prediction across 125 diverse Iowa watersheds using 72-h historical inputs. The conventional approach of scheduled inspection is still absolutely vital, though periodic testing may well miss the gradual degradation that occurs between inspections. abstract: Surface ozone (O3) forms via nonlinear chemistry and is highly non-stationary, complicating 168-h forecasts. abstract: Despite its potential, the automated cervical cytology analysis is severely limited by the lack of rare malignant cell samples and the class imbalance that is frequently associated with them, resulting in biased predictions and limited generalisation capabilities to clinically relevant abnormal categories. abstract: Fire, water, and ice pose persistent challenges to personal protective materials used in harsh environments. Integrating water repellency, ice resistance, antimicrobial activity, and flame retardancy into a single fabric remains particularly difficult for chemically inert aramid fabrics widely employed in firefighting protective clothing. This paper presents a comparative study of three reward formulations for training a TD3 agent to perform three-dimensional path following using a particle kinematic system modeled as double-integrator dynamics. abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems harbour a substantial proportion of global biodiversity yet face intense pressure from multiple stressors. abstract: ABSTRACT Remote sensing of colonial wildlife has largely focused on estimating population size, providing limited insight into internal demographic structure and spatial organization. abstract: Aquaculture has become a major contributor to global food production, but its rapid expansion and intensification have increased concerns regarding the welfare of farmed fish. abstract: Abstract Port digitalization represents one of the most significant transformations in global maritime logistics. In Portugal, a country with a strong maritime tradition and an economy open to international trade, technological modernization of ports generates significant direct and indirect effects across multiple sectors of the national economy. abstract: Abstract Quality control in cayenne pepper fruit is important for maintaining product consistency. The research aimed to evaluate lycopene content and antioxidant capacity as the main indicators of cayenne pepper quality. Visible-near infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy is an emerging technology that can predict lycopene content and antioxidant capacity non-destructively, accurately, and quickly. abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of aircraft engines is critical to the safety of aircraft operations. abstract: Building a maritime power is a talent problem before it is a technology problem, and application-oriented maritime undergraduate colleges sit where the two meet. abstract: The exponential growth of bloated web development frameworks and the pervasive reliance on centralized, third party video conferencing infrastructures present critical challenges in computational overhead, structural friction, and digital sovereignty. abstract: Water exchange is linked to survival in aquaculture, but its relationship with host–environment microbial interactions remains unclear. abstract: Reliable length–age relationships are essential for the effective management of elasmobranchs. abstract: Background Complete blood count (CBC) and biochemical parameters (liver function, renal function, Blood glucose, and lipid profile) are the most routinely used tests in clinical laboratory practice, and serve as critical evidence for disease diagnosis. abstract: Abstract Reliable fish abundance estimation is essential for the operation and management of aquaculture systems, but remains challenging under turbidity, bubble interference, target occlusion, and acoustic reverberation. title: A cross-domain fault diagnosis method for high-speed train axlebox bearings based on time-frequency mapping and adversarial networks
abstract: Abstract The health condition of axlebox bearings in high-speed trains is directly associated with operational safety. However, variations in rotational speed, load, and operating environment induce pronounced domain shift in vibration signals, which undermines the generalization capability of intelligent diagnosis models trained under a single operating condition.To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross condition bearing diagnosis method integrating a CNN BiLSTM hybrid network and multi constraint domain adaptation for cross condition diagnosis of high speed train axle box bearings.

abstract: Abstract Is convection initiation (CI) harder to forecast in some large-scale environments? Using 8,607 radar-detected isolated CI events over South China during 2018–2023 and ERA5 fields, we identify two recurrent pre-CI environments: a thermal environment with broad warm-moist support and a dynamic environment with more organized flow. Across 200 forecast models, dynamic cases generally have lower skill than thermal cases. abstract: The wind energy frictional nano‐generator (W‐TENG) can efficiently collect low‐frequency, random mechanical energy from the wind for self‐powered systems, such as smart farms; however, the practical output signal has severe pulse and fluctuation issues. This article introduces a phase‐shift‐assisted wind‐driven W‐TENG with a ternary contact structure. In Madura, the use of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). abstract: Objectives This study examines the role of selected blue economy logistics indicators in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) and enhancing fiscal balance in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. abstract: Abstract. We apply Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to ICESat-2 along-track height change data to generate spatially continuous glacier height change fields across two glaciated regions with complex topography and dynamic behaviour: Larsen-B (Antarctic Peninsula) and central Southern Svalbard. abstract: ABSTRACT The shipping industry plays a vital role in global trade and also exerts significant environmental and social pressures due to high fuel consumption, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and intensive port activities. Implementing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices offers a strategic pathway to enhance sustainability performance in this sector; however, it remains difficult to determine which managerial and operational actions can most effectively drive improvements in ESG performance. title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. abstract: Abstract Rolling bearing fault diagnosis is critical for the reliable operation of rotating machinery. However, vibration signals collected under varying sampling rates, devices, and operating conditions often exhibit domain shifts, and only limited labeled samples are available in the target domain. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-scale physics-frequency bidirectional Mamba network (MS-PFMamba) for cross-sampling-rate, cross-device, and few-shot bearing fault diagnosis. title: Spatial Distribution and Source Apportionment of Nitrate in Groundwater in a Representative Agricultural Region of the Southern Piedmont of the Qinling Mountains, China
abstract: Abstract In order to study the source of nitrate pollution in shallow groundwater in the agricultural area, surface water, groundwater and soil samples were collected, and the conventional chemical indicators and nitrogen and oxygen isotopes were analyzed. The method of combining nitrate δ15N and δ18O was used to identify the source of nitrate pollution. The results show that the concentration of NO3−(N) in the groundwater is between 3.18mg/L and 10.32mg/L, and the water quality of BC203, TCQ3020 and TCQ3029 wells belongs to Class III(5mg/L). title: Stochastic Operator Residual Learning with Conformal Calibration for Risk-Aware Wind Turbine Maintenance
abstract: Wind turbine maintenance decisions are frequently made under uncertainty, yet conventional degradation models often provide deterministic predictions that ignore the tail risks associated with unexpected component failure. We propose a stochastic operator residual learning framework with conformal calibration for risk-aware wind turbine maintenance. abstract: Accurate load demand forecasting serves as the fundamental prerequisite for data reliability analysis in multi-user heterogeneous load access scenarios. In such environments, the volume of data flows generated by industrial, residential, and commercial loads exhibits complex temporal variation patterns characterized by distinct periodicity and volatility. These patterns are governed by multiple factors including diverse user behaviors, operational schedules, and seasonal variations. title: FSF-RTDETR: a frequency–spatial feature fusion network for eggplant fruit disease and pest detection in complex agricultural scenes
abstract: Detecting fruit diseases and pests in complex agricultural scenes remains challenging due to large target-scale variation, weak lesion features, leaf and branch occlusion, and severe background interference. To address these problems, this study focuses on eggplant fruit disease and pest detection and proposes FSF-RTDETR, a frequency–spatial fusion model. abstract: Avian schistosomes (AS) are trematodes of significant medical importance as the causative agents of cercarial dermatitis, a re-emerging waterborne human disease. Their monitoring has traditionally relied on examination of snail hosts; however, this approach is time-consuming, requires taxonomic expertise and often underestimates their diversity due to low prevalence of infection. title: Research on Warehouse Path Planning for Logistics Robots Based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
abstract: How to efficiently and reasonably carry out path planning has always been a hot spot of research in the field of warehouse logistics robots. We propose a logistics robot warehouse path planning strategy based on the Improved Whale Optimisation Algorithm (IWOA). The whale optimisation algorithm’s convergence speed is slow, making it easy to fall into the limitations of the local optimum. title: Computational Performance of ONNX Runtime and NCNN Frameworks for Real-Time Motorcycle Detection on Raspberry Pi 5: A Yogyakarta CCTV Case Study
abstract: The acceleration of Smart City initiatives across Indonesia has intensified the demand for localized Intelligent Transportation Systems. Although micro-architectures like YOLOv26n offer optimized layer configurations, executing these models for real-time motorcycle detection on standalone edge computers often presents hardware bottlenecks due to software runtime inefficiencies and core thermal stress. This study presents a comparative computational performance benchmarking of the out-of-the-box YOLOv26n architecture across two prominent runtime frameworks: ONNX Runtime and the NCNN framework.

abstract: Accurate tree species information is essential for biodiversity assessment, forest ecosystem monitoring, and adaptive forest management. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery offers a cost-effective and flexible means of repeatedly acquiring very-high-resolution canopy information; however, the image characteristics used to distinguish tree species can vary with vegetation phenology and natural illumination. title: Concentration‐Dependent Growth, Survival and Tissue Responses of Asian Seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) Fingerlings Following Short‐Term Dietary Exposure to Polyethylene Microplastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are emerging aquatic pollutants that may impair fish health through ingestion and tissue‐level toxicity. This study evaluated whether short‐term dietary exposure to fluorescently labeled polyethylene microplastics (PE‐MPs) produced concentration‐dependent changes in growth, survival, intestinal morphology, and skeletal‐muscle integrity in Asian seabass fingerlings. abstract: Traditional fault diagnosis methods face challenges in extracting temporal features from measured signals and achieving noise-resistant robustness in practical measurement scenarios. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight compound fault diagnosis model (TLCN) based on a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) convolutional network. abstract: Introduction Early and reliable fire and smoke detection is essential for effective emergency monitoring, particularly in UAV-based environments characterized by variable illumination, changing object scales, and smoke-related visual disturbances. This study proposes a near-real-time UAV-based computer vision framework integrating YOLO-based object detection, geometric fire-source localization, and visible light communication (VLC). abstract: ABSTRACT Fatigue failures of major structural cables threaten engineering infrastructure. Fiber‐reinforced polymer (FRP) composites are promising alternatives to steel cables, while hybrid composites can overcome the limitations of single‐fiber systems and promote applications in super‐long‐span and high‐tonnage cables. abstract: We review 224 studies of financial data analytics published between 2020 and 2026 and document a mismatch between the questions the field asks and the designs it uses to answer them. abstract: The accuracy of climate reanalyses is limited by observation availability, especially satellite soundings prior to 1979, when operational polar-orbiting satellites become more prevalent. This paper reports on successful efforts to locate the data record collected by the pioneering instrument Special Sensor H (SSH) mounted on four Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) block-5D1 satellites (F-1 to F-4) from 1976 to 1980. title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
abstract: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Although population assignment is a powerful tool, accuracy can be low when populations have unequal odds of being sampled, which may arise from factors such as differences in population sizes, migration patterns, or behavior. abstract: Wind turbines operating in complex terrain are exposed to terrain-induced aerodynamic disturbances, such as strong vertical wind shear, wind veer, turbulence and flow deviation, which increase asymmetric rotor loading and can degrade operational reliability. The quantitative link between such disturbances, the operational response recorded by the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, and the parameterisation of Wind Sector Management (WSM) strategies remains insufficiently documented for real turbines. abstract: Rib formation in continuous-fiber composite rebar imposes geometric constraints that can induce severe axial strain in surface-near fiber bundles, ultimately limiting admissible rib depth even before considering bond optimization with concrete. This study develops a mechanics-based model to quantify the evolution of fiber axial strain during rib shaping and to define a limit-state rib-depth criterion governed by fiber fracture strain. abstract: Background In cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG)-based driving-fatigue detection, most existing decoders are designed around second-scale short windows, whereas fatigue is a slow drift; short-window spectral features provide little direct evidence of that slow drift, limiting fatigue decisions. abstract: Battery safety remains the primary bottleneck for mass electric vehicle (EV) adoption, yet field monitoring is hamstrung by a fundamental asymmetry: complex electrochemical faults must be diagnosed via sparse, low-frequency voltage measurements. Existing methods struggle to resolve the signal ambiguity between overlapping fault modes without hardware upgrades. title: Natural compounds targeting cancer-associated genes: Multi-omics mechanisms and therapeutic potential
abstract: Cancer is caused by excessive expression of oncogenic proteins as well as inactivity of tumor suppressor proteins. In this way, complex gene regulatory processes are altered, leading to uncontrolled proliferation, chromosomal instability, and metastasis. abstract: South Sulawesi possesses abundant renewable energy potential, particularly from hydro, wind, solar, and biomass resources. However, rapid population growth and increasing energy consumption across sectors create challenges in ensuring sustainable energy supply and planning. This study aims to project the mid-term renewable energy supply and demand in South Sulawesi using the Long-range Energy Alternatives Planning (LEAP) model. abstract: The object of this study is the concept of a “route”, which requires reconsideration. A conventional route is represented by a polyline consisting of waypoints and verified in ECDIS; this is sufficient for a navigator but not for an automatic control system that must execute the route. The article proposes a formalization of the digital route of a Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) as an extension of the standard IEC 61174 route format (RTZ) by adding turn arcs with wheel-over points, corridors and safety zones, a speed profile, and time stamps. title: Transport and retention of microplastics during riverbank filtration
abstract: Introduction Riverbank filtration (RBF) is a widely used natural water treatment process; however, the fate and attenuation of microplastics (MPs), within river–aquifer systems is not well understood. This study investigated the occurrence and characteristics of MPs within an RBF system to comprehend the MPs transport behaviour. abstract: Hydraulic infrastructure inspection is laborious due to the massive scale of structures and the need for precise crack measurement. This study presents a pioneering framework integrating unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), and semantic scene understanding to revolutionize hydraulic structural health monitoring. abstract: Abstract Freshwater scarcity is a major global challenge driven by population growth, industrialization, climate change, and declining freshwater resources. This review systematically and critically evaluates recent advances in nanofluid‐assisted solar still desalination, focusing on freshwater productivity, thermal performance, energy and exergy efficiency, stability, economic feasibility, and environmental sustainability. abstract: China’s consolidated maritime enforcement system connects dispersed domestic powers with new obligations under the Ecological and Environmental Code (EEC) and the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. This study examines the relationship between China’s implementation responsibility and the legality of a specified China Coast Guard (CCG) measure. abstract: High-frequency millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) communications are promising for 6G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) services but remain vulnerable to dynamic vehicular mobility, bursty heterogeneous traffic, and heavy-tailed physical blockage. Conventional routing approaches often rely on memoryless channel models, non-differentiable soft-computing heuristics, or centralized optimization that may not adequately capture blockage persistence and tail-latency risks. abstract: Groundwater quality degradation in arid and semi-arid regions requires assessment approaches capable of identifying critical parameter exceedances while minimizing the masking effects commonly observed in aggregated water quality indices. abstract: Accurate prediction of gas turbine maximum power output is critical for electricity market bidding and grid stability in renewable-integrated power systems. Physics-based models cannot adequately capture performance degradation caused by equipment aging, while data-driven models, particularly tree-based ensembles, exhibit poor extrapolation beyond training ranges, posing a critical limitation under increasingly extreme weather conditions. abstract: Robust genotype-to-phenotype (G2P) prediction is essential for accelerating grapevine (Vitis spp.) breeding decisions and genetic gain. In this study, we propose a linear-Transformer (LiT)-G2P, an automated predictive framework that integrates additive genetic variance effects with Transformer-based nonlinear interactions using genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) data. abstract: Abstract Absolute angular position measurement is critical for automated systems, yet conventional optical and magnetic encoders often suffer from complex alignment, vulnerability to dirty environments, or high cost. abstract: Vegetation-growing concrete supports plant growth through interconnected pores, but root-secreted organic acids progressively degrade its cementitious matrix, threatening long-term durability. title: A self-supervised and distillation-guided framework for robust cloud-layer identification in multi-channel Raman lidar networks
abstract: Abstract. Cloud-layer identification is a key prerequisite for automated ground-based lidar processing, but remains challenging in Raman lidar networks because of incomplete near-range overlap, weak high-level cloud echoes, day–night signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) contrasts, energy fluctuations, and aerosol–cloud ambiguity. title: Unveiling Scale‐Dependent Precipitation Microphysics in Typhoon Doksuri (2023) Using Polarimetric Radar Observations
abstract: Abstract Extending previous work focused on tropical cyclone (TC) rainband distinctions, this study employs polarimetric radar observations to examine the multiscale microphysical characteristics of Typhoon Doksuri (2023). The mean vertical profiles of polarimetric variables differ substantially between the inner‐core and outer‐rainband regions, owing to the different proportions and contributions of convection at various scales. title: Bay of Bengal cyclones fuel non-monsoon extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau, particularly outside the summer monsoon season, strongly affects glacier mass balance and downstream water availability, yet the moisture transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study combines high-resolution measurements of the isotopic composition of atmospheric water vapour at Nam Co Lake with isotope-enabled climate model simulations to investigate an extreme snowfall event on 25 October 2022. title: Valorization of yak bone collagen byproducts: computational screening and experimental validation of anti-aging peptides targeting MMP-1
abstract: Abstract Valorization of yak collagen byproducts offers a sustainable route to food-derived bioactive peptides. To prioritize candidate peptides from yak collagen-derived sequences, we developed AgeAttnMLP, an ESM-2-based screening model that achieved an AUC of 0.891 under conventional five-fold cross-validation and 0.879 under an additional cluster-aware grouped evaluation. Screening of yak collagen sequences followed by Alcalase-guided in silico hydrolysis identified TGPPGPSGI, GEPGAPGE, and GPSGEPGTA as lead candidates. title: Robust predefined-time sliding-mode tracking control for a class of nonlinear systems with preassigned convergence constraints
abstract: Abstract This paper addresses high-precision tracking control for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems under the stringent requirement that the convergence time of the tracking error be explicitly preassigned by the user. To meet this requirement, a predefined-time sliding-mode control (PTSMC) scheme is developed. The controller is designed within an auxiliary-variable-based transformation framework, which facilitates the co-design of a nonlinear barrier function and a self-adjusting gain law. title: IoT-enabled multimodal large language model-based framework for compositional food recognition, nutrient profiling, NOVA classification, and cancer risk mitigation
abstract: Background Automated dietary assessment increasingly struggles to evaluate industrial food processing levels, revealing a systemic gap between the visual presentation of meals and their underlying ultra-processed food composition. Although existing dietary monitoring tools can effectively track caloric and macronutrient intake, they lack the qualitative processing assessments required to identify hidden additives and map dietary risk triage quadrants.
