title: Multiclass Classification and Spatial Clustering of Disaster Tweets for Humanitarian Awareness
abstract: Background: Social media is a critical channel of real-time information channel during natural disasters, but the informal and fragmented nature of tweets makes automatic classification difficult. Named entity recognition (NER) can capture contextual cues, such as affected locations. However, how entity information should be incorporated into classifiers and its value for disaster mapping remain underexplored. title: Regulatory quality, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability in a developing economy: Evidence from a Bayesian vector error correction model
abstract: Sustainable management of the environment is among the primary objectives of sustainable development. Although environmental regulation is widely studied in advanced economies, its effectiveness in developing nations like Nigeria, characterized by weak regulatory and enforcement institutions, remains underexplored. title: WF-U-Net: A multi-scale U-Net for wheat breeding plot extraction from UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate delineation of individual wheat breeding plots from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is essential for plot-level high-throughput phenotyping. However, narrow inter-plot buffers and phenology-dependent variations in canopy appearance pose challenges to reliable segmentation. To address these challenges, we developed WF-U-Net, a U-Net-based semantic segmentation framework that integrates a multi-scale convolution module (MSCM) at multiple encoder stages and a multi-scale feature fusion module (MSFFM) at the decoder output. title: Social network based fuzzy decision-analytic model for hydrogen vehicle selection toward sustainable transportation systems
abstract: Abstract The selection of an effective hydrogen vehicle technology is a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) problem with conflicting evaluation criteria and uncertainty in experts’ judgments. To tackle this challenge, this study presents an integrated social network analysis based fuzzy MCDM approach to hydrogen vehicle selection. First, in the present work, Social Network Analysis (SNA) is used to calculate the relative influence of experts using degree centrality. Second, the uncertainty and imprecision in experts’ linguistic assessments are captured in terms of Interval-Valued Fuzzy Sets

title: Design and prototype model for smart autonomous self-balancing bicycle
abstract: There are still a huge demand for safe and sustainable modes of transport which has led to the creation of autonomous self-balancing bicycles. The design and analysis of the self-balancing bicycle with flywheel mechanism assisted by gyroscope is presented in this study. A Lagrangian approach was used to model the tilt dynamics; it includes kinetic energy, potential energy, damping and actuator torque generated by the BLDC motors. abstract: ABSTRACT Solar energy planning has evolved from mapping resource potential and assessing site suitability to increasingly integrating space, capacity, networks, demand, storage, land use, and energy transition goals. This article reviews 129 English-language Scopus records published during 2020–2026 and retrieved through a structured search on October 5, 2026. title: Groundwater Vulnerability Assessment of the Kingston Hydrological Basin in Jamaica Using the GIS ‐Based DRASTIC Model
abstract: ABSTRACT The Kingston Hydrological Basin (KHB) in Jamaica faces serious challenges in water security due to increased urbanisation, limited water resources and inadequate sewage treatment facilities. Nitrate contamination of the alluvial aquifer, coupled with a decrease in rainfall patterns, has resulted in the closure of many groundwater wells and a heavy reliance on surface water systems. This has created an increase in demand for potable water from inadequate surface water resources and water shortages during periods of drought within the KHB and adjoining basins. title: Light exposure reshapes microbial community assembly on plastic in Winogradsky columns
abstract: Plastic pollution in landfills presents a significant environmental challenge, as macroplastics fragment into persistent and harmful micro- and nanoplastics. Despite growing interest in plastitrophs, we know relatively little about how environmental conditions shape their community assembly and function. Among possible determinants, light exposure is likely consequential but remains poorly characterized. title: Cross-modal predictive inconsistency with directional asymmetry modelling for multimodal deepfake detection
abstract: Deepfake detection systems intended for real-world deployment face a persistent gap between benchmark accuracy and field reliability: detectors trained to recognise generator-specific artefacts degrade sharply against synthesis methods unseen during training. We present an audio-visual forgery detection system built on a different operating principle: rather than learning what fake content looks like, it models the causal coupling between a speaker’s acoustic output and facial dynamics that authentic recordings share, and flags departures from that coupling as evidence of manipulation. title: EVALUATING TURKISH CUISINE CHARACTERISTICS USING CHATGPT AND EXPERT ASSESSMENT: A CLEAR METHOD APPROACH
abstract: Turkish cuisine, renowned for its rich culinary traditions, is influenced by various cultures and geographical regions of Turkiye. Defining the general characteristics and features of this cuisine requires the compilation of information from numerous sources. This study aimed to identify the characteristics of Turkish cuisine using the generative chatbot ChatGPT and evaluate the findings using the CLEAR method by culinary experts and academics. title: From seed centres to tray cells: a geometry-aware machine vision framework for full-tray sowing quality assessment in maize plug trays
abstract: Accurate sowing-quality assessment of maize seedling trays requires both reliable seed localisation and correct correspondence between detected seeds and physical tray cells. This study presents a semi-automated machine-vision framework combining heatmap-based seed-centre localisation, sliding-window inference, global non-maximum suppression (NMS), and four-corner-calibrated adaptive grid assignment. title: FLORO: A multimodal geospatial foundation model for ecological remote sensing across sensors and scales
abstract: The proliferation of remote sensing platforms has generated an unprecedented diversity of Earth observation data, creating both the opportunity and the challenge of extracting transferable knowledge across sensors, scales, and environments. Foundation models have emerged as a promising framework for this challenge, leveraging large datasets to learn representations that generalize across tasks and sensing conditions in real-world Earth observation. title: Reverse-learning-enhanced sine cosine algorithm for joint inversion of seismic refraction and Rayleigh-wave dispersion data
abstract: Rayleigh-wave dispersion and seismic refraction observations constrain different but coupled aspects of near-surface velocity structure. This study evaluates a reverse-learning-enhanced sine cosine algorithm (ESCA) for jointly estimating layer thickness, shear-wave velocity, and P-wave velocity in a one-dimensional, horizontally layered medium. title: Tracking lightning-induced mangrove canopy gaps in Panama using multi-temporal remote sensing
abstract: Lightning-induced canopy gaps are an important form of fine-scale disturbance in mangrove forests, with implications for regeneration, canopy structure, and forest heterogeneity. Reconstructing their long-term dynamics remains challenging because recovery is prolonged and historical high-spatial-resolution imagery is temporally sparse and heterogeneous among sensors. This study developed a multi-temporal remote-sensing framework to map and track lightning-induced mangrove canopy gaps in Panama from 2000 to 2020. title: ITS Implementation in Smart Ports: Evidence from Five Comparative Case Studies
abstract: This study examines the real-world operational applications of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) technologies in smart ports and their implications for port management and digital transformation strategies. While ITS applications for road and passenger transportation have been widely discussed in the literature, fewer studies have considered their use in maritime and port operations. title: Mapless UAV navigation in complex environments: A survey on deep reinforcement learning approaches
abstract: As applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) continue to expand across sectors such as logistics, surveillance, and environmental monitoring, the development of safe and robust autonomous navigation capabilities has become increasingly important. Mapless autonomous UAV navigation refers to a UAV’s ability to reach a designated destination along a collision-free and efficient path without human intervention and without relying on a global map. title: Convexity-Preserving Reduced-Complexity Model Predictive Control via Radial Basis Function Networks
abstract: In this study, we investigate Model Predictive Control (MPC) for systems operating under state, control, and output constraints, and propose an enhanced formulation that significantly reduces computational demand. Within the MPC framework, we introduce a novel representation of the control signal based on Radial Basis Function Networks (RBFNs)—well known for their strong function approximation capabilities. title: Public Art and Urban Experience: The Case of Limassol Promenade
abstract: Abstract Public art increasingly contributes to the identity, cultural expression, and experiential quality of contemporary public spaces, particularly along waterfront promenades that function as major urban gathering areas. This study examines the role and spatial integration of public art along the Limassol Promenade in Cyprus and evaluates its contribution to place identity and user experience. abstract: La adopción masiva de herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa (IAGen) por parte del estudiantado universitario ha superado la capacidad de respuesta de las instituciones educativas, especialmente en disciplinas como la ingeniería del agua donde la fiabilidad numérica de los cálculos es crítica para la seguridad de las infraestructuras y la adecuada gestión del recurso. abstract: Introduction Groundwater is the principal source of drinking and irrigation water in semi-arid hard-rock regions, where natural hydrogeochemical processes and anthropogenic activities strongly influence water quality. However, comprehensive studies integrating hydrochemical characterization, multivariate statistical analysis, geochemical modelling, irrigation suitability assessment, and geospatial analysis remain limited for the crystalline aquifers of southern India. abstract: Abstract Groundwater contamination assessments based on sparse wells rarely provide continuous hydraulic head and contaminant concentration fields for plume interpretation. Visually plausible reconstructions may not retain the transport information needed for physical diagnosis. abstract: Hydrogen blending changes the normal pressure–temperature state of natural gas pipelines, which can confound leak characterization when prediction models are transferred across compositions. abstract: Pantai Papuma merupakan destinasi wisata pesisir unggulan di Kabupaten Jember, Jawa Timur, yang menghadapi tekanan lingkungan seiring meningkatnya jumlah kunjungan wisatawan. abstract: Bellandur Lake in Bangalore, India represents one of the most severely polluted urban water bodies in South Asia, necessitating systematic monitoring for environmental management. This study employed Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument imagery to assess spatiotemporal variations in water quality parameters from January 2023 to December 2025. title: Incertidumbre algorítmica y agencia moral en la UCI: comunicar los límites de la predicción clínica.
abstract: Introducción: Los sistemas de inteligencia artificial (IA) pueden apoyar la interpretación de datos y la estimación de riesgos en las unidades de cuidados intensivos (UCI), pero una probabilidad calculada no elimina la incertidumbre ni determina por sí sola qué decisión es adecuada para una persona. Objetivo: Proponer un marco conceptual que distinga entre incertidumbre de los datos, incertidumbre algorítmica e incertidumbre biográfica u ontológica, y examinar sus consecuencias para el juicio clínico y la agencia moral. title: When augmentation backfires: Synthetic-data volume, generator quality, and classifier-side reweighting for minority-class bias correction
abstract: Generative models are often used to compensate for class imbalance in image classification, but their effect on minority-class bias is not guaranteed under low-data conditions. We present a controlled study of imbalance correction on Oxford-IIIT Pets and Oxford Flowers-102 using ResNet-50 classifiers, long-tailed loss baselines, synthetic-volume ablations, and a Swin Transformer architecture check. abstract: Abstract Wildfires are among the most destructive natural hazards, posing significant threats to ecosystems, communities, infrastructure, and economies. Accurately predicting the likelihood of wildfires enhances the effectiveness of preventive actions. Wildfire data is severely imbalanced toward the non‐fire observations due to the rare nature of wildfires. The features included in wildfire data cause separation problems and encounter seasonality. title: A bibliometric analysis on the use of UAV-LiDAR in forest structure attributes estimation
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-Light Detection and Ranging (UAV-LiDAR) is preferred for large-scale forest inventories due to its consistent, repeatable monitoring. While separate reviews exist for UAVs or LiDAR in forestry, global documentation on their integrated application remains scarce. Therefore, this study examines UAV-LiDAR application to: i) provide overview analysis, ii) assess authors’ keywords, and iii) identify emerging research themes in UAV-LiDAR application in Forest structure attributes (FSA) estimation. title: Sediment Transport Simulation under Flood Propagation by 2D HEC-RAS for Tigris River, Iraq
abstract: Changes in the hydrological regime significantly affect water quality and sediment delivery in all river systems. Sediment transport analysis aids in better understanding fluvial dynamics. This paper focuses on river dynamics, which maintain the environment and support low-cost training activities and flood control constructions. The work aims to evaluate the total load sediment transport rate in the case of unsteady non-equilibrium under the condition of flood in 2D waves adopted within the 2D HEC-RAS model. title: Practical Tools for Fire Risk Assessment in Mediterranean Open Woodlands Using Handheld Laser Scanning and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Photogrammetry
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forests are becoming increasingly vulnerable to wildfires. Given this, there is an urgent need for accurate, high-resolution data on canopy fuel characteristics to facilitate fire behavior modeling and guide risk mitigation efforts. This study assesses the performance of handheld mobile laser scanning (HMLS) and low-cost unmanned aerial vehicle digital aerial photogrammetry (UAV-DAP) in estimating key canopy fuel parameters and stand structural attributes, including canopy base height, stand height, canopy fuel load, canopy bulk density, and canopy cover. title: Comparison of ConvLSTM, ConvLSTM with Temporal Embedding, and 3D CNN for Monthly Rainfall Prediction in Bekasi and Surroundings Areas
abstract: Monthly rainfall in tropical regions exhibits complex spatiotemporal variability, requiring models to simultaneously capture spatial heterogeneity and temporal patterns. This study compares ConvLSTM, ConvLSTM with Temporal Embedding (ConvLSTM-TE), and 3D CNN for monthly rainfall prediction using CHIRPS v2.0 data (1990–2025) over a 20 × 20 grid domain (5.75°–6.75° S; 106.5°–107.5° E) covering Bekasi and its surrounding areas. title: Transdisciplinary team science: a field study in understanding and improving complex scientific problem solving
abstract: Introduction Transdisciplinary team science requires foundational teamwork competencies that support complex collaborative problem solving. This study examined the development of these competencies among graduate students from different disciplines. Methods We conducted a field study of a training program grounded in foundational competencies for scientific teamwork. title: GIS-Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia
abstract: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). title: Enhancing direct speech-to-image generation using speech-guided phoneme temporal net
abstract: Speech-to-image generation models aim to transform spoken language into visual representations without relying on text. However, existing models face challenges such as single-entity bias, action attribution errors, and phonetic ambiguity, leading to inaccurate visual outputs. To address these challenges, a novel Speech-Guided Phoneme Temporal Net is introduced to enhance semantic alignment and improve image accuracy. title: Ensemble Kalman Filter Optimization for Convection-Permitting Forecasts in Complex Terrain
abstract: Weather forecasting in complex terrain remains challenging due to mountainous topography, which generates high spatial variability, local atmospheric circulations, and rapidly evolving convective systems. This paper focuses on the optimization of the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) to enhance convection-permitting numerical weather prediction in complex terrain. title: Kaiser window-based S-transform for vibration signal denoising in rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Vibration signal analysis is widely used for bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, but the presence of strong background noise often masks fault-related features, reducing diagnostic accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a noise removal method based on the Kaiser window S-transform (KST), in which the signal is windowed over time using a variable Kaiser window. title: Exploring flexible sensing strategies toward embodied intelligence
abstract: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated into embodied intelligence systems, owing to their conformability to complex morphologies and adaptability to dynamic movements. abstract: Abstract Actor-critic methods with theoretical convergence guarantees constitute an important class of algorithms for multi-objective reinforcement learning. abstract: Selecting a colour palette that suits its design context (application domain, audience, and accessibility profile) affects usability, engagement, and accessibility, yet remains a difficult computational problem. abstract: Abstract Marimo, a natural microalgal-bacterial consortium, represents a low-carbon solution for nitrate pollution control in low-nutrient waters. abstract: Abstract Automatic speech recognition (ASR) is increasingly used to build large spoken-language corpora, yet its role is often treated as a purely technical preprocessing step. abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. abstract: Floating waste accumulation in rivers, lakes, and urban waterways has become a persistent environmental problem that requires efficient and low-cost collection technologies. abstract: Abstract. abstract: The deployment of multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) systems in real-world environments is hindered by domain shift, where performance degrades significantly when test data diverges from the training distribution. abstract: ABSTRACT The temperature field constitutes a core parameter for thermal‐process analysis and equipment optimization. abstract: The electrochemical chlorine evolution reaction (CER) is the cornerstone of the energy-intensive chlor‑alkali industry and is also emerging as a versatile platform for on‑demand chemical synthesis and environmental remediation. abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. abstract: Abstract Spirochetes are a distinctive phylum of spiral-shaped bacteria, defined by their curved periplasmic flagella, which drive motility by deforming the cell body and enabling efficient corkscrew-like propulsion through viscous environments. abstract: We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the dynamic selection of the filter parameter in Evolve–Filter (EF) regularization strategies for incompressible turbulent flows. abstract: The scientific quantification of regional net carbon emissions (NCE) and the elucidation of their underlying mechanisms are of great significance for advancing sustainable development. However, carbon-related research has long suffered from a separation between sources and sinks, and there remains a lack of systematic understanding of the driving mechanisms behind NCE. abstract: ABSTRACT To solve the difficult problem of fatigue life prediction of hydraulic concrete under complex stresses, this work conducts fatigue tests at stress levels of 0.75, 0.80, and 0.85, combined with multi‐model comparisons. Balancing ecological benefits and feasibility in large-scale restoration planning: A multi-objective optimization decision-support framework
abstract: Large-scale ecosystem restoration requires spatial planning tools that identify where limited resources are most likely to deliver durable ecological benefits. Yet ecological feasibility is often treated as an exclusion filter or screening criterion; here, we optimize it alongside biodiversity and other ecological criteria. We developed a multi-objective optimization decision-support framework that integrates ecological feasibility with extinction risk reduction, carbon stock priority, and riparian restoration priority. abstract: Multi-objective optimization in chemical engineering requires balancing conflicting objectives within highly nonlinear, simulation-driven design spaces. Traditional evolutionary algorithms can struggle with maintaining convergence, diversity, and computational efficiency when applied to such problems. This work presents NEMOPSO, a graph-theoretic multi-objective particle swarm optimization framework that enhances search performance through structured leader selection, topology-aware information flow, and adaptive exploration. title: A data-driven method coupling multiple physical constraints for correcting structural errors in groundwater contaminant transport models
abstract: Abstract. Model structural errors are pervasive in groundwater contaminant transport modeling under complex environmental conditions, hindering accurate prediction of contamination transport. Data-driven methods (DDMs) coupled with physical constraints provide an effective approach for correcting structural errors and improving prediction. title: Bendlet-Based Medical Image Fusion Using Modified Spatial Frequency and Contrast Visibility
abstract: Multimodal medical image fusion combines complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities into a single image to support clearer visualization and more informed clinical interpretation. Conventional fusion methods may introduce blurring, reduce contrast, or lose important edge and texture information, particularly when curved anatomical boundaries are not represented effectively. abstract: Camellia oleifera orchard navigation presents considerable challenges, including the limited field of view of ground robots, discontinuous crop rows, and complex shadow interference. To address these challenges, this study proposes a UAV-based method for inter-row navigation line detection using an improved DSConv-YOLOv11 model. title: Attribution and projection of 2020 summer-like hot-wet compound extremes in East Asia using large-ensemble regional climate simulations
abstract: A hot June followed by exceptionally wet July-August conditions in 2020 caused widespread disruption across East Asia; however, the anthropogenic contributions to such hot–wet compound extremes (HWCEs) and their future risk remain insufficiently understood. title: Quantifying Geodiversity in the State of Rio de Janeiro Using a Spatial Grid-Based Approach
abstract: Abstract This article presents a quantitative geodiversity assessment of Rio de Janeiro State using spatial analysis methods applying hexagonal grids and cartographic processing at multiple resolutions. Geodiversity is the variability, relationships, and assemblages of geological, geomorphological, pedological, and hydrological components and processes. title: A hybrid multiverse giza pyramid construction metaheuristic for robust engineering optimization
abstract: Abstract Achieving an effective balance between global exploration and local exploitation remains a fundamental challenge in metaheuristic optimization, often leading to premature convergence or slow convergence on complex engineering problems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel hybrid optimization algorithm, termed Multiverse–Giza Pyramid Construction Optimization (MV-GPCO), which integrates the complementary search mechanisms of the Multiverse Optimization (MVO) and Giza Pyramid Construction (GPC) algorithms within a unified optimization framework. title: Liability for rogue behaviors of agentic AI
abstract: This article addresses liability for harm caused by rogue behaviors in agentic AI systems (AAI), such as specification gaming and deliberate deception. These harms stem from inherent AI vices-intrinsic, inevitable, and unpredictable rogue behaviors of AAI which cannot be fully eliminated with the current state of technological development. Current regulatory frameworks mainly focus on risk prevention but fail to address how liability should be allocated when harms do occur. In response, we conducted a game-theoretic analysis to study the optimal design of legal liability for unpredictable AAI
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

abstract: Background: Oleaster (Elaeagnus angustifolia L.) fruit is a promising plant ingredient for functional bakery products because its incorporation can enhance the nutritional profile of cereal-based foods. However, using oleaster fruit powder in mechanically aerated frozen dough is technologically challenging because the gas-cell structure forms before freezing and, in the absence of yeast fermentation, cannot be restored after thawing. title: Wetbird-DETR: Detection of Waterbirds in Satellite Wetlands of the Middle and Lower Reaches of the Yangtze River, China
abstract: The wetlands of the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River provide important habitats for migratory waterbirds, but repeated image-based monitoring in small satellite wetlands is difficult because birds are often distant, partly hidden by vegetation, and photographed against complex backgrounds. Here, the use of automated object detection was evaluated as a support tool for waterbird monitoring in these habitats. abstract: Introduction Research on heritage experience has examined material settings, cultural meanings, and visitor appraisal through psychological measures and digital visitor records. abstract: Abstract Numerical analysis of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) combines aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, structural, mooring, and control models. Coupling topology is often used as a proxy for model fidelity, although topology describes information exchange whereas fidelity describes the physical processes represented within each subsystem. abstract: Abstract Detecting infrared small targets continues to be difficult because of indistinct object contours, intense background interference, and restricted multi-scale feature extraction. To tackle such problems, this work introduces EDGRU, an edge-oriented dual graph reasoning U-Net which simultaneously utilizes edge information and dual graph logic, and spatial graph attention for robust feature representation. abstract: This study develops and validates a mechanistically consistent plane-strain finite-element framework to elucidate how stiffness contrast and drainage capacity interact in controlling embankment performance on soft clay. A column-wall formulation is combined with coupled deformation-consolidation analysis and benchmarked against full-scale field data, reproducing settlement and excess pore-pressure responses with deviations generally < 15% during construction and < 10% during consolidation. abstract: In 2014, the report A World That Counts, commissioned by the United Nations Secretary-General, argued that better access to high-quality data would improve public decision-making to address major global challenges more effectively (Independent Expert Advisory Group on a Data Revolution for Sustainable Development [IEAG], 2014). title: A lightweight YOLO based framework for real-time seat belt detection in intelligent traffic surveillance
abstract: Abstract Road accidents remain a major cause of fatalities worldwide, and proper seat belt usage significantly reduces the risk of severe injuries and death. Ensuring compliance through automated traffic surveillance systems is therefore essential; however, reliable real-time detection remains challenging due to illumination variations, occlusions, windshield reflections, and low contrast between seat belts and vehicle interiors. title: Assessing threats to freshwater ecosystems: implications for water security management in Spain
abstract: Human threats to freshwater ecosystems overall compromise water security, and identifying these threats is essential to set up the required strategies in managing water resources. The article focuses on Spain as the region of study since this country maintains a long-lasting conflict between the use of water resources and the impacts on freshwater ecosystems. abstract: Landslide is a common geohazard that often occurs in mountainous areas. In recent years, this phenomenon has caused socio-economic losses and raised concerns regarding the conservation of geological heritage sites. In this study, field investigations, laboratory experiments, mapping, and analysis were conducted to assess landslides, causes, influencing factors, and their impact on geological heritage in former Quang Binh province, Vietnam. abstract: Tropical peatland drainage accelerates soil subsidence and carbon loss, yet short-term responses to rewetting in agricultural peatlands remain insufficiently evaluated. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en las universidades plantea desafíos que van más allá de la adopción de nuevas herramientas y que involucran las capacidades de dirección, control y aprendizaje institucional. abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. abstract: Abstract Hydroclimate whiplash describes swings between extremely dry and wet conditions. abstract: Afforestation is a crucial strategy for conserving biodiversity, mitigating climate change, and preventing land degradation to accomplish Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.2. abstract: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used for automated urban inspection, and the spatial layout of UAV nests directly affects inspection costs. abstract: This article presents a statistical forecasting framework for wind speed using two well-known classical forecasting models, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and the exponential smoothing state space (ETS) models with the naïve model as a benchmark for comparison. abstract: Rapid urbanization and inadequate municipal waste management in sub-Saharan Africa have exacerbated severe environmental and public health crises, prominently characterized by the operation of uncontrolled open dumpsites. In Ibadan, Nigeria, major disposal facilities such as La Awotan dumpsite rely heavily on open dumping and unmitigated burning. title: A target-domain augmentation and class-wise alignment framework for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis often has to adapt to a new operating condition with only a few labelled target samples. This setting creates two coupled problems. First, the sparse target support set cannot describe the target fault distribution sufficiently. Second, the same fault class may occupy different feature regions across source and target conditions, which weakens source-domain pretrained classifiers. title: Combining indices of soil pollution due to heavy metals
abstract: Soil contamination indices based on a single heavy metal (HM) fail to satisfy the interests of regulatory authorities, landowners and researchers who are more interested in a comprehensive index by aggregating such measures, facilitating evaluation of the effectiveness of remedial actions. title: Quick Commerce: A Bibliometric Review and Future Research Agenda
abstract: The present review is a systematic literature review-cum-bibliometric analysis of quick commerce (Q-commerce), the retail model that promises to deliver everyday goods within minutes. Through this review, the authors map how the field has evolved, who contributes to it and which themes dominate, and set out directions for future research. title: Merging Reaction to Cognition: A Hybrid Cognitive Strategy for Odor Source Localization in Natural Environments
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical pollutants released into the environment are transported by turbulent flows, generating complex and intermittent plume structures that threaten ecosystems and human health. Rapid localization of emission sources is critical, and field robots equipped with chemical sensors provide a viable means to perform this task. Nevertheless, inferring source location from sensor readings remains difficult due to sparse detections and the absence of reliable concentration gradients. title: Heterogeneous embedded monitoring of common carp pond water quality
abstract: Low-cost internet of things (IoT) systems are increasingly used in aquaculture, but many reports provide limited information on node architecture, signal processing, and validation scope. This paper presents a short-duration proof-of-concept evaluation of a heterogeneous two-node embedded system for a common carp pond. Node 1 used a LattePanda as a sensing node, coordinator, sink, edge gateway, and cloud interface; Node 2 used an Arduino UNO and an XBee router. title: Exploring Beyond Earth: Reconceptualizing Space Exploration as a Human Rights Imperative
abstract: Background Humanity’s transition from episodic exploration to long-duration human habitation poses a fundamental structural challenge to public international law. International human rights law developed within a terrestrial matrix predicated on sovereign territorial jurisdiction, geographical borders, and the natural availability of an unmanaged biological biosphere. In outer space, where national appropriation is prohibited under Article II of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, human existence depends unconditionally on engineered life-support infrastructure and autonomous algorithmic mediation. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines patterns of socioeconomic inequality among Brazil's 26 state capitals and the Federal District, totaling 27 capitals, and assesses the discriminatory capacity of SDG‐related indicators within the country's five major regions. The analysis uses data from the 2024 Map of Inequality among State Capitals, developed by the Sustainable Cities Institute and the Sustainable Cities Program. title: Communicative strategy selection in language anxiety: eye-tracking evidence of EFL learners’ multimodal pragmatic regulation
abstract: In the context of globalization, language anxiety has become a common obstacle for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners in cross-cultural communication. Centered on multimodal communicative strategy selection under anxiety, this study integrates a multimodal discourse analysis framework with eye-tracking technology to unpack EFL learners’ pragmatic regulation mechanisms. abstract: The crustacean shell waste generated by the shellfish industry poses a significant threat to the environment. Extracting chitin from invertebrate exoskeletons can reduce shell-waste disposal costs. This study aimed to convert Penaeus monodon shell waste into chitosan via a fermentation-assisted route and to test one batch of the product as both a coagulant for turbid water and a postharvest coating for grapes. title: Monsoon-driven dry-wet seasonal contrast reveals mitigation opportunity for methane emissions in South Asia
abstract: South Asia is a global methane (CH 4 ) hotspot with strong monsoon-driven seasonality, yet wet-season emissions remain poorly constrained due to persistent cloudiness. Here we quantify dry- and wet-season methane emissions separately over South Asia during 2019–2024 using TROPOMI-constrained analytical inversions. By leveraging satellite observations from downwind regions, we are able to effectively constrain wet-season emissions despite sparse coverage. title: ZOO: A Training-Free Framework for Open-Vocabulary Animal Detection, Segmentation, and Tracking
abstract: Abstract Quantitative extraction of animal visual information often relies on annotated data collected for specific species and recording environments, limiting rapid transfer across biological systems. We present ZOO (Zero-shot Organism Observation), a zero-shot animal visual analysis workflow that requires no additional training or fine-tuning on target species or recording environments. abstract: Abstract The endonuclear symbiont Holospora obtusa invades the macronucleus of Paramecium caudatum using an infectious-form invasion-tip containing a major 89-kDa periplasmic protein implicated in escape from the host digestive vacuole and macronuclear invasion. Sequence-based analyses placed this protein within a Holospora -specific family and predicted an N-terminal membrane-anchoring module and a long α -helical C-terminal region. title: HelioDA-XFE: ERA5-Based Solar Radiation Estimation and PV Potential Classification over Eastern Anatolia, Türkiye
abstract: Accurate assessment of solar energy potential is a core input for renewable energy planning in high-altitude regions such as Eastern Anatolia, where ground measurement stations are sparse. This study proposes HelioDA-XFE, an explainable feature engineering framework that estimates daily surface solar radiation (SSRD) from same-day ERA5 reanalysis fields (concurrent estimation, not forecasting) and assigns relative, radiation-based photovoltaic (PV) resource classes over an analysis domain centred on the Eastern Anatolia Region of Türkiye. title: Post‐Fire Mechanics of Corroded Q690 High‐Strength Steel and Influence on H‐Shaped Columns
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to characterize the residual mechanical properties and axial compressive behavior of corroded Q690 steel after fire exposure. Monotonic tensile tests were conducted on specimens subjected to indoor accelerated corrosion followed by high‐temperature exposure. Based on the results, an ABAQUS finite element model of corroded H‐shaped columns was developed for parametric analysis of post‐fire axial compression. title: Pengembangan WebGIS untuk Pendataan dan Pemantauan Lahan Sawah di Kecamatan Poleang Timur Kabupaten Bombana
abstract: Pendataan dan pemantauan lahan sawah memerlukan integrasi informasi administratif, lokasi, dan riwayat kondisi untuk mendukung pengelolaan pertanian yang sistematis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan WebGIS untuk pendataan dan pemantauan lahan sawah di Kecamatan Poleang Timur, Kabupaten Bombana, serta mengevaluasi kesesuaian fungsi dan penerimaan awal pengguna. title: Wind farm maintenance optimisation strategy considering MFTS distance‐based K‐medoids clustering and mixed Weibull model
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a wind‐resource‐weighted maintenance optimization framework to reduce operation and maintenance (O&M) costs and improve power generation efficiency. Existing clustering methods based on single distance metrics cannot fully capture the multidimensional temporal characteristics of wind‐speed data, while single Weibull models may provide insufficient fitting accuracy under low‐wind‐speed conditions. abstract: This study presents real-time vertical position tracking of an elastic cable winch system using a fuzzy logic-based PD (FLC-PD) controller. abstract: Study region The Indus River Basin (IRB) is a major transboundary river basin in South Asia. title: Measuring and Mapping Urban NO 2 Pollution Heterogeneity Using a Custom Pandora Spectrometer Experiment and Observations From TEMPO
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a primary pollutant present at high concentrations in urban areas. Ground based measurements remain sparse and satellite observations rely on retrievals, so understanding intraurban, diurnal‐scale changes in NO 2 is challenging. We present a novel methodology leveraging the sky scan capabilities of four Pandora spectrometers deployed around the Boston area to improve our understanding of intra‐urban NO 2 variability. abstract: ABSTRACT Metschnikowia bicuspidata , the causative agent of milky disease in the Chinese mitten crab ( Eriocheir sinensis ), is an important aquatic pathogenic yeast in freshwater aquaculture. However, the developmental characteristics and molecular regulation of its biofilm formation remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract This work presents a fully integrated microfluidic opto-electro-mechanical platform demonstrating a proof-of-concept for real-time colorimetric pH sensing in intensely colored textile solutions. The system features acrylic manifold with dual spectral sensors, an embedded magnetic mini-stirrer for rapid mixing, custom bidirectional syringe pumps, and automated fluid routing. abstract: Vertically resolved aerosol observations are crucial for understanding boundary-layer pollution processes and improving air-quality assessments. This study presents concurrent dual-height measurements of submicron aerosol chemical composition at a rural background site using a compact Time-of-Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer at 230 m and a ToF-Aerosol Chemical Speciation Monitor at 4 m, complemented by Sunset OCEC analyzers. title: Parameter estimation and identifiability analysis of stability and tipping points in potentially bistable ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Ecological regime shifts are potentially a common property of ecosystems, describing transitions between alternative stable states that can represent healthy or unhealthy conditions under the same environmental drivers. Once a tipping point, defined as a critical threshold separating alternative stable states, is crossed, the system may degrade and recovery can be difficult, making early detection essential for effective ecosystem management. abstract: Small object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging due to limited pixel representation, complex background interference, and the requirement for computationally efficient lightweight models. To address these issues, this paper proposes LDA-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework built upon YOLOv8 that integrates adaptive refinement of multi-level features and dual-domain attention to enhance fine-grained perception while maintaining low computational cost. abstract: ABSTRACT The growing participation of variable renewable sources in the Brazilian electricity system makes it necessary to understand how their different spatial and seasonal patterns can contribute to the stability of energy supply. In this context, the study evaluated the seasonal dynamics and spatiotemporal complementarity among hydropower, wind and solar resources in Northeast Brazil (NEB), between 1999 and 2022, with a focus on long‐term strategic planning. title: Time-Resolved Compositional and Redox Evolution of Dissolved Organic Matter During Biochar-Amended Aerobic Composting
abstract: Abstract Aerobic composting is a widely applied strategy for organic waste valorization; however, the mechanistic linkage between the structural transformation and macroscopic redox functionality of dissolved organic matter (DOM) under biochar (BC) regulation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the evolution of DOM composition, molecular weight distribution, and electron transfer capacity (ETC) during cow manure composting with graded BC additions (0%, 5%, and 10%). title: A dual-index assessment of warm-season heat stress for a small-island province in Atlantic Canada
abstract: Abstract Heat-stress exposure in maritime regions reflects the combined influence of temperature and humidity, yet these relationships remain poorly characterized in small, cool-temperate regions such as Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada. Here, we characterize warm-season thermal exposure across PEI during a 2020–2025 observational baseline using Humidex, representing human thermal discomfort, and the Temperature–Humidity Index (THI), representing cattle heat-stress risk. title: Spatiotemporal Characteristics and Driving Factors of Snow Drought on the Mongolian Plateau
abstract: Abstract Snow drought exerts widespread impacts on ecosystems and water resources. However, its spatiotemporal variability and key drivers in cold and arid regions remain poorly quantified. In this study, we used the ERA5-Land reanalysis to construct a snow water equivalent index to characterize snow drought. title: Physics‐Constrained Decomposition of Accumulated Fatigue‐Life Deviations After Static Residual‐Stress Correction in Welded Compact‐Tension Specimens
abstract: ABSTRACT Welding residual stress alters crack‐tip driving forces, complicating fatigue crack‐growth life assessment. Static corrections may leave systematic life deviations that are difficult to interpret. This study develops a physics‐constrained framework for diagnosing and decomposing these deviations in welded compact‐tension specimens. abstract: Abstract With the expansion of wind power scale, UAV-based remote sensing technology has become an important approach for wind turbine object detection in intelligent inspection, operation and maintenance, and wind energy resource assessment. abstract: We discuss a novel approach to Premodern Japanese Language Pedagogy (PJLP) with potential applications in other languages and fields. Drawing inspiration from grassroots initiatives such as the DIY and Maker movements, this paper advocates for an approach to AI in Education that fosters instructional and student agency over the pedagogical process. abstract: Abstract We report the first Greater Antillean record of Daptrius chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara), a bird observed between 24 and 31 March 2023 at the Grand Hotel Excelsior Port Royal in Port Royal, Jamaica. Given that this observation was made nearly 800 km from the species’ core range, the observed bird may have arrived via ship assistance, or it may have island-hopped northward through the Lesser Antilles. abstract: Abstract Gridded precipitation products are widely used to assess long-term rainfall and snowfall change, yet their trend reliability remains uncertain. We evaluate 19 (quasi-)global products for three annual statistics: mean precipitation, daily maximum, and wet-day frequency, screening for temporal homogeneity and benchmarking trends against daily and monthly rain-gauge observations. title: Remote sensing and the EU nature restoration Regulation: monitoring biodiversity indicators for integrated forest management
abstract: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear. This review synthesises current evidence on the use of RS for monitoring forest biodiversity indicators defined in the NRR and identifies methodological gaps and operational priorities. title: Weld Defect Detection in TOFD Images Based on Improved YOLOv8
abstract: Small defect indications, low contrast, and background noise make weld defect detection in time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD) images challenging. This study proposes SCW-YOLO, a TOFD weld defect detector based on YOLOv8n. abstract: Abstract: Endocrine disorders result from chronic disturbances in the hormonal regulation and feedback control, which cause metabolic, reproductive, and systemic complications. Despite the advances in disease management with current therapies such as hormone replacement or multi-pathway pharmacological therapies, problems with variable patient response, side effects and the need for continuous monitoring and dose adjustment remain. abstract: This study investigates reactive power compensation using a synchronous motor in a three-phase electrical power system without conventional capacitor banks through MATLAB/Simulink-based modeling and simulation. abstract: Abstract Increasing demand for construction-grade sand and continued generation of iron ore tailings (IOT) from mining create significant challenges for aggregate resource management. Utilisation of IOT in construction remains limited due to variability in mineralogy and particle characteristics, creating uncertainty in performance and restricting industry adoption. title: System dynamics evidence of sub-additive carbon reduction from combined mitigation strategies in multi-echelon logistics networks
abstract: The transition of multi-echelon logistics networks toward carbon neutrality is constrained by the inability of traditional static models to capture complex emission dynamics and time-delayed effects. To bridge this critical gap, this study develops a comprehensive system dynamics framework that captures non-linear feedback mechanisms, nonlinear interactions and temporal delays across transportation, inventory, and ware-housing operations. abstract: Background: Mine haul road conditions directly influence haul truck speed, cycle time, and operational productivity. title: Natural Compounds in Cancer Chemoprevention: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Cancer remains a significant global health challenge, with increasing incidence rates despite advancements in treatment modalities. Chemoprevention, utilising natural or synthetic agents to hinder, delay, or reverse carcinogenesis, has emerged as a promising approach to reduce cancer risk alongside conventional therapies. title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained significant attention in recent years and are rapidly emerging as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel‐based transportation due to their efficiency and environmental benefits. The primary objectives in EV development are to maximize energy utilization and extend driving range both of which depend heavily on enhancing motor performance. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Under the background of digital intelligence technology empowering the real economy, Specialized, Refined, Distinctive and Innovative (hereinafter referred to as SRDI) enterprises, as participants in technological change and a key force in promoting the high-quality development of China's economy, are facing multiple challenges such as market fluctuations, technological iteration and increased external environmental uncertainty. This review focuses on the valorization of second-, third-, and fourth-generation biomass, such as lignocellulosic residues, algal systems and industrial waste streams, in the context of integrated biorefinery systems. abstract: Introduction As AI evolves into agent-based forms, AI threat perception has become a defining workplace concern. abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. abstract: Lakes and other water bodies change over time and are influenced by natural and anthropogenic processes during the hydrological cycle. abstract: ABSTRACT NiFe (hydr)oxides are among the most active oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, yet their local structures, active sites, and synergistic effects remain under debate. title: Reliability analysis of machine operators employed in thermal spraying technology in the context of human resource management using the extended TESEO and HEART
abstract: This paper aims to develop a model for assessing the reliability of thermal spray machine operators using the Technica Empirica Stima Errori Operatori (TESEO) and Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART), which have been expanded to include four additional factors. abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become indispensable tools in programming education and professional software development. However, their output quality remains poorly characterized, particularly in terms of the semantic and linguistic quality of the explanatory text. Traditional evaluation metrics such as ROUGE primarily rely on lexical overlap and therefore only partially reflect the semantic adequacy of code explanations. title: Evaluating seasonal forecasts in Austria using agrometeorological indicators
abstract: Abstract Farmers rely on weather information to guide crop management; however, outcomes often remain uncertain until harvest. This pilot study evaluated downscaled medium- to seasonal-range forecasts for Austria (2018–2022), focusing on air temperature, precipitation, and six crop-independent agrometeorological indicators (stress and suitability metrics). title: Supply Chain Innovation and Business Success: The Mediating Roles of Logistics Performance and Service Quality in the Bangkok Frozen Seafood Industry
abstract: This study examines how supply chain innovation relates to the business success of frozen seafood firms in Bangkok and whether this relationship operates through operational capabilities. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and the Dynamic Capabilities View, integrated into a Resource–Capability–Performance framework, the study positions logistics performance and service quality as parallel mediators. abstract: Drought is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon influenced by both precipitation variability and temperature-driven processes, particularly under evolving hydro-climatic conditions. A comprehensive assessment of long-term drought dynamics across Türkiye is presented using multi-timescale Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) based on data from 21 representative cities across seven geographical regions. title: Advances in Wound Healing and Skin Regeneration: From Biology to Molecular Mechanisms
abstract: Introduction: Wound healing is a highly ordered and regulated physiological process for restoring the integrity of the skin after injury. Chronic wounds, such as diabetic ulcers and burns, still represent a significant clinical problem because of compromised cell reactions and disordered molecular signalling. This review aims to familiarise the readers with aspects of skin biology, wound healing processes, and basic cellular and molecular regulators of tissue repair and regeneration. abstract: Groundwater and terrestrial water storage in mining-affected regions are subject to complex variations, making it essential to accurately characterize their dynamics for sustainable water resource management. This study integrates high-resolution observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and its successor, the GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO), the Global Land Data Assimilation System (GLDAS), and coal-production data to analyze the spatiotemporal variations of terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), soil moisture anomalies (SMA), and groundwater storage anomalies (GWS

title: Investigation of relation between cyber hygiene and news veracity judgements
abstract: Introduction Cyber hygiene is often assumed to enhance individuals' ability to evaluate the veracity of online information, with potential implications for decision-making, social trust, and resilience to misinformation. However, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between cyber hygiene and news-veracity judgment remains limited. Methods This exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations between cyber hygiene and news-veracity judgment among 306 participants. title: A framework to determine the optimum number and configuration of wastewater treatment plants
abstract: Abstract Clean water is essential for life, ecosystems, and economic development. As water treatment technologies advance and sewage systems grow more complex, wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are essential for protecting public health and water resources. However, constructing these plants—particularly in developing countries—remains economically and technically challenging. title: Engineering rice for enhanced abiotic stress tolerance using genome editing
abstract: Rice productivity is increasingly constrained by drought, salinity, heat, cold, submergence, heavy metal toxicity, and herbicide-related stresses. Although conventional breeding has improved stress tolerance, progress remains limited by the complex, polygenic, and environment-dependent nature of abiotic stress responses. abstract: Global biodiversity loss is accelerating, with approximately one million species facing extinction and ecosystem degradation that compromises the welfare of over three billion people. While there is growing awareness and global consensus on biodiversity protection, nation-state governance alone cannot be counted on to address transborder species protection. abstract: ABSTRACT Spices are widely consumed in Morocco and may constitute a significant dietary source of toxic metals such as lead (Pb). This study assessed Pb contamination and associated health risks in six commonly consumed spices (turmeric, black pepper, paprika, cumin, ginger, and cinnamon) collected from Moroccan markets ( n = 200). title: From Natural Hazard to Psychological Impact: An Integrative Conceptual Model of the Role of Geographical Determinants in Psychological Vulnerability to Natural Disasters in Libya
abstract: The psychological fallout of natural disasters is rarely a direct function of the event's physical severity. Instead, it emerges from a complex interplay between hazard characteristics, localized spatial conditions, institutional efficacy, and the psychosocial resources accessible to affected populations. This paper seeks to construct an integrative conceptual model that elucidates how geographical determinants shape psychological vulnerability to natural disasters within the Libyan context. abstract: Brown carbon (BrC) is a light-absorbing component of organic aerosol that contributes to atmospheric radiative forcing by absorbing ultraviolet and visible light. Despite its climatic significance, long-term characterization of BrC in the Seoul Metropolitan Area remains limited, and previous studies have largely relied on single-solvent extraction approaches. abstract: The Jeju Genome Project (JGP) is a genomic and phenotypic cohort established to provide a comprehensive resource for precision medicine on Jeju Island, South Korea. abstract: Sediment transport caused by large earthquakes produces distinctive deposits that help extend our records of these events. To understand the underlying mechanisms of seismically induced sediment transport, we perform particle-resolved simulations of sediment transport over vibrating beds, with earthquake vibrations modelled as sinusoidal horizontal and vertical oscillations. abstract: This research examined the anaerobic co-digestion of Phragmites australis and poultry manure in batch reactors and evaluated the impact of combined pretreatment methods. Two substrate variants were analyzed: Sample A (mechanical pretreatment only) and Sample B (integrated mechanical-thermal-chemical pretreatment) with poultry manure. abstract: The vulnerability of rapidly growing cities to urban flooding reflects physical exposure, built form, and lived experience, but studies of these dimensions are typically conducted separately. abstract: This article explores how a small technologically advanced state, exemplified by Finland, seeks to maintain agency and manage security risks in Sino-US strategic technology competition, and what future options experts envision for it. abstract: Abstract River corridors play a key role in global biogeochemical cycling, with riverbed sediments often accounting for over 90% of ecosystem respiration. abstract: Ports connect maritime services with inland freight networks, so their efficiency may reflect not only terminal-side capacity and operations but also the external conditions under which cargo flows are generated and routed. This paper investigates the association of weather exposure and cargo-origin concentration with heterogeneity in port-efficiency outcomes. title: Dual activities of lysis and capsule degradation enable the bacteriophage protein Lys33795 to effectively disrupt Streptococcus suis biofilms
abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is an encapsulated zoonotic pathogen that can form recalcitrant biofilms. abstract: Managed aquifer recharge using floodwater (Flood-MAR) has emerged as a promising multi-benefit strategy to mitigate drought, groundwater depletion, and flood risk by capturing high-magnitude flows for aquifer recharge. However, widespread adoption is hindered by the lack of landscape-scale screening tools to identify Flood-MAR opportunities. title: Coping with Climate Change in Southeastern Europe: The Case-Studies of Greece and Bulgaria and Their Growing Cooperation with Israel
abstract: The article analyzes the main challenges posed by climate change in Greece and Bulgaria and examines the policies adopted by both countries to address its effects through climate adaptation measures. In this context, the article highlights the importance of technological innovation in climate adaptation policies and explores the emerging cooperation between Greece and Israel, as well as between Bulgaria and Israel, in the fields of environmental protection and climate adaptation.

abstract: Accurate stem and leaf segmentation and phenotypic trait extraction from maize 3D point clouds are essential for understanding plant architectural responses to stress and their relationships with agronomic performance. title: Sample preservation by freezing: impact on sulfite quantification in cooked shrimp
abstract: Sulfites are widely used in shrimp processing to prevent melanosis, yet the effect of freezing on sulfite stability during sample preservation for regulatory monitoring remains unexplored. This study assessed whether frozen storage at −18 °C significantly affects sulfite quantification in cooked shrimp, aiming to validate frozen samples as a reliable alternative to refrigerated samples in official control workflows. title: Technical Evaluation of the Smart Water Jug-Plastic Bottle Disposal System
abstract: This study evaluated the technical performance and behavioral impact of the Smart Water Jug–Plastic Bottle Disposal System (SWJ – PBDS) as a strategy at Ocampo National High School – Senior High School (ONHS-SHS). The research addressed the escalating issue of plastic waste, focusing on reducing plastic bottle consumption through innovative smart sensor technology. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining descriptive and quasi-experimental designs. abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. abstract: Ageing infrastructure in Saudi Arabia faces interacting threats from material deterioration, altered occupancy, extreme environmental exposure and uncertain construction records. abstract: The increasing convergence of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) in manufacturing has introduced cybersecurity risks that threaten production reliability, operational continuity, and safety. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of alternative therapeutic and diagnostic strategies. Among emerging approaches, bacteriophage-derived endolysins have attracted considerable attention as promising tools for combating bacterial infections. abstract: Bamboo is an ecologically and economically significant resource that contributes to biodiversity conservation, soil stabilization, and the livelihoods of rural communities. title: First record of a terrestrial crab preying upon Amazona barbadensis (Yellow-shouldered Amazon) nestlings
abstract: Abstract During routine nest monitoring on Bonaire, we documented two unprecedented nestling mortalities of Amazona barbadensis (Yellow-shouldered Amazon) consistent with assumed predation by a terrestrial crab, Gecarcinus ruricola. The first incident involved a chick approximately two weeks old that exhibited conspicuous limb lesions and a ruptured crop. A subsequent inspection of the same nest revealed a second dead chick in the presence of an adult crab. abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze and optimize the implementation of smart tourism in supporting sustainable tourism development in West Nusa Tenggara through an adaptive governance approach. abstract: The object of this study is the process of manual collection of floating plastic waste using small boats (jukung) in the Martapura River, Riam Kanan Sub-Watershed, Indonesia. The problem is that river cleaning is rarely planned on the basis of measured collection loads, so it is unclear where and when cleanup should be prioritized. Two river segments, each about 200 m long, with high and low population density, were studied over four days with three sessions per day (24 observations, June 2024). This crisis is largely driven by dependence on imported fossil fuels, highlighting the need for reliable and sustainable power sources. abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization in tropical cities is intensifying surface urban heat island (SUHI) effects, posing significant challenges for sustainable urban planning. abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) enables simultaneous acquisition of spectral and spatial information and has been widely adopted across science and engineering. abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. abstract: Wildlife crimes seriously threaten biodiversity and public health security. Identifying the species of wild animals and their products involved in such cases is the key to handling them. This study aimed to establish a wildlife DNA identification system based on a local alignment algorithm, thereby providing reliable technical support for public security organizations with high-precision and high-efficiency species identification techniques. Our study aimed to estimate the prevalence of depression in the Tunisian population and identify associated socio-demographic and clinical factors. title: Future-ready livestock systems: climate resilience, animal welfare and sustainable adaptation
abstract: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, water scarcity, changing precipitation patterns, and emerging disease risks directly affect animal health, welfare, feed availability, reproductive performance, and farm profitability. Nowadays, to overcome these outbreaks, the agricultural industry largely uses aggressive synthetic fungicides. In addition, the expanding aquaculture industry produces a lot of discarded crustacean shells. abstract: Mathematical modeling in ecology is indispensable for deciphering ecological complexity and guiding sustainable resource governance, yet its explicit alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently quantified. abstract: Escalating climate change and unregulated riverbed construction have rendered floods the most devastating hydrometeorological hazards worldwide, posing severe threats to lives and infrastructure. The reliability of hydraulic models in predicting flood risks relies heavily upon the spatial resolution of the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) employed to represent terrain topography. title: Online education and digital learning paradigms in India: An exhaustive review of the literature
abstract: The purpose of this study is to give an overview of the evolution of digital learning paradigms, its implementation in Indian institutions and the challenges and opportunities which it provides. The review also seeks to identify gaps in the current research that can be used to direct future empirical and theoretical research. title: Comparison of Hydrochemical Characteristics of Groundwater in the Qihe River Alluvial Fan of North China over the Past 35 Years
abstract: Groundwater resources play a crucial role in socioeconomic development and domestic water use in piedmont alluvial plain areas. In this study, the Qihe River alluvial fan (QRAF) was selected as a representative area to investigate the evolutionary patterns of shallow groundwater chemistry in the North China Plain (NCP). Based on shallow groundwater monitoring data collected during the wet seasons of 1983 and 2017, the spatiotemporal trends in chemical characteristics and their influencing factors in shallow groundwater in the QRAF were studied using multi-hydrochemical and statistical methods.

Based on the results of the first stage, regression equations were derived. abstract: Introduction The conditions of climatic elements such as temperature, precipitation, humidity, pressure, and wind in a given area directly affect bioclimatic comfort conditions. abstract: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. abstract: Vegetable oils play a strategic role in global food systems. Global supply is largely dominated by soybean oil and palm oil, while production remains concentrated in a limited number of countries. This study examines how delayed supply response and concentration affect vulnerability using global data for 1990–2024. title: Optimal Channel Slope for Stream Restoration to Minimize Flooding and Erosion and Maximize Diversity of Habitat: A First Approximation
abstract: To restore a stream to a more natural condition and still minimize flooding and erosion, the optimal longitudinal bed slope and meander sinuosity are needed. A straight channel can reduce flooding but cause excessive velocity and concomitant bed degradation, incision, and riverbank collapse. Conversely, a highly meandering channel will have slower velocity but higher flow depths that can lead to flooding. abstract: La detección visual de daños en el pavimento requiere información estructurada para apoyar la inspección vial. El estudio analizó la aplicabilidad funcional de una aplicación móvil para registrar posibles baches mediante visión por computadora y geolocalización. abstract: Abstract India’s Nationally Determined Contribution commits to creating an additional 2.5–3 billion tonnes of carbon sinks by 2030. This study examines carbon storage and sequestration in the Western Ghats (WG) from 1992 to 2020, comparing Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESAs) and non-ESAs using the Gadgil and Kasturirangan committee reports. title: The redox code of Leishmania : An introduction and critical review of its metabolic strategies
abstract: Leishmania parasites use specialized survival mechanisms to endure and grow in unfavorable intracellular settings. A strong redox metabolism is essential for immune evasion and long-term intracellular survival. In contrast to higher eukaryotes, Leishmania uses a distinct thiol-based antioxidant system centered on trypanothione, which is not found in mammalian hosts. title: MetabHub: an integrative platform for plasma nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomics using mediation analysis, disease prediction, and risk stratification
abstract: Plasma nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomics offers a scalable molecular readout linking genetic variation, environmental exposure, and clinical physiology to future disease risk. Existing resources typically address metabolite-disease associations, metabolite quantitative trait loci, or prediction separately, with limited support for integrated mediation and longitudinal risk stratification. abstract: The red swamp crayfish ( Procambarus clarkii ) is a globally significant aquaculture species, yet the biological trade-offs between intensive pond monoculture and integrated rice-crayfish co-culture systems remain poorly understood at the intestinal level. This study investigated the intestinal physiological and microbial adaptations of P. clarkii reared in pond (high-input formulated feed) and rice paddy (low-input natural diet) systems for 60 days. abstract: Introduction: Fish milt is currently used predominantly as a culinary product, despite containing numerous biologically active compounds with high value-added potential, including nucleoproteins, enzymes, and proteins. Its integrated processing creates an opportunity to recover biologically valuable compounds, including DNA and hyaluronidase, within a single technological cycle. title: Thresholds and spatial effects of urbanization on ecosystem service supply-demand relationships: a multiscale study of the Wuhan Metropolitan Area
abstract: Rapid urbanization continues to reshape the supply–demand relationships of ecosystem services (ESs), posing increasing risks to regional sustainable development. Previous work has looked at the scale dependence and spatial heterogeneity of urbanization and how they independently impact supply–demand relationships of ESs but they have not been considered jointly. This study investigated the nonlinear effects of urbanization drivers on ES supply–demand relationships in the Wuhan Metropolitan Area (WMA). abstract: The transition to high-penetration wind power introduces critical frequency stability and low-inertia challenges to modern power grids. Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS), characterized by millisecond-level dynamic response and inherent electromechanical isomorphism, offer a physically backed approach to mitigating these vulnerabilities. title: Assessment of drought conditions in arid steppe hot regions of Karnataka, India, using meteorological indices and geospatial approaches
abstract: Drought is a main climatic hazard affecting water resources and agricultural activities in semi-arid areas. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal variability of drought in the hot semi-arid areas of Karnataka, India, using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and Rainfall Anomaly Index (RAI). Meteorological data from 11 grid stations covering 1979 to 2019 were analysed, with the indices calculated at 3-, 6-, and 12-month timescales. title: Temporal Layering and Rule-Based Matching in Distributed Settlement Ledgers: A Multi-Horizon Reconciliation Architecture for Financial Break Detection
abstract: Financial settlement breaks remain a persistent operational risk. Batch-only reconciliation detects them only after end-of-day cutoff, while stream-based approaches often sacrifice coverage or lack shared rule semantics across horizons. This paper presents a multi-horizon reconciliation architecture coordinating three tiers over one transaction stream: daily batch, hourly incremental partitioning, and real-time listener-based interception. title: Multi-omics reveals the response and adaptation of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans BY-3 under arsenic stress
abstract: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ( A. ferrooxidans ) exhibits strong arsenic resistance and plays a pivotal role in biometallurgy and sulfur cycling in ecosystems. In this study, integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were employed to elucidate the molecular response mechanisms of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans BY-3 ( At. f BY-3) under arsenic stress. title: Pakistan-China Friendship at 75: Reflections on a Time-Tested Partnership and Its Strategic Future
abstract: This study examines the historical foundations and gradual evolution of Pakistan-China relations, highlighting the enduring friendship between the two countries over seven and a half decades. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1951, Pakistan and China have developed a close and multifaceted partnership based on mutual trust, mutual respect, shared strategic interests, and consistent diplomatic support. title: THE IMPACT OF LAND USE AND LAND COVERCHANGES ON URBAN FLOOD VULNERABILITY IN KIGALI CITY (2000-2025)
abstract: This thesis assessed land use and land cover (LULC) changes and their impact on urban flood vulnerability in Kigali City between 2000 and 2025. Using GIS, remote sensing and statistical trend analysis, the study analysed multi-temporal changes in built-up land, forest, wetlands, agriculture and other land-cover classes, and related these changes to mapped flood-conditioning factors and flood-risk surfaces. title: Waste cooking oil as a circular economy feedstock: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of biodiesel production
abstract: Rising demand for sustainable energy, together with growing concern over the environmental impact of fossil fuels, has focused attention on alternative biofuels. Waste cooking oil (WCO) is an attractive, low-cost feedstock for biodiesel that simultaneously addresses a waste-disposal problem and reduces reliance on virgin vegetable oils. This review synthesizes the literature on WCO as a biodiesel feedstock, covering feedstock sources and composition, pretreatment and transesterification technologies, and the techno-economic and environmental evidence base.
