title: The potential for large-scale genome editing in finfish aquaculture via germline stem cell culture and transplantation
abstract: Genome editing has emerged as a promising tool to complement selective breeding programmes and accelerate genetic gain in aquaculture. Although CRISPR-based genome editing has been successfully applied in several economically important fish species, its application at an industry-relevant scale remains challenging due to limitations of current delivery methods, which primarily rely on manual embryo microinjection. title: FibriLysins disrupt Staphylococcus aureus biofilms and abscess communities
abstract: The rise of antibiotic resistance, particularly among pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, necessitates innovative antibacterial strategies. Here we introduce FibriLysins, a class of engineered enzymes combining staphylokinase and endolysin, which dismantle fibrin-encapsulated multicellular staphylococcal communities, including biofilms and staphylococcal abscess communities (SACs). abstract: Animal venoms constitute a rich source of bioactive peptides targeting membrane receptors, including G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ligand-gated ion channels. However, identifying receptor-binding ligands directly from complex venom mixtures remains analytically challenging because venoms are highly diverse and conventional screening approaches have limited throughput. abstract: CO 2 and H 2 O are the predominant fluid components in the Earth’s interior, spanning from the crust to the mantle. Fluid–fluid immiscibility in binary CO 2 –H 2 O fluids is of particular interest owing to its implications for geochemical processes and industrial applications, including geological CO 2 sequestration. CO 2 –H 2 O fluids exhibit re-entrant phase separation upon compression, yet, the microscopic origin of this behaviour remains unclear, in contrast to well-studied temperature-induced re-entrant phenomena. title: Measurement of electromagnetic field strength of GSM antennas by using unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: Abstract Conventional electromagnetic field (EMF) assessment around Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) antennas is typically performed from accessible ground-level or rooftop locations, which may not adequately capture the spatial variability around elevated directional antennas. abstract: Abstract Waste cooking oil (WCO) biodiesel offers a circular alternative to diesel, although its higher blending levels can introduce performance–emission trade‐offs. The present work deals with the multi‐response optimization of a compression ignition engine using a combined approach of biodiesel from waste cooking oil (WCO), aqueous ammonia (AH), and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). title: Local pollution challenges in the global energy transition: air quality near hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical plants in the Congolese Copperbelt
abstract: Abstract The Congolese Copperbelt is a major source of copper and cobalt for the global energy transition, but mineral processing creates substantial and poorly documented local air-pollution risks. This study presents a multi-pollutant, multi-directional, and seasonally resolved assessment of ambient air quality around one hydrometallurgical plant in Kakanda and one pyrometallurgical plant in Lubumbashi. abstract: This study examined spatiotemporal patterns of coconut production and their association with rainfall across six provinces of Eastern Visayas, Philippines, from 2010 to 2025. A balanced provincial panel (6 provinces × 16 years; N=96) was analyzed using Mann–Kendall trend tests with Sen's slope, a province fixed-effects regression of yield on bearing-tree density and one-year-lagged annual rainfall, and an area–yield–interaction decomposition. abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic polyethylene terephthalate (PET) upcycling coupled with green hydrogen production offers an energy‐efficient route for plastic waste valorization. abstract: The evolution of digital technology has transformed accounting practices globally, including within the small business sector. In the cities of Jayapura and Wamena, the adoption of digital accounting is crucial for enhancing competitiveness, despite specific challenges. This study examines the impact of accounting digitalization on the efficiency of business operators in these cities. abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt‐based cathodes have attracted considerable attention in aqueous zinc batteries, however, their application remains impeded by intrinsic trade‐off between high electrochemical activity and long‐term cycling stability. Herein, an entropy‐regulated fluoride cathode is proposed to overcome the limitations via co‐engineering electronic and atomic structures. abstract: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is widely used in studies related to atmospheric monitoring, climate variability, and air quality, with the Aerosol RObotic NETwork (AERONET) providing high-quality records. However, AERONET AOD time series frequently contain observational gaps associated with cloud cover, especially in tropical regions characterized by strong hydrological seasonality. abstract: Biofilm formation plays a major role in bacterial persistence across clinical and environmental settings, with particular significance in chronic infections. Achromobacter spp. are environment-borne emerging opportunistic pathogens increasingly recognized in biofilm-associated diseases. title: Equity dimensions of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards: Long-term spatial population projections for New York City consistent with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. abstract: Abstract Electrochemical and ionic signaling play key roles in regulating bacterial biofilm growth, spatial organization, and collective behavior. Delivering these signals with spatiotemporal control can enable biofilm engineering and interrogate fundamental processes. title: Harnessing stress-tolerant plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria for climate-resilient rice agroecosystems
abstract: Environmental stresses pose a serious threat to global rice production. Drought, flooding, salinity, heavy metal contamination, and the excessive use of synthetic pesticides are among the major stressors affecting rice production, with some of these pressures being exacerbated by climate change. This review examines the ecological roles, mechanisms, and potential applications of stress-tolerant plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) as a sustainable strategy to enhance the resilience of rice agroecosystems under adverse environmental conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Recent parallel single‐pixel imaging (PSI) has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional structured‐light techniques in complex reflection and transmission scenarios. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread pollutants in freshwater aquaculture systems, entering through the degradation of pond linings and nets, contaminated aquafeeds, agricultural runoff and atmospheric deposition. abstract: ABSTRACT Gram-negative bacteria deploy type VI secretion systems (T6SSs) to mediate interbacterial competition. Although numerous T6SS effectors have been identified, their pan-genomic repertoires and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood. abstract: Electrical distribution failures in industrial facilities threaten workers, equipment and continuity of production. Arc-flash severity cannot be controlled through hazard labels or personal protective equipment alone: it is shaped by prospective short-circuit conditions, protective-device operating times, equipment construction and the exposure created by maintenance tasks. abstract: Public services planned around averages can conceal structurally underserved residents in dispersed rural territories. This study develops a municipal digital twin simulator for testing drone-assisted emergency access in a Spanish municipality of nineteen settlements covering 406.71 km². abstract: Prior work has recommended the use of Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) to inform operational management of marathons. However, there is limited and potentially conflicting results on the spatial extent at which WBGT should be measured to sufficiently capture racecourse variability. abstract: Knowledge Management (KM) plays a vital role in enhancing organizational performance, competitiveness, and long-term sustainability. Nevertheless, the assessment of KM remains challenging due to the complex interrelationships among multiple criteria, often characterized by uncertainty, vagueness, and conflicting expert opinions. title: Diversity of smallholder rice farmers’ knowledge, perceptions and management practices for soil health in the growing market and agrochemicals-led agriculture in Tanzania
abstract: Agriculture in Tanzania, as in many sub-Saharan African countries, is experiencing political-economic transformations toward intensive-input commercial farming. Despite the implications of these farming models for soil health and the long-term sustainability of agricultural landscapes, little is known about how farmers understand and respond to these changes. abstract: Trait-based approaches have revolutionized ecology by enabling the characterization of biodiversity through species’ ecological strategies. The rapid development of multiple databases has shifted the focus from data availability to the critical evaluation of trait types to explore the functional diversity of taxonomic groups. abstract: Methods for improving the safety of nuclear energy production and use facilities, including nuclear power plants (NPP) and other large industrial facilities in various countries, are presented and discussed. abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid industrial expansion in developing regions has intensified pressure on river systems, raising concerns regarding cumulative water quality degradation. While previous research has established associations between industrial activity and surface water pollution, quantitative evidence linking the scale of industrial land use expansion to river water quality remains limited. This study investigates the relationship between the accumulated scale of industrial land use expansion and river water quality in the Balok River, Kuantan, Pahang. abstract: This paper proposes an Adaptive Security-Margin Tracing for Hosting Capacity (ASMT-HC) method for photovoltaic (PV) integration in radial distribution networks (DNs). The method combines voltage, branch-loading, and reverse-power-flow margins through a Composite Security Margin to directly track the active operating boundary without weighting coefficients. abstract: Hydraulic fracturing (HF) generates large volumes of flowback and produced water (PW), yet the downstream relevance of injected additives remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract As a traditional Chinese double-reed woodwind instrument, the Suona has evolved through representative forms such as the Tang Bili and Qing Sunaiyi. However, systematic studies on its acoustic characteristics across historical evolution remain scarce. abstract: This article shows how the environmental crisis is understood and conceptualized within the Czech conspiritual milieu. It attends to the so-called conspiracy theories, seeing them as a form of knowledge, which is assembled as people develop sensibility to affects, atmospheres, and resonances. abstract: Educational attainment is unevenly distributed across the 30 sub-districts of Karawang Regency, yet regional open data remain in raw form and offer no objective guidance for equity-oriented policy. This study segments the sub-districts by the educational attainment of their residents using K-means clustering. title: Farnesol, lyticase, and tyrosol against Candida albicans biofilms: Interactions with fluconazole and micafungin

abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐produced water (GPW) is increasingly recognized as an important low‐quality aqueous lithium resource. abstract: Hakaluki Haor is a major freshwater wetland in north-eastern Bangladesh, but the spatial concentration of persistent water and the consistency of recent winter open-water change remain poorly resolved. abstract: Digital transformation has become central to defense modernization, yet evidence remains limited on how digital capabilities and management capacity interact with national defense-industry self-reliance to shape national defense posture. This study examines the direct effects of digital transformation, management capability, and defense-industry self-reliance, and tests whether self-reliance changes the effects of digital transformation and management capability on defense posture. abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the pharmacological and computational potential of the methanolic extract of Combretum indicum. abstract: Targeted kinase inhibitors often yield transient or incomplete responses because tumour cells buffer pathway blockade through signalling cross-talk, motivating synergistic drug combinations. abstract: Introduction Environmental health disparities in the United States (US) are evident in PM 2.5 exposure, but few studies have documented wildfire-specific PM 2.5 disparities. Furthermore, aggregating broad racial groups may hide disparities for Asian American (AA) and Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander (NHPI) groups. abstract: La irrupción de la inteligencia artificial (en adelante, IA) en los procesos de diagnóstico médico plantea importantes interrogantes sobre su impacto en el consentimiento informado del paciente. ¿Debe el paciente autorizar expresamente el uso de la IA en decisiones que afectan a su salud? ¿Es suficiente con comunicarle que se utilizará? ¿Qué alcance debe tener la información ofrecida? abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation technology offers a groundbreaking approach to water treatment. However, the relentless pursuit of high energy efficiency has encountered a bottleneck in vapor generation, necessitating consideration of vapor diffusion. title: The 2009–2010 Ouazzane seismic sequence: evidence for a possible active horsetail-like termination of the Jebha Fault, Rif belt, Northern Morocco
abstract: The western-central Rif is characterized by diffuse seismicity, including a pronounced earthquake sequence occurring in 2009–2010 near Ouazzane, southwest of the Jebha Fault. The structural significance of this sequence and its relationship to the regional fault system remain poorly constrained. We analyzed the regional earthquake catalogue, performed double-difference hypocentral relocation and GardnerKnopoff declustering, and integrated regional focal mechanisms with mapped geological structures to investigate the spatial organization and seismotectonic significance of the Ouazzane sequence.

abstract: The flight performance of a golf ball is governed by its surface geometry, which controls boundary-layer transition, separation and wake formation, yet the effects of convex surface topology and of ball mass remain underexplored. abstract: Accurate building extraction from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is important for urban mapping, disaster assessment, and remote-sensing interpretation, but remains difficult because speckle noise, heterogeneous scattering, radar shadow, weak texture, and ambiguous building boundaries can degrade pixel-level predictions. abstract: Abstract Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae represents a growing clinical threat, particularly where multidrug resistance limits treatment options. Here, we report the isolation and characterization of three novel lytic phages from Benin (Kp1Bj_HH11_M23, Kp2Bj_LN294_M23, and Kp10Bj_LN54_14). abstract: Abstract Understanding ecological differences among functional village types can inform rural revitalization. We analysed 4,126 village units in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) at five benchmark years from 2003 to 2023, using an ecological resilience index (ERI) integrating resistance, adaptability and recovery. title: Climate-based suitability scenario models for high-protein crop cultivation in Europe
abstract: Despite several concurrent environmental and nutritional benefits, protein crop production in the EU remains low, and imports remain high. In this research, we aimed to identify areas conducive to cultivating human-grade, high-protein crops. title: Smart and Inclusive Cities: Challenges and Perspectives for Aging in Salvador, Bahia
abstract: This article explores the intersection between smart cities and the challenges posed by global population aging, with a focus on the city of Salvador, Bahia. It addresses whether current smart city initiatives are genuinely inclusive and human-centered, especially for the elderly. Drawing on updated data from the United Nations, IBGE, and WHO, combined with a bibliographic review of recent studies, the methodology follows a documentary and exploratory approach that allows for the correlation between demographic indicators, smart city rankings, and the WHO age-friendly city framework. abstract: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss is increasingly recognized as a grand challenge requiring new forms of innovation, coordination, and knowledge integration across organizational and institutional boundaries. abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are among the most prevalent intracranial tumors in adults. abstract: Future intelligent environments require infrastructure-native interfaces that can sense human activities and directly generate wireless communication events using standard protocols. title: The Influence of Personal and Social Resources on Career Adaptability among Chinese Engineering Undergraduates
abstract: Career adaptability is increasingly important for university students navigating rapid labor-market and technological change. This study examined the predictive relationships of self-leadership, self-efficacy, cognitive flexibility, AI literacy, and social support with career adaptability among Chinese engineering undergraduates. abstract: This study addresses the operational bottlenecks in regional disaster management caused by static, narrative-based Contingency Plans. abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. title: Transcriptomic reprogramming and displacement of mastitis-associated Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by lactic acid bacteria
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is one of the main etiological agents of acute mastitis during lactation, and its ability to persist in biofilms can compromise conventional antimicrobial treatments. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) have emerged as promising probiotic candidates for mastitis management, but the molecular mechanisms underlying their interaction with S. aureus remain poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of three LAB strains ( Limosilactobacillus fermentum I7, Limosilactobacillus reuteri 7SNG3–30 and Ligilactobacillus salivarius 22SNG3-30) to interfere with mature biofilms
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Hysteretic Dynamics of Stream Network Expansion and Contraction Revealed Through High‐Resolution Integrated Hydrological Modeling
abstract: Abstract As landscapes cycle through wetting and drying, stream networks expand and contract, driving material export and biogeochemical transformations with important implications for water quality and ecosystem function. Because it is challenging to measure the extent of the active network, streamflow () is often used as a proxy. However, the relationship remains uncertain, especially for larger catchments where direct observation is labor intensive. title: Ambrisentan ameliorates methotrexate nephrotoxicity through modulation of RhoA/ROCK and PI3K/MDM2-associated signaling: network pharmacology-guided discovery and in vivo confirmation
abstract: Introduction Methotrexate (MTX) is a potent antineoplastic agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by nephrotoxicity, which may result in treatment interruption. Previous evidence indicates that MTX can promote endothelin-1 (ET-1)-associated renal injury. Therefore, this study investigated whether blocking ET-1 receptors with Ambrisentan (AMB) could alleviate MTX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). title: Change-aware contrastive learning framework for dynamic multi-objective optimization
abstract: Dynamic multi-objective optimization problems pose significant challenges due to frequent environmental changes, insufficient exploitation of historical knowledge, and limited generalization capability of predictive models. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Change-aware Dynamic Contrastive Learning framework (CDCL) for dynamic multi-objective optimization. abstract: Aircraft takeoff mass is a critical input to performance models, directly driving thrust, fuelconsumption, and climb performance. When the flight plan is unavailable and the operatorcannot be reached, this mass must be estimated from data accessible for any flight. Thispaper presents a methodology for estimating takeoff mass from takeoff-roll and early-climbperformance using only Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) and weatherforecasts. title: Time-series image velocimetry based on time-delay estimation: a proof-of-concept study
abstract: Abstract In fluid image velocimetry, velocity is conventionally estimated from the inter-frame displacement of image features (e.g., artificial tracer particles). However, this paradigm breaks down when the displacement exceeds the field of view, leading to observation failure. To address this limitation, this study proposes a time-series image velocimetry framework integrating the underlying principles of the pixel intensity cross-correlation and space-time image velocimetry methods. title: Numerical Investigation of the Effects of Equivalence Ratio and EGR on Combustion Characteristics in an n-Heptane Fueled HCCI Engine
abstract: Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition (HCCI) combustion offers low nitrogen oxides and soot emissions with high thermal efficiency, but direct control of combustion phasing is lacking. In this study, the effects of fuel-air equivalence ratio and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) on the combustion characteristics of an n-heptane fueled HCCI engine were investigated using a single-zone chemical kinetic model implemented in Chemkin. title: Microbial processes for sustainable metal recovery and surface engineering
abstract: Microbial manufacturing is emerging as a complementary method to traditional metal processing using microorganisms and their metabolites as functional agents for selective dissolution, recovery, surface modification, and protective mineral formation. This review critically evaluates microbial manufacturing with a focused emphasis on sustainable metal recovery and surface modification and finishing, integrating mechanisms, quantitative performance, process intensification, scale-up, and techno-economic and life-cycle considerations. title: Bioinspired Catalyst Design Accelerated Proton Transfer Kinetics for 1,4‐Butanediol Electrooxidation in Flow‐Cell Electrolyzer
abstract: ABSTRACT The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. Inspired by nature's enzymatic proton transfer systems, we report a bioinspired terephthalate‐modified NiFe‐catalyst (NiFe‐TPA) for efficient BDOR in a flow‐cell electrolyzer. title: Mutations in drug-resistant strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and associated treatment outcomes
abstract: Mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) genes may influence treatment outcomes in affected patients. We identified mutations in rpoB , katG and inhA genes of MTB, causing resistance to first-line anti-TB drugs, and evaluated their association with the treatment-outcomes in patients. Mutations were recorded as detected by line probe assay from 2017 to 2023. Treatment-outcomes of TB patients were retrieved from the Ni-kshay portal. title: Exploring rainfall thresholds for shallow landslides using effective half-life precipitation indices and cluster analysis: a case study in Santos and Guarujá, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Santos and Guarujá have a long history of shallow landslides, with rupture surfaces generally reaching depths of up to 3 m. The slopes are underlain by gneissic and migmatitic bedrocks, where failures occur in immature residual soils, often at the soil–saprolite interface and exacerbated by anthropogenic interventions. An extreme rainfall event in March 2020 triggered a major disaster, resulting in 41 fatalities. abstract: La inteligencia artificial está cambiando la forma en que las instituciones, profesores y estudiantes, aprenden, comparan y comparten conocimiento de manera transformadora. Este artículo considera esta relación más allá de la concepción de un ecosistema pedagógico y plantea la pregunta esencial: cómo la inteligencia artificial puede influir positivamente en la educación universitaria sin socavar la autonomía intelectual y la crucial conexión humana entre las comunidades educativas. title: Vertical accuracy of ASTER, SRTM, and NASADEM digital surface models across Malawi’s diverse topography
abstract: Digital Surface Models (DSMs) are widely used as important sources of topographic information for earth science and environmental applications. The accuracy of DSMs has direct impacts on several environmental calculations and processes. Therefore, it is imperative to select the most suitable DSM based on the aim and accuracy requirements of each application. However, the use of an appropriate DSM has always been a challenge. title: THE ROLE OF EDUCATION IN ENHANCING CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS AND DIGITAL SAFETY AMONG ADOLESCENT GIRLS AGED 13–19
abstract: Education plays a vital role in empowering adolescent girls to understand and respond effectively to cyber threats in an increasingly digital society. This study examines the implementation of cybersecurity education in schools, girls’ perceptions of online safety, and the role of educators in promoting cybersecurity awareness. The study adopts a descriptive research design in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh, using purposive sampling to select 90 female students and 90 teachers. abstract: Background Faced with the dual pressures of a global aging population and strained health resources, community health service centers serve as a hub connecting hospitals with home-based healthcare. abstract: This paper aimed to bridge the skills gap in South Africa through human capital development. Human capital development was one of the key components that led to the success of the Asian Tigers in achieving the criteria of a developmental state. Asian Tigers refer to Asian Countries such as China, Singapore, South Korea, and Taiwan that experienced very fast economic growth starting from the 1960s. abstract: Abstract Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex, which is distinct from that of vertebrate ORs. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. abstract: Cet article analyse les représentations, les usages et les non-usages des intelligences artificielles génératives (IAG) chez des élèves du secondaire en France. abstract: La irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (IAG) en la educación superior ha generado una crisis en los modelos de evaluación tradicionales, cuya validez se centraba históricamente en el producto final. abstract: ISSUE ADDRESSED: This study aimed to quantify Aboriginal adults' exposure to digital marketing of unhealthy food and beverages, alcohol, gambling, tobacco and e-cigarettes; analyse demographic differences in marketing exposure; and describe the nature of digital marketing reaching Aboriginal audiences, including brands, platforms and marketing tactics. title: Shape Memory Alloy Sealing Gaskets for High-Pressure Flange Connections
abstract: Abstract High-pressure flanges are essential components for joining pipes, ensuring sealing, and preventing liquid and gas leakage. Gaskets play a critical role when subjected to high stresses, situation where they can cause irreversible deformations that, combined with fluctuations in mechanical and thermal loads, can compromise their integrity. The present work aims to evaluate the use of shape memory alloy (SMA) sealing gaskets, specifically NiTi alloys. This work establishes a comparative performance analysis of NiTi and AISI 316 stainless steel gaskets under the same operating conditions.

title: D-enantiomeric β-casein 197 disrupts biofilm-associated infection of MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii through superior LPS binding and host cell protection
abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. L-form antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are rapidly degraded by proteases, whereas D-enantiomeric peptides offer enhanced resistance to proteases. Here, we synthesized L- and D-β-casein 197, a milk-derived AMP, and systematically compared their antibiofilm activities against eight clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii. title: A versatile on-axis visualization system for the macromolecular crystallography beamline BM07 at the ESRF
abstract: We describe the design of a new dual-magnification on-axis microscope adapted for actinic illumination on beamline BM07 at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). The instrument combines two cameras equipped with 50 mm and 150 mm focal-length imaging optics, providing low- and high-magnification views of the sample environment, respectively. In addition, the microscope incorporates two lateral optical ports for laser-light injection and collection of back-scattered fluorescence. Salinity Stress Elicits Genotype‐Dependent Responses of Turf and Forage Performance and Seasonal Dormancy Across Multiple Harvests in Orchardgrass ( Dactylis glomerata L.)
abstract: ABSTRACT Limited water availability coupled with increasing soil salinity poses a major challenge to sustainable turfgrass growth and performance. Dactylis glomerata L. (orchardgrass) is a widely distributed cool‐season perennial grass traditionally valued for forage production, with increasing interest in its potential as an alternative low‐input turf‐type species for water‐ and salt‐limited environments. However, despite its adaptability and stress tolerance, information on the salinity resilience and turf‐related performance of orchardgrass genotypes under field conditions remains limited.

title: Chemical drivers of mineral bioavailability and accumulation in microalgae: from speciation to cellular uptake and resource recovery
abstract: Critical and valuable elements are increasingly sought from dilute waste streams, but successful microalgal recovery depends on more than dissolved concentration. This narrative Mini Review examines how pH, redox conditions, ligand complexation, ionic competition, and phycosphere chemistry control elemental speciation and accessibility, and how these constraints interact with biosorption, membrane transport, intracellular homeostasis, sequestration, and stress responses. title: Microwall‐Integrated Terahertz Metasurfaces for Spatially Guided Label‐Free Sensing of Micrometer‐Scale Plastic Particles
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastic pollution is a critical environmental problem owing to its effects on ecosystems and human health. Therefore, technologies capable of accurately detecting micrometer‐scale polymer particles and converting their presence into measurable device‐level signals are indispensable for mitigating their impact. This study proposes a microwall‐integrated terahertz metasurface structure for spatially guided, label‐free sensing of micrometer‐scale plastic particles. title: Türkiye in Africa: strategic realignment through soft power, security, and south–south partnerships
abstract: Objectives This study aims to analyze Türkiye’s strategic engagement in Africa, focusing on its evolving foreign policy approach through soft power, security cooperation, and South–South partnerships. It seeks to understand how Türkiye positions itself as an influential actor in Africa and the implications of this engagement for regional and global geopolitics. title: Natural forests are key for bryophyte conservation, while active land-use reveals homogenous communities with low richness, new records, and habitat indicators in the Eastern Amazon
abstract: Abstract The implementation of strategies that integrate land use with biodiversity conservation has never been more urgent in the Brazilian Amazon. Here, we compared the effects of land-use types characterized by family farming and low-intensity management systems on the community structure of bryophytes and their lineages (liverworts and mosses) in the Eastern Amazon. We evaluated bryophyte communities across natural forest and three active land-use types: managed forest, agroforestry, and açaí monoculture. title: Structured learning with chatbots
abstract: This article presents and examines a writing process model developed to support students’ purposeful interaction with a chatbot acting as a group member in text production. The model structures the writing process into successive phases with clearly assigned purposes, division of labour, indications of chatbot roles to scaffold interaction, decision-making, and workflow management. abstract: The Aquila Optimizer (AO) is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm widely applied to solve complex nonlinear problems. abstract: ABSTRACT The sharp decline in light yield ( LY ) of X‐ray scintillators under extreme high temperatures remains a key bottleneck for their application in high‐temperature radiation imaging. abstract: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolution. Herein, we report the rational design of intermetallic Pt 2 W alloy nanoparticles uniformly anchored on N‐doped carbon nanomeshes (N‐CM), leveraging tungsten's exceptional thermodynamic stability and corrosion resistance to address this dilemma. abstract: To reduce the cost of estimating the probability of a rare event involving a very large number of random parameters, we propose a new strategy for dimension reduction coupled with a surrogate model for the expensive part of the algorithm. abstract: An experimental program was conducted to evaluate the effect of initial curing temperature on cement grout under sulfate attack by wet-dry cycling. title: Unyielding Resilience of the Schengen Area: Adapting to Crises in a Transforming World
abstract: Abstract The Schengen area has recently experienced many crises. Despite occasional references to its potential end, it has proven its resilience. Whilst researchers explore Schengen's borders and databases, few studies have focused on the discourse on Schengen per se. This article fills this gap by examining discursive shifts in the perception of Schengen's resilience during recent crises, especially since 2015 (refugee crisis, COVID‐19, Russian invasion of Ukraine). title: Development of mathematical models of heat exchange in control devices for ground robotic complexes
abstract: The object of the study is the heat exchange processes in isotropic 3D media with foreign thermally active thin inclusions. These media reflect individual structural units of control devices of ground robotic complexes. The study is related to the need for more accurate prediction of the thermal state of digital control devices under significant temperature loads. title: Climate-sensitive patterns of premature cardiovascular mortality in a subtropical city
abstract: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. abstract: Abstract Catenulids are free-living flatworms, common in eutrophic freshwaters such as ponds, ditches, or peatbogs, with most of the diversity described from tropical regions to date. Although the majority of the species have been described from warmer climates, most molecular studies have been done on specimens from temperate zones in Europe. We addressed this gap by sampling for exotic species in localities available in a temperate climate. title: Catching needles in haystacks: a structured search framework to optimise counter-poaching patrols
abstract: Counter-poaching patrols are a primary tool for protecting wildlife in threatened landscapes, yet detection rates of active poaching incursions are typically low and patrol planning frameworks that have been operationalised and performance-assessed remain rare. We describe a structured search framework applied over a decade of counter-poaching operations in the Kenyir Core Area, Malaysia, 1,200 km² of mountainous tropical forest critical to Malayan tiger recovery. abstract: The development of electrode materials with suitable structural and surface properties is crucial for improving electrochemical energy storage systems. Gamma alumina (𝛾-Al2O3) has attracted considerable interest in electrochemical research due to its unique structural and surface properties. title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. abstract: Abstract Precipitation plays a crucial role in Ethiopia’s rain-fed agriculture, ecosystems, and water resources; yet it exhibits, high spatial and temporal variability. However, the sparse gauge network makes accurate monitoring difficult. abstract: Turbidity is the most widely used surrogate for suspended-sediment concentration, yet its calibration is sensitive to particle size, sediment composition and hydraulic regime, and the assumption of a stable reach-wide relation is rarely tested in backwater-affected channels. This study evaluates the turbidity–suspended-solids relationship along a 5,000 m reach of the Erowha River, a distributary of the Forcados system in Delta State, Nigeria, during the wet season, when backwater from the receiving channel governs local hydraulics. title: Effects of Industrial Structure and Industrial Scale on SO2 Emission Intensity: Evidence from the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Industrial transformation and regional economic integration have reshaped the spatial distribution and cross-regional spillover patterns of industrial air pollution. Using a spatial panel model and data from 118 prefecture-level units in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YEB) during 2011–2020, this study examines the direct and spatial spillover effects of industrial structure adjustment and industrial scale expansion on industrial SO2 emission intensity. title: Exploring traditional rice germplasm in Sri Lanka: Morphological diversity, stress adaptation, nutritional value, and future breeding potential
abstract: Sri Lankan traditional rice varieties represent a valuable genetic resource characterized by substantial diversity in morphological, agronomic, adaptive, and nutritional traits. This study synthesizes the key variations observed among traditional germplasm with emphasis on vegetative growth, yield performance, stress tolerance, and nutritional quality to highlight their potential for sustainable rice improvement. title: Wet-year precipitation anomalies and geohazard economic losses in China: A province-year sensitivity and climate-exposure assessment
abstract: : Wet years can become economically costly when hydroclimatic anomalies coincide with geohazard-prone terrain and exposed socioeconomic systems. However, national-scale evidence on how interannual precipitation variability is associated with geohazard-related economic damage remains limited. Using a province-year panel for mainland China from 2003 to 2022, this study estimates precipitation-damage sensitivity within an administrative annual framework that links province-level wet-year anomalies to reported economic losses. title: Quorum sensing research in bioluminescent bacteria: a global scientometric mapping of research trends, knowledge structure and emerging research frontiers
abstract: Abstract Background Quorum sensing (QS) in bioluminescent bacteria underpins bacterial cell-to-cell communication, but the global evolution of this field has not been comprehensively evaluated scientometrically. This study maps QS research in bioluminescent bacteria to assess its developmental trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration networks, and emerging frontiers. title: Beyond Star Trek: Latin American science fiction and the ELSI of emerging technologies
abstract: Science fiction has been recognized as a place of anticipatory governance, with audiovisual productions such as Star Trek serving as prominent references in ELSI’s research on genetics, biotechnology, and human enhancement. Latin American science fiction has developed parallel and largely unrecognized imaginaries involving genetics, computing, and biotechnology from structurally distinct social positions rooted in inequality, colonial erasure, and the historically expendable body. title: Rethinking climate resilience: How digital transformation reconfigures tourism governance in Vietnam
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly promoted as a pathway for strengthening climate resilience in tourism, yet little is known about how it reshapes governance and differentiated adaptive capacity within local communities. Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative case study conducted between 2018 and 2026 in a community-based tourism village in Vietnam, this study examines how digital transformation has reshaped information flows, visitor acquisition, and informal coordination among local tourism actors. title: Sustainable development of high-speed railway to green railway construction in China: practice, countermeasure and prospects
abstract: Purpose This study reviews green high-speed railway (HSR) development in China from a full-life-cycle perspective, focusing on key environmental practices, challenges and future priorities. Design/methodology/approach A structured review of peer-reviewed studies, policy documents, industry standards and railway-sector reports is conducted across six dimensions: land use and biodiversity, embodied carbon, operational energy and emissions, noise and vibration, water and soil environment, and solid-waste management. title: El Futuro de la Arquitectura Actual, en la Era de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA)
abstract: La Inteligencia Artificial (IA) generativa se ha convertido en una herramienta que ha revolucionado la industria creativa, incluida la arquitectura, al ofrecer nuevas posibilidades para la generación de arte, diseño y contenido con la menor intervención humana. En este contexto, el presente artículo analiza la integración de la IA generativa en la arquitectura actual con los retos que plantea en torno a la autoría, originalidad, valor artístico, propiedad intelectual y autenticidad. title: Invisible shield: sprayable supramolecular antimicrobial microscale films for preventing wound and medical device infections
abstract: Wound and device-associated infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilms limit host immunity and antibiotic efficacy, promoting chronicity and resistance. Here, we present a portable, low-cost dual-syringe spray that deposits a thin, self-assembling antimicrobial film directly on wounds and implant surfaces. The device co-delivers oppositely charged hyaluronic acid (HA) and polyarginine (PAR30), a cationic antimicrobial peptide, which rapidly assembles into a conformal micrometric polyelectrolyte complex at the tissue-material interface. title: The Role of Tribal and Dalit Women in Water Conservation: A Case Study of the Western Indian Trans-Himalayan Region
abstract: Water scarcity and environmental degradation are pressing contemporary issues, and the Himalayan regions are especially at risk. The Trans-Himalayas in particular face severe resource scarcity as water availability is totally dependent on the now dwindling supply of glacial meltwater. Women in the Spiti Valley in the Trans-Himalayan region are particularly exposed to these issues because they spend significant time collecting water and fodder for domestic animals and managing agricultural irrigation. title: Towards a green China: energy policy, technological innovation, and green investment as drivers of environmental sustainability
abstract: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and green capital. This review synthesizes recent scholarship to examine how three interlocking levers, energy and climate policy, technological innovation, and green investment, jointly shape China’s transition toward a lower-carbon and more resilient development path. title: Ground wars
abstract: Abstract Above the banana plantations of northern Martinique, drones and satellites read the surface of the land for the stress it endures and the yield it promises. Beneath them, in soil that a synthetic pesticide has saturated for centuries to come, the ground is quietly undoing what was done to it. This lecture gives that undoing two names. title: Behind the organizational chart: The emergence of “gurus” in advice networks
abstract: Explaining the endogenous emergence of “gurus” – high-status professionals who are referred to for advice but are unlikely to seek it themselves – in organizations requires an integrated approach. This approach must consider the interplay of individual attributes (e.g., skills and status), structural factors (e.g., informal networks), and organizational contexts (e.g., knowledge-sharing infrastructure and internal competitiveness) from a dynamic perspective. title: ‘I'm Not Smoking; I'm Just Vaping’: Deciphering the Reasons for and Against Vaping and Intention to Quit Among Young Consumers
abstract: Abstract Vaping has become a defining feature of youth culture and a fast‐expanding consumer practice, yet little is known about how young people rationalize their continued use despite awareness of health risks and social controversy. Drawing on behavioral reasoning theory (BRT) and insights from social identity theory (SIT), this study examines how young consumers construct, compare and prioritize reasons for and against vaping under conditions of uncertainty, thereby deciphering their intention to quit. title: Fibrocalcific phenotypes in calcific aortic valve disease: imaging characterization, treatment timing, and efficacy assessment
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease involves two structural processes, fibrous matrix remodeling and mineral deposition, that contribute unequally between patients, so leaflets of similar hemodynamic severity need not share the same tissue composition. Histologic and multi-omics studies have mapped this heterogeneity across sex, age, and valve morphology, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography angiography (CTA) has brought compositional assessment into living patients and into longitudinal follow-up. title: Changing waters: from waterscape to landscape and back again
abstract: Across Sweden, around 2,400 lake-lowering and drainage projects since the early nineteenth century converted wetlands and lakes into fields, fixing a particular vision of progress into ditches, land deeds, and sediment. This article reviews 82 archival, scientific, and policy sources to ask what was done, why, and when, and to trace how these interventions continue to shape contemporary restoration politics. title: Protección de datos personales y garantía del derecho a la privacidad en Ecuador
abstract: La circulación masiva de información personal en entornos digitales desplazó la privacidad desde la protección del espacio íntimo hacia el control de cada persona sobre sus datos, de allí que el estudio se planteó como objetivo central analizar el régimen ecuatoriano de protección de datos personales y su capacidad para garantizar el derecho a la privacidad. abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study examines how the openly shared tabular portion of a publicly archived corpus of bibliotherapy-informed recommendations can be independently re-annotated and reorganized into a provenance-aware and media-sensitive framework for smart library wellbeing services. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a novel optimization methodology to determine optimal graphene platelet (GPL) distribution patterns and GPL volume fraction (GVF) in axially functionally graded GPL-reinforced (AFG-GPLs) composite curved beams. Existing studies are limited to predefined distribution patterns, restricting GPL-efficient structural design. title: The effects of national security assessments in public procurement on competition, sustainability, innovation, and critical technology procurement
abstract: By strategically leveraging public procurement, governments can harness market competition to drive business innovation and sustainable development. It remains unclear, however, how this premise is affected by heightened security awareness due to increasing geopolitical tensions. Focusing on European Union (EU) member states, we examine how security-oriented practices in public procurement affect tender outcomes. title: Effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis in the Horqin Sandy land
abstract: Background Continuous cropping is a major constraint that limits the sustainable cultivation of medicinal plants. However, the effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and the rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis , particularly in the Horqin Sandy Land, remain unclear. abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of digitalization through internet access in strengthening the economy in North Sumatra Province using panel data for the period 2010–2024 with the Vector Autoregression (VAR) method. The variables used include the Human Development Index (HDI), Investment (INV), Internet Access Users (IAU), Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR), and Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP). abstract: This study examines how the integration of green economy practices and social entrepreneurship shapes sustainable regional development through community empowerment programs in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Employing a mixed methods sequential explanatory design, the study combines quantitative survey analysis using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with qualitative in-depth interviews to explain how ecological efficiency and socially driven innovation jointly strengthen household economic capacity and regional resilience. title: Gender assignment of human nounsin Bantu languages
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how human nouns are distributed across gender values in Bantu languages. In Bantu studies, one gender value is widely described as the “human” gender, and it is generally expected that human nouns are predominantly assigned to it with some notable exceptions. Drawing on lexical data from 45 Bantu varieties in the RefLex database ( Segerer & Flavier 2025 ), the study assesses how consistently this expectation is met across the family. abstract: Introduction Livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (LA-MRSA) of Sequence Type (ST) 398 is widespread in European pig farming, yet molecular evidence linking specific farm strains to finished pork products remains limited. abstract: Abstract On 19 February 2025, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage re-entered the atmosphere over Ireland's west coast. It produced a sustained fireball along its trajectory across the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, northern Germany, and western Poland. Seismic and infrasound stations in the Netherlands and Germany, as well as infrasound arrays in Sweden and Norway, recorded the event. abstract: This study addresses countering unintentional IT insider activity, understood as actions by operators of automated systems that violate official job regulations as a result of behavioural deviation. This problem is reduced to an optimization problem, for which the authors have previously proposed an analytical model and a hybrid method for solving it. abstract: This paper presents the results of an integrated study encompassing archaeological and geological fieldwork, laboratory analysis of materials, and surveys of museums and private collections. These findings demonstrate the widespread use of various geological resources from the Cañadón Asfalto Basin by the indigenous populations that inhabited the current Chubut province in the past. abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is essential for modern electronics, yet conventional fabrication relies heavily on high energy consumption and chemically intensive processes. As sustainability becomes imperative, alternative technologies that lower energy use and carbon footprints are urgently needed. This paper reviews the role of sustainable laser-based processes as potential green solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. abstract: MXene quantum dots (MQDs) provide a chemically versatile platform for metal-ion sensing because their surface coordination environments, defect-associated states, and size-dependent electronic structure can couple molecular recognition to measurable optical responses. abstract: Jordan's energy security is essential given the nation's heavy reliance on imported oil and gas. Southern Ghour is a distinctive arid agricultural zone situated on the Earth's lowest land elevation, closely linked to energy demand, agricultural waste generation, and water scarcity. title: The bias of the biomass - different methods to determine spider biomass in ecological samples
abstract: Biomass is an important functional trait in ecology, because body size and the related mass influence biological parameters such as activity, energy demand, metabolic rates, and consequently population and food-web dynamics. In recent arthropod monitoring projects, however, biomass of samples is often used as a surrogate for abundance to detect population trends across larger spatial and temporal scales. In such monitoring programs, arthropods are typically trapped in a preservative, preventing direct measurement of fresh mass. As a result, biomass is commonly estimated using “drained weight”.

abstract: Cooperative localization in dynamic irregular networks estimates node positions from incomplete, noisy, and time-varying short-range measurements. This paper presents a distributed clustering and alignment method that decomposes global stress minimization into cluster formation, relative localization within clusters, and coordinate registration between clusters. title: TCLNet: A Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection
abstract: Infrared object detection plays an important role in low-light and complex-environment perception. However, infrared images often exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio, weak target-background contrast, and limited texture information, which can degrade detection performance in small-target and cluttered-background scenarios while making it difficult to balance detection accuracy and model complexity. abstract: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is an important indicator of ecological sustainability. The karst ecosystem is extremely delicate, featuring limited environmental capacity, severe erosion, and poor self-recovery capabilities. Quantifying the relative contributions of climate change and human activities to NPP in karst areas remains challenging. abstract: The early period of life is crucial for the development of species-specific traits and, as such, for a correct understanding of the evolutionary constraints and adults’ adaptations. abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish kinetics of oxygen electro‐catalysis, encompassing both oxygen evolution (OER) and reduction (ORR) reactions constitute a major bottleneck for energy conversion and storage devices like water electrolyzers and rechargeable metal‐air batteries. abstract: Land-use changes and human activities continue to pressure the upper Brantas River. abstract: Adverse conditions and work at height affect the safety and efficiency of radio frequency (RF) scanning at telecommunication towers. title: Phenolic profile and biological activities of ultrasound-assisted aqueous-ethanolic extracts of Tamarix hispida Willd
abstract: Tamarix hispida Willd. (Tamarisk; locally known as “zhyngyl” in Kazakh) is a halophyte traditionally used for dysentery, rheumatism, and ulcers, with reported antioxidant and prolyl endopeptidase-inhibitory activities. This study investigated the phenolic profiles and biological activities of 10%, 50%, and 70% aqueous-ethanolic extracts (THU-10, THU-50, and THU-70) obtained by ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE). Phenolic constituents were analyzed by HPLC-DAD, and antioxidant, enzyme inhibitory, anti-inflammatory, and cytotoxic activities were evaluated. Eleven phenolic compounds, including

title: Comparative evaluation of similarity metrics for Chinese retrieval augmented generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved impressive performance in natural language generation but remain vulnerable to hallucinations, particularly in Chinese short-text tasks where evidence grounding is essential. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a promising solution, yet most prior studies rely on cosine similarity over a single embedding model and focus primarily on English benchmarks. In this study, we systematically evaluate eight similarity metrics—Jaccard, Weighted Jaccard, Dice, character n-gram Jaccard, Sentence-BERT cosine, Euclidean, Manhattan, and Levenshtein—together
institutions: Shanghai University of International Business and Economics

title: Consist: Provenance-Aware Caching and Queryable Provenance for Scientific Workflows

journal: The Journal of Open Source Software

title: Behavior of Reinforced Concrete Columns Strengthened with FRP: A State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: Structural columns often require strengthening due to deterioration, increased load requirements, or structural modifications, and their complete replacement prior to the end of their design life is economically impractical. Rehabilitation of Reinforced Concrete (RC) columns using modern materials, such as Externally Bonded (EB) Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (FRP) composites, is widely used. Similarly, Near-Surface Mounted (NSM) FRP is an effective and reliable technique for improving column load-carrying capacity while preserving the architectural profile of the structure after strengthening. title: Panorama actual de la búsqueda de productos naturales con actividad antiandrogénica
abstract: El receptor de andrógenos (RA) es un factor de transcripción nuclear perteneciente a la familia de receptores nucleares esteroideos y constituye una de las principales dianas terapéuticas en el cáncer de próstata resistente a la castración (CPRC). El objetivo de este trabajo es integrar y analizar la evidencia reciente sobre productos naturales con capacidad para modular o inhibir la señalización del RA, así como discutir sus mecanismos de acción y su potencial relevancia frente a los desafíos terapéuticos del CPRC. Se realizó una revisión de la literatura científica publicada entre 2010 y 202

title: Estatuto ontológico de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) desde el realismo moderado de Aristóteles y santo Tomás de Aquino
abstract: La expansión de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) favorece atribuciones cognitivas que requieren una clarificación ontológica. Esta investigación aborda dicha cuestión desde el paradigma del realismo moderado de Aristóteles y santo Tomás de Aquino. Mediante un análisis teórico-conceptual que confronta la fenomenología técnica algorítmica de estos modelos con la ideogénesis intelectual, se sostiene que estos sistemas operan por correlación estadística sin intencionalidad ni interioridad. title: Brechas de desempeño del examen de habilitación para el ejercicio profesional en Enfermería
abstract: Introducción: El examen de habilitación profesional en enfermería evalúa competencias clínicas esenciales; por ello, identificar brechas de desempeño resulta clave para optimizar la formación y asegurar una práctica segura, ética y de calidad. Objetivo: Analizar las brechas de desempeño en los distintos dominios de competencia evaluados en el Examen Nacional de Habilitación Profesional de Enfermería (EHEP). Materiales y métodos: Se realizó un estudio observacional, analítico y de corte transversal, basado en datos secundarios provenientes de reportes oficiales del EHEP (cohorte de junio de 202
journal: Investigación e Innovación Revista Científica de Enfermería

title: La transformación algorítmica del poder público en México: fundamentos para un constitucionalismo de los derechos fundamentales en la era de la inteligencia artificial
abstract: El creciente papel de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en actividades públicas, administrativas y judiciales representa un desafío constitucional que solo puede abordarse a nivel técnico y ético. El diseño y operación de un sistema algorítmico en situaciones que involucren decisiones que puedan afectar derechos fundamentales se convierte así en una cuestión de legalidad, debido proceso, igualdad, privacidad y transparencia, protección judicial efectiva y responsabilidad pública. Este artículo explora la posibilidad de establecer un estándar particular para la evaluación judicial de la acción pú
journal: LATAM Revista Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades

title: Optimal Placement of PV-Based Distributed Generation and EV Charging Infrastructure in IEEE 33-Bus Distribution Networks Using Superb Fairy-Wren Optimization
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and Renewable Energy Systems (RESs) are increasingly growing in popularity, and this requires the application of advanced planning methods for ensuring their optimal integration into modern power distribution networks. This paper outlines a high-level optimization technique for optimal EV charging infrastructure placement and PV-based Distributed Generation (DG) in IEEE 33-bus Radial Distribution Systems (RDS). Proposed approach utilizes the Superb Fairy-Wren Optimization (SFWO) algorithm, nature-inspired metaheuristic widely recognized due to its high resistance agains
journal: AIUB Journal of Science and Engineering (AJSE)

title: Digital Transformation of Work-Integrated Learning in Vocational Education: Microcredential Technology, Collaboration, and Industry Engagement
abstract: Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) is a strategic approach bridging vocational education and industry requirements. This study investigates digitalized WIL implementation in Indonesian vocational schools, focusing on microcredential technology utilization, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industry engagement. A descriptive survey was conducted with 146 respondents from West Java vocational schools, predominantly mechanical engineering programs. Data were collected June-July 2025 using validated Likert-scale questionnaires covering microcredential technology utilization, collaboration, digital
journal: International Journal of Engineering Science and Information Technology

title: Eco-anxiety as a public health imperative: from individual resilience to culturally informed holistic engagement
abstract: Eco-anxiety has increasingly drawn public health attention. Although often conceptualized as an individual psychological burden, eco-anxiety may also serve as a catalyst for collective action. However, prevailing coping strategies largely center on individual resilience, with insufficient focus on social connectedness and the human-nature bond. This narrative review critically examines the limitations of individual resilience as a coping mechanism for eco-anxiety and advocates for a paradigm shift toward holistic engagement informed by Indigenous knowledge systems and traditional Chinese philo
institutions: Sichuan University of Arts and Science

title: Uso de Inteligencia Artificial y Evaluación Auténtica en Iberoamérica: ¿El Problema es la IA o la Forma de Evaluar?
abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa permite resolver muchas tareas escolares sin que el estudiante posea la habilidad evaluada, lo que compromete la validez de la evaluación. Este artículo teórico sostiene que el problema no es de integridad sino de validez, y que la respuesta no está en la detección ni en la declaración del uso de IA, sino en el diseño de la evaluación. Mediante una revisión documental narrativa de literatura reciente, se muestra que los detectores son poco fiables y sesgados contra quienes no escriben en su lengua materna, y que las políticas de declaración son instruccion

title: Microwave-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Microbial Compounds: Principles and Applications
abstract: Microorganisms are rich sources of high-value bioactive compounds, including lipids, pigments, carbohydrates, and enzymes, with applications across the food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and bioenergy industries. The growing interest in sustainable and efficient bioproduct recovery has driven the development of innovative extraction technologies. In this sense, Microwave-Assisted Extraction (MAE) has emerged due to its energy efficiency, rapidity, and reduced environmental footprint. This review explores the fundamental aspects and recent advances in MAE applied to microbial products. The diversi

title: Bacterial interfaces and surface chemistry shape hydroxyapatite mineral architecture during microbially induced calcium phosphate precipitation
abstract: Calcium phosphate biomineralization plays a crucial role in the formation of geological deposits, biological materials, and environmental remediation. While microorganisms are known to influence calcium phosphate precipitation, the relative contributions of bacterial cell surfaces and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) remain poorly defined. This study presents the first microscale investigation of the distinct roles of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial cells and EPS in regulating hydroxyapatite (HAp) mineralization, employing abiotic, EPS-mediated, and bacterial precipitation sy

title: Real-time testing of an optimal fractional-order PI controller for BDFIG-based wind energy conversion systems
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced control strategy for a grid-connected Brushless Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (BDFIG) wind energy system operating under variable wind and grid conditions. The method employs a Fractional-Order Proportional–Integral (FOPI) controller optimally tuned via a novel Cloud Drift Optimization (CDO) algorithm and applied across key control loops, including active/reactive power, DC-link voltage, and grid-side inverter control. title: ‘I think it's a rebrand…’: Pre‐service teachers' conceptualisations of adaptive teaching and differentiated instruction
abstract: Abstract This paper explores how pre‐service teachers (PSTs) conceptualise adaptive teaching in relation to differentiation within the contemporary policy landscape in England. Drawing on qualitative focus group data and informed by Bourdieu's theory of practice, the study examines how pedagogical understandings are shaped by social justice concerns, institutional constraints and emerging professional identities. The findings introduce pedagogical cynicism as a significant lens through which PSTs interpret reform alongside nuanced forms of teacher agency. The study offers original insight into
journal: Journal of Research in Special Educational Needs

title: Kalkolitik Çağ’da Balkan Madenciliği: Teknoloji, Üretim ve Otokton Gelişim

title: Uneven progress toward SDG 11.1 in Africa: a hierarchical clustering analysis of slum prevalence trajectories
abstract: Introduction Slum and informal-settlement prevalence varies widely across Africa, yet less is known about how countries have followed different paths over time. This study examines long-term patterns across African countries from 2000 to 2022. Methods The study used UN-Habitat data on the share of the urban population living in slums or informal settlements across 54 African countries. Countries were grouped according to similarities in their 23-year trajectories. title: Rhizosphere soils of Chilean temperate rainforests: an attractive source of potentially safer plant growth–promoting bacteria
abstract: Although millions of plant growth–promoting bacteria (PGPBs) are currently used in agriculture and soil health restoration, their potential environmental threats have largely been ignored. Here, rhizosphere soils from Chilean temperate rainforests (CTR) were collected and studied as an attractive, novel source of potentially safer PGPBs. A total of 847 isolates was assembled, and representative PGPB phenotypes and biocontrol (BC) activities were screened. title: Navigating multipolarity: India–China relations and the reconfiguration of global and regional order in South Asia
abstract: This paper examines how India and China are reconfiguring global and regional order through three interconnected objectives: the changing nature of global order and its influence on India and China as rising powers, the pragmatic cooperation between the two nations under balance-of-power politics, and their competing roles in reshaping the regional order in South Asia. institutions: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

title: Optimizing biodiversity benefits of NBS in nature-based urban climate adaptation
abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NBS) have the potential to provide solutions to a range of societal challenges, such as climate adaptation, and simultaneously contribute toward biodiversity goals. NBS are increasingly implemented in urban sustainability practice, especially in residential districts and business sites. This provides a great chance to simultaneously enhance local urban nature at the place where people live and work. However, as urban professionals have a predominant focus on climate adaptation functionality, the NBS design often misses opportunities to benefit biodiversity to its full p

title: A validated ordinal diagrammatic severity scale for zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Cucurbita moschata: Screening for tolerant accessions in Peru
abstract: Abstract The squash ( Cucurbita moschata ), a landrace crop with a denomination of origin in Lambayeque, Peru, represents a valuable genetic resource with potential for tolerance or resistance to potyviruses. Among these, Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV) is one of the most destructive viral pathogens affecting cucurbits worldwide. This study aimed to develop and validate a diagrammatic ordinal scale for assessing ZYMV disease severity under field conditions and to identify resistant accessions. title: Built environment and emergency medical services response time in a high-density megacity: multilevel evidence from urban–suburban
abstract: Introduction Emergency medical services (EMS) response time is a key indicator for evaluating the performance of public health system and is closely associated with patient survival rates. However, empirical evidence on the potential relationship between the built environment and EMS response time remains limited, restricting the development of spatially informed strategies for improving EMS system operations. title: Drone data enables high-resolution mapping and reveals hydro-topographic properties of high Arctic tundra vegetation
abstract: Abstract High Arctic tundra vegetation is highly fragmented, reflecting micro-topographical heterogeneity that governs local patterns of snow accumulation and soil moisture, and thus the distribution of plant communities. In this case study from Svalbard, we show the potential of using high-resolution earth observation data obtained with an uncrewed aerial system (UAS) to map and classify tundra vegetation communities, highlighting the importance of fine-scale hydro-topographic features. We used multispectral and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) UAS data with a spatial resolution of 10 cm t

title: Nested multi-source data assimilation coupled with a hydrodynamic model for enhancing water-quantity monitoring accuracy
abstract: Introduction Multi-source data assimilation combines observations and model simulations to improve water-quantity monitoring. Monitoring in the lower Lancang River is challenging because of complex basin conditions and hydropower regulation. This study aims to improve monitoring accuracy and efficiency. Methods We developed a nested multi-source data assimilation framework coupled with a hydrodynamic model. institutions: Ministry of Water Resources of the People's Republic of China

title: Parallel Photon‐Correlation LiDAR With Robust Noise Resistance Driven by Super‐Bunching Light
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance single‐photon light detection and ranging (LiDAR) technology with robust noise resistance provides a powerful means for environmental perception in extreme scenarios. Here, we propose a parallel photon‐correlation (PPC) LiDAR driven by super‐bunching light, enabling noise‐resistant parallel detection in the single‐photon‐counting regime. title: The impact of gait pattern personalization on the perception of rigid robotic guidance: a pilot user experience evaluation
abstract: Introduction Robot-aided gait rehabilitation facilitates high-intensity and repeatable therapy. However, most exoskeletons rely on pre-recorded, non-personalized gait trajectories constrained to the sagittal plane, potentially limiting movement naturalness and user comfort. Methods We present a data-driven gait personalization framework for an exoskeleton that supports multi-planar motion, including hip abduction/adduction and pelvic translation and rotation. title: Prioritizing career readiness by humanizing STEM for undergraduate education success
abstract: Abstract STEM-focused and social science skill sets will be required to successfully address many current global problems. Although providing active learning, communication, and technological skills—often lacking in current curricular approaches—is essential for STEM student success, they alone are insufficient to recruit, prepare, and retain students for rapidly evolving STEM careers. Here, we review practices that, by humanizing STEM, act to both entice students and prioritize their STEM career readiness. We promote combining the development of science career skills with social competencies

title: The mediating effects of perceived quality and brand image between country-of-origin and purchase intention for refurbished iPhones
abstract: This study investigates how Country-of-Origin influences Students’ Purchase Intention toward Refurbished iPhones, with Brand Image and Perceived Quality as mediating variables. A quantitative explanatory design was applied, involving 136 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS). The empirical results revealed that Country-of-Origin positively and significantly affected Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and purchase intention, both directly and indirectly. title: Spitting spiders (Araneae: Scytodidae) from Cretaceous Kachin amber reveal deep divergence times and Burma Terrane‐linked biogeography
abstract: Abstract The family Scytodidae is known for its unique spitting predatory mechanism, but its fossil record is extremely scarce, with reliable Mesozoic records previously lacking. Based on two male specimens preserved in Kachin amber, we report the first unequivocal Cretaceous record of this family—† Stedotuber gen. nov., with two new species, † S. longitibialis sp. nov. and † S. brevitibialis sp. nov. title: La inteligencia artificial como herramienta de apoyo en la valoración de la prueba penal en el Código Orgánico Integral Penal ecuatoriano
abstract: Objetivo: Analizar el alcance y los límites jurídicos del uso de la inteligencia artificial como herramienta de apoyo en la valoración de la prueba penal, a partir de las garantías del debido proceso en el ordenamiento jurídico ecuatoriano. title: The finance sector should capture the full range of climate change risks
abstract: Climate risk assessments used by the financial sector are often based on empirical data from recent decades that do not span the full range of possible futures. We argue that the financial sector needs to embrace risk analysis for all plausible scenarios, not just for median outcomes.

title: Wheat straw-derived lignin nanoparticles combined with postbiotics for antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and antioxidant applications in topical formulations
abstract: Introduction Plant-derived bionanomaterials have emerged as an important interest as a sustainable platform for new drug delivery and antimicrobial applications. In this study, biopolymer-based lignin nanoparticles were synthesized using wheat straw lignin. Method Lignin from wheat straw was extracted and used for the preparation of nanoparticles. title: Regional anthropogenic aerosol reductions temporarily increase probability of record-breaking heat extremes
abstract: Abstract Record-breaking heat extremes are becoming more likely due to anthropogenic climate change, with their probability depending on the regional warming rate. Anthropogenic aerosol forcing modulates these warming rates, and aerosols are declining globally. However, the influence of aerosols on the probability of record-breaking heat extremes remains unclear.
