title: Postbiotics as Regulators of Gene Expression and Enzymatic Activity in Fish and Shellfish: Implications for Growth, Immunity, and Reproduction
abstract: Postbiotics, a novel class of non-viable probiotic-derived feed additives, are emerging as a promising, sustainable alternative to antibiotics and live probiotics in aquaculture. Comprising inactivated microbial cells, cell wall components, and microbial metabolites (e.g., cell-free supernatants, short-chain fatty acids, and bacteriocins), postbiotics have been shown in laboratory and animal studies to enhance growth, modulate immune responses, improve gut health and microbiome balance, and increase disease resistance in fish and shellfish. institutions: Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research

title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. title: Investigation of Mechanical, Thermal, and Morphological Properties of Palm and Tamarind Fiber Reinforced Hybrid Polypropylene Composites: Effect of Fiber Loading, Fiber Ratio, and Alkali Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates hybrid polypropylene (PP) composites reinforced with palm ( Borassus flabellifer ) leaf‐sheath fiber and tamarind ( Tamarindus indica ) fruit‐shell fiber. The effects of fiber loading (5, 10, and 15 wt%), palm:tamarind fiber ratio (1:1, 2:1, and 1:2), and alkali treatment were evaluated. The composites were fabricated by hot‐press compression molding and characterized through tensile, flexural, impact, hardness, water absorption, FTIR, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy. title: Portable and Benchtop Micro-Raman Spectrometer for Organic Matter Characterization in Rocks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Abstract Recent technological advances have produced miniaturized, portable Raman spectrometers, enabling direct field analysis, even under challenging conditions or on samples that cannot be removed from the original site, such as confined artifacts or monuments. This study comparatively analyzed portable and high-resolution Raman spectrometers for organic matter (OM) and mineralogical characterization of bulk outcrop rock and thin-section samples from the Tamengo and Bocaina Formations of the Corumbá group in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. title: Biophilia as a temperament trait, not a universal: children’s attraction and aversion to biodiversity in the United States and Democratic Republic of Congo
abstract: Abstract The Biophilia Hypothesis proposes that biophilia is a universal human instinct, yet empirical support remains limited. This study tests the Biophilia Reactivity Hypothesis, which reframes biophilia as a temperament trait—an early-emerging, biologically influenced, and individually variable attraction to biodiversity. In the first cross-cultural study of biophilia in children, we tested 295 participants aged 3–13 from the United States and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). title: Surpassing Metal‐Centric E‐Waste Recycling: Unveiling Graphite in Spent Lithium‐Ion Batteries Towards Electrocatalytic Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. title: Clinical Task-Driven Design of Gastrointestinal Wet-Adhesive Hydrogels Across the Treatment Course
abstract: Gastrointestinal tissues present a particularly challenging environment for wet adhesion because persistent fluid exposure, chemical degradation, tissue motion, and biological renewal can disrupt both material–tissue contact and therapeutic function. Adhesive hydrogels have consequently evolved from tissue-binding materials into therapeutic interfaces for local drug delivery, wound coverage, hemostasis, and defect sealing. title: Native entomopathogenic fungi as potential biocontrol agents against Tetranychus urticae in strawberry cultivation
abstract: The two-spotted spider mite, Tetranychus urticae , is a major constraint in strawberry production, and its management still relies heavily on acaricides. This study aimed to select native entomopathogenic fungi with biocontrol activity against T. urticae in strawberry cultivation through field sampling, laboratory bioassays, and greenhouse validation. title: A deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm for regional drone routing problem with nonlinear fuel consumption
abstract: With the boom of e-commerce and increasing policy support, regional logistics serving medium- and short-distance transportation have grown rapidly. Large fuel-powered drones are increasingly adopted in this field due to their flexibility and efficiency, yet their deployment has raised concerns regarding pollutant emissions and environmental sustainability. To balance logistics efficiency with environmental responsibility, this paper proposes a regional drone routing problem using large fuel-powered drones, accounting for nonlinear fuel consumption and multiple pollutant emissions. title: YOLOv8-CNR: a lightweight fire and smoke detection model for forest fire scenarios based on improved YOLOv8
abstract: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOLOv8-CNR based on improved YOLOv8n. Methods The model optimizes backbone, neck, and loss function: C3_ConvNeXtv2 enhances flame texture and smoke edge representation; RepNCSPELAN4 strengthens multi-scale flow and small-target smoke features; SIoU improves localization of irregular targets. title: Further on Time-Varying Formation Control for Directed Networks with Switching Topologies
abstract: In this research, the time-varying formation (TVF) control problem is examined for general directed networks (DNs) subject to switching communication topologies, which widely arises in cooperative tasks of multiple mobile robots. In such practical scenarios, time-varying communication links induced by obstacles, agent mobility and bandwidth limitations bring nontrivial challenges for reliable formation maintenance. title: NiN 4 C‐Coordination Stabilized Cobalt‐Based Single Cluster Catalyst with High Active Site Density: Rationally Designed Atomic Architecture Boosts Oxygen Reduction Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of single‐cluster catalysts (SCCs) for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is hindered by difficulties in achieving atomic precision, high site‐density and resistance to aggregation during synthesis and operation. To address these challenges, we report a NiN 4 C‐coordinated cobalt‐based SCC which is synthesized via a gradient pyrolysis‐driven stepwise anchoring strategy that enables the sequential thermal anchoring of Ni and Co species. title: LIQUID LIMIT CORRELATIONS WITH FULLY SOFTENED AND RESIDUAL SHEAR ANGLES IN PROBLEMATIC CLAY SHALE: A BOJONEGORO REGENCY CASE STUDY, INDONESIA
abstract: Problematic clay shale formations in Bojonegoro Regency, Indonesia, frequently cause slope instability, foundation problems, and earthwork failures due to strength degradation. The liquid limit (LL) is a routine index property, while fully softened and residual shear angles are essential parameters for analyzing long-term slope stability in stiff clays and clay shales. This study investigates the relationship between LL and both fully softened and residual shear angles of clay shale samples from Bojonegoro Regency. title: Relación entre la Inteligencia Artificial y Procrastinación en Educación Superior: Una Revisión Narrativa de la Literatura

abstract: A new species of web-loving bug, Heissophila sinica sp. nov . (Hemiptera, Heteroptera, Plokiophilidae, Heissophilinae), is described from Fujian and Guangdong, China. The species was found inhabiting the webs of Orientothele sp. and Vacrothele sp. (Araneae, Macrothelidae). abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores recent advances in cord‐based wick systems that regulate water depth in distillers, a key parameter influencing desalination performance. abstract: This article investigates the brain’s resilience to trauma and adverse experiences, exploring how literature acts as a vital ally in fostering recovery and renewal. abstract: This study presents the first detailed description of bioerosion traces produced by insects in bones from the Santa Cruz Sequence (early Carnian, Santa Maria Supersequence, Brazil). abstract: El aprendizaje de algoritmos suele ser una etapa difícil para quienes están empezando a programar. Si bien las herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa facilitan obtener soluciones, muchas veces reducen parte del proceso de razonamiento, lo que termina afectando la forma en que los estudiantes abordan los problemas. abstract: Early detection of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced during microbial decomposition is crucial for preventing water-quality deterioration and disease outbreaks in intensive shrimp aquaculture. abstract: The Mekong River Basin (MRB) supports the world's most productive inland fishery, but is becoming increasingly fragmented by river infrastructure, with more than 13,000 barriers already present and further expansion expected. abstract: Background: Household food-security programs may address information deficits, ecological practices, and small-enterprise development separately, obscuring the connections between community needs and available assets. abstract: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. abstract: Background: Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who are on mechanical ventilation are at high risk of developing delirium. abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a strategic role in promoting local economic growth, generating employment, and improving rural livelihoods. Despite their importance, MSMEs face multidimensional challenges that constrain their sustainability and competitiveness. This study aims to analyze the challenges affecting MSME development in the villages of Blederan, Kalibeber, and Kejiwan in Wonosobo Regency, Indonesia. abstract: Introduction Understanding the psychological determinants of pro-environmental behavior is critical in addressing the escalating climate crisis. Despite increasing recognition of an important predictor of environmentally responsible actions, the role and interaction of eco-emotions remain insufficiently examined. This gap is particularly evident in non-Western contexts such as India. abstract: Background Endophytic fungi associated with the za’atar plant ( O. syriacum L. ) remain largely underexplored despite their potential as sources of bioactive natural products. title: Towards personalized and lifestyle-inspired soil management: lessons from the gut microbiome
abstract: Abstract Soil microorganisms are key drivers of ecosystem functions supporting biodiversity, food production, and climate regulation. Restoring multiple ecosystem functions under intensive land-use and climate change requires steering microbiome composition. However, this remains challenging due to the high complexity of soils and the assembly rules of their microbiomes. As the extensively studied human gut microbiome has considerable similarities with the soil microbiome, we explore advances in steering the human gut microbiome composition to improve the steering of soil microbiomes.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical dystonia (CD) is considered a basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and brainstem network disorder rather than an isolated focal motor disease. abstract: Post-consumer footwear constitutes a highly heterogeneous and minimally circular segment of the consumer goods economy. Although the sector has a substantial environmental footprint, empirical research on post-consumer footwear collection and reverse logistics remains limited. abstract: Abstract Biomass combustion is critical to Brazil’s energy transition, but high-temperature corrosion remains a major operational barrier in industrial boilers. abstract: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae , is a widely distributed and most destructive disease in rice cultivation, threatening global food security. abstract: The study focused on an analysis of the flood retention pond in relation to land use changes. Este artículo examina el Método MARTZ 5.0 como arquitectura metodológica orientada a convertir información territorial en ciclos de decisión, aprendizaje y regeneración. title: A review of the morphology of ohatsuki (stamen- or ovule-bearing) leaves, with relevance to physiological analyses of Ginkgo biloba
abstract: A Ginkgo biloba variant in which either stamens or ovules are generated on the edge of the leaf is known as “ohatsuki icho”. In this review, we highlight the morphological similarities among ohatsuki leaves, reproductive organs, and the leaves and seeds of fossil plants. Although ohatsuki phenotypes appear to be controlled by sex-related bud sports, their expression seems to be only possible in the river system, in the presence of seasonal winds, suggesting water-related control. We discuss a previous report suggesting that water conductance may contribute to the occurrence of ohatsuki malform

title: Air pollution and climate change impact on respiratory health in Africa: Evidence and interventions
abstract: Air pollution and climate change are global environmental health challenges impacting human respiratory health. In Africa, air pollution compounded by climate change is an important risk factor affecting respiratory health from early life and across the life course. While a lack of epidemiological data underestimates the burden of exposures and the resulting health implications, there is growing evidence that explores these interactions. In this narrative review, we aim to explore the interplay of air pollution and climate change on respiratory health, focusing on vulnerable African population
journal: Journal of the Pan African Thoracic Society
institutions: Red Cross War Memorial Children's Hospital

title: Postponed Nitrogen Enhanced Waterlogged Summer Maize Soil Nutrients by Regulating Microbial Diversity and Network Complexity
abstract: Waterlogging stress and low nitrogen use efficiency are important factors constraining summer maize production in the Huang-Huai-Hai region. However, how postponed nitrogen application modulates soil micro-ecological properties and mitigates yield loss in waterlogged summer maize fields by regulating soil microbial community diversity, co-occurrence networks, and community assembly processes remained rarely explored. title: FISC: a Fluid-Inspired framework for decentralised and scalable Swarm Control
abstract: Achieving scalable coordination in large robotic swarms is often constrained by reliance on inter-agent communication, which introduces latency, bandwidth limitations, and vulnerability to failure. To address this gap, a decentralised approach for outer-loop control of large multi-agent systems based on the paradigm of how a fluid moves through a volume is proposed and evaluated. title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era.This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer th

title: Rapeseed accessions as a climate smart agriculture strategy and food security in arid regions: yield, oil quality, and soil remediation under saline and wastewater irrigation
abstract: Climate change, water scarcity, and soil salinization are major constraints to crop production in the Eastern Mediterranean impacting food security, particularly in marginal lands where conventional irrigation is limited. Climate-smart agriculture approaches that combine stress-tolerant crops with non-conventional water sources may help sustain production while improving soil conditions. title: Exploration of Ethnoscience Content in Madurese Cultural Activities as a Basis for Developing IPAS Learning Strategies in Madrasah Ibtidaiyah
abstract: The teaching of Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) in Madrasah Ibtidaiyah requires learning strategies that connect scientific concepts with students' real-life experiences, yet the potential of local cultural activities as a basis for developing such strategies remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the ethnoscience content of four Madurese cultural products, namely Petis Madura, Rengginang Lorjuk, Terasi Madura, and Batik Madura, and synthesize it into a conceptual framework for developing culturally contextualized IPAS learning strategies. Using a qualitative descriptive approac
journal: Lambda Jurnal Ilmiah Pendidikan MIPA dan Aplikasinya

title: To Understand the Political Climate in Germany, Turn to Art: Review of “Made in Germany? Art and Identity in a Global Nation”
abstract: ABSTRACT The exhibition “Made in Germany? Art and Identity in a Global Nation” ran at the Harvard Art Museums between September 13, 2024 and January 5, 2025. Focusing on labor migration and German re‐unification as its two pillars, the exhibition presented German art since the 1980s and brought new names, many of whom have migration backgrounds, to awareness for the North American audience. The review makes two claims about this exhibition. abstract: Geçmiş olayların incelenmesi; afet risk analizi ve geleceğe yönelik sürdürülebilir senaryoların oluşturulması açısından kritik bir fenomenolojik anlayış sunmaktadır. title: Clinical outcomes and safety of finerenone in patients with heart failure: a real-world observational study in China
abstract: Abstract Objective Finerenone is a highly selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, but data on its benefits in the treatment of heart failure (HF) in real-world clinical practice remain insufficient. This study investigated the benefits and outcomes of finerenone in patients with HF using a single-center, real-world study design. Methods This single-center, retrospective observational study included consecutive patients diagnosed with HF and treated with add-on finerenone between August 2023 and May 2024 at Tongji Hospital, Shanghai, China. title: The Social Dimensions of a Potential GoTo-Grab Merger: A Review of Employment, Driver Welfare, and Regulatory Implications
abstract: The proposed merger between GoTo and Grab represents a major potential consolidation in Southeast Asia’s digital economy, raising concerns about market competition, employment dynamics, and driver welfare. If completed, the merger could give the combined entity more than 90% of Indonesia’s ride-hailing market, highlighting the need to examine the adequacy of existing regulatory safeguards. This study examines the potential implications of the merger for employment, driver welfare, and regulatory effectiveness. title: FROM COLONIAL POLITICAL ECONOMY TO MALAYSIA MADANI: TRACING THE EVOLUTION OF HUMAN-CENTERED DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE THOUGHT OF UNGKU AZIZ
abstract: The article examines the intellectual framework of Ungku Aziz in the development of Malaysia's story from colonial times to the present day under the leadership of the MADANI administration under Anwar Ibrahim. It claims that Malaysia's economic development is a gradual shift from a growth-oriented political economy to a more human-oriented developmental approach. In the colonial era, economic systems were mainly geared towards external capitalist interests, leading to socio-economic disparities and rural poverty. abstract: Purpose. To determine the effective location of a collective concentrate enrichment plant (CCEP) when develo­ping titanium-zirconium deposits using the principle of circular technology. Methodology. The work used a set of research methods: graphical-analytical method – to determine the parameters of technological schemes using the principles of circular technologies, as well as the location of the collective concentrate enrichment factory when moving the mining front; analytical method ‒ to establish the influence of the sequence of collective concentrate factory movements on the volumes of tr

title: Bioinformatics prioritisation of butyrate-associated targets and a four-gene immune-barrier score using public atopic dermatitis transcriptomic cohorts
abstract: We integrated butyrate-associated genes with the GSE32924 atopic dermatitis (AD) transcriptome and identified an exploratory four-gene transcriptomic signature (TP53, JAK2, H2AX, ALDH1A1), with sample-level AUCs of 0.951 in GSE16161, 0.888 in GSE120721 and 0.900 in GSE121212. These findings do not establish clinical transportability or disease-specific diagnostic performance. Immune analyses revealed concordant T-cell and neutrophil signals. title: Distribution and Interactions of Soil Nutrients and Organic Carbon at University of Calabar Campus, Nigeria
abstract: Plant biodiversity depends fundamentally on soil nutrient availability. However, nutrient dynamics within university campuses remain poorly studied, and less attention has been given to soil health, plant biodiversity, and the ecosystem services supported by campus soils. This study evaluated the influence of soil depth on the distribution, relationships, and multivariate interactions of soil nutrients and organic carbon across the University of Calabar campus, Nigeria. title: How do relapses among recovering people affect the spread of drugs in the presence of media coverage
abstract: The spread of drugs continues to pose a significant threat to societies. Given the widespread reach of various media outlets and technological advancements, media-based awareness campaigns can contribute to curbing drug abuse and preventing relapse following recovery. This paper suggests and analyzes a mathematical model of drug addiction that incorporates the positive role of media in raising public awareness and addresses the issue of relapse after recovery. journal: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

title: Case Report: Probable hepatosplenic tuberculosis mimicking undifferentiated connective tissue disease and malignancy
abstract: Background Hepatosplenic tuberculosis is a rare form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis with nonspecific manifestations, often leading to misdiagnosis. Tuberculosis can mimic connective tissue disease by presenting with systemic symptoms and positive autoantibodies, posing a diagnostic challenge. Case presentation We report a 69-year-old woman with polyarthralgia, oral ulcers, and positive autoantibodies including antinuclear antibody (ANA), anti-keratin antibody (AKA), and antiphospholipid antibodies, who was initially diagnosed with undifferentiated connective tissue disease (UCTD). title: Addressing conventional and emerging contamination in resource-limited rural water supplies: a full-scale before-after evaluation of a process upgrade and exploratory surrogate analysis of PFAS and antibiotic removal
abstract: Existing research on emerging-contaminant removal has focused on urban water treatment plants or single contaminant classes under laboratory conditions. However, resource-limited mountainous rural water supplies, where conventional pollutants and trace emerging contaminants—per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and antibiotics—co-occur as a composite pollution burden, cannot be adequately managed by the existing infrastructure. title: Influence of urban spatial structure and land-use distribution on residential and transport emissions in European urban settlements
abstract: Abstract While urban spatial structure and land-use distribution play an important role in shaping greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, their sector-specific effects remain insufficiently understood in comparative urban studies. This study develops a scale-independent comparative framework to examine how functional land-use distribution, spatial configuration, alternative density representations, and broader economic and climatic context jointly shape per capita residential and transport emissions across 104 European cities. Using city-level GHG inventories reported to the Carbon Disclosure Project

title: Hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for operations and maintenance disruption recovery in high-end equipment manufacturing under compound risks
abstract: Compound disruptions in high-end equipment manufacturing can simultaneously fragment operations and maintenance (O&M) resource networks and constrain critical resource flows. Using natural disasters and trade sanctions as representative compound risks of topology-based network fragmentation and capacity-constrained flow bottlenecks, this study addresses a recovery problem in which network reconfiguration changes the feasible space of downstream resource scheduling, while scheduling outcomes feed back through system-level evaluation to influence upstream reconfiguration. title: Temporal Stability and Entropy Generation in Rotational Micropolar Stagnation‐Point Flow Over a Biaxially Stretching/Shrinking Surface With Cattaneo–Christov Heat Flux
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines steady three‐dimensional rotational stagnation‐point flow of an incompressible micropolar fluid over a biaxially stretching or shrinking surface. The energy model combines Cattaneo–Christov heat conduction with thermal radiation and viscous and microrotational dissipation. Similarity transformations reduce the governing partial differential equations to a coupled nonlinear boundary‐value problem that is solved with an adaptive collocation method. institutions: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

title: Dual‐Functional Acetate Intercalation in NiMn‐LDH Cathode: Interlayer Pillaring and Electronic Delocalization Toward Advanced Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are regarded as attractive candidates for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their further development remains constrained by sluggish ion/electron transport and limited structural stability of cathode materials. To overcome these limitations, we designed an acetate‐intercalated NiMn layered double hydroxide cathode (Ac‐NiMn‐LDH) using a template‐guided assembly route. title: Putting your money where your mouth is: Expressions of Chinese nationalist sentiments are not just cheap talk
abstract: Abstract Do nationalist expressions reflect a willingness to pay costs or are they cheap talk? This is important because theories expect nationalism affects a wide range of outcomes that pose costs to participants, including international conflict and participation in boycotts. However, past research has either relied on self‐reports that cannot rule out cheap talk or outcome measures at higher levels of analysis, such as international trade flows, that do not directly link individual‐level nationalist sentiment to behavior. title: El monitoreo acústico pasivo como herramienta para estudios de diversidad funcional en aves
abstract: El monitoreo acústico pasivo (MAP) se ha consolidado como una herramienta fundamental para el estudio de la ecología de aves. Sin embargo, aún son escasos los estudios que aplican el MAP en el análisis de diversidad funcional en aves. En este trabajo describimos las ventajas del MAP para estimar la diversidad funcional así como sus limitaciones. Además, revisamos los enfoques disponibles para incorporar la detección en la estimación de métricas funcionales, presentamos una demostración matemática de algunas limitaciones de los métodos actualmente utilizados, y realizamos simulaciones que evalú
institutions: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

title: Development and characterization of an advanced holographic instrument for atmospheric research
abstract: Abstract. In this study, we develop and characterize an advanced holographic instrument — HOLODROPS (HOLOgraphic DROPlet Sensor) — along with a complementary event-based Particle Image Velocimetry (ePIV) system. HOLODROPS operates in two configurations: (1) HOLODROPS, designed for long-term, high-precision measurements of cloud droplet size distributions, and (2) HOLODROPS-TRACK, designed for short-interval particle tracking to study turbulence and collision-coalescence processes. title: Review of the P-graph Framework and its Applications
abstract: Abstract The P-graph framework was originally developed for solving Process Network Synthesis (PNS) problems in chemical plant design. Using axioms-based combinatorial tools, it reduces the optimization search space by orders of magnitude compared with direct superstructure optimization of the problem topology. P-graph tools also systematically generate maximal network structures, which eliminates human error in problem formulation. title: Enhancing tribological performance in laser powder bed fusion produced Ti6Al4V alloys via Cu-induced lamellar spheroidization
abstract: The tribological performance of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-processed Ti6Al4V alloys is inherently constrained by their lamellar α microstructure, which promotes strain localization, interfacial cracking, and delamination during sliding. Cu-induced lamellar spheroidization provides an effective microstructural strategy to overcome this limitation in this study. title: Subordinación jurídica y subordinación algorítmica: categorías diferenciadas del poder en el trabajo
abstract: El artículo revisita el concepto de subordinación como categoría de poder para distinguir, en él, dos especies jurídico-funcionales visibles en el mundo del trabajo contemporáneo: la jurídica laboral y la algorítmica. Se reconstruye la subordinación como relación asimétrica de reconocimiento, dependencia y legitimación, para mostrar cómo el derecho del trabajo la tradujo en el elemento basilar del objeto de esa disciplina y la justificación de la tutela que le es propia. title: A meta-precautionary solution to the dilemma of precaution
abstract: Abstract This article draws on the cross-disciplinary literature on risk, uncertainty and precaution to address a central dilemma put forward against precautionary principles. According to this dilemma, weak versions of precautionary principles, which hold that policymakers can justifiably adopt precautionary measures even when they lack certainty of impending harm, fail to justify adopting any precautionary measures. institutions: London School of Economics and Political Science

title: Former field relics across Europe: a review
abstract: Former field relics (FFR) are microtopographic features: ridge and furrow, lynchets, terraces, headland ridges, stone walls, and stone heaps, inherited from past farming practices. In Europe, they are often described as being “everywhere”, particularly in landscapes that have escaped modern agricultural intensification. In this review, we provide quantitative support for this assumption by synthesizing over 150 studies on FFR across Europe. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Spin‐State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon‐free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy‐intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐derived Co 3 O 4 electrocatalyst (MD‐Co 3 O 4 ) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co‐MOF‐74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability

abstract: This paper gives an in-depth analysis of a heuristic tackling the Service Location Cloud Problem SLCP, whose efficient implementation is a necessary prerequisite to solve the Generalized Traveling Salesman Path Problem GTSPP so far based on the recommended well-tried decomposition like Figure 1. For a given weighted directed graph, a partial assignment of clusters to graph nodes, a start s and a target t, the GTSPP reads as follows: Find a shortest s-t-walk that visits each cluster at least once! title: The hand of evolution: conservation and divergence of hand paralogs in cyclostomes and gnathostomes
abstract: The Hand family comprises basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors with key roles in the development of the lateral mesoderm, heart, branchial arches and paired appendages in vertebrates. Although Hand1 and Hand2 have been extensively studied in model vertebrates, the evolutionary history and diversification of Hand paralogs in early-diverging vertebrate lineages remain poorly understood. title: A proposal for a systematic hazard factor analysis for complex systems using Hierarchical System Theoretic Process Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a Hierarchical System Theoretic Process Analysis (HSTPA), a hazard analysis method for a system consisting of many components with complex functions. HSTPA is an extension of the System Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), which is used in the early stages of system development to analyse hazard factors arising from interactions between components. STPA has difficulty handling multiple and detailed component behaviours. journal: SICE Journal of Control Measurement and System Integration

title: SALES RISKS OF TRADING COMPANIES: THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PRODUCT POLICY, SALES POLICY AND CONSUMER BEHAVIOR
abstract: The article examines the problem of identifying and managing sales risks of trading companies under an unstable market environment characterized by military threats, logistical constraints, inflationary pressures, digitalization, and transformations in consumer behavior. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the theoretical and methodological foundations for identifying and systematizing sales risks based on determining the relationship between product and sales policies and consumer behavior. abstract: ABSTRACT Driven by the increasing severity of plastic pollution, biodegradable polymers such as poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC), owing to their biodegradability, gas barrier properties, and CO 2 ‐fixing capability, have attracted considerable attention as alternatives to conventional plastics. In this work, PPC/poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT)/epoxidized soybean oil (ESO) composite foams were successfully fabricated via an environmentally friendly supercritical CO 2 foaming process. title: Development of a Context-Based Learning Science Module Integrating Mappi Local Context for Papuan Students
abstract: This Research and Development (R&D) study aims to design and develop a Context-Based Science Learning Module integrating the local wisdom and natural environment of Mappi Regency (Papua) for Papuan students in the Primary School Teacher Education (PGSD) program at Universitas Negeri Jakarta (UNJ). These affirmative-action students frequently face significant cultural and academic transition barriers when learning abstract scientific concepts through unfamiliar metropolitan (Jakarta-centric) analogies. title: Notes on the nesting behavior of the Collared Forest Falcon (Micrastur semitorquatus) in Ceiba trichistandra within a dry deciduous forest of Guayaquil, Ecuador
abstract: The Collared Forest Falcon ( Micrastur semitorquatus ) is a falconid species distributed across the Americas, including Ecuador. Despite its broad geographic range, information regarding its breeding ecology remains limited in many regions. Nesting of this species has been previously reported in caves, human settlements and various tree species. Our observations reveal new data related to the ecology of this raptor in a highly threatened ecosystem, the dry deciduous forest. title: Evaluation of academic reliability and actionability scores of short-format video content: a cross-sectional study

title: Advanced 3D bioprinting of cell-laden bioinks for neural tissue engineering
abstract: Nerve injuries, including peripheral nerve injury (PNI) and central nervous system injury, remain challenging due to the limitations of conventional approaches in recreating the complex neural microenvironment and practical constraints such as donor-site morbidity and immune-related risks. Recent advances in 3D bioprinting enable spatial control over biomaterials, cells, and biochemical cues, facilitating the fabrication of biomimetic, cell-laden hydrogel scaffolds for experimental neural tissue engineering. title: Higher prevalence of rising climate-driven snowmelt potential of rain-on-snow events in the Eastern Continental US
abstract: Abstract Rain-on-snow (ROS) events have significant hydro-geomorphological consequences. While these events have been widely studied, their meteorological capacity to thermodynamically alter or melt snow when unconstrained by snow amount, hereafter referred to as snowmelt potential (SMP), remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to its long-term trends. title: Distributed elasticity: a high-reward, moderate-risk strategy for efficient control modulation in insect flight
abstract: Abstract The environments inhabited by flying insects demand a balance between flight efficiency and flight manoeuvrability. In structural oscillators such as the insect indirect flight motor, efficiency (arising from resonance) and manoeuvrability (arising from kinematic modulation) are typically quid pro quo, with modulation incurring penalties to efficiency. Band-type resonance is a phenomenon that offers, in theory, a strategy to lessen these penalties via careful navigation through a band of efficient kinematic states. title: Exploration of Parents' Experiences and Perceptions regarding The Role of Music in Their children having Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
abstract: The aim of this qualitative study is to evaluate place of music in the life of individuals having ASD with a phenomenological approach. Population of the study consisted of thirteen parents who have a child diagnosed with ASD. A semi-structured question guide was applied, in-depth face-to-face interviews were conducted. Each interview was transcribed verbatim. Themes and sub-themes were determined after marking the codes with consensus of the research team. title: Benchmarking convection-permitting climate simulations for hydrometeorological characterizations: a comparative study of WRF-SAAG and observation-based products in Chile
abstract: Abstract. Over the last years, significant progress has been made in the development of convection-permitting climate models (CPCMs), especially for improving precipitation modeling in regions with complex terrain. Recently, the South American Affinity Group (SAAG) developed a novel high-resolution dataset — hereafter referred to as the WRF-SAAG dataset — by dynamically downscaling the ERA5 reanalysis using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model over South America for the period 2000–2021. title: Novel index on the propensity for digital transformation in agriculture (PADiTIndex)
abstract: Abstract Digital agriculture is one of the levers that will enable food systems to adapt and remain resilient in the face of climate change. However, in addition to being generally slow to take off, its adoption is not geographically uniform. While studies at the producer level have investigated the rationale for this disparity, we argue that it could be that different countries and markets are prepared to absorb digital technologies into their value chains. This study assesses the propensity of different countries and markets to digitally transform their agriculture using a new proposed index

title: Virtual Reality Adoption in Malaysia’s Business Events Ecosystem: A Stakeholder Sensemaking Perspective
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) provides options to achieve higher levels of engagement, personalization, and service delivery in the industry of business events. However, to adopt it, it is necessary to meet the technology requirements, because its value for different stakeholders is perceived differently in the context of organizations and institutions. The present research studies the situation concerning the case of technology adoption in the business events industry in Malaysia from the perspective of stakeholder sensemaking. title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Sustainable Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic HMF‐to‐FDCA Conversion: From Catalyst Engineering to Energy‐Saving Paired Electrolysis Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic and electrocatalytic upgrading of lignocellulosic biomass into value‐added chemicals offers a sustainable route to carbon neutrality. 5‑hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key intermediate because its selective oxidation yields 2,5‑furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a renewable monomer for biodegradable polyesters. title: The Skin–brain Axis in Cutaneous Aging: Neurobiological Foundations and Clinical Implications
abstract: The skin– brain axis is a bidirectional neuroimmunoendocrine axis connecting psychological stress, brain signaling, immune responses, and skin homeostasis. A hypothetical link between dysregulation of this network and skin ageing is neurogenic inflammation, oxidative stress, cellular senescence, inflammaging, and activation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis. abstract: Environmental temperature fluctuations have substantial effects on sulfate-mediated anaerobic remediation of petroleum-contaminated soils, yet systematic investigations into the underlying mechanisms and temperature-dependent degradation signatures remain limited. In this study, hydrocarbon degradation in oxygen-limited microcosms and microbial community succession were characterized over successive remediation stages. abstract: , La alfabetización digital constituye una condición necesaria para que las poblaciones rurales puedan aprovechar las tecnologías de la información y la comunicación (TIC) en actividades educativas, laborales, productivas y sociales. title: Construction Management Perspectives on Flood Control Infrastructure Efficiency: A Case Study of Bay, Laguna
abstract: Flooding remains a recurring problem in the Municipality of Bay, Laguna despite the presence of flood-control infrastructure. This study assessed the efficiency of existing flood-control infrastructure from a construction management perspective, focusing on current condition and performance; structural and functional performance; planning and design quality; construction and execution; construction management performance; operation, maintenance, and community involvement; and implementation and management challenges. A quantitative case study design was employed using a five-point Likert-scale

title: La aplicación de los derechos digitales en Ecuador: privacidad y seguridad en entornos digitales
abstract: La digitalización de la vida cotidiana ha transformado la manera en que las personas se comunican, trabajan y acceden a servicios, generando nuevos riesgos para la privacidad. Es así que el estudio se planteó como objetivo central analizar la aplicación de los derechos digitales en Ecuador, con énfasis en la protección de la privacidad y la seguridad en entornos digitales. En este sentido se empleó un enfoque cualitativo, de tipo jurídico-documental, con análisis de contenido de 11 artículos científicos y cinco instrumentos normativos nacionales e internacionales. title: The transport of protein aggregates to the vacuole suggests a role for lipid droplets in waste disposal in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are organelles found in all eukaryotic cells, yet their contribution toward proteostasis is still poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that LDs in the model organism Saccharomyces cerevisiae function as transporters to which cytosolic protein aggregates attach for transport to the vacuole for degradation. title: The Ijāzah as an Infrastructure of Scholarly Authority: The Legitimation of ʿUlamāʾ within the Haramayn–Nusantara Network (18th–19th Centuries)
abstract: Studies of 18th- and 19th-century ʿulamāʾ networks linking the Haramayn and the Nusantara region have extensively covered intellectual mobility, knowledge transmission, and teacher-student relationships; however, they have not adequately explained the mechanisms that transformed knowledge transmission into the legitimation of ʿulamāʾ authority. title: University incubation ecosystems as a lever for innovation-driven growth: A comparative analysis of institutional and regional contexts in Algeria
abstract: This study examines how institutional and regional contexts shape the extent to which university incubation ecosystems in Algeria convert innovation output into the kind of economic value that sustains innovation-driven growth. Since 2021, business incubators have been formally integrated into Algerian higher education institutions, yet existing research remains largely confined to single-institution, descriptive assessments. title: ACCESS OF FOOD SECURITY THROUGH FINANCE FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRIBUSINESS PERFORMANCE
abstract: Access to finance is vital for improving food security, particularly in developing nations where agricultural production is crucial. Despite several financial interventions targeted at increasing agricultural production, smallholder farmers continue to lack access to reasonable, timely, and sufficient financing, limiting their ability to invest in improved technology and inputs, lowering productivity and food supply. title: Valorization of drilling rock powder in cementitious grout towards greener mountainous transmission construction
abstract: Rapid growth in electricity demand is accelerating the construction of transmission infrastructure across mountainous areas. Improper disposal of drilling rock powder (DRP) generated during transmission-tower foundation construction can disturb fragile mountain ecosystems and increase handling costs. This study examines the reuse of sieved DRP as an equal-mass substitute for Portland cement in cementitious grout. abstract: Biomass-derived porous carbons are promising adsorbents for environmental remediation, yet the relationships between pyrolysis conditions, pore architecture and adsorption behaviour remain incompletely resolved. In this work, nitrogen adsorption–desorption, BET surface area analysis, SEM imaging and isotherm modelling were employed to elucidate the influence of pyrolysis temperature (500- 700 °C) on the morphological and textural properties of biomass-derived carbons. abstract: A theory is elaborated illuminating the nature of moral injury based on evolutionary biology and psychoanalytic object-relations and self psychology, which explains how the betrayal of a moral trust can produce not only the negative moral emotions and losses of social and spiritual engagement characteristic of moral injury, but also the entire spectrum of adverse peri-and post-traumatic stress states. title: Prototyping a 1 kVA Voltage Regulation Power Stabilizer Using Capacitors Bridge Cascade Model
abstract: Voltage instability in domestic electricity supplies can adversely affect the performance and reliability of household appliances and sensitive electronic equipment. This study presents the design and experimental evaluation of a 1 kVA voltage stabilizer based on a capacitor bridge cascade model (CBCM) for improved household voltage regulation. Questionnaire data collected from Dar es Salaam and Coast regions were analyzed to identify challenges associated with existing voltage stabilizers and inform the design requirements. title: Subsurface drainage in salt-affected cropland: A tiered meta-analysis linking soil salinity reduction with crop yield responses
abstract: Subsurface drainage provides an outlet for excess water and leached salts in salt-affected cropland, but its benefits for crop production are not always straightforward. Many studies report soil salinity and crop yield separately, making it difficult to determine how consistently salinity reduction is accompanied by yield recovery across evidence types. abstract: Abstract This study investigates how mineralogical and microstructural alterations associated with alkali–carbonate reaction (ACR) may influence the salt–frost resistance of approximately 90-year-old concrete from the Rupnik Military Line. Historical limestone- and dolostone-aggregate concretes (HCL and HCD) were compared with laboratory-prepared counterparts made with CEM III/B cement and aged for six months in 1 M NaOH at 60 °C (LC3NH60 and RC3NH60). abstract: INTRODUCTION: The second-generation Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib have improved outcomes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) patients but comparative evidence is limited. This study assessed treatment patterns and clinical outcomes among patients with CLL/SLL initiating zanubrutinib or acalabrutinib in diverse real-world healthcare settings. title: ProgrEval: Assisted Generation of Assessment Tasks for Programming Education
abstract: El diseño de evaluaciones constituye una tarea central en el ámbito educativo. En particular, la evaluación en programación presenta desafíos adicionales, ya que no solo requiere valorar la comprensión conceptual y la producción de código, sino también la formulación de problemas, la depuración y la explicación o seguimiento de programas. La elaboración de estas consignas suele realizarse manualmente, lo que demanda tiempo, experiencia disciplinar y criterios pedagógicos sólidos. title: Virtual Embassies and Digital Consular Services Transforming Traditional Diplomatic Practice
abstract: Diplomacy now moves through websites, cloud servers, and online consular portals. These tools reach citizens abroad quickly, yet the governing treaties were written for physical missions. This study aims to examine whether the Vienna Conventions protect virtual embassies and digital consular services. It also identifies legal changes needed to secure their status. The study follows a qualitative design using doctrinal and document analysis of treaties, policies, and scholarly works. title: The microbiome of draught no- and low-alcohol beer
abstract: The microbiological ecosystem of commercially available draught dispensed no- and low-alcohol beers was evaluated, with a focus on identifying predominant microorganisms with spoilage potential and characterizing variation in community structure. More than 50 samples, representing 20 no- and low- alcohol beers (7 different beer styles: lager, India pale ale, pale ale, wheat, radler, pilsner and amber ale; and 17 brands) were collected for analysis across 12 different public houses (accounts) in Nottingham, UK. title: Digital Knowledge Management of Ancient Literary Scenes
abstract: Aiming at the issues of overemphasis on visual effects and insufficient knowledge transmission in virtual simulation of ancient literary scenes, this study constructs a digital knowledge management framework from the perspective of digital humanities. A three-layer semantic mapping model is proposed to realize the knowledge representation of literary texts, and a VR-based knowledge reproduction system with multimodal perception is developed to achieve digital restoration of ancient literary scenes. title: MAPPING THE INDUSTRIAL LOCATIONS, DATA CENTERS AND IBTEC DEVELOPMENT IN THE JS-SEZ
abstract: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) represents a strategic initiative to strengthen cross-border economic integration between Malaysia and Singapore through industrial development, digital infrastructure, and sustainable urban planning. This study maps and analyses the industrial landscape of the JS-SEZ, focusing on the spatial distribution of industrial parks, data centre infrastructure, and the development of Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) Sedenak. title: Critical review and innovations in excavation practices for soft soil conditions
abstract: Rapid urban development increasingly requires deep excavations near existing structures, where soft soils often induce significant wall and ground movements. Accurate prediction and control of these deformations are essential for safety and serviceability. This study compiles an extensive database of excavation case histories with measured wall and ground responses, and systematically classifies geometry, boundary conditions, support systems, and shoring methods. abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a serious global disease characterized by high blood glucose levels, which can lead to severe complications such as cardiovascular disease, neuropathy, and kidney failure. Current treatment options are associated with significant side effects, prompting the need for developing new, more effective medications with fewer adverse effects. Several studies have explored medicinal plants used in traditional medicine for the treatment of various diseases, particularly in the development of new antidiabetic drugs. abstract: Introduction: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a three-dimensional structural spinal deformity, with well-documented biomechanical consequences but comparatively underexplored psychosocial and functional dimensions. Objectives: To map the extent, range, and nature of recent scientific evidence on the psychological and functional outcomes associated with the Schroth Method in adolescents with AIS. title: Enhancing Direct Air Capture through Potassium Carbonate Doping of Activated Carbons
abstract: Abstract Direct air capture of carbon dioxide (CO2) is one of the most promising strategies to mitigate rising atmospheric CO2 levels. Among various techniques, adsorption using porous materials is a viable method for extracting CO2 from air, even under humid conditions. However, identifying optimal adsorbent materials remains a significant challenge. abstract: Abstract In biotherapeutic manufacturing, product quality such as glycosylation profile is typically assessed only after harvest, limiting opportunities for corrective action during cell culture operation. Intracellular nucleotide sugar donors (NSD) directly determine glycosylation outcomes but are rarely measured, even offline, due to analytical complexity and process disruption. title: A chromosome-level reference genome of the largest cervid species - the European moose ( Alces alces ; Linnaeus, 1758)
abstract: We describe a chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly from a male European moose (Alces alces alces). The assembly comprises two pseudo-haplotypes of 3,148 Mb and 3,112 Mb, with sex chromosomes in haplotype one, and 33 autosomes in each haplotype (68 in total). Assembly completeness is high (BUSCO 98.3% and 95.7%), with 21,496 and 20,498 annotated protein-coding genes for haplotypes one and two, respectively. This genome assembly is the most complete so far generated for European moose.

title: Alignment of Workforce Competencies of Marketing Management Graduates in the Philippines: Evidence for Academia and Industry
abstract: This study examined the alignment of workforce competencies of Bachelor of Science in Business Administration major in Marketing Management graduates of North Eastern Mindanao State University, Philippines, with the competencies used in their current employment. title: Leaf spectroscopy detects site-associated functional differentiation in a dominant mangrove species near its northern range margin
abstract: Functional variation within species may be especially important at range margins, yet conventional trait measurements constrain population-level assessments. Leaf reflectance spectroscopy integrates signals associated with pigments, water, chemistry, and structure, potentially revealing functional differentiation. We analyzed leaf spectra from 48 Kandelia obovata trees across a southern reference population (SRP), a natural range-margin population (NRM), and a long-established planted population north of the historical range margin (PNR). title: Policy Responses of Small and Middle Powers Under Asymmetric Economic Coercion: ASEAN 's Responses to the Trump Administration's Reciprocal Tariffs
abstract: ABSTRACT Existing studies on asymmetric economic competition and coercion have largely portrayed small and middle powers as passive actors that either accommodate or adapt to pressure imposed by major powers. Drawing on the responses of ASEAN member states to the Trump administration's reciprocal tariff policy, this article argues that such a perspective underestimates the strategic agency of smaller states. title: IoT Based Smart Safety Wristband Using BLE Zone Sensing and LoRa Long-Range Alerting for High-Density Public Gatherings
abstract: Large religious and public gatherings, such as the Kumbh Mela, bring together millions of people in a small area for a short period. In these conditions mobile networks become congested, and an individual in distress often cannot be identified or reached in time. This paper presents the design of an IoT Based Smart Safety Wristband that combines two complementary low-power radio technologies. title: Relationship between phytolith morphology and physical and mechanical properties in bamboo Ferrocalamus strictus
abstract: Ferrocalamus strictus is a rare bamboo species native to Yunnan, China, and is notable for its favorable mechanical properties. However, the relationship between phytolith morphology and these properties remains unclear. This study measured nine physical and mechanical traits and 26 phytolith parameters in culms from five provenances aged 1–3 years. title: Resource Nationalism and Indonesia’s Nickel Ore Export Restriction Policy, 2020-2025
abstract: The growing strategic importance of nickel in the global energy transition has increased attention to Indonesia’s mineral governance and its policy of restricting raw nickel ore exports. Indonesia introduced a full restriction on raw nickel ore exports in 2020 within a broader regulatory framework aimed at increasing domestic mineral processing and value addition. This study asks how Indonesia’s nickel ore export restriction policy during 2020-2025 exhibits the localizing and industrializing dimensions of resource nationalism. abstract: La alfabetización digital es un elemento fundamental de la inclusión educativa, social y productiva en entornos rurales donde las malas condiciones de conectividad, la falta de dispositivos y la falta de capacitación pueden afectar el uso efectivo de las tecnologías de la información y la comunicación (TIC). abstract: Introduction Nairobi County has the largest HIV prevention programme for female sex workers (FSW) and men who have sex with men (MSM) in Kenya. Monitoring approaches need to be rapid, affordable, and sufficiently robust to capture programme outcomes while meaningfully involving communities. abstract: Abstract A 15‐year‐old, 1.11‐kg, entire, male river cooter ( Pseudemys concinna ) presented with impaired buoyancy and generalised oedema. abstract: This paper formulates and compares a new fractional-order mathematical model of the transmission dynamics and behavioral development of mobile phone addiction across distinct user subpopulations. The model is developed in the context of fractional derivatives. abstract: Mucosal vaccination is attracting renewed interest because many clinically relevant pathogens first encounter the host at gastrointestinal or respiratory surfaces, whereas most established vaccines are administered parenterally and are optimized primarily to induce systemic immunity. abstract: Hillforts are important cultural landscape elements in the history of Latvian Bronze and Iron Age research. Hillfort research has expanded significantly since the proliferation of LiDAR-derived digital elevation models (DEM). This paper analyses factors influencing hillfort placement using free software and accessible datasets, focussing on 10th to 13th-century CE hillforts in eastern Latvia. abstract: Hydrogen is widely recognized as a promising zero-carbon fuel for internal combustion engines due to its zero carbon emissions, high laminar flame speed, and wide flammability limits. In dual-fuel compression ignition engines, substituting part of the diesel fuel with hydrogen can significantly reduce carbon-based emissions while maintaining or improving ther-mal efficiency. abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. title: Limited efficacy of enrofloxacin against Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs
abstract: Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae is an important respiratory pathogen in sheep that leads to pneumonia and reduced productivity, commonly upon co-infection with other opportunistic microbes. Whether M. ovipneumoniae infection can be successfully treated with antibiotics is unclear. Our pilot study evaluated the efficacy of enrofloxacin (Baytril ® ) for treating experimental M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs. title: The Legal Nature of a Space Operator's Liability for Damages Caused to Third Parties: An Analytical Study in the UAE Legislation
abstract: The space sector has become an attractive economic market both for countries and for private entities. With unprecedented technological advancements, the private sector has become a major player in the space field. The regulation of the space sector has witnessed significant development in recent years in the United Arab Emirates, with the UAE enacting numerous laws and regulations to enhance the legal framework for space activities. abstract: The appropriate selection of machining parameters plays a vital role in enhancing productivity, improving surface finish, and reducing machining costs in drilling operations. The present study focuses on optimizing spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and drill diameter to improve Material Removal Rate (MRR) and minimize surface roughness. abstract: ABSTRACT Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antibacterial activity against N. seriolae and evaluate their protective effects in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). title: A new paracortinid millipede genus from caves in northern Vietnam, with descriptions of two new species (Diplopoda, Callipodida, Paracortinidae)
abstract: A new genus, Vietpetalum gen. nov ., of the family Paracortinidae is here proposed to accommodate three paracortinid species from Vietnam: V. marmoratum sp. nov ., V. simplex sp. nov ., and V. kyrang (Nguyen, Stoev, Nguyen & Vu, 2023), comb. nov . abstract: Microalgae are widely investigated for wastewater treatment, nutrient removal, carbon dioxide sequestration and bioproduct production from side resources, such as industrial by-products, hydrolysates, organic wastes and industrial agriculture wastewater. abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this research case study is to analyse the structure, growth, and functioning of the commercial banking industry in India. It examines the role of commercial banks in financial intermediation, economic development, financial inclusion, credit creation, and the mobilisation of savings. abstract: This article aims to develop a multimodal discourse analysis framework grounded in Indonesian national character values to examine relationships among verbal, visual, and layout elements in English-language disaster texts, focusing on the flash floods and landslides in North Sumatra in late 2025. title: Divine and Human Matters of Ireland: Messianic Allegory in James Joyce's Ulysses
abstract: The present article examines James Joyce’s Ulysses through the entwined lenses of messianic allegory, Benjaminian historical theory, and postcolonial critique. Departing from the conventional understanding of allegory as a system of stable symbolic correspondences, the article proposes a model of ‘messianic allegorical disruption’: a mode of figuration in which the ruins of history accumulate without resolution, salvation is perpetually deferred and meaning is produced not through closure but through interruption. title: Beneficial microbes in plant salt stress tolerance: mechanisms, antioxidant defense, and multi-omics insights
abstract: Salinity stress represents a significant environmental challenge that affects plant growth, resulting in adverse impacts on crop productivity and overall yield. Salt accumulation in plants affects cellular homeostasis and provokes osmotic and ionic imbalance. It stimulates higher reactive oxygen species (ROS) production leading to oxidative stress damage and eventual cellular dysfunction. title: Berlin Walls in our neighborhood: a social justice excursion for community college students in chemistry
abstract: Abstract Social inequalities, pervasive in the modern world, silently shape access to education and educational outcomes, especially in the sciences. Yet, natural science curricula rarely acknowledge these influences, often under the assumption that their commitment to objectivity must imply political and socioeconomic neutrality. This paper presents an educational initiative that addresses this disconnect by integrating elemental analytical chemistry with social justice themes. abstract: Abstract Based on the frame of the traditional inverse finite element method (iFEM) with global continuity, an enhanced IGA-iFEM method for handling the real-time shape sensing of beam structures with multiple stiffeners is proposed in this study. This method compensates for the defect of existing iFEM in engineering applications which segmental monitors displacement and strain in discontinuous structures. title: Live imaging of largemouth bass virus dissemination in zebrafish
abstract: Introduction Understanding how viruses infect and spread within a living host is an attractive yet formidable goal. However, our understanding of these processes relies primarily on in vitro imaging studies conducted in cell culture models. title: Multi-Criteria Environmental Assessment of Protected Areas: Ecosystem Services and Use by Visitors
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are currently the planet's primary tool for conserving biodiversity and sustaining the ecosystem services upon which human well-being depends. Despite this, their environmental valuation remains methodologically fragmented, particularly in Latin America, a region where frameworks capable of integrating ecological, economic, and tourism dimensions are scarce. title: How Fire Moves Carbon in North American Ecosystems Shaped by Fire and Grazing
abstract: ABSTRACT Fire interacts with ecosystem carbon in North American fire-grazing rangelands through processes that span chemical forms, soil depths, and temporal horizons. We synthesize empirical evidence on fire-driven carbon redistribution across the continental region where frequent fire and bison grazing historically co-occurred. Across these rangelands, temperate grasses allocate roughly 75–80% of biomass belowground, outside the combustion zone. abstract: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a non-invasive technique for assessing tissue oxygenation and microvascular function. It may be particularly useful in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), where progressive vascular alterations contribute to disease pathophysiology. However, the relationship between optical markers and underlying histological features remains poorly established. abstract: This article examines the transformation of the European Union’s efforts to promote democracy and human rights in Turkey from the 1999 Helsinki Summit to mid-2025. The study analyzes the instruments implemented by the EU, reform periods, and democratic setbacks, and examines the internal and external factors that shape these processes. title: Hospital mortality and discharge destination prediction after fall-related traumatic brain injury in older adults
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Develop prediction models to support care for older adults with fall-related traumatic brain injury (TBI). SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND: Fall-related TBI is a leading cause of hospitalization and death among older adults. Prognostication remains challenging in this population because frailty and comorbidity burden greatly influence recovery trajectories. abstract: Piled raft foundation systems (PRFS) have been increasingly adopted as an alternative foundation system in developed urban areas underlain by soft soils. In such soils, a double consolidation process may occur as a result of both external loading and subsidence, leading to changes in the soil stress state. abstract: Water ice clouds are an important component of the Martian atmospheric water cycle. This study presents a multiple Martian-year climatology of atmospheric water ice clouds on Mars, from observations by the Planetary Fourier Spectrometer Short Wavelength Channel (PFS/SWC) onboard Mars Express. title: An integral soil quality index based on nematodes for mining-impacted Andean soils
abstract: Mining activities, while economically important, have caused significant soil degradation, affecting soil quality, ecosystem functioning, and sustainability in Andean ecosystems. This study developed an integral soil quality index based on physicochemical, microbiological, and nematode indicators to assess soil degradation in the Ollachea mining area, Peru. abstract: Introduction Chronic child malnutrition (CCM) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in socially vulnerable settings, given its association with adverse developmental outcomes. Preventing CCM requires integrated approaches that combine nutritional support, healthcare, and the strengthening of family caregiving capacities. abstract: Tradisi penanaman kepala kerbau dalam berbagai ritus adat di Indonesia—seperti syukuran laut, pembangunan infrastruktur, dan bersih desa—sering menimbulkan ketegangan teologis ketika berhadapan dengan nilai-nilai monoteisme Islam. abstract: Alpine-cold wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to human disturbance, yet the responses and relationships of soil–plant systems to anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Taking the Napahai alpine-cold wetland in north-western Yunnan as the study area, this research assessed the responses of soil and plant systems to different disturbance types and explored the potential relationships among soil properties, microbial indicators, and vegetation characteristics. abstract: This study evaluates the combined effects of projected climate and land-use/land-cover (LULC) change on streamflow and sediment yield in the Teji Catchment, Ethiopia. The analysis covered historical and future periods from the 1980s to the 2060s, with the 1980s, 2000s, and 2020s representing the historical period. The 2040s and 2060s represent projected scenarios. abstract: This study examines how regional characteristics inﬂuence the development of local Smart Tourism Destinations (STDs) in its territory, highlighting that, beyond city level initiatives, regional contexts play a key role by shaping the enabling conditions for smart transformation. Despite this relevance, the extent to which regional strategies aﬀect the development of local STDs remains largely unexplored in the existing literature, resulting in a gap that this research aims to address. abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Persepsi Kegunaan dan Persepsi Kemudahan Penggunaan terhadap Sikap Penggunaan serta Niat Perilaku dalam menggunakan aplikasi SeaBank pada Generasi Z di Kota Denpasar. title: Exclusive quark and gluon dijet production as probes of GPDs at collider energies
abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

abstract: Urban and regional authorities across Europe must design climate-resilient interventions under constrained budgets, while coordinating more closely with private investors and insurance companies. Participatory governance, multi-criteria decision analysis and climate-investment planning are rarely combined in a single, transparent workflow. abstract: Abstract With the rapid urbanization in China, millions of people have moved from rural regions to cities as migrant workers, where many of them face various discrimination and ill treatment. abstract: Canine malignant mucosal melanoma is one of the common cancers with a high mortality rate. title: The bone-biofilm interface: decoding the bidirectional crosstalk in orthopedic implant infections
abstract: Implant-associated orthopedic infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm persistence is coupled to progressive changes in bone and local immunity. This narrative review presents the Bone-biofilm Interface (BBI) as an integrative framework linking microbial biofilms, implant properties, bone cells, immune cells, and the mineralized matrix. abstract: Abstract The detrimental impacts of dye-containing wastewater discharge on aquatic ecosystems and water quality make it a major environmental concern. abstract: La transformación de los currículos universitarios requiere decisiones sustentadas en evidencia acerca de las necesidades de los estudiantes, los resultados de aprendizaje, la pertinencia social y profesional, y las condiciones institucionales de enseñanza. abstract: Abstract This study characterizes the physicochemical and structural properties of empty fruit bunch (EFB) biomass from two main oil palm cultivars Elaeis guineensis (E.G.) and its interspecific hybrid Elaeis guineensis × Elaeis oleifera (O × G) to assess its suitability for energy and biochemicals production. abstract: Current chemotherapy options for lung cancer (LC) are limited by poor tumor selectivity, systemic toxicity, and acquired resistance. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers a promising minimally invasive modality as a potential conservative or complementary approach, yet its clinical adoption has been constrained by suboptimal photosensitizers and unclear mechanisms. title: On the Maturation of Chinese Characters and the Mechanism behind the Contention of Hundred Schools of Thought
abstract: Academic circles hold diverse views on the causes of the “Contention of a Hundred Schools of Thought.” This paper proposes that the maturity, practical application and diffusion of Chinese characters during the Spring and Autumn Period substantially enhanced administrative governance and economic development, bringing the prefecture-county system to dominance. Populations whose intellectual horizons had long been confined to parochial local contexts, metaphorically “frogs at the bottom of a well,” achieved free circulation of information and talent across the Chinese-character cultural sphere.

abstract: Youth unemployment remains a persistent challenge in South Africa, prompting interventions such as the Presidential Employment Stimulus (PES), which places unemployed graduates in internships designed to build employability. abstract: The Xuhuai Arc Tectonic Belt (XHTB), located along the southeastern margin of the North China Craton (NCC) west of the Tan-Lu Fault Zone (TLFZ), remains poorly understood in terms of its formation mechanisms due to limited constraints on deep crustal architecture. abstract: The evolving demands of physical education in contemporary school contexts require future teachers to be equipped with pedagogical approaches that are responsive, adaptable, and grounded in the realities of dynamic learning environments. Nonlinear pedagogy, underpinned by an ecological dynamic’s rationale, offers a theoretically robust and practically flexible approach to teaching and facilitation of learning in physical education. abstract: Abstract The Mexican highlands, a biodiversity hotspot characterized by complex topography and dynamic paleoenvironments, function as "Sky Islands," isolating temperate-adapted species and promoting in situ diversification. This pattern is exemplified by the Mexican Highland Clade (MHLC) of Thamnophis, a genus exhibiting high ecological and phylogenetic diversity in North America. abstract: Background Climate change is intensifying droughts and floods in Sub-Saharan Africa, threatening livelihoods, food security, and habitability in vulnerable landscapes. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on Indigenous knowledge for drought and flood forecasting in Malawi, focusing on forecasting indicators, relationships with scientific forecasting, and implications for climate adaptation and habitability. title: IMPACT OF DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR IN THE TECH AGE: A STUDY WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO KANDHAMAL DISTRICT OF ODISHA
abstract: Emerging technologies have made digital marketing the most important form of commercial communication in today’s world. It has changed the ways in which consumers gather information, compare choices, and make purchases. This study focuses on the effects of digital marketing on consumers in the Kandhamal district of Odisha. title: Land-use change alters microbial metabolic activity while maintaining functional diversity in tropical peat

abstract: La asistencia técnica agrícola es un instrumento de política pública.
