abstract: This study examined the relationship between metacognitive reading strategy awareness and critical reading self-efficacy among gifted middle school students and investigated the unique contributions of different dimensions of metacognitive reading strategies to critical reading self-efficacy. abstract: Abstract Groundwater recharge estimation is fundamental for the sustainable management of water resources, especially in complex hydrogeological systems comprising granular and fractured aquifers. This study investigates recharge dynamics in two sub-basins through the monitoring of Water Table Fluctuation (WTF) in seven wells: five dug wells (DW) located in the granular aquifer (soil) and two tube wells (TW) in the fractured aquifer. abstract: Epoxy composites are vital for high-performance applications, but their high cost and environmental footprint drive the need for sustainable alternatives. title: Integrating digital financial solutions into MSME business models: assessment of MSME readiness for digital financial integration
abstract: The integration of digital financial solutions has become essential for enhancing the sustainability and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), especially in developing economies. This study examined MSME readiness in terms of digital capability, financial literacy, infrastructure readiness, and strategic orientation in relation to the integration of digital financial systems. abstract: La adquisición continua de variables del suelo mediante dispositivos del Internet de las Cosas (IoT) genera datos cuya utilidad depende de su adecuada gestión, visualización e interpretación. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is now among the foremost threats to global health, and the pipeline of new antibiotics has not kept pace with it. A structural driver of resistance is often overlooked: the dominant “single molecule–single target” paradigm of antibiotic design imposes a well-defined selective pressure that bacteria can escape through a single mutation or acquired gene. abstract: Though military fiction should hold a significant place in literature, contemporary novels about recent wars are often categorised as popular fiction and are not extensively studied in British literature for a reading of trauma narratives. Works produced by veteran authors that draw attention to the psychological state of the soldiers are often sidelined. abstract: Softshell turtles ( Pan-Trionychidae ) have a particularly rich fossil record in North America, but only a few fragmentary remains have previously been reported from the Oligocene. abstract: Postharvest loss of perishable fruits and vegetables is a significant challenge which can be mitigated by processing them into shelf stable products. This study investigated the knowledge, attitude and practices (KAP) on consumption as well as drivers for consumer demand of raw and processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya. title: The effect of urban density on stock returns: evidence from satellite imagery and firms in the United States
abstract: Abstract We study how the urban density of the areas where firms are located impacts their stock returns. Using high-resolution satellite images and image segmentation algorithms, we develop measures of building density for the most populated metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) in the US. We find that firms in urban areas with a higher potential for density increase are perceived as less risky in the stock market because they can feasibly sustain their growth, leading to lower stock returns. This effect is stronger for smaller and younger firms.

Additionally, “ion-trapping” effects give rise to sluggish interfacial lithium-ion transport, further restricting battery performance. Developing composite solid electrolytes that simultaneously resolve these two bottlenecks remains a critical challenge. abstract: BackgroundIntradialytic hypotension (IDH) is a frequent hemodialysis complication associated with symptoms, inadequate fluid removal, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes.Evidence from Sudan is limited, particularly during the health-system disruption caused by the 2023 armed conflict.This study assessed the prevalence, associated factors, clinical manifestations, and management of IDH in two Sudanese dialysis centers. abstract: ABSTRACT Biodegradable films have emerged as sustainable alternatives to conventional plastics for food packaging, but their industrial implementation requires balancing functional performance, processability, structure development and end‐of‐life behavior. The resulting nanomaterial was evaluated as an efficient adsorbent for the removal of Pb 2+ ions from aqueous solutions. abstract: Background Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is a common complication of obstetric neuraxial anesthesia. Epidural blood patch (EBP) is the standard treatment for moderate-to-severe PDPH, but it may be deferred or relatively contraindicated when systemic infection is suspected. Current evidence on alternative treatments for PDPH has mainly focused on single interventions, and reports describing combined therapeutic strategies remain limited. title: Perceived emotional intelligence and individual resilience in a cross-sector sample of employees
abstract: Introduction Emotional resilience is a key psychological resource for maintaining well-being and adaptation in the workplace and is closely associated with perceived emotional intelligence. However, understanding of this relationship among working populations remains limited. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between perceived emotional intelligence and resilience and to explore their associations with sociodemographic and occupational variables. abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to be a major global disease, directly impacting endemic regions and indirectly affecting FMD-free regions. Reliable estimates of key epidemiological parameters, such as transmission rates, from empirical field data are scarce yet essential for developing statistical and mathematical models to assess control strategies and inform policy. abstract: Egg production is a critical economic indicator in the Australian poultry industry, particularly for Ross breeder broilers. This study aims to evaluate and determine the most accurate mathematical model for representing the egg production curve of Ross breeders at Baiada Poultry, South Australia. Data from a 34 week production cycle (week 24 to 57) were analyzed using four polynomial regression models: quadratic, cubic, quartic, and quintic. abstract: ABSTRACT Dry eye represents an increasingly prominent public health burden in modern society. However, the limitations of currently available treatment options have necessitated the pursuit of new therapies. Here we report the repurposing of everolimus (Evero), an mTOR inhibitor with poor aqueous solubility, for dry eye management. Reflective thinking is an essential competency in biology learning. abstract: In this study, the effects of thermal insulation thickness applied to the exterior walls of residential buildings on energy consumption and economic performance were investigated under the climatic conditions of Sakarya Province. title: Actitudes hacia las matemáticas de docentes en formación inicial
abstract: Attitudes toward mathematics are a key component of initial teacher education, as they influence how future teachers value and apply mathematical knowledge in educational settings. The purpose of this study was to analyze the attitudes of pre-service teachers toward mathematics, focusing on the cognitive, behavioral, and affective dimensions. abstract: En la formación inicial docente, la alfabetización académica constituye un proceso fundamental para la apropiación de los discursos y prácticas de lectura y escritura propios del campo educativo. En este contexto, el presente artículo analiza las mediaciones pedagógicas desplegadas por los docentes formadores en los procesos de alfabetización académica. title: Democracia deliberativa
abstract: Esta voz presenta un análisis de la democracia deliberativa. En primer lugar, se expone el origen de la democracia deliberativa como área de estudio y su panorama actual. A partir de aquí se aborda la democracia deliberativa desde la teoría democrática. Se define la democracia deliberativa como un modelo de democracia que prescribe que las decisiones colectivas se tomen mediante un proceso argumentativo de intercambio y ponderación de razones entre ciudadanos libres e iguales. abstract: Although flight frequency is a common indicator in cargo planning, the estimand depends on data and model choices. This study builds a panel that follows 52 airports over 39 quarters from 120 monthly releases published by the General Directorate of State Airports Authority (DHMİ) and examines the within-airport relationship between commercial aircraft movements and cargo tonnage alone. title: Sub-aerial biofilms on urban stone surfaces: community structure and microbial co-occurrence networks
abstract: Sub-aerial biofilms (SABs) play a key role in the biodeterioration of stone cultural heritage, yet their microbial composition may vary depending on the colonized lithic substrate. The aim of this study was to analyze the taxonomic composition of SABs in relation to the type of stone substrate. The material consisted of ten SAB samples, including eight collected from a historic cemetery in Kraków and two from retaining walls within the city. title: Mechanism Research Progress of Acupuncture Regulating Vagus Nerve-Cholinergic Anti-inflammatory Pathway in the Prevention and Treatment of Endometriosis-Related Pain
abstract: Endometriosis (EM)-related pain involves multiple links including local inflammatory microenvironment, neurogenic inflammation, peripheral and central sensitization, and autonomic nervous imbalance. Current hormone therapy and surgical treatment cannot achieve sufficient pain relief and are prone to recurrence. abstract: Residential heating electrification requires reliable operation and economically viable electricity tariffs. This study evaluates the field performance and tariff implications of R32 air-source heat pumps integrated with thermal energy storage (ASHP–TES) in five occupied detached houses on Jeju Island, South Korea. title: Genealogías invisibles. Dibujar las redes de la arquitectura moderna (1923–1966)
abstract: Dibujar una genealogía implica decidir qué relaciones forman parte de la historia que representa. Este artículo parte de esa premisa para reconstruir la arquitectura moderna entre 1923 y 1966 a partir de las relaciones profesionales documentadas entre arquitectos y arquitectas. La investigación utiliza el dibujo como método. Cada conexión que se incorpora permite seguir nuevas trayectorias y observar la posición que estas adquieren dentro de una red común. title: Decentralized authentication in VANETs using blockchain and edge computing
abstract: Vehicular Ad hoc Networks are highly dynamic wireless networks that enable communication between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. They enhance road safety by supporting driver-assistance services and advanced transportation applications, such as automated driving and intelligent transportation systems. title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. title: Nonlinear thermo-viscoelastic characterisation and modelling of adhesively bonded joints in CFRP-strengthened steel
abstract: Adhesively bonded carbon fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) plates are widely used to strengthen ageing steel members, but the long-term performance of such retrofits is governed by the adhesive layer’s thermo-viscoelastic behaviour. This paper presents an experimental–numerical framework for the nonlinear thermo-viscoelastic characterisation of a structural adhesive and for evaluating the effects of sustained loading on the CFRP-strengthened steel beams. title: Effectiveness of Dithane M-45 in Suppressing Fungal Disease Improving The Growth and Yield of Red Bell Pepper (Capsicum Annuum L.)
abstract: Red bell pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) production can be constrained by fungal diseases, making effective disease management important for maintaining plant growth and yield. This study examined the response of red bell pepper to Dithane M-45 under field conditions in Tikala Subdistrict, North Toraja Regency, from July to September 2023. title: Brain-wide activity imaging with electron microscopy reveals a distributed brain network for processing threatening somatosensory stimuli
abstract: SUMMARY To understand how brains work, it is necessary to connect neural activity to synaptic-resolution circuit architecture. Recent advances in light-sheet microscopy (LSM) enable whole-brain, cellular-resolution imaging of activity of all neuronal cell bodies, however, most neurons from such datasets cannot be identified. title: Hegemonic decline and grand strategy: A variegated framework
abstract: Abstract How do hegemons respond to relative decline? The existing literature suggests that declining hegemons either cling to the status quo through preventive war and other expansionist measures or retrench. This article argues that hegemonic decline produces incentives for both forms of action. More specifically, I provide a variegated framework that distinguishes between mild and acute decline as two distinct situations through which declining hegemons may pass. abstract: ABSTRACT Using panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2011 to 2024, this study examines the association between biodiversity risk management (BRM) and trade credit provision (TCP). Our results show that BRM positively impacts corporate TCP. Heterogeneity analyses show that the positive effect is statistically significant among non‐heavily‐polluting firms, high‐tech firms, firms in more competitive markets, and firms facing less stringent environmental regulation. abstract: L’article examine l’innovation locale en l’opposant au modèle schumpétérien, centré sur le marché, qui aborde les territoires uniquement dans le cadre de la compétition mondiale. title: Principal component-based regression models for predicting body weight from morphometric traits in Hararghe Highland sheep, Ethiopia
abstract: In smallholder farming systems across the Ethiopian highlands, weighing scales are rarely available, and farmers rely on visual assessment to estimate sheep body weight (BW) for management. This study evaluated multivariate approaches for predicting BW from morphometric traits in Hararghe Highland ewes, Ethiopia. A cross-sectional survey was conducted on 392 ewes from three districts, recording BW and 16 measurements. title: Interside: Blockchain Interoperability Architecture for Supply Chain Tracking
abstract: Modern supply chains rely on permissioned blockchain networks that frequently operate as isolated entities, resulting in fragmented data, limited visibility, and inconsistent governance. This research addresses these challenges by proposing “Interside,” an interoperability framework designed explicitly for multi-network supply chain ecosystems. Using a design science research methodology, the study includes requirement analysis, framework development, prototype implementation, and a preliminary evaluation. abstract: Phylogenetic analysis of the nucleotide sequences of the cytochrome oxidase I gene of specimens of Albanycada Villet, 1989 supported the hypothesis that the genus includes more than one species-level lineage. abstract: Abstract We present a statistical analysis of the intense earthquake swarm near Santorini, Greece, in 2025. title: The land use challenge in the United Kingdom: Finding space for food production and biodiversity
abstract: The nations of the United Kingdom have set ambitious policy targets for land-based activities and outputs including around food production, climate change and biodiversity. As land area is constrained these targets risk not being met without coordinated policy. Maximising the public and private benefits from the land requires understanding the trade-offs and synergies between different activities, and the comparative advantage of different areas in producing different outputs. abstract: Purpose: The sustainable work that a business undertakes in creating a product or service should be visible to all its audiences, as it is a differentiating factor in today's highly competitive market. In this sense, this study seeks to determine whether sustainable businesses use SEO tools to position themselves in their markets, as well as to identify gaps in opportunities and areas for improvement. title: GIS-based inventory and utility assessment of spring resources in the Kashmir Himalaya
abstract: Introduction Mountain springs are the primary source of drinking water and support the livelihoods of many people in the Indian Himalayan Region. These springs face pressure from human activities, land-use changes, and climate change. Detailed records of springs in the Kashmir Himalaya are scarce, making planning and conservation difficult. abstract: The halal tourism industry has emerged as one of the fastest-growing segments of the global tourism economy, driven by the rising number and expanding purchasing power of Muslim travellers worldwide. Malaysia, consistently ranked among the leading halal tourism destinations, positions small and medium enterprises (SMEs) as the operational backbone of this sector, delivering the food, accommodation, transportation, and retail services that shape the Muslim tourist experience. abstract: Studying day-to-day corruption raises hurdles for qualitative teams that cut across methodological, emotional, and ethical domains. Rather than presenting substantive findings on corruption, this article reports a reflexive analysis of those hurdles as experienced by an eight-member, multidisciplinary research team conducting the qualitative grounded-theory phase of the CIRCLE project in Ecuador - a context where discussing corruption often triggers mistrust, discomfort, and political sensitivities. abstract: Este artículo consolida y actualiza una literatura hasta ahora dispersa sobre optimización de minas a cielo abierto, integrando en un solo marco de referencia más de 90 publicaciones producidas entre 1965 y 2026 —desde el algoritmo de Lerchs-Grossmann hasta los enfoques contemporáneos de planificación integrada—, conectando por primera vez la teoría de grafos, modelos económicos, diseño computacional y la gobernanza ASG en una trayectoria conceptual unificada. abstract: Deteriorating food quality and stress-ridden professional commitments have severely affected the health quality and physical efficacy, making it mandatory to monitor the food quality for cautiously limiting the intake of processed eatables. With exposure to debilitating environmental toxins remaining unabated, regular checkups have emerged as essential for adopting timely cautions. abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional climate risk assessments typically consider hazard, exposure, and vulnerability dimensions, but often restrict exposure to spatial hazard intersections, neglecting the operational intensity of infrastructure. This study proposes a geographic information systems (GIS)‐based framework that uses operational exposure derived from freight and passenger flows as the primary metric for network prioritization. abstract: Introduction Lymphatic filariasis is a major public health burden, particularly in endemic regions, with millions suffering from chronic lymphoedema and hydrocele. While mass drug administration aims to restrict transmission, effective morbidity management remains a significant challenge. Homoeopathy has reported potential in managing lymphoedema, yet evidence in cases of grade III and IV lymphoedema is limited. abstract: Abstract This study explored the oat cultivar PD 2 LV 65 as a native source of dietary fiber (DF) and optimized its extraction using response surface methodology. abstract: En el contexto actual, la programación sigue enseñándose predominantemente bajo un punto de vista imperativo, en el que los programas son concebidos como series de instrucciones ejecutables por computadoras. abstract: Introduction For Cunero cattle, hematological parameters and biochemical biomarkers may serve as potential indicators of pre-slaughter stress, though their functional utility requires further validation. These measurements are essential for evaluating animal welfare when they fall within physiological ranges. Methods Blood samples were collected from the coccygeal vein of 100 Cunero cattle (50 females and 50 males) after they were transported from the Apurimac highlands to the municipal slaughterhouse in Abancay. title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI
abstract: Abstract The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an “immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said.” Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. title: Does the Belt and Road Initiative reduce poverty? Evaluating grain trade openness as an intermediate policy outcome
abstract: Introduction Eradicating poverty remains a core objective of global sustainable development. While the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) provides a novel paradigm for inclusive growth, existing evaluations predominantly focus on macroeconomic aggregates, often overlooking the micro-level transmission mechanisms within the agricultural sector. title: From intestinal barrier sensing to glial immune programming: a barrier–immune–glia relay in microbiota-associated neurodegeneration
abstract: The gut microbiota contributes to host homeostasis through metabolic, immunological, neural, and barrier-related pathways, and its role in the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases has received increasing attention. Patients with Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis often exhibit alterations in gut microbial composition, microbial metabolic function, and peripheral inflammatory phenotypes. title: Creación de un centro educativo tecnológico: impulso para el desarrollo económico y social de la región
abstract: El objetivo del artículo fue analizar los fundamentos y las condiciones de pertinencia para crear un centro universitario tecnológico en Asunción, orientado al desarrollo económico y social regional, con referencia temporal en octubre de 2026. Se elaboró una síntesis documental de alcance descriptivo, analítico y propositivo a partir de una revisión sistemática de literatura especializada y reportes de organismos internacionales. La organización del material siguió cuatro ejes: problemática formativa y productiva, competencias tecnológicas, vinculación institucional y condiciones de inclusión

title: Islet extracellular matrix remodelling in type 2 diabetes: implications for β-cell failure and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterised by progressive insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, ultimately resulting in impaired glucose homeostasis. While metabolic and genetic factors are central to disease development, increasing evidence indicates that disruption of the pancreatic islet extracellular matrix (ECM) may be an important contributor to β-cell failure. journal: Exploration of Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases

title: Sustainable biosorptive recovery of Mn2+ from low grade manganese ore leachate using NaOH activated Artocarpus heterophyllus seed derived biosorbent
abstract: Sustainable recovery of manganese from low-grade ores requires efficient and environmentally compatible approaches for treating ore-derived leachates. This study investigates Mn 2+ recovery from an actual manganese-rich pregnant leach solution (PLS) using NaOH-activated Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam. seed biomass (NaOH – Ah SB), an agro-waste-derived biosorbent. title: Educación de jóvenes y adultos en Ecuador: Equidad educativa, inclusión y desarrollo humano
abstract: La educación de personas jóvenes y adultas con escolaridad inconclusa constituye una dimensión del derecho al aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida y un componente potencial de las políticas de equidad en Ecuador; este artículo examina críticamente su relevancia para la inclusión social y el desarrollo humano, con especial atención a las modalidades de alfabetización, educación general básica y bachillerato; se desarrolló una revisión documental crítica de fuentes normativas, publicaciones institucionales y literatura científica, seleccionadas por su pertinencia temática, trazabilidad y capacidad

abstract: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by examining the role of green innovation as a mediating variable in the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing, drawing upon legitimacy theory and stakeholder theory. title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and in vitro validation reveal the molecular mechanisms of bisphenol A-induced MASLD
abstract: Background Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Methods This study combined network toxicology and molecular docking to explore BPA-induced hepatotoxicity targets and pathways in MASLD. title: Phenological characterization and thermal requirements of prominent cultivars of litchi in the Indo-Gangetic Plain
abstract: Aim: Litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.) exhibits marked phenological variability among cultivars, which influences productivity and climate adaptability. This study aimed to characterize and compare the phenological behavior of ‘Shahi’ and ‘China’ using the extended BBCH (Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt and Chemische Industrie) scale and to examine the influence of thermal indices on phenophase progression. title: Time-dependent pharmacokinetic changes and renal SGLT2 expression alterations of dapagliflozin under high-altitude hypoxia in diabetic rats
abstract: Objective This study investigated the time-dependent effects of high-altitude hypoxia on the pharmacokinetics (PK), renal sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) expression, and glycemic response to dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rats. Methods T2DM was induced in male Wistar rats via high-fat diet and low-dose streptozotocin. In the acute study, rats received a single oral dose of dapagliflozin (1 mg/kg) after a 3-day exposure to normoxia or simulated 6000 m hypoxia. title: Comparative Case Study of Production Efficiency, Financial Performance, and Business Risk in Laying Hen Farms with Different Housing Systems and Management Conditions
abstract: The laying hen sector continues to expand in response to increasing demand for animal protein; however, productivity remains sensitive to environmental conditions, particularly temperature fluctuations that affect production stability. The housing system represents a key management factor influencing farm performance. This study aims to compare production efficiency, financial performance, and business risk between closed-house and open-house laying hen systems. title: Implante en OD 26 Maxilar Superior con Elevación del Seno Mediante Técnica Transcrestal: Caso Clínico
abstract: Introducción: El edentulismo es la pérdida total o parcial de los dientes naturales. Su tratamiento consiste en la colocación de implantes con dos tipos de técnicas de elevación de seno maxilar: abordaje lateral o técnica transcrestal. Actualmente, son pocos los estudios que demuestran los resultados clínicos de la técnica transcrestal. Objetivo: aumentar la altura ósea en maxilar superior atrófico mediante la técnica de elevación de seno maxilar transcrestal para colocación de implante en OD 26, y describir los resultados clínicos de osteointegración y supervivencia del implante. title: Yield and energy efficiency tradeoffs in sweet sorghum under different nitrogen management strategies: Mineral vs. recycled organic fertilization
abstract: Sweet sorghum [ Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] biomass production is a promising component of the bioeconomy that combines high productivity with the potential use of local resources and by-products from bioenergy processes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of nitrogen (N) fertilization strategy and N rate on biomass yield and the energy balance of sweet sorghum grown for energy purposes. title: ECONOMIC VIABILITY ASSESSMENT OF ON-GRID PHOTOVOLTAIC SOLAR POWER PLANTS IN THE NORTH DISTRICT OF THE ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR ISLANDS
abstract: This study investigates the economic viability of on-grid solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in the North District of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands through an integrated techno-economic and econometric framework. The analysis examines 15 grid-connected PV projects, ranging from 50 kW to 2 MW, incorporating project-level observations and technical and financial parameters covering 2015–2025. title: Experimental investigation of microstructural and performance evolution in ultrasonic-assisted stir-cast AA8011–5 wt.% TiB2 composites during multi-pass equal-channel angular pressing
abstract: The development of aluminium matrix composites with improved structural and tribological performance has attracted considerable interest for lightweight engineering applications. This work investigates the microstructural, mechanical, tribological, and hot-deformation response of an AA8011 aluminium composite containing 5 wt.% TiB2, fabricated by ultrasonic-assisted stir casting and subsequently processed by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP). title: Differential DNA methylation profiling of spermatogenesis-associated genes in patients with idiopathic hypospermatogenesis: a hospital-based case-control study
abstract: Hypospermatogenesis is a histopathological subtype of non-obstructive azoospermia and is characterized by a decrease in the total number of germ cells within the seminiferous tubule as a result of spermatogenic failure. Germ cell epigenetic reprograming during development shows that the methylation status of testicular DNA is highly distinct in which hypomethylated foci predominates. A unique testicular DNA methylation pattern needs to be established for various clinical and histopathological subtypes of azoospermia, in order to delineate the epigenetic factors associated with the condition. title: Comparative phytolith profiles of the weed grasses Echinochloa colona and Echinochloa crus-galli (Poaceae): implications for species taxonomy
abstract: Introduction Taxonomic delimitation of closely related Echinochloa species is frequently complicated by morphological plasticity and overlapping vegetative characters, necessitating complementary diagnostic approaches. This study aimed to evaluate whether integrated phytolith characteristics can provide reliable discriminatory features for distinguishing Echinochloa colona and E. crus-galli . abstract: Introduction The recovery of multi-trophic soil communities is pivotal to ecological restoration of reclaimed coal mining areas, yet their succession and the driving mechanisms of soil multifunctionality (SMF) across regional gradients remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated three reclaimed coal mining areas in Shanxi Province, China-Pingshuo (north), Gujiao (central), and Qinshui (south)-using a 25-year chronosequence of Pinus tabuliformis plantations ( n = 75). title: Land use transitions drive ecosystem service supply–demand balance: spatiotemporal assessment and risk zoning in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section)
abstract: Growing human interference with natural ecosystems has positioned land use transition as a dominant force shaping the supply–demand equilibrium of ecosystem services (ESs). Focusing on the ecologically vulnerable Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section), this study examined how land use changes from 2000 to 2020 influenced water yield (WY), carbon storage (CS), food production (FP), and soil retention (SR). title: Chatbots municipales y vacío normativo en la Administración Pública argentina
abstract: En los últimos años, distintos municipios argentinos han incorporado chatbots y asistentes virtuales como canal de atención ciudadana y de acceso a trámites de asistencia social, siguiendo el modelo pionero de Boti, del Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Este artículo analiza dicho fenómeno desde la perspectiva del derecho administrativo y de los estándares internacionales de derechos económicos, sociales, culturales y ambientales (DESCA), a partir de un relevamiento de seis casos municipales (Tigre, San Isidro, Vicente López, Quilmes, Lanús y Zárate) y del caso testigo de Boti (CABA). title: “We are just blind there”: institutional invisibility of female genital schistosomiasis in South Africa
abstract: Introduction Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS) remains severely overlooked within neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), disproportionately affecting women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Despite its high prevalence and association with adverse reproductive health outcomes and increased HIV susceptibility, FGS receives minimal attention in research, policy, and clinical practice. Understanding how FGS is or isn’t prioritised within policy implementation is critical for addressing this gap. title: Tumor location in the pancreatic body/tail as an independent risk factor for early recurrence after curative resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Early recurrence after radical resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a primary cause of poor prognosis. Published definitions of early recurrence use postoperative cutoff points ranging from 6 to 12 months. This study aimed to analyze perioperative clinicopathological features associated with early recurrence after PDAC surgery, with particular focus on the impact of tumor location, to facilitate individualized treatment decisions. title: Sustained Higher Education Expansion and Firms' Productivity: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between China's sustained higher education expansion and the productivity of A‐share listed firms from 2004 to 2020. We find that a larger supply of university graduates is associated with significantly higher firm total factor productivity (TFP) on average, a result robust to extensive testing. Mechanism analysis points to three plausible channels: an increased share of skilled labor, strengthened innovation, and accelerated digital transformation. However, the relationship is asymmetric. title: A tuneable multicomponent bioink platform for modelling liquid tumor microenvironment
abstract: The human extracellular matrix (ECM) is a key regulator of tumor progression, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, making its accurate reproduction essential for the development of physiologically relevant in vitro cancer models. Among advanced biofabrication technologies, extrusion-based bioprinting enables the fabrication of reproducible three-dimensional (3D) tumor models with controlled structural and mechanical properties. title: Beyond antimicrobials: multifunctional biomaterials for tissue regeneration
abstract: Biomaterial-associated infections remain a major obstacle in regenerative medicine, wound healing, and implantology. While conventional anti-infective materials have mainly focused on preventing bacterial adhesion or delivering antimicrobial agents, infection control alone is often not enough to restore tissue function. title: Morphological, Palynological and Micromorphological Investigations on Unusual Tanacetum nivale Sch.Bip. (Asteraceae)
abstract: The genus Tanacetum L., is one of the cosmopolitan members of the tribe Anthemideae (Asteraceae), encompassing approximately 160 species. Within Türkiye, 61 taxa are recorded, 27 of which are endemic. This research investigates Tanacetum nivale Sch.Bip. using LM and SEM to assess its morphological, pollen, and achene traits, providing additional characters that may assist in resolving systematic issues within the genus. abstract: This mini review examines the potential roles of proton signaling in the peripheral and central nervous systems and its proposed regulation by keratan sulfate (KS). Protons are central to bioenergetics and rapid chemical signaling, linking metabolism to membrane excitability and receptor activity across tissues. Nanoscale-to-microscale pH transients may add a further layer of intercellular communication in the nervous system through proton-sensitive ion channels and receptors. abstract: Contexto: La enfermedad hepática esteató-sica asociada a disfunción metabólica (MASLD) afecta a más de un tercio de la población adulta global, y su espectro abarca desde la esteatosis simple hasta la esteatohepatitis, la fibrosis y el carcinoma hepatocelular. La biopsia hepática, que sigue siendo el estándar diagnóstico, es invasiva, presenta error de muestreo y no resulta adecuada para el cribado poblacional. title: Traditional Medicine Use and Pharmacist Involvement Among Patients with Diabetes and Hypertension in Semarang, Indonesia: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Patients with diabetes or hypertension often take traditional medicine alongside prescribed drugs, yet little is known about how they involve pharmacists in that use. This descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 110 adult users of traditional medicine, recruited by purposive sampling at a community health centre and a private clinic in Semarang, Indonesia, and surveyed them with a structured questionnaire. abstract: Esta contribución enfoca el uso de una metodología mixta, en concreto la combinación de experimentos lingüísticos y entrevistas metalingüísticas. En primer lugar, se ofrecerá una discusión contrastiva de ambos métodos, resaltando ventajas y desventajas, y debatiendo cómo la combinación permite aprovechar las primeras y mitigar las segundas. Se argumentará a favor de métodos mixtos, ya que permiten contextualizar los datos, aumentar la fiabilidad de las conclusiones y, últimamente, llegar a una imagen más completa del fenómeno estudiado. title: Natural products and extracellular vesicle-associated miRNA networks in perianal infectious wound healing: a critical ethnopharmacological appraisal
abstract: Perianal infectious wounds form a contaminated, moist, mechanically disturbed repair niche that differs from standard cutaneous wounds. This critical narrative review evaluates whether natural-product pharmacology and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated miRNA biology can be linked credibly in this setting. A structured PubMed search updated through 29 September 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar citation tracking, identified direct human perianal studies, anatomically relevant and infection-relevant animal studies, and mechanistically relevant in vitro and in silico evidence. title: A comparative legal analysis of migratory bird conservation along the African–Eurasian flyway
abstract: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African-Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. title: Exploring the relationship between cultural landscapes and psychological well-being through indigenous environmental design in rural China
abstract: Introduction Indigenous environmental design in rural China is increasingly affected by modernization, tourism development, and ecological change. However, empirical evidence concerning the relationship between cultural landscape fidelity and residents’ psychological well-being remains limited. title: El papel de las inversiones europeas: aprendizajes nacionales
abstract: Las inversiones de la Unión Europea han desempeñado un papel decisivo en la modernización económica de España desde su adhesión, pero su contribución efectiva a la convergencia territorial, la transformación productiva y el crecimiento potencial sigue siendo objeto de debate. Este artículo ofrece un análisis institucional y empírico de la trayectoria de las inversiones europeas en España, comparando la lógica redistributiva de la política de cohesión con el enfoque estratégico y condicionado del Mecanismo de Recuperación y Resiliencia (MRR). abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance and sustainable catalytic systems for reduction of nitroaromatics remains an important objective in both environmental remediation and synthetic chemistry. We report herein a CoFe 2 O 4 @GO catalytic system synthesized using co‐precipitation method as a magnetically recoverable heterogeneous catalytic system for the selective reduction of nitroarenes into corresponding amines using sodium borohydride and hydrazine hydrate as reducing agents. title: Evaluation of dragon fruit (Hylocereus spp.) cultivated in the medium lowland agroecosystems based on yield traits and biochemical contents
abstract: Fruit crops are highly susceptible to climate change and global warming, posing a significant threat to fruit production. Recognizing dragon fruit as a potential candidate for climate-smart horticulture, this study assessed its adaptability to medium-lowland agroecosystems based on morphological, yield, and biochemical performance. abstract: ABSTRACT This work reports a novel strategy for fabricating stable and highly efficient shortwave infrared (SWIR) light emitters by incorporating lead sulfide (PbS) quantum dots (QDs) into a cesium lead bromide (CsPbBr 3 ) nanocrystal (NC) matrix. The CsPbBr 3 matrix effectively reduces surface trap states of PbS QDs and significantly enhances their quantum yield. title: A new species of alpine grasshopper of the genus Podismopsis Zubovski, 1900 (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Gomphocerinae) from Central Europe
abstract: Podismopsis kristini sp. nov . (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Gomphocerinae) is described from the Tatras in Slovakia, representing the seventh European species of the genus Podismopsis Zubovski, 1900, and the first record of the genus from the Western Carpathians. The new species inhabits cold, wind-exposed alpine grasslands at 1,820–1,920 m a.s.l. in the upper part of the Žiar Valley in the Western Tatras and is known only from the type locality. title: Beyond electricity generation: Nuclear power plants as circular chemical manufacturing hubs for plastic waste valorization
abstract: Abstract Large nuclear power plants have traditionally been regarded as facilities dedicated to electricity generation. This study proposes a systems‐level concept in which they function as circular chemical manufacturing hubs integrating plastic waste valorization, hydrogen production, carbon utilization, and downstream polymer synthesis within a unified industrial complex. abstract: Objectives CBT101 is a creatine prodrug under development for disorders driven by impaired neuronal energy homeostasis, with initial development focused on creatine transporter deficiency and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. This first-in-human study aimed to assess the safety and tolerability of single and repeated ascending intranasal doses of CBT101 in healthy male volunteers and explored neurophysiological evidence of central pharmacodynamic activity using quantitative EEG (qEEG) and event-related potentials (ERPs). title: Unexpected fault reactivation during underground gas storage in depleted reservoirs: defining operational pressure bandwidths
abstract: Introduction Underground gas storage and emerging subsurface storage applications for CO 2 , H 2 , and N 2 increasingly rely on depleted, faulted reservoirs. In such settings, pressure recovery and cyclic operations may bring faults close to reactivation even when reservoir pressure remains below the initial value and within the range previously experienced during primary production. title: Evaluation of health and economic impacts of atmospheric PM₂.₅ in Tabriz, Iran, using BenMAP-CE and AirQ+
abstract: Air pollution poses a major threat to public health and carries the highest burden of environmentally related diseases. This study evaluated mortality associated with long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ and the corresponding economic burden in Tabriz city. The analysis was conducted using the BenMAP-CE and AirQ⁺ software. We evaluated five scenarios concerning the annual average PM₂.₅ concentration: increases to 35 and 25 µg/m³, decreases to 15 and 10 µg/m³, and a reduction to the theoretical minimum risk level of 2.4 µg/m³. title: Quantitative risk assessment of BSE transmission if insects are reared on residual streams containing animal proteins
abstract: Insect production can play an important role in the bioconversion of residual streams from agri-food production into valuable nutrients for feed and food and as such advance the transition from a linear to a circular food production system. However, under current EU legislation, insect rearing on residual streams containing animal proteins is not allowed because of the risk of animal disease transmission including bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE). title: Mapping the Spatial Dynamics of Drinking Water Quality in Ghaziabad, India
abstract: Urbanization at a rapid pace is estimated to contribute about 1.5 billion people to urban areas by 2030, leading to increasing concerns regarding the provision of safe water and sanitation facilities and changes in land-use patterns and land-cover. In India, urbanization is mainly city-centric and results from migrations from the rural hinterland, with an increase in urban growth of about 250% over the last two decades. title: If you think twice, you might not forget: inhibition and memory-maintenance trade-offs in Russian single vs. Hausa bipartite negation
abstract: Several approaches have attempted to explain the skewed distribution across languages and regions of bipartite compared to single negation, the latter unequivocally the most common, but still often subject to diachronic change. It is a paradox that double negation arises, among other things, to strengthen negation semantically or define its scope, while at the same time, this fortification may lead to its demise. Several grammaticalization pathways result in double, discontinuous negation typologies negating single events or constituents, but such constructions seem to be inherently unstable.

abstract: Sludge drying is the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting stage in the sludge treatment and disposal process. The thermal drying technologies currently employed generally exhibit high energy consumption, which increases the overall cost and energy demand of sludge management. title: Can integrated legal and administrative governance reduce corporate carbon emissions?
abstract: Traditional environmental governance often relies on a single regulatory form, necessitating the exploration of more comprehensive integrated governance models. Utilizing the pilot program of procuratorial public interest litigation in China as a quasi-natural experiment, this study investigates the impact of integrated legal and administrative governance on corporate carbon emissions and the underlying mechanisms. abstract: The rapid expansion of the global halal industry has created opportunities for halal ecosystem development in non-Muslim societies. In South Korea, however, halal industry growth faces challenges related to limited infrastructure, fragmented certification systems, and social stigma toward Islam and halal practices. abstract: The spongy moth, Lymantria dispar , provides a compelling example of how advances in genomic methods can reshape the practical interpretation of intraspecific taxonomy. abstract: Patent enforcement is a critical element in ensuring legal certainty, enhancing innovation, and strengthening a technology-based investment climate. However, patent enforcement practices in Indonesia continue to face significant structural and institutional challenges. abstract: To investigate the potential use of Ginsenoside Rg1 as an adjuvant for the H9N2 avian influenza vaccine, the study examined Rg1’s immunomodulatory effects on an inactivated H9N2 vaccine. abstract: ABSTRACT Precision fermentation has emerged as one of the most transformative approaches in contemporary food biotechnology, enabling the targeted production of high‐value food ingredients through engineered microorganisms. abstract: Despite growing interest in virtual reality (VR) in heritage tourism contexts, empirical evidence on its value beyond single-use applications across the customer journey remains limited. abstract: Wheat productivity is threatened by terminal heat stress, which hampers yields 6-10% per 1 °C above optimal temperatures during grain filling. abstract: In the context of a full-scale war, the relevance of research into women’s loneliness takes on a new significance, shaped by profound personal and psychological changes within society, the consequences of which have implications for both the resilience of the social environment and Ukraine’s overall safety. abstract: Proximity-based urban planning is often presented as a means of promoting urban equity, yet concerns persist that accessibility improvements may reinforce socio-spatial inequalities and gentrification. abstract: Over the past two decades, social networking services have become a pervasive and integral part of young adults’ lives. abstract: ABSTRACT Sleep is an essential yet costly biological process, leaving animals vulnerable to predation and constraining their use of space and time. title: Perceptions of police legitimacy and its influencing factors: evidence from Guangzhou, China
abstract: Introduction Understanding the foundations of public trust in law enforcement is critical for effective governance, particularly in non-Western contexts. While procedural justice theory has received growing empirical attention in China, existing studies have produced mixed findings and largely neglected the combined influence of interactional experiences, neighborhood environmental conditions, and institutionally embedded factors on police legitimacy perceptions. title: Could local climate, forest site and stand conditions mitigate the defoliation in European beech stands? – The case of southern Belgium
abstract: Although climate change has been a major factor in the declining health of European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) stands since the end of the 20th century, it seems that local site and stand conditions may play a key role within the beech’s climax region by exacerbating or mitigating this phenomenon. In this study, we assessed crown defoliation in 1,515 dominant trees distributed across 101 mature beech stands, located along bioclimatic and ecological gradients in the Ardenne region (southern Belgium) during July and August 2022. title: Microbial enhancement of crop abiotic stress tolerance: mechanisms and applications
abstract: Crops aimed at nourishing an exponentially increasing population are frequently vulnerable to a diversity of adverse ecological conditions. Due to climate change, extreme events including flooding, droughts, heat, and frost are expected to further upsurge in the future. To cope with such effects, a wide range of mitigation and adaptation approaches are needed. Even though plants have been engineered to endure stressful conditions, and some have also developed ways of regulating their metabolism, there is still a scarcity of food supply. title: Multi-criteria decision analysis and spatial optimization of sports facilities using GIS and AHP: a case study of ramadi district, Iraq
abstract: Abstract Ramadi District, the capital of Al-Anbar Governorate in western Iraq, faces a severe shortage and unbalanced distribution of sports facilities—a challenge common to many post-conflict and rapidly urbanizing cities in developing countries. This study aimed to analyze the spatial distribution of existing sports facilities and identify optimal locations for new ones using an integrated GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making approach. title: Recent advances in chiral organic room‐temperature phosphorescence with circularly polarized luminescence
abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized room‐temperature phosphorescence (CPRTP) materials combine the dual advantages of long‐lived triplet emission and chiral optical response, demonstrating broad application prospects in information security, bioimaging, and flexible optoelectronics. This review outlines recent progress in organic CPRTP materials from molecular chiral design, aggregation modulation, performance tuning and application scenarios. title: Parametric Insurance in Arid Regions: International Experience and Prospects for Implementation in Uzbekistan
abstract: Climate change, increasing drought frequency and duration, water scarcity and high dependence of agricultural production on irrigation are fundamentally transforming agricultural risk profiles in arid and semi-arid economies. Traditional indemnity-based agricultural insurance, which requires individual loss assessment, is associated with high transaction costs, delayed claims settlement and limited accessibility for smallholder farmers. title: Life Cycle Assessment of Solid Oxide Fuel Cell System for Sustainable Power Generation: A Review
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising technologies for sustainable power generation, offering high electrical efficiency, fuel flexibility and minimal pollutant emissions. Environmental performance of SOFC systems is influenced by operational efficiency, upstream fuel generation, manufacturing, system integration, and end‐of‐life management. This review critically synthesizes the latest life cycle assessment studies of the stand‐alone and hybrid SOFC systems based on the ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 standards. title: Graphene-Derived Nanomaterials for Wastewater Treatment: Bridging Laboratory Performance and Practical Feasibility
abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to remove trace contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, heavy metals, and emerging organic compounds. title: Eco-Friendly and Sustainable Production of Bifunctional Carbon Quantum Dots from Pine Cones: Utilizing Dual Fractions and Exploring Polarity-Dependent Electrochemical Properties for Energy Storage Applications
abstract: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have gained recognition as promising nanomaterials for energy storage applications, owing to their distinctive attributes including high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, superior electrical conductivity, and cost-effective production from renewable sources. title: Urban green space accessibility inequality: spatial and intergenerational disparities
abstract: Urban green spaces provide multiple benefits to human beings; however, green space distribution is rarely equal in most cities. Although green space equity has been assessed in cities worldwide, spatio-temporal analyses and cross-age comparisons on this topic are scarce. To address this knowledge gap, this study utilised bivariate local spatial autocorrelation (BiLISA) to analyse spatial clustering patterns of the Gini coefficient from 2014 to 2019 and to compare inequality levels among young, working-age, and elderly populations in the Taipei metropolis, Taiwan. title: A predictive multi-agent learning framework for energy-constrained ultra-reliable edge systems under stochastic environments
abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency systems operating at the network edge are increasingly constrained by stochastic environmental factors, including energy variability, dynamic workloads, and time-varying communication conditions. Existing learning-based resource management approaches predominantly rely on reactive decision-making and assume stable energy availability, limiting their applicability in energy-harvesting edge systems where uncertainty is intrinsic and future conditions critically influence system reliability. title: Construction of composite hydrophobic coating with insulation and anti-corrosion functions using non-isocyanate polyurethane and silica aerogel
abstract: Thermal insulation and anticorrosion coatings play a critical role in safeguarding industrial equipment and infrastructure. Consequently, the development of high performance, environmentally benign hydrophobic coatings has emerged as a key research priority. Conventional polyurethane coatings rely on toxic isocyanates and petroleum-derived feedstocks, raising significant environmental and occupational health concerns. title: Motor shot noise explains active fluctuations in a single cilium
abstract: Mesoscopic fluctuations reveal stochastic dynamics of molecules in both inanimate and living matter. We investigate how small-number fluctuations shape the collective dynamics of molecular motors using motile cilia as model system. abstract: This article interrogates the Chinese state’s pursuit of ontological security (OS) through the Sinicisation of history, conceptualised as narrative self-grasping. Drawing on Buddhist philosophy and ontological security theory, it argues that China’s quest to achieve existential stability by constructing a coherent, teleological national self – the Zhonghua minzu – paradoxically generates deeper existential insecurity. title: Advancing sustainable competitiveness in freight transport: An integrated framework with system thinking approach
abstract: Freight transport is central to economic vitality, yet a major source of congestion, emissions, and social externalities. Accordingly, the sustainability of freight transport systems is increasingly recognized as a vital element in global efforts to address climate change and improve urban livability. Building on a structured gap analysis, this paper advances the Integrated Freight Transport System Model (IFTSM) for Sustainability Competitiveness by (1) Embedding Reliability, Efficiency, and Attractiveness dimensions, (2) incorporating the Systems Thinking Approach by developing the Causal Loo

title: Unpacking Modern Slavery in Business Research: Conceptualization and Operationalization
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the tragic humanitarian impact of modern slavery, modern slavery research is underdeveloped and advancing slowly. Theoretical studies abound, while there are few quantitative studies with large‐scale empirical evidence to test theory. We review the literature to better understand how modern slavery has been defined and measured. We find a wide discrepancy among conceptual definitions of modern slavery. Only a few studies operationalize (measure) modern slavery. To aid conceptual clarity, we develop a tentative business‐related definition of modern slavery based on our review.

title: Healthcare Professionals’ Experiences of Delivering Fertility Care to Pacific Peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand experience high infertility rates yet low use of assisted reproductive technology services. This qualitative study explored healthcare professionals’ experiences of delivering fertility care to Pacific patients. Using talanoa interviews and interpretative phenomenological analysis informed by Pacific holistic health perspectives, 11 healthcare professionals participated. title: When wildlife damage threatens livelihoods: why national park residents consider a transition to tourism
abstract: Wildlife damage is often expected to push national park residents toward new sources of income, but the appraisals that turn damage into a willingness to move into tourism remain unclear. Drawing on protection motivation theory and questionnaire data from 513 residents in and around the Wuyishan City section of Wuyishan National Park, China, this study distinguishes perceived tourism adaptive efficacy from tourism self-efficacy and examines how these two beliefs relate to intentions to shift household livelihoods toward tourism. title: Adsorption of lead ions from aqueous solutions using magnetite nanoparticles: factorial optimization and isotherm analysis
abstract: Introduction The presence of lead ions in water bodies represents a persistent environmental problem due to their toxicity, mobility, and bioaccumulation capacity, which demands the development of efficient and sustainable treatment alternatives. In this context, the present study aimed to evaluate the adsorption of lead ions in aqueous solutions using magnetite nanoparticles through factorial optimization of operating conditions and isotherm analysis. title: Audiovisual patterns of emotional advertising and physiological engagement: a marketing science perspective on sport storytelling
abstract: Introduction Sport advertising increasingly relies on emotional storytelling, yet the Marketing Science literature lacks systematic, second-by-second evidence on which audiovisual patterns modulate viewers' physiological arousal in real commercials. Methodology This study maps the audiovisual grammar of sport advertising through a secondary analysis of 750 seconds of group-level electrodermal activity (EDA) synchronized with content coding of 22 nationally aired Spanish sport advertisements (2023-2025), viewed by 30 participants. abstract: Recurrence remains common in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (eCRSwNP) despite surgery and type 2-directed therapy, suggesting that epithelial injury mechanisms beyond cytokine signaling remain incompletely defined. abstract: Abstract Salinity is a major abiotic stressor limiting crop production globally. Unlike obligate halophytes, facultative halophytes adapt to saline environments by enhancing their secondary metabolism, particularly under moderate salinity, offering great potential for Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. abstract: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. abstract: Soil salinization threatens global agricultural sustainability and may elevate soil-borne disease risk through coordinated changes in soil conditions and the rhizosphere microbiome, yet long-term field evidence remains limited. abstract: The rise in the deployment of low Earth orbit satellite constellations has reshaped the space utilization landscape, driving unprecedented demand for multi-satellite launches. This trend arises from the growing need for low-latency global connectivity, high resolution observation and more accurate navigation services. abstract: Rain-on-snow (ROS) events are widely recognized as an important cryosphere–hydrology coupling mechanism, yet when and where ROS events translate into river floods remains poorly constrained, particularly in arid high-mountain regions. Here, we provide the first basin-scale assessment of potential flood-inducing ROS (ROS-PF) and actual river-flood-generating ROS (ROS-AF) events across the Tianshan Mountains. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is particularly difficult to manage in immunocompromised hosts, in whom impaired bacterial containment and clearance can coexist with restricted treatment options, altered drug exposure, and anatomically complex infection sites. Susceptibility testing and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) assessment guide antibiotic treatment, while host defenses help determine whether injured bacteria are cleared. abstract: Electro-chemo-mechanical coupling is well established in electric-vehicle batteries, yet its translation from electrode behavior to pack- and vehicle-level performance remains difficult. abstract: Airborne laser scanning (ALS) provides spatially explicit measurements of forest height change that can support the development of climate-sensitive growth and yield models. abstract: This study investigates the role of leadership and policy in sustaining literacy excellence among elementary schools in Benguet Province, Philippines. abstract: This study examines the effects of climate variability on international net migration to Türkiye over the period 1970–2024, incorporating temperature anomalies (1991–2020 baseline) and drought–wetness conditions derived from the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). abstract: Este artículo propone un marco metodológico para el modelado del triple impacto mediante la convergencia analítica de estados financieros tradicionales y reportes de sustentabilidad. journal: Revista de Investigación en Modelos Financieros

abstract: Exposure to environmental stressors such as heat and air pollution is rising in urban areas, placing soft mobility users (e.g., pedestrians, cyclists, and scooter riders) at particular risk—a challenge that will only intensify with climate change. abstract: Non-English dialogue datasets are scarce, and models are often trained or evaluated on translations of English-language dialogues, an approach which can introduce artifacts that reduce their naturalness and cultural appropriateness. abstract: The synthesis of high-purity lepidocrocite-type titanate nanotubes from natural ilmenite minerals remains challenging due to the presence of iron impurities and the limited understanding of their structural stability during thermal treatment. abstract: ABSTRACT Nanotechnology has evolved from empirical traditional material practices to a highly advanced field based on the controlled design and manipulation of matter at the nanoscale. This article aims to provide a critical narrative overview of the evolution of the field of nanotechnology from traditional empirical approaches to modern scientific approaches. abstract: Abstract Urban heat stress poses an increasingly critical challenge in the context of climate change and rapid urbanization, prompting the adoption of Green-Blue Infrastructure (GBI) as a key mitigation strategy. abstract: Introduction To improve health for all demographics in our society, we need a diverse biomedical research workforce in which those affected by health disparities are in positions of power to prioritize and solve preventable differences in health outcomes across various populations. abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon carbide (SiC) and its composite variants are gaining significant traction in the semiconductor and aerospace sectors, owing to their outstanding mechanical strength, large bandgap, excellent thermal resilience, and strong resistance to radiation. title: The Role of the South Korean Saemaul Foundation in Developing a Sustainable Oyster Mushroom Program in Bleberan Village, Special Region of Yogyakarta
abstract: Background: The Saemaul Undong program, developed by the South Korean Saemaul Foundation in Bleberan Village, Yogyakarta Special Region, is designed to promote community self-reliance through the development of oyster mushroom cultivation. This program is implemented in a community that still faces limitations in business diversification, low agricultural productivity, vulnerability to climate change, and limited institutional and technological capacity. Objective: This study aims to analyze the role of the Saemaul Foundation in developing sustainable oyster mushroom cultivation and to identif

title: Non-volant small mammals recorded from Tyto furcata pellets in a human-modified landscape of Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais, Brazil, with an updated regional checklist
abstract: Owl pellets provide a valuable, non-invasive tool for documenting small mammal assemblages, particularly in areas lacking systematic faunal surveys. We used pellets of the American Barn Owl (Tyto furcata), collected during three sampling events (2022–2024), to document the non-volant small mammal fauna of a human-modified rural landscape in São Pedro dos Ferros, Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais, Brazil, the first faunal record for this municipality. We identified 14 species, including two exotic rodents (Rattus sp. and Mus musculus), with a predominance of generalist taxa such as Calomys cf. cerquei

title: Community differentiation and assembly of soil nosZ-type denitrifiers across dominant plant communities in an alpine wetland of Qinghai Lake
abstract: Background Nitrous oxide (N₂O) reduction mediated by nosZ -harboring microorganisms represents the terminal step of denitrification and an important biological sink for N₂O in wetland soils, yet how naturally occurring dominant plant communities are associated with the diversity, taxonomic differentiation, and assembly of nosZ -type communities in alpine wetlands remains poorly understood. title: Legionella Risk Management in Building Water Systems: Current Perspectives from Industry Practitioners
abstract: Building water systems are internationally recognised reservoirs for opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens, including Legionella, the causative agent of Legionnaires’ disease. Inadequate design, operation and maintenance can promote Legionella proliferation and expose building occupants to potentially fatal infection. Effective management is therefore critical; however, there is limited international evidence regarding how guidelines for controlling Legionella risk are implemented in practice. Despite extensive Australian guidance, little is known about the practical management of Legionell

title: A Review of Barriers to Flood-Resilient Retrofitting in Residential Properties
abstract: Riverine flooding poses a significant risk to residential properties worldwide, with climate change exacerbating its frequency and intensity. Although flood-resilient retrofitting (FRR) is increasingly recognized as a mitigation measure for reducing flood damage, its implementation remains low. While existing research has identified numerous FRR implementation barriers, these are often fragmented and lack theoretical integration. This study fills this gap through a theory-driven systematic review of 58 studies, selected from 2,762 articles. A total of 22 barriers were identified and grouped in

title: The Motivation for Cognitive Activities Questionnaire: scale development and validation in French and English
abstract: The current research aimed to develop and validate a novel measurement scale, the Motivation for Cognitive Activities Questionnaire (MCAQ), specifically designed to assess individuals’ motivation to engage in everyday cognitive activities. The MCAQ’s development was informed by expectancy-value theory and self-determination theory. Four studies were conducted to validate the MCAQ in both English and French languages. Through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, a 32-item scale emerged, encompassing four subscales: perceived capacity, intrinsic motivation, identified motivation, and ex
institutions: Laboratoire Inter-universitaire de Psychologie: Personnalité, Cognition, Changement Social

title: Beyond Protein Synthesis: The Multifunctional Role of Functional Amino Acids in Modulating Meat Quality in Ruminants
abstract: ABSTRACT Meat quality is a critical economic trait in ruminant production because it directly influences consumer acceptability, market value, and the long‐term sustainability of the livestock industry. Amino acids (AAs) have traditionally been regarded primarily as substrates for protein synthesis. However, growing evidence indicates that they also regulate multiple aspects of meat quality. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Type III secretion effectors of Xanthomonas oryzae: molecular functions, evolutionary dynamics and implications for rice resistance breeding
abstract: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae ( Xoo ) and X. oryzae pv. oryzicola ( Xoc ) are major bacterial pathogens of rice that cause bacterial blight and bacterial leaf streak, respectively. Successful infection by these pathogens depends largely on a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which delivers diverse type III secretion effectors (T3SEs) into rice cells to manipulate host transcription, immunity, metabolism, and cellular processes. T3SEs in X. oryzae comprise transcription activator-like effectors (TALEs) and a structurally and functionally diverse group of non-TALE effectors, commonly

title: Impacts of shrub coverage for arctic ecosystem carbon uptake and storage
abstract: Abstract. Although shrubs employ distinct water- and carbon-use strategies compared to trees and are increasingly expanding across warming tundra and grassland, they remain insufficiently represented in global land surface models. Here, we incorporated two shrub types, deciduous and evergreen, into the nutrient-enabled terrestrial biosphere model QUINCY, which features a state-of-the-art treatment of soil nutrient dynamics and carbon exchange. We investigate the change in carbon fluxes and storage due to shrub cover, it's response to climate and CO2 fertilization effect and the role of nitroge

title: Fire and Carbon Dynamics: A Global Review of Knowledge and Gaps Across Biomes
abstract: Abstract Purpose of review Fire is a major driver of terrestrial carbon (C) cycling, rapidly releasing carbon accumulated over decades to millennia and reshaping ecosystem structure and function across biomes. As climate change intensifies fire regimes, understanding fire-induced changes in C stocks and fluxes is increasingly urgent. To address this need, we reviewed fire–C studies published over the past fifteen years, focusing on the geographic and biome distribution of existing research, the effects of prescribed burns and wildfires on C pools and fluxes, and methods used to quantify post-f
institutions: Forest Science and Technology Centre of Catalonia

title: Polymeric nanocomposites for eco-friendly and industrial applications: a comprehensive review
abstract: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial area per unit volume scales inversely with the smallest filler dimension, a few volumes per cent of well-dispersed nanofiller can alter the mechanical, electrical, optical, magnetic and gas-barrier properties of the host polymer, at loadings substantially lower than those required with conventional micro-scale fillers. title: Drought modulates soil hydraulic, biological, and physicochemical responses to one-off tillage in a long-term cover-cropped Mediterranean vineyard
abstract: Sustainable soil management is a crucial factor to maintain soil health and long-term functionality in vineyards. In Mediterranean climates, cover crops have become a sustainable alternative to conventional tillage due to their positive effects on soil structure, water retention, and biological activity. Severe drought episodes are increasingly prompting growers to incorporate tillage to reduce water and nutrient competition between cover crops and grapevines. However, the immediate consequences of this practice on soil attributes remain poorly understood. To evaluate whether reintroducing til
institutions: Institute of Agrifood Research and Technology

title: Evaluating Data Collection and Processing Methods in Sustainable Supply Chain Management among Logistics Operators in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined data collection and processing methods and sustainable supply chain management among logistics operators in Lagos State, Nigeria. Specifically, it identified and ranked data collection and processing methods, ranked the economic, environmental, social and operational dimensions of sustainable supply chain management, and assessed whether data collection and processing methods significantly predicted sustainable supply chain management. A descriptive and analytical survey design was adopted. The study targeted an estimated population of 500 logistics and supply chain profess

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF-like nanoshe
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Bifunctional Carbon‐Sensitized Hollow Heterojunctions for Dual‐Mode Sensing of Emerging Contaminant 6‐PPD
abstract: ABSTRACT N‐(1,3‐dimethylbutyl)‐N′‐phenyl‐p‐phenylenediamine (6‐PPD), a ubiquitous rubber tire antioxidant, poses a severe threat to ecological safety due to its pronounced ecotoxicity. This work achieves the unprecedented dual‐mode photoelectrochemical and electrochemical (PEC‐EC) sensing of 6‐PPD through a dual‐mode platform endowed with bifunctional catalytic signal amplification. Integrating a novel hollow Bi@BiOBr/CdLa 2 S 4 heterojunction with multiwalled carbon nanotubes, this dual‐mode platform delivers highly stable, efficiently amplified signals.
