title: Identification and Characterization of a Cytosolic Malate Dehydrogenase as a Potential Drug Target in Echinococcus multilocularis
abstract: Abstract Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the larval stage (metacestode) of Echinococcus multilocularis, is an emerging zoonotic disease with limited treatment options, highlighting the need for new therapeutic targets. Like other helminths, E. multilocularis relies on anaerobic metabolism via malate dismutation, a poorly characterized pathway. In this study, cytosolic malate dehydrogenase (cMDH), a key enzyme in this pathway, was investigated as a potential drug target. Bioinformatic analyses identified three cMDH homologues in E. multilocularis, all exhibiting canonical domain architecture

title: Transformación Digital desde la Mirada del Talento Humano en IPS: Un Estudio Multicéntrico
abstract: Objetivo: Explorar la transformación digital en las Instituciones Prestadoras de Servicios de Salud (IPS) desde la mirada del talento humano en un entorno digital. Metodología: Se empleó una metodología de revisión sistemática; la búsqueda de literatura científica se llevó a cabo entre enero y mayo de 2026, centrada en estudios publicados entre 2015 y 2025. Para ello, se realizaron exploraciones manuales y electrónicas en cinco bases de datos reconocidas por su relevancia académica en el ámbito de la salud: PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SciELO y Google Scholar. publisher: Latin American Association for the Advancement of Sciences

title: A Comprehensive Review of Various Models of Direct Current Motors: Structures, Operating Principles, Classification, and Industrial Applications
abstract: Direct current (DC) motors have been studied for decades, yet they remain relevant to a wide range of motion-control, precision-drive, educational, and specialized industrial applications. The large variety of DC motor configurations, however, has also led to some inconsistency in the way these machines are classified and compared. Terms related to excitation, commutation, construction, and control are often used at the same classification level, even though they describe different aspects of a motor or drive system. title: Exploring Developmental Interactions Between Speech and Orofacial Functions in Preschoolers: A Cross‐Sectional Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Speech and orofacial functions (breathing, swallowing, and chewing) both develop within the stomatognathic system and share common anatomical structures and motor control mechanisms. Theoretical models suggest that early orofacial motor experiences may shape speech development. However, empirical evidence examining these relationships during the preschool years remains scarce. AIMS: This study explored the relationship between speech and orofacial functions in preschool children. We hypothesised that this relationship is not direct but indirect, with oral motor competence, operatio
journal: International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders

title: Gut bacterial extracellular vesicles in glucocorticoid-associated skeletal complications: evidence boundaries and translational challenges
abstract: Long-term or high-dose glucocorticoid (GC) therapy causes major skeletal complications, particularly glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) and glucocorticoid-associated osteonecrosis of the femoral head (GIONFH). Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) produced by gut-resident bacteria are candidate inter-organ messengers, but the GC-specific evidence base is extremely limited. institutions: Luoyang Orthopedic-Traumatological Hospital of Henan Province

title: Nationwide Tracking of A‐Lineage Spread in Western Honey Bees Using Haplotype Sharing, Local Ancestry Mapping, and Migration Inference
abstract: Understanding the spatial dynamics of genetic ancestry is essential for elucidating historical and contemporary patterns of gene flow among populations. Honey bees in the United States have a 400-year history of importation, management, and adaptation to diverse environments. Genetic diversity is a key factor for colony health and resilience. Notably, the most genetically diverse populations in the country originate from the invasive A-lineage (Africanized or 'Killer' honey bees). title: Dark tourism: concepts, practices, ethical challenges and future research
abstract: Purpose This review paper critically synthesizes contemporary scholarship on dark tourism, integrating conceptual foundations, visitor motivations, management practices, ethical dilemmas, sustainability challenges, and emerging research directions. It aims to advance a coherent understanding of responsible dark tourism development through an interdisciplinary lens. Design/methodology/approach A systematic critical literature review of peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 examined on tourism, heritage, psychology, ethics, cultural studies, and sustainability research. title: Türk Mitolojisindeki Yiyecek Tasavvurlarının Kültürel Sürdürülebilirlik Bağlamında Değerlendirilmesi
abstract: Bu çalışma, Türk mitolojilerinde yer alan yiyeceklere yüklenen sembolik anlamların Türk kültüründeki izlerini belirlemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bu doğrultuda tanrısal figürler olan Kayra Han, Erlik Han ve Ülgen Han’ın yer aldığı anlatılar nitel bir yaklaşımla değerlendirilmiştir. title: Green public facilities and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective
abstract: Background This study conceptualizes green public facilities as green-space resources embedded in urban public-resource allocation and examines the relationship between their spatial distribution and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective. Methods Data on 6,871 respondents from the 2021 Chinese General Social Survey were linked to green public facility and public transport point-of-interest data and statistical indicators for 82 districts/counties. title: Reconfiguring aesthetic values: a power-sensitive framework for AI-mediated visual communication
abstract: This conceptual analysis argues that aesthetic values in AI-mediated visual culture are socially constructed and shaped by power relations rather than being universally shared or psychologically neutral. Visual content is now produced, circulated, and evaluated within socio-technical systems governed by platform infrastructures, algorithmic recommendation mechanisms, and data-driven optimization logic. By asking how aesthetic value systems can be reconceptualized through a power-sensitive framework in order to understand AI-mediated visual communication, the conceptual analysis critically reco

title: Multi‐year and multi‐trait evaluation of hemp ( Cannabis sativa L.) genotypes using AMMI, GGE, WAASB, and MGIDI
abstract: Abstract In hemp ( Cannabis sativa L.), yield and agronomic performance are influenced by genotype and year‐to‐year environmental variation. This study evaluated the performance, stability, and multi‐trait superiority of 16 hemp genotypes over four consecutive growing seasons (2022–2025) using additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI), genotype plus genotype × year interaction (GGE) biplot, WAASB, and multi‐trait genotype–ideotype distance index (MGIDI) analyses. title: Assessing changes in electrical resistivity signals in simulated mass and single graves over 18 months after burial
abstract: Abstract Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) has been increasingly explored as a non‐destructive technique for searching for unmarked graves. However, its effectiveness remains uncertain as measured resistivity responses are influenced by burial type, time after burial, soil properties and environmental conditions. Previous studies have reported both positive and negative resistivity anomalies associated with graves, highlighting the need for further controlled investigations. Moreover, limited experimental data exist for ERT measurements over graves containing human cadavers and for mass

title: Genome-wide association study and candidate gene prioritization for stem architectural traits in Tartary buckwheat
abstract: Stem architecture is a key determinant of lodging resistance, yield potential, and mechanical harvestability in Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ), yet the genetic basis of stem-related traits remains poorly understood. In this study, a diverse panel of 244 Tartary buckwheat accessions was evaluated for five stem architectural traits, including plant height (PH), stem diameter (SD), branch number on the main stem (BNMS), node number on the main stem (NNMS), and stem wall thickness (TST), across three field environments (Huize 2025, Songming 2024, and Songming 2025). institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Evolutionary and dynamic constraints converge on a conserved coupling sector in thermally adapted GH1 β-glucosidases
abstract: How protein sequences evolve to maintain functional conformational dynamics under thermal stress remains an important question in molecular evolution. Thermophilic enzymes are often considered to achieve stability primarily through enhanced structural rigidity, yet thermal adaptation may also involve the preservation or reorganization of correlated motions across the protein scaffold. title: Early career challenges of physical education teachers
abstract: Introduction Early career physical education teachers face challenges similar to those of other novice teachers, in addition to field-specific difficulties. Their professional adjustment depends on the interaction between personal psychological and pedagogical resources and the workplace demands. Successfully navigating this process and ensuring adequate socio-institutional support are essential for career development and sustained professional practice. The aim of this study is to reveal the career challenges faced by physical education teachers in their first 5 years of the profession and to

title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes
abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
institutions: Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: Biostimulant potential of Limnospira platensis biomass fermented with lactic acid bacteria in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris): strain characterization, biochemical shifts, and growth promotion
abstract: The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in conventional agriculture poses significant risks to soil health, environmental quality, and food security. Plant biostimulants derived from microorganisms, microalgae and cyanobacteria offer a sustainable alternative. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and cyanobacteria such as Limnospira platensis are recognized for their plant growth-promoting characteristics. institutions: Universidad de las Fuerzas Armadas ESPE

title: An Examination of the "Addiction and Addiction Prevention" Course Using Activity-Based Teaching Methods: A Qualitative Study
abstract: This study aimed to examine prospective educators’ experiences, perspectives, and perceived competencies regarding activity-based instructional practices implemented throughout an undergraduate "Addiction and Addiction Prevention” course. The study employed a qualitative descriptive design utilizing inductive thematic analysis. The study group comprised a complete cohort of 55 undergraduate students (100% participation rate) enrolled in the course and meeting predefined inclusion criteria at a public university in Turkey during the 2025–2026 academic year. title: Indonesia’s Palm Oil Trilemma: Reconciling Biodiesel Expansion, Export Competitiveness, and Supply Resilience under Climate and Governance Constraints
abstract: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative literature review examines the resulting policy trilemma using peer-reviewed research published during 2020-2026 and the IPOSS fourth-quarter 2026 industry outlook as a contextual, explicitly prospective source. journal: Journal of Business Research and Reports

title: Acoustical Materials from Conventional to Cutting-Edge Innovations─An Overview
abstract: Abstract With rapid urbanization and industrial expansion, noise pollution has escalated into a pervasive environmental and public health crisis. Thus, an imperative need arises for both advanced sound mitigation strategies and, especially, a fundamental shift toward sustainability to meet pressing worldwide environmental policies. title: Recent Advances in LDH‐Based Sorbents for Wastewater Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorption is an efficient and environmentally benign technique for wastewater treatment. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are low‐cost materials with high adsorption capacities for a wide array of pollutants. This review comprehensively summarizes recent studies on the adsorption of dyes, metal ions, inorganic anions, and organic contaminants using LDH‐based materials. The effects of preparation methods, cation molar ratios, and calcination temperatures on LDH performance are thoroughly examined. institutions: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies targeting HIF signaling and hypoxia tolerance: opportunities and limitations for personalized interventions
abstract: For acute mountain sickness prevention and the treatment of respiratory, cardiovascular, and nervous system diseases, pharmacological (prolyl hydroxylase domain inhibitors, plant extracts, erythrocyte pyruvate kinase activators, and hemoglobin oxygen affinity allosteric activators) and non-pharmacological approaches (hypoxic training and hypoxic therapy) are used. title: Solenostemma argel Dead Leaves as an Eco‐Friendly and Low‐Cost Adsorbent for Effective Removal of Methylene Blue From Aqueous Media: Adsorption Performance and Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable, low‐cost adsorbents derived from agricultural waste are needed for the removal of toxic dyes from contaminated water. Solenostemma argel dead leaves (SAL) were evaluated as a biosorbent for methylene blue (MB) removal from contaminated water. SAL was characterized by x‐ray diffraction (XRD), N 2 adsorption–desorption (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). institutions: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species
abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds—including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules—that may modulate gut microbiota–host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.

title: The materialities of pigments, paints and personhood in San rock paintings: celebrating the inspiration from David Lewis-Williams
abstract: Most rock art research has been influenced by David Lewis-Williams. He has shown the material primacy of rock paintings, the cautious use of ethnography for emic understandings, and the importance of theory. In addition, his recognition of the impact of ‘critical, radical thought’ on our practice. This radical thought is encapsulated by posthuman ontologies which study the entanglements of humans and more-than-humans. Rock paintings are material and have material effects. title: Wildfire severity reshapes soil organic carbon fractions and stabilization pathways in a subalpine forest
abstract: Introduction Wildfire disturbance is a major driver of soil carbon cycling in subalpine forests, yet differential responses of soil organic carbon fractions to fire severity remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated a subalpine forest in northwestern Sichuan, China, 6 years after wildfire. Four fire-severity classes were established: unburned control (UB), low-severity fire (LSF), moderate-severity fire (MSF), and high-severity fire (HSF). journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: Mycobiota associated with diseased Schrenk’s spruce in mountain forest ecosystems of Kyrgyzstan
abstract: Schrenk’s spruce ( Picea schrenkiana ) is a dominant coniferous tree species in the Western Tian Shan forests and plays an important ecological role in maintaining mountain forest ecosystems in Kyrgyzstan. In recent years, the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve has seen a significant increase in diseased and declining spruce trees, raising concerns about forest health and ecosystem stability. The present study aimed to investigate the fungal communities associated with diseased roots, stems, and needles of Schrenk’s spruce in the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve, Kyrgyzstan. title: Measuring the sensitivity of sand pile geometry to substrate roughness for calibrating friction parameters in the discrete element method

title: When Politics Enters the Waiting Room: Far-Right Electoral Victories Exacerbate Discrimination in Access to Healthcare
abstract: Abstract Far-right political shifts have been linked to increased racism, raising concerns about their impact on minority access to public services. This study investigates whether far-right electoral victories encourage discrimination by street-level bureaucrats, who are expected to act impartially. We conducted a nested research design in Italy, combining a field-experimental audit with a regression discontinuity design focused on municipalities near the electoral threshold for far-right mayors. title: Eficacia de los barnices fluorados en la prevención de la caries dental y en la disminución de la sensibilidad dental.
abstract: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar la eficacia de la aplicación profesional de barniz de fluoruro de sodio al 5 % en la prevención de caries dental y en la reducción de la hipersensibilidad dentinaria en comparación con un placebo. Se realizó un ensayo clínico aleatorizado, controlado, de grupos paralelos y ciego para el evaluador, en el que se incluyeron 124 pacientes de 6 a 65 años con riesgo moderado-alto de caries y/o hipersensibilidad dentinaria (VAS ≥ 4), asignados aleatoriamente (1:1) al grupo experimental (barniz de NaF al 5 %, n = 62) o al grupo control (barniz placebo, n = 62);

title: Factors influencing elderly people’s intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research
abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. institutions: First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University

title: Perspectives of Biomaterial‐Based Sustainable Integrated Micro‐ and Nanophotonics
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor‐based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogenic molecules. This review covers recent advances in nano‐ and microscale biophotonic devices, spanning biopolymer waveguides (with optical losses down to 0.24 dB cm −1 ), bio‐organic LEDs and lasers (luminous efficiencies up to 130 lm W −1 ; lifetimes >3600 h), biohybrid photovoltaics (PCE up to ∼20%), photodetectors, and optoelectronic memristors. title: Entomophagy at India’s nutrition-sustainability nexus: biodiversity, nutritional evidence, food safety, regulatory gaps and a conceptual commercialization roadmap
abstract: India is among the most entomophagically diverse countries in the world. Peer-reviewed inventories document more than 300 edible insect species across at least 14 states, together with a documented but taxonomically separate tradition of arachnophagy in Nagaland and Manipur. Despite this biological resource, India has not converted its edible arthropod tradition into a regulated protein sector. title: From wind-solar accommodation to potential coal-generation displacement: spatial coordination and operational CO2 mitigation in China’s power system
abstract: Wind-solar accommodation does not necessarily yield equivalent reductions in coal generation or emissions. Using 2022 hourly output for 2880 county-level units, 8760-h loads for 31 provinces and data for 2985 coal units or project phases, we compare provincial self-accommodation, neighboring-province pairing, nationwide pairing and national aggregation. title: From Managerialism to Mutuality: The World café as Structured Dialogic Peer Learning in MBA Sustainability Education
abstract: Peer learning and dialogic pedagogy are well established in Higher Education research but remain underutilized in MBA education, where transmissive and expert-centered formats continue to dominate. This article examines the World Café method as a structured dialogic peer-learning architecture within an MBA sustainability and responsible leadership module at a UK business school. title: The development of creative imagination and symbolic thinking through thematic social role-play activity
abstract: Grounded in Vygotsky's cultural-historical paradigm, this article presents a theoretical analysis of the role of thematic social role-play in preschool psychological development, positioning it not merely as a recreational activity but as the leading activity driving psychological maturation. Within this framework, we examine how high-level play serves as the critical foundation for the genesis of creative imagination and symbolic thought—all essential components of the developing child's psychological neoformations. title: Nitrogen management in rainfed castor: a comprehensive analysis of productivity, nutrient use efficiency, economics, energy flow, and carbon footprint
abstract: Introduction Nitrogen (N), an essential plant nutrient characterized by the lowest use efficiency and multiple loss pathways, challenges its management in rainfed castor. Therefore, a field experiment was conducted over three consecutive Kharif seasons (2022-2024) to develop an adoptable N management strategy for rainfed castor cultivation. title: Power system expansion in Ecuador: A stakeholder driven sustainability assessment of generation technologies
abstract: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited investment in new capacity since 2018. In this context, the central government has begun promoting nuclear energy as a medium- and long-term option, despite the country’s lack of experience with this technology and the Electricity Master Plan’s identification of substantial renewable potential. title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms
abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na + and Ca 2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. title: Discriminatory spaces and psychological distress: the role of responses among unaccompanied minor migrants. A mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction Unaccompanied minor migrants in Europe face heightened vulnerability, yet little is known about how discrimination unfolds in their daily lives, how they respond to these experiences, and the impact on psychological distress. The aims of this study are (1) to examine the everyday experiences of perceived discrimination among unaccompanied minor migrants and (2) to test whether responses to discrimination mediate the association between perceived discrimination and psychological distress in this population. title: A novel biodegradable gelatin capsule platform for input-efficient herbicide delivery in transplanted rice
abstract: Background Weed management in transplanted rice requires effective herbicide delivery while improving input-use efficiency and reducing reliance on conventional application practices. This study developed and evaluated a biodegradable gelatin capsule-based herbicide delivery system, subsequently protected through a design patent, as an alternative approach for herbicide application. title: Why is the right side of the brain responsible for the left side of the body? The evolutionary history of a puzzling trait
abstract: In humans, the right motor cortex controls the spinal motoneurons that cause the limbs on the left sides of our bodies to move. Similarly, the right side of the cerebral cortex predominantly receives sensory information about the left side of our bodies and the left side of the outside world. Although there have been numerous papers (dating back at least to Cajal) speculating on the adaptive value of this contralateral organization, to date none appears to have examined its evolutionary history. title: Integrative omics perspectives on the gut-liver axis in chronic liver diseases: mechanisms and therapeutic potential
abstract: Chronic liver diseases, including chronic viral hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), autoimmune liver diseases (AILD), liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), are rising in prevalence and weigh heavily on public health worldwide. The rapid development and integration of multi-omics technologies-including microbiome, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics-have moved the understanding of chronic liver disease pathogenesis and progression into a new phase. title: La exclusión escogida. quienes deben quedar fuera del mundo
abstract: Este artigo discute a noção de exclusão escolhida como uma categoria analítica para compreender as persistentes desigualdades digitais na contemporaneidade. Parte-se da hipótese de que a exclusão digital não decorre apenas de limitações tecnológicas ou infraestruturais, mas também de decisões políticas, econômicas e institucionais que definem quais territórios, grupos sociais e populações serão incorporados aos ecossistemas digitais e quais permanecerão à margem. title: Cableless Power Transmission System : Problems and Prospects
abstract: Abstract Cableless power transmission—the transfer of electrical energy through free space rather than a conductor—now spans commodity near-field chargers, standardized electric-vehicle (EV) charging, kilometre-scale microwave and laser beaming, and in-orbit tests of space-based solar power. Existing reviews usually treat one mechanism, quote peak efficiencies without their geometric conditions, and rarely connect performance to exposure regulation or cost. title: Consenso interamericano de miocardiopatía hipertrófica
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy and poses major diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in Latin America, owing to heterogeneity in resource availability, access to advanced technologies, and the organization of health systems. OBJECTIVES: To develop the first Inter-American Consensus on HCM, in order to standardize the care of these patients tailored to the regional context. title: Triterpenoids – future multi-target compounds against obesity and towards restoration of metabolic health
abstract: Obesity and its associated diseases represent one of the most urgent public health crises of our time, affecting billions worldwide. Current pharmacological agents, such as GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, have demonstrated high clinical efficacy in diabetes and weight management. However, the required lifelong medication is often limited by high economic costs and severe side effects, including gastrointestinal complications. Consequently, the search for complementary therapies is invaluable. This review highlights the potential of natural triterpenoids in obesity management by shifting

title: Recurrent pulmonary infection, a vicious cycle of multifactorial interactions, and prevention/treatment strategies
abstract: Recurrent pulmonary infection (RPI) refers to the frequent and repeated episodes of lower respiratory tract infections. At its core, it represents a vicious cycle arising from the disruption of the homeostatic balance among pathogens, host immunity, and pulmonary architecture. RPI accounts for a considerable proportion of pediatric pneumonia cases, and the cumulative incidence among elderly patients hospitalized for pneumonia is also markedly elevated, imposing a substantial disease burden. title: Influence of LED spectral quality and natural growing conditions on flowering, yield, and fruit biochemical quality of okra (Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench)
abstract: Introduction Climate change poses significant challenges to open-field production of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench), a tropical vegetable crop of high nutritional and economic value. This study evaluated the effects of light-emitting diode (LED) spectral quality on reproductive development, fruit characteristics, yield, mineral composition, antioxidant activity, and total phenolic content of okra. title: The cultural origins of the demographic transition in France
abstract: Abstract This research shows that secularization accounts for the early fertility decline in France. Why the demographic transition began in France a century before any other country is one of the big questions of history because it challenges traditional explanations and because of data limitations. Using a novel dataset crowdsourced from online genealogies, I comprehensively document the decline and its timing. title: Ecological dynamics of gut bacteriophages in food animal production systems: Mechanisms of microbiome modulation and implications for livestock health and production
abstract: Gut bacteriophages (phages) are the most diverse and abundant component of the enteric virome in food-producing animals, and act as core modulators of intestinal microbial community structure and function, with important implications for livestock health and production performance. Predominantly colonizing the intestinal mucus layer, phages mediate dynamic interactions with bacterial hosts and shape gut microecological homeostasis. title: Epidemiological patterns of black pod (Phytophthora spp.) and frosty pod rot (Moniliophthora roreri) in cocoa plantations of Tequendama, Colombia
abstract: Cocoa is an important crop in Colombia and a key productive alternative in post-conflict rural areas. Similar to other tropical production systems, yields are constrained by diseases such as black pod disease and frosty pod rot. This study evaluated the temporal and spatial epidemiological patterns of both diseases on three cocoa farms located in the Tequendama region of Colombia through analyses of disease incidence, severity, disease progress, and spatial distribution. Pod assessments were conducted over a six-month period, recording disease incidence, severity, pod developmental stage, and

title: Sustainable desulfurization through coupled extraction-catalytic oxidation strategy: Mechanisms, materials, and process intensification
abstract: In response to the imperative for sustainable energy and environmental protection, ultra-deep desulfurization of fuels poses a critical challenge. Conventional hydrodesulfurization and emerging non-hydrogenation techniques face limitations in efficiency, economic viability, and ecological sustainability, particularly for refractory sulfur species. Among alternatives, extractive catalytic oxidative desulfurization (ECODS) has emerged as a prominent approach by integrating catalytic oxidation and liquid-phase extraction under mild conditions. title: Solid CO2 sorbents for medium- and high-temperature carbon capture: material design, shaping, and deployment for hydrogen-related processes
abstract: Abstract Due to their high-temperature resistance and potential for process intensification, medium- and high-temperature solid CO 2 adsorbents offer significant advantages in combining carbon capture with thermochemical fuel conversion and hydrogen production. Although significant progress has been made in terms of formulation, microstructure, cyclic stability and reaction mechanisms, practical evaluation must go beyond laboratory-scale CO 2 adsorption tests to encompass, in addition, formability, wear resistance, regeneration strength, reactor compatibility and application potential. title: Cover crop management influences soil properties and grapevine performance across three growing seasons in a subtropical vineyard
abstract: Cover crop management can modify soil conditions and grapevine performance, but these responses may depend on the vegetation-management strategy and growing season. This study evaluated the effects of different cover crop management systems on soil, physiological, yield, and fruit technological variables of Vitis vinifera L. cv. Viognier cultivated in Campo Largo, Paraná, Brazil, for three growing seasons (2023–2026; 2023/24, 2024/25, and 2025/26). title: Neuroimmune communication: from CNS-resident cell networks to the glioblastoma microenvironment
abstract: Neurons, glial cells, and immune cells engage in extensive bidirectional communication within the central nervous system (CNS) through shared receptors, ligands, and secreted mediators. Glial cells — particularly astrocytes and microglia — serve not merely as structural support but as central immunomodulatory hubs that relay neural signals to immune effectors. In the context of CNS malignancies, glioblastoma (GBM) co-opts these neuroimmune networks to establish an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. title: Reflexões sobre o conceito de preservação na Arquivologia Brasileira: uma análise a partir da legislação federal e da produção científica
abstract: This study addresses the concept of preservation in the field of Archival Science, starting from federal legislation and academic production on the subject. It comparatively analyzes the presence and uses of the term "preservation" in Brazilian archival legislation and academic production, seeking to identify continuities, shifts, and changes in how the topic is formulated over time. The research adopts a qualitative approach, of a basic nature, with a deductive method, articulating documentary and bibliographic research. title: Advances in photothermal-driven tumor immunomodulation and synergistic therapy
abstract: Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a local treatment that uses photothermal conversion agents (PTAs) to absorb light and produce heat in tumor tissue. The direct result is tumor ablation. At the same time, heat-damaged tumor cells may undergo immunogenic cell death (ICD). This process is often accompanied by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), followed by dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation. title: The Institutionalization of REIT Sustainability Reporting: Cross‐Country Evidence From ESG Disclosure Regimes and Building Sustainability Policies
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the institutionalization and textual evolution of sustainability reporting among listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, and Japan between 2020 and 2025. Reporting is framed as the joint product of two institutional layers: capital‐market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure regimes and building‐level sustainability policies. journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: Senior Executive Pay and Corporate Sustainability Performance: The Roles of Green Innovation, Governance and State Ownership in China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between senior executive pay and corporate sustainability performance using 14,524 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms over the period 2019–2023. This period provides consistent data availability and encompasses China's transition towards the 2020 dual‐carbon policy. Drawing on agency, managerial power, stakeholder and resource dependence theories, we investigate nonlinear effects, green innovation as a mediating mechanism, and governance and ownership as boundary conditions. journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: Forest endophytes as a biological resource insights into their role in sustainable agriculture and agroforestry
abstract: Abstract Forest ecosystems are the hidden reservoir of beneficial microorganisms, particularly for endophytes, that colonize plant tissue internally without causing any disease symptoms and play a key role in plant health and ecosystem sustainability. Forest-derived endophytic bacteria and fungi are crucial in nutrient cycling, stress resistance and growth promotion via phosphorus solubilization, nitrogen fixation and synthesis of phytohormones. title: From Frege to ChatGPT: Compositionality in Language, Cognition, and Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Compositionality has long been considered a key explanatory property underlying human intelligence: arbitrary concepts can be composed into novel complex combinations, permitting the acquisition of an open ended, potentially infinite expressive capacity from finite learning experiences. Influential arguments have held that neural networks fail to explain this aspect of behavior, leading many to dismiss them as viable models of human cognition. title: Machine learning applications in the heliosphere
abstract: Space weather is the study of the near-Earth impact of the processes on the Sun. In a this era of technology, space weather emerges as a crucial area of study wherein the state of the near-Earth conditions need to be modeled and forecasted. Crucially, the advent of machine learning provides us with opportunities to study this subject in a rather comprehensive manner. In this chapter, we treat the the processes arising from Sun to the impact on the ground as a set of coupled systems, which can be studied in isolation or in a coupled manner. title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Climate Change-Related Health Issues in Africa
abstract: While climate change disproportionately impacts African public health, AI predictive modeling remains heavily constrained. Using a Synthetic Knowledge Synthesis approach and VOSviewer, we conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature, comparing Global and African corpora. Network analysis reveals stark divergences: global research emphasizes complex, predictive models for planetary health, whereas African research focuses on localized, reactive solutions for immediate infectious disease triage. institutions: Zdravstveni dom dr. Adolfa Drolca Maribor

title: CoraLive: Ultra-Low-Power Underwater Vision for Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring
abstract: Effective coral reef protection and restoration demands continuous, long-term underwater monitoring. However, current solutions largely rely on fragmented, manual labor and costly infrastructure, or are severely limited by constrained battery lifespans. In this paper, we present CoraLive, an ultra-low-power underwater camera system for long-term, continuous coral reef monitoring. CoraLive presents a decoupled underwater-shore co-design that minimizes on-board computation and storage, offloading heavy reconstruction and segmentation tasks to offline shore-side processing. title: FASST: A Compact Stateless Atmosphere Model for Long-Term Ocean Coupling
abstract: Coupled climate simulations are computationally expensive, largely because of the atmosphere. We introduce FASST, a coupled climate model that retains the prognostic POP2 ocean while replacing the atmosphere and sea ice with lightweight U-Net emulators. The atmospheric emulator is diagnostic, predicting surface fluxes from the evolving ocean-ice state every $6$ simulated hours, while the sea-ice emulator advances the ice state monthly. title: Conditional Diffusion Generation of DVL and Inertial Signals for Underwater Navigation
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) navigate without satellite positioning and rely on Doppler velocity log (DVL) and inertial sensors for motion estimation. Deep learning methods for processing these sensors require training data covering the motion the AUV encounters, commonly obtained through costly sea trials. To overcome this limitation, we present a conditional diffusion framework that generates synthetic DVL and inertial signals to replace real recordings in training. title: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is often proposed as a low-cost complement to multibeam surveys of ports, but its accuracy is seldom measured on an area the model has never seen. We test SDB in the turbid, shallow and tidal waters of the Abu Dhabi coast against 285,619 multibeam soundings from twelve surveys at six port areas, reduced to Lowest Astronomical Tide. title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
abstract: We developed a machine learning (ML) surrogate trained on instantaneous large eddy simulation (LES) data filtered using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to predict mean flow fields in natural rivers with complex geometries. The surrogate enables efficient prediction of mean flow fields downstream of marine hydrokinetic (MHK) turbine arrays at a fraction of the computational cost of high fidelity simulations, facilitating turbine layout optimization in natural waterways where bathymetry, turbulence, and turbine interactions influence the available energy resource. title: Edge intelligence for distributed acoustic sensing with ultracompact neural networks
abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) transforms optical fibres into dense arrays of vibration sensors for continuous, long-range monitoring with high spatial resolution. Yet converting these large-scale measurements into actionable information with compact models that retain task performance remains challenging. Existing artificial-intelligence approaches are typically optimized for specific sensing environments and tasks, but their computational requirements can hinder deployment in compact, power-constrained field systems. title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra
abstract: Machine-learning models for spectroscopy usually treat a spectrum as a fixed-grid intensity vector, leaving the physical coordinate implicit in the array index. Such models are tied to a single sampling grid, spectral range and resolution, which limits their use when measurement conditions change. Here we represent each spectral point as a pair of intensity and wavenumber and compute Transformer positional encodings from the wavenumber itself. title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. title: A fully convolutional neural network to classify UXOs using multicomponent electromagnetic induction data
abstract: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance relies on electromagnetic induction (EMI) methods to detect and classify buried and submerged metallic objects, but the standard classification workflow requires physics-based inversion and manual expert review. We present a fully convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies UXO directly from multicomponent time-domain EMI data, bypassing the inversion step entirely. title: An all-weather microwave-based AI retrieval of pan-Arctic melt pond fraction
abstract: Melt pond fraction (MPF) is a key variable governing Arctic sea ice albedo and seasonal sea ice predictability, yet existing pan-Arctic MPF products rely almost exclusively on optical sensors, limiting availability under cloud cover and seasonal darkness. This study presents PRISM-MPF, the first pan-Arctic, multi-year, all-weather MPF dataset, derived from PRISM (Polar Retrievals through Intelligent Sensor Merging), a machine learning framework fusing multi-source microwave observations with auxiliary thermal and spatiotemporal information to complement optical products. title: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment
abstract: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. title: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones
abstract: Rapid intensification (RI) is one of the most dangerous and unpredictable phases of tropical cyclones, and its environmental and structural drivers are difficult to identify and separate in observations. Here we introduce CausalVisionRI, a causal-prior-constrained deep-learning system for 24-h RI warning in the western North Pacific. It integrates infrared remote sensing imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and an observationally discovered causal graph into a unified model. title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part II: Passive Detection
abstract: Underwater acoustic passive detection is essential to maritime surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Existing detection systems typically collapse multichannel array observations into a binary decision or a scalar confidence score, offering limited insight into the physical evidence that supports or contradicts a target declaration. title: GeoPrompt: Geometry-Conditioned Prompt Learning for Underwater Open-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary instance segmentation (OVIS) provides a promising solution for marine perception by recognizing and segmenting categories beyond predefined label spaces. Existing OVIS methods usually rely on vision-language alignment, where visual region features are matched with textual category embeddings to recognize both seen and unseen classes. title: Batched NN 4D-Var: a performant hybrid model framework for the Integrated Forecasting System
abstract: Hybrid forecasting systems combining machine learning and numerical weather prediction offer a promising route toward improved forecast skill while preserving physical consistency. In this study, we investigate online learning of state-dependent model-error corrections within the Integrated Forecasting System using 4D-Var. Building on previous work, we represent model error using a neural network embedded within the forecast model and trained from observations through the data assimilation cycle. title: A Review of Deep-learning-based Seismic Data Denoising and Its Promising Paradigm Shift to Foundation Models
abstract: Abstract Denoising is a long-standing and widely-concerned topic in seismic data processing, for it can significantly increase the signal-to-noise ratio of seismic data. Numerous deep learning (DL) methods have shown promising denoising performance, but most of them are task-specific and focus on a certain type of seismic background noise. The real condition that seismic datasets are often contaminated by various types of noises motivates us to explore a well-generalized and versatile DL model for seismic data denoising. title: Spatially-Adaptive Neural-Network Based Extraction of Significant Wave Heights from HF Radar Data
abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) retrieval from high-frequency (HF) radar data conventionally relies on Doppler-spectrum processing and interpretation of the weak second-order scattering continuum. This article investigates adaptive spatial processing for time-domain SWH estimation using ordered envelope statistics. title: Multi-level Constrained Learning for Underwater Image Enhancement
abstract: Underwater image enhancement aims to correct color and recover detail degraded by wavelength-dependent attenuation, scattering, and noise. Paired-reference supervision constrains output similarity, but does not by itself specify the color mapping, the strength of local detail corrections, or consistency with the degraded observation. We propose MCL-UIE, a paired-supervised framework that addresses these requirements by constraining restoration operations and the training objective. title: Coral Discovery: The Division of Cognitive Labor in Autonomous Research
abstract: A research community is only as strong as the way it divides its cognitive labour. The philosopher Philip Kitcher argued that researchers should not all pursue the most promising approach. Credit rules, not a central plan, keep some of them on other lines. We bring this question to autonomous research, where Large Language Model agents improve programs against a deterministic grader. title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
abstract: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. title: Open-set multi-view seahorse re-identification from underwater photograph sequences
abstract: Automated animal re-identification from photograph sequences can facilitate minimally invasive Capture-Mark-Recapture studies at scale. Yet, photographs taken during an observation session can vary greatly in quality, not always providing the necessary information for accurate re-identification. In this paper, we present new methods for taxonomic classification, sex determination, and open-set re-identification from image sequences. title: Surface Conditioning for Zero-Shot Multivariate Correction in a Marine Biogeochemistry Emulator
abstract: Bias correction in process-based models usually means iterative data assimilation with explicit covariance modelling. We propose a lightweight alternative based on a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry (BGC), showing that the conditioning pathway of its autoencoder can serve as an observation injection point. The decoder is conditioned on surface variables via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), originally designed to incorporate physical boundary forcings. title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification
abstract: Developing multiple instance learning pipelines for the classification of whole-slide images involves many interdependent design decisions and expertise in both pathology and machine learning. We present AutoMIL, an open-source framework that applies principles from the field of automated machine learning to tackle this task by automating integral pipeline steps, such as preprocessing, training and evaluation. title: New Wine in an Old Bottle -- NeuralPOM: A Hybrid Ocean Forecast Model with Differentiable Dynamics and Staged Learning
abstract: Coarse-grid ocean circulation models rely on empirical subgrid parameterizations that struggle to capture mesoscale eddies, whereas purely data-driven neural forecasters accumulate trajectory drift, violate tracer conservation, and damp small-scale variability over extended integrations. Here we present NeuralPOM, a hybrid ocean forecast model that couples differentiable explicit mode-split and semi-implicit free-surface implementations of the Princeton Ocean Model (POM) to a conservation-constrained neural corrector. The three-dimensional primitive-equation solver advances the ocean state, wh

title: GNN-VIEW: Visual Inspection and Explanation of Graph-based Earth-System Models
abstract: Machine learning Earth-system models are becoming increasingly important, and so is their development. Graph-based models, one of the most prominent approaches, allow developers to constrain the learning process before training via graph connectivity. Yet, developing these models remains challenging: the graph is built algorithmically with little intuition about the final result beyond static plotting, which requires extra work and is often not detailed enough. Even after successful training, how the model arrives at forecasts remains obscure. We present GNN-VIEW, an interactive browser-based

title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. The proposed model incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation (PDE) into thi

title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. Gaussian localization weights incorporate context uncertainty through covariance inflation, with reflection at domain boundaries and an optional correction for uneven context sampling. Laboratoire d'Informatique, de Modélisation et d'Optimisation des Systèmes

title: Patch-Based Deep Kernel Learning for Data Assimilation and Bias Correction with Extremely Sparse Observations
abstract: Data Assimilation (DA) reconstructs the state of a spatio-temporal system by combining sensor observations with the output of a numerical model. Since model states are high-dimensional while observations cover only a small fraction of the domain, DA is a challenging large-scale estimation problem, central to weather forecasting and oceanography. Classical variational methods such as 3D-Var rely on a hand-crafted background error covariance that assumes unbiased errors, and therefore cannot capture state-dependent correlations or systematic model biases. Moreover, their cost grows with the size

title: Cleaner air strengthens the Pacific trade winds without a detectable change in El Nino
abstract: Air quality policy will cut aerosol and ozone precursor emissions, and studies disagree on how the tropical Pacific circulation and the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) will respond. Here we show, in 12 Earth system models with and without air quality controls, that the cuts strengthen the Pacific trade winds and offset half to two thirds of the weakening projected without them. The response is absent with prescribed sea surface temperatures and detectable only after 2040. It is consistent with the Indian Ocean warming relative to the Pacific, which also ranks the responses to cuts made reg
institutions: CMCC Foundation - Euro-Mediterranean Center on Climate Change

title: Real-Time Conveyor Belt Defect Detection via Edge TPU-Accelerated YOLOv11 on Raspberry Pi 5
abstract: Conveyor belts are vital arteries in continuous bulk material handling, particularly in heavy process industries such as cement manufacturing. Undetected structural anomalies (longitudinal tears, holes, degraded patch repairs, and impact punctures) cause catastrophic belt snapping, costly downtime, and severe safety hazards. While deep learning offers high accuracy, existing models rely on power-hungry workstation GPUs, hindering practical deployment at remote industrial edge points. In this paper, we propose, implement, and validate an end-to-end, low-power edge AI vision system for real-time

title: Stability-Performance Trade-off in Maritime Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Lyapunov-Guided Dual-Timescale Hierarchical RL Approach
abstract: Driven by the ever-growing demand for intelligent maritime services, cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned surface vehicle (USV) operations, together with wireless integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC), have become pivotal in maritime environments. However, the distinctive maritime environment precludes a direct application of terrestrial ISCC models, while sensing, communication, and computation compete for the same spatio-temporal resources, thus yielding inherent performance trade-offs that become particularly severe in resource-constrained ocean scenari

title: Forecasting Visitor Demand from Open AI-Camera Counts and Weather: Lessons from Japan for Saudi Heritage Sites
abstract: Small heritage and nature sites need a few days' notice of busy days to plan staff, overflow parking and shuttles, but most have neither sensors nor forecasting expertise. We test what one artificial intelligence (AI) camera counter per site, a public holiday calendar and a free weather forecast can predict. Using 22 months of open AI-camera counts from three contrasting sites in Fukui, Japan (a train station, a coastal cliff and a mountain summit park), we measure how weather changes visits, forecast daily counts up to a week ahead with only the weather forecast available at the time, test bu

title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
abstract: The Stochastic Transport in Upper Ocean Dynamics project introduced a new paradigm for representing uncertainty in geophysical fluid dynamics through stochastic transport models calibrated from data. This paper provides a synthesis of the principal theoretical and data assimilation developments achieved as part of the project. The central theme of the paper is the transformation of stochastic transport models from a modelling paradigm into a mathematically rigorous framework equipped with analytical, variational, calibration and Bayesian data assimilation methodologies suitable for geophysical

title: Moving bits instead of watts: Accelerating global AI data-centre deployment at the energy-digital-water-land nexus
abstract: Artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented expansion of data centres. However, this growth is increasingly stalled by grid transmission constraints that trap new data centres in years-long connection queues. Unlike electricity, computation can be moved across the globe through fibre-optic networks, but whether this spatial transfer can bypass constrained grids and accelerate global AI data-centre deployment remains unknown. Here we develop a global framework that places future data-centre capacity in energy-abundant regions and routes computational workloads through fibre-optic networ

title: Dynamic conditional density network of wind vectors
abstract: We propose the dynamic conditional density network (DCDN) to correct the bivariate normal predictive distribution commonly used to postprocess ensemble forecasts of wind vectors. The conditional distribution of the observed wind vector given the ensemble forecast may depart from the bivariate normal distribution. DCDN multiplies a bivariate normal reference density by a correction density. The correction density is a B-spline mixture on the probability integral transform scale of the reference density, and a neural network predicts its weights. title: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study
abstract: As the effects of climate change become increasingly apparent, the demand for renewable energy sources such as wind power continues to grow. However, renewables' variable and intermittent nature presents significant challenges in their integration into energy grids. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these issues. Still, its adoption in the energy sector has been hindered by the opacity of many AI models, which often function as black boxes. This paper introduces a carefully adapted GradientSHAP approach to provide interpretability for multivariate, multiste

title: Modelling wide-swath altimeter observation-error correlations with a regularised diffusion operator
abstract: Unaccounted-for observation-error correlations have long been known to be detrimental to the quality of atmospheric and ocean analyses produced by data assimilation (DA) systems. While progress has been made over the past decade on modelling inter-channel error correlations, modelling spatial error correlations remains a challenge for large datasets. Common strategies for mitigating the harmful effects of spatial error correlations, such as variance inflation or data thinning, prevent the extraction of valuable small-scale information from the observations. With the emergence of new sources of
institutions: Centre Européen de Recherche et de Formation Avancée en Calcul Scientifique

title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy
abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is extending from interpretation of existing data to the design and execution of experiments. Space offers distinctive scientific opportunities while restricting physical support. Microgravity and extraterrestrial environments expose phenomena that terrestrial experiments cannot fully reproduce; finite samples, constrained resources, and limited opportunities for intervention complicate sustained investigation. This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and ada

title: Directional Statistics on Circles and Spheres: A New Angle on Data
abstract: Two compass bearings near north can have an ordinary arithmetic mean pointing south: the difficulty is that angles live on a circle, not a straight line. Using real wind observations, diffusion-MRI orientations, and geometric examples from machine learning, this article introduces circular and axial averages, directional variability, and probability models on circles and spheres. The guiding principle is to identify the geometry and symmetries of the observations before choosing a statistical method.

title: Querying Multimodal Scientific Papers with AI: Practices and Preferences Across Blind, Low-Vision, and Sighted Scientists
abstract: Visual diagrams, figures, and tables are central to scientific papers, and convey information beyond what is captured in text. While blind or low-vision (BLV) scientists have traditionally relied on static alternative text to access figures in papers, the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) has made interactive question-answering (QA) a feasible paradigm for visual exploration; yet little is known about how scientists use visual QA in practice or how to improve its accessibility. In this work, we interview five BLV and five sighted scientists across different STEM fields to understand how the

title: Scale-aware and spatially-localised optimisation of kilometre-scale MLWP models
abstract: Preserving fine-scale structure without degrading spatial accuracy is a central challenge for kilometre-scale machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP). We introduce a loss based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform that constrains atmospheric fields jointly by scale, location, and orientation. We evaluate its performance using an experimental joint global--regional FastNet configuration, which produces \SI{1.5}{km} forecasts over the UK alongside $\sim$\SI{31}{km} global forecasts. Relative to both mean-squared error (MSE) and an FFT-based spectral objective, the wavelet loss substanti

title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
abstract: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information.

title: Satellite Intelligence: Distributed Training, Collaborative Inference,and LLM Adaptation in LEO Constellation
abstract: The proliferation of orbital sensing data and the real-time demands of emerging global services are pushing low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks from bent-pipe relays toward intelligent onboard processing. This shift confronts a fundamental tension, where modern artificial intelligence (AI) training paradigms require intensive computation, abundant memory, and stable connectivity, all of which are scarce under the dynamic topologies, intermittent links, and severe size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints of satellite networks. Addressing this tension demands rethinking AI workflows, from
institutions: Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust

title: Recursive moment updates for scalable Bayesian nonparametric regression
abstract: Bayesian nonparametric regression methods have wide applications in statistics and machine learning, but inference can often be expensive or require approximations. This paper introduces a class of recursive moment function updates which are closed form, interpretable, expedient, and fully quantify Bayesian uncertainty through the martingale posterior. title: Exploring perceptual straightness in learned visual representations
abstract: Humans have been shown to use a "straightened" encoding to represent the natural visual world as it evolves in time (Hénaff et al. 2019). In the context of discrete video sequences, "straightened" means that changes between frames follow a more linear path in representation space at progressively deeper levels of processing. While deep convolutional networks are often proposed as models of human visual processing, many do not straighten natural videos. In this paper, we explore the relationship between network architecture, differing types of robustness, biologically-inspired filtering mechani
institutions: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: A Physically-Motivated Stochastic Model of Tropical Cyclone Dynamic Wind Fields
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) pose significant risk to infrastructure and human safety, and the frequency and intensity of large TCs are expected to increase in the future. Quantifying such risk to coastal and inland regions is challenging, largely due to the rare nature of TCs which limits historical data availability. We introduce a new stochastic model of TC wind fields conditional on a small number of physical variables commonly found in synthetic and observed storm track databases. The model consists of a physically-motivated mean trend and an expansion of the residual field into a wavelet fram

title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope
abstract: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference. Because the suspension scatters light far outside the 1.3\textdegree{} field of view, turbidity mainly removes contrast, 4.4- to 4.8-fold on a Siemens star. Rest
institutions: Naval Research Laboratory Remote Sensing Division

title: Tunable Spatial Task Allocation with Application to Maritime Swarms
abstract: In this chapter, we explore how a team of autonomous agents can flexibly reconfigure the distribution of its members across many spatially embedded tasks using a task allocation strategy grounded in a generalization of the recently proposed Nonlinear Opinion Dynamics model. Motivated by an adaptive maritime survey application, we couple opinion dynamics directly to spatial movement and examine how the emergent macroscopic allocation is shaped by the interplay between environmental geometry, nature of social interactions, and task demands. We illustrate in simulation how social coupling in the

title: A neural accelerated roughness-resolved Discrete Element Method (Rough-DEM) for modeling granular systems
abstract: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, te

title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
abstract: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-

title: Water at the molecular frontier
abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinem
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure

title: Search for Ultra-Relativistic Magnetic Monopoles with LHAASO-KM2A
abstract: Ultra-relativistic magnetic monopoles traversing the atmosphere are expected to initiate extensive air showers characterized by a muon deficit and a compact lateral profile. Using 1438.81 live days of data from the LHAASO-KM2A array, we present a search for these cosmic particles within the Lorentz factor range of $10^5$ to $10^7$. A machine-learning classifier utilizing lateral shower shape observables from the electromagnetic detectors is deployed to separate the signal from the hadronic background. No statistical excess above the background expectation is observed, and upper limits at the 9

title: Submerged Immiscible Oil Jet: Breakup Dynamics and Droplet Size Modelling
abstract: Immiscible liquid-liquid jets occur in numerous industrial and environmental settings, including oil spill response and liquid-liquid extraction, yet the coupled evolution of turbulence, interfacial instability, and droplet size distribution across transitional to turbulent regimes remains poorly understood. We present a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a silicone oil jet injected into refractive-index-matched sugar water, employing simultaneous Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and Planar Laser-Induced Fluorescence (PLIF). Beyond the breakup region, mean velocity and Reyn

title: FSVL: Taxonomic Fast-Slow Vision-to-Language Collaborative Framework for Interpretable Confusable Fish Species Identification and Knowledge Generation in the Middle Yangtze River
abstract: The Yangtze River Basin is a critical region for freshwater biodiversity conservation. The implementation of the Yangtze River Ten-Year Fishing Ban has increased the importance of effective aquatic biodiversity monitoring and species-level identification. However, fine-grained identification of closely related freshwater fish species remains challenging due to subtle morphological differences. Existing deep learning methods often struggle to balance classification accuracy and inference efficiency, while LLMs may generate unsupported information when producing specialized biological knowledge.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning
abstract: Every neural-network training run produces not only a model, but also evidence about how models learn. Can these accumulated experiments enable us to predict and compare new training runs before executing them? We study meta-models: models that predict the learning behavior of other models. From this perspective, final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection are different queries to the same training response function. title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
abstract: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $θ\in(0,π)$ is a long-standing open problem, with renewed interest from the recent observations of fractional Chern insulators. In this work we construct variational wavefunctions that build in the exact anyon statistics and combine theory-guided composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton wavefunctions with neural-network correlations on the sphere. title: EvoBench: An Evolving, Diagnostic Benchmark Framework for Environmental Modeling
abstract: Machine learning models are now widely used to predict environmental variable dynamics in domains like hydrology, climate science, agriculture, and ecology. These models are usually compared on fixed benchmark datasets using a single average accuracy score. As models improve, their scores become very close when averaged over large regions and long time periods, so the benchmark can no longer tell them apart, and a single number hides \emph{where} and \emph{when} a model fails. institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: EEGBiFormer: Real-Time EEG Attention Classification via Hybrid CNN-Transformer with EEG-Informed Auditory Protocol Validation
abstract: Sustained attention is critical for academic performance, yet existing auditory support tools are static and not grounded in real-time neural evidence. This paper presents EEGBiFormer, a hybrid CNN-Transformer model for realtime binary classification of attention states, focus versus nonfocus, from 16-channel EEG signals. A custom analog front-end acquisition board was designed and built to collect a task-based EEG dataset. title: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Network for Single-Shot 3D Reconstruction from Fringe Patterns
abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. title: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh: GPU-Native Meshes and Simulation Cases for Physics AI
abstract: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh is the mesh module of the open-source PhysicsNeMo library. It provides mesh processing similar to PyVista, but on the GPU, in batches, and inside PyTorch's automatic differentiation. Like xarray for unstructured meshes, it attaches semantics to data: fields on points, cells, and whole meshes have names and shapes, and a simulation case keeps the complete PDE problem specification, including boundary conditions and their prescribed values. title: Extraction of transverse-momentum-dependent helicity distributions of the nucleon
abstract: We present an updated global analysis of the transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) helicity distributions of the nucleon from measurements of the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry $A_{LL}$ in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS). The analysis incorporates target- and detected-hadron-mass corrections, next-to-next-to-leading-order matching in the small-$b_T$ operator product expansion, and an improved treatment of correlated systematic uncertainties. title: TOWARDS PRECISION-CONTROLLED PARTONIC STRUCTURES FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES
abstract: The internal structure of hadrons is governed by nonperturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and is being probed with increasing precision by modern high-energy experiments. This dissertation presents first-principles calculations of partonic observables using lattice QCD together with effective field theory methods, with controlled systematic uncertainties, advancing from collinear structure to transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) that encode the three-dimensional partonic structure of hadrons.
