title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona
abstract: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific response

title: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment
abstract: An image's original dimensions, aspect ratio, and composition provide important cues that can affect its technical and aesthetic quality. Image assessment methods use resizing, cropping, padding, or patch sampling to accommodate different input sizes. However, these operations can alter or obscure original geometric and compositional cues. Existing assessment models also encode rich multi-level visual evidence that can be further extracted and exploited to improve existing models. title: Towards Quantum Range Query for Spatial-Temporal-Semantic Trajectory Data
abstract: Range query is a fundamental task in geospatial data search and many other downstream applications. Classic range queries often rely on tree-based spatial indexes, of which the query speed depends on the number of indexed points k within the queried range. For instance, a classical B+ tree answers a range query in O(log N + k). For a long time, this speed has long been considered asymptotically optimal in classic database systems, until the recent emergence of quantum computing, where a quantum B+ tree may requires only O(log BN). title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs
abstract: Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. title: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a large language model (LLM) answer questions by retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. However, RAG struggles with multi-hop questions, which require chaining facts spread across several documents through intermediate entities that the question never mentions. Graph-based RAG methods retrieve once from the entities a question names and so rarely recover the full evidence chain. title: The State and Fate of Multilingual, Contextual Evaluation in the NLP World
abstract: Multilingual evaluation benchmarks are the primary instrument for assessing whether large language models generalize beyond English, yet the adequacy of these benchmarks has received little systematic scrutiny. We present a data-driven audit of 51 recent multilingual benchmarks spanning 242 datasets and 219 languages, organized around three pillars: coverage, representativeness, and rigor. Our analysis reveals that coverage is wide but thin with 36% of evaluated languages appearing in only a single benchmark, entire regions (Oceania, the Americas, Central Asia) are near-zero, and a stark task

title: EchoTrace: Diagnosing Recursive Risks in LLM-Powered Recommender Systems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into recommender systems as data augmenters, profile generators, and recommendation modules. While these roles can enhance semantic understanding and recommendation quality, they also introduce LLM-specific risks such as bias and hallucination. These risks become more critical in feedback-loop settings, where LLM-generated signals and recommendations recursively shape future training data and recommendation dynamics. In this paper, we propose a role-aware, phase-wise diagnostic framework for analyzing how LLM-induced risks emerge, propag
institutions: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

title: Cinematize from Unreal: Agentic Choreography for Controllable World Simulation
abstract: Controllable world simulation requires more than visually plausible frames: scenes must retain persistent state, coordinated actions, and editable temporal structure. Generative world models offer flexible visual synthesis, but their outputs do not always expose the objects and transitions needed for precise revision. Graphics engines provide executable state and direct control, yet translating language into valid operations requires specialized knowledge of assets, geometry, and interdependent APIs. We present CineU (Cinematize from Unreal), an agentic system for language-driven world orchest

title: AgenticCity-Bench: Longitudinal Multimodal Observations of Urban Dynamics with Agentic Reasoning
abstract: City systems are shaped by interactions among infrastructure, human activity, and environmental conditions. Existing earth observation and urban benchmarks are limited in unified modeling and in capturing their joint dynamics. We introduce AgenticCity-Bench, a longitudinal multimodal benchmark for multi-layer unified state modeling and agentic city task reasoning. The benchmark covers 16 cities in 12 countries across six continents from 2000 to 2025, and includes 18 modalities spanning urban function, activity, and environmental state. It organizes heterogeneous data sources around a common sp
institutions: Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology

title: The kernel mean embedding of a random probability distribution and its principal components
abstract: Given a random probability distribution \(F\), whose realizations are defined on \(\mathbb R^d\), and a kernel \(k\), our aim is to analyze the properties of the kernel mean embedding, \(μ_F\), of \(F\) as a random element of the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). This establishes a rigorous framework in which kernel statistical techniques for distributional data can be stated both in the sample and population settings and, thus, the asymptotic properties of sample procedures can be properly established. As an illustration of this approach we focus on the principal

title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors
abstract: Prompt optimization should improve the image a user receives without changing the scene the user requested. Yet stylistic rewriting can weaken object attributes and relations even when global text--image similarity remains high. We propose StruPO, a structure-aware prompt editor that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision. The graph exposes what should be preserved, while deletion, reordering, and insertion provide a token-aligned way to modify the prompt. This turns structural feedback from an external critique into a tr

title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
abstract: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear. We ask the reverse question: when an LLM is confident, consistent, and wrong, do users bend towards it? In a within-subjects experiment, 32 participants learned up to five science topics by chatting with five assistants built on the same model (GPT-5-mini). Unknown to participants, each assistant's briefing had 0, 25, 50, 75, or 100% of its facts replaced by plausible falsehoods, and every assistant spoke with full confidence. A surprise quiz after each topic offered the correct fact, t

title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Automatic operator design (AOD) has increasingly adopted large language models (LLMs) to generate problem-specific search and variation operators for multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOCO). Yet most methods evolve the operators while leaving the process that discovers them fixed. This limits adaptation as new Pareto trade-offs and operator interactions change where and how the search should proceed. We introduce HEMO, which makes the AOD harness itself a self-evolving optimization target. HEMO maintains a persistent harness state and updates one module at a time, revising the logic

title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration
abstract: Interactive video world models aim to follow user actions while maintaining scene consistency over extended interactions. History-based methods reuse generated latents to preserve scene content, but three limitations of this reuse contribute to error recirculation. 1) The latent generated at each interaction is retained as history, potentially containing blurred details, geometric distortions, or semantic drift. 2) Although retrieved historical content matches the current scene, it can still contain errors that are carried into the next chunk. 3) New outputs then become history for later inter

title: Repulsive Population Policy Gradients for Behaviorally Diverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The goal of Quality-Diversity Reinforcement Learning (QD-RL) is to find a population of high-performing policies that solve a decision-making problem in diverse ways. Despite recent progress, QD-RL methods predominantly rely on evolutionary operators--including black-box optimizers, mutations, and crossovers--to facilitate exploration and induce diversity. Scaling these methods becomes increasingly costly as policies and behavior spaces grow larger. Building on the Soft QD view of quality-diversity optimization, we introduce \textbf{Re}pulsive \textbf{P}opulation \textbf{P}olicy \textbf{O}ptim

title: Timing Matters Twice: When to Query and When to Skip in Flow-Matching On-Policy Distillation
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) enables flow-matching models to acquire complementary capabilities from specialized teachers through supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, different evaluation dimensions, such as aesthetics and OCR accuracy, and different tasks, such as image generation and editing, emphasize different aspects of the denoising process, suggesting that their effective supervision may occur at different stages. Existing methods typically select supervision states from predefined timestep distributions, which may overlook these phase-dependent differences and incur

title: Steerable Chatbots: Exploring Direct Manipulation Interfaces for LLM Personalization via Activation Steering
abstract: Personalizing LLM responses typically requires users to articulate their preferences through prompting, which can be burdensome at cold start and difficult to articulate in natural language. We introduce an alternative paradigm, steerable chatbots: rather than asking users to describe what they want, let them directly manipulate it via a linear factor. We implement this through activation steering, leveraging a linear scalar to control how strongly a preference is expressed in the LLM’s output. We first assess the computational viability of activation steering as a method to control granular p

title: Facultative Swarming: A Capability, Not a Category, for Multi-Robot Systems
abstract: Collective robotics is split by a long-standing but increasingly artificial boundary between centralised multi-robot systems that prioritise optimality and decentralised swarms that prioritise robustness and adaptivity. We propose a unified control framework, shifting from `obligate' swarms---systems constrained to pure self-organisation---to facultatively swarming systems: hybrid architectures that operate as centrally planned systems under permissive conditions yet degrade gracefully into decentralised swarming under environmental stress. By reframing swarming as a dynamic capability, rather

title: Whale You Go Green? Immediate and Longitudinal Effects of Embodied Conversational AI Avatars on Sustainable Behavioral Tendencies and Pro-Environmental Attitudes
abstract: Embodied conversational AI can be persuasive, but can it motivate people to develop sustainable behavioral tendencies and increase pro-environmental attitudes? We conducted a randomized experiment (N = 576) comparing four embodied avatars--a beluga whale, Greta Thunberg, Emma Watson, and a generic human--with a text chatbot and no-intervention control. All embodied conditions increased immediate sustainable product selection relative to the control (beta = .401-.609, all q <= .0126) and chatbot (beta = .398-.604, all q <= .007), without differing significantly from one another. title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
abstract: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets

title: 3D Occupancy-Language Fields from mmWave Radar
abstract: Radar systems can recover scene geometry and recognize predefined categories, but these outputs do not provide a persistent spatial representation for open-ended language queries. Such queries require linking observations from different viewpoints to the same physical locations. We present TextRadar, a framework that constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic radar observations. The field combines occupancy with scale-dependent language features at surface locations, allowing the reconstructed scene to be queried with new descriptions. A single-frame radar distillation

title: AlphaAnything: Extending Pretrained RGB Generators to RGBA
abstract: Existing RGBA generation methods commonly learn a transparency-specific representation through reconstruction, introducing an additional training stage and potentially altering the RGB decoding function inherited from pretrained models. We present AlphaAnything, a lightweight framework that extends pretrained RGB generators to RGBA directly in their original latent space, without RGBA reconstruction pretraining. AlphaAnything inserts LoRA modules into the generative transformer and attaches an alpha branch to the frozen RGB VAE decoder. Unidirectional RGB-to-alpha feature sharing allows opacit

title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflec
institutions: National Agency for New Technologies, Energy and Sustainable Economic Development

title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make and execute decisions that affect living systems. Yet, to our knowledge, ecological reasoning is not a focus of pre- or post-training. This increases the risk that under operational pressure, they may make decisions to irreversibly destroy living systems. We construct and use a real-data continued-pretraining "coupled welfare" corpus of documented human/biosphere/AI dependency, option value under irreversibility, and recovery from harm. title: What Hallucinations Have We Measured? Semantic Illusion, Confabulation, and Expressed Uncertainty
abstract: Hallucination remains one of the most critical challenges in deploying large language models (LLMs) reliably and safely. Yet the term is used inconsistently across the research community. We argue for a strict definition of hallucinations in LLMs. First, hallucinations should be confident incorrectness, kept separate from expressed uncertainty (UNK)1. UNK reveals that the model may be wrong, whereas a hallucination does not reveal it and is therefore more dangerous in practice. institutions: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-co

title: ConMem: Counterfactual Multi-Scenario Probing for Resolving LLM Memory Misalignment
abstract: Long-term memory is critical for autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents executing multi-session, long-horizon tasks. However, existing memories often inappropriately store, retain, or retrieve over-generalized, misattributed, or privacy-sensitive information, a problem we term memory misalignment. To study this problem, we construct \textbf{MemAlign}, a benchmark comprising 1,079 curated memory cases grounded in synthetic, validated multi-session conversational contexts covering diverse misalignment taxonomies. We then propose ConMem, an algorithm that reframes retention decisions as pro

title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
abstract: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated). IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training,

title: Tracing Subliminal Learning Through Pretraining
abstract: Large language models trained on data generated by other models can sometimes inherit traits unrelated to that data, a phenomenon called subliminal learning. We study both hard label distillation, where students train on numbers generated by a biased teacher, and on-policy soft label distillation, where students generate the data and the teacher's logits provide the learning signal. title: Prototype-Rectified Iterative Self-supervised Manifold Denoising under Severe Acoustic Shift
abstract: Audio-Text Foundation Models (ATMs) fail catastrophically under severe acoustic noise, yet existing adaptation strategies either rely on gradient-based Test-Time Adaptation (TTA), which reinforces noise rather than signal, or on prompt tuning that requires privileged noise annotations unavailable at inference. We address these failures with PRISM (Prototype-Rectified Iterative Self-supervised Manifold Denoising), a training-free, source-free TTA framework grounded in the Affine Noise Hypothesis: severe acoustic noise induces a low-rank affine shift in the multimodal latent space, with more tha
institutions: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
abstract: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream application

title: Assessing the Role of Green Premium and Localized Price Spillovers in Budget Hotels : Evidence from Delhi National Capital Region (NCR)
abstract: Sustainable urban tourism depends on how environmental quality, public transport accessibility, and accommo dation clustering shape visitor mobility and destination development. This study examines these relationships in the budget hotel sector of Delhi National Capital Region, India, an emerging mega-destination marked by rapid urban expansion and uneven infrastructure provision. Using data from 857 budget hotels, we estimate a mixed geographically weighted spatial autoregressive model that captures both spatial heterogeneity and localized price spillovers. The model combines hotel attributes

title: Bezier-Guided Adaptive Flow for Cross-domain Sequential Recommendation
abstract: Cross-domain sequential recommendation aims to alleviate data sparsity and cold-start problems by transferring useful preference knowledge across domains. However, users exhibit varying degrees of preference consistency across domains, while existing methods often rely on global alignment objectives or coarse-grained transfer strategies. Such approaches may introduce irrelevant information and provide limited flexibility in adapting semantic representations to individual user preferences. To address these challenges, we propose BGAFlow, a personalized framework that combines state-adaptive sem

title: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: An Automated Workflow for Power Electronics Schematic Synthesis
abstract: Designing power electronics converters traditionally requires intensive human expertise across topology sizing, commercial component selection, circuit simulation verification, and schematic drafting. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in electronic design automation (EDA), applying standalone LLMs directly to board-level power electronics schematic synthesis suffers from severe engineering hallucinations, including inaccurate analytical sizing, fabricated or mismatched component part numbers, violated voltage derating margins, and broken topological connectivity. In this paper, w
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, togethe

title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
abstract: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. title: Disentangling Robustness and Sycophancy in Multilingual LLMs
abstract: When a multilingual LLM agrees with a user's false premise, is it being sycophantic, or does it simply not know better in that language? Current research does not distinguish these cases: they record only whether the model agreed, not why. We introduce the SC-matrix, that crosses a model's competence (whether it answers correctly under no pressure) with its sycophancy (whether it maintains that answer under pressure). title: ROAD: Modern Adversarial Training for Simple One-Step Distillation at Scale
abstract: One-step distillation turns pretrained diffusion models into fast generators, but strong results often require substantial training machinery and compute. Pure adversarial distillation offers a simpler route, yet has struggled at modern text-to-image scale. To address this limitation, we propose ROAD (Representation-grounded One-step Adversarial Distillation), a one-stage framework that distills text-to-image models with one adversarial objective and a lightweight representation-space critic. title: NaturalEdit: Code Modification through Direct Interaction with Adaptive Natural Language Representation
abstract: Code modification requires developers to comprehend code, plan changes, articulate intent, and validate outcomes, making it cognitively demanding. While natural language (NL) code summaries offer a promising external representation of this process, existing approaches remain limited. Systems grounded in exploratory data analysis are restricted to narrow domains, while general-purpose systems enforce fixed NL representations and assume that developers can directly translate vague intent into precise textual edits. We present NaturalEdit, which treats code summaries as interactive representation

title: Last-Iterate Convergence for Constrained MDPs: From Dual Descent to Primal-Dual
abstract: We study policy optimization for infinite-horizon, discounted constrained Markov decision processes. While primal-dual ($\texttt{PD}$) methods are widely used in practice, their theoretical guarantees typically hold for an impractical mixture policy. In contrast, dual descent ($\texttt{DD}$) methods output a single policy ("last iterate") with guarantees on its performance. However, such methods require iteratively solving entropy-regularized MDPs in an inner-loop, limiting their practical effectiveness. title: The As-If Machine: Personalized counterfactuals make distant policy risks feel close
abstract: Life experiences can shape policy attitudes, but we only live one life. Citizens may therefore fail to support policies addressing risks they have never personally experienced. Narratives can make such risks immediate and personal, but personalized stories remain difficult to produce at scale. Here we ask whether AI can make distant scenarios feel concrete by simulating a participant's life as if that scenario occurred. title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly
abstract: Apple Vision Pro (AVP), the headset Apple introduced as its first ``spatial computer,'' built by a single, vertically integrated vendor, entered the market in February 2024 and has since accumulated a fast-growing body of primary research spanning surgery, education, accessibility, design, and human-computer interaction. In this paper, we adopt the tripartite structure of Leone's 1966 film to organize a systematic review of this literature: we cataloged the validated, working applications of AVP (the good), the persistent technical and ergonomic limitations of a still-early-generation headset

title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to estimate conditional expected outcomes and average treatment effects for specific groups of individuals. Using these estimates to guide scientific decisions requires reliable uncertainty quantification. The challenge is to account simultaneously for two sources of uncertainty: limited-context bias and context variation arising from the small labeled sample supplied at inference. title: FIDE: Fiber-Informed Differentiable Experimental Design for Reference-Relative Law Dynamics
abstract: Aggregate measurements generally leave an evolving population law underdetermined, so different measurement systems can be equally adequate for a scientific task while constraining different aspects of the law. We study how to resolve this residual design freedom in baseline-preserving settings, where an existing dynamical model remains the working baseline outside quantities explicitly valued by the task. \textbf{F}iber-\textbf{I}nformed \textbf{D}ifferentiable \textbf{E}xperimental Design (\textbf{FIDE}) completes each candidate's aggregate constraints by information projection relative to a

title: Direct Forcing: Single-Stage Training with Representation-Space Supervision for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generation enables low-latency streaming, yet prevailing training pipelines separate causal adaptation from distribution matching. Recent representation-based text-to-video methods retain this separation by starting with an ODE initialization stage, even when the target distribution is defined directly by reference videos. We introduce \method, the first single-stage framework that uses reference videos both as paired examples of how a history continues and as a target population for self-generated rollouts. title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. institutions: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: AgenticEvolve: Evolutionary Program Search with Persistent Language Model Agents that Design and Run Experiments
abstract: Evolutionary program search with large language models keeps the structure of an evolutionary algorithm and uses the model as its variation operator. Typically, the model generates each candidate program in a single request from parent programs and their scores. We present AgenticEvolve, an evolutionary program search framework in which each island is run by a persistent large language model agent. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
abstract: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
abstract: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_τf)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+τ})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
abstract: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. title: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization
abstract: Collegiate running in the United States generates thousands of race results annually in cross country and track and field, yet no large-scale dataset has been publicly available for research. Existing websites such as Athletic.net, MileSplit, and TFRRS host results but do not support bulk download, restricting prior analyses to ~500 performances, often skewing studies toward male athletes. institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

title: WebViSE: Scaling Visual Design Intelligence from the Open Web for LLM Website Generation
abstract: Large language models have made remarkable strides in website development, enabling complete and interactive web experiences to be built from natural-language instructions with far less effort. Yet, non-expert users often struggle to articulate sophisticated visual and interaction designs in natural language. Meanwhile, the open web already contains a vast reservoir of such design knowledge, embodied in mature website implementations. title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts
abstract: Wind farm layout optimization becomes increasingly difficult as turbine count grows, especially when high-fidelity aerodynamic models are used. Conventional Kriging-based Bayesian optimization often suffers from low sample efficiency in high-dimensional layout spaces because sparse training data provide limited domain coverage. We develop a Graph-informed Kriging framework that embeds reusable aerodynamic interaction information into the surrogate mean function. title: Assessing Attack Surfaces in Generative Search Engines through Publisher Attributes: A Case Study in Political Domains
abstract: We characterize the attack surface of generative search engines (GSEs) against poisoning attacks in the political domain, from the perspectives of citation selection and personalization. GSEs integrate web search and answer generation with user preferences and backgrounds using large language models (LLMs). They play a crucial role in how users access information on the web. Because anyone can publish content on the web, GSEs are vulnerable to poisoning attacks that manipulate citations to undermine reliable information delivery. title: Pareto Processes for Threshold Exceedances in Spatial Extremes
abstract: Outline : The previous chapter introduced the GEV model for spatial extremes; here, we turn to Pareto processes for modeling threshold exceedances. While exceedances are easy to define in a single location, the challenge now is figuring out what “exceeding a threshold” means across space.

title: Training-Free LLM-Based Recommendation with Post-LLM Item Refinement Using Collaborative Signals
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for training-free recommendation, but LLM-generated user interests are often too broad for fine-grained item retrieval. Existing methods incorporate collaborative filtering (CF) signals in a pre-LLM manner through candidate reranking or prompt augmentation, yielding limited gains. We propose CoRRe, a training-free recommendation framework with a post-LLM paradigm that injects CF signals into LLM-generated item representations, which are later matched with LLM-generated user interests for ranking. institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: Physics-Informed and Data-Driven Composite Disturbance Separation and Predictive Control for Airborne Electro-Optical Gimbals with Multiple Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the constrained pointing control problem of airborne electro-optical gimbals subjected to composite periodic and aperiodic disturbances. Under carrier vibration, input delay, and actuator constraints, achieving line-of-sight stabilization and tracking is challenging. A disturbance-separated model predictive control (MPC) scheme is proposed to compensate these heterogeneous disturbances according to their physical characteristics. title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
abstract: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. title: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations
abstract: Accurate regression need not yield the correct equation after support selection. For a median/sample-standard-deviation threshold in neural PDE discovery, we derive an exact two-signal retention boundary and a complete-vector perturbation bound. title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
abstract: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. Early subject-to-video (S2V) methods condition on a single reference image and must therefore infer the subject's unseen appearance and geometry as the viewpoint changes. To address this limitation, recent methods extend S2V to multiple reference views, providing more information about the subject from different viewpoints. title: OlmoEarth v1.3: Embeddings
abstract: We make some OlmoEarth embeddings. To do this, we train a new model: OlmoEarth v1.3. OlmoEarth v1.3 is designed to condense multimodal, multitemporal remote sensing data into a single digestible 64 or 128-dimensional vector. OlmoEarth v1.3 produces state-of-the-art embeddings. In addition, OlmoEarth v1.3 is a strong encoder backbone -- competitive with OlmoEarth v1 and v1.2 -- while requiring 18% and 53% of the GPU hours to train, respectively. We use OlmoEarth v1.3 to compute global, annualized 10m embeddings, which we release under the OlmoEarth artifact license.

title: ADEPTS: An auto-differentiable framework for time-dependent nonlinear thermo-chemical mantle convection inversion
abstract: Abstract. Time-dependent mantle-dynamics inversion must simultaneously address the high dimensionality of the initial state, nonlinear rheology, and the complex propagation of gradients through long-term thermo-mechanical evolution. Here, we develop a geodynamic inversion framework ADEPTS based on a two-dimensional staggered-grid finite-difference discretization and automatic differentiation, with the aim of jointly constraining the initial temperature field and mantle material properties. The forward model solves the incompressible Stokes equations, the temperature advection–diffusion equatio
institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

title: Causality and Extremes
abstract: Outline : Understanding cause-and-effect relationships in extreme events is crucial across many applied fields. This chapter introduces key causal models, explores methods for learning causal structures, and demonstrates their application using real data from the Seine River network.

title: Toward Open ISA Supercomputing: A Comparative Study of RISC-V, Arm, and x86 Architectures on HPC Workloads
abstract: RISC-V is emerging as a candidate architecture for high-performance computing (HPC), but its competitiveness against established x86 and Arm processors remains difficult to assess because existing studies use different platforms, workloads, and methodologies, and rarely consider energy efficiency. Our work provides an evaluation of contemporary HPC RISC-V, Arm, and x86 processors using a common software stack and methodology. We characterize the Sophgo SG2044 and compare it with the NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip and Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ across four HPC benchmarks (STREAM, HPL, HPL-MxP, and H

title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
abstract: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. Despite numerous prior works on ground robots, aerial robots with high agility and constrained sensor suites face more significant localization drift and thereby demand dedicated active SLAM planning. Moreover, a unified strate
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: DeCoRL: Decomposed Consistency Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Image Composition
abstract: Multi-image composition (MICo) is a critical yet challenging capability for large-scale image editing models, where consistency degrades rapidly as the number of reference images increases. While supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can equip models with basic MICo ability, it provides only implicit supervision on the composed image and often fails to learn reliable object-level correspondence across multiple references. We propose DeCoRL, a reinforcement-learning (RL) framework that improves MICo consistency by decomposing holistic MICo consistency into object-level consistency. DeCoRL first establis

title: Lost in Translation: Investigating Systematic Discrepancies between Parallel English and Chinese Names of American Chinese Restaurants
abstract: Given that the Chinese are one of the oldest ethnic groups to immigrate to the US, their cuisine have become central to the US dining scene and an interesting avenue to study how Chinese immigrants have culturally adapted into American life. In that regard, previous research has focused on analyzing the English names that Chinese restaurants adopt, e.g., finding the use of familiar and typical words. To investigate how Chinese immigrants have culturally integrated in the US depending on social, geographic and demographic contexts, we investigate in this work the under-explored relationship bet

title: ClinVerse: A Realistic Multi-Agent Diagnostic Environment for Training and Evaluating Medical Agents
abstract: Disease diagnosis is a key application of large language model (LLM) agents in healthcare. However, existing medical agents are primarily trained and evaluated with static question-answering data, providing limited opportunities to learn active information acquisition, examination decision-making, and dynamic clinical interaction. To address this limitation, we present ClinVerse, an interactive, real-data-grounded multi-agent environment designed for training and evaluating medical diagnostic agents. Built on ClinPatient, a scalable dataset comprising 150k diagnostic cases derived from real-wo
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Category-Anchored Large Language Models for Next POI Recommendation
abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict a user's next destination from spatio-temporal check-in data, and serves as the foundation for many location-based services. Recent advances incorporate large language models (LLMs) into this task by textualizing user trajectories to exploit their semantic reasoning ability. However, directly generating POI identifiers with such models is unreliable: POIs are sparse, localized, and long-tailed entities with weak natural-language semantics, which creates a semantic-to-entity gap between high-level mobility intent and concrete POI predi

title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
abstract: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic. FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training,

title: DiffAuction: An Auction-Driven Framework for Generative Image Advertising
abstract: Diffusion models enable multiple advertisers to compete for exposure within a shared generated image. Yet existing approaches are computationally costly when generating images under varying target-share configurations, and it remains unclear how the resulting outcomes should be evaluated and priced. To address these gaps, we propose DiffAuction, a framework integrating controllable generation, click-intent evaluation, and auction design. First, our training-free Residual Share Calibration (RSC) decomposes joint-attention updates into product-specific residuals and rescales them according to ta

title: Self-thresholding angular-radial models of extremal dependence
abstract: Assessing compound risks requires a model for routine and extreme joint behaviour together, and a principled answer to where the joint tail begins. We propose the self-thresholding angular-radial (STAR) model: after marginal standardization, the radius given the angle follows a spliced distribution, with a flexible body below an angle-dependent threshold curve and a generalized Pareto tail above it. institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

title: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations
abstract: As multi-agent language model networks become widely deployed, predicting their collective behavior is a critical challenge. Classical distributed consensus theory relies on network topology to predict convergence, structurally assuming that agent updates are convex combinations, population means are conserved, and weights are content-independent. In this work, we demonstrate that these foundational assumptions fail for large language models (LLMs). title: ShadAR: Real-time Prompting On-demand Visual Augmentation in Augmented Reality
abstract: Augmented Reality can reshape our visual perception (e.g., simulating color blindness) yet such effects are typically pre-programmed by experts, making visual augmentation static and inflexible. We introduce ShadAR, an AR system that allows users to describe expected visual augmentations (e.g., "Blur all people") for changing their vision in real time. ShadAR can graphically manipulate AR passthrough real-time via shader injection. When receiving a user’s prompt, ShadAR uses LLMs (GPT5.2) to interpret the user’s intent, analyzes the user’s view with object detection (YOLOv26), generates a pixe

title: Cross-Spectral Feature Fusion for Multispectral Document Binarization
abstract: Historical document binarization remains challenging when faded ink, bleed-through, and background degradation exhibit wavelength-dependent behavior across visible and near-infrared observations. This study investigates whether adaptive cross-spectral feature fusion and targeted structural guidance can improve multispectral document binarization beyond fixed fusion and generic attention mechanisms. Four registered SMADI bands at 500, 600, 700, and 1000 nm are processed using a multi-branch conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). Visible, NIR, and structural feature streams are fused

title: Principal Component Analysis for Multivariate Extremes
abstract: Outline: While previous chapters focused on modeling multivariate extremes, we now turn to dimension reduction methods. This chapter explores ways to reduce the dimensionality of the data while preserving key information relevant to the analysis of multivariate extreme values.

title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints
abstract: This paper studies UAV path planning in areas where GPS signals are not present. Because these drones can easily get lost when they don't have GPS, they must rely on dead reckoning and occasionally pass near cellular towers, which act as landmarks to reset and fix their position. The goal is to find the shortest path from a start to a goal location while keeping the estimation uncertainty within a given bound. institutions: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

title: MAGIC: Margin-gated Contrastive Debiasing with Evidence Restoration for VLM Test-time Robustness Scaling
abstract: This paper studies the problem of test-time robustness scaling for large vision-language models (LVLMs), which aims to mitigate language bias during inference. Existing approaches typically adopt test-time scaling techniques such as contrastive decoding to improve inference performance. Despite the progress, the performance of these approaches is far from satisfactory due to intentional evidence removal during perturbations and redundant inference cost. institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

title: Mix Forcing: Causal Pre-Training via Mixture Attention for Interactive World Models
abstract: While interactive video world models require autoregressive generation, directly adapting pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into autoregressive ones with teacher forcing can disrupt their visual priors and degrade autoregressive generation quality. In this paper, we introduce Mix Forcing, a causal pre-training paradigm for interactive video world models, implemented with the Mixture-of-Bidirectional-and-Autoregressive (MoBA) attention. institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
abstract: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. Inspired by sensorimotor control, our mechanics-grounded two-layer framework inferred object-driving and grip-stabilizing c
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Effect-Size Estimation and Confounding-Aware Permutations for PERMANOVA
abstract: Motivation: PERMANOVA is widely used to test associations between covariates and high-dimensional data with arbitrary distributions, such as ecology, metabolomics, or microbial community profiling. In these contexts, its effect size measure (R2) is generally used to indicate how much the high-dimensional measurement covaries with respect to a separate, univariate measure. However, as we show, this conventional effect size is inflated under the null, resulting in values that do not accurately reflect the conventional expectation of "variance explained." title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use
abstract: Large language models operationalize an intuitive, view of meaning as use. We argue that it faces a rule-following challenge. Using Kripke's interpretation of Wittgenstein, we argue that finite histories of use do not determine a unique rule for future extension. This reframes the debate about OOD generalization but also about NLP evaluation; benchmarks that measure performance on fixed use cases or local robustness, we argue, do not by themselves establish semantic competence. To evaluate whether models preserve rules and concepts under principled domain extension, we propose to evaluate two

title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive

title: From Gaze to Guidance: Interpreting and Adapting to Users’ Cognitive Needs with Multimodal Gaze-Aware AI Assistants
abstract: Current LLM assistants are powerful at answering questions, but they have limited access to the behavioral context that reveals when and where a user is struggling. We present a gaze-grounded multimodal LLM assistant that uses egocentric video with gaze overlays to identify likely points of difficulty and target follow-up retrospective assistance. We instantiate this vision in a controlled study (n=36) comparing the gaze-aware AI assistant to a text-only LLM assistant. The gaze-aware assistant was rated as more accurate and personalized in its assessments of users’ reading behavior, and users

title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
abstract: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) conjectures that they do as they scale, but without a proof it offers neither a guarantee nor a recipe. We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. title: Collascope: Supporting Serendipitous Asset Exploration for Collage-Based Storytelling
abstract: Collage-based storytelling requires visual elements that support emerging narratives and inspire creative reinterpretation. Existing tools, however, rely largely on keyword- and image-based retrieval, offering limited support for serendipitous exploration beyond existing assets. We introduce Collascope, an interactive system that helps creators (1) concretize story intent with interactive element groups, (2) expand the exploration space based on concepts or cutouts towards conceptual and visual dimensions, and (3) develop grounded, traceable ideas in parallel with collage composition. institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

title: SimTO-Robust: Automated Design of Soft Grippers Robust to Grasp Pose and Object Geometry
abstract: Robotic grippers operating in unstructured environments must robustly grasp objects of different shapes and sizes despite perception and positioning errors. Soft grippers that can achieve this robustness through intelligent mechanical design rather than sophisticated control software offer a promising solution. However, no existing computational design framework explicitly optimises soft gripper morphology for robustness across object geometries and grasp poses. institutions: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

title: Agentic Hazard Mapper: Emulating Expert Map-Making with AI Agents for Risk Communication
abstract: Hazard maps are essential tools for public risk communication, preparedness, and evacuation planning, yet effective cartographic design is not always ensured due to limited access to cartographic expertise across local governments and communities. We present Agentic Hazard Mapper, a multi-agent system that automates hazard-map production by emulating professional cartographic workflows and iterative design trade-offs while adapting design decisions to different data, locations, and hazard contexts. We conducted a formative study with map experts to inform the system design, followed by a user

title: Estimation and Inference for One-pass Streaming Function-on-Function Regression
abstract: In many applications, functional pairs are collected sequentially from a data stream. Existing function-on-function regression methods are primarily designed for batch data, and bootstrap inference has become one of the most popular approaches. However, this procedure may be infeasible when observations cannot be stored. In this paper, we propose a one-pass functional SGD estimator that updates upon each observation's arrival without data storage, and a weighted rolling validation rule is provided for step size selection for implementation. Further, an online multiplier bootstrap is developed
institutions: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. institutions: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

title: What's Old Is New: Improved Learning from Small-Group Tutorials
abstract: The ubiquity of Large Language Models poses a challenge to student learning in homework-based college courses, where access to easy homework answers devalues the intended productive struggle. To address this concern, we propose Oxbridge-style weekly tutorials, where students present homework problems without notes in a small group with an instructor or TA. We conducted a randomized experiment in an introductory probability class to evaluate the effectiveness of tutorials, finding a significant positive effect of tutorial enrollment on exam grades. We discuss the implementation, challenges, and

title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts
abstract: Learning an unfamiliar visual category requires more than adapting a classifier: the model must connect its visual evidence to a useful semantic name. A pre-trained vision-language model can retain discriminative image features while providing a weak textual anchor for the target concept. We address this imbalance through context-grounded semantic anchoring. Our framework, SynerNet, learns concept-specific name embeddings, exposes them to compatible linguistic contexts, and conditions their representations on visual evidence. title: Mean estimation in spatial functional data
abstract: Functional mean estimation exhibits a sparse-to-dense phase transition as the number of measurements per curve increases. For spatially indexed functional data, however, dependence between nearby curves and increasing spatial sampling density fundamentally alter this transition. We investigate this phenomenon under a unified framework allowing both increasing-domain and infill asymptotics, with irregular temporal observations. Our analysis identifies two distinct sources of estimation error: an observation-level component governed by the total number of measurements and a curve-level component
institutions: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

title: Detecting Fine-Grained Differences between Image Datasets
abstract: Detecting whether and in particular how two data distributions differ is a fundamental statistical problem. For example, we might be interested in which concepts (expressed in natural language) differ between two classes, the outputs of different generative models, or the same model with different prompt specifications. When working with large and complex image datasets, we intuitively think that first selecting concepts from a broad list using fine-grained patch embeddings, and then optimizing the concepts to better fit the data is an effective workflow. However, prior work instead uses MLLMs

title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
abstract: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. Reaction wheels generally have higher size, weight and power as well as cost, compared with magnetorquers, but have performance advantages. We consider a hybrid system relying on a single reaction wheel and three magnetorquers, using a trajectory planning control method that focuses on meeting pointing goals and minimizing the need to desaturate the reaction wheel. title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
abstract: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video data

title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
abstract: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. title: Lychee: Certified Screening of Inverted Lists for High-Recall Vector Search
abstract: Nearest-neighbor search over embedding vectors matches faces against watchlists, transactions against known fraud patterns, and medical images against confirmed cases, where a missed neighbor is a missed threat, fraud, or diagnosis. Because an approximate index cannot report which queries lost a true neighbor, these applications require recall of 0.999 to 0.9999, at a cost far below that of exact search over billions of vectors. title: Inverse scattering problem for the fifth-order Schr${\rm\bf\ddot{o}}$dinger operator on the whole axis
abstract: A method of solution for the inverse scattering problem for the linear fifth order Schr${\rm\ddot{o}}$dinger operator is found. Two closed systems of linear singular integral equations are obtained. From solutions to these equations, potential on the left and right half-axes is restored unambiguously.

B. Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

title: Inertial Steering and Motion Prediction of Tracked Vehicles on Low-Adherence Surfaces
abstract: Tracked vehicles are widely used in off-road applications, but their conventional motion models often rely on no-slip assumptions that become inaccurate on low-adherence surfaces. Rather than treating inertial effects arising from slip as a disturbance to be minimized, this work investigates how inertial effects arising from a moving mass can be deliberately exploited for steering on low-friction surfaces. A dynamic model for an articulated tracked vehicle with a passive trailer is developed, allowing inertial effects from trailer motion to be captured. The approach is experimentally evaluated
institutions: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process. We therefore ask whether ordinary reasoning failures and adversarially induced failures can be characterized using the same internal coordinates. Towards this end, we in this paper study a white-box diagnostic framework CauTrace to disclose the root-cause of why LLM fails from three fundamental inspections: Functional States, Propagation of Representation, Temporal-State Coordination and Reasoning Trajectory. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
abstract: Repository-level coding benchmarks largely assume that tasks and environments remain unchanged throughout execution. In software development, code, dependencies, runtime state, and requirements can change while an agent is still working. We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents under such mid-execution changes. From the same saved history and workspace, a Clean continuation proceeds without intervention, while a matched Shifted continuation receives a task-relevant update. title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions
abstract: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). title: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination
abstract: Hallucination detection is critical for deploying large language models (LLMs) in real-world applications. Due to strong empirical performance, internal representation-based methods have emerged as the prevailing direction for detecting hallucinations, yet they remain largely model-specific and often fail to generalize to unseen LLMs. In this paper, we study an important yet underexplored problem, termed cross-model hallucination detection (CMHD), which aims to train hallucination detectors on source LLMs while ensuring performance on unseen target LLMs. The core challenge of CMHD lies in cros

title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). title: PolyUQuest: Verifiable Structure-Aware Web RAG over Heterogeneous Graphs
abstract: Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems treat web pages as flat text, losing the structural and semantic signals encoded in HTML. We present PolyUQuest, a verifiable, structure-aware web RAG framework built on a heterogeneous graph that unifies hyperlink topology between pages, DOM hierarchy within pages, and entity-relation knowledge across pages. A two-tier router dispatches each query to one of three retrieval modes matched to its structural need, including direct block retrieval, cross-page graph traversal, and multi-hop entity reasoning. title: Improving Precision in Cluster-Level Pricing Experiments with Temporal Switchbacks
abstract: Online pricing systems often cannot randomize treatments at the user level because prices are deployed over operational units such as routes, regions, or markets. This creates low-powered A/B tests due to persistent cluster heterogeneity, seasonality, and autocorrelated demand. We study temporal switchback designs for cluster-level pricing experiments, where each cluster alternates between treatment and control over time. Using LATAM Airlines ancillary-pricing data and calibrated simulations, we show that switchbacks can substantially reduce standard errors relative to parallel cluster designs

title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. title: Music of the Deep: An acoustic blueprint of sperm whale codas
abstract: Sperm-whale codas are usually described by the number and timing of their clicks. Earlier acoustic studies showed that individual clicks and longer coda sequences contain additional organization. We ask how that organization compares with music, whose smaller sounds also form larger units and ordered sequences. We compare codas with performed violin music, drum grooves, and sung melodies. title: Less Is More: Balancing Positive and Negative Space in Visual Concept Blending
abstract: Graphic designers often blend visual concepts to communicate multiple ideas within a single image, leveraging positive and negative space to create balance, emphasis, and aesthetic appeal. While computational methods have begun to support automatic concept blending, they largely overlook the role of spatial composition in the design. To address this gap, we present an automatic pipeline that explicitly applies positive and negative space throughout the blending process. title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
abstract: Engineers who audit a declared specification of an engineered system need to know which physical constraints it respects, which it violates, which field was altered and how to correct it. NeSySpec is an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic audit framework, built on Logic Tensor Networks, that answers these questions in one pipeline. title: Persistent Geospatial Outage Scenario Construction for Interdependent Infrastructure Simulation
abstract: Extreme weather events are producing persistent geographic patterns of power-grid disruption across the United States, yet these patterns are rarely incorporated into geospatial simulation of interdependent infrastructure failures. This paper presents a data-driven geospatial simulation framework that transforms persistent outage patterns into empirically grounded regional simulation scenarios for interdependent power-communication cascade simulation. title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200–600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. title: Mostly Reading: What Open-Book Scores Measure in Document-Level LoRA Adapters
abstract: Single-document LoRA adapters have been proposed as units of knowledge to be merged and retrieved; yet open-book scoring, with the document in the prompt, can credit a document's own adapter (its specialist) for reading that document as readily as for holding it. Training one adapter for each of 150 Wikipedia articles on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, we find that open-book scores mostly measure a reading behaviour every adapter shares: a random adapter trained on another document recovers 82 % of the specialist's open-book advantage over the base model but only 2 % of its advantage on a cloze probe t

title: Virtual Placebo: a scoping review of control conditions in randomized controlled trials of psychological immersive virtual reality interventions
abstract: Research on immersive virtual reality (IVR) as a therapeutic tool is growing rapidly, with randomized controlled trials (RCTs) now commonplace. Yet the control conditions in many of these studies that claim strong specific IVR effects vary from usual care to active immersive experiences, making it difficult to draw clinically meaningful conclusions. We conducted a scoping review of recent literature on psychological IVR interventions to assess the main forms of control conditions used and their relations to study outcomes. title: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
abstract: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. title: PageLLM: A Multi-Grained Reward Framework for Whole-Page Optimization with Large Language Models
abstract: Whole-page optimization (WPO) decides how search and recommendation results are surfaced to users, and large language models (LLMs) open a new route to it by treating page generation as sequence generation. Adapting LLMs to web-scale WPO, however, remains bottlenecked by the need for costly human annotations and by the mismatched granularity between page-level coherence and item-level placement. In this work we show that these two challenges are coupled: implicit user feedback alone suffices for alignment, provided the reward signal is decoupled into two complementary granularities. title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents
abstract: In finance, the answer that matters is usually the current one: prices, rates, and disclosures hold only as of a given day, so retrieving up-to-date facts is a core capability of a financial agent. Yet most financial benchmarks overlook timeliness. They fix each answer at annotation time, so the gold goes stale as markets move and, once leaked into training data, rewards recall rather than search and analysis. title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
abstract: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
abstract: Position bias—the systematic effect of where key information is located on retrieval effectiveness—is a critical concern in information retrieval. Although recent studies have identified such bias in dense retrievers, existing analyses focus predominantly on monolingual English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for controlled evaluation. title: PACEE: Parent-Centered AI Scaffolding for Emotion Education in Early Childhood Conversations
abstract: Emotion education is critical for children aged 3 to 6. However, existing technologies depend substantially on direct child-AI interaction, overlooking the central role of parents in guiding early emotional development at home. To address this gap, we conducted co-design sessions with five kindergarten teachers and five parents to identify key parental challenges and opportunities for AI support in family emotion education. title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
abstract: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. title: Whole-Body Motion Guided Reference Generation for Uncertainty-Aware Compliant Assistance
abstract: Exoskeletons have shown great potential for augmenting human physical capabilities, yet generating reliable assistance remains challenging because human motion patterns and interaction requirements vary substantially in practice. To address this problem, a dual-loop assistance strategy is proposed to couple multimodal exoskeleton trajectory generation with variable admittance control, where trajectory variance links the outer-loop generator and the inner-loop controller.
