title: AutoCSF: A Provably Safe Indexing Framework for Filter-Augmented Compressed Static Functions
abstract: We consider the problem of building space-efficient indexes for static key-value datasets with highly skewed value distributions. A standard technique for this task is to augment a compressed static function (CSF) with an approximate set membership prefilter to handle a dominating value and break the one-bit-per-key barrier. However, we observe that prior approaches decide when to apply such a prefilter using idealized cost models or data-driven heuristics, and, as a result, can recommend using a prefilter in regimes where it actively increases space usage. title: Spherical Brownian Diffusion for Language Modeling
abstract: Continuous diffusion language models involve two coupled design choices: how to corrupt continuous token representations and how to invert that corruption at generation time. Recent work has explored language generation on the unit sphere through geodesic and von Mises--Fisher (vMF) paths, raising the question of which forward process to use on this geometry and how much that choice matters relative to inference. title: Efficient Quantum Optimization via Dissipative False Vacuum Decay
abstract: Efficient quantum solvers for computationally hard problems are highly desirable for near-term quantum platforms. Here, we propose a cavity-based dissipative quantum solver for a class of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems encoded in atomic-spin Hamiltonians with a few discrete single-spin-flip transition energies. We show that the cavity-based quantum solver exploits dissipative false-vacuum decay in configuration space to facilitate escape from metastable local minima in rugged energy landscapes. title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
abstract: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel. In most practical situations, hyperspectral images are affected by spectral variability (SV) also known as intra-class variability, which is caused by different physical phenomena including atmospheric effects, intrinsic variability of the pure materials and illumination or topographic changes. title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
abstract: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization problems. Unlike conventional methods, which suffer from instability of the forward sensitivity function, the proposed approach projects optimization problems to system dynamics optimization problems in Hilbert space to increase stability, diminish memory requirements, and lower computational cost. title: On-the-fly Estimation of Quantum-Corrected Thermodynamics in LAMMPS
abstract: We present a native implementation of the Two/Three-Phase Thermodynamics (xPT, $x \in \{2,3\}$) method within the LAMMPS molecular dynamics framework, termed FixXPT. xPT is an approach for obtaining absolute, quantum-corrected thermodynamics (entropy, enthalpy, free energy, heat capacity, diffusivity) from the density of states function, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function of an equilibrium trajectory. title: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation
abstract: We present LucidLyra, a framework that makes generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances in a feed-forward manner from video latents. While generative 3D reconstruction can synthesize virtual environments from a single image, downstream applications in robotics and physical AI require not only visual realism but also access to scene semantics and object identities. title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents interact with Web services to perform tasks on users' behalf. Errors during these interactions can disrupt execution and prevent task completion, motivating external intervention. However, agents may self-recover through continued execution, raising the question of when to intervene and when to wait for self-recovery. We present an empirical study of errors and self-recovery in LLM agents. We construct ReInBench, a dataset containing 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and Web tasks. title: Compound Climate Risk-Aware Electricity Dispatch: Trajectory-Based Modeling for Power System Resilience
abstract: In recent decades, emerging compound hazards in a changing climate have increasingly threatened power system resilience and posed new challenges to electricity dispatch. Conventional Value-at-Risk (VaR)-based risk-aware dispatch provides a tractable means of managing stochastic net demand deviations caused by distribution feeder outages. title: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the accuracy and calibration of Decision and System One models on rheumatology examination questions and diagnostic vignettes. Methods: Two benchmarks were analysed: 172 text-based rheumatology questions from Spanish specialty-training examinations (expanded RheumaMIR dataset) in Spanish and English, and 70 English diagnostic vignettes from RheumBench, each with 5-18 candidate diagnoses, 52 of which included the correct reference diagnosis. title: FATE-5: Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for Continuous Big Five Personality Control
abstract: Controlling personality in large language models is important for building conversational agents that can be customized to different users and interaction settings. However, existing personality control methods often face a tradeoff between strong trait expression and natural dialogue generation. We introduce FATE-5, Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for the Big Five, a two-stage framework that separates personality encoding from naturalness alignment. title: NumTrace: Auditing the Number Provenance of Financial Analyst Agents
abstract: A numerical claim generated by a financial analyst agent can match a number in a company filing but refer to the wrong entity, concept, period, unit or scope. A check based on reference answers can mark such an answer as wrong but does not explain why it fails. In this paper, we present NumTrace, a new benchmark that audits the provenance of each numerical claim made by financial analyst agents: its source and financial semantics. title: sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation
abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) distills multi-step diffusion models into few-step generators by minimizing reverse KL divergence. Despite its strong performance, DMD guides samples by local density alone, which introduces two limitations: teacher scores can be unreliable in regions of low teacher density, and the mode-seeking behavior of reverse KL can collapse the student onto a subset of the teacher modes. title: SoftBART-CORM Models for Density Regression
abstract: Flexible modelling of the conditional distribution of a response given predictors is important in many applications where nonlinear effects, heteroskedasticity, and multimodality may be present. We introduce the SoftBART-CoRM, a predictor-dependent infinite mixture model that combines the interpretable component structure of Compound Random Measures (CoRMs) with SoftBART priors on both mixture weights and component-specific parameters. title: $N \to Δ$ Transition Form Factors in the Thermal AdS/QCD Soft-Wall Model with Modified Propagators
abstract: We investigate electromagnetic (EM) and axial vector (AV) form factors of the nucleon-Delta baryon transition within the thermal AdS/QCD soft-wall model. While the vector bulk-to-boundary propagator admits a well-behaved analytical solution, the transverse axial vector equation of motion involves the vacuum expectation value of the bifundamental scalar (generating chiral symmetry breaking). title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
abstract: Synthetic rewrites, where a language model rewrites a natural document e.g. into a target style, are now a standard ingredient of pretraining corpora. However, critical aspects of their use remain poorly understood, such as how much compute should be spent rewriting training data and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform the rewriter. title: The Evolution and 'Chineseness' of Urban Screens in China: From Propaganda Posters to Smart City Interfaces
abstract: Urban screens have become a global feature of the media city, yet their developmental paths are not universal. This paper argues that the evolution of urban screens in China constitutes a distinct paradigm of media urbanism, termed Chineseness, understood here not as cultural essence but as a relational, historically situated configuration of three linked elements: deep-rooted lineages of public communication; state-steered technological leapfrogging driven by industrial policy and mega-events; and a regulatory paradox that enables spectacular scale while tightening operational control. title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
abstract: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. title: Nuclear fission: from fundamentals to frontiers
abstract: Nuclear fission, the division of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter fragments, is a process of fundamental importance to nuclear physics, energy production, and the origin of the elements. This chapter, part of the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, provides a pedagogical introduction to a broad array of topics in fission physics, progressing from the macroscopic liquid-drop model and microscopic shell corrections through fission dynamics, observables, modern theoretical frameworks, and experimental techniques ranging from traditional double-energy methods to inverse kinematics at radioactive-i

title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. title: Me, Myself, and My Voice: Exploring Cultural and Linguistic Identity in AAC AI-generated Voices
abstract: Voice is a central element of identity. We recognize people by their voice, and we uniquely express who we are with it. For people who rely on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, such as speech-generating devices (SGD), the device’s voice becomes an identity marker others associate with them. Yet, it is hard to find a voice that truly aligns with one’s identity both linguistically and culturally. title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates
abstract: Safety alignment for Large Language Models is heavily focused on English with limited multilingual representation, particularly damaging low-resource language performance. Related open training datasets are often limited in size or do not follow region-localized harmful topics to broaden the scope of alignment beyond cultures. title: Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model
abstract: Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) provide a unified description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse spatial structure of the nucleon. We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. title: $Ψ$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
abstract: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce $Ψ$-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. title: AI-driven structural informatics reveals diverse glycosylation machinery across double-stranded DNA viruses
abstract: Abstract Glycosylation is widespread in biology and shapes molecular recognition, yet the diversity and biosynthetic organization of viral glycosyltransferases (GTs) remain poorly understood. Here we integrate structural-alphabet-guided searches and structure similarity networks with genomic-neighbourhood and biosynthetic gene cluster embedding analyses to examine viral GT-A proteins. title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task performance. Video editing provides a useful testbed for this question, combining multimodal perception, long-horizon planning, and tool use with delayed outcome feedback. abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. title: Fault-tolerant shallow recurrent decoders for sparse sensing with missing sensor measurements
abstract: Real-world sensing systems are inherently imperfect: sensors may fail, intermittently disconnect, operate with asynchronous sampling rates, and be subject to noise, leading to measurement streams that are irregular, incomplete, and heterogeneous. Nevertheless, sensing strategies for real-time state reconstruction typically assume synchronous and continuously active sensors, a constraint that substantially limits their applicability in operational environments. title: From Sea Surface Height to Velocity - A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Inferring upper-ocean velocity from altimetric sea surface height (SSH) remains challenging below 50~km, scales now resolved by the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. Conventional methods rely on geostrophic or cyclogeostrophic balance. Here, we demonstrate that deep learning can predict the full velocity vector from SSH and environmental data and recover derivative-based diagnostics, including spectral energy flux. title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. title: Sampling Design and Confidence Tubes for Integral Curves on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: We estimate the integral curve of an unknown vector field from noisy tangent vector field on a known compact Riemannian manifold. We consider two sampling settings: independent observations at random locations that have already been collected, and a fixed response budget that allows subsequent locations to be chosen using pilot information. title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
abstract: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. Yet vision models pretrained on terrestrial images become less reliable underwater, where turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation alter scene appearance. Existing adaptation methods either spread adapters equally across the encoder depth or select layers using the divergence between two fixed domains. title: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation
abstract: Behavior Cloning has demonstrated promising generalization capabilities for robotic manipulation in terrestrial environments. However, marine visual distortions and dynamic currents create a severe domain shift that remains a key bottleneck in adapting generalist architectures to underwater field manipulation. title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
abstract: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged. For a Gaussian variational autoencoder (VAE) with constant input skip $0\leqα<1$, a model without a skip can be written in skip form by multiplying its decoder output by $b=1-α$ and its noise variance by $b^2$. The distribution of observations and latent variables and its exact generative scores stay the same, while reconstruction mean squared error (MSE) is multiplied by $b^2$. abstract: Radon measurements of the air in the soil in a 40 m deep borehole were combined with meteorological data and evaluated using artificial intelligence. The purpose of the study is to analyze the factors influencing radon levels. Neural networks were employed for this purpose. title: Human-Led AI-In-The-Loop Drift Forecasting for Faster Marine Casualty Response
abstract: Summary When a vessel loses propulsion it becomes a drift-dominated casualty, and the response team must begin preparing decisions on towage, refuge, authority notification and specialist salvage engagement before the casualty picture is complete. The information available in the first hour rarely supports the decisions that must be made in the first hour. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Marine propulsion shafting operates under complex, variable conditions, where stern bearing wear and pedestal settlement redistribute loads, migrate vibration energy, and distort the shaft orbit, threatening safe operation. abstract: Abstract. Compound hot and dry events cause damage to ecosystems and society. title: Sustainability Pathways and Policy Efficacy in a Rapidly Urbanizing Megacity
abstract: Shanghai's industrial dynamism and rapid urbanisation have put strain on numerous aquatic habitats, extending from the Huangpu and Suzhou Creek networks to the Yangtze River delta. The purpose of this study is to present both primary and secondary research on Shanghai's water-quality issues and assess the sustainability performance of major policies influencing the city's results: the Yangtze River Protection Law (2021–), the Sponge City Program (2014–), China's Water Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (the "Water Ten Plan," 2015), and national water reuse/resource recovery programs.

abstract: Air entrainment often plays a crucial role in determining impact loads exerted by free-surface wave flows interacting with structures, yet its modeling is often oversimplified in numerical approaches. In this study, a two-phase numerical model, based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method coupled to a conservative Allen–Cahn interface-capturing equation, is employed to perform three-dimensional simulations of dam-break waves propagating over a dry bed and impacting vertical walls. title: Experimental and Numerical Studies of the Open Hole Compression Strength of Molded‐Hole Laminates
abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper, open‐hole compression (OHC) tests were conducted on quasi‐isotropic (QI) laminates to compare the performance of drilled and molded holes. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) models were established for both drilled and molded laminates based on the Hashin and Puck failure criteria, respectively, to characterize the stress field around the hole. title: Analisis Jangka Panjang Propagasi MJO dan Respons Konvektif di Benua Maritim Indonesia (1996–2025)
abstract: The characteristics of Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) propagation over multi-decadal periods in the Maritime Continent remain relatively understudied, despite the fact that variations in its duration and propagation success may significantly influence long-term convection patterns. This study analyzes MJO propagation during the period 1996–2025 and its impacts on Outgoing Longwave Radiation (OLR) anomalies, wind divergence, and moisture transport using NCEP–NCAR Reanalysis data and the Real-time Multivariate MJO (RMM) index. title: Atmospheric pressure, temperature, and online search activity for epilepsy: A daily time‐series study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Meteorological conditions have been investigated as potential short-term correlates of epileptic seizures, but findings remain inconsistent. This study examined whether daily meteorological variation was associated with population-level online information-seeking for epilepsy. METHODS: A daily time-series study was conducted in Lombardy, Italy, from September 1, 2021, to September 2, 2026. title: Fingerprints of Airborne Plastics in Urban PM2.5: Applications and Implications
abstract: Abstract To better identify emission sources of airborne plastics, we employed nine plastic-associated chemicals (PlsACs) in 240 daily PM2.5 samples collected in Singapore during 2018–2020. A unique PlsAC, tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (I168O), is most abundant, accounting for 90% of the total quantified PlsACs and identifying at least 40% more PM2.5 linked to respirable airborne PlsACs. title: Revealing the Microphysical Distribution Characteristics of Arctic Mixed‐Phase Clouds
abstract: Abstract As a typical cloud type in the Arctic, the microphysical characteristics of Arctic stratiform mixed‐phase clouds (MPCs) are essential for understanding interactions among Arctic clouds, aerosols, and radiation. This study uses 1‐year of shipborne observations from the Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) expedition in the Arctic Ocean. title: Contrasting distribution and biomass trends of two sympatric redfish (Sebastes) species off Southeast Greenland
abstract: Sustainable harvest of fish stocks requires regular monitoring of abundance and biomass in space and time. In Southeast Greenland, two Sebastes species, beaked redfish ( Sebastes mentella ) and golden redfish ( S. norvegicus ), coexist and have been harvested together. However, the species differ greatly in stock status as beaked redfish are depleted, while golden redfish have a surplus of exploitable biomass. title: Ultra‐Thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites—Material Overview and Aspirations
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultra‐thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites (µt‐TBDC) are emerging as a transformative alternative to conventional continuous‐fiber composites, offering the potential to overcome longstanding limitations in manufacturability, waste, and design flexibility. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of µt‐TBDCs, spanning manufacturing, forming, mechanical characterization, and multi‐scale modelling. title: Contrasting impacts of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under different climate backgrounds
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under both pre-industrial and pre-industrial +1 K climate states, using the reduced-complexity climate model Fast Ocean Rapid Troposphere Experiment version 2 (FORTE2) with Systematic Regional Aerosol Perturbations simulations. Results show that increased Asian sulfate aerosols reduce extreme precipitation, characterized by lower frequency and weaker intensity over East and South Asia in both climates, but the suppression is more pronounced over northern India in the +1 K climate. title: Calculation of range-height indicator (RHI) scan eddy dissipation rate (EDR) map based on Doppler Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) velocity data
abstract: An algorithm based on a structure function approach is developed to calculate the Eddy Dissipation Rate (EDR) map from range-height indicator (RHI) scans of short range Light Detection and Ranging (SRLs) at the Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA). With particular consideration on the temporal and spatial resolution of the Doppler velocity data from SRLs as compared with EDR maps from long-range Light Detection and Ranging (LIDARs) already in use at HKIA. The characteristics of such RHI EDR maps is studied in representative cases of building-induced turbulence and terrain-induced turbulence.

title: Classifying meridional movement of the south Asian high: spatiotemporal characteristics, regional climate impacts and formation mechanisms
abstract: The South Asian High (SAH) is an important component of the Asian monsoon system. Studies have indicated that meridional movement of the SAH can exert substantial influences on the weather and climate over surrounding and remote regions. This study shows that the meridional movement of the SAH can be divided into three types. The first type represents the meridional movement of the whole SAH (WBSM). title: Spatial heterogeneity of air temperature and precipitation trends: a multi-scale physiographic perspective from central Mozambique (1994–2023)
abstract: Abstract Central Mozambique encompasses coastal, inland, and high-elevation environments, yet long-term climate trend assessments based on meteorological station data remain limited. Spatial and temporal trends in mean air temperature and total precipitation were analyzed across ten locations over the period 1994–2023. Missing values were reconstructed using monthly scaling with NASA POWER data. title: An experimentally calibrated MBD–DEM framework for ice fracture, fragmentation, and dispensing in a refrigerator ice maker
abstract: In the highly competitive home appliance market, the dispensing and crushing performance of built-in ice makers has become a critical quality attribute affecting both user satisfaction and product competitiveness. However, conventional product development processes still rely heavily on reactive trial-and-error approaches, which may lead to substantial economic losses during the later stages of mass production. title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. title: Investigating the transition in ice dynamics from a land- to lake-terminating glacier using a simple glacier dynamics model
abstract: Abstract. Glaciers interact with adjacent proglacial lakes through a range of thermomechanical processes. These interactions occur in addition to climate-driven ablation and are capable of amplifying or modifying climatic effects through various feedback mechanisms. In particular, the connection between lake water-level and the subglacial hydrological system can reduce basal friction, which in turn leads to increased glacier flow and dynamic thinning. title: Numerical study of hybrid Euler–Euler multiphase modeling in bottom-purged industrial-scale steel ladle
abstract: Abstract In steelmaking, inert gas injection is widely employed during ladle refining to enhance mixing and promote chemical reactions. Argon is injected through the bottom of the ladle, inducing a turbulent recirculating flow that improves heat and mass transfer. This agitation promotes molten metal homogenization, inclusion removal via the slag layer, alloy mixing, and slag-metal reactions. In this study, a numerical model based on a Hybrid RANS/LES turbulence approach was developed to simulate gas–liquid flow in an industrial 185-ton steel ladle. title: Investigation of multi-DOF WEC S-shaped buoy configurations in the nearshore region of East China
abstract: This study proposes a multi-DOF WEC employing S-shaped buoy profiles and a mechanically integrated PTO system tuned for site-specific nearshore wave conditions. The system uses heave and coupled surge/pitch motions, while the proposed PTO mechanism mechanically synthesizes the corresponding modal responses into a unified transmission path and represents their damping contributions through a single equivalent PTO damping coefficient. title: How ENSO controls the propagation speed of seasonal onsets in Java–Bali: satellite rainfall evidence over two decades
abstract: Indonesia, as a tropical maritime continent, exhibits a seasonal rainfall pattern influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Variations in the Wet Season Onset (WSO) and Dry Season Onset (DSO) have broad implications for agriculture, water resources and disaster mitigation. This study aims to analyse the climatology and interannual variability of WSO and DSO over the Java–Bali region (104–116°E), using satellite-based rainfall data (1998–2024). title: Direct Reuse of Uncured CFRP Prepreg Scraps for Structural Applications: Experimental Qualification and Numerical Validation of an Automotive Battery Case
abstract: ABSTRACT The high demand for fiber‐reinforced composite materials generates large quantities of uncured prepreg waste, still in pristine condition, usually landfilled or incinerated. Among the various established recycling routes, direct reuse of these scraps represents an attractive strategy to reduce both raw material consumption and manufacturing waste, while preserving the original constituents' properties, and avoiding energy‐intensive recovery processes or the use of hazardous chemicals, thus moving an energy demanding industry toward sustainability. title: Environmental and Operational Implications of Dynamic Positioning Failures in Offshore Operations: A Review of IMCA Reports from 2018 to 2024
abstract: Dynamic Positioning (DP) systems are widely used in offshore operations such as drilling, subsea construction, cable laying, offshore renewable energy support, and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) operations. As offshore activities become increasingly dependent on DP capability, failures in DP systems may result in operational disruption, safety concerns, and environmental exposure. Although advances in automation and redundancy have improved DP system reliability, the offshore industry continues to report DP incidents and undesired events. title: Boosting triboelectric nanogenerators via hierarchical textures: insights from coupled adhesion contact and electrical modeling
abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are an emerging nanotechnology for distributed energy harvesting, where introducing hierarchical micro/nanotextures onto contact interfaces effectively enhances electrical output. However, existing theoretical models lack the capability to guide the design of hierarchical textures, particularly overlooking the gap-dependent variation of surface charge density, which is a key factor governing the electrical output. title: Late Quaternary lake filling and drying in northern Australia's largest freshwater lake
abstract: ABSTRACT Lake Woods, Jurrkulu, is northern Australia's largest freshwater lake filled today in strong Indo–Australian summer monsoons (IASM) to maximum depths of ~5 m. On the western margins of the lake, two large arcuate ridges occur 20 to 40 m above the lake floor and inset within these are other mid‐elevation lake deposits, such as depositional ridges, which suggest past filling events much higher than the modern maximum. title: Influence of climate warming and land-cover change on aerobiological pollen season in Estonia
abstract: Abstract Pollen allergy is an increasing public health concern in Europe, as climate warming alters flowering phenology and airborne-pollen dynamics. This study analysed temporal and spatial changes in pollen seasons in Estonia using aerobiological monitoring data from Tartu, Tallinn, and Pärnu. Temporal changes were assessed by comparing two monitoring periods in Tartu (1990–1998 and 2012–2022), while spatial differences were evaluated across stations in contrasting climatic settings. title: Disentangling atmospheric transport and mixing processes over mountains: overview of the preliminary field campaigns of the project DECIPHER
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the rationale, experimental design and preliminary outcomes of two field campaigns undertaken as part of the project DECIPHER at two mountain sites in the Italian Alps to investigate surface-layer processes and turbulent fluxes associated with slope-wind systems. The first campaign (23 July-29 October 2024) was concentrated at Col Margherita (2543 m above sea level (ASL) )and nearby Passo Valles. title: Parametric Study on Cyclic Behavior of Hexagonal Concrete-Filled Steel Tubular Columns
abstract: The seismic performance of columns plays a decisive role in the safety of steel–concrete composite structures. Although the seismic behavior of concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) columns has been extensively investigated. However, the cyclic behavior of hexagonal concrete-filled steel tubular (HCFST) columns equipped with continuously distributed Perfobond Rib (PBL) shear connectors along the column has not yet been comprehensively studied. title: Multi-hazard risk assessment and classification of elder care institutions in China: An integrated vulnerability framework
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid population aging and the continuous expansion of the elder care system in China, disaster risks facing elder care institutions under multiple hazards have emerged as a critical challenge for public safety and social governance. In this study, a Multi-dimensional Risk Index (MDRI) was developed for elder care institutions (ECIs) by integrating a Hazard Level Index (HLI), a Community Vulnerability Index (CVI), and an Institutional Vulnerability Index (IVI). abstract: Abstract This study investigates lithosphere–atmosphere interactions during the 2016 Central Italy seismic sequence, providing the first systematic analysis of atmospheric impacts across the entire series within a complex tectonic setting. The static displacement fields of the main events were modeled using the Okada formulation and validated against GPS observations. title: Hydrological control and distributed rainfall-runoff modeling of flood inflows from the Bt River to the Aghien Lagoon (Cte dIvoire) using the ATHYS software
abstract: Quantifying hydrological contributions from tributaries to lagoon systems represents a major challenge for understanding the functioning of coastal hydrosystems and for the sustainable management of water resources, particularly in tropical environments exposed to strong climatic and anthropogenic pressures.This study aims to assess flood contributions from the Bété River to Lagune Aghien, a strategic potential resource for the drinking water supply of Abidjan, through distributed rainfall-runoff modeling using the ATHYS model.The methodological approach relies on hydrometeorological time seri

title: Temporal and climatic drivers of uncomplicated malaria in Ghana: Regional Generalised Additive and Generalised Additive Mixed Model analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, despite recent reductions in cases due to various interventions. The endemicity of the disease varies across regions, influenced by diverse seasonal and temporal factors that support mosquito proliferation and malaria cases. This study used a Generalised Additive Models to explore the impact of weather conditions on malaria cases in Ghana. title: Remote sensing of leaf area index as an indicator of ecosystem resilience to El Niño-driven climate variability in the UK
abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) influences vegetation far beyond the tropical Pacific, but its imprint on temperate maritime vegetation, where the teleconnection acts indirectly through winter circulation, temperature and precipitation, has rarely been quantified at the site scale. title: Analysis of the Contribution of Potato Production to the Local Socioeconomic Structure in Fena Fafan Subdistrict, South Buru Regency
abstract: Fena Fafan Subdistrict is the only region in South Buru Regency producing potatoes, situated at an elevation of 575 meters above sea level—an altitude ideal for optimal potato growth. This study aims to analyze the contribution of potato production to the local socio-economic structure. A descriptive quantitative method was used, utilizing secondary data from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) for the years 2020–2024. title: Integrating conventional tagging and acoustic telemetry improves estimates of post-release survival for a highly targeted reef fish
abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of post-release survival is fundamental to fisheries stock assessment and effective management. Conventional tag-return studies and acoustic telemetry are commonly used to estimate this probability, yet each approach has limitations when applied independently. Using gag (Mycteroperca microlepis) as a case study, we integrated data from a large-scale conventional tagging program and an acoustic telemetry experiment into a discrete-time statistical modeling framework that links relative recapture risk with telemetry-derived fate. title: Integrated in vivo Anti-Inflammatory, Antioxidant-Related, and Preliminary Acute Oral Toxicity Responses to Gracilaria gracilis Extract
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress reinforce one another and are important targets in the development of marine-derived pharmacological candidates. This study evaluated the in vivo anti-inflammatory and antioxidant-related effects of an ethanol extract of BRIN-authenticated Gracilaria gracilis and included a separate preliminary single-dose oral toxicity assessment. Dried seaweed (300 g) was macerated with 96% ethanol in three 24-h cycles at a 1:3 (w/v) ratio, producing 24.5 g extract (8.17%, w/w). title: A methodology for integrating Life Cycle Assessment into a Multidisciplinary Design Analysis and Optimization framework for sustainable launcher development
abstract: The increasing number of orbital and sub-orbital launches makes it necessary to investigate the environmental impacts of launch vehicles and to incorporate eco-design considerations into their development. In response to these emerging concerns, the European Space Agency has promoted the use of the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology as a standardization to support the mitigation of environmental impacts associated with present and future space missions. abstract: Abstract Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites following the modest February 2022 storm. title: Production-Stage environmental and Techno-Economic assessment of green hydrogen production in Ghana: Comparing Solar, Wind, and biomass pathways
abstract: Country-specific assessments of suitable green hydrogen pathways remain limited for resource-endowed Sub-Saharan African countries, including Ghana. The study assesses the cradle-to-gate environmental impacts and techno-economic performance of four hydrogen production pathways using solar, wind, and biomass. GIS screened sites for technical potential, while life-cycle impacts per kg H 2 followed ISO 14040/14044. title: Radiation regimes shape microbial light-harvesting strategies and network organization on glacier surfaces
abstract: Glacier cryoconite hosts metabolically active microbial communities despite exposure to solar radiation, which both provides energy and imposes stress. However, how radiation regimes are associated with microbial energy acquisition strategies and ecosystem organization remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 85 cryoconite metagenomes, including 47 from Arctic glaciers and 38 from Tibetan Plateau glaciers, representing contrasting long-term radiation environments. abstract: The Lp(a)HORIZON trial aimed to determine whether lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] reduction using the drug pelacarsen could reduce cardiovascular (CV) risk in patients with both established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and an Lp(a) level ≥70 mg/dL (approximately 149 nmol/L), whose other CV risk factors were otherwise already treated optimally (1). title: Seasonal Modulation of ENSO Teleconnections to Horn of Africa Rainfall
abstract: Abstract Rainfall over the Horn of Africa (HoA) exhibits pronounced interannual variability linked to the El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO). However, the seasonal evolution of ENSO‐driven rainfall anomalies is not adequately explained by the ENSO, particularly the Niño3.4 index. The results here show that nonlinear interactions between ENSO and both semiannual and annual migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone generate a combination mode (C‐Mode) that modulates the timing and amplitude of the HoA regional rainfall. title: Corrosion Hotspots Strongly Localize Crack Origins But Provide Conditional Timing Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Published specimen‐level data from 36 pre‐corroded structural‐steel fatigue specimens relevant to offshore applications were re‐analyzed to separate crack‐origin localization from crack‐initiation timing. Localization was available for 34 specimens and digital‐image‐correlation‐based timing for 21. title: Enhancement Pathways for Urban Water Ecological Resilience
abstract: Enhancing urban water ecological resilience (UWER) is increasingly essential as climate change, rapid urbanization, and ecological degradation intensify pressures on urban aquatic systems. However, knowledge of the mechanisms required to systematically enhance UWER remains fragmented across the ecological, technological, and governance domains. This narrative review synthesizes the current understanding of UWER by examining its conceptual foundations, key drivers, mechanisms, and enhancement pathways. title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
abstract: Abstract Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). title: 40 °C heat extremes are no longer implausible in the Nordic countries
abstract: Abstract The Nordic countries of Norway, Sweden, and Finland have traditionally been characterised by less intense heatwaves than continental Europe. However, during recent events, such as the 2026 heatwave, exceptionally high temperatures have been observed across large parts of Europe, with temperatures of 40 °C reaching further north than previously observed. title: Development and Application of Dynamically Similar Model Materials for Blasting in Reef Limestone
abstract: To address the difficulty of sampling reef limestone and poor dynamic replication by conventional similar materials, this study introduces wave impedance as a key dynamic index for designing similar materials for reef limestone blasting. An orthogonal experiment examined five parameters: barite powder content, aggregate-to-binder ratio, cement-to-gypsum ratio, foaming agent dosage, and fiber content, using range and linear regression analyses. title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
abstract: The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m−2 d−1) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m−2 d−1), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. title: Biases and predictability limits of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones in subseasonal prediction systems
abstract: Abstract Subseasonal prediction of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones (ETCs) is critical for anticipating associated weather extremes, yet biases and predictability limits of ETC activity in current forecast systems remain insufficiently quantified. Here, using hindcasts from ten state-of-the-art subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction systems within a Lagrangian tracking framework, we uncover a common and pervasive bias: the multi-model ensemble consistently predicts fewer and weaker cyclones at a one-month lead, underestimating frequency by 10-18% and intensity by approximately 13%,

title: Participación, comunicación y gobernanza del litoral valenciano: lecciones de dos procesos deliberativos
abstract: Esta investigación tiene como objetivo analizar las barreras, oportunidades y prioridades para avanzar hacia una gobernanza costera integrada y adaptativa en la Comunidad Valenciana, un territorio con elevada fragmentación institucional, presiones urbanísticas y vulnerabilidad climática. title: The impact of atmospheric rivers on the water level and hydrology in a lake in south-Central Chile
abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are major drivers of hydroclimatic extremes in mid-latitude regions, with important implications for water resource management and climate services. This study evaluates the hydroclimatic and hydrological response of Lake Villarrica in south-central Chile to AR landfalls during 2000–2024. ARs were identified using an ERA5-based catalog and classified as Zonal (ZARs) or Tilted Atmospheric Rivers (TARs) according to integrated vapor transport direction. title: Climate change effects on analogues of contrasting extratropical cyclones over the UK, Ireland and France
abstract: Abstract. Extreme extratropical cyclones present major socio-economic risks in the United Kingdom and are sensitive to anthropogenic climate change. Robust projections of the aggregate properties of extreme cyclones based on climate-model output have emerged in recent years. However, such projections average together cyclones with a range of contrasting dynamical characteristics potentially obscuring climate change effects on particular types of cyclones and the airstream structures within them. title: Science and policy to manage nitrogen with cover crops—The Maryland experience
abstract: During the 1980s, research showed nitrogen-stimulated eutrophication was contributing to the Chesapeake Bay's deterioration, and cover crop research shifted from legumes to replace fertilizer, to winter cereals to reduce nitrogen (N) leaching. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) adopted nutrient regulations and added technical and financial resources promoting N-capturing cover crops and N-use efficiency. title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
abstract: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. title: Assessment of Human Thermal Stress Dynamics and Regional Drivers Across the Arabian Peninsula During 1990–2022 From Observations
abstract: ABSTRACT Human thermal stress is intensifying in the Arabian Peninsula (AP); however, a lack of consensus in observational evidence continues to limit a quantitative understanding of trends and the relative influence of the meteorological drivers underlying regional variability. title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. title: Hydrokinetic energy recovery using a controllable-pitch propeller on a kite-assisted ship: Propeller performance mapping and a notional route case study
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of wind-assisted ships, the propeller may operate as a turbine. Because harvesting efficiency is strongly dependent on blade pitch, this study maps the propulsive and generative performance of a controllable pitch propeller (CPP) by simulating the Potsdam Propeller Test Case (PPTC) across a wide range of blade and advance angles. The power coefficient ( C P ) reaches 0.22 at design pitch, but achieves a global maximum of 0.44 at a 215° reversed pitch. title: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
abstract: Abstract. Nuclear conflicts could ignite intense urban fires that inject considerable amounts of black carbon (BC) into the upper atmosphere, with the potential to disrupt global climate. While uncertainties in the total BC injection remain large, relatively few modeling studies and limited model diversity have explored the climatic response to low-to-moderate BC injections, leaving key aspects of their climate impact poorly understood. title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
abstract: Abstract The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides the first systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the “middle-of-the-road” SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget. journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Experimental Study of Duct Cross-Sectional Area Reduction on Oscillating Water Column Performance Using Wave Period Variations
abstract: The development of renewable energy is a key approach to reducing fossil fuel dependence. This study examines the effect of modifying duct geometry into a convergent nozzle shape in an Oscillating Water Column (OWC) system. Experiments were conducted in a laboratory wave flume using sensors to measure wave height and pressure across nine wave period variations. Results show that reducing the cross-sectional area increases pressure by 57% and velocity by 44%, consistent with Bernoulli’s principle. title: Long-term climate variability and implications for groundwater recharge potential and saltwater intrusion vulnerability in the Cape Flats Aquifer, South Africa
abstract: The Cape Flats Aquifer (CFA) is a critical groundwater resource supporting urban, agricultural, and ecological needs in the Western Cape, South Africa. However, its sustainability is increasingly threatened by seasonal climate variability, which strongly influences groundwater recharge. This study examined seasonal rainfall and temperature variability and their potential implications for groundwater recharge and susceptibility to saltwater intrusion in the CFA. title: Nonlinear oscillatory flow regimes with mixing in a two-layer fluid under a rigid lid
abstract: Abstract We propose a nonlinear long-wave model describing the propagation of internal waves and turbulent mixing in a two-layer fluid under a rigid lid in the Boussinesq approximation. This model allows for the inclusion of non-hydrostatic effects in the lower layer, density non-uniformity and flow vorticity in the upper layer, as well as mixing at the interface. title: Convection‐Permitting Simulations of Extreme Hourly Rainfall and Land‐Surface Impacts in the Middle‐Lower Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Abstract Extreme precipitation events frequently cause severe socioeconomic losses, making accurate forecasting critical. However, prediction of extreme precipitation remains challenging due to multi‐scale nonlinear interactions. Previous studies have largely attributed extreme rainfall to large‐scale circulation or mesoscale convective systems, the role of complex underlying surfaces remains insufficiently understood. title: Dynamic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves
abstract: This study investigates the seismic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves, considering dynamic soil–structure interaction (SSI). The analysis is conducted using the OpenFAST numerical framework, extended with an SSI model to represent the dynamic impedance of pile foundations. Additionally, the tool was adapted to account for the non-synchronous excitation at the different supports that arises from the arrival of obliquely incident planar waves or surface waves. title: An Investigation of the Characteristics of Indian Summer Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems Under Stratospheric Aerosol Geoengineering
abstract: Abstract Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems (LPSs) that govern the rainfall of the Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) contribute more than half of its rainfall and extreme rainfall events. In this study, we explore how LPS activity changes under greenhouse warming and Stratospheric Aerosol Intervention (SAI) using simulations from the fully coupled CESM2.1.3 climate model. We simulate three different climate scenarios: CTRL (control climate), 2XCO2 (doubling of ), and UNIFORM (a globally uniform stratospheric sulfate aerosol forcing superimposed on the 2XCO2 climate). title: Novel Filament‐Wound FRP Composite Tubes Integrated Grid Ribs and Multi‐Angle Winding Layer: Manufacturing, Interfacial Behavior and Proof‐of‐Concept Validation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial slip between concrete and fiber‐reinforced polymer (FRP) tubes remains a key concern in concrete‐filled FRP tube members. This study proposes a novel concrete‐filled FRP tube integrated with designable grid ribs and multi‐angle winding layers (GR‐CFFT). The internal grid ribs are intended to enhance rib–concrete mechanical interlocking, reduce interfacial slip, and improve the contribution of longitudinal reinforcement layers to flexural resistance. title: Can advanced sand-based models predict the behaviour of silty sands? A comprehensive experimental and numerical assessment
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the monotonic and cyclic behaviour of five natural silty sands. Based on an extensive laboratory programme comprising drained and undrained monotonic triaxial tests, as well as undrained cyclic triaxial tests, four advanced constitutive models originally developed for clean sands, Hypoplasticity with Intergranular Strain (Hypo+IGS), Sanisand, Hypoplasticity with Intergranular Strain and semifluidized state and fabric change effects (Hypo+ISA-SF), and Sanisand with memory surface and semifluidized state (Sanisan

title: Quiet Time Ionosphere‐Thermosphere Predictability During Sudden Stratospheric Warmings in TIE‐GCM
abstract: Abstract We investigate the predictability of the ionosphere‐thermosphere (IT) region during sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs) by using subseasonal hindcasts in the Community Earth System Model, version 2 with the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (CESM2 [WACCM6]) to force the lower boundary of the TIE‐GCM. The extension of subseasonal hindcasts into the IT region enables the first comprehensive investigation of IT predictability during SSWs. institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: A hybrid statistical–dynamical approach for seasonal prediction of the boreal winter stratosphere
abstract: Abstract The winter variability of the Northern Hemisphere Stratospheric Polar Vortex (SPV) is characterized by extreme events known as Sudden Stratospheric Warmings (SSWs). SSWs feature a rapid temperature increase and a reversal of the zonal winds in the SPV, exerting a downward impact on the troposphere. Yet, despite their importance, current seasonal prediction systems (SPSs) show limited skill in forecasting SPV variability and SSW occurrence. title: Spatial representativeness of total column ozone monitoring in Reykjavik, Iceland, and its regional significance in the North Atlantic region
abstract: Abstract In 2021, a double monochromator Brewer spectrophotometer was installed in Reykjavik, Iceland, complementing the long-term Dobson total column ozone (TCO) observations at this site. To assess the spatial representativeness of this TCO time series, the reanalyzed ERA5 TCO daily mean values in the area north of N 40° have been analyzed. A good agreement was found between the Brewer and ERA5 TCO, with almost no systematic bias and a RMSE of 7.7 DU (2.1%). title: Climate change induced hydrological regime shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin in Central Asia
abstract: Mountain river basins in Central Asia are highly sensitive to climate-driven changes in snow and glacier melt, yet the magnitude and timing of the resulting hydrological regime shifts remain poorly quantified. To address this gap, we assess present and future hydrological shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin with the SPHY glacio-hydrological model. We improved the representation of snowmelt and snow infiltration, which redistributes water to delayed baseflow and improves winter and spring discharge. institutions: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF

title: How Does Terrain Relief of the Tibetan Plateau and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau Individually Modulate Summer Regional Hourly Extreme Precipitation in the Sichuan Basin, China?
abstract: Abstract The influence of terrain relief over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau on summer regional hourly extreme precipitation (RHEP) in the Sichuan Basin (SCB) under two dominant synoptic patterns remains poorly understood. Here, this study uses multi‐case Weather Research and Forecasting sensitivity experiments, in which the terrain relief of two plateaus is individually smoothed, to systematically investigate these modulation mechanisms. title: A synoptic overview of the EUREC 4 A field campaign
abstract: Abstract We present an overview of the important synoptic features that occurred during the EUREC 4 A field campaign. These results are based on workshops bringing together forecasters and researchers to look in detail at cloud patterns in the region of interest (Barbados and the upstream trade winds) and how they were influenced by synoptic features. Consistent with previous studies, we found that the influence of, or lack of, midlatitude and subtropical features was important for cloud patterns. journal: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society

title: A physics-based two-dimensional reduced order model for hydro-elastoplastic response of panel under bow flare slamming impact: Validation and application
abstract: While high-fidelity methods, such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)- Finite Element Analysis (FEA) coupling, can accurately capture structural collapse under severe slamming when the modeling and analysis conditions are appropriately specified, their high computational cost makes them impractical for repeated use in early-stage design or risk screening. In this paper, a physics-based two-dimensional reduced-order model (ROM) is proposed and developed to efficiently estimate the dynamic elastic-plastic response of plate panels between stiffeners subjected to slamming loads. title: Black carbon aerosols intensified India’s 2015 mega heatwave and expanded heat stress exposure
abstract: Abstract Large-scale climatic drivers are known to amplify heatwave temperatures, whereas aerosols have complex regional temperature responses depending upon aerosol composition. With the help of recent observations and chemistry-coupled regional climate model simulations, we show that coincident aerosols—black carbon in particular—elevated the heatwave intensity of India’s deadly 2015 heatwave event. title: How Can Local Knowledge and Infrastructure Engineering be Bridged for Tsunami Resilience? A Systematic Scoping Review of Socio-Technical Mitigation Framework
abstract: Tsunami resilience research has advanced significantly in both indigenous knowledge and engineering-based mitigation. However, these domains are often treated in isolation, which limits the development of integrated socio-technical catastrophe risk reduction solutions. This review examines how recent literature conceptualizes the relationship between local knowledge and tsunami mitigation engineering and operational planning, identifies mitigation functions that bridge these domains, and highlights existing knowledge gaps in socio-technical tsunami resilience. journal: Bulletin of Social Studies and Community Development

title: A new method for detecting aerosols: combining atmospheric detection LiDAR technology with intelligent driving technology
abstract: Abstract. The existing aerosol mobile detection system has problems such as over-reliance on labor power and difficulty in conducting continuous operations in toxic and polluted environments. This paper presents a new method for detecting aerosols. The method combines atmospheric detection LiDAR technology and intelligent driving technology. Through modular design (including control module, aerosol detection module, environment sensing and positioning module, and wire control chassis module), an intelligent cruise detection system for aerosols was built. title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Stratosphere–troposphere exchange of ozone
abstract: Stratosphere-troposphere exchange (STE) of ozone is a significant source of tropospheric ozone, influencing air quality, atmospheric chemistry and climate forcing. This assessment synthesizes recent advances in understanding the magnitude, mechanisms, variability and future evolution of ozone transport across the tropopause, updating earlier reviews using observations, reanalyses and global chemistry-climate models. journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences

title: Climate risk assessment in tropical wetlands through integrated hydroclimatic, land cover, and community knowledge
abstract: Abstract Climate-risk assessments in tropical wetlands increasingly combine hydroclimatic and land-cover data, but rarely integrate them with structured community evidence on experienced impacts and adaptation priorities. We address this gap in six communities around the Complejo Cenagoso de Zapatosa, a Ramsar site, and the Morales wetland in the Colombian Caribbean. We integrated hydroclimatic records and climate-extreme indices (1991-2020), land-cover change and runoff-potential analysis (1991-2020), flood-susceptibility modelling, and structured participatory evidence from 106 participants.

title: Analysis of technologies for biogas production through filtration and utilisation of wastewater in an urban environment

title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
abstract: Abstract. Compound dry–hot extremes (CDHEs) are among the most damaging climate hazards. Most metrics used to diagnose them are estimated at monthly or seasonal resolution or rely on precipitation-based drought proxies that can miss fast soil moisture-driven land–atmosphere feedbacks. This paper delivers two tightly linked products for global CDHE monitoring over land (excluding Antarctica) at 0.1° resolution for 1961–2023: (i) a continuous, daily severity index, i.e. the Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI), and (ii) a companion, event-based CDHE catalogue derived fro

title: The Eco‐Digital Dimension in Children's and Young Adult Literature for Early Childhood and Primary Teacher Education: An Exploratory Inquiry
abstract: ABSTRACT Although ecological topics are gaining increasing relevance in children's and young adult literature, the intersection between environmental sustainability and digital media remains under‐researched. The two main research questions of this qualitative exploratory study are: how the eco‐digital dimension manifests within contemporary children's and young adult literature formats (RQ1), and how an eco‐digital webbook format can be integrated into initial teacher education for kindergarten and primary school (RQ2). title: Conservation of migratory species at risk: environmental conditions experienced from pre‐gestation to parturition affect fall recruitment in migratory caribou
abstract: Annual variations in environmental conditions can strongly affect vital rates such as survival and recruitment. These effects are likely to be exacerbated in highly seasonal environments and in species facing substantial energetic needs during specific seasons. For instance, pregnant migratory females must balance energy expenditure between long-distance travel and gestation. Little is known, however, on the environmental factors influencing recruitment in species exhibiting long-distance migrations. title: Effects of microphysics and gray-zone convection on MCS organization: A case study of unprecedented extreme rainfall in South Korea
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) embedded in quasi-stationary fronts are major drivers of extreme precipitation over South Korea, yet simulating their organization and rainfall structure remains challenging. This study investigates how cloud microphysics and gray-zone convective parameterization modulate MCS and non-MCS precipitation and the phase and amplitude of precipitation in extreme event that recently occurred in South Korea. title: Urbanization Enhances Inner‐Core Rainfall During Tropical Cyclone Landfall
abstract: Abstract How urbanization modulates precipitation in landfalling tropical cyclones (LTCs) remains poorly understood. Previous studies disagree on whether the mechanism is primarily dynamical or thermodynamic, particularly within the inner core under intense wind–rain conditions. Using high‐resolution simulations and storm‐relative framework, we quantified the effects of urban land‐cover change (ULCC) and anthropogenic heat (AH) on peak inner‐core precipitation during Typhoon Bebinca's 2024 landfall in Shanghai. title: More than meets the eye: artificial eyelashes as an unrecognized source of microplastics and heavy metals
abstract: Despite growing concern over microplastic pollution, leave-on cosmetic products such as artificial eyelashes remain largely unexplored as sources of microplastics and associated contaminants. Here, nine artificial eyelash products were characterized for polymer composition, heavy metal content, and fiber release under simulated environmental conditions. Three polymers were identified: PBT (55.56%), PET (33.33%), and PVC (11.11%). Metal profiles varied widely across samples, with several metals of toxicological concern (Al, Ba, Co, Cr, Cu, Pb, Sb, Zn) detected but not declared on product labels

title: Methodological Approaches to Analyzing the Economic Impacts of Geoclimatic Risks in Russia
abstract: Global geoclimatic shifts pose substantial risks to the Russian economy, including infrastructure degradation, declining agricultural productivity, and structural challenges associated with the energy transition. The study is motivated by the need to critically evaluate existing climate-economic modeling approaches and assess their applicability to Russian conditions. The objective is to propose an ensemble framework capable of addressing structural uncertainty in climate-economic projections. Method . title: Secondary ice production affects tropical convective clouds under different aerosol conditions
abstract: Abstract. Secondary ice production (SIP) modulates tropical convection, but its interactions with aerosol loading remain uncertain. Using the UK Met Office Unified Model with detailed SIP parameterizations, this study investigates how multiple SIP mechanisms affect a Hector storm under weak instability and varying cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentrations. At moderate aerosol loading (Nd = 400 cm–3), SIP substantially enhances the ice phase. title: Influence of groundwater seasonality on suspended sediment dynamics, in a 20 km 2 Mediterranean mountainous catchment
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the interplay between groundwater and surface runoff in controlling suspended sediment dynamics within the Galabre catchment, a 20 km² Mediterranean mountainous catchment characterized by extensive badland areas. Using an End-Member Mixing Analyzing framework that accounts for event-specific variability in end-member chemistry, the study quantifies surface runoff and groundwater contributions during 86 flood events spanning three hydrological years. title: Cessation of Nearby Low‐Frequency Earthquake Activity Following the December 2024 M w 7.0 Mendocino Earthquake: The Likely Role of Pore Pressure Reductions
abstract: Abstract Earthquakes affect surrounding fault systems through multiple mechanisms. Here, we examine a rare cessation of activity in 27 families of low‐frequency earthquakes (LFEs) that likely reflect fault creep at the southern edge of Cascadia subduction, near the Mendocino triple junction. These sources usually exhibit nearly daily activity but were shut off for ∼7–25 days following the December 2024 moment magnitude ( M w ) 7.0 Mendocino fault earthquake. title: Heat extremes threaten cattle and outdoor workers across northern Australia’s extensive grazing systems
abstract: Australia is projected to warm throughout the 21st century, raising the risk of dangerous heat for livestock and the people who work with them, yet these changes have not been quantified for the extensive grazing systems of northern Australia. Here we employ a seven-model ensemble of regionally downscaled climate projections to quantify future changes in cattle heat load and the maximum safe metabolic rate for outdoor work under lower- and higher-emission pathways (Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) 1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0) at mid- and late-century. title: Project Management Maturity Profiles in Turkish Shipyards: A P3M3® Assessment
abstract: Shipbuilding is a complex project-based production environment in which maturity scores averaged across shipyards can obscure important organizational differences.This study assesses project management maturity in 32 Turkish shipyards using the Portfolio, Programme and Project Management Maturity Model (P3M3 ® ) version 2.1 Self-Assessment Tool and examines whether an aggregate result conceals distinct maturity configurations.One manager from each participating shipyard completed a Turkish questionnaire distributed through the Turkish Shipbuilders' Association (GİSBİR).The analysis covered 24

title: Experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy
abstract: This study presents a proof-of-concept experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy converter (WEC). The proposed concept consists of an array of surface-penetrating buoys connected through a shared closed-loop hydraulic power take-off (PTO) system. abstract: Os sistemas de água doce na Amazônia brasileira oriental estão cada vez mais vulneráveis à expansão do uso da terra, à mineração, à intensificação agrícola e ao enfraquecimento da governança ambiental. title: A Lower Bound on the Altitude of the Hiroshima Firestorm Plume From Ray Optics
abstract: Abstract Projections of nuclear winter are critically sensitive to the height of soot lofted by firestorms, yet direct observations of firestorm plumes are scarce. Here, a lower bound is established for the height of the Hiroshima firestorm plume 97 min after detonation. This bound is obtained via a ray‐optics calculation using the Enola Gay 's flight log, which gives the location and time when the plume was last visible. title: Effect of sub-critical fluid shear flow on granular bed strength
abstract: Interactions between fluids and granular materials are prevalent on the Earth's surface. In the case of fluid flow over a sediment bed, the fluid imparts a shear stress to the granular materials. When the applied shear stress is above a critical value, the grains become entrained in the fluid flow. Prior experimental studies have shown that granular beds subjected to a sub-critical fluid flow can strengthen in the same direction as the sub-critical flow. title: Corrosion lifetime prediction of electro-galvanized iron using potentiodynamic polarization and multiphysics simulation under different process and environmental conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a process- and environment-dependent corrosion lifetime prediction model was developed for electro-galvanized iron (EGI). EGI specimens with different crystallite sizes were fabricated by controlling the plating current density. The differences in crystallite size were evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. title: Carbonation of silicate minerals contributes to atmospheric CO2 drawdown in glacier-fed streams
abstract: Abstract Glacierized landscapes produce abundant fine-grained reactive minerals that play a pivotal role in high-altitude inorganic carbon cycling, mainly through geochemical weathering. However, our understanding of the relationship between glacially comminuted mineral dissolution, precipitation of secondary phases and inorganic carbon cycling in the world’s glacier-fed streams (GFSs) remains elusive. title: Global sampling characteristics and coverage complementarity of 12 GNSS radio occultation constellations
abstract: Abstract. This study uses observations from COSMIC-2, FY-3, GRACE-C/D, KOMPSAT-5, MetOp-A/C, PAZ, PlanetiQ, Sentinel-6A, Spire, TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X, TM-1, and YY-1 during 1–7 January 2026 to compare their spatial distributions, grid coverage, local-time sampling, and retrieval accuracy; it also assesses the benefits of multi-mission integration and the potential effects of COSMIC-2 retirement on the integrated observing capability. title: A multi-indicator framework for assessing the likelihood of ENSO impacts across southern Africa
abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the dominant source of seasonal predictability for southern Africa, yet operational guidance rarely conveys which agriculturally relevant variables it can skillfully predict, or where ENSO impacts are most likely. title: Breaking the Ice: Contributions and Challenges for Andean Glaciological Research Led by Women
abstract: Abstract This study examines the participation of women in Andean glaciology over the past four decades, combining a bibliometric analysis of 204 peer-reviewed articles (1983–2022) and a survey of female first authors (2018–2022). Results show a steady increase in women-led publications, rising from 8 percent in the 1980s–1990s to 30 percent in the past decade. title: Quantifying and attributing CO emissions over Central Asia using TROPOMI and explicit observational uncertainty
abstract: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified daily, gridded CO emissions in Central Asia (Xinjiang-China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan) for 2019–2024. title: Effect of freezing rain-induced changes in dry deposition on particulate matter concentrations in Hubei, China
abstract: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a critical aspect of urban air quality degradation, and vegetation mitigates atmospheric PM concentrations via dry deposition, offering a natural, sustainable, and cost-effective strategy for pollution mitigation. abstract: The Medical Journal of Australia (MJA)-Lancet Countdown on health and climate change in Oceania was established in 2017 and produced its first regional assessment in 2018 and annual updates from 2019 to 2025. It examines five broad domains: (1) health hazards, exposures and impacts; (2) adaptation, planning and resilience for health; (3) mitigation actions and health co-benefits; (4) economics and finance; and (5) public and political engagement. abstract: The operational efficiency of water-lubricated rotary interfaces—fundamental load-bearing and sealing elements in fluid-energy systems—is severely bottlenecked by the inherently low load-carrying capacity of low-viscosity water films. Conventional surface texturing and uniform wettability approaches offer only limited improvements in simultaneously enhancing hydrodynamic pressure, suppressing wear, and maintaining sealing integrity. abstract: Study region Southwest China (SWC). Study focus This study identifies the decadal drought background of frequent droughts in SWC since the early 21st century, quantifies the roles of precipitation and potential evapotranspiration (PET), and evaluates vegetation impacts. Monthly precipitation and PET during 1961–2023 were used to calculate the 12-month Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI12).
