title: Climate change impacts on the predicted performance of optimized building-integrated photovoltaics
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) are a promising strategy for enhancing building energy performance and reducing carbon emissions. However, most design optimization studies rely on historical climate datasets that may fail to capture the operating conditions buildings will experience under climate change. This study develops a computational framework for the multi-objective optimization of BIPV envelope systems using future climate projections from the CanESM5 model under the SSP3-7.0 scenario. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response of bamboo fiber-reinforced C40 concrete. Bamboo fibers were incorporated at dosages of 1.5%–4.5% and used in three states: uncarbonized, carbonized at 300 °C, and carbonized at 800 °C. title: Cometary impacts an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth
abstract: Abstract An early period of cometary bombardment has long been speculated to provide an important source of prebiotic feedstock molecules, required for the origins of life on Earth. In support of this interpretation, comets boast a rich diversity of volatile organic molecules, with many thought to be limiting for prebiotic chemistry. Modelling studies suggest, however, that a significant proportion of these molecules will be destroyed during hypervelocity impact. abstract: Abstract Although temperature variability (TV) has been linked to an increased mortality risk, the independent effect of intra‐day TV remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between intra‐day TV exposure and cause‐specific mortality in a Chinese population. We collected daily mortality data and meteorological variables from 2016 to 2022 in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, China. title: Replica revolutions in rock art: from physical replicas to virtual reality libraries via contemporary art
abstract: Rock-art replicas generally are judged as more or less faithful substitutes for inaccessible originals. While previous studies have demonstrated the value of replicas for individual archaeological experiments, we reconceive them as persistent interdisciplinary research infrastructure. Drawing on reflections from original sites, we compare physical copies with virtual environments, developing criteria for evaluating replicas. title: Structural variation of cooling and heating energy demand with degree-day estimation method
abstract: Degree-day methods are essential for estimating building heating and cooling energy demands. We investigate the sensitivity of cooling and heating degree-day models, CDD26 and HDD18, at national and regional scales across mainland China. Non-observational datasets overestimate national heating demand while severely underestimating cooling demand. title: Regional covariation between climate-normalized storm rarity and landslide magnitude in Taiwan is sensitive to rainfall timing
abstract: Abstract Climate-normalized rainfall rarity may facilitate comparisons across climates, but pooled rainfall–landslide associations can obscure regional structure and rainfall timing. We examined 994 reported rainfall-induced landslides in Taiwan (1987–2018) using 2-km hourly precipitation and generalized extreme-value climatologies for 1980–2019. Rainfall rarity ( T max ) was defined as the maximum of 1–72-h duration-specific return periods, not the recurrence interval of an entire storm. title: Study on the mechanical properties and resistance to wetting–drying cycles of red clay stabilized by enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP)
abstract: Abstract In view of the problem of strong water sensitivity and susceptibility to dry and wet alternating damage of red clay, this study proposes to use plant-source Enzyme-Induced Carbonate Precipitation (EICP) technology for eco-friendly stabilization. title: An assessment of overbank flow-statistics within the context of environmental flow rules
abstract: Characterizing diversity in river flow regimes is crucial in informing river flow management guidelines for protecting freshwater ecosystems. In partly-confined reaches, river exhibit substantial lateral and vertical interaction when flow inundates its floodplain patches. A knowledge gap exists at the intersection of environmental flow assessment, overbank exceedance flow dynamics, and real-world policy application. title: Increasing the critical shear stress in sandy beds to control bed scour using alkali-activated cement
abstract: Scouring during flood events is a critical problem in hydraulic and geotechnical engineering, threatening the stability and service life of bridge piers and abutments, foundations, and embankments. This study evaluates the use of alkali-activated cement (AAC) derived from ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) for the prevention of streambed scour and to enhance the erosion resistance of sandy soils. title: Hydrodynamic Flood Modelling and GIS-Based Risk Mapping for Identifying Urbanization-Safe Zones in Hanwella, Sri Lanka
abstract: Urban expansion in flood-prone regions increases exposure to hydrological hazards and makes flood-informed land-use planning increasingly important. Hanwella, located in the Kelani River basin of Sri Lanka, is particularly vulnerable to flooding due to intense rainfall, river overflow, and growing urban pressure. This study develops a two-dimensional hydrodynamic flood modelling framework based on the shallow water equations and applies a Godunov-type finite volume method with the Harten–Lax–van Leer (HLL) Riemann solver to simulate water-level dynamics in the Hanwella region. title: Extreme event assessment and model diagnostic for attribution of the record-breaking July 2025 heat in Shandong, China
abstract: Abstract In July 2025, Shandong Province, China, experienced a record-breaking regional extreme heat event. Based on observational data from 77 meteorological stations (1961–2025), this study assessed the event’s extremity and systematically examines the feasibility of its attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models. The event reached a magnitude close to that of a 1-in-50-year event in the current climate, with 84.4% of stations recording high-temperature days (HTD, Tmax ≥ 35 °C) ranking among their top three historical values and 50.6% setting new records.

title: Energy-efficient scheduling of LNG terminals: A coupled terminal-pipeline optimization framework for coordinated peak-shaving
abstract: At LNG terminals, electricity accounts for approximately 98% of the total energy consumption, with key power-consuming equipment in the transmission system contributing around 90% of the electricity demand. This study focuses on the gas and liquid transmission processes at LNG terminals and proposes a multi-period optimization model designed to maximize user satisfaction and minimize electricity operating cost. title: Global health impacts of the 2018–2019 heatwaves and air pollution events under warmer climates
abstract: Extreme temperatures and ambient air pollution are closely linked and impose substantial global health burdens, yet their regional responses to additional warming remain poorly understood across the world. Using a storyline approach based on the exceptionally warm years 2018 and 2019, we examine how heatwaves (HWs), fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), ozone (O 3 ), and their separately estimated mortality burdens respond to two counterfactual climates at +2 K and +2.75 K warming levels. title: Numerical study of liquid-side mass transfer beneath a moving wavy boundary
abstract: This study investigates liquid-side scalar transport beneath propagating interfacial waves through numerical simulations of the Navier–Stokes and scalar transport equations in a moving reference frame. A wave-phase decomposition of the transport equations is employed to characterize near-surface scalar fluxes and to develop a physically based parameterization for the scalar transfer velocity. title: Comparing surface albedo and land surface temperature of reflective roofs across five United States Cities
abstract: Abstract Rapid urban expansion and increasingly intense summer heat have heightened interest in reflective roofing as an urban heat-mitigation strategy. This study evaluates associations among roof type, surface albedo, and land surface temperature (LST) across five climatically distinct U.S. urban regions: Chicago, New York City (NYC), Las Vegas Valley (LVV), Los Angeles (LA), and Houston. abstract: Pipeline lifting operations involve large displacements and rotations, evolving suspended lengths and pronounced curvature variations, while the equilibrium configuration is generally unknown a priori. Classical catenary models provide highly efficient descriptions of perfectly flexible suspended lines but neglect bending stiffness, whereas geometrically nonlinear finite-element models can reproduce the complete structural response by solving computational heavy nonlinear systems and, when required, unilateral contact problems. title: Dynamic and thermodynamic drivers of regional drought changes in Africa under different global warming levels
abstract: Abstract Drought events pose severe threats to socio-economic stability, with impacts particularly pronounced across Africa due to limited adaptive capacity. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of projected changes in drought characteristics, their physical drivers, and socioeconomic implications under different global warming levels (GWLs) and emission scenarios. title: Cuencas piggy-back de Limón Sur, Costa Rica
abstract: A morphotectonic analysis of the piggy-back basins of southern Limón, Costa Rica, is presented to evaluate their geomorphic evolution and relationship with active tectonic deformation. Seven basins were analyzed using geomorphic metrics derived from digital elevation models, including basin area, elevation, mean slope, local relief, and the normalized channel steepness index (ksn), complemented by drainage network analysis. abstract: Subsea pipelines are vulnerable to anchor-induced structural damage during ship mooring operations, particularly from raising and dragging interactions. This study quantified the effects of the pipeline burial depth on the structural damage response under these two loading scenarios in a soft clay seabed. title: At the crossroads of change: Executive functions in the age of emerging simulation technology – A scoping review and driving simulator study on adaptive performance
abstract: Simulators are pivotal in advancing mobility technology, yet human adaptation in the context of these technologies remains underexplored. This study investigates the role of core executive functions (working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility) in adaptive performance within driving simulators based on a scoping review identifying a research gap and conducting a driving simulator study addressing it. title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
abstract: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Calcium leaching degrades concrete durability through progressive dissolution and decalcification of cement hydrate phases, yet it is commonly modelled by assuming local equilibrium between the pore solution and solid hydrates. While useful for estimating how much calcium is eventually depleted, such approaches do not fully resolve the kinetic coupling among hydrate dissolution, ionic transport within the bulk concrete and across the concrete-solution interface, and ultimately porosity evolution. abstract: Study region This study was conducted in the Santa Fe River Basin (SFRB), a tributary basin of the Suwannee River in the Southeastern USA. The SFRB is an agriculturally important, groundwater-dominated watershed, which overlies the Upper Floridan Aquifer (UFA). abstract: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. abstract: Abstract Predicting the response of Antarctic ice to climate change requires detailed knowledge of its shallow structure, but direct measurements are challenging. Traditional seismic surveys are logistically demanding, and surface remote sensing provides limited information about subsurface layers. abstract: Industrial infrastructure in Saudi Arabia is undergoing expansion and renewal with the environment being as much a factor as the infrastructure itself with exposure to extreme heat, flash flooding, complex supply chains and highly interdependent utility services. abstract: This study investigates the impact of mitigation strategies on pedestrian-level thermal conditions in four European cities with distinct climatic and morphological characteristics: Barcelona, Athens, Ljubljana, and Senigallia. Although reflective and vegetation-based interventions have been widely investigated, direct comparisons of their effects on both air temperature and pedestrian thermal comfort across contrasting urban environments under extreme conditions remain limited. abstract: Abstract This study investigates how aerosol perturbations influence precipitation formation in supercooled stratiform clouds with different supercooled liquid water content (SLWC). abstract: ABSTRACT Meteorological dry–wet abrupt alternation (M‐DWAA) is an important compound climate extreme that can impose complex stresses on agricultural and ecological systems through rapid shifts between water deficit and excess moisture. abstract: Individuals selected for the Inca capacocha ritual, sacrificed at high-altitude sites to act as messengers to the mountain deities, are occasionally found preserved as frozen mummies, providing key insights into Inca life and religious practices. Here, the authors present results of toxicological analyses of hair and nail samples from eight human sacrifices interred near volcanic peaks in Peru and Argentina. abstract: Abstract Plantation forestry underpins rural livelihoods, wood and energy security and landscape restoration in Ethiopia, yet the country lacks a forestry-specific climatic classification to support species deployment and plantation planning. This study developed the first national climatic classification framework for exotic plantation forestry in Ethiopia by integrating temperature and a temperature-adjusted moisture index and quantifying regional temperature–elevation relationships. abstract: Abstract On 29 March 2026, a localised swathe of damaging winds affected parts of northern and eastern England, producing notable damage from southeastern Yorkshire to north Lincolnshire. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Rising thermal stress has emerged as a critical challenge for socio-economic systems and public health in the ongoing climate change scenario. In Northern India states like Uttar Pradesh, where a large population share is engaged in climate-sensitive livelihoods, increasing heat-related thermal stress poses substantial risk of income and productivity loss, alongside an escalating burden of heat-related health outcomes and healthcare expenditure. abstract: Topographical membrane surface patterns are a promising approach for increasing transmembrane flux and reducing foulant deposition. In this study, we investigated the anti-biofouling propensity of TFC membranes with micrometer-scale patterns. abstract: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and methodological provisions for developing a mechanism aimed at enhancing the transfer potential of agricultural holdings’ logistics centers. abstract: Abstract. abstract: A three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer model of a 400 W high-power LED fishing lamp (Scheme A) was established in COMSOL Multiphysics by coupling Heat Transfer in Solids, Heat Transfer in Fluids, laminar flow, and non-isothermal flow. The effects of input power, heat sink fin thickness, inlet air velocity, and heat sink structure on junction temperature and thermal behavior were analyzed and validated using infrared thermal imaging. title: Comparative study of second harmonic generation at 1030 nm in BiBO and LBO crystals using a 57 W picosecond laser
abstract: We present a systematic experimental comparison of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in bismuth triborate (BiBO) and lithium triborate (LBO) nonlinear crystals, driven by a 1.3 ps, 91 kHz laser at 1030 nm with up to 57 W of average input power. Both crystals yielded 32 W of second harmonic (SH) output at 515 nm, corresponding to a conversion efficiency of 56%, which to the best of our knowledge represents the highest SH output power reported in the green spectral region using a BiBO crystal. title: A review of carbon fibre reinforced polymer–steel hybrid structures for dynamic mechanical systems
abstract: This paper reviews the suitability of carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP)–steel hybrid structures as load-bearing components of dynamic mechanical systems. The literature is evaluated against structural requirements, including load-carrying capacity, fatigue resistance and durability, and motion-related requirements, including inertial properties, vibration and damping. title: Efficient Finite Element Modeling of Initial K0 Geostress and Shear-Slide Stability in Sloping Ground
abstract: Abstract Reliable initialization of in situ $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 stresses and efficient stability analysis are fundamental to robust finite-element modeling of infinite slopes. Yet, existing modeling schemes either apply gravity loading with an indirect $${K}_{0}-\nu $$ K 0 - ν mapping that is not mechanics-consistent for sloping ground, or require large computational domains that are expensive for repeated analyses. In this study, an efficient FEM framework is developed that retains the gravity load procedure (GLP) and addresses its stress-initialization limitation for homogeneous infinite slopes.

title: Role of hydrometeorological variables and catchment area to flood generation over the monsoonal climate region of India
abstract: Abstract. Indian River basins experience frequent flooding during the Indian summer monsoon rainfall and pose several challenges to the large population of the region. To effectively manage flood risk in the region, a better understanding of flood-generating mechanisms is essential, yet hydrometeorological and catchment drivers controlling flood processes are poorly explored across India. title: Investigating the thermal properties of hollow blocks building envelope composite sections used across Egypt
abstract: Studying the thermal properties of building materials used in building envelope cross-sections is crucial for enhancing indoor thermal comfort and improving energy efficiency. This study aims to experimentally determine the thermal properties of building envelope wall sections using the heat flow meter (HFM) technique. The thermal properties, including thermal conductivity, thermal resistance, U-value, and specific heat, were investigated for the most common building materials and composite wall sections used in the Egyptian context. abstract: Flooding remains one of the most frequent and destructive hydro-meteorological hazards in South Africa, causing substantial socio-economic losses, infrastructure damage, and threats to human life. In response to increasing flood risks associated with climate variability and extreme weather events, the South African Weather Service has increasingly adopted impact-based severe weather early warning systems designed to communicate not only meteorological hazards but also their likely consequences for communities, infrastructure, and livelihoods. abstract: Abstract. Low hydraulic conductivity (K < 10-10 m/s) is a key factor for effective long-term barrier performance, and argillaceous formations are promising candidates due to their strong aquitard characteristics. title: Development and characterization of eco‐friendly fire‐resistant 3D ‐printable concrete utilizing recycled nickel slag
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the utilization of industrial nickel slag waste to develop eco‐friendly fire‐resistant 3D concrete printing (3DCP). The benefits of waste nickel slag are bifold: it serves as a partial replacement, reducing carbon‐intensive cement and enhances fire resistance. A varying dosage of nickel slag was introduced as a cement replacement in printable mixes, and the rheological characteristics, mechanical behavior, and fire resistance were systematically evaluated. abstract: ABSTRACT Embedded co‐cured damping composites (ECDCs) have been developed as a potential approach to address the stiffness–damping trade‐off in lightweight load‐bearing structures. By embedding viscoelastic layers during co‐curing, ECDCs reduce the interfacial limitations associated with conventional bonded damping treatments while maintaining structural performance. abstract: Elucidating the origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays remains a central challenge in modern astrophysics. The Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory (SWGO) will deploy a kilometer-scale detector array on natural water surfaces, where detector position deviations must be constrained within 2 m to enable high-fidelity observations. abstract: The ‘democratic wave’ in relation to citizen involvement in climate change policy challenges is illustrated here in the Irish context through the Citizens’ Assembly on Climate Change. The National Dialogue on Climate Action (NDCA) has sought to broaden the time and space for citizen input into climate change policy formation. abstract: We examine the onset of wave breaking in highly viscous gravity-driven vertical falling liquid films in a quiescent atmosphere via multiphase direct numerical simulations. Both Newtonian and Herschel–Bulkley liquids are considered. Analysis of the force balance acting on wave humps shows that the transition from travelling waves to breaking states is governed primarily by the competition between gravitational and capillary forces. abstract: Abstract Restoration of degraded areas and post-disturbance rehabilitation after wildfire encompass critical approaches for reducing and reversing impacts of wind erosion and sand and dust storms (SDS). However, the broad outcomes of dryland restoration and rehabilitation for wind erosion and SDS remain underexplored. Wind erosion is an emerging issue in the Great Basin of the western United States, exacerbated by invasive annual grasses and associated wildfire. abstract: This paper addresses the problem of conducting high-resolution geomagnetic surveys in urban environments using a crowdsourced approach based on mobile devices. Existing solutions, such as CrowdMag, are primarily focused on global data collection and do not provide capabilities for operational mapping of local technogenic anomalies. The question of the reliability of anomaly detection based on mass measurements performed by various non-professional devices under real-world conditions remains open. Sequence variants, however, are interpreted against the phenotype supplied when the test is requested, and phenotypic specificity carries evidence weight in variant classification. abstract: Abstract Flocculation‐thickening is an important solid–liquid separation operation in chemical engineering. The flocculation in the thickener feedwell plays a key role in the tailings slurry thickening process. This study develops a sequential multiscale model for a lab‐scale deep cone thickener to examine the effects of feed solids concentration on flocculation and settling. abstract: Background: The increasing demand for lightweight, durable, and impact-resistant automotive components has accelerated the adoption of composite materials in vehicle structural applications. Conventional metallic bumpers provide adequate strength but contribute significantly to vehicle weight, which adversely affects fuel efficiency and environmental sustainability. In this study, we apply a synthesis inversion framework to refine sector‐specific methane emissions for the Melbourne region in Australia, using in situ atmospheric observations and a Bayesian inversion approach. abstract: This paper investigates the grammaticalization of the numeral ‘one’ in Slavic languages at the syntax-semantics interface. abstract: Abstract Elastic metamaterials can suppress vibration propagation through elastic-wave bandgaps, providing an effective strategy for low-frequency broadband vibration reduction. In this study, the mirror symmetry of a standard star honeycomb (SSH) is progressively broken to develop a single mirror star honeycomb (SMSH) and a chiral star honeycomb (CSH). abstract: Climate-driven socio-economic change during Late Antiquity remains a topic of debate, especially over the extent to which climatic instability shaped economic structures and subsistence strategies within the Roman Empire. While the effects of political fragmentation have been extensively documented for urban contexts, responses of rural households remain less understood. abstract: Restricted access to architectural heritage limits expert observation, documentation, and preservation planning. This study examines how mobile augmented reality (AR) can support stable, structured observation when the deployment space differs from the heritage site. Because one-to-one physical–virtual correspondence and global registration rarely hold, we prioritized cognitive coherence over geometric accuracy. title: Cropland and population exposure to extreme precipitation events in Central Asia under future climate change
abstract: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming and an intensifying hydrological cycle, with important implications for extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, future changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs remain insufficiently quantified in this climate-sensitive dryland region. Here, we projected changes in EPE characteristics and associated cropland and population exposure across CA using daily precipitation simulations from five bias-adjusted ISIMIP3b global climate models under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5. abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for resilient and sustainable infrastructure has encouraged the development of advanced cementitious composites with enhanced impact resistance. This study investigates the impact performance of reinforced concrete columns incorporating rubberized engineered cementitious composites (RECCs) through finite element modeling. abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. abstract: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous background. Here we show a real-time dual-telescope normalization in which two identical plastic-scintillator telescopes operate in parallel, one viewing open sky as a reference and one viewing the target. abstract: Converter-interfaced wind turbines inherently lack the inertial response of synchronous generators, reducing frequency stability in low-inertia power systems. While virtual synchronous machine control enables wind turbines to emulate inertial behaviour, the practical limits of inertia provision and the dominant mechanisms constraining performance remain poorly understood. title: Tectonics on Early Earth Driven by Earth's Changing Shape During Tidal Recession of the Moon
abstract: Abstract Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early‐Earth dynamics: rotation. abstract: Climate change and population growth are increasing pluvial flood risks in cities. Blue-green infrastructure emerges as a sustainable adaptation strategy to help cities manage stormwater and flooding while also providing important social and ecological benefits. abstract: Introduction: Spinal tuberculosis (STB) remains a significant health burden in tuberculosis-endemic regions, including India. Diagnosis is challenging because conventional microbiological methods, including acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture, have limited sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of GeneXpert MTB/RIF in comparison with conventional histopathological examination (HPE) for the diagnosis of STB. title: Quantitative Indicators for Assessing the Sustainability Impacts of Frugal Innovations
abstract: ABSTRACT Frugal and social innovations are considered more likely to support sustainability than conventional innovations. However, indicators for assessing their sustainability impacts remain scarce. Although the need for such indicators, especially for frugal innovation, has been emphasized repeatedly, only a few studies address this issue, and even fewer propose quantitative measures. abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel continuous arched composite cross‐section caisson‐type underground garage structure to meet urban underground space development demands. abstract: Open pit coal plans rely on geological models built from widely spaced drill holes, so errors in seam continuity pass directly into tonnage and stripping ratio forecasts. This study quantifies how integrating infill drilling and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) with existing drill hole data changes the seam model, and the coal tonnage, overburden volume and stripping ratio derived from it, within an unchanged pit boundary. abstract: Abstract Detachment of authigenic reservoir fines by breakage with consequent migration in rock, straining, and permeability decline has been widely reported for several technological and natural processes. abstract: This study assesses the Europe-wide potential for multi-sector integration of water electroly-sis, wastewater treatment plants, and district heating networks, enabling by-product oxygen and waste heat utilization to improve energy efficiency and reduce system costs. abstract: Abstract The blade tip clearance in a semi-open mixed-flow pump induces tip leakage flow (TLF). abstract: Pelvic spine loss has evolved repeatedly in stickleback species and represents an intri-guing opportunity to study genetically parallel adaptation. While previous work has identified key loci associated with this trait, the extent to which different populations rely on the same genetic mechanisms remains unclear. abstract: Background: Grief is theorised to be characterised by wave-like reactions, yet little is known about how these reactions unfold between moments. abstract: The increasing use of the adhesive bonding technology in various industries requires reliable models to predict the lifetime of bonded joints under cyclic loading and environmental conditions. abstract: This study evaluates biophysical agricultural land suitability across the twenty districts of Erzurum, the fourth-largest province of Türkiye by surface area, by integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). abstract: Abstract FLOWS (FLOws of Water and Solutes in soils) is a dynamic physically-based model to simulate water flow and solute transport in the soil–plant–atmosphere system. abstract: Abstract Persistent and problematic toxic metal and metalloid pollutants (in particular, As, Hg, Pb, Cd, and Cr) have long been challenging and expensive remediation targets in contaminated surface and subsurface environments. abstract: Seasonal snowmelt is a vital water resource for downstream populations and supports ecological processes in the mountainous Western United States. abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. abstract: With the ability to directly image Earth-like exoplanets and search their atmospheres for biosignatures, the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will also collect high signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) reflected-light photometry and spectra of nearby gas giant exoplanets. Such high-quality data would allow investigations into the formation and evolution of low-mass, low-temperature gas giants and could enable the detection of exomoons around these planets. abstract: The problem of poor energy management and rapid degradation of components in single-source electric vehicles is addressed in this article. The vehicle's performance during acceleration and regenerative braking is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. abstract: Embryonic development is shaped by maternal and zygotic factors but how the interplay between these factors contributes to phenotypic variability and impacts specific populations of brain cells, and subsequently neurodevelopment, remains largely unknown. Here, we reveal a double hit phenomenon that impacts microglia and microglia precursors during development. Using zebrafish, we identified a mutation in sry-related HMG box gene-17 (sox17) that exhibits a maternal effect phenotype presenting as a reduction of microglia in the brain and precursors in the yolk sac. title: Minerais da transição energética no Brasil: mapeamento quantitativo e análise estrutural dos projetos de lítio, terras raras e grafita
abstract: Este artigo mapeia e analisa a estrutura empresarial e a maturidade dos projetos brasileiros de lítio, terras raras e grafita. A partir da extração por substância no SIGMINE/ANM, com corte em 1º de setembro de 2026, foram tratados 7.813 processos únicos, dos quais 219 em fases avançadas, sob 62 titulares, classificados em dois eixos: perfil e natureza do controlador, segundo Dougherty, e maturidade técnica do ativo, aferida por relatórios em padrões internacionais e pela CFEM. abstract: The long range propagation of acoustic waves in Earth's atmosphere is sensitive to winds and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Thus, infrasound observations have a strong potential to improve numerical weather models by data assimilation methods. However, because acoustic waves propagate slowly, the atmospheric parameters can change during the propagation of the acoustic waves. This change of atmosphere properties is usually not taken into account by infrasound simulation tools which generally assume stationary atmosphere models. abstract: Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. abstract: Inertial modes are low-frequency global oscillations in rotating fluids, restored by the Coriolis force. Long-term observations of horizontal flows on the solar surface have led to the detection of various inertial modes on the Sun, opening a new window into the structure and dynamics of the solar interior. Here, we focus on recent advances in the theoretical modeling of solar inertial modes within a purely hydrodynamic framework, leaving magnetohydrodynamic effects beyond the scope of this review. title: Climate change, sea level rise, and the agricultural revolution
abstract: We test various hypotheses for the invention and spread of agriculture: higher temperatures, increased seasonality, carbon dioxide fertilization, sea level rise, and technological progress on the extensive margin. We successfully replicate Matranga (QJE 2024). His seasonality hypothesis survives alternative data, estimators, and competing hypotheses. Population density played a role in the invention of agriculture, while spatial diffusion was important for its spread. title: Modeling Broad-Frequency-Band Water-Wave Experiments with Generalizations of the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation
abstract: Waves generated by storms gradually disperse, forming swells that can travel thousands of kilometers across the ocean's surface. The evolution of deep-water swells, which are unaffected by the seafloor, can be modeled by the nonlinear Schrodinger (NLS) equation and its generalizations. These models typically assume that the wave trains are comprised of a narrow band of frequencies. We present measurements from a new series of laboratory experiments in which the broadbandedness is increased and show that generalizations of the NLS equation can accurately model these measurements.

title: SD3: The First Operationally-Proven, Fully Heterogeneous-Accelerated Global Kilometer-Scale Model with Inline Physics Architecture
abstract: We present Super Dynamics on the Cube (SD3), the first operationally-proven, fully heterogeneous-accelerated global kilometer-scale model. Through a full-stack reconstruction in native CUDA C, SD3 introduces an "Inline Physics" architecture that deeply couples its non-hydrostatic cubed-sphere dynamical core with fast physical processes. title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
abstract: Europe's future power system will rely heavily on wind and solar power and must remain resilient during prolonged periods of low wind and solar generation, known as variable renewable energy (VRE) droughts. To capture such rare events, adequacy assessments increasingly draw on decades of weather data, but the conversion of weather into power is largely treated as fixed. title: The Fate of Ice Sheets on Near-Synchronously Rotating Land Planets
abstract: Rocky exoplanets orbiting M dwarf stars are often assumed to be synchronously rotating, such that water-trapping in ice sheets on the permanent nightside may pose a threat to habitability. However, in compact M dwarf systems, gravitational interactions between planets may cause the substellar point to librate or circulate on millennial timescales and sporadically change direction or speed. Here, we use a 3D global climate model to quantify, for the first time, the water-trapping capabilities of these "near"-synchronously rotating exoplanets, with TRAPPIST-1e as our test case. title: Impact of Cumulus Parameterization and Cloud Microphysics on WRF Simulation of an Extreme Rainfall Event over Maharashtra, India: A 3 by 3 Factorial Assessment
abstract: Simulating extreme monsoon rainfall over the Konkan coast and Western Ghats remains challenging at 9 km resolution, where convection is partly resolved and partly parameterised. This study evaluates the sensitivity of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations of the 5-7 July 2026 Maharashtra rainfall event to cumulus and cloud microphysics schemes. Nine simulations employed a 3 x 3 factorial design combining WSM6, WDM6 and Thompson microphysics with Kain-Fritsch, Tiedtke and Grell-Freitas cumulus schemes. abstract: Porting a regional weather model in its entirety to a graphics processing unit (GPU) requires complete implementation of the dynamical core and all physical processes, and improved computational efficiency. This paper introduces WRF-JAX v1.1.28, a JAX reimplementation of the WRF 4.5 dynamical core and the complete CONUS physics suite. title: PyPSA-Libya: An Open-Source Energy System Model for National Decarbonization and Hydrogen Export Pathways
abstract: Libya possesses significant renewable energy potential that remains largely untapped. This paper presents PyPSA-Libya, a national-scale model built on the PyPSA-Earth framework, designed to explore optimal transition pathways for the Libyan power sector. title: Bounded entropy production constrains hierarchical decision-making in homing pigeon flocks
abstract: Collective decision-making requires individuals to reconcile diverse, often conflicting opinions to reach a common course of action. However, within a group, individuals rarely exert equal influence, leading to non-reciprocal communication patterns manifested as leader-follower relationships and social hierarchies. Here, using homing pigeon flocks as a model system, we develop a trajectory-based framework to infer and quantify hierarchy within navigating living collectives. abstract: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$ν$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. abstract: GOWC (Global Observing-conditions Weather Catalogue) is an open web application that takes the user from a target to an exposure plan across 2,642 catalogued observatory sites. It computes seeing, airmass, extinction, precipitable water vapour, sky brightness and signal-to-noise from live Open-Meteo meteorology, including pressure-level profiles, and tests most of these outputs against an independent reference. abstract: We analyze scale-by-scale budgets of velocity and buoyancy second-order structure functions using Large Eddy Simulation of the BOMEX trade-wind cumulus layer. The simulation utilizes a $10\,\mathrm{m}$ grid resolution under the anelastic approximation, incorporating moist thermodynamics to capture phase changes. abstract: To understand the mantle evolution that has caused the observed histories of mare volcanism and radius change of the Moon, we developed a 3-D regional spherical shell mantle convection model with magmatism. Magma generated by decompression melting segregates from the convecting matrix and percolates upward through it. abstract: Nanosecond repetitively pulsed discharges in air cross-flows exhibit distinct plasma morphologies that can expand the spatial extent of bulk plasma regions and increase the residence time of reactive radicals within the flow field. abstract: The complete Wess-Zumino (WZ) action and stress-energy tensor (SET) of the conformal anomaly in both two and four dimensions is given. abstract: Space-based quantum information networks require simulation tools that capture orbital dynamics, probabilistic quantum operations, and classical coordination. We introduce QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for the design and performance evaluation of satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. abstract: This thesis explores the astronomical use of observations from the VLBI Global Observing System (VGOS), a next-generation geodetic network designed to improve the precision of terrestrial and celestial reference frames and Earth orientation parameters. Although primarily conceived for geodesy, its wide frequency coverage and regular monitoring of compact active galactic nuclei (AGN) provide valuable opportunities for astrophysics. abstract: Abstract Sea ice alters nitrate (NO 3 − ) availability in polar oceans, yet the influence of sea‐ice type on NO 3 − sources and cycling remains poorly constrained. abstract: Deep-sea ferromanganese nodules (FNs) are important mineral resources, and their abundance is a key parameter for resource assessment. In this study, the association between FN abundance and seafloor topography near 113 geological sampling stations in the Pacific Clarion–Clipperton Fracture Zone is investigated. abstract: The low spatial resolution (300–400 km) of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experience (GRACE) and the 11-month data gap between GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) complicate the evaluation of long-term ice mass loss at sub-region scale. Although several studies have downscaled GRACE data for water storage evaluation, efforts to downscale ice mass change are limited. abstract: The extent of the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets during Marine Isotope Stage 3 (MIS 3, 57-29 ka) is generally poorly constrained due to limited stratigraphic control, a lack of geological deposits, and inconclusive dates. abstract: The development of sustainable sample preparation strategies is increasingly important for reducing the environmental footprint of analytical methods. abstract: Coral reefs are in global decline due to climate change, shifting reef ecosystems from 24-hour net heterotrophy to autotrophy, altering carbon cycles and reducing resilience to stressors. Red Sea coral reefs experience some of the warmest waters globally, exceeding 30 °C and reaching up to 38 °C on reef flats during summer. title: Seasonal icings reveal subsurface water drainage of a Greenland Ice Sheet outlet glacier
abstract: Abstract. In many glacial settings, winter outflows of proglacial water create stratified domed ice structures on glacial forefields. These structures, called naledi, provide an opportunity to characterise the solute fluxes of hydrological systems in winter which are poorly constrained compared to summer outflows which are dominated by supraglacial meltwater input. title: Western Arctic wintertime mixed-phase clouds: Observed modulation by sea ice conditions, long-term variabilities and trends
abstract: Abstract. To assess the long-term interaction between sea ice conditions and Arctic mixed-phase cloud (MPC) properties, fourteen winter seasons of observations from the North Slope of Alaska are analysed. MPC properties are set into context with sea ice conditions by determining the sea ice sectors which are most relevant to interact with the observed clouds. A conical sector of 6° and 50 km radius of upstream sea ice concentration (SIC) is considered based on the azimuth direction of the maximum water vapour transport (WVT) within the atmospheric boundary layer. title: Detecting whale vocalizations up to 2.5 kHz using a seafloor distributed acoustic sensing array with incorporated loops
abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) is an increasingly popular tool for marine mammal monitoring. Until recently, most monitoring efforts targeted lower frequency sounds made by large baleen whales and were not optimized for the mid-frequency signals made by many other marine mammals. This is partially due to the directivity of the DAS system and the spatial averaging effect of the gauge length, which acts as a low-pass filter, markedly decreasing signal amplitude above 300-500 Hz, depending on the angle of incidence. title: Assessing the Distribution of Seagrass and Halophytic Habitats in the Nin Coastal Lagoon, Croatian Adriatic Sea, to Support Future Monitoring and Management
abstract: The coastal wetland in the Nin Lagoon, Croatia, represents a valuable and ecologically sensitive transitional ecosystem between land and sea. The aim of this study was to determine the presence and distribution of halophytic communities and seagrasses and to create a detailed vegetation habitat distribution map of the study area. Field research was conducted through visual census, photographic documentation, GPS mapping of vegetation, and the use of an unmanned aerial vehicle (DJI Mavic Air 2; SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, China) to generate high-resolution orthophoto imagery. title: Caspian Sea Regression and Climatic Aridisation as Factors in the Transformation of Coastal Landscapes of the Russian Caspian Region
abstract: Aim. To identify the spatiotemporal patterns and main directions of transformation of coastal landscapes in the Russian Caspian region under the combined influence of modern Caspian Sea regression and climatic aridisation. A comparative regional analysis was conducted for the Volga delta, Kalmyk and Dagestan sectors of the western Caspian coast, with detailed studies concentrated in the Dagestan sector. title: Movements and habitat use of the invasive blue crab Callinectes sapidus in Mediterranean coastal lagoon
abstract: Abstract The Atlantic blue crab ( Callinectes sapidus ), an invasive and ecologically impactful decapod species, has rapidly proliferated across the Mediterranean Sea, prompting concerns over its effects on native ecosystems and local economies. Despite its growing presence, knowledge of its behavioural ecology in Mediterranean coastal systems remains limited. This study presents the first acoustic telemetry-based assessment of C. sapidus within its invasive range, focusing on movement patterns, activity levels, and habitat preferences in Biguglia Lagoon, Corsica (Northwestern Mediterranean).
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Integrating underwater photo transects and environmental DNA to assess coral genus composition in nearshore reefs of Madura, Indonesia
abstract: Understanding coral community composition is essential for reef conservation, particularly in data-limited tropical regions such as Indonesia. This study compares genus-level coral detections from Underwater Photo Transect surveys and environmental DNA metabarcoding on nearshore reefs of Gili Genting and Gili Labak, Madura, Indonesia. Because the molecular component was a preliminary site-level survey using limited water volume and a descriptive presence-absence interpretation, we treat its results as exploratory signals rather than definitive evidence of local occurrence. title: A physical coastal vulnerability index for site-specific assessment
abstract: Assessment of coastal vulnerability is essential for protecting coastal areas from natural hazards and extreme weather events. In the United Kingdom (UK), low-lying coastal zones frequently experience inundation, flooding, landslides, coastal erosion, and cliff failures, all of which are intensified by climate change. Although the UK possesses one of Europe's longest and most geomorphologically diverse coastlines, this diversity limits the effectiveness of standard assessment tools such as the Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI), which often fail to capture site-specific characteristics. title: Unraveling antimalarial resistance in Plasmodium vivax in Southeast Asia: from molecular markers to phenotypic and clinical evidence—A scoping review
abstract: Abstract Background Plasmodium vivax antimalarial resistance remains an important but understudied challenge in Southeast Asia. Although several molecular polymorphisms have been investigated as potential markers of antimalarial resistance, the available evidence remains scarce and fragmented, particularly regarding their associations with phenotypic drug susceptibility and clinical treatment outcomes. title: High alkalinity mitigates the negative impacts of high-CO2 ocean on foraminiferal calcification quantity and quality
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification threatens marine calcifiers, but the independent effects of seawater pH and total alkalinity on shell formation remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally decoupled pH and alkalinity to examine their effects on shell growth and density in the large benthic foraminifer Amphisorus kudakajimensis . Low pH under present-day alkalinity substantially reduced shell weight, volume, and density, whereas simultaneously elevated alkalinity largely compensated for these negative effects. title: Distinct Structural Trajectories of Dissolved Organic Matter Across the Yangtze River Estuary
abstract: Abstract The Yangtze River Estuary (YRE) serves as a critical land‐ocean interface where hydrodynamic mixing and biogeochemical processes jointly regulate dissolved organic matter (DOM) cycling. However, the structural variability of DOM across estuarine gradients remains poorly understood. Here, untargeted metabolomics was applied to investigate the structural diversity and spatial variation of DOM in surface waters across the freshwater, transition and adjacent marine zones of the YRE. title: An opportunistic case study exploring the relevance of boat characteristics for noise monitoring in the very shallow waters of the Finnish Archipelago Sea
abstract: Underwater noise and its effects on marine life are globally recognized. While most research has focused on shipping noise in deep waters, noise emitted by small boats has gained attention in recent years. Recreational traffic’s contribution to coastal soundscapes is substantial, however assessments are currently challenged by several factors. title: Global Patterns in the Nutrient Composition Delivered by Seabirds to Coastal and Island Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Consumer‐mediated nutrient dynamics are crucial for sustaining ecosystems. While most research has focused on the magnitude of seabird‐derived nutrient fluxes, the role of species and diet composition in shaping nutrient quality remains largely unexplored. We aim to test whether the stoichiometric composition of seabird‐derived nutrient subsidies is spatially structured. Location Global. Time Period 1950–2025. title: Field testing the influence of settlement recesses and nighttime feeding lights on coral recruitment
abstract: Previous studies show that two promising technologies can increase recruitment probability and survival: (i) helix recesses for entraining coral larvae and (ii) night-time feeding lights for improving subsequent survival. We evaluated whether these technologies can be combined to improve coral settlement and survival under in situ reef conditions on concrete restoration modules designed for a large-scale hybrid reef deployment in Hawaiʻi. title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
abstract: Abstract Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens, comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. Here, we generated a high-quality de novo genome assembly of the starlet cushion star, Asterina gibbosa, enabling full-length gene identification of Sfps. title: Paleosalinity of Ediacaran fossils in South Australia
abstract: Ediacaran fossils of South Australia have been interpreted in two contrasting ways: marine invertebrates vs soil lichens. Paleosols with desert roses and eolian interbeds with adhesion warts are two lines of evidence, among many, for non-marine deposition. Geochemical paleosalinity indices provide new tests of these divergent interpretations. Boron content is low in freshwater, but high in marine rocks, and as a paleosalinity proxy can be compared with gallium (freshwater has B/Ga <3). title: Stable Isotope Research for Human Bioarchaeology in Southeast Asia: A Review of Research Trends, Gaps, and Opportunities
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the increasing number of studies undertaking isotopic analyses on archaeological material, some regions of the world and certain research foci remain underresearched and underrepresented. One of these regions is Southeast Asia, where bioarchaeological research was only comparatively recently established compared with other regions of the world. title: Labor transformation and sustainability risks in smallholder farm households: a scoping review from Indonesia
abstract: Labor transformation in smallholder farming households has become a critical yet underexplored dimension of agricultural sustainability, particularly in developing countries. This scoping review examines global research on labor transformation and its implications for agricultural sustainability, with a particular focus on Indonesia. Using the Arksey and O’Malley framework, the study integrates bibliometric analysis (VOSviewer) and thematic analysis (NVivo) to identify major research patterns and conceptual gaps in the literature. title: Shell hash promotes growth in Pacific littleneck clams ( Leukoma staminea ) by altering pore water chemistry
abstract: Abstract. Bivalves that build calcium carbonate skeletons are at particular risk from ocean acidification, and mitigation strategies will be needed to keep coastal populations healthy. It can be energetically costly for organisms like clams and mussels to build their shells under low pH conditions, and acidification can lead to shell dissolution. Adding crushed shells (shell hash) to beach sediments, a practice used by some Indigenous communities and aquaculturists, may mitigate the negative effects of ocean acidification by altering the chemistry of the pore fluids they live in. title: Steroid hormones produced by coral-associated Endozoicomonas influence coral immune response during thermal stress
abstract: The coral microbiome is believed to play a crucial role in sustaining corals and enabling adaptation to perturbations. A ubiquitous group of coral-associated bacteria, known as Endozoicomonas, are hypothesized to provide essential metabolites to corals, although detailed dynamics of the interactions between host and microbe are poorly understood. title: Anthropocene mineralogy and geochemistry of nearshore surface sediments from urban-influenced coastal zones of Athens (Greece) and Fujairah (UAE)
abstract: Abstract Coastal zones adjacent to urban areas and harbors are often impacted by marine traffic, shipyard activities, sewage discharge, and waste accumulation. These pressures interact with seafloor sediments composed mainly of inorganic particles, mixed with organic matter and marine biota. While most sediments contain common minerals such as quartz, clays, and Fe oxides/oxyhydroxides, increasing attention has focused on "Anthropocene minerals" introduced since the Industrial Revolution and the Atomic Age. title: Fine‐Scale Variability of Cold‐Water Coral and Sponge Communities on Protected Northeast Pacific Seamounts
abstract: ABSTRACT Cold‐water corals and sponges (CWCS) on Northeast Pacific seamounts form important biogenic habitat that is intersected by a broad oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) and exposed to ongoing deoxygenation. Many seamounts in this region lie within marine protected areas (MPAs), making an understanding of fine‐scale community structure particularly relevant for conservation and management. title: Seawater Quality and Heavy Metal (Cd, Pb, Zn) Accumulation in Green Mussels (Perna viridis), Cilincing, North Jakarta
abstract: Anthropogenic pressure in the coastal waters of Cilincing, North Jakarta, degrades water quality and threatens green mussel (Perna viridis) aquaculture safety. This study analyzed water quality status using the Pollution Index (PI), environmental parameter interactions via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Cd, Pb, and Zn bioaccumulation based on the Bioconcentration Factor (BCF) in P. viridis across five sampling stations representing estuary, reclamation, and nearest, middle, and farthest aquaculture zones. abstract: Groundwater potential zone mapping in the hilly coastal regions is becoming a prerequisite for sustainable groundwater resource management. The groundwater potential zones of Chattogram District were delineated by the integrated GIS-based Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy-AHP) approach. Ten groundwater-controlling thematic layers were prepared and reclassified, weighted with the AHP method and fuzzy-AHP, and integrated using weighted overlay analysis in ArcGIS. title: Coarse-mode sea spray aerosols enhance warm rain formation in marine low clouds
abstract: Abstract. Precipitation in low clouds affects cloud responses to aerosol perturbations, thereby impacting aerosol radiative forcing of climate, a significant but indeterminate contribution to uncertainty in future warming. The onset of drizzle formation in marine low clouds may be influenced by the presence of supermicron sea salt aerosols. title: AIS-based noise models underestimate vessel noise exposure risk to marine mammals
abstract: Vessels are the dominant source of anthropogenic underwater noise, with well-documented effects on marine mammal behaviour and physiology that may ultimately compromise individual fitness. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) provides standardized, global, high-resolution positional information for most commercial and passenger vessels, making AIS-based noise models widely used to assess exposure risk. institutions: University of Veterinary Medicine Hannover, Foundation

title: Environmental microbial communities and host selection shape larval microbiomes
abstract: Ocean warming is altering abiotic environments and biotic interactions experienced by marine organisms, where sensitive early developmental windows occur in biologically complex seawater communities. The impact of these interactions on developmental processes and fitness in hosts is not well understood, but likely contingent on the establishment of a host-associated microbiome. Here, we hypothesize that temperature and microbial exposure during embryogenesis influence larval microbiome assembly and host morphology. title: Algal metabolites effect on sea urchins: Reproductive disruption as a possible driver of coevolution
abstract: Chemical defenses shape ecological interactions across marine food webs, yet their reproductive and evolutionary consequences in macroalgae-grazer systems remain largely unexplored. Here, we integrate physiological, developmental and molecular assays to investigate how secondary metabolites from two brown algae, Ericaria brachycarpa and E. crinita, modulate reproduction and early development of their natural grazer sea urchin Arbacia lixula. title: From co‐occurrence to temporal coupling in a coral defender guild
abstract: Coral‐dwelling decapods can improve host fitness by defending corals against corallivores and sediment accumulation, yet the temporal dynamics linking co‐resident defenders remain poorly understood. Guard crabs Trapezia and snapping shrimp Alpheus provide complementary benefits to pocilloporid corals, and previous, largely cross‐sectional work has reported behavioral accommodation, non‐random co‐occurrence, and effects on host‐associated community assembly, patterns that suggest their association reflects facilitation instead of independent use of shared habitat. title: Distribution of Seahorses ( Hippocampus spp.) Along the Brazilian Coast Highlights Habitat Associations and Regions of Conservation Interest
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the geographic distribution and habitat associations of seahorses is fundamental for developing effective conservation strategies, yet comprehensive syntheses at national scales remain scarce. Brazil encompasses a wide diversity of coastal and marine ecosystems inhabited by three seahorse species ( Hippocampus reidi , H. erectus and Hippocampus patagonicus ), but available information has remained fragmented across scientific publications, museum collections, technical reports and monitoring programmes. title: A 4000-year record of parallel collapse in the ecological niche of Black Sea top predators
abstract: Marine ecosystems face multifaceted threats stemming from historical overexploitation and environmental degradation. Despite existing research, there are notable gaps in understanding the long-term dietary dynamics of marine organisms in the context of anthropogenic impacts. To address these gaps, we utilized stable isotope analysis as a proxy for dietary niche and examined changes in the Black Sea over a 4000-year period, focusing on ancient and contemporary samples from cetaceans ( Phocoena phocoena , Delphinus delphis , Tursiops truncatus ) and fish ( Scophthalmus maximus ). title: A coastal beach seed bank shows high diversity, but low similarity to the adjacent forest vegetation in an Amazonia Marine Extractive Reserve
abstract: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. title: Culture and Isolation of Bacteria Associated with Mediterranean Corals
abstract: ABSTRACT Corals harbor a diverse bacterial community that facilitates adaptation and sustains their health. In coral holobiont research, culture-independent approaches have transformed the existing paradigm. Molecular techniques, such as metabarcoding, revealed a high diversity of previously unrecognized bacterial symbionts. Coral microbiota characterization has relied on these techniques over the last decade, but relying solely on them does not provide a detailed understanding of the dynamics of the coral holobiont complex. title: Effects of Sustained Tensile Stress on Localized Corrosion Evolution of 5A06 Aluminum Alloy in Natural Seawater
abstract: ABSTRACT In marine engineering structures, components made of 5A06 aluminum alloy are often subjected simultaneously to sustained tensile stress and corrosion in natural seawater; their initial surface condition may further influence the initiation and propagation of localized corrosion. In this study, in situ potentiodynamic polarisation under constant load was combined with scanning electron microscopy and quantitative pit‐depth measurements to investigate the localized corrosion behavior of 5A06 aluminum alloy in natural seawater. title: Tubastraea coccinea (Cnidaria: Anthozoa) is the globally dispersed species of Sun Coral
abstract: Species of the genus Tubastraea (sun corals) have dispersed globally over recent decades, but morphological trait identification has led to taxonomic confusion, with multiple authors proposing conflicting species identifications due to high morphological plasticity and overlapping diagnostic traits. We combined global-scale molecular phylogenetics with chromosome-level genome assemblies to resolve this taxonomic issue. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the environmental niche and potential distribution of the Pacific sierra ( Scomberomorus sierra ) is critical for fisheries management across the eastern Pacific Ocean (EPO). We used MaxEnt to model S. sierra habitat suitability across the EPO (30° N–30° S to 120° W) using 169 vetted occurrence records and monthly CMEMS environmental layers (2004–2018): sea surface temperature (Temp), sea surface salinity (Sal), surface geostrophic currents (UCOMP, VCOMP), mixed layer depth (MLD), and sea surface anomalies (SSA). title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. title: Documenting the Undocumented: The Case for Integrating Local Water Ownership Into Marine Governance in Åland
abstract: Efforts to protect marine and coastal environments in Åland, Finland, increasingly emphasise integrating local water ownership into formal governance. This study examines how such integration can be strengthened, particularly in contexts where privately owned coastal waters and established management traditions are highly significant. By using Avelino’s empowerment framework, with a mixed-methods approach, the study addresses two questions: What approaches can be employed to identify biologically valuable marine areas in Åland that are not currently recognised or justified by the government? abstract: Abstract The most widespread animal life cycle includes a planktonic larval stage that is environmentally induced to settle and rapidly metamorphose into a benthic juvenile. Although this transition is critical for survival, how planetary cues such as light interact with local ecological signals to prepare the genome for such rapid reprogramming remains poorly understood. title: Fossil shark teeth record a microscale pathway for ferromanganese oxide nucleation and Li–Ni enrichment in deep-sea biogenic substrates
abstract: Abstract Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. Here, we integrate Micro-CT, SEM-EDS, EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, TEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XANES to reconstruct the initial stages of Fe–Mn oxide (FMO) formation in fossil shark teeth from the Rio Grande Rise (southwestern Atlantic Ocean). title: Assessing Diversity, Carbon Stock Quantification and Economic Valuation of Mangrove Forest along the Coastal Areas of Davao Oriental, Philippines
abstract: This study assessed the diversity, aboveground carbon stock, and economic value of mangrove forests along the coastal areas of Davao Oriental, Philippines. Field-based mangrove inventories were conducted using three 100-m transects comprising 20 plots and a total sampled area of 2000 m². The sampling was intended to characterize the mangrove community at the assessed field sites and is not treated as statistically representative of all mangrove forests in the province. abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs are essential ecosystems for the functioning of the planet and human well-being, providing three-dimensional habitats for a great diversity of marine life and multiple ecological, economic, and cultural services. Coral reefs are constructed by hermatypic corals, which maintain a symbiotic relationship with dinoflagellates of the Symbiodiniaceae family, which provide them with up to 90-95% of their energy in exchange for shelter and nutrients. abstract: Lycengraulis grossidens is economically important for artisanal fisheries and prey of top predators in the Río de la Plata (RP) (SW Atlantic). title: Analysis of Coastal Abrasion Vulnerability at Pasar Bawah Beach, South Bengkulu, Using Landsat Imagery
abstract: Recently, Pasar Bawah Beach has been facing the risk of rapid abrasion, threatening damage to the infrastructure around the beach. This study aims to identify the rate of abrasion and map changes in the coastline and the characteristics of parameters that influence abrasion at Pasar Bawah Beach in Manna, South Bengkulu. abstract: Abstract Surface and groundwater resources in semi-arid coastal regions are highly susceptible to salinity buildup, hydrochemical changes, and human activities, which compromise their usability for drinking, irrigation, and industry. This study assesses the hydrogeochemistry, spatial variation, and suitability of surface and groundwater in Gujarat's Coastal District Porbandar (CDP). abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean warming is currently leading to distributional shifts of species and an alternation of coastal communities. Vulnerable species that are most sensitive to ocean warming are able to use several acclimation mechanisms, with one of the fastest being a shift in and shuffling of their partnerships with symbiotic microorganisms. abstract: Abstract Given the unprecedented climate-induced impacts on the marine environment, the conduct-oriented marine environmental protection obligation (MEPO) has become highly inadequate. This article argues for a normative evolution of the obligation in response to the global climate crisis. By examining key advisory opinions of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea and the International Court of Justice, this study analyzes the interpretation of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea as a dynamic instrument. abstract: Early life history traits strongly influence survival and recruitment in small pelagic fishes, yet regional variation in these traits remains poorly understood for young-of-the-year (age-0) mackerels in Kuroshio-influenced coastal systems. We examined diet composition, onset of piscivory, otolith-based growth, and hatch-date composition of juvenile chub mackerel Scomber japonicus and blue mackerel Scomber australasicus collected from the Uwa Sea, western Japan, in 2021, 2022, and 2025. abstract: As the global water stress intensifies, seawater desalination (SWD) is increasingly deployed as a supply-side strategy for enhancing freshwater availability. Critical scholarship has questioned whether technically oriented approaches to desalination adequately address the socio-political drivers of water scarcity and the governance conditions shaping desalination policy. Sediment environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding can complement existing survey methods, but its ability to discriminate among habitats and to reliably assign taxa must be critically evaluated. Here, we analyzed sediment samples from 10 areas in the Nordic Seas and adjacent Arctic, including the Arctic Mid‐Ocean Ridge (AMOR), continental slope habitats, and abyssal environments. abstract: This study examines the spatial relationships among three religious landmarks in Nha Trang, Vietnam: the Ponagar Cham temple complex, Long Son Pagoda and its hilltop Buddha statue, and the Catholic Stone Church. title: Public perceptions and knowledge of nationwide shellfish reef restoration
abstract: Large-scale restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems is increasingly used to address biodiversity loss, yet its long-term success depends on public awareness, understanding, and support. Despite rapid expansion in shellfish reef restoration worldwide, little is known about how the public perceive these ecosystems or the value of restoring them. We surveyed 867 coastal and metropolitan residents living within ~50 km of shellfish reef restorations across Australia to assess public knowledge, perceptions, and perceived benefits of shellfish restoration. abstract: The research is dedicated to the study of the ecogeographic distribution of the Cyperaceae Juss. family in Azerbaijan, related to the dynamic changes occurring in plant communities formed under the influence of landscape diversity and climatic factors through RS (Remote Sensing) and GIS. Based on the results of the study, 115 taxa consisting of 14 genera belonging to the Cyperaceae family were identified. title: Geochemical and granulometric fingerprints of 8200 years of westerly wind variability in inner‐fjord lake sediments from Svalbard
abstract: The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on Earth. As sea-ice diminishes, surface boundary conditions (roughness and air-sea coupling) change and open-water fetch increases, potentially strengthening the effective wind forcing on Arctic coasts. These changes can be recorded in lake sediments through the deposition of wind-blown grains and elements, offering insights into past wind and climate dynamics. abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs are increasingly threatened by climate change and local anthropogenic stressors, prompting the development of artificial substrates for reef restoration. Although substrate material is often considered a key design variable, the relative influence of surface topography on early benthic colonization remains insufficiently resolved. Objective: To evaluate the effects of experimental substrate material and surface topography on early benthic community assembly at Islote Zacatoso reef, Mexican Pacific. abstract: Metagenomic characterization of foodborne pathogens in Nigerian seafood remains critically limited. This sentinel case investigated Vibrio species in a single crab (Callinectes spp.) from Eleko Beach, Lagos, Nigeria, using shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the PacBio Onso platform. title: The Noisy Work of Uncertainty Visualization
abstract: Better representation of the uncertainty in a data visualization is a focus of recent research activity. A problem with the current literature is that there is a lack of clarity about the definition of uncertainty and what it means to represent it in a plot. This confusion has led to conflicting results in the literature, especially in experiments that assess the effectiveness of different uncertainty representations. title: Negative Residual Topography in Global Back‐Arc Basins Scales With Slab Dip
abstract: Abstract Dynamic topography above subduction zones is widely inferred, but its magnitude and controls remain poorly constrained at the global scale. Here, we estimate residual topography across a range of back‐arc basins by correcting bathymetry for sediment loading, crustal structure, and lithospheric age, and compare the anomalies with slab geometry and subduction parameters. Most basins show negative residual topography, and the anomalies become more negative with increasing slab dip. title: Population genetic structure and spring−summer spatial distribution of common minke whales (Balaenoptera acutorostrata) in feeding grounds and migratory corridors of the western North Pacific
abstract: Abstract Information on population genetic structure, movement, and distribution is fundamental for effective management of marine species. In the western North Pacific, the common minke whale faces both bycatch and commercial whaling, the latter having resumed in Japanese waters in 2019. In this study, we refined the population genetic structure and spring–summer spatial distribution of this species using 6196 genetic samples collected in feeding grounds and migratory corridors during 1994–2024. abstract: Known as the Troad in ancient sources, the Biga Peninsula has been one of the principal settlement regions of northwestern Anatolia since prehistoric times. The coastal settlements lining the Çanakkale Strait provided an important geographical setting for interregional interaction throughout prehistory. title: Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio-temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio-temporal variation.
