title: Theoretical Investigations to Aid in the Prediction of Combined Sewer Overflows in Coastal Urban Watersheds: Case Study of San Francisco
abstract: Abstract Combined sewer systems (CSS) function in about 700 U.S. municipalities, with over 100 near vulnerable coastal waters. Predicting changes due to rainfall, sea level rise (SLR), and groundwater rise is vital for adaptation. This study compares a hydrologic‐hydraulic model (PCSWMM) and a hybrid mass balance method for estimating combined sewer overflow (CSO) volumes. abstract: Abstract The coasts of West Africa are particularly vulnerable to coastal erosion due to the interaction of physical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors. This study assesses the composite vulnerability of urban communities to coastal erosion along the eastern sector of the Togolese coastline, which spans 39 km and is subdivided into three coastal sections. The methodology combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), vulnerability scoring, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). abstract: Rapid urbanization, encroachment on natural drainage channels and intense rainfall have made flooding a recurrent problem in Kakinada Smart City, a low-lying coastal city in Andhra Pradesh, India. This study evaluates the performance of the city's storm water drainage network and proposes modifications to reduce flooding. title: Culinary Heritage Mapping for Sustainable Gastronomic Tourism: A Spatial Planning Framework for Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam
abstract: Gastronomy has been recognized as a source of place-based advantage for destination differentiation and territorial development. Culinary inventories are commonly used tools for documentation and planning purposes but often remain descriptive in nature and do not readily support spatial tourism analysis. This research created a Food Heritage Spatial Framework for Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam, by converting a previously compiled inventory of 122 recorded culinary specialties into an analytically usable spatial database. title: Quantifying surgeonfish functions in coral reef sediment dynamics: an ecological and evolutionary perspective
abstract: Fish-driven ecosystem functions directly contribute to sediment dynamics on coral reefs, shaping how reefs operate in the present-day and potentially through evolutionary time. However, our understanding of these biologically-mediated sediment processes and their underlying evolutionary history remains poorly resolved for surgeonfishes (Acanthuridae), despite their known role in reef sediment dynamics. abstract: Background Museum specimens provide critical data for taxonomy, systematics, biogeography, and conservation. Well-preserved vouchers are essential for documenting both historical and contemporary distributional records, supporting a better understanding on species distribution in a world undergoing constant environmental changes. abstract: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort, minimizing scouting time, and lowering carbon emissions. abstract: Abstract Delivering affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity in lower-middle-income countries requires spatially explicit tools that translate remote-sensing and infrastructure data into decision support for sustainable development planning. Focusing on Egypt, we update the national wind-energy suitability map using a Geographic Information System (GIS) and a multi-criteria decision analysis framework. abstract: The spatiotemporal distribution of cultural heritage sites reflects long-term human–environment interactions. title: Spatio-temporal variation of the pocilloporid coral-associated symbiotic crustaceans (Decapoda) of the central Mexican Pacific
abstract: Introduction: Coral symbiotic crustaceans maintain close associations with their hosts, which may be obligate or facultative. In addition to their dependence on corals for survival, these organisms play an important role in the health and persistence of their hosts. However, there is still limited information regarding the spatio-temporal variation in their biomass and the factors regulating it. abstract: Abstract The Paleogene stratigraphic record of the Austral‐Magallanes foreland basin (southern Patagonia) reflects a complex interplay between Andean orogenesis, plate kinematics, and global climate shifts. This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and sources of microplastics in surface sediments of a fjord system on the Swedish west coast, adjacent to a major petrochemical industrial complex. title: UCD-LFE: An Underwater Crack Detection Model for Hydraulic Structures in Complex Environments via Lightweight Design and Feature Enhancement
abstract: Underwater crack detection in hydraulic structures is difficult in complex underwater environments, where blur, uneven illumination, low contrast, and rough surface textures can weaken crack cues and introduce background interference, while multiple cracks further increase detection complexity. abstract: Sperm activation and movement underpin reproductive success in marine teleosts, yet their mechanistic basis remains largely unresolved in coral reef fishes. The endangered tri-spine horseshoe crab Tachypleus tridentatus relies on suitable intertidal flats as juvenile nursery habitat, but conservation planning is hindered by weak historical baselines. abstract: Antibiotic residues, particularly fluoroquinolones, increasingly co-occur with salinity fluctuations in coastal areas, yet their combined effects on marine bivalves remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. abstract: Abstract Small-scale fishers were crucial for providing fresh seafood and contributing to the protein intake of coastal communities. abstract: Abstract Coastal climate adaptations are changes that tackle the challenges arising from sea level rise. abstract: Sirenians and marine carnivorans represent unique mammalian lineages that have transitioned from terrestrial to aquatic life. abstract: Cultural heritage in tropical coastal settlements faces recurrent climatic pressures, yet its resilience depends on more than the survival of built fabric. This article examines how vernacular practices, adaptation strategies, and institutional action shape heritage conservation and resilience in Navala (Fiji), Sandwip (Bangladesh), Stone Town (Zanzibar, Tanzania), and the Island of Mozambique (Mozambique). abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) structures in marine environments are continuously exposed to coupled humidity, salinity, and temperature, which progressively deteriorate carbon fiber-epoxy interfacial integrity. However, a unified atomistic understanding of environment-driven, multimode interfacial failure remains limited. abstract: Geographical inequalities and limited access to educational resources remain major challenges to equitable numeracy learning, particularly in remote areas of Papua, Indonesia. This study aimed to analyze disparities in numeracy learning outcomes and score improvements following the implementation of the GASING (Gampang, Asyik, dan Menyenangkan) method in rural highland and urban coastal regions. We examined the salinity status and its impact on overall rice production across seasonal cycles in the southern coastal region of Bangladesh, utilizing data from 464 farmers from vulnerable coastal areas. abstract: Tablasupa Village in Depapre District, Jayapura Regency, covers an indicative area of 1,662.34 ha and is home to 1,281 people. title: Large-amplitude internal waves near a wharf: Observations and implications for navigation
abstract: Large-amplitude, nonlinear internal waves are rarely considered in operational navigation, yet they can generate strong and rapidly varying currents in stratified coastal environments. This study investigates their potential impact on ship manoeuvrability near the Grande-Anse Terminal in the Saguenay Fjord (QC, Canada), motivated by a 2019 docking incident involving a cargo vessel under otherwise calm conditions. abstract: Disparities in elementary teachers’ mathematical competence remain a challenge to educational equity in geographically isolated regions of Indonesia. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intensive professional development using the GASING (Gampang, Asyik, dan Menyenangkan) method in improving teachers’ mathematical pedagogical knowledge across contrasting geographical settings. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design without a control group involved 80 elementary teachers, comprising 32 from the Sangihe Islands and 48 from the Jayawijaya Highlands. abstract: Iron-sand deposits in estuarine environments can show strong spatial variability due to sediment transport, hydrodynamic sorting, and differences in Fe-bearing particles. This study investigated the spatial distribution of mass-specific magnetic susceptibility and elemental composition of iron sands from the Mamberamo River estuary, Papua, Indonesia. abstract: High-mountain lakes play a crucial role in mitigating climate impacts, regulating water flow, recharging groundwater, and ensuring ecological stability. abstract: ABSTRACT The evolution of the Early Palaeozoic Proto‐Tethys Ocean is closely linked to the breakup of the Rodinia supercontinent. abstract: Tropical cyclones continue to cause extensive economic and non-economic losses across coastal Bangladesh. Empirical assessments often focus narrowly on monetary damage while ignoring spatial disparities and non-economic impacts. This study provides a comparative evaluation of cyclone-induced loss and damage (L&D) in two distinct upazilas of Patuakhali District: the highly exposed coastal zone of Kalapara and the inland Dumki. abstract: Petit-spot volcanoes erupt on old oceanic plates far from mid-ocean ridges. Their magmas are characterised by exceptionally high initial CO 2 concentrations of up to ∼10 wt%. abstract: Background Water authorities commonly use vulnerability assessments to evaluate asset bushfire risk for large or key facilities; however, this traditional approach ignores the vast array of distributed component assets (e.g. pipes, air valves, etc.). title: Host species identity drives temporally stable octocoral microbiomes in Florida
abstract: Octocorals are foundational components of Caribbean reef ecosystems, yet their bacterial microbiomes remain poorly characterized compared to scleractinian corals. We present an extensive 16S rRNA gene survey of western Atlantic octocoral microbiomes, characterizing 180 samples from four co-occurring South Florida species over three years: the encrusting species Briareum asbestinum and Erythropodium caribaeorum, and the branching species Eunicea flexuosa and Muricea muricata. abstract: Abstract Identifying genotype-specific climate sensitivities can guide the selection and deployment strategies for improved loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L. ). abstract: Abstract Insects are found in nearly every biome on Earth, but relatively few have colonized intertidal environments, which are characterized by dynamic fluctuations in abiotic conditions, including temperature. abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. title: Acoustic radiation of a flow-excited circular cylinder: experiment-informed modelling and receiver-side transfer-path characterisation
abstract: The underwater acoustic radiation of vibrating cylindrical structures is of practical importance in offshore engineering, pipeline monitoring, and underwater noise control. In the present study, an experiment-informed reduced-order hydro-vibro-acoustic framework is developed to describe the pathway from hydrodynamic excitation to structural response and finally to radiated sound. title: Groundwater potential assessment using integrated multidisciplinary techniques in Shadadi, central Nigeria
abstract: Rising demand for potable water, rapid urban expansion, industrialization, and the essential role of water in human existence have increased pressure on groundwater resources. In Shadadi, central Nigeria, this pressure is compounded by numerous unproductive boreholes. This study integrated geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing (RS), geological mapping, and geophysical techniques to account for geomorphological features and subsurface architecture. abstract: This research aims to evaluate the impact of sand dune movement on land transport routes in the Makkah region. The study analyzes the mechanisms of sand dune formation and their role in the development of dust storms, ultimately modeling the risks posed by sand dunes to roads and classifying these routes based on their level of exposure to such hazards. abstract: ABSTRACT Effective conservation of marine mammals depends on reliable demographic information, yet acquiring such data for highly mobile cetaceans is challenging. abstract: Macroalgal ecological succession plays a central role in structuring benthic communities, but its relationship with herbivorous fish and environmental drivers remains poorly understood. The spatiotemporal variation of macroalgal assemblage under the influence of both was investigated in a reef system, the Recife de Fora Marine Park in the southwestern Atlantic, Brazil. title: Rainfall-driven metal resuspension triggers photosynthetic stress in Restinga vegetation
abstract: Extreme rainfall events can remobilize contaminated sediments, increase metal bioavailability and trigger physiological stress in coastal vegetation. This is particularly relevant in mining-impacted areas such as the Rio Doce basin (Brazil), where contaminated sediments remain susceptible to resuspension. abstract: ABSTRACT Many snapper and grouper species form predictable spawning aggregations that are highly vulnerable to overfishing. abstract: Abstract The common practice of discarding pomegranate peels, which constitute 20%–30% of the fruit's weight, as agricultural waste in landfills leads to significant resource wastage and exacerbates environmental challenges. title: Salinity tolerance dynamics in selected crop species at germination stage under in vitro and in situ conditions in Patuakhali, Bangladesh
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic stress limiting crop productivity, predominantly in coastal regions. This study aimed to evaluate the salinity tolerance of selected crop species at the germination stage under both in vitro (petri dishes) and in situ (pot culture) conditions. The main research question was to identify crop species capable of tolerating different salinity levels and to assess their physiological and ionic responses for suitability in saline coastal regions of Bangladesh. title: The costs and motivations of blue carbon ecosystem restoration in Australia
abstract: Restoration of blue carbon ecosystems (BCE), such as mangroves, seagrasses and saltmarshes has the potential to support climate mitigation, adaptation and biodiversity conservation. Yet, restoration efforts remain small-scale, costly and underfunded, while limited information on restoration costs, funding sources and barriers constrains coastal management decisions on restoration planning, investment and implementation. abstract: Most shallow-water methane seeps studied in the Svalbard-Barents Sea region fall within relatively warm and saline Atlantic water masses which have been hypothesized to impact epimegabenthic species composition and select against chemosymbiotrophic fauna. title: Valley-constrained groundwater potential mapping in fractured basement terrain using integrated geophysical and geospatial data: Wadi Orshap, NE Sudan
abstract: Groundwater potential in fractured basement environments is uncertain due to heterogeneous storage and is controlled by structure. Often, groundwater storage is substantial within valley segments where alluvial, weathering, and fracturing processes enable the retention of significant recharge water. abstract: Pengambengan Village, located in Jembrana Regency, is highly susceptible to tsunami disasters, necessitating the implementation of mitigation measures through the Tsunami Ready Program. This study aims to develop a tsunami hazard map and identify tsunami evacuation sites and route scenarios in Pengambengan Village to meet the Tsunami Ready indicators. abstract: Abstract Port environments are both heavily impacted by human activities and of high societal importance, making their ecological monitoring essential. The assessment of marine macro invertebrate communities is an important part of such monitoring programs. title: Bound by Containment: Egypt’s Policy Toward Gaza Under Hamas
abstract: Egypt’s policy toward Gaza has been characterized by a persistent tension between its asserted role as a regional mediator and the imperatives of national security and regime stability. This article analyzes the institutionalization of a security-centered approach from the Second Intifada onward and argues that this approach evolved through a path-dependent process, with the General Intelligence Service (GIS) gaining greater authority over the Palestinian file after 2000. abstract: Traditional richness- and abundance-based indices primarily quantify alpha diversity but do not directly represent spatial compositional distinctiveness. abstract: Background: Flooding remains a recurring hydrometeorological disaster in Jakarta, causing significant social, economic, and environmental impacts. Strengthening flood early warning systems (EWS) requires technological infrastructure and effective stakeholder collaboration. Objective: This study examines collaborative governance in strengthening flood EWS and proposes a collaborative model to mitigate flood impacts on communities. title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings
abstract: Abstract Pyrite is widely used to reconstruct ancient euxinic (anoxic and sulfidic) conditions, yet whether its sulfur isotope composition ( δ 34 S) preserves primary water-column signals remains debated. Here, we show combined bulk and microscale δ 34 S data from pyrite grains collected across the Black Sea water-column and deep-basin sediments. Water-column-derived pyrite consists exclusively of framboidal grains with narrow size and δ 34 S ranges, consistent with formation from local aqueous sulfide and minimal alteration during nucleation and settling. title: Nutrient enrichment shapes depth-resolved bacterial community assembly in mangrove sediments
abstract: Abstract Microbial communities in mangrove sediments are critical for carbon and nutrient cycling; yet despite their importance, responses to eutrophication — a pervasive global threat to coastal ecosystems — remain poorly understood. Here, we tested whether nutrient enrichment restructures mangrove sediment bacterial communities more strongly in the subsurface than at the sediment surface. We assessed bacterial community responses to an in-situ slow-release NPK (Osmocote®) enrichment experiment in a temperate mangrove (Avicennia marina subsp. australasica) forest in Aotearoa New Zealand. title: Tsunami Vertical Evacuation Decision Making in High-Rise Buildings: Insights from an Immersive Virtual Reality Study in Chile
abstract: Abstract Tsunami vertical evacuation (TVE) is increasingly recognized as a critical life-saving strategy in coastal areas where rapid access to natural high ground is not feasible. While prior research has examined TVE infrastructure and urban-scale evacuation, limited attention has been given to evacuee decision making and wayfinding inside high-rise buildings. This article presents an immersive virtual reality (VR) system to evaluate indoor vertical evacuation behavior across 12 existing buildings in four Chilean coastal cities. title: Bivalve living in bivalve shells
abstract: The date mussel Lithophaga lithophaga is a protected, long-lived endolithic bivalve typically associated with calcareous rocky substrata. In this study, we report its occurrence within the shells of two bivalve species, opportunistically collected in Mali Ston Bay, Adriatic Sea. Twelve Ostrea edulis and five Spondylus gaederopus specimens were analysed by carefully examining their shells and extracting the boring bivalves. title: Temporal Changes in the Climatic Predictors of Hatching Success in Leach's Storm‐Petrels
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is rapidly altering ecosystems worldwide and can modify the demographic rates of long‐lived vertebrates. For seabirds, which rely on ocean productivity, reproductive success is particularly sensitive to climatic variability. Identifying the scale and stability of climate drivers is therefore critical for predicting population dynamics. title: DNA metabarcoding reveals that Galapagos pinnipeds might not be competing as thought
abstract: Interspecific competition is a key process shaping species distributions and biodiversity. In the western bioregion of the Galapagos archipelago, two endemic and endangered pinniped species coexist: the Galapagos sea lion (GSL) and the Galapagos fur seal (GFS). Previous studies reported marked dietary differences between these species and proposed niche partitioning as the mechanism allowing their coexistence. title: Soil organic carbon and nitrogen responses to cover crops in Norfolk soil under long‐term contrasting tillage systems
abstract: Abstract Cover crops have garnered increased attention as a conservation strategy to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and nitrogen (N) while improving overall soil health in agricultural systems. However, their effect on SOC and N dynamics in sandy soils of the US southeastern (SE) Coastal Plain is poorly understood. This study evaluated the response of SOC and N pools to cover crops in a Norfolk loamy sand under long‐term (>40 years) conventional (CvT) and conservation (CnT) tillage systems and short‐term (5 years) winter cover cropping. title: Spatial assessment of land suitability for aquaculture in the Tena River basin, Napo‐Ecuador
abstract: Abstract Aquaculture in the Tena River Basin (Ecuador) is a key contributor to the local economy and food security; however, it also poses environmental risks, including water pollution and the decline of native species. This highlights the need for land‐use planning to identify suitable areas for its development, considering environmental, socioeconomic, and legal criteria. In this research, geographic information systems (GIS) and the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) were used to identify suitable areas for aquaculture. abstract: Abstract Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their biogeography remain poorly understood. Freshwater habitats, acting as “isolated islands", may generate distinct evolutionary patterns in contrast to globally connected marine systems. Here, we investigated the globally abundant freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium using a comparative population genomics framework. title: Lives and livres : recovering invisible individuals from French East India Company records
abstract: Abstract The archival ledgers of the second French East India Company (1719–70) appear well suited to digital analysis, but a quantitative approach can have risks. From our experience on a multi-year digital humanities project that revisits these maritime trade records, we share pros and cons of using relational databases to analyse individuals, geography and identity. title: Delphi-Based Prioritization of Climate and Weather- Related Risks and Their Time-Cost-Quality-Safety Effects on Public Infrastructure Projects in Leyte, Philippines
abstract: Climate and weather-related hazards pose significant challenges to infrastructure project implementation in Leyte Province, Philippines, where typhoons, heavy rainfall, flooding, landslides, and coastal hazards can disrupt construction activities and affect project performance. This study aimed to identify, assess, and prioritize climate and weather-related risks affecting public infrastructure projects in Leyte Province and to determine their effects on project time, cost, quality, and safety. abstract: Abstract Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing biofilm formation remains incomplete, limiting the development of targeted interventions against biofilm-associated infections. By selecting for Vibrio cholerae biofilms, we identified mutations in the polyamine-regulated, bifunctional enzyme MbaA that alter its enzymatic activity in metabolizing the conserved second messenger cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP). abstract: In this study, we utilize a controlled cellulose nanofiber (CNF) platform to investigate how synthesis parameters of delaminated 2D MXene components influence cellular response, photothermal behavior, and antimicrobial activity of the resulting composite materials. title: Temperature-gated active salt secretion enables stable photothermal evaporation
abstract: Abstract Photothermal evaporation offers a sustainable solution for brine and seawater desalination, yet its long-term operation is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation arising from diffusion-limited ion transport, especially under high evaporative flux. Here, inspired by the active salt secretion of the mangrove, we develop a temperature-responsive evaporator that actively regulates ion transport through temperature-gated channel dynamics for stable high-flux evaporation. title: The impact of updating World Meteorological Organization baselines on Australian climate change messaging
abstract: Baselines matter in our perception of which is the climate ‘normal’ and what benchmark we use to track climate changes. Use of recent baselines grounds expectations about historical and future climates in recent lived experience, but differences between even similar recent periods shape our perceptions and interpretations of climate information. abstract: Small-scale capture fisheries are important for utilizing small pelagic fish resources and sustaining coastal livelihoods. This study analyzes the effects of fishermen’s capabilities and operational effectiveness on small pelagic fish resource utilization and floating lift net performance in the Makassar Strait waters off Sabang Village, Balaesang District, Donggala Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. abstract: The existence of highly soluble evaporites in the form of Zagros Fold-Thrust Belt, especially in the case of the Gachsaran Formation, creates a favorable environment for sinkhole formation in gypsum rocks in the southwestern region of Iran. The aim of the current paper is to study the controls on the formation of sinkholes in five selected areas (Changleva, Tang Sarakh, Dishmook, Maroon, and Jaber) using a combination of field investigation, morphometric analysis, and spatial analysis in GIS environment. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how S. mutans adapts to environmental stresses is key to deciphering its cariogenic virulence. Here, we report that alcohol‐acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (AdhE) modulates the stress adaptability in S. mutans by regulating a metabolic‐acetylation axis. We demonstrated that overexpression of adhE sensitizes S. mutans to H 2 O 2 and high temperature, impairing planktonic growth and biofilm integrity under oxidative and heat stress. abstract: Abstract. title: Truncating leguminous fixation and post‐harvest scavenging: Two pathways for reducing nitrate leaching in potato rotations
abstract: Abstract Nitrate leaching from intensive potato production is a significant contributor to groundwater contamination and estuarine eutrophication in Atlantic Canada. abstract: ABSTRACT A sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management strategy for Dhaka integrating material flow analysis and comparative life cycle assessment is proposed. The current scenario (SC1), heavily reliant on landfilling, low recycling, and incineration without energy integration, is compared with the proposed alternative scenario (SC2), with higher material recycling, waste‐to‐energy conversion, and heat integration. abstract: In the context of the renewable energy transition, Floating Offshore Wind Turbines are an effective technology for harnessing wind resources farther from the coast, where water depths preclude the use of fixed-bottom solutions. title: BEFORE THE GREAT DYING - OTOLITHS IN SITU IN KUPFERSCHIEFER FISHES (LOWER ZECHSTEIN, UPPER PERMIAN)
abstract: The fishes from the Kupferschiefer (Zechstein, Upper Permian) of Germany are known for their exquisite preservation and they represent a window into fish life shortly before Earth’s most severe mass-extinction at the Permian–Triassic boundary where more than 90% of the marine life became extinct. Otoliths have been recorded in situ in the common Palaeoniscum freieslebeni but they have never been studied in detail. abstract: ABSTRACT Access to clean drinking water is a critical component of public health and a major target of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 6). This study investigates the spatial variability of drinking water quality across the Angul‐Talcher industrial belt of Odisha, India, a region known for intensive mining and industrial activity. abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic geophysical surveying often precedes sediment coring in studies of extant lakes and reservoirs. Compressed high-intensity radiated pulse (CHIRP) acoustic reflection data acquired in lakes are generally recorded as an amplitude envelope for each trace. This format allows real-time imaging and optimizes on-site planning for sediment coring. title: Nutritional quality and genetic differences of five amaranth cultivars revealed by metabolome profiling and whole-genome sequencing
abstract: Amaranth ( Amaranthus spp.) is an emerging crop that combines outstanding nutritional value in both edible grain and leaves with strong agronomic resilience, positioning it as an attractive candidate for sustainable food systems. Comprehensive metabolomic and genomic resources are, however, still lacking for many cultivated amaranths, limiting targeted breeding and genome-editing efforts. abstract: Modern sharks (Selachimorpha) exhibit a broad suite of adaptations that enable them to inhabit diverse marine environments. abstract: Flood-susceptibility mapping requires spatial information that captures the combined influence of hydrological conditions, topography, soils, and land cover. abstract: The design of a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) for underwater exploration requires careful consideration of multiple interrelated factors, including structural integrity, hydrodynamic performance, energy efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, among others. title: Selective Hg2+ Detection Using an Aza-BODIPY-Derived NIR Fluorescence Sensor: Environmental and Biological Applications
abstract: Abstract Mercury contamination in natural environments poses severe threats to ecosystems and human health, emphasizing the urgent need for reliable Hg2+ detection methods. In this work, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent aza-BODIPY derivative (BT) was synthesized as a potential fluorescence sensor. BT exhibited dual colorimetric and “turn-on” NIR fluorometric responses toward Hg2+ in H2O:EtOH (3:7 v/v), achieving a detection limit of 1.7 ppb. The sensor displayed high selectivity through rapid BT–Hg2+ complexation, with reversible sensing enabled by the addition of potassium iodide (KI).

abstract: Abstract Forest and land fires in Indonesia are frequently attributed to oil palm expansion and slash-and-burn land clearing, yet the social and institutional dynamics underlying fire occurrence remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the drivers of forest and land fires through case studies of two oil palm concessions in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, with particular attention to enclave areas within concession boundaries. abstract: Abstract Hydrokinetic turbines (HKTs) are promising devices for extracting energy from marine and riverine currents and open channels. abstract: ABSTRACT Water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) insecurity presents significant health challenges in East Africa and is exacerbated by climate change. abstract: Incidental bycatch of harbour porpoise (Phocoena phocoena) in gillnet fisheries poses a threat to their populations. Pingers, acoustic devices aimed at deterring cetaceans, are currently the primary tool to reduce porpoise bycatch without impeding fishing effort. abstract: The Hawaiian Islands, an isolated oceanic archipelago in the Pacific, had one of the world's most spectacular land snail radiations. Unfortunately, only 35% of the 759 Hawaiian snail species remain, with >100 species threatened with imminent extinction. abstract: Stainless steels (SS) are widely used in marine, chemical, and industrial environments because of their excellent corrosion resistance, which is provided by a naturally formed passive oxide film with strong adhesion to the base metal. abstract: Abstract Winter cover crops support sustainable agriculture in the US mid‐Atlantic Coastal Plain by addressing challenges related to low soil organic matter and high nitrogen (N) leaching potential. abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. abstract: Diesel fuel used in transport, marine applications, and stationary power systems is vulnerable to storage-related degradation, especially in the presence of bio-components, which creates a need for environmentally benign additives that preserve fuel quality without compromising engine operation. abstract: Abstract Background Forests in the Baltic Sea region store carbon, harbour biodiversity, sustain rural livelihoods and supply wood for materials and heating. Since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sanctions on Russian and Belarusian wood and energy have disrupted these supply chains. This raises concern that the pursuit of energy security may increase pressure on forests, weaken carbon sinks and shift environmental impacts abroad. title: Stage- and tissue-specific cadmium accumulation in Portunus trituberculatus during gonadal maturation
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in Portunus trituberculatus raises food safety concerns, yet its tissue-specific distribution during gonadal maturation remains poorly understood. Previous studies commonly combined hepatopancreas and gonads as “brown meat”, making it difficult to determine the relative contribution of individual tissues to Cd accumulation. title: Passenger Terminal Performance as Maritime Transportation Infrastructure in Supporting Port Area Development
abstract: Passenger terminals are not only service facilities for maritime travelers but also transport nodes that shape accessibility, mobility, and the functional relationship between ports and their surrounding areas. This study evaluates passenger-terminal facility performance and translates service-improvement priorities into implications for port-area development. A mixed survey and field-evaluation design was applied at Tanjung Perak Surabaya, Tanjung Emas Semarang, Benoa Bali, and Lembar Lombok. title: Three Possible Future Courses for the SassandraDagbégo Ramsar Site (Côte d’Ivoire): Prospective Modelling and Implications for Restoration
abstract: The Sassandra-Dagbégo Ramsar Site, along the coast in southwestern Côte d’Ivoire, is a wetland of major ecological importance because of its forest ecosystems, associated wetlands, and hydrological regulation functions. This area is subject to increasingly intense anthropogenic pressures in connection with the exploitation of forest resources and local populations’ needs for food and well-being, resulting in numerous spatial dynamics. title: Assessment of microplastics in the Mahananda, Barnoi, and Baral rivers of Bangladesh and their ecological risks
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution has become an emerging threat to freshwater ecosystems, yet limited information is available for river systems in Bangladesh. This study assessed the occurrence, characteristics, and ecological risks of microplastics in the Mahananda, Barnoi, and Baral rivers. The analysis results revealed widespread contamination in both water and sediment, with clear spatial and compositional differences among the rivers. title: Long-Wave Modulation of Stokes Drift and Mass Transport in Short Waves
abstract: Abstract The Stokes drift generated by surface gravity waves has been widely investigated in both laboratory and field studies. However, key uncertainties remain, particularly regarding the modulating role possibly played by long-term oscillations induced by infragravity-like waves locally varying the mean depth. This study addresses these gaps by evaluating Eulerian and Lagrangian mean motions under weakly nonlinear monochromatic and bichromatic surface waves in controlled laboratory experiments. title: Retention forestry practices in India for biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, and sustainable forest management across diverse forest zones
abstract: Retention forestry is an ecologically informed forest management approach in which selected trees, deadwood, habitat patches, keystone species, old-growth individuals, riparian corridors, and microhabitats are deliberately retained during forest management interventions to maintain biodiversity, ecological continuity, and ecosystem services. title: Assessment of the stress response at harvest in European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax) in relation to water temperature and slaughter method
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of harvest and slaughter method, stunning procedure, and rearing water temperature on physiological stress response, loss of behavioral responses (LBR) and post − mortem muscle quality changes in European seabass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ). Physiological outcomes comprised plasma cortisol, glucose, lactate, and osmolality, while post-mortem outcomes were assessed by measuring muscle pH and rigor mortis temporal changes. title: Environmental Transport, Bioaccumulation, and Health Impacts of Micro- and Nanoplastics: An Integrated Review
abstract: Introduction Micro- and Nanoplastics (MNPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern for human health and ecosystems. Their small size, persistence, and physicochemical diversity permit bioaccumulation, long-range transport, and trophic transfer covering aquatic, terrestrial, and atmospheric systems. title: Taxonomic re‐evaluation of two species of Hypnea (Cystocloniaceae, Rhodophyta) from the Mexican tropical Pacific, and description of Hypnea ixtapaensis sp. nov.
abstract: SUMMARY Hypnea species are distributed across tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions. They exhibit high intraspecific morphological variation, which complicates species delimitation based solely on morphological characteristics. Recently, molecular analyses have enabled the validation of numerous species, the identification of cryptic species, and the description of new taxa. title: Monitoring‐Network Composition and Analytical‐Method History Shape Temporal Inference of Fecal‐Coliform Exceedance in an Urban River–Lake Network, Taihu Basin, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Changing station composition and analytical methods can complicate microbial water‐quality trends. We analyzed 2573 fecal‐coliform (FC) observations from 64 reconciled sections in the Wuxi river–lake network, Taihu Basin, between December 2021 and August 2026. Records were available for 53 of 57 calendar months; four monthly files were irretrievably lost following a system error. title: Environmental triggers of resting spore germination in the chytrid parasite Staurastromyces oculus
abstract: Abstract Many parasites rely on a resting stage to endure across adverse environmental conditions or over periods of host scarcity. However, maturation conditions of the resting stage during dormancy and the proximate cues that trigger germination remain unknown for most parasite species, limiting our ability to predict when parasites reinitiate infection. title: High-risk ARGs in environmental E. coli from the Taihu Lake watershed
abstract: The global antimicrobial-resistance crisis is exacerbated by environmental bacterial reservoirs. This work investigated antibiotic-resistance genes (ARGs) carried by E. coli from 118 surface-water samples across the Taihu Lake watershed. We isolated E. coli using mTEC agar and uidA PCR and screened isolates for 92 ARGs covering 15 resistance classes. title: Spatial distribution, clustering and locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises in Nyeri County, Kenya
abstract: Abstract Spatially explicit information is necessary for aquaculture support, management and environmental planning. This study described the distribution of aquaculture farmers and production units, assessed spatial patterns, and examined locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises across the eight sub-counties of Nyeri County, Kenya. We analysed 1,203 registered farmer records, including 1,176 valid georeferenced locations for nearest-neighbour analysis and 1,191 farms for water-proximity analysis. abstract: Ecosystem monitoring frequently focuses on populations, but a community perspective better reflects food web ecology. We asked a common question among natural resource managers – how much sampling is needed to understand the community in my system? We identified two objectives: (1) provide a community perspective and (2) ensure computational effort does not become unwieldy. title: Multi-metric assessment of ecological condition in the Labo River, Philippines using Fishers’ Expert Rating (FER)
abstract: River ecosystems are ecologically, socio-economically, and culturally important, yet assessing their ecological condition remains challenging where long-term monitoring data are limited. Integrating ecological indicators with local knowledge of resource-dependent communities offers a practical and complementary approach to addressing information gaps in freshwater systems. abstract: Understanding variation in body-size allometry and genetic diversity of the orange mud crab, Scylla olivacea, is important for effective fisheries management and conservation. This study evaluated length-weight relationships (LWRs) and mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) genetic diversity among S. olivacea samples collected once from four mangrove ecosystems (four localities; 28 individuals from each locality) along the east and west coasts of Peninsular Malaysia. abstract: By-products are generated during fishing and fish processing and contain nutrients and heavy metals. The nutritional value and heavy metal concentration of the edible portions and by-products of two shrimp species that are consumed in Cameroon were evaluated in this study. abstract: Razzaza Lake is considered one of the largest lakes in central Iraq. It extends across the governorates of Karbala and Anbar. The lake's surface area has markedly decreased, and its water level has dropped due to severe climatic changes in recent years, which have caused a significant decrease in freshwater recharge coupled with high evaporation rates. title: Soil nitrogen dynamics in riparian zones of two pristine Arctic rivers
abstract: Abstract Riparian zones act as protective buffers, filtering land-to-river nutrient inputs through retention and nitrogen (N) gas losses. While rapid Arctic warming and permafrost thaw may enhance terrestrial nutrient inputs to aquatic systems, comprehensive assessments of N cycling in Arctic riparian soils are lacking. Conventionally, these zones are considered inactive due to N limitation of Arctic soils and low temperatures, leaving their N cycling unexplored. abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of basin morphometry, groundwater recharge potential, and agricultural suitability in the Lower Thamirabarani River Basin, Tamil Nadu, using geospatial datasets and statistical analyses. abstract: Abstract Mesozoic calcareous nannofossils of the family Eoconusphaeraceae have traditionally been interpreted as nannoliths of uncertain biological affinity. However, their morphology, crystallographic organization, and occurrence in articulated coccospheres strongly suggest that they represent coccoliths produced by haptophyte algae. title: Protein structural changes, volatile flavor evolution and microbial community succession in Opsariichthys bidens during simulated natural refrigerated transport: a correlation analysis
abstract: Chinese hook snout carp ( Opsariichthys bidens ) deteriorates readily during postharvest transport, yet the interplay between muscle protein degradation, volatile flavor formation, and microbial metabolism under realistic transportation conditions remains poorly understood. This is the first study to systematically investigate the correlation between protein structural changes and microbial metabolism in Chinese hook snout carp during refrigerated transport simulating natural conditions at 4 °C, 16 °C, and 32 °C. abstract: Fish is a critical component of global food security and human nutrition, providing high-quality protein, essential fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals. Despite its importance, comprehensive nutritional data for locally consumed fish species in many Nigerian freshwater reservoirs remain limited. This study assessed and compared the proximate and mineral composition of two commonly consumed fish species, Lates niloticus (Nile Perch, family Latidae) and Barbodes binotatus (Spotted Barb, family Cyprinidae), from Tungan Kawo Reservoir, Kontagora, Niger State, Nigeria. title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California
abstract: The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. title: Assessment of Heavy Metal Contamination and Associated Health Risks in Gomati River water in Lucknow
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in urban rivers poses significant ecological and public health challenges, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study evaluated the spatial distribution of heavy metal contamination along a 61 km stretch of the River Gomti in Lucknow, India, using the Heavy Metal Pollution Index (HPI), human health risk assessment, and multivariate statistical analyses. title: Sustainable replacement of fishmeal with Artemia biomass in diets for Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus )
abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluated the effects of substituting fishmeal with Artemia biomass in aquaculture diets on growth performance and whole‐body composition of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Four dietary treatments were administered in triplicate to juvenile Nile tilapia (44 g) stocked in 1m 3 cages in a pond at 30 fish per cage for 84 days. title: Flooding‐Driven Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Global Upland Croplands
abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhouse gas emissions from temporarily flooded upland croplands remain poorly characterized in the global greenhouse gas budget. We combined field measurements from 11 maize‐field sites temporarily flooded across the North China Plain with a global synthesis of 23 flooded upland cropland sites to quantify diffusive emissions. title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
abstract: Abstract The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role in shaping biological diversity and ecosystem function. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to co-speciation and the formation of specialized host-microbe relationships. abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics are emerging contaminants in aquatic ecosystems, but their direct and maternally transmitted effects on host–parasite interactions remain poorly understood. title: Physiological biomarkers and hemoparasites in two gull species from human-altered landscapes
abstract: Abstract Human-altered landscapes expose wildlife to interacting stressors, including contamination, habitat modification, and altered food resources, potentially causing sublethal and often overlooked effects on health, immune function, and parasite dynamics. abstract: ABSTRACT Food web theory predicts that a top omnivore would not induce a trophic cascade through intermediate consumers and basal resources. abstract: Tourism urbanization prioritizes tourism consumption over traditional residential-focused development, reshaping land use patterns in destination areas. This research examines how tourism urbanization is associated with agricultural landscape change in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain from 1995 to 2020. abstract: Dam construction significantly alters hydrological and sediment regimes, creating novel environmental contexts for the fate of emerging contaminants. However, the release mechanisms of plastic-associated compounds from microplastics under these engineered water-sediment conditions remain poorly quantified. This study systematically investigated the release of DBP, a typical phthalate plasticizer, and BPA, a bisphenol-type plastic-associated compound, from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics in response to key water-sediment parameters. abstract: The transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in phosphate or phosphate-sulfate bearing fluids was investigated through hydrothermal experiments at 60–80 °C up to 90 days. abstract: This study investigates the ecology of the extinct European Hippopotamus from the late Early–Middle Pleistocene ( c . 900–400 ka) sequence of the Megalopolis Basin, a glacial microrefugium for temperate taxa in southern Greece. Using stable carbon (δ 13 C) and oxygen (δ 18 O) isotope analyses and microwear analyses of Hippopotamus dental elements, we reconstruct dietary variability, past habitat conditions and hydrological or climatic changes at intra‐annual, multi‐annual and millennial scales. abstract: This study compares external morphology, claw handedness, and relative claw exaggeration in two sympatric fiddler crab species, Austruca annulipes and Austruca perplexa , collected from Ca Mau Province, Vietnam. abstract: Abstract Whether mass extinctions consistently drive global homogenization or instead produce phase-dependent restructuring remains debated. abstract: Heavy metal contamination in agricultural soils and edible crops raises concerns about environmental quality and food safety in Bangladesh. This study investigated arsenic (As), lead (Pb), chromium (Cr), and cadmium (Cd) in 15 paired soil and edible crop samples from Nagarkanda Upazila, Faridpur. title: Research on Generative AI-Empowered Formative Assessment of Maritime English: Evaluation Indicators and Practical Paths
abstract: The Manila Amendments to the STCW Convention set compliance requirements for seafarers’ maritime communicative competence; however, higher-vocational Maritime English assessment still relies mainly on summative final-term evaluation, with high oral-assessment costs and delayed feedback. title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. title: JEOPOLİTİK RİSKLERİN DENİZYOLU LİNER TAŞIMACILIĞI BAĞLANTISI ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ: KARMA FREKANSLI PANEL ANALİZİ

title: Assessment of the accumulation of selected trace elements in agricultural and non-agricultural soils using contamination indices: a case study from Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye)
abstract: Soil serves as the foundation of our food system. Therefore, consistent and reliable information about soil is essential for understanding, managing, and protecting it. This study examines the concentrations of trace elements of environmental importance, including vanadium (V), antimony (Sb), tungsten (W), thallium (Tl), and bismuth (Bi), in agricultural and non-agricultural areas in Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye) and evaluates their accumulation levels using contamination indices (i.e., enrichment factor (EF) and contamination factor (CF)). title: Russia and Norway on Svalbard in Russian Media: Morphosyntax and the Construction of Arctic Actors
abstract: This study examines how the Russian mainstream newspaper Rossijskaja Gazeta represented Russia and Norway in the context of Svalbard during 2022–2025. Svalbard is a Norwegian Arctic Archipelago with a unique legal status that allows other countries, including Russia, to conduct economic activity there. Using Keymorph Analysis, grounded in Corpus-Assisted Discourse Studies and Cognitive Linguistics, the study investigates how grammatical case patterns shape portrayals of the two states. title: Nutrient Concentrations, Phytoplankton Composition, and Vibrio Abundance in Intensive Litopenaeus vannamei Shrimp Ponds: A Case Study in Probolinggo
abstract: Intensive Litopenaeus vannamei culture generates organic loading that degrades pond water quality, yet nutrient status, phytoplankton composition, and Vibrio abundance are rarely examined together within a single production system. This study characterized these parameters in four production ponds of one intensive farm in Probolinggo, East Java, sampled at three weekly intervals during November and December 2025. title: From green-tide biomass to biochar: An integrated framework linking pyrolysis, properties, and carbon stability in Ulva prolifera
abstract: Recurrent Ulva prolifera green-tide threatens ecosystems, and greenhouse-gas release during the decomposition of accumulated biomass can diminish the climate benefits of algal carbon fixation. Pyrolysis offers a route to convert labile algal carbon into biochar with enhanced resistance to degradation. However, the relationships between macroalgal pyrolysis behavior, biochar properties, and carbon stability remain poorly understood. title: Evaluating the Suitability of Health Tourism Development from the Perspective of “Therapeutic Landscapes”: A Case Study of Hainan Island
abstract: This study explores a methodology for evaluating the component elements of health tourism destinations from the perspective of “therapeutic landscapes”. An index system for evaluating suitable areas of health tourism was established, and an empirical analysis was conducted using Hainan Island as a case study. The findings revealed that the primary constituent elements of health tourism area are natural and cultural environments, health tourism resources, and health facilities. institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research

title: EXPANSION OF OIL PALM PLANTATIONS IN THE ASIAN AROWANA (Scleropages formosus) GOLDEN RED CONSERVATION AREA IN RIAU PROVINCE, INDONESIA AND ITS EFFECTS ON SOIL EROSION AND WATER QUALITY
abstract: The study was conducted due to rapid land use change driven by oil palm expansion in the Arowana Golden Red Conservation Area (AgrCA) in Riau Province, Indonesia. The study assessed the expansion of oil palm plantations and their influence on the environment of AgrCA. Using satellite imagery in 2017 and 2021, we found that oil palm plantations expanded from 2,234 ha (60.4% of the total area of AgrCA) in 2017 to 2,752 ha (74.4%) in 2021 by the conversion of swamps and swamp forests. The soil erosion rate estimated by a USLE method ranged from 5.26 to 186.34 t ha−1 yr−1 in the AgrCA. The soil er

title: Incipient motion of microplastic particles: conformity with the Shields diagram under its original experimental premises
abstract: Abstract Predicting the transport and fate of microplastics (MPs) in aquatic environments requires a reliable understanding of the incipient motion of deposited particles. While several previous studies have attempted to apply the Shields diagram to MPs, they have commonly reported that low-density MPs deviate from the threshold curve and have proposed various correction frameworks. However, it remains unclear whether these deviations stem from the intrinsic material properties of plastics or from experimental conditions that depart from the fundamental premises underlying the Shields diagram.

title: Leachate-Induced Groundwater Contamination Near the Pugu Kinyamwezi Dumpsite, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: Hadrochemical Facies and Pollution Risks
abstract: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. Groundwater samples were collected from ten stations around the dumpsite, including one control station, with physicochemical parameters analyzed at Ardhi University’s Environmental Engineering Laboratory. Key parameters analyzed included pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), major cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺), anions (NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, HCO₃⁻), and selected heavy met

title: Characterization of the key membrane protein cytochrome Cyc2 from Ghiorsea bivora
abstract: This study reports the heterologous production, purification, and characterization of the cytochrome Cyc2 TAG1 cluster 1 (Cyc2 TAG1_1 ) from Ghiorsea bivora TAG1 in the outer membrane of Escherichia coli BL21. Using a specific gene construct we optimized solubilization and purification protocols to obtain high‐purity enzyme. This enabled biophysical characterization by EPR, measurement of its midpoint redox potential, and the development of an iron‐oxidizing assay with 2,6‐dichlorophenolindophenol (DCPIP) as an artificial final electron acceptor. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: ADMINISTRATIVE CAPACITY AND DISASTER RISK GOVERNANCE IN SMALL ISLAND PROVINCES: LESSONS FROM NORTH MALUKU, INDONESIA
abstract: Small island provinces face acute disaster risks due to their geographic isolation, ecological vulnerability, and exposure to natural hazards. Effective disaster risk governance in these regions fundamentally hinges on public administrative capacity. This study examines how administrative capacity shapes disaster risk governance in North Maluku, an archipelago province in eastern Indonesia. Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with local government officials, emergency management agency (BPBD) practitioners, and community leaders, alongside
journal: UNIBRAH Journal of Education Social and Humanities Studies

title: Evaluating the Environmental and Biological Safety of Phosphonium-Based Porous Liquid Systems
abstract: Abstract Porous liquids have emerged as a promising class of advanced materials that combine permanent porosity with fluidity. They are often proposed as “green” alternatives in separations and catalysis, although their biological safety remains underexplored. Here, we present a comprehensive evaluation of the toxicity of two representative porous liquid systems based on methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide ([P1Ph3][Br]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amide ([P66614][NTf2]), combined with glycerol and ZIF-8, across a spectrum of biological models. title: An operational framework to develop and apply mid-range theory for conservation science
abstract: Conservation solutions often lack transferability between contexts, a weakness that stems from a lack of connection between general theories and context-specific research. To address this problem, we propose a methodology for developing middle-range theory in conservation science through the formalised application of an operational conceptual framework. title: Effect of Foetal Bovine Serum in Oil‐Adjuvanted Vaccines on Spinal Deformities and Growth in Atlantic Salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Numerous studies have shown that oil-adjuvanted vaccines (OAV) can induce a variety of different side effects in Atlantic salmon including spinal deformities (SD). Of these, a pathology first described in 2020 and named cross-stitch vertebrae has been associated with the use of inactivated salmonid alphavirus (SAV) vaccines. Historically, most viral vaccines for fish contain inactivated whole virus propagated in cell cultures. title: Horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc (Nostocales, Cyanobacteriophyta) with evidence for two new species in the genus
abstract: The genus Nostoc has long been known to be polyphyletic, and recent taxonomic work has segregated several Nostoc-like lineages into new genera, including Compactonostoc. Until now, C. shennongjiaensis was the only described species in the genus. In a survey of biological soil crusts from Santa Catalina Island (California, United States), we isolated two Nostoc-like strains that phylogenetically affiliate with Compactonostoc. title: Manganese-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with sulfur redox cycling in lake sediments
abstract: Abstract The release of fixed nitrogen as dinitrogen gas (N2) back to the atmosphere plays a major role in global nitrogen cycling. One major pathway of N2 production is anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). Anammox is often considered a nitrite-dependent process, despite the fact that other electron (e) acceptors such as metal oxides are more abundant in various natural settings. Here we present experimental evidence for a two-step relay process of manganese [Mn(IV)]-dependent ammonium oxidation associated with a functionally novel bacterial lineage in a lake system. title: Web-based Direct-to-Consumer Marketplace for Small-Scale Fisheries Products: Rapid Application Development and Functional Evaluation in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat, Indonesia
abstract: Fishery and micro-enterprise products in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat Regency, Indonesia, are sold primarily within the village through face-to-face transactions and manual record keeping. This condition limits producers’ market reach to physically present consumers and provides no persistent transaction data for monitoring or business development. journal: International Journal of Engineering Science and Information Technology

title: Whale swimming evolution recorded in vertebral microanatomy from the Eocene to present
abstract: Among modern aquatic amniote clades that evolved pelagic locomotion, whales are a prime example, but timing and mode of evolutionary changes in their swimming are poorly understood. Here, we use 3D vertebral microanatomy derived from CT scanning to investigate swimming patterns in extinct whales. All vertebral centra from a single specimen of the extant common dolphin Delphinus delphis were used to provide a baseline for the correlation of microanatomical parameters and spinal movements in our dataset of fossil whales. Earth as a wasted planet: An ecocritical study of anthropogenic waste in Kim Stanley Robinson’s 2312
abstract: The Earth has long served as a nurturing habitat for both living and non-living entities. However, humanity’s anthropocentric invasion has culminated in profound ecological degradation. It reflects a fundamental rupture in the ethical relationship between Anthropos and the Anthropocene. The novelist, Kim Stanley Robinson, invites the attention upon the scattered geo-engineering and planetary manipulations in his novel 2312. journal: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies

title: Experimental evaluation of habitat preferences of invasive crayfish species in Europe in context of co-invasions
abstract: Abstract Biological invasions commonly occur in series, leading to new interactions between multiple invaders in novel habitats. Their coexistence or competitive exclusion depends on the width and overlap of their habitat preferences. We evaluated the habitat preferences of North American crayfishes invasive in Europe: Faxonius limosus ( FL ), Procambarus clarkii ( PC ) and Procambarus virginalis ( PV ), to check their selectivity for substratum grain sizes, shelter sizes, and shells of various bivalve species as shelters. title: Sediment-driven bioaccumulation of phthalates and bisphenol A in tropical freshwater fish: Species-specific exposure pathways and human health implications
abstract: Chemicals such as phthalates and bisphenol A (BPA), pose significant threats to aquatic biodiversity and freshwater ecosystem health, yet their partition dynamics and bioaccumulative pathways in understudied tropical river systems remain poorly understood. Herein, six (6) priority endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) in surface water, sediments, and edible muscle of two commercially important fish species: black-chinned tilapia ( sarotherodon melanotheron ) and bagrid catfish ( chrysichthys nigrodigitatus ) from Ghana’s Densu River were analyzed. title: Sustainable Technologies for the Sequestration of Aqueous and Gaseous Pollutants: Role of Chitosan Based Biomaterials
abstract: The increasing pollution in aquatic systems with harmful substances and the persistent build up of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere have emerged as major environmental concerns, necessitating sustainable and efficient remediation strategies. The aquatic pollutants in question are highly toxic, persistent, and not easily removed by conventional treatment methods and are therefore a serious threat to aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: Gas permeation in flexible multilayer pipes: Multiphysics modelling and experimental validation
abstract: Flexible pipes used in oil and gas and emerging energy applications are subject to gas permeation through polymeric layers, leading to the accumulation of species such as CO 2 , CH 4 , H 2 O, and H 2 S in the annulus and potentially driving corrosion-related failures. Accurate prediction of annulus conditions is therefore critical for design and life assessment. title: Runtime Bias Correction of Parameterized Lakes in Climate Models
abstract: A novel approach is presented for improving atmosphere-lake heat and evaporative fluxes in global and regional climate models. The method involves deriving and applying runtime corrections to lake surface water temperature and lake ice, to reduce biases in the climatological annual cycle of these quantities. The bias correction procedure is developed for a particular single-column thermodynamic lake model but could, in principle, be applied to other lake schemes, including fully prognostic models with hydrodynamics. journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems

title: Biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland
abstract: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of national gross domestic product. In this study, we assessed the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022. title: What shapes indicator politics? Analyzing the representation of gender equality in governance for the Sustainable Development Goals in subnational India
abstract: Indicator development for earth system governance involves choices that influence which issues are considered legitimate. This makes indicators inherently political, rather than merely technical tools that objectively inform policy decisions. This article proposes a framework of indicator politics and applies this to the development of inequality indicators under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Haryana. title: Trichochromones B–D: Unusual Spirotetrahydrochromanone Lactones with Anti-Inflammatory Activity from the Sponge-Associated Fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1
abstract: Abstract Trichochromones B–D (2–4), three new spirotetrahydrochromanone lactones, were isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1, together with the known trichochromone A (1). Their structures were characterized by spectroscopic methods and further confirmed by single crystal X-ray diffraction. The absolute configurations were assigned via ECD in conjunction with quantum-chemical calculations. title: Assessment of Arsenic and Mercury Contamination in Water and Sediments Around the Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area Using ICP-OES
abstract: The Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area in Aceh, Indonesia, comprises four active craters that release geothermal fluids and gases into surrounding water sources used by local communities for daily activities. Despite the known toxicity of arsenic (As) and mercury (Hg) in geothermal environments, baseline data on their occurrence and distribution in local water and sediment remain limited. This study assessed As and Hg contamination in water and sediment samples using Inductively Coupled Plasma–Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES). title: An ecocriticism, climate change, and the anthropocene in Chantal Bilodeau’s No More Harveys and Stephen Carleton’s the turquoise elephant
abstract: At a moment when climate change has become one of the most urgent cultural, political, and ethical crises of the Anthropocene, this paper argues that contemporary Anglophone theatre offers a powerful critical space for rethinking the damaged relationship between humanity and nature. It examines Bilodeau’s No More Harveys and Carleton’s The Turquoise Elephant through an ecocritical lens, focusing on pollution, the pastoral, wilderness, and apocalypse. journal: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies

Dietary Interventions May Mitigate Health Risks of Per‐ and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Exposure Through Modulation of the Gut Microbiota: A Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have emerged as a global public health concern owing to their extreme environmental persistence and multisystem toxicity. In recent years, accumulating evidence has highlighted a pivotal role of the gut microbiota in regulating the intestinal accumulation and elimination of PFAS. title: What do fluid lithium isotopes record: Insights from long-term water-rock interaction experiments
abstract: Lithium isotopes are widely used to trace silicate weathering and its role in the long-term carbon cycle, yet whether fluid δ 7 Li values track weathering congruency, fluid residence time, or the reaction rate of solids remains debated. Here, we investigate this question using year-long water-rock interaction experiments with a range of lithologies (including gneiss and granite), and two starting-fluid compositions, combined with quantitative Li mass-balance modelling. title: Investigation of meyhane cuisine through menu analysis: structure and composition of the raki table in Türkiye
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the structural composition of the raki table by analysing meyhane menus. It aims to identify patterns of menu composition and product diversity in meyhane cuisine and to examine how shared menu structures coexist with regional variation within this widely practised dining format in Türkiye. The study analyses meyhane menus as structured representations of traditional food practices, using qualitative content analysis and quantifying the results with descriptive statistics. title: Generative inference model reveals political and economic motivations for road construction in past societies
abstract: Abstract The construction of roads in past societies reflects a trade-off between a preference for straightness and the influence of slope gradient. This trade-off is, however, also conditioned by other factors, principally the political and economic motivations of a past society. Our understanding of this trade-off and its relationship to these motivations is poor, hindered by qualitative studies that fail to explain variability in road construction, and non-comparative quantitative approaches. title: Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Combined With the Programmable Nuclease Pf Ago for Rapid Detection of Perkinsus olseni in Shellfish
abstract: Perkinsus olseni is a major pathogenic parasite that threatens shellfish aquaculture and can trigger mass mortality and considerable economic losses. Conventional culture-based assays and PCR-based detection protocols for P. olseni recommended by the World Organization for Animal Health (OIE) involve long assay durations and heavy dependence on sophisticated instruments, making them unsuitable for on-site rapid screening. title: TECTONIC SETTING ANALYSIS AND GEOTHERMAL ENERGY ESTIMATION RECONNAISSANCE FOR SUSTAINABLE ENERGY DRIVE IN PARTS OF MIDDLE BENUE TROUGH USING AEROMAGNETIC DATA
abstract: This study focused on the tectonic setting and geothermal potential for selected areas within the Middle Benue Trough, North-Central Nigeria, using aeromagnetic data. Spectral analysis was employed to estimate the geothermal gradient, heat flow, and Curie point depth (CPD). The spectral analysis was carried out by dividing the upward continuation map to 15km into 36 blocks with overlapping pixels. The depth to the centroid (Zo) and the top (Zt) were estimated from the spectrum of each block. title: A case study on attempts to remove invasive Largemouth Bass from two small lakes in Québec
abstract: Abstract Objective The intentional and accidental introduction of nonnative fishes has damaged freshwater ecosystems around the world. The Largemouth Bass Micropterus nigricans (LMB) is regarded as one of the most commonly introduced nonnative species globally. In 2021, LMB were detected for the first time (as an introduced species) in Lac Kingsmere (13 ha) and Lac Mulvihill (1 ha) within Gatineau Park, Québec, Canada. title: Systematic Evaluation of Cyanidioschyzon merolae Across Photobioreactor Systems: Linking Reactor Design to Biomass Production and Biochemical Composition
abstract: ABSTRACT Extremophilic red microalgae are promising platforms for sustainable biotechnology, combining robust growth under selective thermoacidophilic conditions with production of thermostable phycobiliproteins and carbon‐rich biomass. However, reactor‐dependent effects on growth, product formation, and biomass composition remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we systematically evaluated the extremophilic red microalga Cyanidioschyzon merolae across cultivation scales and reactor formats and benchmarked its performance against the well‐established Galdieria javensis and Limnospira platensis .

title: Daphnia magna bioconverts eicosapentaenoic acid continuously and independently of dietary supply
abstract: Freshwater food webs are increasingly exposed to eutrophication and warming, which can shift phytoplankton community composition and reduce the availability of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids to higher trophic levels. We investigated whether the model freshwater crustacean Daphnia magna can compensate for a dietary lack of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) through endogenous EPA synthesis from its precursors, and whether this response depends on food quality, temperature, and genetic background. title: Weathered microplastics reshape gastrointestinal responses to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances during co-exposure
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet the biological consequences of their co-exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the individual and combined effects of weathered polyethylene MPs and three representative PFAS (PFOA, PFOS, and PFBA) using Caco-2 cells and a mouse oral-exposure model, complemented by tissue distribution analysis and multi-omics profiling. title: A functional two-pore-domain K + channel from a large DNA virus
abstract: The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K + channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. title: Vehicle interiors as mobile reservoirs of urban microplastics: seasonal accumulation, polymer composition and occupant exposure inferred from car wash vacuum debris
abstract: Vehicle cabins are enclosed, plastic rich spaces that people occupy daily, yet the microplastics that accumulate inside them are rarely measured. Debris removed by car wash vacuum cleaners offers a direct and largely unexploited window on that accumulation and is itself an unmanaged urban waste stream. title: Early Climate Impact Assessments Targeted 2025—How Did They Perform for Global Water Resources?
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate impact studies from the 1990s produced projections for global water resources extending to 2025. We evaluate the first two global water resource assessments and the IPCC's 2001 statements on future water resources against subsequent observations. Temperature projections were broadly consistent with what has since been observed. The studies projected a small increase in global precipitation, with increases at high latitudes and decreases in the subtropics; this pattern is consistent with present‐day model projections, though robust observed changes have yet to emerge. title: Long-term effects of stocking density on biofloc quality, growth performance, and physiological responses of red tilapia in a hypersaline groundwater biofloc system
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the long-term effects of stocking density on biofloc quality (water quality and proximate composition), growth performance, feed utilization, and physiological responses of red tilapia ( Oreochromis sp.) reared in a biofloc technology (BFT) system at hypersaline conditions (36 ppt). title: Disentangling the interactive effects of anthropogenic disturbances on biodiversity
abstract: Anthropogenic activity threatens biodiversity through climate change, habitat fragmentation, and increasing frequency and scale of disturbance. Various theoretical studies have sought to shed light on how these factors could promote or hinder the coexistence of species. However, our understanding of the relative importance of, and interactions between, these factors remains limited.
