title: An online tool for near real-time exploration of cattle population and bovine tuberculosis trends in Ireland
abstract: Abstract Background In Ireland, there has been an increase in bovine tuberculosis (bTB) incidence between 2015 and 2024, placing increased pressure and focus on the bTB programme. Providing access to the latest bTB statistics and trends in a user friendly and accessible format would significantly support researchers, policymakers, and enhance public understanding through transparent communication. title: Morphological variation of the conus arteriosus in Chondrichthyes: Implications for ecology and evolution
abstract: Cartilaginous fish have diverse morphological traits that are essential for understanding their evolutionary history and ecological adaptations. abstract: Cellularization is the coordinated division of a multinucleate cell into many cells, a common life cycle transition across eukaryotes. abstract: By snapping their claws, snapping shrimp create cavitation bubbles that release supersonic pressure waves when they collapse. abstract: Mineral dust is one of the major light-absorbing impurities in snow and ice, and affects snowpack and glacier melting. abstract: Schoolyards represent a critical asset for mitigating climate-related heat exposure among children. Young children in elementary school are a group particularly vulnerable to rising temperatures, heat waves, and prolonged exposure to high thermal stress. abstract: Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE) is an approach that is widely used to monitor the occurrence and distribution of pathogens shed by human populations through wastewater. This review critically evaluates the application of WBE of enteric viruses within a One Health paradigm. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing their isoprenoid metabolism remain poorly understood, which poses a major bottleneck in engineering them for greater production efficiency. title: Reindeer habitat selection and movement change with cumulative impacts from mining and wind power development
abstract: Industrial expansion often occurs in landscapes already affected by multiple disturbances, leading to cumulative impacts on biodiversity and local communities. With the societal pressure for an rapid ‘green transition’, land-use changes intensifies, yet most impact assessments remain local and project-based, disregarding cumulative impacts. We conceptualized and disentangled key dimensions of cumulative impacts and integrated them within habitat selection, calving site selection, and movement analyses in a case study of reindeer and Sámi reindeer husbandry in Scandinavia. title: Indeks Pencemaran dan Kondisi Ekologis di Tiga Sungai di Kota Yogyakarta
abstract: Dinamika ekologis sungai perkotaan, seperti yang melintasi Kota Yogyakarta, rentan terhadap tekanan antropogenik, namun pemahaman komprehensif mengenai interaksi antara kondisi abiotik, tingkat pencemaran, dan respons keanekaragaman hayati pada tiga sungai utamanya (Winongo, Code, dan Gajah Wong) masih terbatas. abstract: Chirostoma arge (Jordan and Snyder, 1899) is a fish endemic to the central plateau of Mexico important for fishing in natural reservoirs such as Lake Chapala. Unfortunately, little is known about this species of the Atherinopsidae family, which is listed as Data Deficient by the IUCN Red List. This study’s objective was to determine the sex ratio, the stage of gonadal maturity in each sex, the spawning season and to estimate the relative condition factor, the minimum standard length and the standard length at first maturity. title: Changes in Thermal Growing‐Season Characteristics in Estonia During 1965–2025: Regional Variability and Methodological Sensitivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal growing‐season characteristics in Estonia were analysed for 1965–2025 using daily mean air temperature observations from 15 meteorological stations. Start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and growing‐season length (GSL) were determined using both the traditional Raik–Tarand method and the internationally standardised ETCCDI definition to evaluate their comparability in spatial patterns, annual variability, and long‐term change. title: Water governance and population health: Evaluating the efficacy of drinking water standards in Angren, Uzbekistan
abstract: Ensuring safe drinking water that meets both hydrochemical and physiological standards remains a key environmental challenge. In industrial regions, evaluating local water sources against international criteria is essential to identifying hidden risks to public health. This study investigates the hydrochemical characteristics of surface and groundwater in Angren, Uzbekistan, and evaluates their specific impact on public health within the framework of national and international safety standards. abstract: This study evaluated the thermal resistance performance of spherical cryogenic storage tanks on liquefied natural gas carriers operating between the Tangguh refinery and the Jawa Satu Floating Storage Regasification Unit to address the operational challenge of cargo shrinkage. The natural evaporation of cryogenic fluids during maritime transportation represented a physical loss of energy supply and caused a significant financial burden on the national energy supply chain. title: Landscape composition, patch size, and local characteristics shape ant and beetle assemblages in naturally patchy indigenous forests
abstract: Indigenous forests are important reservoirs of terrestrial arthropod biodiversity, but naturally patchy forests are understudied compared to human-fragmented forests. We evaluated the relative influence of landscape composition, patch size, and local characteristics on ants (Formicidae) and beetles (Coleoptera) in Southern Mistbelt Forests in South Africa. These forests exist as small patches within a fire-prone grassland matrix, with the grasslands undergoing modification for forestry, agriculture and rural development. abstract: This research explores the global ecological crisis as a structural failure in the relationship between humans, law, and nature, rooted in the anthropocentric paradigm. Although Indonesia possesses rich theological values regarding nature conservation, the eco-theological response has tended to be ethical-spiritual and lacks legal-formal enforcement. This qualitative research with a juridical-normative approach aims to reconstruct the epistemology of Islamic law through Shofiyullah Muzammil's Qira'ah Mu'āṣirah fī al-Ahkām method, synthesized with Jasser Auda's Systems Theory. title: An internally consistent framework for calculating cascading probabilistic earthquake risk and its application to a case study in New Zealand
abstract: Abstract. Quantifying the combined effects of earthquakes and their cascading hazards is essential for realistic risk assessment, yet such approaches remain limited in practice. Dynamic frameworks that explicitly correlate hazard intensities and their uncertainties across cascading perils provide more consistent and physically plausible impact estimates, offering greater value for resilience planning and risk management. title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of the Seaweed Sensory Space Through Consumer‐Evoked Associations Across Ireland, Norway, Spain, and Turkey
abstract: Understanding the sensory space of a product category is a valuable tool in New Product Development, particularly for emerging food categories such as seaweed, where consumer familiarity remains limited in many markets. The current work explored the sensory associations of consumers willing to try seaweed products across four European countries (Ireland, Norway, Spain, and Turkey) through a cross-cultural online survey. title: Filling a geographic gap in the Antarctic distributions of Philodina gregaria and Adineta grandis record from the Syowa Oasis, East Antarctica
abstract: We report the first confirmed records of two widely distributed Antarctic bdelloid rotifer species, Philodina gregaria and Adineta grandis , from the Syowa Oasis, East Antarctica. To verify their taxonomic identity, we applied an integrative approach combining morphological observations, mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) sequencing, Bayesian tree reconstruction, and four species-delimitation methods (GMYC, bPTP, ABGD, and ASAP). title: Sustainable urban development: An integrated assessment of Kazakhstani cities
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstract Rapid urbanization has increased pressure on urban systems, creating challenges related to resource efficiency, waste management, and environmental protection. These challenges are particularly acute for Kazakhstan, where cities differ substantially in their resource use, environmental conditions, infrastructure, and socioeconomic characteristics. This study aims to conduct a comparative assessment and identify the key characteristics of urban metabolic profiles and sustainable development in Kazakhstani cities. title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
abstract: Abstract Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. title: PELAGIX: An Intelligent Decentralized Framework for Verified Quantification and Transparent Trading of Blue Carbon Assets
abstract: Mangrove carbon assessments require spatially explicit methods whose assumptions, data support, and verification status remain traceable. This study presents an integrated workflow for operational mangrove mapping, modeled above-ground carbon (AGC) estimation, complementary carbon accounting, parameter sensitivity, and a prototype digital measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) provenance layer for a Sundarbans area bounded by approximately 88.10–89.10°E and 21.50–22.35°N. title: Microplastics as vectors and reservoirs of pharmaceuticals and drugs of abuse: experimental evidence, mechanistic predictions and analytical challenges
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly investigated as particulate phases capable of interacting with emerging organic contaminants in aquatic environments. This review critically evaluates experimental evidence for pharmaceutical-MP interactions and distinguishes it from mechanistic extrapolation for drugs of abuse, for which direct sorption data remain largely unavailable. Environmental occurrence data for drugs of abuse are used to establish environmental relevance and prioritize target analytes rather than as evidence of sorption onto MPs. title: The ‘Great Frost’ of 1708–9 in Britain and the Condescensions of Posterity
abstract: Abstract This article explores the ‘great frost’ of 1709 and its impact on economic life in Britain, challenging a popular view that, based on gross domestic product (GDP) estimates, it was catastrophic. It shows that the annual GDP figures for the period have such wide error margins that they cannot establish the scale of the disruption; that the severe winter was felt in southern but not northern Britain; that there were, in any case, means of partially mitigating such disruptions; and that the economic difficulties that were experienced had various causes, not just those of a bad winter. title: Liquid polymer enhances methanogenesis and restructures prokaryotic communities in freshwater sediments
abstract: Abstract. The widespread use of synthetic hydrophilic polymers, such as polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), has raised concerns about their potential effects on environmental biogeochemical processes, yet their impact on sediment ecosystems remains largely unexplored. We investigated how PVP influences methane (CH4) production and prokaryotic community composition in freshwater sediments over a 56-day anoxic incubation. title: Warming vs. browning: a dual mechanism behind net ecosystem production of shallow brown aquatic systems
abstract: Abstract. Northern lakes are warming and browning due to increased cDOM inputs, altering water column C:N:P ratios and temperatures that regulate photoautotrophic and heterotrophic production. Yet the relative importance of warming versus browning, and their combined effects on nutrient stoichiometry and microbial dynamics remain unclear. title: Combined effects of heatwaves and pollution on freshwater invertebrates: a scoping review of experimental approaches
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are highly vulnerable to climate change and anthropogenic pollution. Climate change is characterized particularly by an increase in average temperatures, with more intense, longer, and more frequent heatwaves (HWs). While the effects of contaminants are well documented, sometimes in the context of global warming, the impact of HWs, either alone or in combination with pollution, remains poorly studied in freshwater invertebrates. title: TECHNOGENIC POLLUTION OF RIVER WATERS IN THE ATYRAU REGION: HYDROCHEMICAL RISK ASSESSMENT FOR RECREATIONAL USE
abstract: River waters in the Atyrau region are utilised intensively for both economic and recreational purposes. The distinctive natural-climatic conditions of the region and ongoing technogenic loading exert a direct influence on the spatial variability of water quality. Consequently, assessing the hydrochemical state of river waters—specifically identifying areas with high pollution risk—is a matter of critical importance. title: “Compete, Cooperate... Why not both?” Player orientation and hybrid vs. competitive mechanics in gamified crowdsourcing with JellyfishGO!
abstract: Sustaining participant engagement while maintaining data quality is a central challenge for games with a purpose (GWAPs). In this article we examine whether player orientation (according to Bartle’s taxonomy) shapes contribution volume under competitive and hybrid (intra-team cooperation + light inter-team rivalry) GWAP mechanics. Although the design provisioned a purely cooperative arm, too few cooperative-only sessions materialised for session-level analysis, so the empirical comparison is Competitive versus Hybrid. title: Ecological and human health risk assessment of heavy metals in sewage sludge to ensure safe agricultural use
abstract: The use of sewage sludge in agricultural lands is one of the sludge management options that must be ensured to avoid environmental and health consequences. Considering the content of heavy metals in sewage sludge, the aim of this study was to measure the concentration of these elements in sewage sludge and assess the ecological and health risks resulting from its use in agricultural lands in southwestern Iran using Monte Carlo simulation. title: Social inequality among Neolithic fisher-foragers: Statistical analysis of grave goods from three Pitted Ware Culture cemeteries on Gotland, Sweden
abstract: How was burial wealth distributed within a Neolithic fisher-forager society? This paper explores this question by analyzing the distribution of burial goods at three different Middle Neolithic Pitted Ware Culture (PWC) cemeteries located on Gotland, Sweden, dating to c. 3000–2300 BCE. Specifically, our dataset consists of 40 burials from Visby, 51 burials from Ajvide, and 51 burials from Västerbjers. abstract: Abstract Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is a widely used biodegradable polyester. Still, the range of applications may be further broadened by extending the property range and improving recyclability. To address this issue, we gradually exchanged the adipate and terephthalate units, respectively, of PBAT with rigid spiroacetal units. title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. title: Co-benefits of managing saline cropland for the Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Soil salinization can constrain food production and alter nitrogen (N) losses to air and water, with implications for agricultural and environmental sustainability. These processes are linked to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet their implications for SDG-related outcomes remain poorly quantified. Here, we integrate spatially explicit global N budgets, satellite-derived crop canopy responses, and evidence from a meta-analysis of saline soil management practices to assess salinity-associated changes in SDG proxy indicators and the potential benefits of optimized management. abstract: ABSTRACT While solar‐driven photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting offers a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, sluggish interfacial charge transfer and long‐term instability remain critical bottlenecks. title: Soil Physicochemical Alteration Associated with Dolomite Influx Along the India–Bhutan Border
abstract: Abstract Dolomite, a calcium magnesium carbonate mineral, can adversely affect soil properties when present in excessive amounts. The India-Bhutan border region of West Bengal has experienced substantial declines in the quality and yield of fresh tea leaves, potentially associated with dolomite influx from the neighbouring lower Himalayas through recurrent flooding and the use of river water for irrigation. abstract: Conservation and utilization for traditional villages have shifted from individual-village to integrated regional planning. However, insufficient understanding of the spatial heritage connections among traditional villages has resulted in ambiguous cluster delineation and unclear spatial patterns, hindering concentrated and contiguous conservation. Thus, in this work, social network analysis was used to systematically investigate the heritage spatial relationships and spatial patterns of Huizhou traditional villages at the overall, meso, and individual levels. title: Effects of irradiance and pH on growth, photophysiology, and high-value metabolites production in Chlamydomonas acidophila
abstract: Abstract Acidophilic microalgae represent a promising but underexplored source of bioactive metabolites with potential biotechnological applications. Herein, we evaluated the influence of pH and irradiance on the growth performance, photophysiology, and metabolite profiles of a strain of the acidophile Chlamydomonas acidophila . title: Characterization of a novel topoisomerase inhibitor (NBTI) with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, including mycobacterial pathogens
abstract: Abstract Resistance to fluoroquinolone antibiotics is rising across bacterial pathogens, including the important pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ), posing a major threat to global health. Novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs) can overcome fluoroquinolone resistance. However, the only FDA-approved NBTI, the triazaacenaphthylene compound gepotidacin, is not indicated for mycobacterial infections. title: Same stimuli, disparate roles and nature across six types of theme parks
abstract: This study investigates how the same experiential attributes play different roles in shaping visitor experience evaluations and emotional responses across six theme park types. Based on 1660 questionnaires, a theme park experience scale was developed for cross-type comparison. The findings show that the psychological characteristics of experience dimensions vary across park types in their functional roles and cognitive–affective nature. title: Effect of an Occupational Health and Safety Educational Intervention on Knowledge, Practices, Musculoskeletal Disorders, and Injuries Among Oilseed Processing Workers
abstract: Occupational hazards, injuries, work-related illnesses, and fatalities remain core public health challenges in industrial settings. Workers in oilseed processing factories are exposed to multiple occupational risks; however, evidence regarding the effectiveness of occupational health and safety educational interventions in these settings remains limited and not explored and examined. abstract: Abstract Unlike jawed vertebrates that rely on immunoglobulin (Ig)-based adaptive immunity, jawless vertebrates utilize variable lymphocyte receptors (VLRs) for antigen recognition. Despite extensive studies into VLR diversity and antigen recognition, the molecular mechanism coupling VLR engagement to lymphocyte activation remains unexplored. title: Geographic Distribution of Adult Salmon Enteritis ( ASE ), Enterocytozoon schreckii , and Ceratonova shasta in Chinook Salmon Oncorhynchus tshawytscha (Walbaum, 1792) in Select Oregon and Washington State Hatcheries and Expanded Histopathologic Description of ASE
abstract: Adult salmon enteritis (ASE) is a severe intestinal disease affecting spring Chinook Salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) in the Pacific Northwest. ASE is strongly associated with prespawn mortality (PSM), a critical concern for endangered populations and continued Chinook Salmon management. This study characterizes the geographic distribution of ASE across Oregon and Washington watersheds, examines its association with two common parasites (Ceratonova shasta and Enterocytozoon schreckii), and provides detailed histopathological characterization of the disease. abstract: The presence of residual antibiotics in aquatic environments have become a significant ecological concern. This work developed a 2D metal-organic framework (MOF) and graphene oxide (GO) hybrid platform using a copper terephthalate framework, denoted Cu-TPA 1-x /GO x , for electrochemical detection of chloramphenicol (CAP). title: Real-World Outcomes of the Solitaire™ and React™ Devices from India’s First Multicenter Mechanical Thrombectomy Registry
abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is a low utilization of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in India and lack of a nationwide registry or data. This registry aimed to study the systems of care, functional outcomes, and cost effectiveness of MT treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: Patients were treated with Solitaire™ X and/or React™ catheter as the primary device/s. title: Compensatory abundance dynamics between an omnivore and a herbivore in agricultural landscapes
abstract: Population ecology grew from a question about how competition governs animal abundance, and its classic models center on intraspecific competition, by which a population is regulated toward its own carrying capacity. But abundance also responds to competition between species. Where two species draw on a shared carrying capacity, density compensation can occur, a decline in one offset by an increase in another. title: Hypoxic preconditioning promotes recipient monocyte adaptation to improve heart transplant outcomes
abstract: Acute heart allograft rejection remains a major barrier to long-term transplant survival, yet the mechanisms by which environmental factors influence recipient alloimmunity remain poorly understood. Clinical observations have suggested improved transplant outcomes at higher elevations, but the underlying biology has not been established. abstract: Abstract The 1976 Seveso disaster prompted a major shift in European industrial safety, leading to the Seveso Directives to prevent major chemical accidents. This review outlines the evolution of the Seveso framework, specifically focusing on the transition to the Seveso III Directive. title: Population‐Level Assimilated Dietary Responses of Black Bears to Baiting
abstract: ABSTRACT Wildlife feeding through intentional or unintentional practices can result in increased human‐wildlife conflict, disease transmission, population growth, and altered behavior. abstract: This study investigates the influence of friction stir processing (FSP) on the microstructural evolution, corrosion behaviour and electrochemical performance of Mg–2Gd–2Yb alloy shows potential for further evaluation in short-duration cathodic-protection applications. The as-cast base material (BM) was processed using two FSP conditions: FSP02 (2 passes, 33 mm/min, 1400 rpm) and FSP04 (4 passes, 33 mm/min, 1400 rpm). abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrasound‐assisted extraction (UAE) is promising for recovering seaweed bioactives, but confounding amplitude/power, energy input, and treatment time complicates mechanistic interpretation and cross‐study comparison. abstract: Knowledge about species' distributions is essential for understanding biodiversity patterns and predicting responses to climate change. The shapes of species' density distributions reflect how their performance varies across their range – shaped by environment, biotic interactions, and dispersal. abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels hold great promise for flexible electronics, electronic skin, and soft robotics, yet simultaneously achieving high strength, toughness, and conductivity remains challenging. abstract: ABSTRACT Air is receiving increasing recognition as a biologically rich source of taxonomically diverse environmental DNA (eDNA). Airborne eDNA has been sampled using various stationary devices, but if we can access it using mobile collection methods, we can rapidly assess biodiversity at large spatial scales. title: Integration of climate adaptation into spatial planning in Turkish cities: A comparative evaluation
abstract: Climate change adaptation is increasingly recognized as a core concern of spatial planning, yet the extent to which local adaptation priorities are reflected in statutory land-use decisions remains uncertain.This study evaluates climate-spatial integration at the local level in Türkiye and asks: To what extent are the thematic priorities in local climate adaptation plans reflected in the existing statutory spatial planning framework?A multi-source qualitative comparative research design was applied to four metropolitan municipalities-Sakarya, Konya, Muğla, and Samsun.Directed qualitative conte

title: Landslides: Challenges and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Landslides are among the most significant natural hazards worldwide, causing extensive financial and human losses and destroying natural resources annually. Therefore, comprehensive investigation of these hazards is an unavoidable requirement for future human life. A landslide is a natural disaster that claims human and animal victims every year. In addition to loss of life, landslides cause millions of dollars in financial damage globally. title: Environmental Impact of Landform and Landuse/Landcover Changes In Upper Ijai Basin, Manipur, India
abstract: Landform and landuse/landcover changes in upper Ijai Basin of Manipur have led notable environmental degradation driven primarily by current jhumming, expanding settlement, agricultural, infrastructural development and increase in population.These changes have increased soil erosion, sedimentation, surface runoff and risks of floods and landslide.The study area lies between 24 0 37 / 59.718 // N to 25 0 0 / 46.4796 // N latitudes and 93 0 32 / 20.126 // E to 93 0 47 / 58.87 // E longitudes.Present research is carried out using survey of India (SOI) topographic map on 1:50,000 scale and LANDSAT

title: Integrating parasite and host molecular diversity to delineate priority conservation areas in Mexico
abstract: The trematodes are one of the most diverse and abundant groups of parasites in the world; this plays fundamental roles in ecosystem functioning by regulating and influencing food web dynamics. However, these are not considered in the conservation planning. This study explores public databases to integrates, for the first time, molecular and distributional data of trematodes and their vertebrate hosts (fishes, birds, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals) to identify Priority Conservation Areas (PCAs) in Mexico through genetic diversity indices (nucleotide diversity π and haplotype diversity Hd). title: High-resolution mapping of pluvial flooding in ungauged agricultural catchments
abstract: Abstract. Accurate pluvial flood mapping in ungauged agricultural catchments is often constrained by a lack of calibration data. This study evaluates a parsimonious, high-resolution (1 m) distributed framework assessing peak discharge along concentrated flow paths, validated against 39 events in two nested experimental catchments (84 and 111 ha). title: Identifying knowledge gaps in a biodiversity database and their spatial determinants
abstract: Open-access biodiversity databases are valuable resources in the structuring and accessibility of species occurrence data. By compiling different data sources, they reveal the uneven spatial distribution of knowledge, with certain areas and taxonomic groups being better represented. Understanding the determinants of spatial and taxonomic knowledge gaps helps in informing the use of open-access data. title: Discrepancia entre superficie planimétrica y topográfica en San Andrés Tuxtla: implicaciones para la gestión municipal
abstract: El estudio aborda la discrepancia entre superficies planimétricas y topográficas en San Andrés Tuxtla, Veracruz, subrayando sus implicaciones fiscales, jurídicas y ambientales. La cartografía oficial reporta una extensión planimétrica de 955,3 km², pero el análisis con datos LiDAR de alta resolución (5 m) revela que la superficie real topográfica es mayor, de un incremento superior al 1,3%, lo que implica una diferencia efectiva de más de 12,3 km² adicionales respecto a la cifra oficial. title: Cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction of conifer fine roots
abstract: Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze-thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. Motivated by yellow-cedar decline, we evaluated competing mechanisms of freeze-thaw hydraulic dysfunction (xylem embolism and cortical lacunae) and whether root economics strategy predicts susceptibility. title: A framework to assess trajectories of societal and biological extinction
abstract: Threatened species that are societally extinct, which refers to the loss of a species' presence in human societies, are less likely to receive conservation attention, potentially resulting in their biological extinction going unnoticed. However, little is known about the process and forms of such extinction. Thus, we aimed to quantitatively demonstrate the concept of societal extinction. title: Paradigms in Practice: Urban Planning Theories and Governance Dualism in Batam
abstract: Batam was conceived as an ambitious state-led spatial experiment to rival regional industrial centers like Singapore through special economic zone policies, technocratic blueprints, and massive infrastructure investments. However, decades of development have placed the city in an ambiguous position, characterized by persistent socio-spatial inequalities and institutional friction. title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa modulates Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance
abstract: Abstract This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. The effects of co-culturing with Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ) on Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) virulence and survival under sub-MIC antibiotic exposure were assessed in vitro using 12 bacterial combinations. These combinations were divided into three groups: standard, co-isolated (from the same patient), and random combinations. abstract: Pelabuhan merupakan tempat kerja berisiko tinggi yang memerlukan pengawasan K3 berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis penerapan Safety Patrol sebagai upaya pengawasan K3 pada kegiatan operasional PT Pelindo Multi Terminal Branch Belawan. title: Modelación hidrológica e hidráulica del riesgo de inundación en la quebrada San Francisco, Piura, Perú
abstract: En cuencas con escasa información hidrometeorológica, delimitar zonas inundables exige combinar datos alternativos, evidencia de campo y modelación. Se modeló el comportamiento hidrológico, hidráulico y geoespacial de la quebrada del caserío San Francisco (Tambogrande, Piura, Perú) para identificar zonas inundables y estimar el riesgo. title: Nano–bio interfacial coupling regulates microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation: Mechanistic insights and multi-objective optimization
abstract: Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) is governed by the coupling between bacterial physiological activity and mineral nucleation; however, regulating such bio-mineral coupling remains challenging. Nanomaterials (NMs) offer reactive nano–bio interfaces that can link bacterial immobilization with heterogeneous CaCO₃ nucleation, yet their contribution to biomineralization efficiency remains mechanistically unclear. abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is a signal molecule in organisms of all kingdoms of life, acting as a second messenger during stress responses, growth and developmental processes. Nitric oxide synthases (NOS) are enzymes that produce NO by catalyzing the oxidation of L-arginine to citrulline and NO. title: Assessment of Pump- Based Drinking Water Quality Compliance with World Health Organization Standards in Central Gondar, Ethiopia.
abstract: Access to quality water is critical for public health; however, Ethiopia is grappling with challenges stemming from inadequate infrastructure and limited resources. This study evaluated the quality of drinking water sourced from large and medium-sized pump-based systems in Central Gondar, comparing the findings against WHO water quality standards. Employing an explanatory mixed methods research design, 415 respondents were selected through systematic sampling. title: Economic and financial assessment of the adoption of best management practices in Mediterranean citrus farming
abstract: Aim of study: To assess the financial and economic feasibility of adopting agricultural Best Management Practices (BMPs) in lemon farming, accounting for environmental externalities and comparing them with conventional and organic production systems. Area of study: Region of Murcia (SE Spain). Material and methods: The study applies a financial and economic investment evaluation framework to lemon farming systems. title: SEASONAL AND LAND USE INTERACTION ON WATER QUALITY IN THE CAMPO ALEGRE STREAM, GOIANO CERRADO: EVIDENCE OF URBAN IMPACT
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Brazilian Cerrado face escalating degradation from agricultural expansion and urban growth. Understanding the synergistic interaction between land use and seasonal hydrological pulses is critical for water resource management. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal dynamics of water quality and potential ecotoxicological risks in the Campo Alegre Stream basin (Santa Helena de Goiás, Brazil). abstract: Abstract The medicinal flora of the state of Sinaloa, Mexico, is widely used by rural and highland communities; however, scientific information regarding its phytochemical profile, antioxidant capacity, and toxicological safety remains scarce and fragmentary. title: Droughts in Africa: Adult Malnutrition and Occupational Change During Recurring and First‐Time Droughts
abstract: ABSTRACT How costly are droughts to adults' nutrition in Africa? Do people adapt to recurring droughts? We measure severe droughts using detailed satellite‐based index of greening observed bi‐monthly on a relatively high‐resolution 0.083° grid between 1982 and 2015, that captures persistent and severe deficits in soil moisture relative to grid‐cell and time‐of‐year normal moisture. abstract: As águas subterrâneas são um recurso importante para o abastecimento e o desenvolvimento urbano, o que exige a avaliação de sua vulnerabilidade à contaminação. Este estudo avaliou a vulnerabilidade intrínseca dos aquíferos em Maceió–AL pelo método GOD, com dados do Sistema de Informações de Águas Subterrâneas (SIAGAS). abstract: Specialised professional skills are required for sustainable facilities management to achieve operational effectiveness in commercial green buildings. The interest in the development of green buildings in Nigeria is on the increase, but empirical evidence on the competencies required to manage these facilities after occupation is still limited. The study examined the technical, managerial and interpersonal competences needed for sustainable facilities management in commercial green buildings in Lagos State, Nigeria. title: A cross-cultural assessment of Indigenous fire impacts on a culturally significant species: A case study from the Laynhapuy Indigenous Protected Area, northern Australia
abstract: Contemporary fire management increasingly calls for the inclusion of Indigenous peoples and knowledge systems, recognising that Indigenous burning has shaped landscapes for millennia. Yet research combining Indigenous and Western knowledge systems to evaluate how Indigenous fire regimes support culturally significant fauna remains rare. Working with the Yolŋu Yirralka Rangers in the Laynhapuy Indigenous Protected Area, northeast Arnhem Land, this study used a ‘both-ways’ Before-After-Control-Impact design to understand short-term responses of waṉ'kurra (northern brown bandicoot, Isoodon macrou

title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
abstract: Phase-transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase-transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction-powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. title: Genomes of Argia emma (Odonata: Coenagrionidae) and Epeorus albertae (Ephemeroptera: Heptageniidae) as novel resources for evolution, ecology, and conservation research
abstract: Paleopteran insects (Odonata and Ephemeroptera) occupy a crucial position in insect evolution and are ecologically significant indicators of freshwater ecosystem health. Recent improvement in the number of publicly available genomes and transcriptomes have advanced understanding of genome size evolution, morphological innovation, and ecological responses in these orders. abstract: Abstract Fish larvae feeding management represents one of the critical points for survival and aquaculture success. The larvae of many fish species require live feeds during early development, typically before being transitioned to formulated feeds through a process known as weaning. Despite the importance of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) , to Brazil’s aquaculture industry, the optimal timing for weaning and its effects on larval development remain unclear. title: Real-time quantification of fluid flows around bubbles during directional solidification
abstract: Directional solidification of bubbly liquids plays a critical role in shaping the microstructure and properties of many materials, yet the fluid dynamics governing bubble behavior during solidification remain poorly understood. Using cryo-confocal microscopy and particle image velocimetry, we quantify fluid flows around bubbles during solidification of water containing surfactants and tracers. abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are bio-based plastics produced by bacterial fermentation from renewable resources. PHAs with unsaturated bonds can undergo post-biosynthetic chemical modification or crosslinking to improve material properties. Previous studies have demonstrated that sulfur-vulcanized PHAs exhibited rubber-like properties and increased toughness. title: Material biography and technical utility of 8th-century wooden garden infrastructure: evidence of timber reuse in Unified Silla, Korea
abstract: Waterlogged wooden structures from royal garden contexts provide rare evidence of ancient landscape management and woodworking practices. This study investigates eleven wooden elements excavated from Wolji Pond, a royal garden of the Unified Silla Kingdom (eighth century CE), to evaluate possible timber reuse within aquatic installations. abstract: ABSTRACT The present study evaluated the consequences of dietary β‐glucan on growth, haematobiochemical parameters, and stress‐related gene expression in stinging catfish, Heteropneustes fossilis . A basal diet was supplemented with 0%, 0.05%, 0.1%, and 0.5% yeast β‐glucan and administered to fish at 7%–4% of body weight per day for 100 days. title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. title: Differential Patterns in β‐Diversity Among Plants, Soil Fungi and Insects Across Two Subarctic Landscapes
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Whether different organism groups show similar β‐diversity across space has major implications for biotic interactions. We compared β‐diversity patterns of three kingdoms across the same set of 40 sites, while explicitly accounting for sampling effects. title: Perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands among Chinese enterprise respondents: an exploratory network analysis
abstract: Workforce-needs surveys can conflate broad endorsement, uniform answering and specific relations among knowledge domains. We applied a measurement-aware diagnostic analysis to perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands. In a non-probability online survey, 93 Chinese enterprise respondents rated seven study-specific knowledge domains and selected six generic competencies; no invitation denominator was retained. abstract: Inflation control in archipelagic regions faces distinct challenges: dependence on inter-island supply, weather and shipping risks, and data fragmented across agencies. This article describes the design of SIKENDALI AMBON, a governance change project that integrates price, production, stock, demand, distribution, and logistics data into a logistics balance, an Early Warning System (EWS), and a Decision Support System (DSS) for Ambon City's Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID). title: Plasmid–plasmid interactions reshape extracellular vesicle cargo and antimicrobial resistance gene transfer potential
abstract: Plasmids are major drivers of bacterial horizontal gene transfer, including transfer of antimicrobial resistance. Plasmid dissemination extends beyond conjugation to include extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated transport. Although bacterial EVs can carry plasmid DNA, mechanisms governing which plasmids are incorporated into EVs remain poorly understood. title: Experimental study on performance and durability of Guangzhou soft soil solidified by a new slag-fly ash based cementitious material
abstract: The development of sustainable alternatives to Portland cement for soft soil stabilization is of great significance for reducing carbon emissions and enhancing infrastructure longevity. This study investigates a one-part slag-fly ash geopolymer binder containing solid sodium silicate for stabilizing Guangzhou soft clay. The optimal mix proportion was a slag-to-fly ash ratio of 90:10, a solid activator dosage of 14% relative to the precursor mass, and a water-to-binder ratio of 0.6, achieving a 28-day compressive strength of 2.01 MPa, 14.9% higher than the pure slag system. title: A double diamond model-based design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds
abstract: This study aims to improve patient experience and healthcare professionals' operational efficiency during patient transfer by proposing an integrated design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds within the Double Diamond framework.First, initial user requirements were identified through User Journey Map (UJM) analysis and multi-stakeholder interviews to explore key challenges and potential design needs during the medical transfer process. title: Subsurface temperature profiles across ten Egyptian cities: mapping low-enthalpy geothermal potential for regional energy adaptation
abstract: Abstract We present comprehensive data of daily subsurface temperature profiles for ten Egyptian cities, derived from Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. While ground temperature is a critical parameter for geothermal energy applications and building thermal performance, long-term measured subsurface temperature data across Egypt remains scarce. title: Targeting Response Regulator PprB Protein With Natural Compounds to Develop Novel Therapies Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: The pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) is recognized as an international pathogen of significance due to its multidrug resistance and strong ability to create biofilm as the basis of chronic and device-associated infections. The two-component regulatory system PprAB is important in the biofilm network, where the response regulator PprB regulates binding, aggregation, and biofilm production in the extracellular environment. title: Enhancing urban water resilience through green infrastructure in Kathmandu, Nepal
abstract: Rapidly growing cities in developing countries, including Kathmandu, Nepal, are struggling to handle water issues driven by both urban growth and climate change. Conventional grey infrastructure is unable to address the rising problems of flooding, polluted water, and declining groundwater recharge. This work evaluates how Green Infrastructure (GI) might help make Kathmandu Valley more sustainable and enhance ecosystem resilience through better water management. title: Legacy effects of selective coppicing on forest regeneration in Bronze Age Italy
abstract: Unambiguous evidence of sophisticated woodland and land-use management in Bronze Age southern Europe is presented from the Terramare culture in northern Italy. Archaeological layers dated to ~3,600 years ago reveal a society whose economy was structurally dependent on wood, used as both building material and fuel, defining what we term here a 'Wood Age' culture. abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on the growth performance, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome of a hybrid fish ( Megalobrama amblycephala ♀ × Culter alburnus♂ ). title: Rancang Bangun Aplikasi Bank Sampah Digital Berbasis Web Dan Mobile Untuk Pengelolaan Bank Sampah Unit Di Desa Rawa Panjang
abstract: Bank sampah di Desa Rawa Panjang, Kecamatan Bojonggede, Kabupaten Bogor telah beroperasi sejak 2021 melalui 32 unit yang tersebar di 24 RW, tetapi pencatatan transaksi, tabungan, dan pelaporan masih dilakukan secara manual sehingga rawan kesalahan, lambat, dan tidak sinkron antarunit. title: Selective feeding and niche differentiation in adult boreal Odonata revealed by DNA metabarcoding
abstract: Abstract Diet choice plays a key role in shaping species interactions, trophic dynamics and ecosystem function, yet the extent to which insect meso‐predators exhibit dietary specialisation and prey selection remains poorly understood. Understanding how meso‐predators partition resources and respond to prey availability is therefore important for interpreting food web structure and ecosystem dynamics. abstract: The ancient city of Palenque, in the Mayan territory, was established in a strategic position between the piedmont of the Sierra de Chiapas and the alluvial plain of the Michol River. The city became prominent during the Classic period (250–900 AD), when landscape modifications were carried out at different scales and with varying degrees of intensity during its construction. title: Governance-mediated value in sustainable trail tourism: shared responsibility, legitimacy, and stewardship in a nonprofit network
abstract: Long-distance walking trails support sustainable rural tourism, generating economic, environmental, and social value for host communities. Their viability often depends on governance arrangements involving public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and local tourism businesses that collectively manage environmental resources and visitor infrastructure. abstract: Shape memory alloys, particularly nickel-titanium, are widely used in medical technology for stent fabrication. Laser cutting of NiTi stents requires minimizing heat input and surface contamination to preserve the superelastic material properties and reduce post-processing effort. Ultrashort pulsed laser processing is well suited for this purpose, although a heat-affected zone remains. abstract: Arthropods are essential for maintaining soil ecosystem functioning. However, their full diversity remains insufficiently explored due to their taxonomic complexity, the limitations of traditional methods such as morphotaxonomy, and constraints associated with DNA barcoding approaches. In this study, we applied COI-based DNA metabarcoding to survey soil arthropod richness and community composition at a single timepoint across 28 long-term monitoring sites in Switzerland representing three land-use types, i.e., arable land, permanent grassland, and forest. abstract: Despite its role in local economic empowerment and broader economic growth in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, tourism activities can also present negative impacts for a tourism destination and tourists as consumers, particularly when the activities threaten the authenticity of the said destination. This phenomenon, often referred to as overtourism, raises legal issues regarding whether existing consumer-protection duties and remedies address losses from changed destination conditions. abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic introductions of non-native trout for recreation has had widespread effects on native ecosystems and their inhabitants. The Lahontan Cutthroat Trout (LCT; Oncorhynchus henshawi ) is native to western North America and is simultaneously experiencing population declines and hybridization due to climate change and non-native trout introductions, respectively. title: The cervical microbiome in hispanic populations in Texas and Puerto Rico with and without cervical dysplasia
abstract: Abstract Within the United States, Hispanic women, especially those in Puerto Rico, face an increased risk of cervical cancer development. The objective of this study was to explore the cervical microbiota of Hispanic women at high risk of developing HPV-induced cervical dysplasia or with cervical dysplasia treated in Texas and Puerto Rico. Cervical swab samples were collected from 296 participants (N = 80 Texan Non-Hispanic White, N = 98 Texan Hispanic, and N = 118 Puerto Rican Hispanic) during each patient’s initial visit and subjected to 16S V4 rRNA gene sequencing for microbiome profiling.

Fungal eremophilanes (EMPs), which share a conserved bicyclic core yet exhibit extensive oxidative diversification, provide an ideal model system to address this problem. abstract: Habitat fragmentation alters biodiversity patterns and ecological connectivity across agricultural landscapes. Here, we investigated how Patch-Corridor-Matrix (PCM) landscape components influence animal community structure within a vineyard-dominated landscape in Southern Italy. abstract: While conventional delivery systems can improve the intestinal efficacy of poorly soluble bioactives like curcumin (Cur), their solid-state structures and reliance on complex processing or chemical crosslinking often constrain their broader food applications. This study investigated liquid, polymer-rich complex coacervates between fish gelatin and fucoidan (COA) for the efficient encapsulation and enhanced intestinal delivery of Cur. title: A novel nudivirus from the Jonah crab (Cancer borealis: Brachyura)
abstract: Nudiviruses are double stranded DNA viruses known to infect arthropod hosts. Around 20 different nudiviruses have been identified from crustacean hosts alone. In crustaceans, the hepatopancreas is the primary target of infection, where nuclei appear hypertrophic under histological preparation due to a growing intranuclear viroplasm. title: Images of St. Theodore of Bathys Rhyax in the light of the results of the recent studies of the suburbs of Constantinople
abstract: Bathys Rhyax was a cult place near Constantinople dedicated to St. Theodore. Two artefacts associated with the site depict the saint, and bear inscriptions that confirm their connection to Bathys Rhyax. The first is an enamelled plaque dating from the 12th–13th centuries which is kept in the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg. The second is a lead seal dating from the second half of the 12th century in the collection of the Numismatic Museum in Athens. abstract: Abstract Metal Additive Manufacturing (AM) process selection is affected by uncertainty in techno-economic data and decision makers’ preferences. When competing technologies achieve similar overall performances, deterministic Multi-Criteria Decision-Making methods may produce strict rankings that do not adequately reflect the robustness of the underlying evidence. This work proposes a methodological framework for interpreting probabilistic Analytic Hierarchy Process results obtained through Monte Carlo simulation. abstract: Abstract An adsorbent, cross-linked chitosan-nicotinic acid beads (CLC-NAB) were fabricated in a sustainable green method and used effectively for the selective adsorption of mercury(II) from aqueous solutions. The CLC-NAB were characterized by swelling study, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM and elemental analysis. abstract: ABSTRACT Ancient tea agroforestry landscapes in Southwest China are structurally complex systems that may support high arthropod diversity, yet their biodiversity value remains poorly documented. We used COI metabarcoding of Malaise‐trap bulk samples to assess flying arthropod assemblages at four tea‐associated sites in the Mengku Ancient Tea and Cultural System, Yunnan, China: a wild ancient tea tree community, a village‐adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, a forest‐adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, and a young‐shrub tea plantation. title: Cell size asymmetry regulates neural stem cell proliferation and lineage expansion in the Drosophila brain
abstract: Abstract Asymmetrically dividing invertebrate and vertebrate stem cells can generate unequal sized sibling cells. However, the functional implications of cell size asymmetry (CSA) are underexplored. Here, we use Drosophila neural stem cells (NSCs) to investigate how changes in CSA impact NSC proliferation and cell fate decisions. Using live cell imaging, NSC lineage analysis, and gene expression profiling, we find that altering CSA increases the NSC pool but decreases lineage size and the number of differentiating progeny cells. title: Indirect costs of floods: a case study of highways road users
abstract: Abstract. Hydrometeorological events have a significant impact on road infrastructure and traffic flow. Floods can lead to the collapse or weakening of bridges, compromise river protection, and inundate riverine roads, thereby restricting or halting the traffic. These events incur additional user costs owing to the increased travel times resulting from the rerouting and reduced speeds on the affected roads. abstract: Nigeria has lived with floods, erosion, drought, pollution and conflict-driven displacement for decades, yet the performance of its disaster programmes is still judged more by activity than by the reliability of results. This article asks whether the principles and tools of Total Quality Management (TQM) can make disaster risk reduction (DRR) and recovery more dependable. abstract: Despite decades-old bans, persistent organic pollutants (POPs), including organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), remain a public health concern owing to persistence and bioaccumulation. abstract: Abstract Acetic acid bacteria and lactic acid bacteria are core microbial components in traditional Chinese vinegar brewing, where biofilm-associated microflora form unique and stress-resilient consortia. This study explored bacterial adaptive responses and biofilm development in bicultures of Acetobacter pasteurianus with individual Lactobacillus strains. Across all bi-cultures, A. pasteurianus exhibited a competitive dominance over Lactobacillus strains. abstract: Abstract DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis; yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, 3D genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. abstract: Abstract Primary freshwater crabs are keystone aquatic species, yet the potential impact of climate change on their distribution and conservation status remains unknown, particularly in biodiversity-rich areas such as South Africa. We employed maximum entropy and climatic niche modelling to evaluate the effects of climate change on the distribution of 17 Potamonautes species in South Africa and estimate protected area coverage for suitable habitats under both current and future climate projections of increased temperature, and the impact on the conservation of these species. abstract: ABSTRACT Acinetobacter baumannii , a critical priority pathogen, is also notable for its biofilm-forming abilities on medical devices like ventilators, catheters, and surgical drain tubes. abstract: Arctic tundra soils are sources or sinks of the greenhouse gases (GHGs) nitrous oxide (N 2 O), methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), but the simultaneous regulation of these GHGs by soil types remains unclear. abstract: This conceptual paper approaches the phenomenon of food waste in hospitality and tourism through the Marxist theory of labor. abstract: Este trabajo describe un modelo analítico pensado para analizar el éxito operativo de algoritmos en procesadores de escala intermedia ruidosa (NISQ) mediante un enfoque probabilístico. abstract: Abstract Hippophae rhamnoides plantations mitigate Gobi expansion and ameliorate soil quality, yet their effects on microbial communities in rhizosphere versus bulk soils across plantation ages remain unclear. abstract: Central Kalimantan is a significant pineapple-growing area in Indonesia, where cultivated pineapples exhibit morphological differences across production sites. abstract: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. abstract: Abstract The widespread use of non-food-grade paper for food packaging in developing countries poses an un-recognized public health threat, yet comprehensive assessments of trace element (TE) contamination in such materials remain scarce. abstract: The direct functionalization of α ‐C(sp 3 )─H bonds offers a powerful strategy for converting abundant feedstocks and complex molecules into value‐added products, yet sustainable catalytic platforms that avoid precious‐metal photocatalysts remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a metallaphotoredox system that combines recyclable carbon nitride nanosheets with nickel catalysis for the direct α ‐C(sp 3 )─H cross‐coupling of ethers, amides, and benzylic substrates under visible light. title: Alternative pathways for recognizing effective governance of Indigenous territories are critical to achieve global biodiversity targets: Lessons from Asian spiritual landscapes
abstract: Global conservation policy and state governance remain grounded in resource-oriented, secular frameworks. These can conflict with Indigenous peoples' and local communities' (IPLCs) relational ontologies, in which landscape elements are sentient beings, ancestral territories, and abodes of 'more-than-human' entities. abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling catalyst crystallinity is crucial yet challenging in electrocatalysis. Herein, ZIF‐67‐derived cobalt–nickel sulfide (CoNiS) with continuously tunable crystallinity from amorphous to semi‐crystalline and fully crystalline was synthesized by controlling sulfurization time. The semi‐crystalline CoNiS (a/c‐CoNiS, ∼35% crystallinity) delivered optimal oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and urea oxidation reaction (UOR) activity, requiring only 292 mV and 1.379 V to reach 100 mA cm −2 , respectively, outperforming both amorphous and crystalline counterparts. abstract: Los cambios en los manuales de Geografía e Historia de la Educación Secundaria Obligatoria (ESO) tras la reforma educativa de 2020 exigen un análisis por su relevancia como herramienta en la docencia y la materialización práctica del currículo. title: Centrifuge investigation of pile base effect on the lateral load capacity for large diameter rigid piles embedded in sand
abstract: Large-diameter drilled shafts show rotational-behavior under lateral loads inducing pressure on pile base, which may affect the lateral load capacity. This study examines the effect of pile base pressure (p base ) to the lateral load capacity of large-diameter drilled shafts in sand. A series of centrifuge tests were conducted on model piles with varying slenderness ratios (L/D) and soil conditions, where p base was directly measured. title: Integrative analysis of climate change drivers using ISM DEMATEL approach for structural decision making
abstract: This study aims to explore and structure the complex interplay of key climate change drivers using an integrated Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) approach. By focusing on 14 variables identified through expert consensus, the study seeks to uncover the hierarchical structure and causal relationships influencing climate change, particularly within the context of developing countries such as Indonesia. title: Does the Conversion of Biogenic Organic Nitrates to Nitric Acid Control the Lifetime of Atmospheric Nitrogen Oxides Over the Eastern U.S.?
abstract: Abstract Airborne measurements over the Southeast US during the summer of 2013 revealed the evolution of nitrogen oxides and nitric acid that was markedly different from that over the Northeast US during the winter of 2015. We can reconcile the observed trends by invoking nitrogen oxide reservoir species formed under elevated NO x environments that then convert to HNO 3 . title: Vertical distribution of magnetic susceptibility in permeable sandy soils
abstract: Arenosols are deep sandy soils with coarse texture, low water-holding capacity, rapid permeability and low nutrient content. Despite of their low agricultural potential, they support both protected natural and productive forests. Iron, although low in content, plays important role in pedogenesis and coloring of these soils. Magnetic susceptibility represents very useful proxy tool to assess the content of ferrimagnetic forms of iron oxides in soils. However, magnetic susceptibility of Arenosols is very rarely described. title: Spatial metabolic insights of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm treatments using stable isotope labeling with DESI mass spectrometry imaging
abstract: Bacteria form biofilms on diverse substrates, and these communities can cause persistent infections owing to their elevated antibiotic resistance. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of chronic infections because of its ability to form biofilms, which makes it difficult to eradicate with conventional antibiotics. The metabolic response of P. aeruginosa biofilms to antibiotic treatment, however, remains only partially understood. Here, desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI) was used to map the spatial metabolic responses of mature and developing P. aeruginos

title: Risk Analysis of CD-BIM Integration in Structural Jetty Schematic Design: Time Performance
abstract: The early design stage of jetty infrastructure is crucial for setting the project's budget and time. However, current digital processes often do not fully integrate these tasks. Computational design and Building Information Modeling (BIM) have sped up design cycles through faster iterations and improved coordination. Still, they have also increased the likelihood of mistakes, extra work, and project delays. This research analyses risks in design processes that practitioners judge as having a significant impact on design time performance and how to mitigate them. The analysis identified 66 pote

title: Honeycomb monolith-based multichannel reactor for methane bioconversion into ectoine
abstract: A novel gas-liquid multichannel bioreactor based on cordierite honeycomb monoliths was engineered and operated under internal gas and liquid recirculation for methane bioconversion into ectoine. The assessment of the volumetric gas-liquid mass transfer coefficients for O 2 ( k L a O 2 ) in this novel bioreactor showed values up to 1472.7 ± 111.6 h −1 , representing an increase of one order of magnitude over conventional bubble column reactors. title: Spatial and Seasonal Assessment of Physicochemical Water Quality in the Lower Tapi River
abstract: Deteriorating of river water quality has become an important environmental challenge in India, particularly where river system is relied upon for drinking water supply. The Tapi river serves as major water resources for Surat. The study evaluates the seasonal variation and quality of water status of Tapi river in Gujarat, India, using the Weighted Arithmetic Water Quality Index (WAWQI) method. This study presents a yearlong assessment (Dec. 2024 to Nov. 2025) of seasonal and spatial variations in water quality at five selected sites: Galteshwar, Kamrej, Utran, Causeway and ONGC Bridge. journal: Research Journal of Chemistry and Environment

title: Nano-Boron Enhances Boron Accumulation and Alters the Tomato Leaf Metabolome: Molecular Modeling of Leaf-Surface and Boron Transporter–Metabolite Interactions
abstract: Abstract Boron (B) deficiency severely limits tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) productivity and fruit quality, particularly in alkaline or low-organic-matter soils, while conventional foliar boron fertilizers suffer from low uptake efficiency and environmental losses. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel nanoboron (NB) formulation and evaluated its efficacy compared with boric acid using physicochemical characterization, molecular simulations, greenhouse studies, metabolomics, and field validation. title: The densified city and the powerline right-of-way encroachment in Nigeria: Greening as an important intervention.
abstract: Urban densification is generally promoted as a strategy for sustainable development. However, it may also produce unintended consequences, such as exposure to environmental hazards. This study examines potential electrical hazard exposure in relation to the powerline right-of-way (ROW) encroachment in Port Harcourt Metropolis, a rapidly densifying oil and gas industry hub in southern Nigeria, using a mixed-method approach that combines geospatial datasets and social survey data. abstract: Abstract Enhanced weathering (EW) of silicate minerals has emerged as a promising carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy, with potential benefits for soil fertility and crop performance. However, the soil processes that determine these co-benefits remain poorly constrained. In particular, interactions between basalt amendments and soil biota such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) may influence nutrient mobilization and plant uptake, but these effects have rarely been quantified. title: Recorded storm damage and mortgage servicing complaints in US counties
abstract: Storms push households into contact with mortgage servicers over missed payments, forbearance and insurance. We ask where that contact becomes formal complaints. We assign 228,803 of 280,348 mortgage complaints filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau from 2015 to 2024 to counties and compare 898 isolated county exposures to NOAA tropical-storm and hurricane reports in 18 storm months with unexposed counties. title: Reframing Stakeholder Roles in Multistakeholder Partnerships: A Role Theory Approach to Collaborative Action on Food Waste
abstract: ABSTRACT Multistakeholder partnerships (MSPs) are promoted as collaborative arrangements to address food waste, yet most research focuses on core stakeholders directly involved in food production and consumption, leaving the roles of supporting stakeholders underexplored. This study redirects attention to these vital actors, such as governmental bodies, financial institutions, and industry associations, whose engagement can be important to initiating, stabilizing, and sustaining collaboration. title: PCOMMUNITY EDUCATION ON GREEN BELT STRUCTURING AND PARTICIPATORY ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY MONITORING AROUND COAL-FIRED POWER PLANT X
abstract: Coal-fired power plants secure baseload electricity but expose neighbouring settlements to fly ash, stockpile dust, flue gases (SO2, NOx) and noise, while residents are usually treated as passive recipients of these impacts and have no means of checking air quality themselves. This participatory action research designed, implemented and evaluated an education programme on multi-strata green belt structuring and citizen-science environmental monitoring for communities around Coal-Fired Power Plant X. title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. We describe two related but diverged groups of conjugative megaplasmids (>300 kilobases) in the human gut microbiome, which we named Hodors. title: A Basic Matrix Protein Songin Selectively Promotes Aragonite Aggregation and Modulates Calcium Carbonate Crystallization in Hyriopsis cumingii
abstract: Abstract In China, the pearl industry of Hyriopsis cumingii contributes approximately 80% of pearl production. Matrix proteins play crucial roles in shell and pearl biomineralization. However, the functions of basic matrix proteins in H. cumingii remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a novel predicted secreted basic matrix protein, designated Songin, from the freshwater pearl mussel H. cumingii. title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade-off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor-acceptor (D-A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge-transfer efficiency-with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. title: Multiscale bamboo reconstruction enables adsorption-coupled solar evaporation for contaminated water treatment
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation efficiently separates water from nonvolatile contaminants but provides limited control over pollutants retained at the evaporation interface. Here, we report a bamboo-derived adsorption-coupled solar evaporator (ASE) created by multiscale reconstruction of bamboo. title: Simulating an imaging atmospheric radio telescope to observe cosmic gamma rays and cosmic neutrinos
abstract: Observations of cosmic gamma rays with energies above the 10 12 electronvolts (TeV) regime are often a direct probe of events where our theoretical predictions are challenged by extreme conditions. Because high energetic cosmic gamma rays are rare, one needs collection areas with the size of roughly a dozen football fields (10 5 m 2 ) or more to gather significant counting statistics in a short time. title: Redirecting gypsum scaling in pervaporation desalination via activated alumina granules
abstract: Membrane scaling, particularly CaSO4 (gypsum) crystallisation, severely limits the practical application of pervaporation (PV) desalination for high-salinity wastewater treatment. Herein, an online interception strategy using nitric acid-activated alumina granules (AAG) is proposed to redirect gypsum scaling from the membrane surface to a sacrificial medium. By tuning nitric acid activation, the physicochemical properties of AAG were optimised. abstract: This study established a dual-strategy framework for heavy metal mitigation in date palm products by integrating physicochemical washing of whole Zahidi fruit with biosorption by inactivated Lactobacillus biomass in date syrup. A sequential baseline-creation design helped distinguish measured solid-phase metal changes from potential true removal. Phase 1 evaluated tap water washing, chemical soaking (citric acid, deionized water, NaHCO₃), and ultrasonication on Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺, and As partitioning, alongside semi-trained sensory evaluation. title: QUALITY OF LIFE OF RESIDENTS IN GAS FLARING COMMUNITY IN AKWA IBOM STATE, NIGER DELTA REGION, NIGERIA
abstract: Gas flaring remains a persistent environmental and public health issue in Nigeria’s Niger Delta, particularly in Akwa Ibom State, where crude oil extraction is widespread. This research compares the quality of life (QoL) of residents of a gas flaring community (Mkpanak) and a non-gas flaring community (Okposo) in the Niger Delta region of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional, comparative survey was conducted. Multistage sampling was used to sample 389 respondents. title: Optimizing seismographic network strategies for earthquake surveillance under linguistic pythagorean fuzzy dynamic knowledge
abstract: Global seismographic networks (GSNs) capture fine details of ground motion signals, assisting scientists and governments in detecting and characterizing earthquakes and other seismic events worldwide. Continued improvements in these networks enhance knowledge about Earth structure, atmospheric interaction, and geological hazards. title: “And why here?” Reading Hong Kong in Nick Joaquin’s The Woman Who Had Two Navels
abstract: Nick Joaquin (1917–2004) is a Filipino literary master and national artist whose numerous works include the prize-winning novel The Woman Who Had Two Navels (1961). Its plot revolves around the Manilan protagonist Connie Escobar’s flight into Hong Kong and her insistence that “she [has] two navels” (1). title: Experimental investigation of suction flow enhancement in submerged jet pumps via perforated mixing chamber
abstract: Liquid–liquid jet pumps are essential in dredging, slurry transport, and submerged mixing applications, yet their suction performance remains constrained by the limited entrainment area in conventional solid-walled mixing chambers. This study experimentally investigates the geometric modification of using perforated mixing chambers that enable distributed radial suction driven by the hydrostatic pressure differential between the surrounding fluid and the low-pressure core induced by the motive jet. abstract: ABSTRACT Bio‐based aerogels are a compelling class of sustainable materials, with some of them distinguished by their exceptional thermal superinsulating performance, i.e. conductivity lower than that of air. However, their practical use is limited by poor stability in humid environment. Pectin/polyurea aerogels were developed to address this issue. abstract: N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) serves as a key carbon source and regulatory signal for secondary metabolism in actinomycetes, yet its role in Actinokineospora remains poorly understood. Here, genome mining, transcriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to investigate GlcNAc-supplemented Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) supplementation on endocrine and metabolic profiles of forty-five nulliparous rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle. Animals were randomly assigned to one of three diets: control (CNT), 5% extruded linseed (L), and 5% extruded linseed plus 0.2% Padina pavonica extract (LPP). abstract: Cosmogenic Selection (CGS) is proposed as a conceptual framework for examining how organized reality develops across physical, biological and cognitive domains. Its central proposition is that what persists changes what can happen next: differences enter relationships, some consequences are retained, and retained organization reshapes or expands subsequent possibilities. title: Tailored Graphene Oxide Incorporated PES/CA Mixed‐Matrix Loose Nanofiltration Membranes for Water Softening and Divalent Salt Removal
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving a simultaneous enhancement of permeability and selectivity remains a central challenge in nanofiltration membrane design. Here, we report the fabrication of high‐performance polyether sulfone–cellulose acetate (PES/CA) mixed‐matrix membranes via phase inversion, employing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a pore‐forming agent and graphene oxide (GO) as a hydrophilic nanofiller to precisely tailor membrane structure and transport behavior. title: Integrated Topological, Physical, and Functional Vulnerability of Road Networks to Compound Seismic-Landslide Hazards in the East African Rift
abstract: Abstract Road networks in tectonically active regions face compound seismic and landslide hazards that can simultaneously disrupt multiple links. However, existing vulnerability assessments typically examine physical, topological, and functional dimensions in isolation and address only single hazard types. This study presents an integrated three-dimensional vulnerability framework combining graph theory, geographic information systems, and multi-criteria decision analysis to assess the compound seismic-landslide vulnerability of northeastern Ethiopia’s federal road network.
