title: Fibrinolytic and coagulation activities of crude extracellular preparation from Bacillus cereus group strain SF-4
abstract: Fibrinolytic enzymes have attracted considerable attention as potential alternatives to conventional thrombolytic agents because they degrade fibrin, a major structural component of blood clots. Fermented seafood products are promising sources of protease-producing microorganisms; however, fermented bamboo clam (Solen sp.) rusip remains underexplored as a source of bacteria with fibrinolytic potential. title: Isoprenoid quinone profiling using a novel semi-quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method: application to wastewater sludges
abstract: Isoprenoid quinones are ubiquitous redox lipids that mediate electron transfer in various cellular processes across all domains of life. These molecules also serve as taxonomic and metabolic markers, facilitating the characterisation of microbial communities. However, their structural diversity and extreme hydrophobicity are challenging for comprehensive detection and quantification in complex biological matrices. title: Type VI secretion drives reciprocal growth inhibition among symbiotic Vibrio fischeri strains
abstract: Bacterial cells are often in direct contact with one another and compete for nutrients and space. The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a contact-dependent mechanism that enables bacteria to deliver toxic effectors into neighbouring cells. Vibrio fischeri is a bacterial symbiont of the Hawaiian bobtail squid Euprymna scolopes and encodes a T6SS on its second chromosome (T6SS2) that promotes interference competition among strains within the squid light organ. title: Lipoprotein(a): Bridging the gap between risk prediction, measurement, and emerging therapeutics
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined lipoprotein and a well-established causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Despite increasing recognition in clinical guidelines, Lp(a) testing remains underused, and targeted therapies are only now emerging. This narrative review summarizes the biology, cardiovascular risk, measurement challenges, emerging therapies, and translational barriers of Lp(a), highlighting its role in contemporary cardiovascular prevention. title: A Low-Cost IoT Smart Pill Box with Physical Intake Verification: Design and Evaluation in Real-Life Use
abstract: Medication non-adherence undermines the treatment of chronic diseases, and reminder applications cannot show whether a dose was taken. This paper reports a 52-day field evaluation of a low-cost smart pill box that registers each intake event with an infrared sensor and a reed switch, time-stamps it with a battery-backed clock, queues events locally during network outages and forwards them to a Laravel server that alerts the patient, a caregiver and a physician by staged e-mails. abstract: Understanding species distributions is essential for biogeographical and ecological studies. This study reports the geographical ranges of two large-size octannulate species of the leech genus Orobdella Oka, 1895, O. octonaria Oka, 1895, and O. nakahamai Nakano, 2016, based on newly collected specimens. title: Leptospira qPCR Positivity in Terrestrial Micromammals and Dogs in Saen Thong (Tha Wang Pha District), Ecological Analysis in Micromammals, and Leptospira Diversity Across Animal Hosts in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Human leptospirosis is a disease of public health importance in Thailand, but the animal species involved in the transmission cycle have not been fully uncovered. This study investigated Leptospira infection in dogs and terrestrial micromammals in rural Nan Province, Thailand, and the pathogen diversity. Sera from 95 seemingly healthy dogs and kidney samples from 399 micromammals were analyzed using real-time PCR for Leptospira detection, followed by conventional PCR and sequencing of infecting Leptospira . title: Nested economies of scale in global city mass
abstract: Abstract A long-standing puzzle in urban science is whether there is an intrinsic match between human populations and the mass of their built environments. Existing models assume proportionality: each additional resident demands the same amount of building material. Our analysis of more than 3,000 cities worldwide challenges this linear assumption. title: Aflatoxins contamination of aquafeed: Toxicological impacts and mitigation strategies in finfish and crustacean aquaculture
abstract: Mycotoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi that pose a significant challenge to the safety, productivity, and sustainability of global aquaculture. Aquafeed ingredients, particularly cereals, oilseed meals, and other plant-derived protein sources, are frequently contaminated with mycotoxins, including aflatoxins (AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2), ochratoxin A (OTA), fumonisins (FB1), trichothecenes (T-2 toxin), and zearalenone (ZEA). title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of reservoir storage in the Algarve region (Southern Portugal): implications for regional water security
abstract: ABSTRACT The Algarve region in southern Portugal relies heavily on reservoirs to support domestic water supply, irrigation, tourism, and other economic activities. This study examined the spatio-temporal dynamics of storage in six major reservoirs: Bravura, Arade, Funcho, Odelouca, Odeleite, and Beliche, using monthly and annual storage data from 2012 to 2025. title: Phytochemical Profiling and Anticancer Potential of Ipomoea hederifolia L. Root Extract: LC–MS Characterization and Molecular Docking Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer remains a major global health burden, with millions of new cases reported annually. Plant‐based products are gaining popularity due to their remarkable biological activity and fewer side effects. The Convolvulaceae family exhibits promising anticancer effects; Ipomoea hederifolia is one of the species rich in bioactive secondary metabolites. This is the first study that aims to investigate the anticancer potential of the plant against HepG2 cells. title: Cellulose acetate nanoparticles: impacts of concentration and exposure time on the biochemistry and hematology of juvenile Colossoma macropomum
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the physiological impacts of acute-exposure of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) to different concentrations of cellulose acetate nanoparticles at different sampling times. A total of 120 juvenile C. macropomum (38.91 ± 5.57 g and 13.76 ± 0.74 cm in total length) were distributed in 12 tanks of 150 L, in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The juveniles were kept in water containing cellulose acetate nanoparticles (CANs) at four different concentrations (treatments): 0 mg L − ¹, 0.01 mg L − ¹, 0.10 mg L − ¹ and 1.00 mg L − ¹. title: A practical guide to using Q‐methodology in conservation science
abstract: Abstract Conservation scientists and practitioners are increasingly incorporating social research methods into their work. Q‐methodology is an established social research tool with multiple potential applications in conservation, but its uptake remains comparatively limited. Q‐methodology integrates qualitative and quantitative approaches, providing an accessible, effective technique for identifying subjective perspectives on conservation topics. It is particularly well suited to describing diverse views on a particular topic and understanding the foundations of conflict. In addition to genera

title: Status and ontogenetic structure of rare wild populations of Vitis vinifera (Vitaceae) in Uzbekistan
abstract: Vitis vinifera is an ancient fruit crop whose wild populations constitute a valuable genetic resource for grape breeding. In Uzbekistan, these populations are rare and fragmented, and the species is listed under Category 3 in the national Red Data Book (2019). This study assessed the ontogenetic structure, demographic characteristics, and conservation status of six wild cenopopulations of V. vinifera in Uzbekistan. title: Agronomic traits and fruit quality of milk thistle ( Silybum marianum ) genotypes under water stress
abstract: Abstract Milk thistle ( Silybum marianum (L.) Gaertn.) is an important medicinal plant, yet limited research has addressed its agronomic performance and genetic diversity under water‐limited conditions. This study evaluated the potential of 28 Iranian ecotypes and one foreign accession to assess variation in agronomic traits, oil concentration, and methanol extractable dry matter under normal irrigation and drought stress during two growing seasons. Drought stress reduced several yield‐related traits; however, some ecotypes, particularly those originating from southern regions of Iran, maintai

title: Recent advancements in photosynthetic microalgae for microbial activity, nutrition, and health benefits
abstract: Abstract Microalgae, with their complex aerobic photosynthetic system, contribute 40%-50% to atmospheric oxygen (O2), and are increasingly recognized as a source of nutrients in many countries (including China, Japan, and India). Although numerous reviews discuss microalgae for biofuel production and wastewater treatment, a few reviews address their applications in health benefits, food ingredients, microbial activity, and regulatory considerations for safe consumption. In this review, the collection, summarization, comparison, and discussion from the recent literature (past five years) on mic

title: Integrating Spirulina cultivation as a bioregeneration step in a closed loop CO2 absorption process: Experimental validation
abstract: The integration of microalgal cultivation with CO₂ capture via chemical scrubbing can improve carbon utilization efficiency while reducing operational costs. However, the reciprocal effects between absorption and cultivation units need further investigation. This study evaluated the integration of carbonate-based CO₂ capture with cultivation of the alkaliphilic cyanobacterium Spirulina sp. in a Bicarbonate-based Carbon Capture and Algae Production System (BICCAPS). The effects of bicarbonate concentration, air sparging, medium recycling and absorption promoters were investigated experimentally

title: Air quality and noise exposures near an urban freight railyard in Canada
abstract: Growing demand for freight rail alongside trends in residential land use can lead to increased railyard activity near populations. Railyard locomotive and train movements generate air and noise pollution associated with adverse health effects. We sampled gaseous and particulate pollutants and measured sound levels over 15 months in a Toronto (Ontario, Canada) residential neighbourhood surrounding an active freight marshalling railyard. journal: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment

title: Impact of the 1 April 2026 Artemis II Rocket Launch on the Upper Atmosphere: TIMED/GUVI Observations
abstract: Abstract The NASA Artemis II rocket was successfully launched at 06:35 p.m. ET (22:35 UTC) on 1 April 2026 from the Kennedy Space Center (28°35′28″N 80°39′03″W). The rocket plume caused enhanced Lyman α emission (up to ∼3 kR) observed by TIMED/GUVI on 2–6 April (5 days). Its peak intensity decreased linearly from April 3 at a rate ∼740 R/day. The half‐maximum width of the zonal Lyman α intensities at 20°–30° latitude (at ∼01:30 p.m. local solar time) increased from ∼3,000 km on April 2–∼9,000 km on April 6. institutions: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by integrating a Ti-based metal–organic framework with a green-synthesized NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS binary core–shell heterostructure for visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution. title: STRENGTHENING LOCAL ECONOMIES THROUGH ECOTOURISM: EVIDENCE FROM BINTANG DISTRICT CENTRAL ACEH PROVINCE, INDONESIA
abstract: This study investigates the role of ecotourism in strengthening local economies in Bintang District, Central Aceh by identifying key potentials within natural and socio-cultural resources. It explores how assets such as Lake Laut Tawar, agrobased livelihoods, and community enterprises can drive sustainable economic development. The study analyzes stakeholder collaboration, focusing on governance, participation, and community empowerment. It evaluates contributions to income diversification, employment, and micro-enterprise growth while identifying structural and institutional constraints. The

title: From climate hazards to diet and physical activity pathways: Investigating policy intersections for health in five global South Cities
abstract: Introduction Climate change, rapid urbanization, and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) pose intersecting threats to public health in low- and middle-income countries. While evidence supports integrating health into climate policy, limited attention has been paid to how climate change and urban resilience policies address key NCD-related pathways, particularly diet and physical activity. journal: The Journal of Climate Change and Health

title: Urinary kisspeptin as a non-invasive reproductive biomarker in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does
abstract: Kisspeptin is an upstream regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and plays a critical role in the estrous cycle and pregnancy in domestic animals. The KISS1 gene, also known as the "metastatin" gene, has emerged as a promising diagnostic biomarker in reproductive physiology across livestock species. This study aims to explore the dynamics of urinary/plasma kisspeptin and their creatinine-normalized ratio during the bovine and caprine estrous cycle and pregnancy. Experimental animals comprised two groups (cyclic and pregnant). The cyclic group consisted of 12 cyclic crossbred cows
institutions: National Institute of Animal Nutrition and Physiology

title: Development of Lemuru Fish Protein Hydrolysate–Moringa Leaf Formulation (HPILK) as a Supplementary Feeding for Stunting Children
abstract: Background: Stunting remains a major nutritional problem in Indonesia, highlighting the need for locally developed, nutrient-dense supplementary foods. Objective: This study aimed to develop a beverage powder formulated from lemuru fish protein hydrolysate and Moringa leaf powder (HPILK) and evaluate its sensory characteristics, nutritional composition, and potential nutrition claims. Methods: Lemuru fish hydrolysate was produced enzymatically and combined with Moringa leaf powder. title: Enzymatic Transformation of Soluble Nonreactive Phosphorus Compounds to Improve Phosphorus Removal and Recovery Potential from Wastewater
abstract: Abstract A substantial fraction of total phosphorus (TP) in the environment exists as soluble nonreactive phosphorus (sNRP). These compounds can resist treatment processes and therefore persist in wastewater effluent, posing challenges for meeting stringent TP limits and long-term eutrophication risks. We employed an integrated experimental and chemoinformatics approach to evaluate the chemical diversity of sNRP and its impact on the fate of sNRP during enzymatic treatment. title: A Self‐Cleaning Solar Evaporator Based on MXene/Aramid Nanofiber Aerogels for Efficient Water Desalination
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its high energy conversion efficiency and broad accessibility to solar energy, interfacial solar steam generation presents a promising, and cost‐effective solution for desalination of saline water. However, salt accumulation on evaporator surfaces remains a major challenge, especially in the case of high‐salinity environments as the blockage it creates significantly hinders the efficiency as well as continuity of the evaporation process. title: A century of soybean breeding increased photosynthetic capacity but not NPQ relaxation
abstract: Accelerating photoprotective regulation to improve carbon assimilation is a promising strategy to increase crop productivity. Although rapid non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation has been validated as a target through metabolic engineering, it remains unclear whether conventional breeding has improved this trait. Here, we investigated whether more than a century of soybean breeding enhanced NPQ relaxation alongside light-saturated carbon assimilation and seed traits. institutions: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology

title: Traceable Privacy and Cybersecurity Compliance Control Baseline for Indonesian Academic Information Systems
abstract: Academic information systems process student identities, academic records, library transactions, authentication logs, learning analytics, and third-party service integrations. In Indonesia, privacy and cybersecurity compliance is difficult to operationalize because legal obligations are often separated from system risks, IT governance controls, ownership, and audit evidence. This study develops a traceable privacy and cybersecurity compliance control baseline for Indonesian academic information systems. title: New insights on Suretta nappe structure and lithostratigraphy revealed by high-resolution geological survey of Val di Lei (Central Alps, Italy)
abstract: This contribution presents a 1:10.000 scale geological map of the Val di Lei basin (Italian Central Alps), produced within the framework of the Italian National Geological Mapping Project (CARG). The area mainly exposes rocks of the Suretta nappe (Middle Penninic) and minor portions of the Avers nappe (Upper Penninic). The Suretta nappe comprises a polymetamorphic basement, Carboniferous–Permian metaplutonites, and a Permian–Mesozoic metasedimentary cover. title: Climate variability and change as an emerging operational challenge to malaria control among district malaria focal persons in Dar es Salaam Tanzania
abstract: Malaria transmission in Tanzania has declined significantly over the past decade, following the scale-up of vector control and case management interventions. However, climate change may threaten these gains through long-term changes in climatic conditions that could influence mosquito breeding patterns and transmission dynamics. Short-term and seasonal fluctuations in rainfall and temperature, may also influence malaria risk and disrupt vector control activities, particularly during heavy rainfall. District malaria focal persons are responsible for implementing and coordinating malaria control
institutions: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences
Mbeya University of Science and Technology

title: Quantum Chemical Insight into Species Competition in Electrochemical Upgrading of Bio-Oil
abstract: Abstract Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents an alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value-added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. title: Optimizing Renewable Energy Capacity Development Using Standard-Pseudo Multi-Mode Gradient Descent Algorithm for Australia’s 2050 Net-Zero Transition
abstract: Australia’s transition toward net-zero emissions (NZE) requires the integration of renewable energy (RE) sources with substantially different capacity requirements and operational characteristics. However, existing transition assessments provide limited quantitative evaluation of how “Proposed”, “Anticipated”, and “Committed” renewable capacity additions may influence the required capacity pathway. title: Assessing the impacts of projected climate scenarios on irrigation reliability and reservoir sustainability in Sri Lanka’s dry zone
abstract: Abstract Climate change poses major challenges for irrigation water management in Sri Lanka’s dry zone. This study assesses the performance of the Nachchaduwa reservoir under historical and projected climate scenarios using multiple General Circulation Models (GCMs). Eight GCMs were ranked through compromise programming, with the top three models bias-corrected and downscaled to generate climate projections for the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) scenarios: SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, under near-future (2015–2050) and mid-future (2051–2075) conditions. title: Quantifying urban heat: A spatiotemporal study of climate change and population growth in Ikorodu, Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: Climate change and rapid urban growth are increasingly altering local climatic conditions in cities across the Global South.One important manifestation is the urban heat island (UHI) effect, whereby built-up urban areas experience higher temperatures than surrounding less-developed areas.This study examines the relationship between climate change, urban growth, and rising temperatures in Ikorodu, a rapidly expanding peri-urban area of Lagos State, Nigeria.Using simulated but realistic datasets derived from Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) records, Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Chang

title: Determinants of Enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by Product Type: Focus on Fixed-Effects Models
abstract: This study analyzed the effects of paid claims, government subsidy rates, and disaster relief grants, among other factors, on enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by product type. The study employed a fixed-effects model and proposed policy improvements to analyze panel data constructed from the insurance records of 229 local governments from 2013 to 2025. title: Financial and economic performance of coconut plantation rejuvenation assisted by engineered wood products: A Fijian case study
abstract: Coconut plantations support the livelihoods of millions of smallholder families globally, including a high proportion who live in poverty. Many growing regions are caught in a ‘senility trap’, with large areas over the age of 60, with nut yields well-below their potential. Presently, senile palm removal incurs high direct costs and opportunity costs associated with foregone nut production before replanted coconuts become commercially productive. title: Food waste to biomass approach: A sustainable strategy for the production of alternative microbial culture media for filamentous fungi growth
abstract: The valorization of organic waste is still one of the challenges in the path towards environmental sustainability and a circular bioeconomy. This research aimed at assessing the ability of three substrates of organic residues (olive pomace, potato peels and the green seaweed Ulva lactuca) to be used as alternative culture media for filamentous fungi. Mycelial growth on these media was compared with the conventional Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Sabouraud media using three fungal species namely Fusarium oxysporum (F1), Fusarium solani (F2) and Alternaria alternata (N2) as biological models. institutions: Université Djilali de Sidi Bel Abbès

title: Ammonia and methane mitigation from dairy manure using sulfur‐based manure storage additives
abstract: Abstract Dairy manure storage is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and other air pollutants, including methane (CH 4 ) and ammonia (NH 3 ). Easily deployable mitigation strategies, such as manure storage additives, can help reduce the environmental impact of dairy production. Sulfur‐based manure storage additives, specifically gypsum (CaSO 4 ), have been proposed as low‐cost manure amendments that may influence CH 4 emissions; however, their potential to mitigate NH 3 emissions and their effectiveness across sulfur dosages remain unclear. title: Prospecting for efflux pump and repressor genes in rivers of the Amazon region of Brazil
abstract: BACKGROUND: The spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria in water bodies poses a significant public health concern. Efflux pumps represent critical mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, regulated by genetic repressors that aid bacterial adaptation to environmental stress. This study profiles the diversity of efflux pump genes and genetic repressors in the surface waters of the Cereja (Bragança) and Uraim (Paragominas) rivers in the Amazon region of Brazil. title: Vaccinia virus growth factor induces divergent signaling programs and biological outcomes from cellular epidermal growth factor
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling is a major pathway that controls cellular growth, survival, proliferation, and differentiation. Viruses often hijack this pathway to create a favorable environment to support their replication. Vaccinia virus (the prototype member of poxviridae) encodes its own viral growth factor (VGF). VGF is a secreted viral polypeptide with sequence and structural homology to the cellular EGF, which binds to and activates EGFR signaling. title: From Monomer to Mesh: The Biochemical Maturation of Gel-Forming Mucin Glycoproteins
abstract: Abstract Secreted mucin glycoproteins, which form the scaffolds of the mucus hydrogels coating tissue epithelia, are among the most complex molecules in nature. Mucin protein backbones are typically more than 5000 amino acids in length, become stapled into domain folds by over 100 disulfide bonds, and contain thousands of potential sites for O-glycosylation. title: Revealing the Values of Eco-theological Islamic Education in the Blora Manganan Tradition through the Perspective of Scientia Sacra Nasr
abstract: The global environmental crisis stems from the modern desacralization of nature. This study explores the Manganan tradition in Blora, Indonesia, as a living system of Eco-theological Islamic Education through Seyyed Hossein Nasr’s Scientia Sacra. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, this study collected data through participant observation, semi-structured interviews with six informants, and documentation in Panolan Village, Blora, in July 2025. title: Mitigating Weld Defects in AISI 4145 Medium-Carbon Steel During Shielded Metal Arc Welding
abstract: Welding defects pose significant challenges to product quality and productivity in manufacturing industries. Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) is the most widely used welding method in developing countries such as Ethiopia. This thesis identifies and addresses the root causes of welding defects in SMAW of medium carbon steel (AISI 4145) at Akaki Basic Metal Industry (ABMI), and optimizes welding parameters to enhance weld quality and reduce defect rates. title: Charting the Course: Practical Steps for Philippine HEIs to Embark on Internationalization
abstract: In response to a global imperative and local legislative mandates like the Transnational Higher Education Act (RA 11448), this paper provides a practical seven-step roadmap for Philippine Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) to systematically initiate and strengthen their internationalization efforts. By integrating UNESCO’s regional student mobility data with a case study of Panpacific University and comparative insights from University of Santo Tomas (UST) and Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU), this study proposes a Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) -based framework of seven strategic actions th

title: Regulatory aspects of risks posed by veterinary medicinal products to European necrophagous birds: A case study with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used in human and veterinary medicine to treat pain and inflammatory diseases. However, the uncontrolled treatment of free-roaming and sheltered livestock with NSAIDs, mainly diclofenac, has caused catastrophic impacts on the biodiversity of necrophagous birds. For instance, a decline of up to 95 % in populations of various species of vultures occurred in South Asia from the late 1990 s to the early 2000 s. title: Occurrence and distribution of plant-parasitic nematodes in flooded rice-producing regions of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Rice ( Oryza sativa L.) is a crop of great economic and social importance for many countries around the world. Brazil is among the countries with the highest rice production in the world, and the state of Rio Grande do Sul accounts for more than 70% of national production. However, biotic threats, including plant-parasitic nematodes, may limit rice production across the state’s producing regions. title: The Use of Space in Neanderthal Campsites: Evidence from Spatial and Taphonomic Analyses of Charcoal Remains from Level Ra of Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstract: Abstract This work aims to investigate the formation processes of the charcoal assemblage from level Ra at Abric Romaní, a well-preserved Middle Palaeolithic rock shelter in north-eastern Spain that was occupied by Neanderthals. To this end, we adopted an anthracological approach that combines both taxonomic and taphonomic observations. title: Ecology and conservation of subterranean biodiversity of Greater Lisbon, Portugal
abstract: Abstract Subterranean ecosystems harbour fauna moulded by extreme and stable conditions such as absence of light, narrow temperature ranges, high humidity and low availability of organic matter. The adaptations of cave fauna, coupled with the isolation of populations, often lead to a higher incidence of endemics and greater vulnerability to environmental changes. These ecosystems face severe threats caused by pollution and overexploitation, habitat loss and climate change, particularly evident in areas of increased human pressure as capitals of countries. title: DIGITAL HEALTH ADOPTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH BETTER HEALTHCARE PERFORMANCE BUT PERSISTENT INEQUITY IN BANGLADESH: A NATIONWIDE CONVERGENT MIXED-METHODS STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELLING STUDY
abstract: Background: Bangladesh is scaling digital health under its Digital Health Strategy 2023–2027, yet empirical evidence on how adoption relates to health-system performance and equity is fragmented. We examined how governance, change management and implementation barriers shape digitalization adoption, and how adoption relates to performance, patient-reported outcomes and perceived health inequality. title: A DPSIR-based scoping review of land degradation in Borana Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: This study examines land degradation in Ethiopia’s Borana Zone using the Drivers–Pressure–State–Impact–Response (DPSIR) framework. Land degradation poses a growing threat to pastoral livelihoods and ecosystem stability in arid and semi-arid regions. The study aims to synthesize existing evidence on the causes, state, impacts, and responses related to land degradation in the area. A scoping review approach was employed following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature was retrieved from Google Scholar and Web of Science. title: One-Step Growth Curve Analysis of a Bacteriophage Infecting Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Background: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic gram-negative bacterium associated with the contamination of edible bird’s nest (EBN) production systems. Pseudomonas aeruginosa may infect swiftlets and produce pigments that cause greenish staining of EBN, thereby decreasing the product's quality and market value. Bacteriophages are promising biocontrol agents owing to their host specificity and environmental safety. journal: Journal of Applied Veterinary Science And Technology

title: The Trichoptera of Panama XXX. Trichoptera of the Piedra Jabón Geosite with description of a new species
abstract: Herein we report on preliminary data for the Trichoptera assemblage for the Piedra Jabón Geosite, a proposed UNESCO defined geological site located in Coclé Province, near Penonomé. Seven streams were sampled during 2022–2023. A total of 81 species were identified distributed among 12 caddisfly families. title: Hydrogeochemical controls and human health risk assessment of trace metals in groundwater from volcanic aquifers in Kikatiti Ward, northern Tanzania
abstract: Groundwater hydrochemistry, seasonal variations, and human health risks associated with trace metals ( Pb , Hg , and As ) were evaluated across the volcanic aquifer system of Kikatiti Ward, northern Tanzania. Hydrochemical conditions were strongly influenced by seasonal hydrological shifts, silicate weathering, and volcanic geology. title: Listado de fauna silvestre en categoría de riesgo de conservación en Isla del Carmen y Laguna de Términos, Campeche, México
abstract: Los listados documentales de fauna en riesgo pueden sobreestimar el número de taxones cuando los registros de ocurrencia a nivel de especie se cruzan directamente con categorías normativas asignadas a subespecies. title: Rapid Composting Behavior and Properties of Sustainable PLA /Thermoplastic Corn Starch Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Plastic food packaging extends shelf life but causes environmental pollution. Biopolymers such as poly(lactic acid) (PLA) are gaining interest as sustainable alternatives. However, PLA has limitations including slow biodegradation rate, brittleness, and high production cost. This study aims to address these issues by incorporating thermoplastic starch (TPS), a low‐cost, biodegradable biomass based on corn starch, into PLA to develop fast‐compostable biocomposites. title: Participatory Mapping of Village Potential to Support Local Development Planning in Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This community service program identified, classified, documented, and mapped the development potential of Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Southeast Sulawesi, between 1 May and 1 June 2026. We combined a participatory approach with descriptive analysis, treating the village government and residents as partners who checked and corrected our findings rather than as mere respondents. abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. abstract: An in silico investigation was performed to study the interactions between the commonly encountered resin monomers and the major salivary proteins. title: Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments
abstract: While organic amendments are promoted for enhancing soil quality, their impacts on the net global warming potential (GWP) and the underlying microbial mechanisms in the maize system remain elusive. By using a long-term field experiment established in 2007 under a winter wheat-summer maize rotation system, a field study was conducted to investigate the effects of different organic-amended treatments (manure application and straw return coupled with conventional or no tillage) on greenhouse gas (i.e., nitrous oxide [N 2 O] and carbon dioxide [CO 2 ]) emissions, soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks a

title: Visitors’ perceptions and demand preferences for cultural ecosystem services in urban parks for sustainable tourism management
abstract: Abstract Urban parks serve as vital public spaces for recreational activities. However, key scientific questions remain regarding how, and to what extent, socio-demographic characteristics influence visitors’ perceptions of different types of cultural ecosystem services (CESs). Two further questions concern how park visitor typologies and their characteristics can be systematically identified, and how the demand preferences of different visitor groups for CESs can be understood. title: Efficacy of raccoon removal in urban and rural sites in northern Illinois
abstract: Abstract Raccoons ( Procyon lotor ) are opportunistic and highly adaptable mesopredators that may negatively impact avian and reptilian species. Although wildlife professionals often utilize predator control techniques to manage raccoons, information to guide management activities is lacking. We analyzed the efficacy of raccoon removal within urban and rural sites in northern Illinois, USA, during 2022–2024. abstract: Abstract The brain is one of the most complex animal organs and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II . This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals while it has been lost from vertebrates. title: Hierarchically Wrinkled Silver Ink as a Platform for Fully Integrated Stretchable Electronic Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of high‐performance stretchable electronics continues to be limited by the fundamental trade‐off between electrical conductivity, mechanical resilience, and cost‐effective manufacturability. This work introduces a Silver Hierarchical Responsive ink (SHRink), a universal approach for the fabrication of highly stretchable interconnects, wirings, and skin‐interfaced electrodes. title: Comparative Analysis of Aerobic Bacteria, Green Microalgae, and Diatoms in Domestic Wastewater Treatment: Pollutant Removal, Lipid Profile, and Biodiesel Properties
abstract: Microalgal systems are receiving significant attention for wastewater treatment because of their effective treatment performance while simultaneously generating valuable biomass for energy recovery. This study compares the performance of three biological systems - green microalgae, diatoms, and aerobic bacteria for the treatment of real domestic wastewater. Each system was operated in semi-continuous mode at different solid retention times (SRTs) of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 days. title: Additive genetic effects of two large effect loci shaping age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Fitness-related traits are shaped by both additive and non-additive genetic effects, resulting in a complex and context-dependent genetic architecture. However, the relative contribution of these components remains poorly understood, particularly for major-effect loci underlying life-history traits. In this study, we investigated the additive genetic contributions and potential epistatic interactions between 2 unlinked major-effect loci, vgll3 and six6, that influence age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). title: Farmer and advisor perspectives on soil amendments: motivators, barriers, and insights for scaling
abstract: Soil amendments such as gypsum, structure lime, and pulp and paper mill sludge have multiple localised agronomic and broader environmental benefits, but their uptake by farmers remains limited. This exploratory mixed-methods study examined farmers’ and advisors’ perceptions of factors influencing soil amendment adoption through interviews with 11 farmers and 5 agricultural advisors in Southwest Finland, complemented by a nationwide survey of 20 advisors, which provided supplementary perspectives on advisor perceptions. title: Assessment of possible interactions between Citrus aurantifolia leaf alkaloid-rich compounds and relevant protein targets in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats
abstract: Aim: This study assessed the neuroprotective effect of lime (Citrus aurantifolia) leaf via the interaction of its inherent alkaloid compounds with specific neuronal protein targets [acetylcholinesterase (AChE), adenosine deaminase (ADA), and monoamine oxidase (MAO)] in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats. title: Integration of Landscape Aesthetics and Sustainable Business Models in Kaliaren Village Land Utilization
abstract: This research aims to identify and optimize land use in Kaliaren Village through the integration of landscape aesthetic aspects and the development of sustainable business models. Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach, this study maps the existing conditions of land use, analyzes aesthetic and economic potential, and explores the perception of the community and stakeholders through observation, in-depth interviews, Focus Group Discussions, and spatial analysis. title: Novelties in Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae) from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Revisiting the Dimerostemma collection in Rio Grande do Sul, the southernmost state of Brazil, one new species of Dimerostemma is described and another is resurrected. Although previously synonymized under Dimerostemma arnottii , Dimerostemma oppositifolium is here resurrected based on its distinct opposite leaves, linear to lanceolate leaf limbs, and specific pappus scale measurements. Additionally, Dimerostemma ramboi is described as a new species endemic to the state of Rio Grande do Sul. title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator ( Alligator mississippiensis ) based on fluctuating thermal regimes
abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determines sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. title: Phase engineering of Mo x C regulates electronic structure and interfacial hydrogen-bond networks over Ru sites for pH-universal hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Metallic ruthenium (Ru) represents a promising Pt alternative for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, achieving efficient HER, particularly under pH-universal conditions, remains challenging due to sluggish interfacial water dissociation kinetics. Herein, we report a phase engineering strategy that utilizes well-defined cubic and hexagonal molybdenum carbide (α–MoC/β–Mo2C) supports to regulate Ru–MoxC metal–support interactions and interfacial microenvironments. title: Computational prioritization of fungal-derived H1 receptor ligand candidates for allergy-related research
abstract: Activation of the G-protein-coupled histamine H1 receptor (H1R) contributes to allergic responses such as bronchoconstriction, vasodilation, and pruritus. This study aimed to computationally prioritize novel fungal-derived compounds for H1R-targeted investigation based on predicted binding characteristics, pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles, and BBB permeability. abstract: ABSTRACT Lightweight structural materials capable of simultaneously sustaining mechanical load‐bearing and dissipating extreme impact energy remain a long‐standing challenge, as conventional systems are constrained by the intrinsic trade‐off between stiffness and toughness under dynamic loading. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a strain rate triggered network locking strategy that enables adaptive mechanical reconfiguration in poplar fibres (PFs) and shear stiffening gel (SSG) composites (PSCs). title: Pace-dependent reorganisation of shoulder-hip coordination in front crawl swimming
abstract: Shoulder and hip roll are distinct but coordinated components of body roll during front crawl swimming, yet shoulder-hip coordination has largely been examined using discrete measures. This study applied continuous relative phase (CRP), Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM), and complementary coupling analyses to a previously published kinematic dataset, to examine shoulder-hip coordination during sprint and 400 m pace front crawl. title: Quantification of influencing parameters on plug-holing and smoke extraction efficiency for multi-point lateral vents in tunnel fires
abstract: In tunnel smoke extraction systems, the multi-point lateral vent configuration is critical for fire emergencies. However, variations in the fire heat release rate and the vent layout often cause non-uniform plug-holing at individual vents, which reduces the smoke extraction efficiency. To address this challenge, a theoretical method was developed to identify and quantify plug-holing. title: Integrating ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 Management Systems with Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction in Niger Delta Oil Operations
abstract: Oil operations in the Niger Delta sit inside the same floodplains, creeks and villages that host millions of residents. Hazards such as spills, fires, floods and pipeline failures rarely stop at the fence line, yet the management systems that govern them usually do. This paper argues that ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) and ISO 14001 (environment), both built on the same high-level structure, can be deliberately extended to include community-based disaster risk reduction (CBDRR). title: Estimating the causal effect of extreme flooding on urban property markets: A case study of Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: The May 2024 floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil, triggered a pronounced spatial repricing of climate risk in the city’s housing market. Using a Bayesian structural time-series framework, we estimate an average causal impact of a 4.7% increase in sale prices and a 9.1% increase in rental price indices, driven primarily by price appreciation in elevated, flood-resilient neighborhoods. Our econometric approach accounts for nonlinear trends and macroeconomic controls, isolating the causal effect of the disaster. title: Andrographolide Combined With Voriconazole Enhances Antifungal Activity Against Aspergillus Species
abstract: Azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus is increasing globally, necessitating novel combination strategies to restore the efficacy of first-line antifungals such as voriconazole (VCZ). Andrographolide (ADR), a natural diterpene lactone, has shown limited direct antifungal activity but exhibits synergistic effects with amphotericin B and immunomodulatory properties. abstract: Abstract The habitual and controlled use of fire among Neanderthal groups, together with the residential use of caves and rock shelters, represents a major turning point in the emergence of Paleolithic camp bases. In Middle Paleolithic sites, the interrelation between shelter geomorphology, fire-use locations and activity areas has been interpreted as evidence of spatial organization. title: Policy Strategy To Reduce Unemployment In Bengkulu Province
abstract: This study examines the structural challenges of unemployment and labour-market development in Bengkulu Province. Despite an open unemployment rate (TPT) of 3.20% in May 2026, the province recorded 37,242 unemployed people, while 65.45% of employed people worked in the informal sector. title: Antibiofilm Activity of Zinc Sulfate Against Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from Clinical and Retail Meat Sources in Baghdad, Iraq
abstract: Biofilm formation was investigated among 60 Staphylococcus aureus isolates obtained from both retail meat and clinical samples in Baghdad, Iraq. These isolates were divided into 75% (45/60) clinical isolates and 25% (15/60) meat-derived isolates. Biofilm formation among all isolates was evaluated using the microtiter plate assay, while the presence of the biofilm-associated genes icaA, icaB, icaC, and icaD was determined by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). title: SPATIAL VARIATION OF TUBERCULOSIS OCCURRENCES IN ILORIN, KWARA STATE NIGERIA
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is one of the deadliest infectious diseases globally. It was responsible for 1.6 million deaths in 2019 and the leading cause of mortality from a single infectious agent, especially in developing countries. In Africa, the incidence of TB was estimated to be rising, with 1500 deaths daily. Despite current global efforts to reduce TB, Nigeria’s TB prevalence is increasing in many communities. abstract: Organophosphorus flame retardants (OPFRs) are chemical additives used to prevent combustion and slow down the speed of flame propagation. We evaluated levels of urinary OPFRs metabolites, serum sex hormones, and semen quality among men in southern Taiwan. OPFR exposure was assessed by quantifying the concentrations of five OPFR diesters in urine samples. title: Decoupling Sustainability Reporting and Social Media Communication After a Sustainability Scandal: Strategic Silence, Selective Disclosure and Legitimacy Stabilisation
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how corporate sustainability disclosure evolves across a legitimacy‐threatening event by analysing the interaction between formal sustainability reporting and social media communication. Using a qualitative, longitudinal, event‐centred single‐case design, the study investigates a major Italian organic meat producer over the 2021–2024 period through formal sustainability reporting, Facebook content and stakeholder interactions, regulatory and contextual documents and selected economic indicators. title: Food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children and parents in southern Peru: A cross-sectional study using projective techniques
abstract: Peru's school feeding program applies largely uniform menus across regions with very different food cultures, yet little is known about how children and parents in these regions represent food. This cross-sectional study compared food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children (10-12 years) and their parents in five cities of southern Peru (Arequipa, Cusco, Moquegua, Puno and Tacna). title: Berberine-functionalized biogenic silver nanoparticles inhibit quorum-regulated curli mediated biofilms in emerging MDR uropathogenic Enterobacter hormaechei
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant Enterobacter hormaechei is being increasingly reported in urinary tract infections (UTIs), where its ability to form quorum-regulated, curli-rich biofilms contributes to antibiotic tolerance and persistence. Targeting both quorum sensing (QS) and amyloid-mediated biofilm stability may provide an alternative strategy to conventional antibiotics. title: Tail movements and prey displacement: A new observation in Erythrolamprus miliaris (Serpentes: Dipsadidae) and a potentially overlooked pattern in xenodontine snakes
abstract: Tail movements associated with prey capture have been reported in snakes under a variety of functional contexts, including caudal luring, caudal distraction, and prey flushing. Herein, we describe an unusual predatory interaction between the semi-aquatic snake Erythrolamprus miliaris and a toad of the genus Rhinella under controlled laboratory conditions. title: Evolution of aroma-active compounds and precursor-aroma relationships in spiced brine-stewed pork intestine during stewing
abstract: Pork intestines are widely appreciated for their distinctive flavor and texture, yet their dynamic development during spiced brine stewing remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated GC-MS, GC-IMS, GC-O-MS, and eOAV analyses highlighted six major aroma-active compounds, with ethyl maltol and eugenol showing high potential aroma relevance. abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the public health problems that requires serious attention because it can increase morbidity and mortality rates. The spread of tuberculosis cases is influenced by various patient characteristics such as gender, age, area of residence, treatment status, and occupation. This study aims to determine the distribution of tuberculosis cases based on patient characteristics in the working area of the Simeulue District Health Office in 2026. abstract: Drug-resistant bacterial infections seriously threaten public health, and the formation of a biofilm barrier plays an important role. Drug-resistant biofilms are difficult to remove because the penetration and specificity of traditional antimicrobial drugs are poor, and the microenvironment in the inner layer of biofilms is hypoxic. Herein, we developed activatable aptamer-functionalized pro-photosensitizers (APMB) by modifying the clinical photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) with an aptamer that can specifically bind to drug-resistant bacteria. abstract: This study determines the components of a groundwater flow system associated with Lakes Pátzcuaro and Cuitzeo. The objectives are: a) to delineate flow trajectories and b) to identify the pathways that contribute to lake recharge. The methodology included water sampling, hydrogeochemical, isotopic, and statistical analysis of groundwater and surface water. title: Análisis y diseño para la administración de un sistema computarizado de una empresa automotriz
abstract: La gestión de la capacitación articulada con las competencias laborales es un requisito normativo en la industria automotriz, establecido por las normas IATF 16949:2016 e ISO 9001:2015; sin embargo, en muchas organizaciones estos procesos todavía se administran con formatos físicos y hojas de cálculo. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los procesos de gestión del capital humano de una empresa automotriz de la Comarca Lagunera, con aproximadamente 800 colaboradores, y diseñar un sistema computarizado para administrarlos. title: Decoupling environmental suitability from realized recruitment through ontogenetic environmental filtering in a long‐lived Mediterranean palm species
abstract: Abstract Long-lived plants facing anthropogenic disturbance often exhibit recruitment failure despite persistent reproductive adults, generating extinction debt masked by longevity. However, whether adult presence reliably reflects environmental suitability for recruitment remains unclear. Here, we examine ontogenetic niche differentiation and its consequences for recruitment in Jubaea chilensis , an endangered long-lived Mediterranean palm with an aging population. title: Paving over the source: Land use change and the everyday struggle for water in Mbale town, Kenya (2014-2025)
abstract: Secondary cities are where Africa’s urban future is being decided, yet they remain academically invisible. While Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu are extensively studied, towns like Mbale-Vihiga County’s administrative capital absorb over 60% of Kenya’s urban growth with no commensurate infrastructure. This study seeks to find out what happens when a town urbanizes over its own catchment. title: Spatial modeling for the protection of waterways in the Quinsaloma canton, Los Ríos, Ecuador
abstract: This research aims to spatially model the protection of watercourses in Quinsaloma canton (Los Ríos, Ecuador), for the integrated management of water resources. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining quantitative and qualitative techniques, including surveys of 90 residents and interviews with community leaders. title: Regulating soil pore structure and water infiltration in saline-alkali soil: The dominant role of cotton biochar particle size
abstract: Biochar, due to its porous structure and particle size characteristics, can affect soil porosity and thereby improve the drainage function of saline-alkali soil. This study aims to quantitatively evaluate the influence of biochar particle size on the pore characteristics of saline-alkali soil. title: Ion and particle size distribution measurements in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: seasonal insights and challenges in new particle formation event characterization
abstract: Abstract. New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of atmospheric aerosols and cloud condensation nuclei, influencing climate and air quality. title: Segmented lithospheric architecture beneath the Middle—Lower Yangtze River metallogenic belt constraints by magnetotelluric array data
abstract: The Middle—Lower Yangtze River Metallogenic Belt (MLYMB) is a major Fe-Cu-Au-Mo polymetallic belt in eastern China. However, the deep geodynamic processes responsible for the contrasting metallogenesis characteristics of its individual ore districts remain under debated. We constructed a three-dimensional (3-D) lithospheric-scale resistivity model using magnetotelluric (MT) data from 160 stations. abstract: Abstract The ubiquitin-proteasome system, which serves as one of the most common cellular degradation pathways, plays a critical role in maintaining proteostasis. Yet, the correlation between the ubiquitin-proteasome system and antiviral defense remains to be defined. In this work, pharmacological inhibition of proteasomes via treatment with MG132, which inhibited proteasome activity during viral infection, facilitated antiviral effects in vitro. abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorption of proteins and other biomolecules on stainless steel and other functional metallic surfaces is a key interfacial phenomenon in food processing environments, leading to progressive surface accumulation of organic residues. abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. abstract: Interactions between microorganisms and their mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including viruses and plasmids, impact microbiome dynamics. CRISPR-Cas systems are important regulators of these host-MGE interactions, but a global understanding of the diversity, activity and roles of CRISPR spacers across Earth's biomes is still lacking. title: Hollowing Out Nanofibers for Enhanced Visual Brightness and More Effective Solar Heating
abstract: The temperature rise of a solar-heating textile is controlled by both generation and dissipation of heat. However, current designs mainly focus on increasing light absorption to generate more heat, often darkening the material while leaving thermal management largely overlooked. Herein, hollowing the nanofibers in a nonwoven mat produces a counterintuitive "brighter-yet-hotter" advantage over their solid (core-shell) counterparts. The polyacrylonitrile/polypyrrole double-shelled tubular nanofibers are fabricated by selectively removing the poly(ε-caprolactone) core from core-shell nanofibers.
institutions: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

abstract: ABSTRACT The formation of peptide 2D crystals with well‐organized molecular arrays by primary nucleation mechanism have provided an efficient way to incorporate biofunctions into the underlying single layer graphene and MoS 2 , leading to broad applications for biosensing, biomedicine and bioelectronics. Further realizing a high‐level architecture of peptide 3D crystals coupling with the underlying nanomaterials would expand its applications for the next‐generation bionanodevices, while facing a big challenge. title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
abstract: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae , and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. title: Integrated geochemical and spatial analysis of trace element redistribution in salinized arid agro-landscapes: Evidence from the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan)
abstract: Arid agro-landscapes are highly vulnerable to the soil degradation caused by long-term irrigation and climatic constraints.This study investigated the spatial patterns and geochemical characteristics associated with trace element redistribution in salinized irrigated soils of the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan).A geochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling units from representative sampling sites was analyzed for trace element composition using energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (EDXRF).A separate physicochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling un

title: Spatiotemporal NDVI Analysis of Kipengere Forest Reserve Dynamics in Tanzania: Evidence from 1995 to 2026
abstract: Forest ecosystems are of great importance for biodiversity conservation and water resource regulation but are increasingly subject to environmental and land-use changes. The study analysed the spatiotemporal dynamics of vegetation condition in the Kipengere Forest Reserve, Southwest Tanzania from 1995 to 2026 using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) generated from Landsat satellite images. journal: American Journal of Environment and Climate

title: Remote sensing-based analysis of land use in spring protection zones in Southern Brazil
abstract: Springs are important ecosystems that help maintain water quality and quantity and are legally protected in Brazil as Permanent Preservation Areas (PPAs). They play a key role in aquatic ecosystems and help maintain biodiversity. The study aimed to characterize land cover in PPAs surrounding springs in the micro-watersheds of Jacarezinho, Paraná, Brazil. We mapped the springs of four micro-basins in the municipality and assessed vegetation cover in their PPAs using MapBiomas remote sensing data and geoprocessing tools. The results showed that agricultural areas predominate, with only 5.9% of s
journal: Journal of Environmental Analysis and Progress
institutions: Universidade Estadual do Norte do Paraná

title: Shallow Cumulus Cloud Statistics in Real‐Case Large‐Eddy Simulations and Their Dependence on Soil Moisture
abstract: Abstract The ability of weather and climate models to reproduce the statistical properties of shallow cumulus clouds (SCCs) is critical for representing boundary‐layer transport, cloud cover, and cloud‐radiative effects. This study investigates statistical properties of SCC ensembles using the Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic model in large‐eddy simulation mode for three cases during the Field Experiment on Submesoscale Spatio‐Temporal Variability in Lindenberg campaign. journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems

title: Biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality show contrasting recovery patterns across tropical forests with different logging histories
abstract: Globally, a growing proportion of logging‐disturbed tropical forest is recovering, holding great potential for biodiversity conservation and ecosystem functioning. However, how ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) and its trait‐based predictors in these secondary forests differ from those in old‐growth forests remains unknown. title: Liquid crystalline nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of gentamicin and rhDNase against mature Escherichia coli biofilms
abstract: Biofilm-associated infections remain a major clinical challenge due to restricted antibiotic penetration, matrix-mediated antimicrobial tolerance, and rapid degradation of biofilm-disruptive therapeutics in protease-rich environments. Here, liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) were developed as a nanostructured co-delivery platform for gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), integrating antibiotic delivery with enzymatic disruption of the biofilm extracellular matrix. title: Retrospective evaluation of repeated dose dermal toxicity studies in North American agrochemical risk assessment
abstract: Current North American pesticide regulations mandate route-specific repeated-dose dermal toxicity (RDDT) studies for dermal exposure risk assessment. To evaluate the scientific necessity of this study requirement, a proof-of-concept retrospective analysis was conducted on conventional active pesticide ingredients with Syngenta end use product registered in North America (NA) from 2001 to 2025, examining publicly available risk assessments for 51 pesticides assessed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) and 43 by the Health Canada Pesticides Regulatory Directorate (PRD).

title: Coordination‐Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n‐type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. title: Interfacial Co–Ni Dual‐Site Synergy in Confined Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 Heterostructures for Electrocatalytic Water Splitting
abstract: Although heazlewoodite‐type nickel sulfide (Ni 3 S 2 ) exhibits promising hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, its application in overall water splitting remains limited by sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics associated with insufficient water activation. Herein, Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen‐rich spongy carbons are constructed to regulate interfacial electronic properties and unlock Co–Ni catalytic synergy for efficient water electrolysis. title: A Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assembly and Demographic History Inference of Ostrya rehderiana
abstract: Ostrya rehderiana is a critically endangered plant species with an extremely small population size. However, the absence of high-quality genome assembly has impeded the understanding of the causes and genetic consequences of its endangered status, especially how theses genetic consequences result in the failure of its population regeneration. In this study, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long-read sequencing, Hi-C, Illumina resequencing, and RNA-seq data to generate a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and annotation for this species. title: Las tecnologías educativas para enseñar geografía e historia
abstract: Este artículo analiza el uso de tecnologías educativas en la enseñanza de geografía e historia mediante una revisión bibliográfica narrativa crítica de siete publicaciones de 2021–2026. Se realizaron búsquedas dirigidas y se contrastaron datos bibliográficos en revistas, registros académicos y organismos oficiales. La selección comprendió revisiones, investigaciones sobre enseñanza y un informe institucional. title: Two Ume6 target gene classes in the biofilm regulatory network of Candida albicans
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofilm formation by the fungal pathogen Candida albicans is a major source of infection. The biofilm regulator Ume6 forms complexes with partner transcription factors Efg1, Ndt80, and Upc2 to drive expression of biofilm-related genes. Here we present chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing (ChIP-seq) data for Ume6-chromatin association in both wild-type and efg1 Δ/Δ ndt80 Δ/Δ upc2 Δ/Δ backgrounds. title: Monospecific cover crops perpetuate soil biotic homogenization in croplands across diverse soils
abstract: Abstract Croplands are known to support significant soil biotic homogenization. Cover crops are commonly used as a sustainable agriculture practice; however, many times these cover crops are composed of single‐species. Unfortunately, the influence of monospecific cover crops on soil biotic homogenization remains virtually unknown. Here, we performed a common garden experiment including soils from 27 agricultural fields across mainland China and two major cover crops grown separately in monoculture: a legume ( Vicia villosa Roth) and a gramineae ( Lolium multiflorum Lam.). title: Integrated fertilizer management and agrometeorological conditions associated with yield and nutritional quality of Boro rice
abstract: Increasing rice production while improving grain nutritional quality is essential for global food security. We hypothesized that integrated fertilizer management combined with a suitable rice variety would enhance grain yield, nutrient uptake, and nutritional quality compared to conventional fertilizer management, while agrometeorological conditions would help explain variations in crop performance. title: Effects of heatwaves and larval host plant on overwinter performance of a generalist herbivore
abstract: Abstract Heatwaves are increasing in frequency and severity due to anthropogenic climate change and may play a role in recent insect declines. Heatwaves can occur during any season, and how insects are affected by heatwaves may depend on an insect's phenology and life stage when the heatwave occurs. Most research investigates summer heatwaves; however, winter heatwaves may have greater negative impacts on insects than summer heatwaves, but further investigation is necessary. title: Characterization and multi-response optimization of epoxy–castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell and marsh barbel powders
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable polymer composites has led to the use of agricultural waste and natural materials as alternative reinforcements. The present work deals with the characterization and multi response optimization of epoxy castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell powder (CSP) and marsh barbel powder (MBP). Hand lay-up casting technique was used to prepare six formulations with different loadings of natural powder and with 20 wt% castor oil, cured at room temperature. title: Does telehealth narrow the urban-rural gap? A dual assessment of in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility
abstract: Telehealth has been proposed to reduce rural prenatal care barriers, but its equity effects depend on whether predicted accessibility translates into observed utilization. We examine whether predicted and revealed in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility diverge across the urban-rural continuum of South Carolina and whether these measures align with ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA)-level birth-related need, measured as average annual live births by residence. title: Estimation of Dietary Microplastic Ingestion: Empirical Analysis for Delhi-NCR
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly detected in food products and may contribute to human exposure through daily dietary consumption. However, information on dietary MP exposure in Delhi-NCR, India, remains limited. This study aimed to investigate MP contamination in commonly consumed food items and assess their potential contribution to dietary exposure among residents of Delhi-NCR. An online survey involving 175 participants was conducted to determine the consumption frequency of eight food items: potato, egg, apple, potato chips, whole wheat flour, instant noodles, honey, and chicken. journal: Journal of Food and Nutrition Sciences

title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
abstract: Abstract Modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago. However, limited genomic data from individuals dating between 45,000 and 20,000 years ago still restricts our understanding of population dynamics and admixture during the Upper Palaeolithic. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM, 26.5–19 cal kya), Gravettian culture-associated populations were widespread and genetically diverse, comprising at least two distinct genetic groups, referred to as the Fournol and Věstonice clusters. title: Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Anti‐Melanogenic Activity of a Novel Pectic Polysaccharide From Alhagi camelorum Fisch
abstract: Hyperpigmentation disorders motivate the search for structurally defined and effective natural depigmenting agents from plant-derived polysaccharides. The present study characterized the structural features and evaluated the anti-melanogenic activity of ACP-II-1, a novel pectic polysaccharide isolated from Alhagi camelorum Fisch. ACP-II-1 had a molecular weight of 26.145 kDa and contained GalA, Rha, Gal, Ara, GlcA, and Xyl at respective molar proportions of 0.798, 0.072, 0.053, 0.052, 0.016, and 0.009. University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Surface Subsidence as an Effective Indicator of Methane Emissions From Underground Coal Mines
abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from underground coal mining remain a major and uncertain anthropogenic source. This study tests whether surface subsidence, a direct consequence of underground mining, can serve as an indicator of CH 4 emissions. We use the Changzhi coal belt in Shanxi of China, a major emission hotspot, as a case study. Time‐series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar analysis of Sentinel‐1 SAR data (November 2019 to October 2024) revealed persistent subsidence across the region. title: Discovery and Structure Elucidation of a New Polyketide‐Derived Tetrahydropyran‐Containing Conjugated Fatty Acid Derivative Isolated From Typhonium blumei
abstract: ABSTRACT A chemical investigation of the 95% EtOH extract of Typhonium blumei led to the isolation of a new polyketide‐derived tetrahydropyran‐containing conjugated fatty acid derivative ( 1 ), together with four known compounds ( 2 – 5 ). The structure of compound 1 was elucidated through comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including 1D and 2D NMR spectra ( 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, DEPT, HSQC, HMBC, COSY, and NOESY), as well as HR‐ESI‐MS data. title: A Tension‐Controlled Arthroscopic Technique for Fixation of a Glenolabral Articular Disruption Lesion in an Overhead Athlete
abstract: Glenolabral articular disruption lesions are rare post-traumatic injuries that occur after shoulder instability events particularly in young, high-demand athletes. Managing these injuries can be challenging especially in overhead athletes who require a degree of physiologic laxity to preserve throwing mechanics. Although various treatment methods have previously been described, literature addressing these injuries in overhead throwers remains limited. title: A Comprehensive Review on Furcellaran‐Based Food Packaging: Applications, Developments and Horizons
abstract: ABSTRACT Growing concerns regarding the uncontrolled proliferation of plastic materials, which pose significant environmental challenges, have prompted researchers to seek innovative, eco‐friendly alternatives to conventional petroleum‐based packaging. Among various biological sources, seaweed has emerged as a very promising candidate. These seaweeds are rich in polysaccharides that can act as biopolymers in sustainable food packaging formulations. title: Formulation of Lutjanus johnii (Snapper) fishballs with concentrated syrup and Levisticum officinale (lovage) extract: Assessing integrated antioxidants for enhanced fishery products
abstract: Fishballs, ready-to-eat products with high nutritional value, can utilize lower-value fish species more efficiently. However, rapid spoilage from lipid oxidation and microbial growth is a major challenge. In this study, fishballs were prepared with varying lovage extract concentrations (T1: 0%, T2: 0.25%, T3: 0.5%, T4: 0.75%, T5: 1%) and 5% concentrated syrup, frozen at −38°C and stored at −18°C, with evaluations on days 1, 15, 30, and 45. title: Responses of functional trait networks and hub traits of submerged macrophytes to water depth variation in an impounded lake of the South‑to‑North Water Transfer Project, China
abstract: Trait network analysis have been widely used to unravel the effects of variable environments on submerged macrophytes communities. However, few studies focused on the response of submerged macrophytes to variable water depths in impounded lakes from a whole plant trait network perspective. Here, we carried out a field study aimed to evaluate variation of functional traits, detect hub traits and clarify trait network topologies among different water depths. title: Effects of 4R nitrogen management on corn silage production
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) is one of the critical and costliest inputs for corn silage ( Zea mays ) production. Excessive N applications decrease profits for growers via increased cost of production and raise environmental concerns. The four core principles of the 4R nutrient stewardship framework—right source (S), right rate (R), right time (T), and right place (P)—aim to optimize N management. Most previous studies evaluating N management for corn silage only examined one or a few 4R practices. title: Energy efficient data gathering in load balanced clustered wireless sensor networks with compressive sensing
abstract: Rapid energy loss from continuous sensing and data transmission often shortens network lifespan. This work suggests Bernoulli holomorphic swarm optimized Hermite polynomial compressive sensing (BHSO-HPCS), an energy-efficient data collection method, to overcome this difficulty. The suggested approach minimizes energy usage without sacrificing network performance by combining compressive sensing (CS) and load-balanced clustering algorithms. title: GSK3 Inhibition During Annelid Head Regeneration Results in a Hyper‐Proliferative Blastema and Impaired Differentiation
abstract: A major goal of regeneration biology is to uncover the molecular mechanisms that allow a wide range of animals to replace body parts through regeneration. Glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK3) is known to have significant regulatory influence on developmental pathways that are integral to successful regeneration in several animal groups. Annelids include some of the most highly regenerative animals known and, although GSK3 has been studied during regeneration in several species, its major roles remain unclear. title: Combined supplementation of L-carnitine and stevioside enhances performance, stress tolerance, immune competence, and molecular responses in Nile tilapia
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of dietary L-carnitine (500 mg/kg) and stevioside (450 mg/kg) on growth performance, physiological responses, stress tolerance, immunity, antioxidant status, and molecular regulation in Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ; initial weight 3.84 ± 0.12 g) over 90 days. Fish were fed a control diet or diets supplemented with L-carnitine, stevioside, or their combination. title: Mixture-dependent mechanical response of asphalt mixtures under saline freeze–thaw conditioning
abstract: Saline freeze–thaw exposure can alter the mechanical response of asphalt mixtures, yet these changes may depend on mixture characteristics and salt concentration. This study investigated two dense-graded asphalt mixtures, Binder and Topeka, under an accelerated saline freeze–thaw conditioning protocol. Specimens underwent eight freeze–thaw cycles in distilled water or NaCl solutions with nominal initial mass concentrations of 5% and 10%, while unconditioned Dry specimens were retained as reference groups.
