title: The complete chloroplast genome of diploid Hieracium tomentosum (Asteraceae, Cichorieae)
abstract: Hieracium is a megadiverse genus within the family Asteraceae, in the tribe Cichorieae subtribe Hieraciinae. We report here the complete chloroplast genome of the diploid Hieracium tomentosum L. The assembled plastome measures 153,218 bp in total length with one large single-copy (LSC, 84,604 bp), one small single-copy (SSC, 18,438 bp), and two inverted repeat (IR, 25,088 bp) regions. It comprehends 127 genes, including 83 protein-coding genes, 8 rRNA genes, and 36 tRNA genes. abstract: Although fiscal and monetary instruments are calibrated for economic stabilisation rather than for environmental ends, they act directly upon the volume and composition of the activity that generates environmental pressure, and the literature has largely assessed their consequences on the implicit assumption that expansions and contractions are reflection of one another. title: Chemical fingerprinting of a furniture waste landfill fire: parent and alkylated PAHs, organophosphates and environmental-health risk assessments
abstract: Abstract Fires at furniture-waste storage sites are an under-researched source of persistent organic contaminants. This study characterized 13 charred furniture-waste samples collected after a landfill fire in Tychy, Poland, using GC–MS to determine parent and alkylated PAHs and organophosphate esters (OPEs), and to perform screening-level environmental and human-health assessments. title: Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Differential Expression of Virulence Genes in Xylella fastidiosa Cultured Under Different Nutrient Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited, insect-vectored pathogen. To capture the metabolic changes that underlie its adaptation to both nutrient-rich and xylem-like environments, we performed transcriptome analyses on two reference strains, Temecula1 and 9a5c, sampled at early and late exponential phases in a complex laboratory medium (PWG) and a defined, xylem-mimicking medium (PIM6). title: A polyphenol-rich fraction from Tagetes erecta enhances mitochondrial SIRT3 activity and suppresses ROS-associated adipocyte maturation and lipid accumulation
abstract: Obesity-associated metabolic disorders are strongly associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, but therapeutic approaches targeting mitochondrial regulatory pathways remain limited. Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3), a major mitochondrial NAD + -dependent deacetylase, regulates mitochondrial metabolism and redox homeostasis and may therefore represent a promising target for metabolic disease intervention. title: Integrating tectonically guided fractured-rock groundwater exploration and community based governance for water security in Pakistan
abstract: Pakistan faces a growing water crisis driven by climate change, groundwater depletion, declining water quality, and increasing demand. We propose a hybrid framework that integrates regional structural geology with community-based water governance to improve long-term water security and climate resilience in the Indus River Basin. title: The Role of Information Technology in Revitalizing Afghanistan’s Position along the Historical and Modern Silk Road

title: Impressive cave-adapted japygids (Diplura, Japygidae) from Mediterranean and Southeast Asia caves
abstract: Three specimens of Dipluran Japygidae, collected from two widely separated caves – one in the western Mediterranean and the other in Southeast Asia – have revealed the existence of an impressive, distinctive and unusual cercal amour pattern, unlike that of other Japygidae, characterized by two to three pairs of subsymmetrically arranged teeth. title: Beyond heatwave vulnerability rankings: Sustainability dimensions and urban vulnerability profiles
abstract: Heat vulnerability indices are widely used to rank urban areas, yet they provide limited information about how heat vulnerability is embedded into urban sustainability or why similar aggregate scores may reflect different component configurations. This study examines whether different sustainability dimensions are associated with heatwave vulnerability and identifies associated urban profiles across 72 Hungarian urban units: the 23 districts of Budapest and the 49 largest cities. title: Bacterial pathogen-dependent responses to high-frequency ultrasound-based hurdle treatments
abstract: High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) is a promising non-thermal technology for food decontamination, although its antimicrobial mechanisms and interactions with natural antimicrobials remain poorly characterised. This study evaluated HFUS at 760 kHz, alone and in combination with green tea extract (GTE), against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative foodborne bacteria. title: Early Maize Growth In Rhizoboxes Under Ageratum Conyzoides Leaf Extract And Chicken Manure
abstract: Maize requires adequate nutrients during vegetative growth, and organic fertilizers can serve as an alternative nutrient source to inorganic fertilizers. Babadotan (Ageratum conyzoides L.) leaves contain nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium and may therefore be used as a aqueous leaf extract. This study evaluated the effect of babadotan leaf extract and chicken manure on the vegetative growth of maize (Zea mays L.) grown in rhizoboxes. title: Predicting tree growth using light availability as an indicator of competition
abstract: Tree growth modelling and predictions are essential components of forest planning and ecological research. Airborne laser scanning data can provide detailed information about tree crowns, where primary photosynthesis happens. The aim of this study was to investigate, whether intercepted solar radiation received by tree crowns, modelled using drone-based Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data, can be used as an indicator of competition in individual tree growth models instead of traditional competition variables such as basal area or basal area of larger trees. title: Financiamiento Popular y Solidario: Percepción y rol en el fortalecimiento emprendedor en Machala, Ecuador
abstract: El fortalecimiento del emprendimiento se ha convertido en un aspecto trascendente para el desarrollo socioeconómico en Ecuador. Este estudio se enfocó en analizar la incidencia del Sistema Financiero Popular y Solidario en la experiencia de crédito de emprendedores del cantón Machala-Ecuador. title: Formal Total Synthesis of (±)‐Carexane L Enabled by a PPA‐Mediated Fragmentation–Cyclization Cascade and Heck Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a succinct formal total synthesis of the rearranged aromatic sesquiterpene (±)‐carexane L, an indanone‐based natural product derived from the roots of Carex distachya Desf., a species indigenous to the Mediterranean maquis, commencing from benzoic acid. abstract: We report X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) analyses of 88 obsidian artifacts from the Early Horizon (aka Formative Period) site of La Puntilla in the Southern Nasca Region (SNR) of south-central Peru. title: Temporal controls on fluid–rock interaction in the evolution of the Abovyan iron oxide–apatite deposit, Armenia
abstract: Iron oxide–apatite (IOA) deposits are globally significant sources of Fe, P, and Rare Earth Elements (REEs). Although input of hydrothermal processes into their origin is acknowledged, direct temporal constraints on the duration and style of their hydrothermal evolution remain scarce. The Abovyan deposit in central Armenia, hosted by late Miocene andesites, is one of the youngest known IOA systems worldwide and the only example in the Lesser Caucasus, providing a rare opportunity to address this problem. abstract: Abstract Table beet ( Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris var. vulgaris ), also known as red beet, garden beet, or beetroot, is an important crop with both nutritional and agricultural value, yet high-quality genomic resources for this taxon are limited. abstract: Northern peatlands provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration that mitigates climate change. Warming and land use threaten many peatlands, but a unique subclass of peatlands called aapa mires are currently listed as Least Concern in Europe. abstract: In multi-robot formation control systems, trajectory planning plays a crucial role as it determines the ability of a formation to follow desired paths smoothly and accurately. This study presents a framework for Mecanum-wheeled robot teams, combining quintic-polynomial waypoint generation, a virtual-structure model, an artificial potential field for tracking and obstacle avoidance. abstract: Abstract During high rainfall events, one reason for flooding in urban rivers is hydraulic blockages or obstructions in channels. These may cause damming and an immediate increase in upstream water levels, leading to inundation of surroundings. The accuracy of flood models is strongly dependent on the representation of the topography of floodplain and river geometry, so incorporation of such blockages and obstructions in rivers' model geometry needs to be taken into account. abstract: Fennel ( Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) is a vital seed spice crop cultivated in arid and semi-arid regions of India, where water scarcity and nutrient inefficiency constrain productivity. title: International transport corridor and firm capacity utilization: Evidence from the China-Europe Railway Express
abstract: The China-Europe Railway Express (CERE) serves as an important international transport corridor connecting the Eurasian continent and plays a vital role in promoting economic and trade cooperation between China and countries along the route, as well as in advancing the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). title: Determinants of Crop Diversification in Boro Rice‐Based, Wetland Farming Systems in Bangladesh
abstract: The haor landscape of Bangladesh is highly reliant on Boro rice cultivation, making farm households vulnerable to recurring floods and climate-related risks. Crop diversification can intensify agricultural resilience and reduce production risks. This study examined the pattern, extent, and determinants of crop diversification using a cross-sectional field survey performed in 2023 among 240 farm households in three purposively selected upazilas (Itna, Mithamoin, and Nikli) of Kishoreganj district. title: The influence of accountability on procurement performance: a case study ministry of blue economy and fisheries Zanzibar
abstract: Accountability is a foundational pillar of procurement governance, yet quantitative evidence on how accountability mechanisms specifically shape procurement outcomes within individual government ministries in Zanzibar remains scarce. This study examined the influence of accountability on procurement performance at the Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries (MoBEF), Zanzibar. title: UShER-TB: scalable, comprehensive, accessible phylogenomic analysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for the Tuberculosis (TB) disease, remains a leading global infectious disease killer, and genomic epidemiology is essential for understanding its transmission dynamics. Computational limitations prevent comprehensive phylogenetic analysis of the publicly available Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes. Here, we create UShER-TB, a comprehensive pipeline for scalable phylogenomic MTB analysis. title: Multi-environment evaluation of finger millet genotypes for agronomic traits, yield stability and adaptability for summer cultivation
abstract: Identification and advancement of high yielding and early maturing finger millet genotypes for summer season is essential for crop diversification in the Indo-Gangetic flood plains to enhance food security and production efficiency. The current experiment studied 145 finger millet genotypes under six contrasting environments namely: E2, E4, and E6 (summer) and E1, E3, and E5 (rainy) in three consecutive years (2021–2024) to identify parents suitable for the development of specific varieties and superior genotypes for summer cultivation. title: Halogenation of Sesquiterpene γ-Lactone Molecules: New Compounds, Structure and Biological Activity
abstract: This article presents the results of halogenation studies on seven sesquiterpene γ-lactones readily obtainable from plant material: the germacranolide argolide, the eudesmanolide isoalantolactone, and the guaianolides arglabin, achillin, grossheimin, grossmisin, and leucomisine. Sesquiterpene γ-lactones occurring in plants of the Asteraceae (Compositae) family constitute an important class of terpenoids, among which chlorine-containing compounds are distinguished by pronounced biological activity. abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Mating patterns in plant populations are shaped jointly by the local availability and relatedness of potential mates, both of which can vary through time in disturbance-prone habitats. We aimed to investigate how a year-to-year change in local plant densities and spatial genetic structure (SGS) influence opportunities for inbreeding and outcrossing in a predominantly self-compatible population of Arabidopsis lyrata subsp. lyrata located in a fore-dune habitat at Rondeau Provincial Park, Ontario. title: Chloroplast Genome Characterization and Phylogenetic Implications of Reyesia and Salpiglossis (Salpiglossideae, Solanaceae)
abstract: ABSTRACT Solanaceae represents one of the most economically significant families among flowering plants. abstract: El estudio propende por la optimización de los procesos organizacionales, mejorar la calidad y satisfacción de los usuarios con un modelo de información oportuna y relevante para la toma de decisiones, situación que se da debido a la ausencia de un sistema de control de gestión basado en indicadores. abstract: Medical tourism is a strategic growth sector in India, with foreign visitors for treatment in 2025 at 507,244, and the market is expected to grow from USD 8.7 billion to USD 16.2 billion by 2030. With Hyderabad's recognized hospitals and exemplary aviation connectivity, Telangana, with its vision of creating a regional hub under the Telangana Tourism Policy 2025-30, has set its sights on becoming a regional hub. title: Enhanced auditory gain and tinnitus-like behavior in mice lacking KCTD12, an auxiliary subunit of GABAB receptors
abstract: Precise regulation of neural gain is essential for accurate sensory processing and relies on inhibitory mechanisms that constrain neuronal responsiveness. Disruption of inhibitory control has been implicated in disorders characterized by abnormal sensory perception, including tinnitus, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating inhibitory signaling remain poorly understood. title: Host seasonal trophic strategies linked to dietary‐microbiota coupling: A potential mechanism mediating the coexistence of sympatric small rodents
abstract: The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host-specific gut microbiota responses. We compared the herbivorous Brandt's vole (Lasiopodomys brandtii) and the granivorous Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus), two sympatric rodent species with divergent trophic strategies inhabiting the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. title: Climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across agroecological zones in Gedeo, Ethiopia: evidence from problem confrontation index and multinomial regression
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens apiculture by reducing floral resources, water availability, and colony productivity. Although beekeepers adopt various adaptation measures, barriers to effective adaptation remain poorly understood across different agro ecological settings. This study examined the determinants and severity of climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across three agro ecological zones in Gedeo Zone, southern Ethiopia. abstract: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional hydrogels combining mechanical robustness, autonomous self‐healing, electrical conductivity, and stimuli responsiveness remains challenging. Here, we report a thermoresponsive, self‐healing dual‐network hydrogel reinforced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), integrating reversible dynamic crosslinking, ionic liquid‐mediated phase transitions, and electrical conductivity. abstract: Abstract Peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) result in severe functional impairments and pose a significant clinical and socio-economic burden. Although autologous nerve grafts remain the clinical gold standard, their use is limited by donor availability and associated morbidity. title: And after burial? Corrosion structures of high-lead glazed ceramics in Al-Andalus objects from Palmela Castle (West Portugal)
abstract: The study of the degradation of archaeological objects is essential for guiding their conservation and restoration, alongside understanding possible formal and aesthetic changes that may have occurred since their burial. Several difficulties hinder these studies as numerous factors, both intrinsic and extrinsic, are involved in the degradation processes. In the present work, we focused on a group of representative green and honeydew transparent glazed fragments from Pamela Castle, dated between the 9th and 11th centuries. abstract: During the Canton System, the Thirteen Factories in Guangzhou formed a cross‑cultural visual field in which Harbor Scene Paintings (HSPs) served as both commodities and sites of Sino-Western visual negotiation. Drawing on visual culture studies and the pictorial turn, this study constructs a comparative cross‑cultural visual analysis framework. title: When seeds change hands: gender, intersectionality, and access to seed in rural Senegal
abstract: Abstract Despite advances in understanding seed circulation in rural communities, little is known about the gendered and intersectional power relations that shape farmers’ access to seed. Based on a case study in a Bassari community of southeastern Senegal, we examine the roles of women and men in seed circulation and explore who maintains and who controls access to seed for six staple crops. abstract: River corridors play an important role in maintaining the diversity and ecological functions of spontaneous plants. Within urban river corridors, spontaneous plant communities are exposed to both urbanization in the surrounding landscape and lateral hydrological variation between water and land. title: Donor Geometry Engineering for Regulating Spatial Charge Distribution in Heptazine‐Based D‐A Porous Organic Polymers Toward Efficient Photocatalysis
abstract: Regulating the spatial charge distribution in donor-acceptor (D-A) porous organic polymers (POPs) to suppress charge recombination remains a formidable challenge in the field of photocatalysis. Herein, donor geometry engineering as a design method is proposed to address this issue. Three novel heptazine-based donor-acceptor porous organic polymers (D-A POPs) with varied fusion patterns and connection sites of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) donors have been constructed. abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing an effective hydroxyl reservoir to optimize adsorption behavior of Pt‐based catalysts toward oxygen/carbon‐containing intermediates represents a key challenge for enhancing the CO tolerance of the anodic methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) and the kinetics of the cathodic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in fuel cells. title: Study on gas flow characteristics and pulse blockage removal regulation in unstable collapsed boreholes
abstract: Gas drainage boreholes easily suffer hole wall collapse and coal particle blockage under in-situ stress and mining disturbance, drastically lowering gas extraction efficiency. To avoid the drawbacks of traditional dredging technologies, including drainage interruption and borehole wall damage, a gas pulse blockage removal method is proposed to achieve non-contact dredging using transient high-pressure gas. title: Decoding cryptic diversity of moss populations in a forest-tundra ecotone
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryptic speciation is widespread among bryophytes, and it appears common in arctic and subarctic mosses where cryptic lineages may occur sympatrically in the environment. However, cryptic lineages are rarely considered in genetic diversity assessments. This situation poses a challenge, as the complex population structure resulting from cryptic speciation, along with factors like the predominance of clonality, can lead to inaccurate estimates of biodiversity. title: Anionic DOPG liposomal biointerfaces modulate physiological heterogeneity in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
abstract: Colloidal interfaces formed between lipid vesicles and living bacterial cells may regulate both dispersion organization and cellular state, yet their behavior during storage remains poorly understood. Here, anionic 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoglycerol (DOPG) liposomes, either unloaded or prepared with fluvastatin, were combined with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and monitored for 28 days at 4 °C. title: The prevalence of misreporting and misinterpreting correlation coefficients in biomedical literature
abstract: Correlation coefficient is widely used in biomedical and biological literature. Yet, its frequent misuse and misinterpretation undermine the credibility and reproducibility of the scientific findings. abstract: Redox conditions strongly influence mantle phase equilibria and arc magmatism, yet the processes driving elevated oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) in subarc mantle remain unresolved. abstract: The disposal of chrysotile asbestos waste poses significant environmental hazards, while heavy oil residues demand costly pretreatment to remove toxic metals and sulfur. This study presents a circular economy approach to convert acid-leached chrysotile asbestos waste into a functional chemisorbent for the simultaneous demetallization and desulfurization of heavy petroleum residues. abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their effects on coating microstructure and tribology. title: Creatio ex nihilo, ordenación del caos y la teoría de la información en Génesis 1
abstract: Partiendo de una visión ontológico-teológica de la creatio ex nihilo, se aborda la creación en Génesis 1 como la ordenación de un caos que también depende ontológicamente de Dios. Se argumenta que la información es crucial en el proceso creador, con la palabra divina como fuente de información constituyente. Para ello se muestra que la estructura del relato sacerdotal de la creación presenta la palabra divina como principio organizador del espacio, el tiempo y la vida. Se hace notar también cómo el ser humano, creado a imagen de Dios, tiene la tarea de mantener el orden.

abstract: Abstract Voucher specimens are central to studying threatened taxa. However, errors in their locality data can distort understandings of these species’ distributions, and in extreme cases may even misguide assessments of species’ conservation statuses. The Perth slider, Lerista lineata , represents an informative exemplar of this situation. title: Designed Protein‐Based Physical Crosslinker for Triple Helical Collagen Biomaterials
abstract: Collagen plays a pivotal role in animal body structure, but hydrogels of reconstituted collagens often have poor mechanical performance. Chemical crosslinking or the addition of other biopolymers are often used as a remedy. Inspired by the many natural collagen-interacting proteins that modify the mechanics of collagen hydrogels, we explore protein-based physical crosslinking of collagen as a route to modulate the mechanics of collagen hydrogels. abstract: Classical Differential Evolution (DE) solves the Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (MDVRPTW) efficiently but struggles to maintain time-window feasibility. abstract: Microplastics released from food packaging have become an emerging food safety concern and may contribute to intestinal inflammation. abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to characterize the chemical constituents of the methanolic extract of Euphorbia anacampseros using high‐performance liquid chromatography (HPLC–DAD) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analyses. abstract: Abstract High-resolution spatial transcriptomics is still cost-prohibitive and dominated by short-read sequencing, limiting in situ detection of transcript structures. Here we present a low-cost, lab-made, high-density bead-in-microwell chip assembled by routine centrifuge and decoded by a tri-part combinatorial long-barcode strategy. title: Structural Mechanisms of Urban Traffic Congestion in Dili, Timor-Leste
abstract: Urban congestion in small developing capitals exhibits structural characteristics distinct from those observed in larger metropolitan regions. This study develops a perception-based Structural Equation Model (SEM) to analyze the dynamics of congestion formation in Dili, Timor-Leste. title: Urban ecological resilience in the digital era: the role of data factor marketization and spatial spillovers
abstract: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Invasive aspergillosis (IA) represents one of the most frequent invasive fungal infections in paediatric patients with risk factors. abstract: Bacterial diseases including red-leg syndrome (RLS), edema syndrome (ES) and meningitis-like infectious disease (MID) cause massive economic losses in farmed bullfrogs ( Rana catesbeiana ), yet their divergent pathophysiology and host-immune signatures remain poorly compared. abstract: Salmonella is a pathogen that causes gastrointestinal illness in consumers. abstract: Abstract To address the high path redundancy, poor smoothness, and low planning efficiency exhibited by the Bi-directional Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (Bi-RRT) algorithm in complex dynamic environments, an improved Bi-RRT* algorithm for collision avoidance path planning in mobile robots is proposed. abstract: The paper explores the challenges and opportunities of implementing the Curriculum and Assessment Policy Statement (CAPS) and the Progression Policy in secondary schools in Chris Hani District, Eastern Cape Province. The paper aimed to identify the barriers to effective CAPS implementation while highlighting the potential benefits of the Progression Policy. title: Effect of Progressive Muscle Relaxation and Nature Sounds on Alarm Fatigue in Intensive Care Unit Nurses: A Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intensive care unit (ICU) nurses are exposed to numerous alarms, many of which are unnecessary and lead to alarm fatigue. This phenomenon, caused by desensitization to alarm sounds, reduces nurses' responsiveness to critical alerts and threatens both their well-being and patient safety. Alarm fatigue has been linked to elevated stress, burnout and errors in patient care, underscoring the need for effective interventions. title: Salinity imposes selection on the occurrence of antibiotic resistance genes in lake ecosystems under increasing salinization
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in lake ecosystems with salinization remain insufficiently understood, particularly with respect to water-sediment differentiation. Here, we investigated the role of salinity in shaping targeted ARGs and intI 1 across surface water and surface sediments in a lake ecosystem experiencing increasing salinization in an arid and semi-arid region. title: Analytical instability and aqueous degradation of carbapenem antibiotics: formation of β-lactam-retaining transformation products
abstract: Carbapenems are last-resort antibiotics used to treat severe infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. Despite their clinical importance and documented consumption, they remain largely undetected in environmental monitoring studies. This study investigated whether the lack of detection of carbapenems in environmental studies reflects analytical limitations, rapid degradation, or both. abstract: Abstract This study presents multi-epoch photometry from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer to investigate variability in white dwarf debris disks, utilizing the full 14.5 yr mission datasets pre- and post-cryogen. This study clarifies acidity accumulation under limited water exchange by integrating field monitoring, hydrodynamic–tracer simulation, and a soil-column experiment reproducing tidal cycling in paddy soils. abstract: Abstract Amorphous jellyfish gelatin powders readily absorb moisture during storage, leading to caking, agglomeration, and reduced functionality. This study evaluated the effects of drying method, activated carbon (AC) treatment, simulated packaging configuration, and simulated storage conditions on the critical relative humidity (RHc) and physicochemical stability of jellyfish gelatin powders. abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) plays a critical role in plant immune responses. The 9-cis-epoxy-carotenoid dioxygenase ( NCED ) gene family encodes pivotal rate-limiting enzymes in ABA biosynthesis. Although NCED family members have been identified in multiple plant species, genome-wide systematic analysis of NCEDs in Lilium spp. remains lacking. In this study, a total of 72 NCED genes were identified from the genomes of L. regale, L. sargentiae , and L. davidii var. unicolor . title: A bias-aware indicator framework for prioritizing surveys of data-deficient freshwater leeches in China
abstract: Sparse and spatially biased occurrence records complicate survey planning for freshwater invertebrates. We evaluated a bias-aware indicator framework linking taxon documentation with a fixed 40:40:20 ranking of environmental similarity to documented occurrence contexts, documentation gap and freshwater support. Contemporary accessibility was evaluated separately to characterize documentation associations and inform survey logistics. title: Water stable isotopes reveal the ecohydrological importance of stemflow infiltration for mature and juvenile European beech
abstract: Stemflow of forest trees can contribute a significant fraction of water to forest's water fluxes; however, it is still unclear whether and to what extent trees and their neighbours use stemflow for water uptake and supply. We applied deuterium-enriched stemflow equivalent to a 23-mm throughfall event to adult Fagus sylvatica trees to trace stemflow through the soil and trees. abstract: BACKGROUND: Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, contributing disproportionately to the global burden. Persistence of the disease is driven by sub-optimal vaccination coverage and heterogeneous transmission patterns, but the specific spatio-temporal dynamics and the quantitative impact of vaccination gaps at the sub-national level are not fully characterized. abstract: ABSTRACT Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. title: Critical Appraisal of North African Medicinal Plant Activity Against Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii cause hospital outbreaks across North Africa, where access to newer antibiotics is limited and plant-derived agents are widely proposed as alternatives. This critical narrative review appraises what the published evidence from Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia can support. abstract: Aechmea blanchetiana is a bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest, occurring predominantly in Restinga ecosystems characterized by sandy soils and fluctuations in water availability. This study evaluated the anatomical, physiological, photochemical, biochemical, and morphological responses of in vitro-grown A. blanchetiana previously cultured with calcium silicate (CaSiO₃) and subsequently exposed to polyethylene glycol (PEG)-6000-induced osmotic stress. abstract: La confluencia contemporánea entre la transformación tecnológica, la automatización basada en modelos generativos de lenguaje y las secuelas afectivas en el entorno educativo posterior a la pandemia global ha configurado un escenario complejo, caracterizado por la fragilidad estructural y la sobrecarga informacional. title: Estimating soil water retention curves from co‐located in situ water content and matric potential sensors
abstract: Abstract The soil water retention curve (SWRC) governs water storage and redistribution in the vadose zone and is a key input for hydrologic and agroecosystem models. Laboratory evaporation methods provide high‐quality SWRCs but are destructive and represent static conditions that may not reflect in situ soil behavior under natural field conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Seven known phenolic compounds ( 2 – 8 ) along with one new phenolic compound ( 1 ) were isolated from the heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae). abstract: The study assessed awareness and constraints to the utilization of climate-smart agriculture technologies among arable-crop farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to examine the awareness levels of arable farmers on climate-smart agriculture technologies; and identify the constraints faced in the utilization of CSA technologies among arable crop farmers in the study area. abstract: Bathycoelia distincta (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) is one of the most economically important stink bug pests of macadamia in South Africa. Recent field bioassays have indicated reduced efficacy of synthetic pyrethroids in certain pest populations. Target-site resistance associated with mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene, particularly at the knockdown resistance (kdr) and super-kdr loci, is widely documented in other insect taxa. abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing "impact trajectories"). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. title: Zn-doped CoNiCr medium-entropy phosphide electrocatalyst on Ni foam for alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: In alkaline media, the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is hindered by sluggish kinetics arising from the high energy barrier of water dissociation and suboptimal hydrogen adsorption. Controlled heteroatom doping and structural engineering can efficiently modulate hydrogen intermediate adsorption and boost HER performance. title: Space economy and strategic development in ASEAN pathways to 2035
abstract: The ASEAN space economy is entering a rapid growth phase toward 2035, alongside a global market projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion. ASEAN’s share is expected to scale to approximately USD 80–200 billion, driven by three key engines: Earth Observation (EO) commercialization, SATCOM expansion via high-throughput systems, and rising demand for ISR and Space Domain Awareness (SDA). abstract: Hydrogen is a by-product of electrochemical phosphorus removal, but its environmental and economic relevance has rarely been assessed. abstract: Abstract Decarbonising the hard-to-abate maritime and aviation transport sectors will be challenging. While alternative renewable fuels, such as biofuels and E-fuels, show promising potential for substituting traditional fossil fuels, they carry challenges regarding the required expansion of variable renewable energy (VRE) and the availability of sustainable biomass. abstract: Brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) requires considerable soil moisture throughout its life cycle, therefore, its cultivation in water constraint area is difficult. Though different soil moisture conservation technologies and lower water use irrigation systems have been developed for crop cultivation, their successful deployment largely depends on the locality, especially on soil characteristics. abstract: The detrimental effects of heavy metals on food substances are concerning because they pose a threat to human health and food security in general. This study evaluated heavy metal concentrations and assessed the associated human health risks in wild oyster mushroom (Pleurotusostreatus) from southeastern Nigeria. Using stratified random sampling method, representative mushroom samples were collected from the five states of southeastern Nigeria (Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo). abstract: Agroforestry is increasingly recognized as a nature-based solution (NbS) to interconnected global and local challenges, including climate change, land degradation, biodiversity loss, and livelihood insecurity. By integrating trees with crops and livestock, agroforestry enhances ecosystem services such as carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and soil fertility, and diversifies farm income. abstract: ABSTRACT The redlegged earth mite, Halotydeus destructor , is an invasive pest of grain and pasture crops in Australia. abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective treatment of tuberculosis is often hampered by anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATB-DILI). abstract: Abstract Background Households provide an ideal setting to study SARS-CoV-2 transmission modes due to the close proximity and extended exposure among members. title: Land-based search and rescue training: evolution and simplification
abstract: Land-based search and rescue training in Aotearoa New Zealand has undergone substantial change, yet there has been limited examination of how these changes have affected the analytical foundations of search management. This review was undertaken to identify what concepts, tools and competencies have been retained, modified or lost in the Managing Land Search Operations course that evolved into Manage the Initial Response and Extended Search Planning. abstract: Tourism is a comprehensive industry that integrates diverse service sectors with complicatedly concurrent resource consumption and pollution. It forms a complex water-energy-carbon (W-E-C) footprint system that poses synergistic challenges to sustainable management. This study employs a multiregional input-output model and Structural Path Analysis to identify tourism’s W-E-C footprints and critical supply-chain paths in China. abstract: Maximizing the agricultural value of biogas slurry while mitigating its environmental risks requires precise blending and irrigation, yet optimized methodologies remain underdeveloped. This study employs Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) numerical simulation to analyze the fluid dynamics of three designed mixed fertilizer pipeline structures. abstract: Recommendations for sustainable diets agree on the need to reduce consumption of animal products, especially in wealthy countries. Legumes are expected to play a pivotal role in providing food protein substitutes in this context, but their adoption by consumers remains too slow to meet the sustainable development goals. Plant-based substitutes, such as yoghurt-like products, suffer from poorer sensory and nutritional properties than their dairy references. abstract: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for over 90% of oral malignancies and remains associated with high morbidity, recurrence, and poor long-term survival rates. To address these clinical challenges, the development of multifunctional nanotherapeutic systems capable of improving active stability and localized anticancer activity has become a vital focus in oral oncology and dental nanomedicine. abstract: Background and purpose Resin-modified glass ionomer cements (RMGICs) are commonly utilized as restorative materials because of their ability to release fluoride, form chemical bonds with tooth structure, and desirable biocompatibility. Nevertheless, their comparatively low mechanical strength limits their application in regions subjected to high stress. abstract: Chigger mites (larval Trombiculidae) are obligate ectoparasites, some species transmit Orientia tsutsugamushi , the causative agent of scrub typhus. Despite their public health significance in rural Southeast Asia, relationships between chiggers infesting wildlife, domestic animals and those present in the surrounding environment remain poorly characterised. abstract: Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals. abstract: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) have emerged as a critical instrument for advancing urban sustainability and climate resilience, particularly in developing countries where rapid economic-driven urbanization intensifies exposure to climate risks. There is little theoretical coherence and well-organized knowledge regarding patterns of collaboration. abstract: Abstract We report a comprehensive study of the dynamic mechanical properties of polyborosiloxane (PBS) tested using uniaxial compression, shear rheometry, compression DMA, impact loading, and vibrational transmissibility on a commercially available PBS formulation. abstract: Abstract Directed evolution of enzymes is generally performed toward a specific substrate, which predictably improves enzyme activity toward the probe substrate. However, it is difficult to predict whether evolved enzymes will be selective or promiscuous toward other substrates. title: Heterogeneity of child and adolescent asthma determinants across urbanization stages: a 21-year global analysis
abstract: Urbanization reshapes environmental exposures, lifestyle, and health systems, yet global evidence on how child and adolescent asthma risk factors evolve across development stages remains limited. Using panel data from 149 countries (2000–2020), this study applied clustering and coupling coordination analysis to identify stage-specific pathways of urbanization and air quality transitions. abstract: Abstract African economic history has experienced a revival during the 21 st century through the globalisation of economic history as a field and a growing interest in how history has shaped current economic inequalities. This survey reviews the development of the field since its initial foundations, and illustrates the ways in which more recent work has diverged in its methods and approaches. abstract: Abstract In semiarid western US dairy systems, field evidence remains limited on whether processed manure products can sustain silage corn ( Zea mays L.) productivity and improve soil health. abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, driving continued research for innovative therapies with enhanced specificity and efficacy. abstract: This study evaluates vegetation dynamics and drought conditions in the semi-arid agricultural landscapes of Kaman (Türkiye) using integrated remote sensing data. NDVI and NDMI derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2, together with land surface temperature (LST) and Sentinel-1 soil moisture, were analyzed to assess vegetation–environment interactions. title: The Role of ICT in MENA Environmental Sustainability: A Panel GMM Approach
abstract: Climate change poses a major threat to environmental sustainability worldwide, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, which faces rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, and air pollution. The role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in environmental sustainability remains debated, as studies report both positive and negative effects. abstract: Seasonal migration in birds involves a substantial spatial redistribution of avian biodiversity each year and drives seasonal changes in community composition. Migrants experience different combinations of species interactions over space and time, generating regular disassembly and reassembly of bird communities throughout their annual cycles. abstract: This article critically investigates the constitutional, statutory, institutional, and fiscal arrangements governing the allocation and exercise of taxing powers in Nigeria, focusing on the position of Rivers State within Nigeria’s federal structure. abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. abstract: Abstract Sodium nitrate (SN) is a promising molten salt phase change material with high energy storage capacity and thermal stability for high-temperature latent heat thermal energy storage systems. abstract: Abstract Catalytic function in enzymes is generally considered a fixed property of the protein scaffold. abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. abstract: Significance: Cerebral water fraction is physiologically relevant to brain fluid dynamics, glymphatic function, cerebral edema, and dehydration, yet it is not routinely measured in wearable neuroimaging. title: Clonality in European black poplar conservation units using genomics
abstract: Aim of study: We performed a fine scale characterization of two European black poplar (Populus nigra) in situ conservation units, using a large sample of individuals and a comprehensive set of genetic markers. This information is pivotal to understand the population dynamics of the units for implementing conservation and management plans. abstract: This article compares the narratives of Moses in the Qur'an and the Bible and explores ‘thinking beyond the narratives.’ Existing comparative studies often focus only on identifying similarities and differences. abstract: Aquatic hyphomycetes are an ecological group of anamorphic fungi that play an essential role in decomposing plant substrates in lotic environments. This narrative review compiled studies highlighting the biotechnological potential of this group, contributing to the understanding of its applications and perspectives. abstract: Early childhood education is increasingly recognized as a critical site for climate learning, yet there is a need for further exploration around how educators introduce ecological responsibility in developmentally meaningful and emotionally attuned ways. This qualitative multi-case study examines how three preschool teachers engaged young children in water-centered storytelling and inquiry as an entry point into climate literacy. abstract: Coal gangue disrupts microbial diversity and impairs nutrient cycling, constraining sustainable regional development. Traditional bioremediation relies on functional microbial traits, yet they often fail to colonize and perform in carbon-limited environments despite exogenous carbon inputs. abstract: Somalia’s drought is conventionally read as a drying and warming trend that erodes food production. This study asks whether the decisive change lies in the variance rather than the mean, and how cereal production responds. Monthly Combined Drought Index values for 73 districts are joined to seasonal production of maize and sorghum, the two staple cereals, for 45 crop growing districts from 2001 to 2025, then analysed with trend and variance tests, panel fixed effects and a threshold regression. title: Subsidence inversions – the surface water vapour thief
abstract: Abstract A deep anticyclonic subsidence inversion reached near‐surface levels over southern England on 25 April 2026, resulting in relative humidity levels falling below 15% widely and sub‐10% in the Reading and Wokingham area. Such low levels in lowland England have very few historical precedents within the last century or more. Furthermore, careful analysis of the automatic weather station psychrometer records from the University of Reading Atmospheric Observatory on this occasion suggests that the relative humidity here may have fallen briefly below 6%.

abstract: Abstract Melanoma is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by significant phenotypic plasticity, allowing tumor cells to transit between different phenotypic states. While the primary transcriptional markers defining these states are well-established, the non-coding regulatory networks that stabilize these phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Chemical control may be available to effectively and extensively reduce the effects of the most fungal disease but field application of these chemical fungicides may present a danger to the health of humans, animals, and the environment. abstract: Abstract The genetic resources of wild Solanum plants constitute reservoirs of variability of interest for the conservation and improvement of Andean crops. abstract: Background: Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP), a highly contagious disease of cattle, is a major constraint to cattle production in Tanzania. abstract: The uniform and efficient drying process is still a big problem in the decentralized orthodox tea industry, especially in the field of using cost-effective and eco-friendly thermal drying equipment. abstract: Background: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory and immune-mediated oral mucosal disease characterized by epithelial damage, basal cell degeneration, and recurrent lesions. abstract: Citizen science has rapidly moved beyond simply crowdsourcing data to become a novel platform for environmental and informal science education. However, few studies document the informal learning outcomes of citizen science, particularly in youth or Extension education. abstract: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is widely used in tropical agriculture, yet its effects on non-target ectothermic vertebrates remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Context Termites, like other pattern-generating organisms, often create vegetation heterogeneity. title: Evaluation of an NS1-Based ZIKV/DENV IgG ELISA approach for serological differentiation in a dengue-endemic setting
abstract: Abstract Zika virus (ZIKV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus that has recently emerged as a global health threat. abstract: Abstract Diffuse sources and resulting surface water quality impairments are major challenges for achieving advanced environmental goals as formulated in the EU Water Framework Directive or in the Zero Pollution Ambition of the European Green Deal. abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Small tofu enterprises may rely on these fuels when cleaner alternatives remain financially or operationally inaccessible. abstract: The genus Ferula (Apiaceae) is widely distributed across Central and Southwest Asia and is recognized for its diverse secondary metabolites and traditional medicinal uses. abstract: Informal settlements are commonly characterized by concentrated populations, inadequate infrastructure and poor living conditions that may constrain household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. Anchored on Urban Political Ecology (UPE) theory, this study examined the implications of informal settlement characteristics for household WASH services in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya. abstract: Abstract Dynamic stall is a highly unsteady aerodynamic problem that restricts the performance of pitching airfoils used in helicopters, wind turbines, and UAVs. abstract: Delivery service companies in Indonesia face a decline in the number of shipments due to the large number of competitors and uncompetitive shipping price offers. abstract: Scaffolds have proven useful as matrices for cell culture, tissue ingrowth, organ formation, mechanical support, drug screening platforms, and localized delivery systems. abstract: TATA-box binding protein (TBP) associated factors (TAFs), together with TBP, com-pose transcription factor IID (TFIID), which is an essential complex for transcription initiation and regulation. In this study, a total of 124 TAF genes were identified in four Gossypium species. TAFs were divided into six subgroups based on the phylogenetic tree analysis. title: Whole genome sequencing, assembly, and functional annotation of Hyphopichia burtonii Y951 isolated from Vitis vinifera L. cv Cabernet Sauvignon grape must
abstract: Hyphopichia burtonii is a non-conventional yeast present in diverse environments including bread, cured meat, grape must, zebra dove droppings and corn weevil. Strains derived from different environments display different traits. However, limited information exists on the genomic diversity of this species. Here we present the genome of H. burtonii Y951 strain isolated from grape must and proven to have antifungal activity against various grapevine fungal pathogens. The genome was sequenced using PacBio long-read technology, and a high-quality de novo genome assembly was generated using the Fly

title: Antibacterial mechanism of a multitarget antibacterial peptide CpAtt against Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) poses a serious threat to food safety and global health, driving the demand for natural and safe antimicrobials. CpAtt, an attacin-like antimicrobial peptide identified previously in our laboratory, demonstrated potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus. This study systematically elucidated the multi-target antibacterial mechanisms of CpAtt against S. aureus. title: Characteristics of Secondary Aerosols and Ozone During Intense Biomass Burning Episodes in Northeast China: Insights From High‐Resolution Time‐of‐Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer
abstract: Abstract Springtime haze in the intensive agricultural regions of Northeast China is closely associated with large‐scale open biomass burning (OBB), yet the resulting chemical evolution remains poorly understood. Based on the field campaign utilizing a High‐Resolution Time‐of‐Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer (HR‐ToF‐AMS) in Harbin during 2022, we identified OBB as the primary driver of intense haze episodes, characterized by sharp increases in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) and synergistic surges in associated inorganic species. title: BRIDGING THE RELIGIOUS VALUE–ACTION GAP: ISLAMIC DA'WAH INSTITUTIONS AND PRO-ENVIRONMENTAL BEHAVIOR
abstract: Purpose – This study examines how Islamic da'wah institutions contribute to pro-environmental behavior grounded in Islamic values, through which mechanisms those values are internalized, which strategies institutions employ, and where the evidence remains weak. Design/methodology/approach – A systematic literature review guided by PRISMA 2020 searched Google Scholar, Garuda, SINTA and DOAJ, supplemented by citation chasing and Scopus-indexed publisher platforms. institutions: Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University Jakarta

title: Mechanical, microstructural and rheological assessment of recycled polycarbonate/ABS blends modified with ABS-g-MA compatibilizer and a multifunctional epoxy chain extender
abstract: Upcycling recycled polycarbonate (rPC) into higher-value engineering blends remains challenging because recycling-induced chain scission compromises toughness and melt integrity. In this study, a dual reactive approach combining interfacial compatibilization with synthesized maleic-anhydride-grafted ABS (ABS-g-MA) and reactive chain extension using the multifunctional epoxy chain extender Joncryl ADR 4300 was employed to upgrade rPC/ABS blends. title: Interactive effects of drug use and social vulnerability on health outcomes among street involved youth in a prospective cohort study from Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Background/objectives Street-involved youth experience overlapping behavioral and structural vulnerabilities that increase the risk of adverse health outcomes. However, longitudinal evidence examining whether social vulnerability modifies the health effects of drug use remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. This study investigated the independent and interactive effects of drug use and social vulnerability on adverse health outcomes among street-involved youth in urban Indonesia. title: An integrated multilayer environmental impact assessment framework for accelerating sustainable energy infrastructure permitting
abstract: The deployment of sustainable energy infrastructure in the European Union is now limited less by technology costs than by the duration and unpredictability of permitting. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), the main authorization instrument for energy projects, evaluates the impacts of a proposal. What it does not evaluate is the quality of the governance process through which those impacts are assessed and decided, so risks arising from institutional fragmentation, weak stakeholder coordination, or the exclusion of affected groups stay invisible until they surface as objections, litigation

title: Sepideh Kashani and Indian Rhetorical Techniques
abstract: Sarvar-e A'zam Bakuchi, known by the pen name "Sepideh Kashani," is a prominent figure in Persian poetry. Her literary works—distinguished by rich imagination, creativity, and the innovative use of literary devices—demonstrate that she not only mastered the traditional techniques and rhetorical devices of the Persian language for conveying meaning and connecting with her audience but was also well-versed in the fundamental principles of Indian rhetoric (*Alankara*). title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
abstract: Abstract Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. title: Xin-II shows cardioprotective effects in a rat model of chronic heart failure: An integrated network pharmacology and transcriptomic
abstract: BACKGROUNDChronic heart failure (CHF) is a major global public health burden.Mongolian Medicine Xin-II has shown promising clinical efficacy in the management of cardiovascular diseases, including coronary heart disease and arrhythmias.However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. AIMTo evaluate the therapeutic effects of Xin-II on CHF and investigate the potential molecular pathways underlying these effects using an integrated approach combining network pharmacology and transcriptomic sequencing. title: Bioprocessing of Talaromyces purpurogenus for production of dihydromonascorubrin with a powerful antioxidant and antimicrobial activities integrated with the network-guided target prediction and molecular docking analyses
abstract: Abstract The antibiotic resistance of pathogenic microorganisms due to the irresponsible use in healthcare and agricultural practices is one of the global threats for the human, especially immune-compromised patients. Thus, searching for a novel compounds from fungi with unique affinity to combat the drug-resistant microorganisms was the objective. Talaromyces purpurogenus # PZ292970.1, an endophyte of palm tree Elaeis guineensis , has the highest productivity of azaphilone pigment (25.5 AU410/ml), with a strong activity against E. coli (MIC value 6.8 µg/ml), S. aureus and C. albicans (MIC val

title: Responses of soil characteristics and bacterial communities to agricultural irrigation with different treatment levels of wastewater
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of domestic wastewater treated at different treatment levels on the biochemical characteristics of irrigated soils. Raw domestic wastewater was subjected to four treatment processes: (1) grit sedimentation; (2) grit sedimentation combined with ultrafiltration (UF); (3) grit sedimentation combined with anaerobic activated sludge treatment followed by UF; and (4) grit sedimentation combined with aerobic activated sludge treatment followed by UF. title: Topographical Imagination in Marina Cvetaeva’s «Pis'mo», «O Germanii», and «Natal'ja Gončarova»
abstract: In a substantial number of her texts – poetry as well as prose – Marina Ivanovna Cvetaeva (1892–1941) constructs contrasting dimensionalities: one-dimensional lines, two-dimensional planes, and three-dimensional objects are set in contrast to one another. She juxtaposes squares and flat surfaces with open landscapes, towers, and cathedrals. These images are frequently articulated through geometric imagery, yet they have thus far received little analysis or commentary in the scholarly literature. title: Testing the theory of planned behavior in predicting evacuation intentions during storms
abstract: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely applied to predict human behavior across diverse domains; however, its application in disaster contexts remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the utility of TPB in predicting intentions to prepare evacuation plans in hurricane-prone areas. Using a quantitative approach, an online survey was administered to adults residing in Florida, yielding 816 valid responses. Attitude toward evacuation planning, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control were measured using validated Likert-scale items. Data were analyzed us

title: Surgical delay is not associated with increased mortality in Greenlandic hip fracture patients: a 5-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Hip fractures are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Guidelines recommend surgery within 24 h, but Greenland’s vast geography and Arctic weather often delay surgical treatment. Our aims were (1) to describe the time until surgery among hip fracture patients in Greenland and (2) to evaluate its association with 30-day and 1-year mortality. All patients with hip fracture ICD-10 codes DS720, DS721 and DS722 from 2018 through 2022 were included. Data on time of diagnosis, time to operation, reason for delay, ASA score, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and time of death were collec

title: Understanding Phosphorus Dynamics in Martian and Lunar Regolith Simulants: Insights for Space Agriculture
abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) is a vital nutrient for plant growth and development, making it essential for sustaining agriculture as human colonies are established in space. However, there is limited knowledge of native P forms and of the interaction between applied P and the lunar or Martian regolith. This highlights the need to examine how this essential nutrient interacts with the regolith for sustainable P management. In this study, we completed P adsorption experiments, followed by desorption experiments, to assess P retention and release in lunar and Martian regolith simulants. Additionally,

title: Design and Analysis of a 5 m3 Excavator Bucket for Coal Handling Using Topology Optimization and Finite Elemen Analysis
abstract: Conventional excavator bucket designs frequently exhibit over-engineering, which reduces operational efficiency due to excessive structural mass. This study aims to optimize the PC500 bucket with a capacity of 5 m³ to reduce mass and evaluate fatigue. 3D modeling was performed using SolidWorks, while Finite Element Analysis (FEA) testing was simulated through Ansys Workbench. The load simulations applied the parameters of HARDOX 400 steel material. The topology optimization results successfully reduced the bucket mass by 10.65%, from 2,702.04 kg to 2,414.31 kg. journal: Turbo Jurnal Program Studi Teknik Mesin

title: The Impact of Purposeful Humor on Student Engagement and Learning in an Elementary Classroom: An Action Research Study
abstract: The purpose of this action research study was to explore how humorous science books can be purposefully integrated into elementary science instruction to enhance student engagement and conceptual understanding. Participants included nineteen second-grade students, ages seven to eight. The study examined the impact of teacher-led, intentional humor embedded in science texts featuring jokes, playful language, and a narrative voice. Data were collected through pre- and post-surveys assessing students’ understanding of grade-level science concepts, as well as their interest in and enjoyment of sci
journal: International Journal of Studies in Education and Science

title: Temperature‐Regulated Morphological Evolution of NiCo‐Carbonate‐Layered Double Hydroxides for High‐Performance Supercapacitor Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Supercapacitors, renowned for their advantages of low‐cost, high‐power density, excellent cycling stability, environmental benignity, and superior safety have gained widespread application in diverse fields. However, their further development is limited by drawbacks such as low energy density. NiCo‐carbonate layered double hydroxide (NiCo‐Carbonate LDH) is a promising electrode material, but its two‐dimensional (2D) nanostructures tend to agglomerate, reducing capacitance utilization. title: Pre‐service teachers' descriptions of UDL engagement guidelines that supported asynchronous professional experience coursework
abstract: Abstract The growth of asynchronous delivery in higher education has made it increasingly important to examine the conditions that support meaningful student engagement. This article reports on a qualitative case study of five pre‐service teachers (PSTs) enrolled in fully asynchronous professional experience (PEx) coursework at a large Australian university. PEx is the work‐integrated learning component of initial teacher education (ITE), where university coursework connects with supervised practice in schools and early childhood settings. The study draws on Universal Design for Learning (UDL)
journal: Journal of Research in Special Educational Needs

title: DOUBLE-DIFFUSIVE GRAVITY CURRENTS IN POROUS MEDIA – IMPLICATIONS FOR APPLYING DENSITY COMPENSATION IN AQUIFER THERMAL ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS
abstract: To improve the efficiency of aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) systems, it is desirable to minimize the spreading of the buoyant injectedfluid. One proposed approach is density compensation, whereby asolute like salt is added to the injectate to increase its density andreduce buoyancy-driven spreading. This study investigates the physicsof double-diffusive porous media gravity currents and thereby assesses,from a small-scale fluid mechanical point of view, the benefits anddrawbacks of such density compensation. title: Structural Design and Misalignment Compensation Performance Evaluation of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer Diaphragm Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT The stiffness of diaphragm couplings directly affects the performance and reliability of mechanical systems. This study proposes a carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) diaphragm coupling. A finite element model was developed in ABAQUS and validated through torsional and axial stiffness tests. At a torque of 3000 N·m, the torsional stiffness error was 7.5%. At an axial displacement of 2 mm, the errors were 1.0% for axial compressive stiffness and 12.7% for axial tensile stiffness. title: Unravelling Genotype × Year Interactions and Yield Stability in Wheat Under Rainfed Conditions in the Temperate Western Himalayas Using AMMI , GGE , and BLUP Approaches
abstract: ABSTRACT Genotype × year (G × Y) interactions significantly complicate successful variety selection, especially in dryland (rain‐dependent) ecosystems experiencing intense climate fluctuations. In this study, the grain yield, agronomic performance, temporal response patterns, and parametric stability of 10 different spring bread wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes were comprehensively evaluated over three consecutive growing seasons (2019–2022) at a temperate dryland farming location using AMMI, GGE biplot, and BLUP‐based linear mixed model (LMM/WAASB) approaches. title: A Comparative Study of Component-Provided Reconstruction-Based and Flexible-Linking Concept Mapping Designs in Collaborative Problem Solving
abstract: This study compares two integrated concept mapping designs within a collaborative problem solving (CPS) setting. The first employs a component-provided reconstruction-based (CPRB) concept mapping approach with real-time automated diagnostic feedback (Kit-Build), while the second uses a component-provided flexible-linking (CPFL) approach with delayed human-mediated feedback (Figma). title: Three‐Dimensional Resistivity Imaging Constrains Crustal Heterogeneity Beneath the 2010 Yushu Ms 7.1 Earthquake Rupture
abstract: Abstract The 2010 Yushu (eastern Tibetan Plateau) Ms 7.1 strike‐slip earthquake ruptured unilaterally toward the southeast but left a hypocentral segment without mapped surface rupture, followed by a two‐stage reorganization of aftershocks. We present a 3‐D electrical resistivity model from 70 quality‐controlled magnetotelluric sites acquired shortly after the event. Alternative data‐component inversions, 2‐D/3‐D comparisons, and anomaly‐focused forward tests identify the best‐resolved features. title: Valorization of endemic sigupai aceh rice husk as a renewable cellulose source for nanocellulose production via sulfuric acid hydrolysis
abstract: Endemic rice varieties can create locally abundant lignocellulosic residues. This study evaluates Sigupai rice husk, an Aceh endemic biomass, as a feedstock for cellulose nanocrystal production through alkaline delignification, hypochlorite bleaching and controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis at 1, 2 and 3 mol/L. The work tests how increasing acid concentration affects yield, residual non-cellulosic material, crystallinity, surface chemistry and particle-size distribution. title: Co‐Infection of Aeromonas veronii and Citrobacter braakii in Yellow Catfish ( Tachysurus fulvidraco )
abstract: Recently, a disease outbreak was observed in farmed yellow catfish (Tachysurus fulvidraco) in Tianjin, China. Naturally infected fish exhibited surface haemorrhages, abdominal distension, anal redness, and hemorrhagic ascites. Histopathological examination revealed systemic lesions in the stomach, intestine, liver, and spleen. Two Gram-negative bacterial isolates, designated PFL and PFS, were isolated from the liver and spleen of diseased fish, respectively. title: Hepatitis E in suspected acute hepatitis cases in Brazil: A comparison with hepatitis A
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an underrecognized cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide, with growing public health relevance, particularly in settings where routine diagnostic testing is limited. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is another epidemiologically related hepatitis virus, but few studies have directly compared these infections in Brazil. institutions: Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul

title: Multi‐Omics Analyses Identify Candidate Genes Associated With Stage‐Specific Quality Formation in Mulching‐Treated Moso Bamboo Shoots
abstract: Bamboo shoots are nutrient-rich edible resources, and organic mulching promotes earlier shoot emergence and increases yield. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating mulching-treated shoot (MtS) development remain unclear. Field experiments across three Moso bamboo forests, combined with biochemical profiling, metabolomics, and transcriptomics, examine MtS development. title: Expressive Priority and Goal Structure and Complexity During Collegiate, Faculty, and Professional Chamber Music Rehearsals
abstract: The purpose of this study was to discover the artistic conceptualizations and priorities of collegiate, faculty, and professional musicians during the moment-to-moment decision-making of a rehearsal. We utilized musicians’ verbalizations during chamber music rehearsals as a vehicle for exploring their thought processes. Analysis 1 investigated the rehearsal targets ensembles prioritized as a percentage of total rehearsal time allocated to each. title: Structural analysis of ribbon-bounding faults in Tessera terrain, Venus
abstract: Tessera terrain preserves locally the earliest tectonic processes on Venus. Ribbon extensional fabric is one of the most pervasive structural features of Tessera, characterized by alternating radar-bright and dark scarps interpreted as long, narrow graben. Here we have determined the geometry of ribbon-bounding scarps to understand their origin and post-formational evolution. We conducted a global survey of 130 radar-bright scarp widths in Magellan, Cycle 1, left-looking, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images from all the crustal plateaus and main tessera occurrences. title: Ultra-lightweight mid-IR methane sensor for in-situ UAV-based measurements: Design and demonstration
abstract: Abstract. We developed an ultra-lightweight mid-infrared laser spectroscopic sensor for precise, rapid mobile measurements of atmospheric methane concentrations aboard small uncrewed aerial vehicles. The design is simple and compact, featuring a Herriott-type multi-pass cell in an open-path configuration. A single board computer with two on-chip microprocessor units allows rapid data acquisition and onboard wavelength modulation spectroscopy, making the sensor a stand-alone turnkey instrument. Including the dedicated battery, the sensor weighs 1.2 kg and consumes up to 11 W of electrical power

title: Limestone reaction and crop yield in sandy soil of Bahia’s Cerrado, Brazil
abstract: Soil amendment is an essential step toward the introduction or maintenance of intensified agricultural production systems. The aim of the present research is to assess lime’s response to crops rotation and sandy soil yield in Bahia’s Cerrado region, Brazil, under controlled conditions. The experiment was conducted at completely randomized design with four replications. The crops were grown in pots filled with 20 kg of Oxisol (14% of clay). title: Development of NiO/borophene hybrid platform for non-enzymatic electrochemical sensing of malathion
abstract: Malathion (MAL), a widely used organophosphate pesticide effecting environment and causes serious health hazards. Herewith, this work introduces a highly sensitive electrochemical sensor for the sensitive detection of MAL in various environmental samples by utilizing NiO/borophene nanomaterial. The sensor was fabricated via solvothermal method and was characterized to confirm its structural and electrochemical properties. title: Leaving X: How scale insects repeatedly evolved alternatives to chromosomal sex determination
abstract: Abstract Reproduction is a core feature of life, yet it is still unclear why sex determination systems are conserved for hundreds of millions of years in some taxa but repeatedly turn over in others. A prime example is the true bugs; the vast majority of families employ a conserved X sex chromosomal system, but in scale insects (Coccomorpha), sex determination systems are more varied. Scale insects may retain X chromosomes, employ a form of haplodiploidy known as paternal genome elimination (PGE), or reproduce via selfing as simultaneous hermaphrodites. title: Numerical investigation of magnetohydrodynamic Williamson nanofluid flow through non-Darcy porous media with variable viscosity and internal heat source
abstract: Problem statement This work numerically examines the combined influence of an induced magnetic field (IMF), temperature-dependent viscosity, and internal heat generation on the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) transport of a non-Newtonian Williamson nanofluid through a non-Darcy porous medium. title: Screening and characterization of endophytic bacterial isolates associated with Echinops kebericho M. and Lepidium sativum L. and evaluation of their potential role
abstract: Endophytic bacteria (EB) associated with medicinal plants contribute to plant growth by enhancing nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and phytohormone production. This study aimed to isolate and characterize potential endophytic bacterial isolates (EBIs) from Echinops kebericho Mesfin and Lepidium sativum L., two traditional Ethiopian medicinal plants, and to evaluate their ability to utilize various growth substrates. ROS‐Responsive Micellar Delivery of Bergapten for Coordinated Attenuation of Oxidative Stress and Neuroinflammation in Neonatal Hypoxic‐Ischemic Brain Damage
abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain damage (HIBD) represents a leading contributor to neonatal death and persistent neurological impairments, yet effective therapeutic options beyond hypothermia remain limited. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and Toll-like receptor (TLR)-mediated neuroinflammation contribute to neuronal loss during hypoxic-ischemic injury. Here, a ROS-responsive antioxidant nanomicellar system (BGT@NPEP) based on an NPEP-PEG-PPG (NPEP) platform is reported for targeted delivery of the anti-inflammatory coumarin bergapten (BGT) to ischemic neonatal brain tissue.

title: Scientific Understanding Across Disciplines: In Varietate Concordia?
abstract: Abstract Understanding is a generally acknowledged aim of science, but the way in which understanding is pursued and criteria for when it is achieved differ widely across scientific disciplines. This paper offers a comparative analysis of this disciplinary variation, aimed at revealing differences as well as commonalities in methods and criteria for achieving understanding. Starting-point is the contextual theory of scientific understanding (De Regt 2017), which was developed to accommodate contextual variation in criteria for understanding.
