title: Germination Responses of Black Cumin (Nigella sativa L.) Seeds to NaCl Induced Osmotic Stress Expressed
abstract: Salinity is one of the major environmental stress factors limiting agricultural production. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of different NaCl concentrations on seed germination and early seedling development in the Çameli variety of black cumin (Nigella sativa L.). The experiment was conducted using NaCl concentrations of 0, 50, 100, 150, and 200 mM NaCl concentrations, which corresponded to osmotic potentials of 0, -0.244, -0.487, -0.731, and -0.974 MPa, respectively. title: Nutraceutical-rich oil from passion fruit by-products of beverage processing by green extraction
abstract: Processing passion fruit beverages generates substantial agro-industrial by-products that are rich in bioactive compounds. Valorizing these by-products through green extraction offers a sustainable route to transform them into high-value oils while supporting responsible food-waste reduction. title: Dual-mode (light/dark) active nanocellulose–MOF–carbon dot filters for airborne bacterial suppression in hospital environments
abstract: Airborne microbial contamination in hospitals is a major driver of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). So far, most commercial air filters capture microorganisms but do not inactivate them, and they rely on non-biodegradable polymers. Here, we engineered bio-derived nanocellulose filters from oil palm empty fruit bunches and endowed them with dual-mode (light/dark) antimicrobial activity by integrating zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and N/S-doped carbon dots immobilized on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (NS/CDs@MSN). title: Bacterial cellulose biosynthesis using native microorganisms from a mixture of non-centrifugal sugars and apple juice
abstract: Bacterial cellulose (BC) is a biopolymer with numerous potential applications, although it is associated with considerable production costs of conventional culture media. In this study, BC biosynthesis was investigated using native microorganisms from a mixture of non-centrifugal sugars (NCS) and apple juice as a low-cost alternative substrate. Sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene identified Acetobacter persici and Bacillus sp. among principal species associated with cellulose biosynthesis. title: Effect of Hybrid Castor Nutshell/Pineapple Leaf Fiber Loading on Creep Behavior of Epoxy Composites
abstract: Epoxy composites can undergo time-dependent deformation under sustained loading, limiting their dimensional stability, while agricultural residues offer potential as sustainable reinforcements. This study evaluated the effect of hybrid castor nutshell (CNS) and pineapple leaf fiber (PALF) powder loading on the displacement response and fracture-surface morphology of epoxy composites. CNS and PALF powders (75 µm) were combined at a 50:50 weight ratio and incorporated at total loadings of 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20wt%. title: Crash-loaded roll-formed multi-chamber steel sheet structures – algorithmic optimisation, manufacturing and testing
abstract: The usage of high-strength steel sheet metals in crash absorbing structures can favour efficient and lightweight designs. For multi-chamber structures made of sheet metals, roll forming is one of the most notable manufacturing methods regarding mass production. The Graph and Heuristic based Topology optimisation is a well-established software tool to optimise crash-loaded multi-chamber structures. title: Bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria as silage inoculants to reduce methane emissions in late lactation dairy cattle
abstract: Abstract Enteric fermentation in ruminants is the largest agricultural source of methane (CH₄) and contributes to global warming. Practical mitigation strategies are therefore needed for sustainable dairy production. This study evaluated a silage inoculant composed of bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains, Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis SL242 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP58 in late-lactation, spring-calving Holstein cows. title: An Introduction to the Typology of Idiomatic Phrases in the Literature of Chinese Chán Buddhism
abstract: This article examines aspects of the typology and historical development of idiomatic phrases (chéngyǔ 成語) in premodern Chinese Chán Buddhist literature, situating them within broader debates on the origins of Chinese idioms. Challenging the prevalent view that idioms primarily derive from classical written sources, the study argues—based on a large-scale database analysis—that many idioms originated in the colloquial language of a respective period and eventually were incorporated into Chán texts, or were “invented” in the context of Chán literary creativity. title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury
abstract: Abstract Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Here, we report that during early acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, hepatocytes exhibit transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. While spatial transcriptomics (ST) provided robust evidence for this arrest in the mid-zone, support for a similar arrest in pericentral hepatocytes was limited. title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
abstract: Abstract The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. abstract: Abstract Mafic and ultramafic rocks are sources of critical minerals and also provide a medium to securely store CO 2 . abstract: ABSTRACT Black soil (Mollisol), characterized by high soil organic matter (SOM), is becoming more vulnerable to extreme heat events, yet the effects of heat on decomposition of SOM, thus N 2 O emission remain unclear. abstract: Reliable foundation design for power-transmission towers in mountainous terrain requires accurate knowledge of shallow weathering and bedrock geometry, yet steep relief, irregular bedrock, and uneven weathering limit point-based drilling and conventional surveys at the approximately 22 m × 22 m tower footprint. Here, natural-source seismic frequency imaging was adapted to this setting through a multi-constrained characteristic-frequency workflow, a diagonal-crossing observation system, and terrain-adaptive acquisition. abstract: We develop a bonded-particle model for magneto-elastic rods that unifies large deformations, contact, and long-range magnetic interactions within a single discrete-element framework. abstract: Abstract Ammonia is a major contributor to eutrophication, making its reliable monitoring essential for protecting aquatic ecosystems and safeguarding water quality. Here, we report a miniaturized electrochemical platform based on a platinized Pt wire for the voltammetric determination of ammonia in natural and drinking water samples. abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. abstract: ABSTRACT Flowering plants contain a plastid-localized ɑ-amylase (AMY3) with several recognized domains: two N-terminal carbohydrate-binding modules, an alpha-alpha hairpin that binds the catalytically inactive activator β-amylase9, and a C-terminal catalytic domain. abstract: ABSTRACT In arid and semi‐arid ecosystems, burrows serve as vital sanctuaries providing wildlife shelter, nourishment, and thermal buffering. These benefits attract multiple species into confined spaces, potentially facilitating interspecific pathogen transmission. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of burrow use in Senegal's Niokolo‐Koba National Park, quantifying interspecific cohabitation, identifying influential characteristics, and documenting the potential for zoonotic pathogen transmission. abstract: OBJECTIVES: Maximum gape and bite force are two key metrics of primate craniodental performance, but without mitigating adaptations, large gapes are associated with reduced bite force. abstract: Abstract The molecular mechanisms that drive (lymph-)angiogenesis are crucial to understand diseases, such as lymphedema, that are caused due to malformations of the lymphatic vasculature. Recently, an interaction between the secreted protein Svep1, a key regulator in lymphangiogenesis, and the transmembrane receptor Tie1 was shown in zebrafish, human, and mice. title: Navigating Complexity Through Mixed Methods Research: Insights from a Large-Scale Interdisciplinary Environmental Study of Biodiversity and Human Wellbeing
abstract: This paper explores the challenge of navigating complexity within mixed methods research process, drawing on a large-scale interdisciplinary environmental project exploring the wellbeing dimensions of human interaction with woodland biodiversity. Reflecting on the design and implementation of a multiphase mixed methods project involving over 9,000 participants, we examine how complexity emerged through the phenomenon under investigation, the structure of the research design, and the collaborations through which knowledge was produced. abstract: Entrepreneurial dynamism can be fostered through either continuous energetic activity (CEA) or the introduction of new ideas (INI), both of which drive significant systemic change. abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. abstract: This study examines how Azerbaijan’s dark tourism potential can be transformed into sustainable tourism revenue by identifying key strategic and institutional factors. abstract: Pickering emulsions are stabilized by coating droplet surfaces with solid particles that provide exceptional stability and suppress coalescence. abstract: Acacia senegal is an important drought-tolerant species, but limited information exists on how vertical soil moisture affects its early growth from different provenances. abstract: This study investigates the relationship between knowledge management processes and sustainable earthquake awareness among enterprises operating in the Aydın Efeler Organized Industrial Zone (OIZ), Türkiye. abstract: Organic farming is widely associated with environmental benefits and is commonly assumed to promote soil organic carbon (SOC). abstract: Horizontal gene transfer via conjugative plasmids is a major driver of bacterial evolution. abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether sellers' religious identity functions as an observable halal signal in informal food markets when Muslim consumers have limited access to formal, verifiable halal information. abstract: The cultivation of rice (Oryza sativa L.) in flood-affected areas of Bangladesh is severely hampered by submergence stress, particularly during the Aman season. abstract: Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is an important edible legume cultivated worldwide and widely used in human nutrition. abstract: The article reconstructs the axiological profile of the aesthetic-cosmological domain of evaluation in Old English texts (7th–11th centuries) and explains its distinctive features. abstract: Uracil accumulation in DNA is a pervasive threat to genomic integrity, yet the global dynamics of how uracil overload drives genome instability remain elusive. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Cultural heritage sites represent invaluable repositories of human history and collective memory, offering visitors immersive experiences beyond conventional tourism. title: The Identity of Wild Banana from Bengkulu Revealed by Internal Transcribed Spacer Region
abstract: Wild bananas are important genetic resources, yet many populations in Indonesia remain poorly documented. This study identified a wild banana specimen from Rejang Lebong, Bengkulu, Indonesia, using morphological observations and molecular analysis of the nuclear ribosomal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region. Morphological characterization included vegetative and reproductive traits, while genomic DNA was extracted from dried leaf tissue and amplified using universal ITS primers. title: Effect of Water Curing, Interval Spraying, and Raffia-frond covering on Compressive Strength Development of Normal-Strength Concrete
abstract: Concrete curing is essential for maintaining moisture conditions required for cement hydration and compressive-strength development. This study evaluated the effects of continuous water curing, interval spraying, and raffia-frond covering on the compressive-strength development of concrete at 7, 14, 21, and 28 days. A 3 × 4 factorial experimental design comprising three curing methods and four curing ages was adopted, with three replicate specimens per treatment combination, giving a total of 36 concrete cubes. title: AN EVALUATION OF COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE LEVEL ON SPATIAL UTILIZATION IN LANDSLIDE PRONE AREAS IN NGARGOYOSO SUB DISTRICT YEAR 2025
abstract: Land-use change in Ngargoyoso District has increased due to tourism expansion. Situated on Mount Lawu's slopes with high landslide susceptibility, improper spatial utilization and low public understanding of Spatial Planning escalate disaster risks. This study aims to analyze public knowledge levels regarding spatial utilization in landslide-prone areas and its influencing factors in 2025. The research employs a descriptive quantitative approach supported by explicit qualitative data. Primary data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 99 heads of households selected via stratif
journal: Indonesian Journal of Environment and Disaster

title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. title: Museums, taxonomic uncertainty and ‘lost species’: a case study of the Critically Endangered Siau Scops Owl
abstract: Of the world's Critically Endangered (CR) and Data Deficient (DD) birds, ~27% are ‘lost species’ (lacking verified documentation for >10 years). Some may await rediscovery, and others are probably already extinct, but a few may prove never to have been valid species. Identifying these latter cases is an urgent conservation priority so as not to waste finite resources on costly and futile searches. We identify 11 ‘lost’ bird species that warrant urgent taxonomic scrutiny, including three currently assessed on the IUCN Red List as CR. abstract: Abstract In a recent study, we presented an ion-specific parametrization of the electrolyte Cubic-Plus-Association (eCPA) equation of state, which we refer to as ms-eCPA, for phase equilibria of CO2 and CH4 in six-ion multisalt brines (Na+, Cl–, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, SO42–). Here we develop the computational methods that make ms-eCPA usable in compositional reservoir simulation, and we extend it to additional gases (N2, H2, C2H6, and C3H8). title: Psychological flexibility in the work-caregiving interplay of employed family caregivers of people with dementia (DAILY-FLEX): Protocol of an experience sampling study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Employed family caregivers of people with dementia face competing work and caregiving demands that can negatively affect well-being across both domains. The Work-Home Resources model proposes that demands and resources influence cross-domain functioning through changes in personal resources. Psychological flexibility (PF), the ability to remain open to difficult experiences while acting in line with personal values, may represent a dynamic personal resource in this process. title: A multi-criteria decision framework for evaluating refinery oily sludge valorization in red ceramics
abstract: This study develops a multi-criteria decision framework for the comparative evaluation of refinery oily sludge (ROS) valorization in red ceramics. Laboratory-scale ceramic specimens containing 0, 5, and 10 wt% ROS were fired at 950°C and 1050°C. Water absorption (WA), flexural strength (FS), and thermal conductivity (TC) were integrated with study-specific indicators of clay saving (CS), water saving (WS), and theoretical ROS energy contribution (REC). title: Content and design validity of "SIKOMPOS" interactive multimedia: Integrating problem-based learning and critical-thinking processes in elementary science
abstract: This article reports expert validation during the Development stage of an ADDIE project for SIKOMPOS, an HTML5 multimedia product that embeds the five Problem-Based Learning (PBL) stages in the Grade V ecosystem learning. Each interface feature maps to one of the following: clarification, assessment, inference, or strategy. Three expert validators independently rated 33 items covering science content, PBL alignment, multimedia design, language, and critical-thinking facilitation. title: Quantum protocols for time synchronisation and distribution: a critical assessment
abstract: Precise time synchronisation underpins critical infrastructure from telecommunications and financial markets to power grids and scientific metrology. Several families of quantum protocols have been proposed and demonstrated for clock synchronisation and time distribution, exploiting entangled photon pairs, quantum key distribution (QKD) correlations, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and entangled clock networks. abstract: Background Osteosarcoma (OS), the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, commonly develops chemoresistance to conventional apoptosis-dependent therapies (e.g., doxorubicin) in metastatic/recurrent settings, leading to poor prognosis. Ferroptosis—an iron-dependent cell death pathway driven by lipid peroxidation—offers a promising alternative, yet clinical translation of synthetic inducers is limited by poor druggability. title: ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models
abstract: Background Air pollution is one of the leading global environmental health risks, associated with millions of premature deaths annually. It represents a substantial share of the global disease burden. Despite well-established epidemiological associations, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain only partially understood. There is a need for systematic approaches toward mechanistic understanding that connect particulate matter exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects. title: Active paper sheets incorporating encapsulated essential oils preserve the volatile profile of melon galia (Cucumis melo L. var. reticulatus) during storage
abstract: Galia melon ( Cucumis melo L. var. reticulatus) is a highly appreciated but perishable fruit whose characteristic aroma, mainly driven by esters, deteriorates rapidly along the cold chain. This work evaluated active paper sheets impregnated with microencapsulated essential oils (EOs) as a tool to preserve the quality of Galia melon during a simulated commercial cold chain. Melons were packaged either with the active sheet (ACT) or without it (control, CTRL) and stored for 7 days at 5 ºC (cold storage), followed by 4 days at 24 ºC (commercialization simulation), with sampling at days 0, 7 and 1

title: Recurrent Tuberculosis Among People Living with HIV in a High-Burden Setting of Andhra Pradesh, India, 2017–2023: Findings from a Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Introduction Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of mortality among people living with HIV (PLWH). Recurrent TB after successful treatment completion is associated with poor outcomes. Limited data exist on long-term post-TB treatment outcomes among PLWH in India. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3,357 PLWH aged ≥15 years who completed antituberculosis treatment (ATT) between 2017–2021 across 14 ART centers in Andhra Pradesh, India. title: High-loading rice husk valorization in recycled HDPE/PET fine–cell biocomposite foams with tailored lightweight mechanical, acoustic, and environmental performance
abstract: Rice husk is an abundant agro-industrial residue, yet achieving controlled foaming at very high biomass loading remains challenging because the reduced polymer fraction restricts cell growth and compromises mechanical integrity. This study addresses this limitation by developing fine-cell biocomposite foams containing 70 wt% rice husk in recycled high-density polyethylene/recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rHDPE/rPET) matrix. title: Hendra virus infection: Current insights into an emerging zoonotic disease
abstract: Hendra virus (HeV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic Henipavirus maintained naturally in Pteropus flying foxes, with horses serving as the principal amplifying host for recognized human infection. Since its emergence in Australia in 1994, HeV has remained geographically restricted but continues to pose substantial public-health and veterinary risks because of its high mortality, severe respiratory and neurological manifestations, and sensitivity of spillover dynamics to ecological change. title: Standardizing freshwater macroinvertebrate taxonomy: a Lithuanian operational taxa list for ecological quality assessments and biodiversity research
abstract: Taxonomic discrepancies pose a significant barrier to national data synthesis and accurate biomonitoring reporting. We compiled a standardized operational taxa list of freshwater macroinvertebrates known to occur in Lithuania, with the goal of improving comparability and ecological quality assessment reliability of biomonitoring data. A national list of freshwater macroinvertebrates was created by synthesizing literature and biomonitoring data. title: Deconstructing Partitiviridae proteins reveals the evolutionary determinants behind their origin and ecological breadth
abstract: Abstract Viruses represent a primary source of biological diversity, yet the specific mechanisms by which viral proteins shape host range remain unclear. Members of the family Partitiviridae offer a minimalist model to address this question: despite their collectively broad host range, they typically encode only an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) and a capsid protein (CP). title: Medjool Date Seed Polysaccharides Attenuate DSS‐Induced Colitis and Associated Hepatic Oxidative Injury in Mice, Accompanied by Gut Microbiota Alterations
abstract: ABSTRACT Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that is often accompanied by oxidative stress, immune imbalance, disruption of the intestinal barrier, and liver complications linked through the gut‐liver axis. In this study, we explored the protective effects of Medjool date seed polysaccharides (MDSP) in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)‐induced colitis mouse model. title: Evaluating Fermented and Non‐Fermented Lettuce‐Based Biostimulants Through a Design of Experiments Approach to Address Agronomic and Microbial Impacts in Strawberry Soilless Cultivation
abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive agriculture relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers, which contribute to green‐house gas emissions and to the degradation of soil quality and microbial biodiversity. In line with circular‐economy principles, the conversion of organic biomass into biostimulants through fermentation has emerged as a sustainable strategy to support plant performance. title: Wheat straw mulching and compost application effects on lima bean productivity, seed quality, and weed density under arid irrigated conditions
abstract: Abstract In the irrigated arid regions of Iraq, soil degradation and severe evaporative demand constrain legume productivity. Although ecological intensification using organic amendments is widely promoted, the specific mechanisms governing crop–weed–soil interactions remain poorly understood. A field experiment was conducted in Baghdad (spring‐summer 2025) using a split‐plot factorial design (3 × 3 factorial with three replications) to evaluate the individual and combined effects of wheat straw mulch (0, 5, 10 cm) and compost (1, 2, 3 t ha −1 ) on lima bean ( Phaseolus lunatus L.) performance

title: Synergistic effects of fibrolytic enzymes and lactic acid bacteria on cassava leaf silage quality and microbial community
abstract: Cassava leaves are a valuable protein-rich feed resource, but their high fiber content and poor fermentation characteristics can reduce silage quality. To address these challenges, this study evaluated the synergistic effects of fiber-degrading enzymes and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the fermentation profiles, nutritional quality, and microbial community of cassava leaf silage. title: Optimizing intra‑row spacing and seed tuber weight to enhance yield, quality, economic return, and profitability of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) in Nepal
abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is an important food and cash crop in Nepal, but its yield remains below potential partly due to suboptimal plant spacing and seed tuber size management. This study evaluated the effects of three intra-row spacings (70 × 25 cm, 70 × 35 cm, 70 × 45 cm) and three seed tuber weight classes (21-30 g, 31-40 g, 41-50 g) on growth, yield, tuber size distribution, starch yield, and economic performance of potato cv. title: Temporal Shifting of Influenza Subtype Dynamics in Pakistan Following the COVID‐19 Pandemic: A 10‐Year FluNet Analysis, 2015–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions caused unprecedented suppression of influenza circulation globally. Pakistan, with its high population density and evolving surveillance capacity, lacks long-term data on post-COVID-19 influenza patterns, essential for guiding vaccine policy. METHODS: We extracted weekly virological data for Pakistan from the WHO FluNet platform (January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024). title: Growth under mild drought: transcriptomics comparison of perennial ryegrass genotypes with differential tolerance to water deficit
abstract: Mild summer droughts rarely threaten perennial ryegrass survival, but sensitive cultivars may halt growth early, reducing yields. This study examined the transcriptomic responses to mild drought (5 days without watering) and rewatering in two genotypes with contrasting leaf growth behaviors. title: Variation in the essential oil composition of wild Artemisia absinthium from Hamadan, Iran, across phenological stages
abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate variations in the essential oil composition of a wild Artemisia absinthium population from Hamadan, Iran, across three phenological stages (pre‐flowering, flowering, and post‐flowering) using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry analysis. The essential oil profile showed variation among developmental stages, with changes in the relative abundance of major constituents and chemical groups. title: Polylactic co-glycolic acid (PLGA)-based nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract: A potential therapeutic strategy against oxidative stress and diabetes in rat model
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. abstract: Sixteen triterpenoid alkaloids, including twelve previously undescribed ones named myribuxines A–L ( 1 – 12 ), were isolated from the twigs and leaves of Buxus myrica H. Lév. To our knowledge, this species has not yet undergone any phytochemical or pharmacological investigation. title: Multimedia-integrated physics instruction: Impact on student engagement in Tanzanian secondary schools
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of multimedia integration on student attitudes and engagement in physics education in Tanzanian secondary schools. A convergent mixed-methods case study was conducted in four government schools in Mbeya Region with 96 Form Two students and two physics teachers. Grounded in Mayer’s cognitive theory of multimedia learning and Vygotsky’s social constructivism, the eight-lesson intervention used PhET simulations, videos, and animations on sustainable energy sources. title: Self-powered neural intervention via piezoelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are electromechanical energy-conversion devices constructed from piezoelectric materials. They convert physiological motion, local tissue deformation, or externally applied mechanical stimuli into localized electrical signals and have attracted considerable interest in self-powered neural interventions. title: Closing the loop: business model and feasibility study for a standalone paper recycling unit in Egyptian universities
abstract: Abstract Universities generate substantial volumes of paper waste, yet much of this valuable resource remains underutilized despite increasing commitments to circular economy and sustainable campus initiatives. Paper recycling within university campuses has the potential to reduce solid waste generation, lowering paper procurement costs, and supporting sustainability-focused education. title: Abundance and species diversity of mosquitoes (Diptera, Culicidae) in endemic areas for arboviruses in the Eastern Amazon, Brazil
abstract: Combating the spread of arboviruses in the Amazon relies on understanding the diversity of Culicidae, particularly potential vectors. Areas with historical records of vector occurrence provide crucial insights into the factors driving epidemic emergence. Furthermore, anthropogenic activities, such as deforestation and demographic pressure on the forest, are considered the primary drivers of new outbreaks, creating a scenario of high ecological receptivity for pathogens of public health concern. title: Informalidad laboral, calidad del empleo y vulnerabilidad económica en México: evidencia territorial de las entidades federativas
abstract: Labour informality is a structural constraint preventing high employment levels in Mexico from translating into economic well-being. This study analyses the relationship between labour informality, job quality and economic vulnerability across Mexico’s 32 federal entities. A quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive-comparative design with a longitudinal perspective is used, drawing on the National Survey of Occupation and Employment and INEGI’s labour poverty measurement. title: Analysing resource management outcomes: an actor-centred power approach
abstract: This paper presents an adapted methodological Interest-Power-Outcome (IPO) framework for analysing environmental resource management outcomes by integrating the Actor-Centred Power (ACP) framework with Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA). The framework aims to analyse how actors involved in resource management use their power in pursuit of specific interests, and how their interventions on the ground can either align with or diverge from intended policy outcomes in a resource system. title: Shaping biodiversity from within: How experts' perceptions of values, rules and knowledges influence biodiversity assessment
abstract: Abstract While biodiversity conservation has had its local success, worldwide biodiversity loss continues rapidly. Despite the push towards more inclusive and equitable approaches, conservation practices often reinforce existing conceptualizations of biodiversity, excluding other ways of knowing and valuing nature. This paper explores the process of assessing biodiversity among a group of habitat experts. Our study contributes to the literature with empirical understanding of the tension between objective and more pluralistic, relational understandings of biodiversity among a group of experts.

title: When carbon counts differ: the complexities of biogenic carbon accounting in BECCUS and why accounting choices matter
abstract: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for system-wide emissions and removals. However, lifecycle assessment, national greenhouse gas inventories and carbon-market frameworks apply differing accounting approaches, producing divergent mitigation estimates. title: Emissions variability of greenhouse gases within and between sites during late‐season corn production in Mississippi
abstract: Abstract Variability of greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes and emissions among replicates in a study area can have an impact on results depending on the statistical tools used to assess significant differences among fixed effects. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of site and time (i.e., date) and the variability within and between sites on soil GHG (carbon dioxide [CO 2 ], methane [CH 4 ], and nitrous oxide [N 2 O]) fluxes and emissions from two fields under the same management practices during late‐season corn ( Zea mays ) production in Mississippi. abstract: ABSTRACT Larvae of Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) can cause complete defoliation of Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl., commonly known as bottle gourd, resulting in substantial yield losses in India. title: Paper waste derived cellulose nanofluids for enhanced oil recovery in high temperature high salinity sandstone reservoirs
abstract: Conventional enhanced oil recovery (EOR) methods often exhibit reduced efficiency under high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) reservoir conditions, necessitating sustainable and high-performance alternatives. This study investigated cellulose nanoparticles (CNPs), defined as nanoscale cellulose particles derived from paper waste, for HTHS EOR applications. title: Investigating the effects of dexmedetomidine in cecal ligation and puncture‑induced septic rats
abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality, and ferroptosis has been implicated in sepsis-associated organ injury. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an α2-adrenergic agonist with anti-inflammatory properties, may modulate this process. We examined whether DEX protects against cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)– induced septic lung injury and alters ferroptosis-associated markers in rats. title: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development
abstract: Maternal perceived stress, mental health, and physiological dysregulation during pregnancy can alter the intrauterine environment, shaping infant development through fetal programming processes. Nonetheless, few longitudinal studies in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have jointly examined psychological and biological factors in relation to infant outcomes. title: Migration and the Geography of Life Expectancy: Selective Sorting and Spatial Dependence Across 172 Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT International migration has grown rapidly in recent decades, yet its relationship with population health is difficult to disentangle from the economic, structural and geographic characteristics of the places migrants move to. This study examines whether international migration is associated with population‐level life expectancy after accounting for confounding and the data's spatial structure. abstract: The peak onset of mental disorders occurs during adolescence; therefore, youth mental health conditions have become a major global public health concern, imposing substantial social and economic burdens. Depression and anxiety exhibit distinct developmental and sex-specific patterns, and prior studies indicate that teacher-student relationships and screen time significantly influence school-aged children's mental health conditions. title: Hide and Skin Preservation in Ethiopia: Traditional Practices, Improved Techniques, Quality Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Hides and skins are important livestock by-products and the principal raw materials for Ethiopia’s leather and leather-products industries. Their value, however, depends not only on the number of animals slaughtered but also on how promptly and correctly the pelts are removed, preserved, stored and transported before tanning. abstract: Hybrid seed production in chili is more efficient when using male-sterile plants. Indonesia possesses a wide range of commercial hybrid chili pepper varieties that can serve as alternative sources of CMS genetic resources. abstract: This paper extends the concept of regional resilience to address economic inactivity as a key economic outcome, and to consider health and demography as sources of regional vulnerability and resilience. Economic inactivity in Great Britain rose sharply following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, but in geographically uneven ways. abstract: African horse sickness (AHS) is a severe, vector-borne viral disease of equids associated with high mortality and substantial socioeconomic losses. This study aimed to describe the temporal, seasonal, and spatial distribution of reported AHS outbreaks and assess vaccination coverage in North Shewa Zone, Ethiopia. abstract: Invasive plants are species introduced outside their natural range and often cause ecological or economic harm. We investigated its genetic diversity in Western Polesie, Poland, and assessed larval microbiota and mycobiota. Mitochondrial COI and 16 S rRNA, and nuclear ITS1 markers of B. schneideri were analyzed using haplotype and nucleotide diversity estimates, Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, and median-joining networks. abstract: Abstract Radical-pair-based magnetic compass mechanisms are believed to depend on spin-selective reaction pathways modulated by the Earth’s magnetic field. This study aimed to characterize the hydroethanolic extract of T. willdenowii and evaluate its antioxidant, antimicrobial, antifungal, and insecticidal activities. abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common heart disease of cats and is conventionally characterised by its ventricular phenotype. The clinical events that determine quality and duration of life in affected cats, however, are atrial in their proximate pathophysiology. abstract: This study investigates discursive borderwork in online communication about the war in Ukraine. It examines how borders are drawn through the dynamics of nomination and stancetaking and their relationship to identity construction at both the micro scale of individual references and the macro scale of single comments and interactional exchanges. abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric scaffolds can conform to irregular bone defects and deliver wireless electrical stimulation, yet whether their mechanical and electrical functions persist throughout the months-long course of bone remodeling, as well as whether the regenerated bone ultimately recovers load-bearing function, remains unresolved. abstract: BIFLEX is a flexible underactuated gripper inspired by the human thumb–index pair and designed for distal precision pinch and proximal adaptive holding. Building on a previously developed soft-hybrid Fin-Ray finger, this study combines finger-geometry optimization, four-bar kinematic synthesis, and shared single-motor actuation through a four-bar and tendon–pulley transmission. abstract: Abstract Background To reveal the physiological mechanism by which exogenous indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and 6-benzyladenine (6-BA) regulate sprout number in stumped Pinus yunnanensis seedlings, optimize hormone application schemes, and provide a theoretical basis for its asexual cutting propagation, this study adopted a two-factor three-level completely randomized block design. abstract: Soil fertility depletion caused by declining organic matter and imbalanced nutrient inputs is a major constraint to barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) production in the Ethiopian highlands. A field experiment was conducted during the 2022/2023 main cropping season at Holeta Agricultural Research Center, Ethiopia, to evaluate the effects of integrating nitrogen fertilizer, vermicompost, and farmyard manure on soil properties and barley productivity under a randomized complete block design with three replications. title: UAV-based CWSI estimation for tomato water stress monitoring
abstract: Thermal infrared (TIR) imaging has been widely applied as a prominent remote sensing technique to assess plant water conditions. Recent advances in TIR imaging, primarily the use of high-resolution TIR cameras mounted on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their integration with water-sensitive indicators, have further enhanced its applicability for crop water stress monitoring. abstract: Strawberries are valued for their sweet-sour taste, color, and aroma. abstract: Abstract Soil is a non-renewable natural resource essential for supporting plants, animals, and microorganisms. abstract: Green hydrogen production through renewable-powered water splitting is pivotal for achieving net-zero carbon emissions. abstract: Abstract Drought stress poses a significant threat to agricultural productivity, particularly in regions with limited water availability. abstract: In Rwanda, smallholder dairy farmers are increasingly experiencing the effects of changing weather patterns, which influence pasture availability, water resources, and milk production. abstract: Wildfires pose an escalating environmental, economic, and social threat in the Peruvian Andes. This study examines wildfire disaster risk management (DRM) across seven Andean regions, assessing legal frameworks, institutional actions, and the integration of Integrated Fire Management (IFM). abstract: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. abstract: Emotions are widely invoked to motivate climate action, yet how different forms of emotional activation translate into costly, real-world pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) remains unclear. This study examines whether positive emotions triggered by (i) recalling past PEB and (ii) engaging with environmental social media content increase subsequent donations to an environmental NGO. title: Beyond degrees Celsius: Mapping competing justice scenarios in Australia's energy transition
abstract: The energy transition is routinely framed as a technical challenge. But transitions are socio-political undertakings. The struggle over what counts as a “just transition” is a struggle over what a liveable future should look like. Facts alone cannot settle this dilemma because the struggle rests on competing ideas about what a just transition is for . abstract: Climate-induced water stress is projected to hamper soybean yield and seed/grain quality globally, unless climate adaptive management practices are adopted. abstract: Deforestation and intensifying extreme climatic events are reshaping ecosystem functioning globally and increasing the risk of crossing tipping points in social-ecological systems. abstract: This article addresses the question of what financial resources are available to the world’s most climate exposed and vulnerable countries, and how this fits within and contributes to the broader South-South financial landscape. It presents original empirical data and institutional analysis to show new trends where emerging Southern-led public banks and financial institutions are deepening and broadening the global financial architecture, and why they feel compelled to do it. abstract: Abstract Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze, represents a commercially significant crop, primarily recognized for its pharmacologically active secondary metabolites, including catechins and caffeine. abstract: Abstract: Background: Nanoparticles have gained considerable attention as versatile platforms for the diagnosis and treatment of different diseases, particularly cancer. Lipid-coated hybrid nanoparticles (LCHNPs), comprising a polymeric core enveloped by a lipid shell, offer improved targeting and potential solutions for multidrug-resistant cancers. abstract: ABSTRACT The Dinaric karst encompasses a network of over 10,000 caves and represents one of the world's most important subterranean biodiversity hotspots. abstract: Comprehensive Summary Stretchy organic solar cells require active layers that can not only tolerate large tensile deformation but also resist crack propagation after damage initiation. title: Land fragmentation, tenure insecurity, and irrigation water management in Egypt: a hybrid review and sensitivity analysis
abstract: Egypt has one of the tightest water budgets in the world, while its farmland has been divided into ever-smaller holdings for a century. This paper connects these two issues by pairing a structured literature review with a transparent sensitivity analysis based on Egyptian census data and Nile Delta field studies. It asks how holding size and tenure affect irrigation water application, and how much of the excess consolidation might recover. abstract: The Starry Night : whether its sky represents spontaneous fantasy or a realist depiction has gone unanswered for over a century. abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is increasingly displacing rural populations, and migration may reduce economic losses from environmental stress. However, climate events and migration can also entail social and psychological costs overlooked by economic measures. This paper examines the relationship between climate events and life satisfaction in Bangladesh and whether migration mediates this relationship. abstract: Psychiatric pharmacotherapy is among the most widely practiced and epistemically contested domains of contemporary medicine. abstract: This paper examines how physical disaster risk affects sovereign debt distress in emerging and developing economies. Using a Generalized Panel Smooth Transition Regression model, I show that the sovereign consequences of storms and earthquakes are strongly state-dependent. abstract: Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), commonly used as the sodium salt (NaCMC) and also known as cellulose gum, carmellose or E466, is an ionic cellulose ether widely used in foods, pharmaceuticals, drilling fluids, detergents, paper products and lithium-ion battery slurries. abstract: This contribution argues that language, as well as individual languages, are not autonomous objects merely described by epistemic practices. abstract: There is a lack of consensus regarding the diagnosis and treatment of bacterial pyelonephritis (PN) in dogs and cats. abstract: The Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) Programme is a flagship initiative of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), aimed at identifying and preserving Agricultural Heritage Systems for future generations. abstract: Air pollution is increasingly recognized as an important environmental factor associated with immune dysfunction and disease susceptibility. This narrative review critically synthesizes current evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which airborne pollutants may alter immune homeostasis and influence adaptive resilience. abstract: Recent elections in the United States have seen online rumors become a regular feature of election discourse as voters and election officials work to navigate a sea of digitally spread claims and propaganda. For the uninitiated, these rumors can feel overwhelming and random, sowing doubt about the integrity and legitimacy of recent elections. abstract: Disaster research in high-income settings shows that better-resourced communities see population inflows and faster recovery, while disadvantaged communities suffer prolonged population loss. abstract: Equal participation in co-located discussion is important for effective collaboration, yet people often hold back when they anticipate negative interpersonal or professional consequences, especially when raising a point requires voicing it themselves. abstract: Agent harnesses enable large language models to act through tools, observe the results, and iteratively work toward a task goal. abstract: Models of injection-induced aseismic slip commonly assume uniform in-situ stresses along the fault, and thus predict rupture growth symmetric about the injection point. title: Hyaluronic acid over-expression drives tissue architecture in both healthy and diseased states
abstract: Tissue architecture is shaped by a variety of biomechanical and biochemical mechanisms, including morphogen patterning, differential growth, and spatial variations in cellular contractility. These mechanisms typically emphasize forces generated within cells. Here, we explore a complementary mechanism in which intercellular space itself exerts forces that shape tissue architecture. abstract: Accurate optical characterization of high-albedo scattering media is fundamentally limited by integrating-sphere measurement errors. Scattering events spatially redistribute photons, leading to lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias measured reflectance and transmittance. title: LesionStudio: A Patient-Informed Platform for Task-Specific Optimization of Emission Tomography Reconstruction and Analysis
abstract: Purpose: For task-specific PET and SPECT reconstruction optimization, we developed LesionStudio, an open-source platform incorporating patient background heterogeneity, realistic lesion morphology and texture, and lesion-background interactions beyond conventional phantoms. Methods: LesionStudio, a Python framework built on PyTomography, inserts lesions into PET/SPECT data using modality-specific forward projection and stochastic background ablation. title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. title: Light-Cone Friedel Oscillations: a Window into van Hove Superconductivity
abstract: Van Hove (vH) singularities can enhance superconductivity by generating a large pairing susceptibility. Yet, it remains challenging to experimentally establish whether pairing really occurs near these points. We show that the saddle-point dispersion near a vH point gives rise to a `light-cone' vH-selective behavior of Friedel oscillations, which is drastically different from the familiar concentric circles. Each vH point maps onto its own real-space light-cone sector, allowing STM around a single impurity to measure whether---and how strongly---that saddle-point quasiparticle sector is gapped.

abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks, but the origin of their angular momentum remains uncertain. title: Language Scent: Exploring Cross-Language Information Navigation
abstract: While multilingual users often switch between languages when seeking information, this process remains undersupported by current systems where information is typically siloed by language. Our formative study reveals that users select their search language based on its perceived value for their current information need, a concept we formalize as language scent. abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. abstract: Audio dramas weave dialogue, sound effects, and music into immersive stories. Creators often adapt books into audio dramas, but this process remains labor-intensive, requiring them to interpret source material, author scripts, generate audio assets, and assemble them on a timeline. abstract: The Burrows-Wheeler transform (BWT) is the core of many compressed full-text indexes and most read aligners. abstract: Measures of urban expansion quantify land consumption but obscure how separated settlements coalesce. We examine India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975-2025) using percolation-like analysis. Critical distances marking the largest settlement-merger events contracted in 47 cities, the median falling 46% from 650 to 350m. abstract: Resonance-induced excessive vibrations can degrade performance, reduce reliability, and shorten the service life of engineering structures. To reduce the risk of resonance, structural natural frequencies are generally engineered to be shifted away from excitation frequencies. title: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment
abstract: The simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem arises in multi-robot applications such as perimeter security and environmental monitoring, where robots must survey a region of interest and coordinate to enclose targets once they are detected. Surveillance favors spatial dispersion for coverage, whereas containment requires target-centric cohesion for enclosure. abstract: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many models now supporting generation conditioned on multiple reference images and textual instructions. abstract: This paper analyzes the sustainability of the marine insurance market in the Black Sea region amid ongoing geopolitical instability and an escalating risk environment. title: Updated Estimates of Radiocarbon‐Based Deep Ocean Circulation Age
abstract: Abstract The deep ocean circulation age based on radiocarbon was last determined almost 20 years ago, when digital archiving was not standard practice. title: Genomic changes revealed by repeated sampling of kelp exposed to an extreme marine heatwave
abstract: Abstract Extreme climatic events are increasingly recognised as potent evolutionary forces, imposing sudden pressures on natural populations. While their ecological impacts are well documented, the genomic consequences remain less clear. abstract: Abstract. Mesoscale eddies are a fundamental component of ocean circulation and play a crucial role in shaping the three-dimensional distribution of ocean temperature and salinity. However, observational constraints have long limited systematic, global-scale quantification of eddy-induced thermohaline variability. abstract: Ballast water management (BWM) supports vessel stability while preventing the transfer of harmful aquatic organisms and pathogens. title: A multivariate analysis framework for interpreting long-term zooplankton community dynamics
abstract: Multivariate analyses are widely used to characterize plankton community dynamics in long-term datasets, which often exhibit sparse sampling. These datasets typically require multiple multivariate approaches to describe patterns in community structure, relate those patterns to environmental variation, and identify the taxa contributing to observed differences. title: Rebuilding the ship at sea: crisis politics and EU polity formation since 2008
abstract: The European Union has been in crisis on an ongoing basis since 2008. A wealth of scholarship has charted the contours of the crisis period, often emphasising the EU’s institutional weaknesses and tendency towards sub-optimal or incomplete solutions. Yet the EU has also proven capable of resilience, marshalling both policy and political resources to ‘rebuild the ship at sea’. To understand the cumulative consequences of the post-2008 period for the EU we must understand it as a compound polity, bringing together analyses of both fragility and resilience into a coherent account. abstract: Journalism plays a vital role in shaping how societies interpret and legitimize global environmental controversies. This study compares how Chinese and U.S. media discursively frame China’s distant-water fishing (DWF)—a domain where environmental, economic, and geopolitical interests intersect. title: Navigating a Critical Issue: The Legal Status of the Strait of Hormuz in International Law
abstract: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and is indispensable to international energy trade. Its legal status remains contested because Iran signed but did not ratify the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), while Oman is a party. This article examines three questions: the treaty and customary rules governing passage; the rights and duties of coastal, belligerent, and neutral states during armed conflict; and the implications for maritime security and economic stability. abstract: Liquefied-hydrogen (LH₂) carriers and hydrogen-fuelled ships operate cryogenic systems near −253°C, far below the −183°C boiling point of oxygen, so that atmospheric oxygen can condense as an oxygen-enriched liquid on cold surfaces. abstract: Abstract. The global ocean absorbs a significant portion of anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions. Tracking the fate of absorbed CO2 and its impacts requires an internally consistent global observational dataset spanning decades. abstract: Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose tests dissolved) are not always present in sediment samples. Identifying where FOLs are preserved is a necessary first step towards determining what promotes their development and burial. abstract: Rynchops albicollis, commonly referred to as the Indian Skimmer or Indian Scissors-bill, is the only skimmer species found in the Indian subcontinent. Its small global population, with 2,450–2,900 mature individuals, is experiencing a continuous decline, and the species was up-listed to ‘Endangered’ by the IUCN Red List in 2020. title: Assessing biodiversity responses to climate change in South Africa using National Living Planet Index
abstract: South Africa’s biodiversity is increasingly threatened by climate change, yet system-specific impacts across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems remain under-quantified. This study examined whether rising surface air temperatures are statistically associated with vertebrate population trends, using a reweighted National Living Planet Index (LPI) to represent ecological change. abstract: Abstract Reducing threats to sea turtle eggs and hatchlings is critical for increasing hatching survival and recruitment, which supports the recovery of sea turtle populations. However, changes in temperature and rainfall from climate change have been identified as emergent risks to the nesting success of sea turtles globally. abstract: This systematic literature review examines the implementation and impact of the Indonesia Education Report Card (Rapor Pendidikan) within the Merdeka Belajar (Freedom to Learn) framework. abstract: Rivers play a central role in the global distribution of plastic pollution. Despite recent research showing that the majority of plastic is not transported to the sea, most plastic transport models have not explicitly included plastic retention in rivers. abstract: The article examines Polish political parties’ reactions to the war in Ukraine. The statements of Polish decision-makers and opposition demonstrate that, contrary to expectations derived from literature, the ‘rally round the flag’ effect was short and the war became quickly politicized. abstract: Casuarina equisetifolia L. is a key pioneer tree species for coastal shelterbelt plantations in tropical and subtropical regions. However, long-term reliance on a limited number of superior clones has narrowed its genetic base and reduced stress resistance, which necessitates the selection of elite individuals and the construction of molecular identities to support precise germplasm identification. title: Selected Trace Metals in Four Major Surface-Water Reservoirs of the Houston Metropolitan Area
abstract: This technical note reports selected trace metals in four major surface-water reservoirs associated with the Houston metropolitan region. Shoreline surface-water samples from Lake Houston, Lake Livingston, Lake Conroe, and Clear Lake were analyzed for As, Cd, Cu, Pb, Ni, and Zn by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) following U.S. EPA Method 200.8 quality-control procedures. abstract: Nigeria’s estuarine waterfronts illustrate a persistent governance failure in which regeneration is pursued through demolition rather than negotiated upgrading. abstract: Microplastic pollution has become a widespread environmental concern due to the extensive use of plastic materials and their persistence in environment and possible interaction with biota. Microplastics are generally considered to be small pieces of plastic particles with a size less than 5 mm and they can originate either from fragmentation of larger plastic debris or from direct emissions from industrial, waste and consumer products. abstract: Coastal and offshore fisheries play a vital role in the Pacific Island economies, food security and cultural heritage. While the past two decades has seen increased recognition of gender dimensions of fisheries, managers, practitioners and industry partners have not yet tackled the problem of gender‐based violence (GBV) in the sector. abstract: Ukraine has long been one of the leading suppliers of qualified seafarers to the world merchant fleet. Most Ukrainian seafarers serve on foreign-flagged vessels, and their earnings are a significant source of foreign currency for the national economy. The introduction of martial law in 2022 created a governance dilemma for the state. Men of military age face restrictions on leaving the country, and the state has mobilization needs. title: Splice seeding as an alternative to conventional twine-wrapping for Saccharina latissima cultivation: biomass yield, substrate efficiency, and commercial implications
abstract: Abstract As the emerging temperate kelp industry seeks to scale in the west, established seeding methodologies, principally twine and direct seeding, present persistent bottlenecks in hatchery costs, space requirements, and operational reliability. This study evaluates splice seeding, a precision-spacing technique common in East Asian kelp aquaculture, as an alternative approach for Saccharina latissima cultivation. Seeded twine was cut into 3 cm sections and manually inserted into 12 mm twisted cultivation ropes at 5, 10, and 20 cm intervals; conventional twine-wrapping served as the control.

title: Arthropods communities in organic orchards and adjacent hedgerows on Terceira Island (Azores, Portugal): a dataset supporting biological control research
abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. title: Compound-Specific Carbon and Hydrogen Isotope Fingerprinting Resolves Dominant PAH Sources in Sediments from a Major Shipyard Harbor
abstract: Abstract Accurate source discrimination of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in industrialized coastal sediments remains challenging because multiple pyrogenic sources often exhibit overlapping molecular signatures. Despite frequent elevated PAH contamination in sediments near shipyards, the dominant sources remain poorly constrained. In this study, compound-specific dual isotope analysis (δ13C and δ2H) was applied to surface sediments from Okpo Harbor, a major shipbuilding center in South Korea. abstract: Abstract. Satellite altimetry has successfully monitored inland waters for more than 30 years and is increasingly important as the demand for freshwater grows and climate change accelerates. Launched in December 2022, the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite is the first to provide 2D spatially distributed elevation measurements, with a 21-day revisit time and better coverage depending on latitude and a nominal requirement to detect lakes as small as 0.06 km2. title: Vertical Distribution and Regression Modelling of PM2.5 under Seasonal Meteorological Influences in Visakhapatnam
abstract: Urban growth and expansion have aggravated the volume of fine particulate matter pollution, especially in the high-rise cities. The present research examines the vertical distributions of PM2.5 in the city of Visakhapatnam, in India. It is the centre of industrial manufacturing, vehicular operations in the city, with regular air quality control exceeding the threshold of air quality standards. The observation of data was conducted from roof top of buildings, which are at different levels of 35m and above to 150m in two urban areas in the summer and winter seasons. title: RRBF-KMA: high-resolution radar–gauge merged precipitation dataset for South Korea (2016–2024)
abstract: Abstract. This study presents a long-term, high-resolution precipitation dataset over South Korea generated by merging nationwide composite radar reflectivity with dense rain gauge observations from the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). The dataset provides precipitation at 10-minute temporal resolution and 0.5 km spatial resolution on a regular grid of 2305 × 2881 pixels, covering the period from 2016 to 2024. abstract: Rickettsia species are arthropod-hosted endosymbionts classified into phylogenetic and serological groups, heterogeneous concerning their ecologies. This study aims to screen ticks and mites deposited in the Acarological Collection at Center of Taxonomical Collections at Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais, Brazil, for rickettsial occurrences, making available genetic data on hosts and bacteria. abstract: BACKGROUND: A highly sensitive spectrofluorimetric method was developed for the determination of delafloxacin based on fluorescence derivatization with 9-fluorenyl methyl chloroformate (FMOC-Cl). The derivatization reaction was performed at room temperature in borate buffer (pH 8.0), producing a strongly fluorescent derivative suitable for sensitive quantitative analysis. title: Service connection for posttraumatic stress disorder following military sexual trauma: Impacts of military rank and branch on claim award denial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Military sexual trauma (MST) is a pervasive issue among U.S. service members that often leads to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). After separation, Veterans may file service connection claims with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) for MST-related PTSD to access compensation and health care. Claims are reviewed, assessed by clinicians through forensic interviews, and rated to determine eligibility. title: Comparative Assessment of Climate Change Impacts and Farmers’ Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices in Tropical Crops Production Systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens tropical crop production through erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events that reduce crop productivity and disrupt farm management. This study assessed climate change impacts and farmers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) across banana, cassava, and mixed-cropping systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines. abstract: INTRODUCTION. title: The Maya Preclassic in the mid‐elevations of tropical Mexico
abstract: ABSTRACT The Mesoamerican Preclassic period offers a laboratory for understanding how interactions between climate and early human occupation have shaped tropical ecosystems. Although the environmental history of the Maya lowlands during this period is relatively well known, mid‐elevation regions remain poorly understood. Here, we present a multiproxy sedimentary analysis from Lake Nahá, tropical mountains of southeastern Mexico, to elucidate climate–human interactions. title: Improved Constraints on the Surface of LHS 3844 b from Its Mid-infrared Spectrum
abstract: Abstract The thermal emission spectra of terrestrial exoplanets provide a window into their surface compositions and corresponding geological processes. Close-in rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs are ideal targets for these studies, as observations have shown that most have little to no atmosphere. LHS 3844 b is an ultrashort-period super-Earth orbiting a nearby M dwarf, and is the most favorable target that does not have a dayside magma ocean. abstract: This study assessed the implementation of multilevel support systems and context-based pedagogical interventions to address foundational literacy and numeracy gaps across five public elementary and secondary schools in the Third Congressional District, Division of Leyte, during School Year 2026–2027. title: Redescription of Uranoscopus bicinctus Temminck and Schlegel 1843 (Teleostei: Uranoscopidae): an integrative approach resolves taxonomic uncertainty related to variation in body colouration and oral luring organ
abstract: Abstract The highest diversity of the family Uranoscopidae (commonly known as stargazers) is in the Indo-Pacific. Many guidebooks and studies from the region have found the number and identification of species to be difficult to determine, especially in the genus Uranoscopus . abstract: Abstract Climate change is increasing the frequency, severity and persistence of droughts, particularly in Mediterranean‐type ecosystems, where seasonal water limitation strongly constrains forest canopy condition and ecosystem functioning. Satellite‐derived vegetation indices provide a valuable approach for assessing canopy‐level responses to drought over broad spatial and temporal scales. title: Isopycnal Pathway for Small‐Particle Export in a Decaying Cyclonic Eddy Revealed by a BGC‐Argo Float
abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies influence carbon export through production, subduction, mixing, and particle redistribution. title: Authentic Deeds And Notarial Accountability In Fisheries Vessel Transactions
abstract: Illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing is commonly addressed through patrols, vessel monitoring, licensing controls, and criminal enforcement. These measures remain incomplete when the legal identity and ownership history of a vessel cannot be verified. This article examines the legal function of authentic deeds in fisheries-vessel transactions and clarifies the accountability of Indonesian notaries within an ownership-transparency framework. title: Against the tide: law, illegality and the everyday in Corrubedo
abstract: Abstract ‘Corrubedo’ is one of many stories Ben Judah tells in This is Europe: The Way We Live Now . It follows Graña, a fisherman from the titular Galician town who, faced with the erosion of his community, is forced to answer what Martha Nussbaum terms a ‘tragic question’ and joins the crew of Kunlun , a vessel sailing to Antarctica to poach Patagonian toothfish. title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of a bryozoan-associated microbial complex from the Hanjiang River, China
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bryozoans are ancient colonial animals that have existed for over 470 million years and are widely distributed across aquatic environments. Recently, many spherical colloids (average diameter≈1 meter in diameter), containing bryozoans and diverse microorganisms, were found in the Hanjiang river in China. In this study, we investigated these bryozoan-dominated microbial complexes using metagenomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and complementary approaches. title: Comparative assessment of phytoplankton community using different filtration methods based on environmental DNA metabarcoding—a case study of Caohai Wetland
abstract: In environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, the choice of filter membrane material and pore size governs DNA enrichment, detection sensitivity, and taxonomic representativeness of aquatic communities. This study employed eDNA metabarcoding to evaluate the influence of various filter membranes on the phytoplankton community within Caohai Wetland. Four membrane materials with a pore size of 0.22 μm were tested: mixed cellulose esters (MCE), polyethersulfone (PES), nylon (NY), and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and three pore sizes were tested with the MCE membranes: 0.22 μm, 0.45 μm, and 0.8 μm.

title: DRY FISH MARKETS IN INDIA: TRADE PERFORMANCE, PRICE TRENDS AND MARKET CHALLENGES
abstract: The paper mainly centered upon dryfish outlets in India. It has found that dried fish market in India is a key part of the fisheries industry providing income to producers traders manufacturers and consumers. It is marked by limited production, price differences across regions, several ways of taking goods to markets, and the increase of both domestic demand and exports. Primary hurdles relate to the lack of storage, poor sanitation, difficult transportation, changing prices, and underdeveloped markets. title: Paralytic shellfish toxin production in Alexandrium minutum (Dinophyceae): Insights from omics integration using toxigenic and nontoxigenic recombinant progeny
abstract: Paralytic shellfish toxins (PSTs) are produced by certain species of cyanobacteria and dinoflagellates. Part of the PST biosynthetic pathway has been elucidated in cyanobacteria, and the implication of some sxt genes has been confirmed by experimental studies. Contrary to cyanobacteria, knowledge about PST biosynthesis in dinoflagellates is more limited and generally restricted to comparative studies with the cyanobacterial pathway. title: UAV monitoring of geomorphic trajectories in foredune resilience
abstract: Barrier islands function as dynamic buffers that reorganize under chronic and episodic forcing. Foredune morphology reflects the balance between gradual wind-driven growth and rapid wave-induced erosion, but this coupled response is difficult to resolve with infrequent, high-cost LiDAR surveys. Here, we use high-resolution UAV photogrammetry to track foredune change on Jekyll Island, Georgia. title: Recruitment of fishers and international law violations
abstract: Recruitment (or manning) agencies are critical actors in sourcing workers for fishing vessels, especially in Asia. While studies have demonstrated the human rights abuses and labour rights violations to which fishers (especially migrant fishers) are subjected, less focus has been accorded to the role of recruitment agencies and their potential violations of international law. title: Sovereignty and meteorology: China, France, and the 1932 Xisha Islands dispute
abstract: An intense debate broke out between China and France over the sovereignty of the Xisha Islands in the early 1930s, in which meteorology played a key role. Scholars have paid increasing attention to the relationship between science and politics; this article demonstrates the multifaceted role of meteorology in asserting sovereignty in the context of East Asian international politics. The establishment of a meteorological observatory on the Xisha Islands was designed to demonstrate China’s administrative control over the territory, and to reinforce its sovereignty. title: Finfish intake is associated with persistent chemical burden and a PFAS-mediated pathway to γ-glutamyltransferase in Korean adults
abstract: Abstract Seafood carries nutrients and persistent chemicals in the same meal, yet population studies have treated it as one food group. title: Polystyrene Microplastics Impair Cellular Immune Responses in Galleria mellonella Following Controlled Internal Exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are emerging environmental contaminants with increasing evidence of immunotoxic effects in invertebrates; however, their underlying cellular mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated whether short‐term internal exposure to 1 μm polystyrene microplastics affects immune and oxidative responses in Galleria mellonella . title: Characterization of microplastics in human seminal fluid by absorption-reflection infrared spectrometry
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants that pose a potential risk to both environmental and human health. These polymeric particles, smaller than 5 mm, can be taken up and distributed within the human body, reaching the reproductive system. This study focuses on the detection and characterization of MPs in human seminal fluid using absorption-reflection infrared spectrometry, enabling precise identification of polymer type, morphology, composition, shape and particle size. abstract: Reservoir sediments accumulate potentially toxic elements from both catchment weathering and human activity, and concentration-based indices regularly confound the two. abstract: Biodiversity refers to the structural, functional and evolutionary variability among living organisms across genetic, species and ecosystem hierarchical tiers. abstract: Abstract. Explosive volcanic sulfur emissions into the stratosphere form sulfate aerosol particles which are an important driver of climate variability. Volcanic sulfur emissions are required both by climate models using interactive stratospheric aerosol schemes, as well as simpler volcanic aerosol models typically used to provide stratospheric aerosol optical properties for climate models which cannot simulate stratospheric aerosols interactively from precursor emissions. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Pakistan consumes an estimated 500 million disposable pens annually, generating roughly 2,300 tonnes of unrecovered plastic waste.
