abstract: Despite increasing interest in inland fisheries as a means of supporting food security, livelihoods, and rural development, inland fisheries in South Africa remain poorly integrated into food systems, with significant uncertainty regarding supply chains, consumer demand, and product quality. We assessed the market feasibility of sharptooth catfish (Clarias gariepinus) harvested through the Darlington Alien Fish Harvest Project in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. title: Do tripwires deter? How small forward deployments contribute to deterrence
abstract: Forward-deployed tripwire forces are one tool used to enhance the credibility of security guarantees. Cold War conventional wisdom holds that these vulnerable deployments improve deterrence by increasing the credibility of the sending state’s commitment to fight to defend the host, but recent scholarship has challenged their effectiveness. These new critiques argue that because tripwire forces lack capability, and publics do not punish leaders who back down, they do not deter. abstract: ABSTRACT ‘What we teach is true to us’, one social studies teacher reflected when describing the curricular standards guiding his Dubai classroom. abstract: Mud crabs (Scylla spp.) and spiny lobsters (Panulirus spp.) are premium seafood, but evidence on live handling, freshness indicators, processing, food safety, and shell utilization is rarely integrated across the postharvest chain. title: Ruins in the Field: Materiality, Spectres and Pluritemporal Encounters of the Oxford University Arctic Expedition
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how encounters with ruins and spectres in the field inform (post)colonial trajectories of exploration and research. It does so by illustrating how the material indeterminacy and haunted materialities of ruins play into the relationship between self, landscape and history that explorers (and researchers) construct during fieldwork. title: Hope, temporality, and wonder at the end of the world
abstract: This article interrogates the conceptual terrains of hope, temporality, and wonder in the context of the Anthropocene, arguing that dominant framings of hope – anchored in ontological loss and critique – risk reproducing modernist binaries they seek to dismantle. While hope has been widely deployed as a tool for imagining alternatives to modernity, its reliance on affirmation or negation often tethers imaginaries to reactive postures vis-à-vis the modernist project. abstract: This study aimed to develop and provide preliminary psychometric evidence for a School-Based Management (SBM) implementation instrument integrating Maluku’s local potential, Indonesia. abstract: Did Alexander actually want to cross the Hyphasis (Beas) River and advance to the Ganges? abstract: This essay examines the establishment of Christian hegemony through the theological and legal framework of the Doctrine of Christian Discovery (DoCD), tracing its roots from medieval Europe to its application in the Americas. Citrus medica L. cv. ‘Liscia’ has traditionally been used for its pharmacological properties; however, its essential oil remains insufficiently characterized. This study provides the first integrated evaluation of C. medica cv. ‘Liscia’ essential oil (CMLEO) for its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anti-quorum-sensing activities using complementary in vitro and in silico approaches. title: Ensuring a reliable blood supply during a pandemic in a Caribbean setting: The Curaçao experience
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: National blood systems require a resilient mechanism for ensuring safe blood supply during pandemics. For small island developing states (SIDS) additional specific challenges exist not normally addressed in guidelines and the literature. Here we describe the model used by the Caribbean island of Curaçao for pandemic preparedness during the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Morphophysiological diversity in rice: A trait-based framework for carbon capture, allocation, and genotype selection
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) provides a primary source of caloric intake for over half of the global population. Aligning grain production with climate mitigation requires understanding how plant traits influence carbon balance under contrasting water regimes, which affect both trait expression and the fate of plant-derived carbon in soil and greenhouse-gas emissions. Here, the morphological and physiological attributes that govern carbon acquisition, allocation, and retention in rice were reviewed. title: Interaction between the East Asian summer monsoon and Westerlies as shown by desert shrub-ring records from the Alxa Plateau, Northwest China
abstract: Abstract. The variations, driving mechanisms, and interactions between the mid-latitude westerlies and the Asian summer monsoon represent a critical focus in global change research. Extensive research has investigated climate change and its drivers across multiple timescales in the core regions of both westerlies Asia and monsoonal Asia. However, studies are far fewer in the arid inland deserts at the interactive margin of these two circulation systems, where precipitation restrict the distribution of trees. title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles.

title: A COI barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods supports biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe
abstract: Terrestrial molluscs are important components of terrestrial ecosystems, yet they remain poorly represented in molecular biodiversity assessments. Although they occur in a wide range of habitats, their inclusion in such studies is constrained by the lack of reliable genetic reference data, particularly in Central Europe. In Poland, despite a well-documented malacofauna comprising approximately 179 species, genetic data remain scarce. abstract: This study examines the drivers and barriers of branding strategy implementation in an Islamic secondary school, using MTs Darul Arifin, Muaro Jambi Regency, as a case study. In an increasingly competitive educational environment, Islamic schools are required to manage institutional branding strategically while maintaining their religious identity. This research employed a qualitative case study approach. abstract: Sustainable destination development calls for a view of sustainability that extends beyond its economic, sociocultural and environmental pillars to political and technological considerations. Drawing on the stimulus– organism–response (S-O-R) framework, this study examines how Generation Z tourists' perceptions of destination sustainability relate to perceived value, tourist satisfaction and electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM) intention. abstract: In the environment, heavy metals are present in the air, water, food, and many consumer products. Some heavy metals are essential to the human body, but only in high concentrations. Heavy metals play an important role in the human organism and are called essential minerals, while others are not known to be beneficial to our health, or, more precisely, are toxic. The toxicity of heavy metals to humans is clearly caused by long-term or high-level exposure to common pollutants. High concentrations of heavy metals may cause health problems. title: Constructing guaranteed and mean coverage Bayesian tolerance intervals in an unbalanced one-way random effects model with heterogeneous error variances
abstract: This study introduces a Bayesian framework for constructing the two-sided mean coverage tolerance interval, alongside the one-sided and two-sided guaranteed coverage tolerance intervals for an unbalanced one-way random effects model with heterogeneous error variances. The Bayesian simulation technique originally proposed by Wolfinger was utilized to develop the two-sided Bayesian guaranteed coverage tolerance interval. title: Spatial Distribution and Hydrogeological Controls On Hydrocarbon Contamination in Groundwater in Ogale, Niger Delta, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater contamination by petroleum hydrocarbons is an environmental concern in the Niger Delta, where oil-related activities threaten groundwater resources used by surrounding communities. This study investigated the spatial distribution of total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene and xylenes (BTEX) in groundwater in Ogale, Rivers State, Nigeria, and examined their relationships with selected hydrogeological parameters. title: Legume pre‐crops can improve following cereal yields and reduce climate impact
abstract: Abstract Legumes are increasingly promoted as a diversification strategy to mitigate externalities in low‐diverse cropping systems. Their inclusion can enhance agronomic performance of subsequent crops and reduce external inputs, potentially improving sustainability of current agricultural systems. This study aimed to (i) compare the pre‐crop effect of legumes and cereals on the yield and quality of a following cereal crop and (ii) assess the environmental impact of rotations with and without legumes. title: From comparison to inclusion: post-Soviet immigrant parents’ perspectives on Canadian schooling
abstract: Immigrant parents bring a unique set of beliefs and practices to the K-12 education of their children in the host countries, which are not always aligned with teacher expectations. Based on qualitative interviews (N = 46) with immigrant parents from 10 countries of the former Soviet Union whose children attend Canadian high schools, we show that immigrant parents approach their children’s education from a comparative perspective. abstract: The India–European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) concluded negotiations on 27 January 2026 andis now moving through the legal and approval process required before entry into force. For Indianexporters, the agreement is particularly important in textiles and pharmaceuticals, two sectors wheretariffs, regulatory requirements and scale strongly influence competitiveness. title: Palaces of chance and bloodlines of influence: Existential currents and recurring motifs in the poetry of Nathan Shepherdson
abstract: This paper explores influences on and motifs within the creative practice of Australian poet Nathan Shepherdson, the author of ten books of poetry including, most recently, how to spear sleep (2021), parallel equators (2023), axolotl waltz (2024) and soft meteorites (2024). title: Assessing the Current State of Compensation, Support, and Resettlement upon State Land Recovery in Thanh Hoa Province
abstract: Industrialization, urbanization, and the rollout of key infrastructure projects in Thanh Hoa province in recent years have driven large-scale land recovery, while compensation, support, and resettlement remain a sensitive task that directly affects residents' rights and project timelines. This study assesses the current state of this work in Thanh Hoa province during 2023-2025, since the Law on Land No. 31/2024/QH15 took effect, identifying achievements, limitations, causes, and appropriate solutions. abstract: Abstract We present the weak gravitational lensing dataset from the Super-pressure Balloon-Borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT), which imaged 30 galaxy clusters during its 45 night flight in 2023 April–May. SuperBIT is a first-of-its-kind balloon-borne imaging telescope that achieved near-diffraction-limited observations in near-space conditions above 98% of the Earth’s atmosphere. title: Association between Antimicrobial Resistance Phenotypes and Biofilm-Associated Virulence among Clinical Isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae
abstract: Background: Klebsiella pneumoniae is an important opportunistic pathogen increasingly associated with multidrug resistance and persistent healthcare-associated infections. Biofilm formation may enhance bacterial survival, reduce antimicrobial susceptibility, and contribute to treatment failure. This study evaluated the association between antimicrobial resistance phenotypes and biofilm-forming capacity among clinical isolates of K. pneumoniae. title: Epigraphs and Ontology: Divergent Paratextual Functions in Postmodern Novels versus Science Fiction and Fantasy
abstract: This study explores the divergent ontological functions of epigraphs in late-20th-century Anglophone fiction, contrasting their roles in postmodern literary novels versus science fiction and fantasy. Postmodern epigraphs often destabilize fictional worlds, fostering ontological hesitation and irony, as seen in works by Pynchon and McEwan. Conversely, science fiction and fantasy employ epigraphs – frequently fictitious or intra-world quotes – to consolidate and authenticate their fictional universes, as exemplified by Frank Herbert’s “Dune”. title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
abstract: Abstract Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. title: The perceived reasons for participation in private tutoring in the Sultanate of Oman
abstract: Private tutoring (PT) is becoming increasingly widespread around the globe, and the Sultanate of Oman is no exception. Even though the Omani educational system witnesses continuous development, PT is gaining popularity. The present research paper aims to explore the reasons that drive the need for private tutoring lessons as perceived by the students, parents, and teachers. Three distinct questionnaires were developed based on a review of pertinent literature to collect data for this descriptive analytical study. title: Mapping the beyond GDP field: Canonical concentration and insular invisibility in three decades of multidimensional prosperity measurement (1995–2026)
abstract: Three decades after the Stiglitz Commission's call to measure “beyond GDP”, multidimensional prosperity frameworks have proliferated, yet cross-linguistic mappings of their paradigmatic and territorial composition remain scarce; existing reviews rely on English-only searches. This article characterises the conceptual, methodological and territorial structure of multidimensional prosperity frameworks published between 1995 and 2026, and tests the robustness of the resulting patterns to alternative definitions of the review scope. abstract: Abstract Docosapentaenoic acid (DPA, 22:5n-3) is an intermediate omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid with emerging biological significance, yet its metabolic fate in fish remains poorly defined. title: Influence of vetch– Brachiaria intercropping and phosphorus fertilisation on soil nutrient dynamics and forage mineral composition of Brachiaria varieties under a Mediterranean climate
abstract: A field experiment consisted of a 4 × 4 × 2 factorial layout in a randomised complete block design with four replicates at the Mariendahl and Welgevallen sites, Western Cape province, South Africa. abstract: Background: DUWLs easily become colonized by microorganisms due to narrow tubing, intermittent flow, and stagnation allowing adhesion and biofilm formation to occur. Patients and dental health-care workers are potentially at risk of exposure to microorganisms during procedures if contaminated outlet water is present. abstract: Abstract. CO2 is the main contributor to global warming, and cities now account for more than two-thirds of emissions of this gas. Atmospheric observatories located on the outskirts of cities are therefore important facilities for measuring the impact on atmospheric composition of the emission reductions planned by cities. The Saclay observatory, part of the ICOS and ACTRIS research infrastructures and located 20 km southwest of Paris, has been monitoring greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4), reactive gases (NOx, O3, CO), and carbonaceous aerosols (eBC) since 2012. abstract: OBJECTIVE: This paper examines how the National Best Practice Unit Tackling Indigenous Smoking (NBPU TIS) supports program-funded organisations through collaboration, knowledge exchange and culturally responsive practice, and how these processes strengthen community-driven approaches to reducing smoking and vaping prevalence among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. title: Competencias investigativas del docente universitario y su impacto en el acompañamiento de tesis
abstract: La elaboración de una tesis constituye una etapa compleja de la formación universitaria donde el estudiante articula decisiones teóricas y metodológicas con la orientación de un docente asesor. El estudio tuvo como objetivo determinar el impacto de las competencias investigativas del docente universitario en el acompañamiento de tesis de pregrado en educación. title: Let's talk data archiving: practical insights into FAIR and long-term data management from early-career perspectives
abstract: Research data provide the basis for scientific discovery, yet their long-term value depends on careful curation and documentation. Data archiving is often treated as a final administrative task rather than an integral part of research. This report summarizes key insights from an interactive seminar organized by the Association of Polar Early Career Scientists (APECS) Germany, which explored practical approaches to making data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) from early-career perspectives. title: From Primary Production to Value-Added Fish Products: International Technology Transfer in A Rural Rice-Fish Farming Community
abstract: Small-scale rice–fish farmers commonly market harvested fish as fresh products, limiting opportunities for product differentiation and downstream value creation. This community engagement program aimed to strengthen the initial capacity of a rice–fish farming community in Lubuk Bayas Village, North Sumatra, Indonesia, in value-added fish processing, food hygiene, product diversification, and market preparation through international academic collaboration. title: Persian Literature and Cultural Life in Central Asia: From Civilizational Roots to the Reform Movements in Bukhara (Late Nineteenth Century – Early Twentieth Century)
abstract: This study examines the transformation of Persian literary and cultural life in Bukhara and its wider Central Asian environment from the nineteenth century to the early twentieth century, with particular attention to the relationship between literature, education, literacy, journalism, and cultural identity. abstract: Hierarchical and latent variable models are fundamental in ecology, fisheries science, and epidemiology, but fitting them efficiently relies on automatic differentiation (AD) combined with approximations such as the Laplace approximation. abstract: The study assessed the management for supply chain of the essential household commodity–cooking fuel at Palo, Leyte during CY 2025. Cooking fuel stands as an essential household commodity directly linked to food security, public health, and livelihood stability. Yet in disaster-prone municipalities such as Palo, Leyte, supply chains remain vulnerable to typhoons, price volatility, transport disruptions, and institutional fragmentation. title: Reconstructing the dietary history of Japanese black bears through stable isotope analysis of hair
abstract: Abstract The population of Japanese Asiatic black bears ( Ursus thibetanus japonicus ) has been increasing in Japan, leading to more human–bear conflicts, including crop damage and an increase in the lethal removal of bears. However, it remains difficult to verify whether captured bears were directly involved in such damage. title: WHY PROCUREMENT CORRUPTION PERSISTS DESPITE E-PROCUREMENT: EVIDENCE FROM PROSECUTED CASES IN MALAYSIAN PUBLIC AGENCIES (2007–2020)
abstract: Electronic procurement (e-procurement) is widely promoted as a transparency and anti-corruption tool, yet prosecuted procurement corruption cases in Malaysia have persisted despite nationwide adoption in 2004. This qualitative study examines where, how, and why corruption survives in a digitalised procurement environment by reviewing 30 fully prosecuted public-procurement corruption cases from 2007–2020 obtained from the Malaysian Anti- Corruption Commission (MACC) and triangulating them with semi-structured interviews with four enforcement-agency investigation officers. title: Asymmetric Migration Shapes Genetic Structure of the Invasive Avian Vampire Fly ( Philornis downsi ) Across the Galápagos Islands
abstract: Biological invasions on islands provide a natural framework to study how dispersal and connectivity influence evolutionary and ecological processes. abstract: Aprender a aprender es una competencia para organizar y regular el propio aprendizaje en función de las necesidades, del contexto y principalmente de los objetivos trazados. El artículo expone los resultados de un estudio que tuvo como objetivo comparar las diferencias de la competencia aprender a aprender en función del género y edad de un grupo de 436 estudiantes universitarios de Lima-Perú. title: Advances in Coordination Chemistry–Based Sensors for Monitoring Toxic Metal Pollutants in Aquatic Environments
abstract: Toxic metal contamination of surface water, groundwater and wastewater threatens ecosystems and the communities that depend on them. Conventional methods such as atomic absorption spectrometry and inductively coupled plasma-based techniques are reliable but need laboratory facilities, which restricts routine monitoring in remote and resource-limited settings. abstract: La preparación laboral de los estudiantes con discapacidad intelectual requiere prácticas seguras, repetibles y relacionadas con el trabajo. abstract: Proses painting menggunakan cat, thinner, spray gun, dan kompresor sehingga berpotensi menimbulkan paparan kimia, bahaya fisik, serta kebakaran. title: Assessment of Potentially Toxic Elements in Tea Beverages Prepared by Vendors Within Bayero University kano Old Campus: Implications for Public Health
abstract: Tea is one of the most widely consumed beverages worldwide, making contamination by potentially toxic metals a public health concern. abstract: This article advances the evolving field of Idiomatics, devoted to the rigorous study of idiomatic and figurative language. It is organized into five main sections, framed by a preamble and a prologue that establish the conceptual stage, and concluded by an epilogue and a coda that reflect on the work’s implications and future directions. Positioned between inherited nomenclatures and emergent inquiry, the article confronts a labyrinth of competing terms that have long obscured conceptual clarity. title: Understanding socio-economic valuation in UK urban development through the lens of power
abstract: Improving social and environmental outcomes, especially health outcomes, is a central priority in the development of urban areas, and there have been many attempts in the UK and internationally to model and measure these outcomes in order to improve quality of life. Quantitative methods often appear to carry more weight than qualitative methods, though what weight they are afforded by different actors and stakeholders across the many systems of urban development is not well understood. title: Polyphonic Resistance: Countering Erasure in Palestinian Poetry
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how contemporary Palestinian poetry articulates and potentially disrupts the exclusion of experiences of harm from dominant frameworks of representation. Against the background of erasure, we examine how poems address epistemic injustice and intervene in the politics of visibility and voice, notably in the context of the annihilation of Gaza. Situating Gaza within historic harm that extends back to the Nakba, our analysis foregrounds the longue durée of harm. abstract: Although Nannochloropsis oceanica (N. oceanica) is widely exploited for feed and oil production, its protein fraction remains underutilized. Here, we developed a virtual-to-experimental workflow to discover antioxidant peptides from N. oceanica protein hydrolysates. abstract: This study provides the first comprehensive characterization of seven key pollutants [lithium (Li), cobalt (Co), aluminum (Al), manganese (Mn), nickel (Ni), copper (Cu), and sulfate (SO 4 )] in production-process wastewater from five major secondary battery-related industrial sectors and in 26 full-scale secondary battery wastewater treatment plants (SBWTPs) treating wastewater from nine sectors. title: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
abstract: BACKGROUND: Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. RESULTS: Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban-rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. abstract: Cassava commercialisation is increasing in Kenya, mainly due to recent emphasis on its role in enhancing food security and income generation. However, smallholder cassava farmers still receive low prices for their products, constraining their ability to maximise returns. There is limited empirical evidence on how cassava product attributes influence market prices. title: Public attitudes toward speed safety camera enforcement and critical elements of support in British Columbia, Canada
abstract: Background This study aimed to determine the views of British Columbia (B.C.) residents on acceptance and wider adoption of automated speed enforcement (ASE) in their province and local communities. The specific objectives of this study were to determine 1) the proportion of B.C. residents who approve/disapprove of ASE; 2) the characteristics of people who approve/disapprove of ASE; and 3) the critical elements that would engender support for ASE. abstract: This legal mapping paper aims to aggregate state-specific policies on the impact of criminal legal system contact—more specifically, the impact of criminal convictions—on social work licensure. Situating these policies within an abolitionist analysis and the larger history of social work in the United States, the paper attempts to expose the contradictions alive within the profession’s discourse. abstract: Flood has become one of the most destructive environmental hazards in South-Eastern Nigeria. It displaces communities, destroys farmland, and reshapes public discourse on climate vulnerability. While hydrological and policy studies have examined its physical and administrative dimensions, little attention has been paid to how language constructs, naturalizes, or contests the disaster's meaning. title: Long-term land-atmosphere carbon monoxide exchange from a tall tower in a rural Central European region
abstract: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric trace gas, significantly influencing the atmosphere's oxidative capacity and indirectly affecting climate. However, the net land-atmosphere exchange of CO remains highly uncertain due to the scarcity of long-term monitoring. This study presents and analyses a 10-year-long CO flux data series from a tall-tower eddy covariance (EC) system operated in a rural Central European region. abstract: The community service program in Tuwung Village, Central Kalimantan, aims to address overproduction and fluctuations in catfish prices through downstreaming and food diversification. The solution offered is the transfer of technology for producing catfish sticks seasoned with natural Mekai leaf (Albertisia papuana Becc.) as an organic, non MSG flavor enhancer. abstract: The claim that the “first kiss” on the screen in the People’s Republic of China (P.R.C.) appeared in Romance on Lushan Mountain (1980) needs to be corrected. This study argues that the first kiss on screen in the P.R.C. should be in the film Caravans with Ring, produced by Shanghai Film Studio in 1954. title: Banal Nationalism and Imperial Memory in Urban Space: Exploring the Memorialization of Captain Scott in Cardiff’s Semiotic Landscape
abstract: This article examines memorials and tributes to explorer Captain Robert Falcon Scott within the semiotic landscape of Cardiff, a major logistical and financial base for the British Antarctic Expedition 1910-13. Using a “walking approach” grounded in Multimodal Critical Discourse Analysis, it explores how their design, material form, spatial setting, and historical context shape the (re)production of discourses and construct Scott’s legacy through interaction with the urban environment. title: Investigating emerging contaminants in dams from the Vhembe District in Limpopo and, for the first time, in the Orlando Dam, Gauteng Province, South Africa
abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including certain organophosphate pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, and metals, as well as pharmaceuticals such as antiretroviral drugs (ARVs), are contaminants of increasing concern in freshwater sources in South Africa (SA). One surface water sample from each site was collected from dams in an urban area, Gauteng Province, and from a rural area, the Vhembe District in the Limpopo Province in SA. title: A Study on Impact of Incoterms on Freight Cost and End-To-End Documentation
abstract: International trade rests on a quiet but consequential piece of legal shorthand: the Incoterm. A three-letter code decides who pays for freight, who insures the cargo, who clears customs at either end, and who absorbs the cost when something goes wrong along the way. For a freight forwarder sitting between exporter and importer, that code is not background detail — it is the operating instruction for every shipment that crosses the desk. abstract: Abstract This study presents the first AVA-resolved retrospective assessment of wildfire smoke impacts on 2020 Oregon Willamette Valley Pinot noir by merging phenolic diglycoside (PDG) biomarker concentrations with sensory appraisals and marketplace performance. title: Im/mobilities and the Occupying Gaze
abstract: This article considers how the occupying gaze transforms bodies and objects into suspended sites of gendered and political violence. While in peacetime waiting suggests ennui and stasis, the im/mobility that occurs at Israeli checkpoints is entangled with power, including who decides how time is valued, and how and whose bodies move (and where to). abstract: Biochemistry and haematology analytes can provide information on the health status of individual animals or populations in direct comparison to expected values or reference intervals developed using the same analysis methodology from a healthy reference population of the target species. Point-of-care analysers are increasingly used in the assessment of wildlife health; however, their effective use in wildlife species requires establishment of appropriate expected values from clinically healthy animals. abstract: Abstract The understanding of the user engagement, selection and adoption of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in developing countries is important to deploy measures to sustain their use. As part of a project developing, deploying, and empowering communities in developing countries with ICS, this study screened the awareness and choice selection factors for end users selected for ICS adoption. title: Comparative Analytical Characterization and Chromatographic Profiling of Virgin and Recycled Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and its copolymeric variants represent a critical class of thermoplastic polymers widely deployed in packaging, industrial textiles, and consumer products due to their tensile strength, dimensional stability, and chemical resistance. PET materials are broadly categorized into virgin polyester (vPET), derived directly from petrochemical feedstocks, and recycled polyester (rPET), produced via the mechanical or chemical reprocessing of postconsumer polymer waste. title: First record of Youngia japonica (L.) DC. (Asteraceae: Tribe Cichorieae) in Aotearoa / New Zealand
abstract: We report the first verified records of Youngia japonica subsp. japonica (Asteraceae: Tribe Cichorieae) in northern Aotearoa / New Zealand. Five populations have been discovered across Tāmaki Makaurau / Auckland and Te Tai Tokerau / Northland. Specimens were identified using morphological characteristics consistent with flora descriptions, and verified through sequencing using nrDNA ITS (ITS1 and ITS2 spacer regions) and the chloroplast trnH-psbA intergenic spacer. title: Evaluation of Wheat Genotypes for Combined Heat and Drought Stress Tolerance
abstract: A field experiment was carried out from November 2021 to April 2022 to assess the tolerance of five wheat genotypes to combined heat and drought stress. The study followed a split plot design with three replications. The main plot treatment consisted of two growing conditions (normal condition and combined heat and drought condition) and the sub-plot treatments consisted of five wheat genotypes (BARI Gom 29, BARI Gom 30, BARI Gom 31, BWMRI Gom 3 and BAW 1290). title: Sustaining Life under Extraction: Environmental Justice and Community Capabilities in Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap
abstract: Extractive pressures threaten collective life despite economic gains. This study examines how environmental injustice reshapes substantive opportunities to sustain livelihoods and pursue valued collective futures. Environmental justice and community capabilities frame readings of Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu [Taboo Land] and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap [Fire, Clouds, and Smoke]. title: Human in vitro airway models to assess point-of-contact respiratory toxicity of surfactants: development and evaluation of a repeated-exposure study design
abstract: Repeated-dose exposure studies can provide insights into the toxicity of test substances, including dose-response relationships, cumulative effects, delayed responses, and reversibility of effects. A limited number of in vitro studies have assessed the effects of repeated exposure of respiratory cells to chemicals applied as liquids (via direct pipetting). title: Transforming Canadian Federal Governance in a Polycrisis
abstract: Abstract Since 1995, scientific consensus has linked human activity to climate change, yet the political and financial power of the carbon economy remains entrenched. Under conditions of polycrisis, many states continue to miss emissions targets and, in some cases, retreat from climate commitments. abstract: Introducción: La identidad es un fenómeno que, por su naturaleza social y psicológica, no puede definirse de manera estática. title: Heat exposure and perceived academic functioning among nursing students in a tropical higher education setting: a qualitative study
abstract: Background: Extreme heat presents a growing challenge for nursing education in tropical regions. However, there is limited qualitative evidence regarding students' experiences across commuting, campus, and learning environments. Aim: This study explores nursing students' experiences of heat, its perceived impact on academic functioning, and both personal and institutional responses. abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive legal audit investigating the systemic water shortage in Bengaluru and its direct implications on fundamental rights, particularly the right to life, dignity, and livelihood under the Constitution of India. With a population exceeding 13 million heavily reliant on distant river supplies and rapidly depleting groundwater, Bengaluru faces a recurring structural deficit, marked by a documented official shortfall of over 500 million liters per day and widespread drying of borewells. abstract: A total of 121 proposals were received online for consideration of registration of germplasm for unique/superior traits. abstract: Abstract Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. abstract: Recent anthropology theorizes borders primarily as technologies of exclusion that perpetuate structural inequality and racialized violence. This perspective downplays the varied cultural meanings of boundaries that shape identities within and amongst countries of the global south, ultimately resting on a neo-functionalist model of borders and boundary-making. abstract: The European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages recently broke new ground by supporting two languages that had previously died; and not just under its fairly tokenistic, unburdensome Part II, but the much more extensive (and expensive) Part III. abstract: ABSTRACT Earthquakes often occur in clusters (foreshocks, mainshocks, and aftershocks) and can lead to cumulative structural damage. abstract: Helen of Troy is usually read through her beauty, her abduction, and her responsibility for the war. This article asks a different question: why does the presence of one desired woman occasion such different courses of response in those who meet her, and how does each of those courses change over time? abstract: Squalene-based oil-in-water emulsions underpin established vaccine-adjuvant platforms, while palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) provides a potentially recoverable non-animal source of squalene. This qualitative literature review critically integrates research on PFAD separation, pharmaceutical impurities, squalene-emulsion mechanisms, formulation stability, clinical vaccine evidence, and sustainable manufacturing. abstract: A Fe₂O 3 @ZIF-8@CeO₂ core–shell nanocomposite was reported as a highly effective sorbent for the dispersive solid phase extraction of Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cu(II) ions from honey. title: Early-life forage modulation is associated with ruminal microbiota and metabolic profiles in yak calves
abstract: Abstract Early-life dietary intervention plays a critical role in shaping ruminal microbial colonization, fermentation capacity, and functional maturation in young ruminants. However, how forage composition regulates rumen microbiome establishment and microbiota-associated metabolism during early yak development remains poorly understood. abstract: Traditional natural fermentation of cigar tobacco leaves is stochastic and often yields inconsistent quality. abstract: Abstract Wastewater surveillance (WS) has been widely adopted as a cost-effective and population-representative infectious disease monitoring tool and is increasingly being applied to bacterial and antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) targets. However, some of these targets may persist in pipe biofilms and detach into wastewater, complicating accurate WS interpretation. abstract: Abstract Invasions are narrated. They are narrated afterwards, when it comes to the construction of their meaning and legacy, and they are narrated in advance, when their logic and supposed necessity are first established. In fact, invasions—notwithstanding their very real and horrific physical and social consequences—cannot be fully understood without studying the stories that are told about them. title: Transforming Household Waste Into Economic Value Through Youth-Led Waste Banks Based on Asset-Based Community Development in Urban Nigeria

title: Pauta. Soporte nutricional en el paciente crítico
abstract: La malnutrición es frecuente en niños críticamente enfermos y se asocia con mayor morbimortalidad, infecciones, ventilación mecánica prolongada y mayor estadía hospitalaria. El soporte nutricional constituye, por tanto, un componente esencial del tratamiento integral en cuidados intensivos pediátricos. Esta pauta propone estandarizar la evaluación, indicación, implementación y monitorización del soporte nutricional del niño crítico, integrando recomendaciones internacionales y herramientas aplicables a la práctica clínica.

abstract: Abstract The global decline of insect pollinators is now well documented and recognized publicly from all over the Earth in a wide variety of ecosystems. Because a great deal of pollinator‐relevant environmental regulation (e.g., pesticide limitation, invasive species control) happens at the subnational level, an understanding of the subnational conservation status of these organisms is needed for targeting actions and monitoring their efficacy. Under these conditions, planets whose masses and radii are incompatible with both bare rocky interiors and extended H-dominated atmospheres are therefore expected to host high mean molecular weight atmospheres, making them promising candidates for volatile-rich hot water worlds. title: Prioritizing the Improvement of Expedition Service Quality in Indonesia Using an Integrated Logistics Service Quality (LSQ) and Three-Dimensional Model
abstract: This study investigates expedition service quality in Indonesia in response to rapid e-commerce growth and increasing logistics demand. Despite industry expansion, persistent service issues such as delivery delays, lost goods, and poor customer service remain prevalent. This research aims to identify priority attributes for service quality improvement by integrating Logistics Service Quality (LSQ) with a three-dimensional model consisting of the Kano model, Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA), and Goal Difficulty (GD). abstract: Powdered activated carbon (PAC) removes pollutants from water efficiently, but its fine particles are difficult to separate and reuse. A retained polymer shapes PAC into separable beads, films or flakes, or functionalizes granular activated carbon (GAC), but it dilutes the carbon and slows uptake. In some systems, the polymer also adds binding sites for specific contaminants. abstract: Abstract The integrated use of organic and inorganic fertilizers improves soil physicochemical properties and wheat productivity, whereas sole reliance on inorganic fertilizers leads to declining soil fertility. In the Bita District of Southwestern Ethiopia, the limited use of lime and coffee husk biochar constrains soil fertility improvement and wheat yields. title: Mapping the evidence on heliciculture – a scoping review
abstract: Heliciculture represents a promising avenue for achieving sustainable production of protein-rich food and feed. Snail farms are spreading at a gradual and uneven pace in several countries, however veterinary support for animal health issues in this field has never been thoroughly developed. Similarly, literature about heliciculture is also scarce and scattered. abstract: As cross-cultural interactions continuously transform global dietary habits, the traditional Japanese rice seasoning (furikake) offers an innovative blueprint for Thai food product development. Inspired by this concept, a novel instant Thai sour curry rice topping was formulated. This product successfully integrates a high-protein nutritional profile with superior consumer palatability and extended storage stability. title: Craft and Industrialization: Uncovering the Plasticity and Frontier of Craft
abstract: Abstract Craft as an approach to work has been proposed as an alternative to industrial mass production. While industrialization has led to the replacement of craft logic with industrial logic to create uniformity and scale operations, the role of craft in industrialization remains ambiguous. Building on the analysis of engineering work performed at an R&D laboratory in the pulp and paper industry, we explore how and why craft enables industrialization. abstract: This protocol documents a critical case analysis of Gordienko’s 2025 review Impact of War on Soils. The principal conclusion is that a low-quality compilation can acquire the institutional status of knowledge by reproducing the external form of a scientific publication while failing to perform the verification, differentiation, comparison and synthesis required of its declared genre. title: Taxonomic identity and associated revisions of Populus szechuanica var. tibetica
abstract: Abstract The genus Populus represents one of the most taxonomically challenging plant groups, with P. szechuanica var. tibetica standing out as a typical representative of such taxonomic perplexity. Extensive taxonomic confusion surrounding this variety involves a multitude of related taxa, which has imposed considerable adverse impacts on the research and utilization of poplar species. abstract: This article examines factors associated with sectoral participation in global value chains (GVCs), distinguishing among overall, simple and complex participation and between short- and long-run relationships. Using a panel of 56 sectors in 43 economies from 2001 to 2014, the study estimates dynamic fixed effects and cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) models. abstract: Marine video understanding is crucial for a wide range of real-world applications. However, existing marine video datasets suffer from limitations, including the limited number of data samples, fine-grained text descriptions, and detailed visual attributes. To address these limitations, we introduce a large-scale, video-text dataset featuring rich, in-the-wild visual attributes tailored for complex marine environments. abstract: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. title: Reward-Guided RRT* for Budgeted Task and Motion Planning
abstract: Robotic missions involving spatially distributed tasks often require jointly selecting rewarding locations and planning feasible motions under limited travel budgets. This paper proposes Reward-Guided RRT*, a new sampling-based framework that constructs a budget-feasible mission through a sequence of locally joint task-selection-and-motion-planning stages, evaluated directly in the continuous state space, without requiring a precomputed task-transition graph. title: Multiphase Gas Structure in JWST Little Red Dots
abstract: Abstract JWST has uncovered a population of compact high-redshift galaxies, `little red dots' (LRDs), exhibiting broad Balmer emission lines that often show narrow absorption features and strong Balmer breaks --- spectral signatures attributed to dense gas surrounding rapidly growing black holes, but whose small-scale structure remains unknown. A striking feature of LRD spectra is that the H$\beta$ absorption is systematically deeper than H$\alpha$, yet in any homogeneous gas this ordering is physically impossible. title: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss
abstract: The Persona Selection Model (PSM) posits that post-training selects a persona the model learned during pre-training. Work on subliminal learning has shown that models can impart covert signals (like "love of owls") into semantically unrelated outputs like strings of numbers, and that students trained on these outputs inherit those traits. In this work I show that by evaluating the likelihood of such outputs under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header, a method I call persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE), one can decode these subliminal signals and classify between them.

title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
abstract: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. abstract: As the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory begins its Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), satellite operators are racing to launch Orbital Data Center (ODC) satellites into low-Earth orbit. We present an impact assessment of a simulated $\sim$1 million ODC satellite constellation, arranged per recent filings across two low-Earth and two Sun-synchronous orbit regimes, on one year of Rubin Observatory LSST observations. abstract: The nature of dark matter remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics, with weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) among the leading candidates proposed to account for the observed anomalies across cosmic scales. If WIMPs annihilate or decay in the dense dark matter haloes of nearby galaxies, the resulting high-energy electrons/positrons can produce synchrotron radiation in the presence of ambient magnetic fields, yielding a potentially detectable radio signature. title: Enhancing coarse bathymetric grids using a generative model: An arctic case study
abstract: Bathymetric mapping of ice-covered polar seas remains a major challenge. Persistent sea ice restricts systematic surveys, while icebreaking operations degrade multibeam echosounder (MBES) data quality through noise, hull vibrations, and ice interference. As a result, digital terrain models (DTMs) from bathymetric surveys in ice-covered regions are often fragmented, coarse, and incomplete, limiting interpretation of seafloor morphology, including glacial landforms used to infer former glacier extent and ice-sheet dynamics. Here, we present the first global time of emergence analysis of MHW characteristics of the ocean surface using simulations from 21 Earth system models from the sixth Coupled Model Intercomparison Project under moderate (SSP2‐4.5) and high (SSP5‐8.5) greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. We present a 4-million-year record of eolian evolution from the Philippine Sea to deconvolve these two distinct transport systems on the basis of grain-size modeling and geochemical fingerprinting. abstract: ABSTRACT Crevice corrosion is a known issue for high chromium steels exposed to seawaters. However, it occurs also for mild and low alloy steels. Herein observations are reported for initiation and corrosion progression of mild steel. Crevices 30 to 200 µm in size, with outstands up to 100 mm, were considered, all exposed for up to 4 years in quiescent Pacific Ocean seawater. abstract: Abstract Global rivers are increasingly threatened by fragmentation and sediment accumulation in reservoirs and dams. The Water‐Sediment Regulation Scheme (WSRS) has been widely implemented to mitigate these challenges, yet its ecological impacts on estuarine fisheries remain poorly quantified. abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data provide high-frequency visual observations and low-frequency identity/location messages, respectively. abstract: Particle size distribution is an important physical characteristic of coastal sediments, influencing sediment transport, depositional behavior, permeability, packing characteristics, and particle–fluid interactions. The present study investigates the particle size characteristics of beach sand collected from Haffa Beach, Salalah, Sultanate of Oman, using sieve analysis and moment-based particle diameter calculations. abstract: Background: Heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring during real-world closed-circuit rebreather (CCR) diving remains methodologically challenging. This exploratory case report describes phase-related HRV variations obtained from a wearable device during a military CCR dive. abstract: Giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii) is one of the freshwater commodities in Indonesia with high market demand. This study investigated boron-doped mesoporous bioactive glass (B-MBG) nanoparticles as a dual-payload delivery system for the combined administration of tetracycline and selected hydrophobic phytochemical adjuvants, including berberine, curcumin, and resveratrol. title: Isobaric Crystallization of Aqueous Magnesium Chloride Solutions at Icy Moon Conditions
abstract: Abstract Subsurface oceans inside icy moons are expected to contain dissolved salts whose crystallization controls the mineralogy of their hydrospheres and potentially their surfaces. title: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse

title: Metocean-Dependent Blade-Pitch Control of Floating Wind Turbines: Balancing Regulation and Pitch Activity
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbines operate under continuously varying atmospheric and ocean conditions, whose influence is not explicitly accounted for in conventional blade-pitch controller scheduling. As a result, control strategies designed to provide strong rotor-speed regulation may introduce unnecessary blade-pitch activity under certain environmental conditions. abstract: Abstract Hydroclimatic variability is projected to intensify under continued warming, yet the evolving likelihood, rapidness, and seasonal timing of drought‐to‐pluvial transitions remain poorly quantified. abstract: Abstract Renowned for having one of the highest concentrations of greenhouses in the world, Campo de Dalías, located in the southeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in the southwest of the province of Almeria in Spain, offers a compelling case for understanding the evolution of how water has been valued and managed in agriculture. abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are increasingly used to reduce uncertainty in regional climate projections by exploiting relationships across models between observable historical predictors and projected changes. Using the Tibetan Plateau (TP), a region of complex terrain, as a testbed, we compare two widely used predictors for constraining future TP warming: large-scale global mean surface air temperature (GSAT) and regional Tibetan Plateau surface air temperature (TPSAT). abstract: The magnetic Penrose process (MPP) is one of the most efficient mechanisms for extracting rotational energy from a magnetized Kerr black hole (BH), enabling charged particles to reach very-high energies. title: National Monitoring of Mangroves has Outpaced their Integration into Climate Policy
abstract: Ambitious global targets for mangrove conservation have advanced rapidly in recent years, yet the implementation of these commitments depends largely on national monitoring systems and policy processes. Despite widespread reliance on country-reported data for setting and evaluating targets, little is known about how national mangrove statistics are generated or how they interact with climate policy frameworks. abstract: This study explored a knowledge- and data-driven dynamic risk assessment method for oil and gas pipelines subjected to cascading disaster chains. title: A Ridge-Penalised Fourier Autoregressive Framework for High-Dimensional Periodic Time Series Dataset
abstract: Time series associated with the seasonal climate are highly persistent with strong periodic behaviour making reliable statistical forecasting a challenge. Integrated autoregressive models on a conventional framework may fail to represent multifrequency seasonality. Fourier Autoregressive (FAR) models offer flexibility but may experience instability when the model complexity escalates in nature. title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption
abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. title: Addressing seablindness: defense diplomacy and NATO-GCC cooperation in countering naval hybrid threats
abstract: This article examines the strategic potential of defense diplomacy in enhancing cooperation against maritime hybrid threats between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). Hybrid threats, marked by ambiguity, deniability, and cross-domain tactics, pose acute risks to the Gulf’s dependence on maritime trade, energy exports, and subsea digital infrastructure. abstract: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. abstract: This paper presents a finite element strength assessment of a ship double bottom structure. A detailed three-dimensional finite element model is developed to describe the structural arrangement and complexity of the double bottom, including plating and longitudinal and transverse stiffening. abstract: Abstract Plastic debris accumulation in natural ecosystems is a major environmental challenge. Yet production continues to grow because plastics often deliver lower life-cycle impacts than available alternatives. Due to severe material- and application-specific constraints, neither mechanical nor chemical recycling can presently be deployed at sufficient scale to prevent substantial environmental leakage. abstract: Declining amphibian and reptile populations in Costa Rica, particularly at mid-elevations, underscore theurgent need for updated herpetofaunal inventories in vulnerable, anthropogenically disturbed areas like the CentralValley. abstract: As extreme heat has become one of the most deadly climate risks in cities today, a fundamental question is rarely asked: where does a city’s heat-disaster response capacity actually come from? Taking Shanghai from 1873 to 1949 as a case study, this study reconstructs summer extreme heat events by integrating Xujiahui Observatory temperature observations with modern newspapers and municipal archives. title: Efficient Degradation and Recycling of Waste Formaldehyde Polymers to Value‐Added Diindolylmethane Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT The effective degradation of formaldehyde polymers catalyzed by Y(OTf) 3 with indole derivatives in water has been achieved, yielding a series of diindolylmethane compounds with added value. It provides a new route with additional potential for the upcycling of waste paraformaldehyde and polyoxymethylene plastic as a green alternative C1 synthon.

title: A global overview of pigeon–fruit interactions
abstract: Pigeons are widespread worldwide. abstract: Abstract This study evaluates classical and contemporary wind tunnel blockage correction methods for propeller testing, with a focus on slipstream effects in closed section tunnels. title: Selection of the Parameter of the Synchrony Estimator for the Correlation Between Time Series Sampled at Different Time Points
abstract: Abstract The synchrony estimator with parameter $$\beta $$ β for the correlation between two time series observed at different time points is defined as the standard Pearson correlation coefficient computed using a fraction $$\beta $$ β of the pairs of the two series corresponding to the smallest time differences. Two problems limit the use of the estimator in applications. First, no rule is available for selecting $$\beta $$ β . Second, it has been argued in the literature that the estimator only partially exploits the information in the data, since it does not use all available observations.

abstract: Research into collocation learning in second and foreign language environments has gained significant scholarly attention. abstract: Against the background of global climate warming, the impact of high-temperature variation on urban economic growth has become an increasingly important issue in climate economics and urban sustainability research. abstract: Abstract Cacay (Caryodendron orinocense) is a native tree species increasingly cultivated in commercial plantations in the Colombian Orinoquía for its high-value nuts and oil, but the effects of this emerging tree crop on biodiversity remain poorly understood. abstract: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. abstract: Plant volatile organic compounds (VOCs) play a key role in defence against herbivores and in mediating multitrophic interactions. abstract: Abstract Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. abstract: Anthropogenic carbon emissions remain closely linked to the structure and short-run adjustment of financial and industrial systems. abstract: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China's counties and promoting rural social development. abstract: Abstract Pigments in open-air rock art are often in heavily deteriorated superimposition sequences, limiting visualisation using standard photographic approaches. abstract: Two important indicators of climate change are the decline in Arctic sea ice area and the increase in average temperatures globally. abstract: Stowage planning for Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) vessels can be represented with different mathematical formulations for efficient stowage plans: hybrid-slot, grid-based, and lane-based representations. abstract: We present the first direct measurements of the neutron background at the Colorado Underground Research Institute (CURIE), a shallow-underground facility with an effective overburden of approximately $400$~m.w.e.\ in the Edgar Experimental Mine in Idaho Springs, Colorado. title: Statistics of Extremes for the Insurance Industry
abstract: Outline : Insurance risk is driven by rare but extreme losses, making extreme value statistics a vital tool for modeling large claims. This chapter explores how these methods support risk management and pricing, especially in reinsurance.

abstract: Designers require different design spaces across creative stages: broad during exploration, and targeted during refinement. abstract: Public service encounters are among the most visible ways in which citizens assess the competence, fairness, and responsiveness of the state. abstract: This study investigates the structural paradox of waste compensation policies in the Bantargebang Integrated Waste Treatment Plant (TPST), Bekasi, which has emerged as a consequence of megapolitan Jakarta's massive waste accumulation. Although local regulations explicitly mandate citizens' rights to environmental compensation, implementation remains trapped within a rigid, bureaucratic approach. title: Major Maritime Casualties under India's Merchant Shipping Act, 2025: Liability, Response and Limitation
abstract: The Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 marks a significant transition in India’s maritime legal framework by consolidating and restructuring the law governing maritime casualties in closer alignment with international conventions. This paper examines the liability, response obligations and limitation rights arising from a maritime casualty involving a collision between an oil tanker and a container vessel in Indian territorial waters. title: Coordinating Individual and System Change in the Marketing System: The TISI Framework for a Circular Plastics Economy
abstract: Single-use plastics (SUPs) remain a major obstacle to a circular plastics economy. Interventions to reduce them have typically pursued either system-level (S-level) measures or individual-level (I-level) behaviour change campaigns, and participatory work has tended to engage consumers or stakeholders at only one of these levels. title: Legal Protection of Civil Servants Against Identity-Based Spatial Coercion in Indonesia’s Local Elections
abstract: Indonesian election law requires civil servants (ASN) to remain neutral but largely treats them as potential violators rather than rights-holders needing protection from coercion by regional heads who influence their careers. This study examines how identity-based coercion through kinship, religion, ethnicity, or birthplace ties, and spatial coercion through formally valid personnel sanctions, infringed civil servants’ rights during the 2024 regional head elections (Pilkada) and why the legal framework failed to protect them. abstract: For Riexpress, a logistics service provider that handles land, sea, and air shipping, customer assessments are now formed long before goods reach the recipient, starting from when customers become familiar with the company through its digital channels. title: School Administrators’ Perceptions of Educational Leadership: Strengths and Areas for Development
abstract: This study aims to examine the perceptions of school administrators working at preschool, primary, secondary and high school levels about educational administration, their strengths and aspects that need to be developed. In the study, in which phenomenological design, one of the qualitative research designs, was used, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 school administrators determined by maximum diversity sampling, and the data obtained were evaluated by content analysis. abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the mediating effect of acculturation on the relationship between workplace discrimination and work conditions and migrant workers' intention to re-enter Malaysia for employment. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed using a non-probability sampling approach that combined quota and convenience sampling. abstract: The forest management unit (FMU) of Dampelas Tinombo was the formation of the FMU organization based on the typology of the area in Central Sulawesi. The organization's growth cycle encourages this FMU model as a strategy for institutional formation across stakeholders. This research aimed to identify and describe patterns of power and connectivity between stakeholder actors in the management of production forest areas at FMU Dampelas Tinombo (Unit IV). abstract: This study examines the coffee supply chain in East Lombok Regency from the perspective of Maqāṣid al-Sharī‘ah, focusing on economic justice, farmer welfare, and sustainability. Using a qualitative case study approach supported by spatial analysis, data were collected through interviews with farmers, collectors, traders, and consumers, complemented by documentation and a literature review. abstract: This study aimed to examine and analyze the role of corporate governance in moderating the influence of green intellectual capital and blue accounting disclosure on corporate sustainability performance. The study employed an associative quantitative approach. The population consisted of 91 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period, and a sample of 21 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 105 firm-year observations. title: Hop-and-sink locomotion and escape in benthic copepods under localized suction flow
abstract: Abstract Benthic copepods inhabit complex boundary layers where flow varies rapidly, yet their sensory-motor responses to localized hydrodynamic signals remain poorly understood. We quantified the behavior of the harpacticoid Tigriopus californicus under no-flow and localized suction flow using 3D particle tracking velocimetry of both copepod trajectories and the surrounding flow. Copepods frequently entered the water column and maintained a hop-and-sink gait, spending ~40% of time jumping with peak speeds up to 68 mm s−1. title: Comparative Feasibility Analysis of Mass Transit Options for Mangaluru-Udupi-Manipal Corridor
abstract: Objectives: Evaluate the techno-economic viability of a proposed ₹20,000 crore Heavy Metro system vis-a-vis alternate transit modalities (e.g., the inland waterway-based Water Metro) for the linear Mangaluru-Udupi-Manipal (MUM) urban corridor. abstract: The archipelago region of South Halmahera relies on sea transportation to maintain the continuity of supply for community needs and to expand market access for local commodities. This study analyzes the characteristics and role of traditional shipping (pelayaran rakyat), assesses the effectiveness of logistics distribution services, and formulates strengthening strategies through Pasar Baru Babang Port. abstract: The Punta Norte Patagonia orca (Orcinus orca) population/ ecotype exhibits a unique foraging strategy that involves intentionally stranding onto beaches to capture pinnipeds, primarily Southern sea lions (Otaria byronia, formerly Otaria flavescens). One adult male orca from this population was a prolific hunter. Between 1 February and 30 April, each year from 2006 to 2011, he conducted a total of 319 attacks and 173 successful captures. title: Demographic and environmental factors associated with canine cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma development in Australia: a retrospective matched case-control analysis
abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a common canine skin tumour that occurs more frequently in high ultraviolet (UV) environments. Despite Australia's consistently high UV exposure, large-scale epidemiological studies on canine cSCC are limited. This study investigates the frequency of canine cSCC in Australia, its geographic patterns relative to UV index, and its association with animal-level risk factors. title: Women at the Core of Climate-Smart Agriculture: Advancing Equity and Food Security through Empowerment
abstract: Climate volatility threatens global food security, particularly in developing nations where female farmers face severe resource barriers. This narrative review synthesizes empirical research published between 2010 and 2026 to evaluate women’s empowerment, climate-smart agricultural adoption, and household food security. Applying structured narrative frameworks, 44 academic studies and policy reports were synthesized across four major academic databases. abstract: Rationale: Regional allergen exposure varies with climate, lifestyle, and developmental stage. Evidence from coastal southeastern China remains limited, particularly across the full age range and across multiple allergic phenotypes. This study described age-related patterns of allergen sensitization in patients with allergic disease in Wenzhou, China, and evaluated associations with sex, season, clinical phenotype, polysensitization, and allergen co-occurrence. abstract: The present study examines occupational well-being, psychosocial well-being and quality of life among women domestic workers in Coimbatore District, Tamil Nadu. Women domestic workers make a significant contribution to household management and family care; however, many experience socioeconomic disadvantages, employment insecurity, low wages, inadequate social protection and limited awareness of labour rights. title: A food-web-centered framework for interpreting PFAS trophic magnification in aquatic ecosystems
abstract: Reported trophic magnification factors (TMFs) for per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) vary substantially among aquatic food webs, complicating comparisons across compounds and ecosystems. Interpreting this variation requires consideration of chemical properties, ecological processes and the methods used to estimate concentration–trophic-level relationships. abstract: Microplastic source attribution remains a major challenge because conventional analytical techniques primarily identify polymer types while providing limited information on the origin and environmental history of plastic materials. This study evaluates the potential and limitations of stable carbon isotope analysis (δ¹³C) for tracing common plastic polymers at the global scale. title: Linking Flow Regime Metrics to Spawning Migration Behavior of Threatened Green Sturgeon: Implications for Water Management in Regulated Rivers
abstract: ABSTRACT Flow regime alteration is among the most pervasive threats to freshwater ecosystems globally, and migratory species are particularly vulnerable to these impacts. Despite this, specific aspects of flow regimes that shape spawning migrations remain poorly understood for most threatened species. Functional flow frameworks offer a promising tool for identifying ecologically meaningful flow targets, especially for threatened species, like the Sacramento River population of green sturgeon ( Acipenser medirostris ). abstract: This study assessed the implementation and effectiveness of the Protected Area Community-Based Resource Management Agreement (PACBRMA) monitoring system within the Siargao Island Protected Landscape and Seascape (SIPLAS) in the Province of Surigao del Norte during Calendar Year 2025 as basis for strengthening community participation and protected area management. abstract: Vibriosis caused by Vibrio alginolyticus is a major bacterial disease in Asian seabass (Lates calcarifer) farming and leads to significant economic losses. The overuse of antibiotics has contributed to antimicrobial resistance, so there is a need for an effective prevention and control method, such as a vaccine against V. alginolyticus. abstract: Situated within the broader field of climate security, this article examines how climate change impacts on the (in)security of Indigenous communities and asks whether and how Indigenous epistemologies may offer new avenues to deepen the understanding of climate security interlinkages. This will be done through an empirical examination of official, written documents published by six representative Indigenous organisations in the context of the circumpolar Arctic, a region severely affected by climate change which simultaneously constitutes the home of more than 400,000 Indigenous subjects. title: Nitrous oxide dynamics across nitrogen and pH gradients in headwater streams
abstract: Abstract. Headwater streams in agricultural landscapes can contribute substantially to nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, yet the environmental controls on stream N₂O dynamics remain poorly resolved, particularly in systems with low pH. We investigated 72 Danish headwater streams spanning broad gradients in pH (5.0 - 8.8), land use, and soil type to identify the main drivers of N₂O variability. title: Indigenous Peoples and the Rights of Nature: A comparative analysis of environmental justice from the Philippines to the global stage
abstract: Abstract The Rights of Nature (RoN) framework provides that nature has inherent rights independent from economic and environmental rights of humans. To realise this, nature's own legal standing in court needs to be recognised. This article discusses the interconnection of the RoN framework and the rights of Indigenous Peoples, emphasising the need to fully integrate the RoN framework into State‐based legal systems to protect the rights of Indigenous Peoples and the environment. title: The Alternative to “Harm” in the ESA “Take” Claims
abstract: Wildlife agencies recently finalized major changes to regulations interpreting the Endangered Species Act (ESA). These regulations remove longstanding habitat protections for endangered and threatened species. To better protect wildlife and to solidify habitat protection’s role in Section 9 ESA litigation, conservation groups should bring more claims arguing that proposed projects “harass” wildlife by changing or destroying their habitat. This Note explores the potential effectiveness of “take” claims that allege “harass,” rather than “harm,” in the habitat modification context.

abstract: Abstract Riparian terrestrial insects face floods or accidental water exposure; however, their ability to fly off the water surface is unclear. Non-riparian species did not initiate flight from the surfaces of experimental lentic water, whereas 19 riparian species did. abstract: Offshore wind power (OWP) and offshore energy hubs (OEHs) have recently become stable components of decarbonisation efforts across the EU. To this end, a plan to construct "Energy Islands" was institutionalised in Danish policy in 2020, alongside ambitions to scale up OWP capacity by 6 GW. abstract: Abstract Healthcare interoperability between openEHR and HL7 FHIR remains challenging due to fundamental differences in data modeling approaches and the lack of standardized transformation mechanisms. This paper presents FHIRconnect, a novel domain-specific language (DSL) and open-source transformation engine that enables standardized, bidirectional data exchange between openEHR and FHIR healthcare standards. With the development of shipping practices, existing calculation rules face new issues concerning expense recognition, procedural connection, and special risk handling. This paper takes the 2022 "Common Maritime Loss Calculation Rules of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade" as the main research object and compares them with the 2016 "York-Antwerp Rules" and the current "Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China". abstract: Abstract Nearly half of Earth’s seasonal freshwater storage variability occurs in human‐managed reservoirs, resulting in large areas of reservoir‐bed that are episodically inundated or subaerially exposed. abstract: Abstract This text follows a well-known botanist along the shoreline of a Philippine island as he takes photographs of nipa palm ( nypa fruticans ), in its passage from plant to building part. It is January 1940 and David Fairchild is interested in plants for the collection of his new botanical garden in Miami, nicknamed ‘the kampong’. title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AS A RESPONSE TO CLIMATE CHANGE: REFLECTIONS ON LOCAL EXPERIENCES IN BENIN AND SENEGAL
abstract: The fight against the effects of climate change at the central level does not exclude the need for local authorities to also adapt. The role of municipalities is often overlooked, but remains essential due to their proximity to social realities. While the state is committed to combating climate change at the international level, the effective transfer of some of its powers to sub-state entities would require them to resort to national law. Administrative law, because it aims to serve the public interest, must logically include the fight against climate change through its tools and enforcement
