abstract: Climate change threatens ecosystems and human well-being, making the identification of regional vulnerabilities essential for targeted adaptation. This study developed a Climate Change Jurisdictional Vulnerability Index (CC-JVI) for South Africa through the integration of socio-economic indicators (Statistics South Africa) and environmental variables (NASA online database). abstract: Abstract This special dossier examines how understandings of Andean glaciers transform under the planetary crisis, defined by humanity’s impact on geophysical processes at a planetary scale. abstract: Moodjar (Nuytsia floribunda), a sacred Noongar tree from southWestern Australia, is known colloquially as the Christmas tree because it flowers at the end of the year. abstract: Abstract The Transient Climate Response to cumulative Emissions (TCRE) is the cornerstone of estimates of carbon emissions budgets to future warming targets, characterizing the near-linear relationship between the increase in global mean temperature and cumulative emissions of CO2. TCRE is derived from highly sophisticated Earth System Models (ESMs) - some, however, lack important processes known to have a large impact on TCRE. title: Climate justice: Is there an individual right of citizen to climate neutrality?
abstract: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural standing (legitimación activa) remains strictly constrained. Both CJEU and Spanish jurisprudence require proof of direct, individualized harm, preventing citizens from challenging public or corporate inaction on an individual basis. Currently, regulatory mechanisms reduce citizens to submitting administrative complaints or claiming post-damage civil compensation.

title: El himno de carácter ritual: el caso de los Himnos órficos
abstract: This article proposes an approach to the hymn genre in the Greco-Roman world to analyze its forms, functions, and how, through its composition and performance, it became a type of poetic offering to the gods. As an example, we examine the Orphic hymns, an imperial-era hymnal used by a Dionysian cult association. This collection invokes the favorable presence of numerous gods through the accumulation of epithets that highlight their genealogy, exploits, and power, not only to obtain divine favor but also to honor them through the power of the word and the burning of aromatic offerings.

title: "Neither Dead nor Lost – Uncovering Critical Law Stories at a Critical Time"
abstract: Law reform, in part at least, is about trying to see a way forward when there just does not seem to be one, or when the way forward is just too hard to bring into being. By many people putting their feet in front of each other, change can happen. Lecretia is testament to that. title: Tourism Facilities, Price, Cultural Performances, and Service Quality as Determinants of Visitor Satisfaction: Evidence from Balekambang Heritage Park Indonesia
abstract: The increasing number of visits to tourist destinations does not necessarily translate into higher visitor satisfaction. Previous studies have primarily examined the effects of tourist facilities, prices, and service quality, while the role of cultural performances in shaping visitor satisfaction remains relatively underexplored, particularly in public-space and cultural heritage destinations. This study examines the effects of tourist facilities, prices, cultural performances, and service quality on visitor satisfaction at Balekambang Park, Surakarta. title: Safeguarding and Promoting the Cultural Values of the Khmu People in Nghe an Province: A Stakeholder-Based Approach
abstract: Safeguarding the cultural heritage of the Khmu (Khơ Mú) people in Nghe An requires attention to living practices and to the relationships among communities, authorities, cultural professionals, educational institutions, and market actors. This study analyses stakeholder roles, potential tensions, and governance conditions in safeguarding and promoting Khmu cultural values. Qualitative document analysis integrates heritage-management scholarship, Vietnamese legislation, UNESCO instruments, and publicly documented initiatives in Nghe An. title: Saudi Arabian and Emirati Climate Diplomacy toward Pacific Island Countries: Motivations, Practices, and Limits
abstract: Why do hydrocarbon-exporting states pursue climate diplomacy toward Pacific Island countries that call for an accelerated fossil-fuel transition? This article compares Saudi Arabian and Emirati engagement from 2010 to September 2026 through a qualitative analysis of official documents, regional communiques, climate-policy texts, project records, and scholarly literature. It combines status seeking, niche diplomacy, institutional assets, and recipient agency in a framework linking motivations, practices, and outcomes. title: Changes in Migratory and Breeding Status of One Great Egret Over Eight Years
abstract: GPS and accelerometer data from a Great Egret (Ardea alba) tagged in September 2018 on Tomales Bay, Marin County, California, U.S.A. were recorded for eight breeding seasons. Following the first two breeding seasons after being outfitted with a GPS tag this individual migrated south (1535 km and 472 km, respectively) but remained resident in subsequent years, consistent with an age-related shift in migratory behavior. title: Djing.gii Gudjaagalali (children stars) school clinic; evaluation of a novel primary care led rural school based integrated model of care
abstract: Abstract Background There are more than 1.36 million children living in remote, rural and regional Australia. These children and young people have significantly worse health outcomes than their urban peers and experience inequities in healthcare access. This study explored key components of the integrated care model, including access, coverage, availability, affordability, improved health and equity. Methods General Practitioner (GP) clinical records for 105 students aged 4–18 years were analysed to demonstrate their care journey through the clinic between May 10th, 2022, and June 30th, 2024.

abstract: Changes in monsoon rainfall, temperature, agricultural production, and water availability can have an impact on India's industrial sector. El Niño is a major climate phenomenon that affects global weather patterns. El Niño-related climate disruptions may result in both new industrial opportunities and economic disruptions due to the interconnection of consumer demand, manufacturing, energy, transportation, and agriculture. journal: The Paradigm Chronicle Journal of Academic Inquiry and Critical Thought

title: ECOTOURISM AS A PATHWAY TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN SULTANATE OF OMAN: IMPACTS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND FUTURE POTENTIAL
abstract: Ecotourism is to provide conservation and responsible behavior among its stakeholders. Oman seeks to diversify its economy and reduce its dependence on oil; ecotourism has emerged as a promising approach to promote economic growth while safeguarding the environment and engaging local communities. This research focuses on the perspectives of key stakeholders understanding of how ecotourism is being perceived, the benefits it generates, and the challenges it encounters. title: Global Value Chain Participation and Inequality in Agro‐food Industries in the Global South
abstract: ABSTRACT Since the 1990s, global value chains have been a central vehicle for development strategies in Global South countries, driving their integration into the global economy. Much critical scholarship has highlighted the adverse social and environmental costs, the asymmetries of power in inter‐firm relations, and the unfair distribution of benefits that often arise from value chain participation. title: Tracing the Evolution of Air Ionisation Research in Romania. Nearly a Century of Scientific Progress and Interdisciplinary Perspectives
abstract: Air ionisation is an important component of atmospheric electricity, with implications for environmental quality, bioclimatology, and human health. Although research on this phenomenon has a long tradition in Romania, its historical development and diversification across scientific disciplines require systematic synthesis. This study employs a historical-descriptive review of scientific publications, research reports, conference proceedings, and studies conducted in Romania from 1938 to 2026. title: Reimagining Sustainable Natural Resource Governance through the Paradigm of Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘ah and Ecological Justice
abstract: The exploitation of natural resources and environmental degradation call for sustainable governance grounded in ethical and normative values. This study aims to identify Islamic principles in responding to contemporary environmental governance challenges and their relevance to sustainable natural resource management. title: WHAT DOES A CHOKEPOINT COST, AND WHO PAYS? OIL EXPOSURE, FISCAL RESILIENCE AND THE DISTRIBUTION OF DISRUPTION IN CHINA, INDIA, PAKISTAN AND THE UNITED STATES
abstract: A blocked shipping lane is a security problem and a budget problem at the same time. It is also a distribution problem: a price rise is a loss for those who buy oil and a gain for those who sell, ship, insure or store it. This paper asks whether the amount of oil a country imports, or the buffers behind those imports, better explains how badly a chokepoint disruption hurts it, and who inside each country ends up paying. title: Erosion of state resilience as a challenge to internal security – proposal for analytical framework enabling the early identification of social and institutional threats
abstract: The aim of the article is to present the erosion of state resilience as a useful analytical category in the study of internal security and a proposal for a three-level analytical framework for monitoring signs of a weakening of the state’s resilience before an overt crisis arises. The article is based on the analysis of the relevant literature, comparative analysis and model synthesis. title: TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY AS DRIVERS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN BANGLADESH: A REVIEW OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
abstract: Bangladesh, a nation rich in cultural heritage and natural beauty, possesses significant untapped potential in its tourism and hospitality sectors. Despite this, the contribution of these industries to the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has historically been modest compared to global averages. Recognizing tourism as a catalyst for economic growth, there is a growing imperative to understand and enhance its role in the country's development trajectory. title: Economic Policies toward Taiwan’s Indigenous Peoples, 1684–1874
abstract: This article examines economic policies toward Taiwan’s Indigenous peoples during the early Qing period (1684–1874) through documentary analysis. Major policies included the tongshi system, the Aboriginal Affairs Subprefect, restrictions on reclamation, acculturation and education, and tax reductions. These measures aimed to maintain social order, regulate Indigenous–Han relations, protect Indigenous livelihoods, and facilitate economic development. title: Complex Ecological Relationships and Scientific Non Recognition
abstract: This overview examines three contributions on Hector’s and Māui dolphins through an expert–AI inquiry into complex ecological relationships and scientific non-recognition. It asks how research programmes can produce accurate observations while leaving consequential causal connections untested. The contributions address the exclusion of records, the limited causal reach of demographic models, and allegations of institutional obstruction. title: Regulatory Trends in Ukraine’s Port Sector: Rules, Policies, and Risks
abstract: The article examines Ukraine’s port-sector regulatory framework for establishing public-private partnerships (PPPs), the risks to private investment in strategic maritime infrastructure, and how pre-war contracts cannot address military threats, destruction, operational disruption, and prolonged force majeure. title: Decomposing drivers of global temperature change after net zero
abstract: Abstract Net-zero CO2 (NZCO2) and greenhouse gas emission (GHG) targets are central to the development of mitigation scenarios. Projected global surface air temperature (GSAT) change after NZCO2 depends on several factors that broadly fall into two categories: scenario-specific factors that account for the diversity of possible mitigation pathways to net zero and beyond, and model-specific factors that describe the climate system response, captured in the zero emissions commitment (ZEC). title: Mesolithic discoveries at Dagsmosse
abstract: The Mesolithic of eastern Central Sweden is strongly associated with knapped quartz, pecked axes and a lack of preserved organic materials like bone, antler and wood. This picture stands in sharp contrast to the Mesolithic assemblages of Southern Scandinavia, rich in preserved organic remains. Many of the latter finds come from wetland sites. In this paper it it is argued that wetlands are often overlooked within contract archaeology and research in Central Sweden, exacerbating the problem. abstract: Bamboo-Based Headwater Conservation and Its Utilization as Alternative Energy in Facing Energy Crises and Military Threats. Bamboo management may connect headwater protection with local energy diversification, provided that biomass extraction does not undermine soil cover and ecological functions. This article examines the evidence supporting this connection through a focused narrative review of eleven journal articles published between 2020 and 2026. abstract: This article approaches the alternative protein transition by noting with the EAT-Lancet Commission that the existing world-food-system is a main driver of global warming. Building on eco-feminist and eco-Marxist critiques of the world-food-system, the article notes how this system organizes not only agriculture, animal husbandry, logistics, diets, and markets across the planet, but also profoundly unjust social relationships. title: Chasing Bubbles: Toward a Standardized Approach for Quantifying Methane Ebullition Using Bubble Traps in Streams and Rivers
abstract: Abstract Ebullition transports large quantities of the potent greenhouse gas methane (CH4) from stream sediments into the atmosphere. However, the use of different sampling designs complicates comparisons of CH4 emissions estimates between studies. Here, we present the first systematic review of sampling designs used in the past for assessing fluvial CH4 ebullition rates. abstract: This paper examines whether the Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras and Satiyaputras stood under Mauryan authority during the reign of Aśoka (r. 268/272–232/235 BCE), and if so, in what sense. title: Exploring the impact of corporate governance and external audit quality on creative accounting practices
abstract: The current study adopts a multivariate model to investigate the impact of board size, board independence, managerial ownership, audit committee independence, and external audit quality (proxied by audit fees) on creative accounting practices. Data for the study were obtained from commercial banks’ annual reports published on the Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) during the period from 2017 to 2021. abstract: Imagism – introduced by Ezra Pound – informs a theoretical paradigm for modern poetry writing. title: Conservation governance challenges in the Karakoram: Analyzing the institutional transitions of Central Karakoram National Park, Pakistan
abstract: Global commitments to conserve 30% of land by 2030 place renewed emphasis on protected areas (PAs), yet governance shortcomings and distributional conflicts often undermine both conservation and socio-economic development outcomes. This paper examines PA governance in Central Karakoram National Park (CKNP), Pakistan’s largest national park in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), a region marked by constitutional ambiguity, contested land tenure, and infrastructure-driven market integration. title: Enhancing Risk Knowledge in Civil Society Organization Leadership: Case‐Based Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT The escalating complexity of China's disaster risk landscape demands a new strategic leadership from civil society organizations (CSOs) to navigate systemic and cascading risks. While the national policies increasingly formalize the role of CSOs in disaster risk reduction (DRR), existing training provisions do not adequately develop the risk‐informed competencies required in practice. title: Climate Justice for Small States: Loss and Damage, and the Limits of International Law A Case Study of Timor-Leste
abstract: This article examines the structural inadequacies of international climate law in addressing loss and damage experienced by small, climate-vulnerable states, with particular reference to Timor-Leste. Grounding its analysis in Article 2 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Article 3 of the Paris Agreement, the article interrogates the tension between the aspirational language of climate justice and the operational constraints embedded within existing legal frameworks. abstract: Krisis iklim yang ditandai kenaikan suhu global, cuaca ekstrem, dan degradasi ekosistem menuntut perubahan perilaku yang berakar pada nilai, bukan sekadar pengetahuan. title: The Locust Motif as Political Commentary in Joe Ushie's A Reign Of Locusts
abstract: This study examines Joe Ushie's deployment of the locust motif as political commentary in A Reign of Locusts, analyzing how the poet transforms this biblical symbol into contemporary criticism of Nigeria's governance failures. Using archetypal criticism grounded in Carl Jung's analytical psychology and Northrop Frye's literary theory, the research investigates how Ushie uses the locust's collective and destructive nature to represent corrupt Nigerian political leadership. title: Paris as a Sporting City: Reframing the Past in the 2024 Olympic Games
abstract: The long history of French sport and tourism played an integral role in the Paris Olympics 2024’s planning. The Paris games transported spectators around the city and country to sporting facilities from different eras of France’s sporting development, each reflecting the desires and needs of governments and sports stakeholders working both in concert and in opposition. Olympic organizers showed how Paris as a sporting city centred on world class facilities, such as the Stade de France, but they also included atypical temporary spaces including the Chateau de Versailles. title: Commending the Non-Commissioned Officer's Leadership as a Predictor of Occupational Burnout and Operational Performance Among Junior Enlisted Personnel of the 560th Air Base Group
abstract: Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs) provide frontline guidance and support in demanding military environments, where operational workloads can affect personnel well-being and performance. This study described junior enlisted personnel’s assessments of NCO leadership, occupational burnout, and operational performance at the 560th Air Base Group, Brigadier General Benito N. title: From Farm to Table Measuring Host Communities’ Relationship with the Plant World in Instagram Tourism Reels
abstract: Regenerative tourism claims to move beyond sustainability by restoring ecosystems and communities, but whether its communication enacts that claim has not been measured. The article annotates ten Instagram reels and captions from five regenerative, sustainable and neoliberal accounts, across 34 nodes and 261 values, yielding 1,737 multimodal and 565 linguistic annotations. title: Translatability of Laf’dhul-Jalaalah: A Comparative Analysis of Yoruba Translations of the Holy Quran
abstract: This study examines the linguistic, theological, and cultural difficulties involved in rendering Lafḍhul Jalālah (“Allah”) into Yoruba language, with a comparative focus on four major Yoruba Qur’an translations: CT1, ST2, AT3, and MT4. title: La prevención del delito en la República Popular China: fundamentos normativos y proyección criminológica
abstract: This article offers a legal-criminological analysis of the Chinese public security system. It examines the normative, institutional, and technological foundations underpinning crime prevention in China, highlighting the integration of criminal law with broader policies and mechanisms of social supervision. The study explores how this framework enables early intervention against criminal behaviour while prioritising the collective interest. title: Urban Exodus After COVID-19? Internal Migration Trends Pre- and Post-pandemic in Germany
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been linked to increased net migration gains in suburban, peri-urban, and rural areas, at the expense of larger cities, contributing to suburbanization in many Western countries. Post-pandemic trends are less understood, but recent evidence indicates a return to pre-pandemic levels of internal migration intensity. This study examines internal migration trends in Germany in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, drawing on comprehensive flow data from 1991 to 2024. title: The Many Routes to the Ubiquitous Bradley–Terry Model
abstract: The rating of items based on pairwise comparisons has been a topic of statistical investigation for many decades. Numerous approaches have been proposed. One of the best known is the Bradley–Terry model. This paper seeks to assemble and explain a variety of motivations for its use. Some are based on principles or on maximizing an objective function; others are derived from well-known statistical models, or stylized game scenarios. They include both examples well-known in the literature as well as what are believed to be novel presentations.

title: Operational Accountability in U.S. Museum Collections: A Risk-Based Framework for Documentation, Inventory Verification, and Location and Movement Control
abstract: Catalogue records alone do not guarantee that a museum can account for its collections. Inventories, storage moves, audits, and reconciliation projects have exposed cases in which objects remained in institutional custody while their identity, legal status, location, or associated information had become uncertain. This structured narrative review draws on 23 sources, including 12 peer-reviewed publications, together with museum standards, audit findings, and institutional collections work. abstract: Despite rapid growth in electric vehicle (EV) adoption, few studies have systematically quantified how national income, urbanization, and income inequality are jointly associated with EV charging infrastructure worldwide.To address this gap, this study analyzed cross-sectional data from 100 countries spanning all world regions and income groups.Results show that GDP per capita is the strongest correlate of charger density (beta = +0.49,p < 0.001), with high-income countries reporting an average of 81 chargers per 100,000 people, compared to fewer than 1 in low-income countries.Urbanization als

abstract: Techniques of formalization are widely used in philosophy and other disciplines as tools for analysis and research. While epistemological and methodological aspects of formalization have received quite some attention in the meta-philosophical literature, the politics of formalization—the entanglements of formalization with power relations, and in particular the impact of formalization for projects of liberation or oppression—has received comparatively little attention. title: Across North America: Reginald Arthur Lorrain and the Making of a Missionary
abstract: This article examines the North American years (1899–1902) of Reginald Arthur Lorrain, an Englishman who subsequently served for several decades as a Christian missionary among the Maras of the Indo-Burma borderland. Drawing on Lorrain’s unpublished personal diary, the study traces his passage through the agricultural, industrial, and itinerant-labour economies of Manitoba, Ontario, and the southern United States, and argues that the hardship, physical risk, and social marginality he encountered there constituted a formative, if unintended, preparation for his later missionary vocation. title: Looking back, looking ahead: Local perspectives on landscape changes and native‐tree restoration in Madagascar
abstract: Abstract Across sub‐Saharan Africa, tree‐based restoration efforts are dominated by exotic tree species due to their rapid biomass accumulation and short‐term economic returns. abstract: Abstract Ecosystem restoration is a crucial response to human‐induced land degradation, which threatens biodiversity and ecosystem functions, poses food and water insecurity and undermines livelihoods, cultural values and human–nature relationships. For restoration to be effective and equitable, it is essential to understand how social and ecological factors interact to shape restoration processes and outcomes. abstract: This study examines perceived price volatility, service quality, and store loyalty in relation to grocery-store choice in Mahakam Ulu. abstract: Climate change and water-related disasters significantly affect water security and livelihoods, particularly in vulnerable communities. In Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), women often bear the burden of domestic water collection, yet their role in water governance remains limited. The objective of this study was to examine gendered dimensions of access to water security and participation in water-related decision-making across household, community, and institutional levels in Lao PDR. title: Extension Demonstrations and Field Days for Promoting Climate-Resilient Alley Cropping: A Case of Glen Arm, Maryland
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an extension field day in increasing participants’ knowledge, perception of sustainability, and willingness to adopt climate-resilient alley cropping (CRAC) in Glen Arm, Maryland. The field day included a tour to the demonstration site along with a classroom participatory discussion on key CRAC practices, including vegetables, fruit trees, cover cropping, water harvesting, composting, mulching, and integrated pest management. abstract: Abstract: The global burden of female infertility is substantial and rising, with environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EEDs) now recognized as important modifiable contributors. abstract: Background and objectives: Antimicrobial stewardship initiatives are designed to improve the appropriateness of antimicrobial use and thereby maximize benefits and minimize risks. Qualitative research with key stakeholders in human and animal health is critical to inform a One Health definition and to support global stewardship efforts. abstract: Population visibility, daily interactions, institutional responses, material constraints and community solidarity all need to be taken into consideration in understanding perceptions of social change in refugee hosting contexts. This study analyzes the primary survey data of 460 respondents from villages supporting Rohingya refugees and villages adjacent to Rohingya refugee camps in Bangladesh. abstract: The current study aims to investigate the multimodal features employed in the "Devil True Heirs" digital poster in constructing meaning and to uncover the underlying ideologies conveyed through its multimodal design. A descriptive qualitative approach was adopted, with the digital poster as the sole unit of analysis. abstract: This paper introduces FOWT-Benchmark, an open-source state-space benchmark model for diagnosis and control studies on floating offshore wind turbines (FOWT). abstract: This study critically reinterprets human rights values embedded in the Qur’an and Hadith through the philosophical hermeneutics of Hans-Georg Gadamer and Paul Ricoeur in contemporary Muslim societies. abstract: This study examines the determinants of student dropout in Tanzanian government secondary schools over the period 2020–2024. abstract: The period 1993-1999 was a challenging period for the Nigerian Armed Forces as it was a period which saw the imposition of sanctions on Nigeria’s military regimes by Western Countries following the refusal of the military to return power to civilian rule in the aftermath of the annulment of a democratic election in 1993. abstract: Little is known about the cognitive health of older adults living in rural Ecuador, where more than 70% of the rural population experiences multidimensional poverty. abstract: Abstract Climate change does not only impact farmers, but the perception and adaptive capacities of local stakeholders have not been well studied. abstract: This study examines taxpayers' perceptions of the tax concept through metaphors. Metaphor analysis is an effective tool for revealing how taxpayers make sense of the tax concept. This research used qualitative data collection techniques to compile and thematically classify metaphors produced by taxpayers from different sociodemographic groups about taxation. abstract: The presence of the Banjarese ethnic group in Malaysia dates back to the late 19th and early 20th centuries when mass migration from South Kalimantan began. As one of the ethnic minorities in Malaysia, the Banjarese have had to adapt their way of life and coexist with various other ethnicities. abstract: Abstract This paper reinterprets Epicurean ethics as a strategic lens for sustainable capitalism, emphasizing its relevance beyond traditional philosophical discourse. By focusing on the concepts of ataraxia (tranquility) and aponia (absence of bodily pain), the article proposes a pragmatic ethical framework for business leaders navigating ecological and social challenges. abstract: Visible innovation does not establish the continuity of living performance traditions. This article examines how selective change relates to continuing practice in Janger Banyuwangi, Indonesia. abstract: The number of people living with dementia and related costs continue to grow worldwide. Although generally associated with memory difficulties, non-cognitive symptoms of dementia are common and usually stem from unmet needs. abstract: This study investigated many organisations that have ethics problems even though they have many laws. abstract: Air pollution remains a major environmental and global health concern, particularly in industrial areas where emissions from factories impact air quality and human well-being. This study examines the perception of air pollution and its associated health risks among residents living near a steel factory in Ifelodun Local Government, Kwara State, Nigeria. abstract: This study analyzes the fiscal independence of Tidore Islands City during 2021–2025, identifies factors associated with low Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD), and formulates measures to strengthen local fiscal capacity. abstract: Abstract Estonian companies increasingly recognise the importance of corporate social responsibility (CSR), yet their understanding of its substantive link to equal treatment remains limited. Although employers often include equality principles in internal policies, such commitments are largely declaratory and reflect a narrow understanding of equal treatment, often reducing it to the gender pay gap. abstract: Despite many technical factors such as water quality, biosecurity, and infrastructure impacting the success of intensive shrimp farming, the successful implementation of these requirements also depends on the workers' engagement. abstract: This study examined the influence of Performance Appraisal Practice and Cultural Intelligence on Employee Performance mediated by Employee Engagement among Generation Z and millennial employees in Jakarta's creative industry. abstract: Abstract Parliamentary committees are critical venues of legislative work. abstract: The decline of indigenous languages threatens linguistic diversity, cultural identity, and the intergenerational transmission of heritage. This study examined the factors influencing language shift and dialect drift in the survival of the Eastern Subanen dialect in Purok 4, Lampasan, Don Victoriano, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. abstract: The growing environmental crisis threatening the sustainability of tourist destinations in Indonesia calls for a management framework that is not only ecological and economic, but also ethical-theological. abstract: Accelerated carbonation of recycled concrete aggregates (RCA) can fix CO₂ while modifying aggregate properties, but most reported uptake values come from laboratory-produced aggregates that do not reproduce the heterogeneity of material leaving a real recycling line. abstract: Türkiye has become a prominent player in mediation diplomacy since 2003, as the Justice and Development Party (AKP) have prioritized mediation engagements across the world, leveraging it as a strategic instrument of Turkish foreign policy. abstract: Prominent calls have been made to radically shift current teaching provision in higher education towards critically ‘transformative’ pedagogies that align with the pressing imperatives of sustainability. abstract: Hunter‐based monitoring programs offer a cost‐effective approach to large‐scale wildlife monitoring, but their performance depends on sufficient observation effort and robust assessment of estimate precision. abstract: Military service exposes personnel not only to life threat but also to events that violate deeply held moral beliefs, such as killing, failing to prevent harm, or being betrayed by trusted leaders. title: Ultrathin passive cooling coatings with high solar reflectance via pore-engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce cooling-related energy consumption; however, achieving near-unity solar reflectance and strong thermal emissivity in thin, scalable coatings remains a non-trivial challenge. Here, we demonstrate that pore-size-engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) can serve as efficient scattering elements in polymer nanocomposite coatings for radiative cooling. title: The Dynamics of Corporate Crime and "Follow the Money" in the Tin Mining Scandal: Challenges for Indonesian Special Criminal Law
abstract: The tin mining scandal in Indonesia reveals the complexities of corporate crime, which inflicts massive financial and economic losses upon the state. This normative legal study analyzes the dynamics of corporate criminal liability and the effectiveness of the "follow the money" approach in tracing and recovering assets derived from mining-related crimes. The findings indicate that the current special criminal law regime faces substantial challenges particularly in applying the doctrines of vicarious liability and identification theory to link the actions of corporate officers to schemes of cor

title: The critical foundations of truly sustainable environmental auditing
abstract: This essay addresses the urgent need for transformative action in environmental governance by exploring the role and essential functionality of environmental auditing. While critical scholarship has questioned the overemphasis on reporting in both research and practice, this essay promotes the obligation on critical accountants and auditing researchers to actively debate and develop the concept of environmental audit, rather than accepting it as a given by businesses, audit providers, policymakers, standard setters, and regulatory authorities. title: Teaching mythology with video games: two workshops for secondary education
abstract: Abstract There is a long history of integrating games in classical pedagogy, although most of these studies have focused on history teaching or Latin and Greek language acquisition. In this article, I extend prior research on antiquity game-based learning to illustrate how video games can also be used for mythology education, or the familiarity with particular stories and characters which have inspired artworks, political movements, and other cultural phenomena throughout history. After outlining the different ways in which video games present Greco-Roman myth, I present two workshops which I

title: Law after empire
abstract: This paper examines how legal knowledge circulates in post-colonial contexts, arguing that the authority of law after empire is produced through the ongoing movement of people, institutions, and epistemic practices along new and old imperial routes. Drawing on comparative research on three regional courts, the Caribbean Court of Justice, the now-shut down Central American Court of Justice, and the East African Court of Justice, the paper reframes post-colonial legality not as a story of transplantation, diffusion, or mere dependency, but as a dynamic process of circulation and translation. title: Termitomyces striatus : A Novel Mycofood With a Rational Pharmacological Approach
abstract: The folk population of India has a mycophilic inclination, and wild mushrooms may help sustain their livelihood. One such wild mushroom has been reported from India and is traditionally consumed as a myco‐food by ethnic communities. ITS rDNA‐based phylogenetic analysis identified the collected mushroom as Termitomyces striatus . To explore its therapeutic prospects, an ethanol extract (TP‐ETH) was prepared. title: A common pathogenic founder variant in Rwandan breast cancer cases
abstract: Germline data from African populations remain sparse, limiting characterization of population-specific BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants (PV). In a study of 175 Rwandan women with breast cancer, 7 unrelated carriers (4% of cases; 22% of PV carriers) harbored the same BRCA1 frameshift PVs, c.4065_4068del (p.Asn1355Lysfs*10), which is extremely rare in gnomAD yet recurrent in European, Asian, and Middle Eastern cohorts. Whole-exome sequencing and haplotype analysis of all 7 carriers revealed a shared ancestral block of approximately 581 kb surrounding the variant, and extended haplotype homozygosity a

title: Canid’s cradle: multigrain den site selection by wolves on the Scandinavian Peninsula
abstract: Carnivores can have different habitat requirements and vary in their sensitivity to disturbance across stages of their life cycle, particularly during reproduction. Despite being highly adaptable and able to tolerate substantial human disturbance, wolves ( Canis lupus ), may rely on specific habitat characteristics when selecting den sites to reduce human-related risks and enhance pup survival. Using multi-grain resource selection functions (MRSFs), we evaluated resource selection at wolf den sites. title: La cabaña del tío Tom: análisis traductológico de una adaptación al español dirigida a un público juvenil
abstract: La obra Uncle Tom’s Cabin de Harriet Beecher Stowe es un clásico de la literatura publicado en 1852 que denuncia la situación racista que vivían las personas de color estadounidenses, quienes, por su etnia, estaban sometidas al esclavismo de la época. La relevancia de la obra fue tal que incluso se consideró uno de los detonantes de la Guerra de Secesión y, rápidamente, empezó a traducirse a cientos de idiomas, siendo uno de ellos el español. journal: SKOPOS Revista Internacional de Traducción e Interpretación

title: Cultured Mining Governance in the Perspective of Siyasah Dusturiyah: Evidence from Sand Mining in Boyolali Regency
abstract: Mining activities in Boyolali Regency provide economic benefits but also generate socio-environmental and governance challenges. This study examines sand and rock mining governance through the perspective of Siyasah Dusturiyah and proposes a governance model based on prophetic values. Using a socio-legal approach, the study analyzes mining practices in Cepogo, Musuk, and Selo District through field findings, legal analysis, and environmental data. journal: Journal of Law Politic and Humanities

title: Understanding the Basic Concepts of International Law
abstract: International law is often described as a system lacking a legislature, a compulsory judiciary and a central enforcement authority. These institutional limitations have long prompted questions about its status as law. This article reviews the fundamental concepts that give the discipline its structure and coherence. Adopting a doctrinal and conceptual approach, it draws on principal treaties, the jurisprudence of the International Court of Justice and leading scholarship, while setting aside historical narrative and detailed institutional analysis. journal: International Scholar Journal of Arts and Social Science Research

title: Enhancing Experimental Reliability Through Rainfall Simulator Calibration Under Intense Rainfall Rates
abstract: Acknowledging the benefit of Rainfall Simulators (RS) is continuously growing among researcher, mainly for laboratory-scale models where natural rainfall is either unavailable or inconsistent. RS put forward a reliable platform for replicating specific rainfall events under standardized set-up, making them invaluable for erosion, hydrology, and slope stability research needs. The present work offered a cost-effective Dripping Rainfall Simulator (DRS) for application on a 1.2 m² test plot area. title: Effectiveness of a structured educational program on knowledge about medication errors and stress of conscience among psychiatric nurses
abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication errors are a persistent threat to patient safety in psychiatric settings, where complex pharmacotherapy and ethical conscience heighten nurses' stress of conscience. AIM: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a structured educational program on knowledge about medication errors and stress of conscience among psychiatric nurses. METHODS: A one-group pre-post quasi-experimental design was implemented with 89 nurses from Assiut University Psychiatric Hospital and at Assiut Mental Health Hospital (Ministry of Health hospital), Egypt. title: ESCHATOKRATIA AS THE IDEAL REGIME IN HOMER
abstract: This paper explores the ideal regime in Homeric epics from the perspective of political philosophy, challenging both the "pre-political" taxonomies of political anthropology and the exclusionary Platonic-Aristotelian legacy. By adopting Luc Ferry’s distinction between moral and existential values, the study argues that Homeric sovereignty is rooted in the human encounter with mortality and finitude. title: La policía bajo la mirada de las chicas: un estudio cualitativo sobre experiencias, control y legitimidad policial
abstract: Over recent decades, criminological research has paid increasing attention to citizens’ perceptions of the police. However, studies on young people’s perceptions remain limited, particularly among underrepresented groups. This article examines the perceptions of a group of girls with histories of offending, drawing on their experiences of police contact. Through 32 biographical interviews and thematic analysis, the meanings attributed to these interactions are explored. title: Languages, Memory and Religion: The Literature of the Morisco Diaspora
abstract: ABSTRACT Literature written by the Moriscos during their diaspora in North Africa, especially in the 17th century, offers three fundamental pillars for its analysis: the languages in which it is written, their emotional and intellectual relationship with their land of origin and their host countries, and, finally, religion. Through the combination of these pillars, it can be observed how Morisco texts are essentially Islamic texts, but, at the same time, texts embedded in the Spanish culture of their time. title: La criminalización de la pobreza: un enfoque desde la Criminología y el Derecho Penal
abstract: The criminalization of poverty raises questions about how socioeconomic conditions shape exposure to institutional control and the consequences of criminal justice involvement. This study aimed to analyze the normative, procedural, and sanctioning mechanisms associated with this relationship and their criminological and legal implications. A critical synthesis of recent empirical research was organized around three dimensions: coercive regulation of subsistence activities, inequalities during criminal proceedings, and the economic effects of sanctions. journal: Journal of Economic and Social Science Research

title: Medicine and Mass Incarceration
abstract: American jails and prisons are ripe for analysis by medical humanities scholars. Carceral institutions have been an especially salient feature of American history since the late-twentieth century, when U.S. incarceration rates began surging and culminated in what has come to be known as "mass incarceration." This article suggests a handful of topics medical humanities scholars might consider in relation to mass incarceration, including correctional medical care privatization, the drug war, and HIV/AIDS, chronic diseases, women's health, aging, and death in prisons. title: The conditions for digital integration: A comparative case study of three TVET colleges in KwaZulu-Natal
abstract: Digital technology has spread unevenly through South Africa’s public technical and vocational education and training (TVET) colleges. This article examines what determines whether the technology available to a college becomes part of everyday teaching. It reports on a comparative study of three public TVET colleges in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), ranging from a well-connected urban college to a dispersed rural college, drawing on interviews with managers, institutional documents and three complementary theoretical perspectives. journal: Journal of vocational, adult and continuing education and training

title: ‘Hymen Checks’ – Assessing the Use of Two-Finger Tests in India’s Judicial Discourse on Rape
abstract: Abstract Two-finger test refers to the physical examination of female genitalia for the purpose of determining virginity. This colonial-era test is invasive and degrading, has no scientific basis, and can neither prove nor disprove allegations of rape. In 2013, the Indian Supreme Court emphasised that this archaic test violates the right to privacy, bodily integrity and dignity of the rape prosecutrix. title: Divergent approaches to the accommodation of substate demoi in Canada and the United States
abstract: Abstract Canada and the United States both have populations in which racial and ethnic minorities, substate national societies, native peoples and majority groups coexist. In this article, I contrast the United States and Canada, focusing on their contrasting political cultures, models of federation, legal nation-building mechanisms and so forth, in order to evaluate these states’ potential for accommodating minority nations. First, I analyze how Canada’s multicultural and multinational political culture has encouraged the recognition of substate national societies through a decentralized mode

title: Rilvegostomig Plus Trastuzumab-Deruxtecan for Early-Stage Breast Cancer
abstract: Importance: The I-SPY2.2 trial tests personalized treatment strategies to improve outcomes while reducing exposure to standard chemotherapy in patients with high-risk early breast cancer (EBC). Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd), an antibody drug conjugate targeting low ERBB2 (formerly HER2) expression, combined with rilvegostomig (R), a bispecific antibody targeting programmed cell death 1 protein and T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain as initial therapy in I-SPY2.2 (RT-DXd). title: Reconstructing spore evolution recalibrates the timescale of land plant diversification
abstract: The origin and evolution of land plants precipitated fundamental changes to the Earth system and enabled the diversification of life on land. Their early evolution is documented by a rich fossil record of sporopollenin-walled spores that is difficult to interpret because the evolution of plant spore characteristics is unresolved. We employ a suite of ancestral state estimation methods to elucidate the pattern of spore character evolution among land plants. title: The life and work of Ernest Sydney Keeping
abstract: Abstract This article reviews the life and contributions of Ernest S. Keeping (1895–1984), a British‐born physicist who became a mathematics professor at the University of Alberta in 1929. He played a pivotal role in shaping the university's Mathematics Department, serving as its head from 1954 to 1961, and continuing to teach until 1970, nine years after his official retirement. Recognized for his research and dedication to promoting statistics, particularly through the publication of educational materials, Keeping was one of the first honorary members of the Statistical Society of Canada. title: The Influence of Human Resource Competencies, Internal Control Systems, and Service Innovation on Financial Performance
abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of human resource (HR) competence, internal control systems, and service innovation on the financial performance of PT Pelindo Jasa Maritim Region 4. The research employed a quantitative approach by distributing questionnaires to 53 respondents consisting of management, finance, and operational staff across five operational areas of PT Pelindo Region 4. The data were analysed using multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that HR competence has a positive effect on financial performance, particularly in the understanding of accounting standards

title: LANGUAGE IN THE POETRY COLLECTION MUSĀFIR WA-NĀSIK BY MUḤAMMAD IBN ʿABD AL-RAḤMĀN ĀL ʿABD AL-QĀDIR
abstract: This study examines the linguistic levels in the poetry collection Musāfir wa-Nāsik by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Āl ʿAbd al-Qādir, at four levels: the syntactic, the morphological, the phonological, and the lexical. It follows a reciprocal approach that joins grounding in theory with the application of rules to texts, combining the descriptive and the inductive methods by tracing selected examples in the collection and then recording the phenomenon each illustrates. title: Improved European native seed supply chains are essential for the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation
abstract: Abstract To support the implementation of the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR), there is an unprecedented need to scale up ecosystem restoration, which requires radical improvements to the European seed supply chain, especially for herbaceous species. The fundamental tradeoff between the need for local provenance and climate resilience, as well as practical constraints on seed availability, generates a bottleneck for restoration practice and may jeopardize the implementation of the NRR. title: Intelligent Democracy and Intelligent Epistocracy
abstract: In Intelligent Democracy, Jonathan Benson defends democracy’s epistemic merits. However, rather than focusing on the abilities of individual democratic institutions, Benson advocates a systemic perspective according to which we must understand how different institutions, each with their own strengths and weaknesses, interact to achieve more in aggregate than any could alone. title: History and current value of ancient barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) varieties – a review
abstract: Ancient barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) varieties were not subjected to modern breeding. They were well adapted to their environment but lost importance over time due to the development and cultivation of higher-yielding varieties. This contributed to a loss of plant genetic resources. However, in the context of climate change and a growing population, as well as increasing consumer interest in new and high-quality products, these ancient barley varieties are receiving renewed attention. This review provides a history of ancient barley varieties, as well as an overview of the available data regard

title: Blue-eyed bargains: Nazi-era acquisitions at the museum of far eastern antiquities in Sweden
abstract: This article examines the provenance of cultural objects acquired by the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities in Stockholm during the National Socialist era. Taking the 1937 acquisition of two Chinese bronze tripods from Josef Plaut as its point of departure, the study investigates the circumstances of the sale in relation to the Washington Principles and the Terezín Declaration. The analysis subsequently expands to the museum’s acquisition practices between 1933 and 1938. This process identifies a further case involving the 1934 acquisition of books and journals from the scholar Alfred Salmony.

title: Unlocking Affixes in the ESL Community College Classroom: The Language of Law, Science, and Technology
abstract: Since vocabulary plays a significant role in second language acquisition, expansive vocabulary targets should be set and pursued. This paper explores the results of introducing affixes to develop vocabulary and increase motivation for beginner to intermediate-level English language learners (ELLs) pursuing academic disciplines in law, science, and technology at a New York City community college. journal: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research

title: Human dimensions of Asiatic black bear presence in Akita City, Japan
abstract: Human-bear interactions with Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus) are increasing in Japan. Examining public perceptions towards bears and bear management is timely with shifting lethal control legislation and rapid spread of negative human-bear interactions throughout Japan. Akita City is one site of recent upsurge in social conflict triggered by increasing human-bear conflict. title: Efforts to Combat Illegal Cigarettes by the Medan Customs and Excise Office
abstract: The circulation of illegal cigarettes is an excise crime that threatens state revenue and can distort competition in the tobacco industry. This study examines how the Medan Customs and Excise Supervision and Service Office of Intermediate Customs Type B (KPPBC TMP B Medan) handles the circulation of illegal cigarettes through preventive and repressive law enforcement. It also adopts a statutory approach that examines the relevant laws and regulations. The research applies an empirical-juridical approach and legal interpretation based on statutory provisions. title: Incorporación del informe respaldatorio del instructor en el reglamento de disciplina para los centros de formación policial ante la impugnación de sanciones por faltas leves y medias del aspirante a servidor policial
abstract: La normativa sancionatoria de los centros de formación policial es un mecanismo fundamental para cimentar la disciplina de una institución jerarquizada; aplicada de manera objetiva, proporcional y conforme al debido proceso, ayuda a que el aspirante a servidor policial comprenda las normas y asuma la responsabilidad de sus actos, por lo que ninguna norma disciplinaria debe aplicarse de modo que vulnere los derechos humanos. title: SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL AND MANAGEMENT IN THE LECTURE AREAS OF FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC BIDA, NIGERIA
abstract: Solid waste, a type of land pollution comprises of any discarded solid or semi-solid material resulting from anthropogenic and animal activities in households, industry, institutions, commercial establishments, and public spaces. The research aims to study solid wastes disposal and management in the lecture areas of the Federal Polytechnic, Bida. Descriptive research design was employed for the research. 100 questionnaires were administered to the respondents, inclusive of 60 students, 20 academic staff and 20 administrative staff based on the proportion of their population size. title: A Comparative Conceptual Analysis of "bənê hā'ĕlōhîm" ("Sons of God") in the Qur'ān and Jewish Texts: Examining the Attribution of Polytheism to Jews in the Story of 'Uzayr in Qur'ān
abstract: This paper offers a comparative conceptual analysis of the expression bənê hā’ĕlōhîm (בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “Sons of God”) within Jewish theology and the Qur’ānic reference to ʿUzayr in verse Q 9:30. Employing an intertextual framework informed by Julia Kristeva’s theory of textual transposition and late antique Qur’anic hermeneutics, this study reassesses the dialogue between the Qur’anic corpus and its Biblical/post-Biblical subtexts. title: Bringing social cohesion into forest landscape restoration: Identifying future pathways toward more integrated social‐ecological restoration
abstract: Abstract Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) is increasingly recognized as a key strategy to address land degradation, biodiversity loss and climate change. However, its long‐term success depends not only on ecological outcomes but also on social processes that shape restoration implementation and sustainability. This study explores the relationship between social cohesion and FLR in central Togo, examining how social cohesion influences FLR implementation and how participation in restoration activities can, in turn, shape social cohesion. institutions: Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research

title: Anonymita nebo peníze: jak české dezinformační weby (ne)dodržují zákony
abstract: Článek se zabývá finančními příjmy českých dezinformačních webů a otázkou, zda tyto weby dodržují relevantní právní regulaci. Téma vychází z existujícího výzkumu, který identifikuje finanční příjem generovaný prostřednictvím online obsahu jako důležitý faktor motivující řadu aktérů k vytváření a šíření dezinformací. Tento článek navazuje na výzkum finanční motivace dezinformátorů v českém prostředí, na jehož základě identifikuje tři relevantní zdroje finančních příjmů dezinformačních webů: online reklamu, neoznačenou reklamu a příspěvky čtenářstva, na které se zaměřuje provedená právní a obsah
journal: Časopis pro právní vědu a praxi

title: Older adults’ intention to use extended reality in China’s Yellow River Basin: an extended Technology Acceptance Model with intergenerational support
abstract: As older adults become an important segment of China’s tourism market and family-based multigenerational travel becomes more prevalent, extended reality (XR)-enabled cultural heritage tourism raises a broader question about older adults’ access to technology-mediated cultural participation. Although XR may enrich cultural heritage tourism, older adults’ engagement with XR may be shaped by digital barriers and varying levels of family-based support. title: Geopolitical Risk, Commodity Prices, and Islamic Stock Index Performance: The Role of Macroeconomic Factors
abstract: This study analyzes the influence of geopolitical risk, oil prices, and gold prices on the performance of Islamic stock indices and examines the role of exchange rates and inflation as moderating variables. Monthly data from the Dow Jones Islamic Market (DJIM) during the conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East between February 2022 and October 2024 were analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with STATA. title: Criminal governance and the shift from local to transnational actor: a case study on the evolution of the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC)
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the relationship between criminal governance and the internationalization of organized crime, using the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) expansion towards Europe as a case study. It argues that governance can facilitate the transnational expansion of criminal organizations by fostering internal cohesion, regulating illicit markets, and enabling civilian control. title: Peran Keputusan Pembelian Dalam Membentuk Kepuasan Pelanggan Pada E-Commerce Fashion Di Kota Depok
abstract: Perkembangan e-commerce telah meningkatkan persaingan pada industri fashion sehingga pelaku usaha perlu memperhatikan kualitas produk, kualitas layanan, dan promosi penjualan untuk mendorong keputusan pembelian dan meningkatkan kepuasan pelanggan. title: Preferencias y motivaciones en la selección de personajes de videojuegos: un estudio de género e identidad en América Latina
abstract: This study analyzes the motivations and preferences behind the selection of video game characters among Latin American players of different genders. The objective is to explore players’ preferences regarding the characters they choose and to understand the engagement dynamics and interpretations they construct around characters of different genders. A quantitative online survey was conducted in several Latin American countries between April and May 2024, yielding 1,305 valid responses. title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
abstract: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. title: Learning Ethics in the Qur’an
abstract: The ethics of learning constitute an essential aspect of Islamic education—particularly within pesantren (Islamic boarding schools)—which demands a balance between the mastery of knowledge and the cultivation of character. The narrative of Prophet Moses and al-Khiḍr in Q.S. Al-Kahf [18]: 65–82 provides a Qur’anic basis for examining these dimensions of learning. This study aims to analyze the ethics of learning in the narrative and their relevance to contemporary pesantren education through a tafsīr tarbawī approach. title: Cultured Meat is (not) Vegan Meat Discursive Boundary-Making in User Comments
abstract: The production of cultured meat is gaining regulatory approval in countries worldwide, with the global market being estimated to grow substantially over the next few years. However, its recognition as an effective technology in tackling issues concerning human health, the environment, and animal welfare has been received with mixed feelings across different countries. Given its defining principles, the issue is particularly relevant to the vegan community, which has embraced opposing perspectives on it. journal: Annali di Ca’ Foscari Serie occidentale

title: Beyond the campervan lifestyle: A social cartography of contemporary campervan tourism
abstract: Campervan tourism has become an increasingly important segment of outdoor recreation and tourism, with growing economic, environmental, and territorial impacts. Despite its relevance, research has largely focused on specific subcultures, destinations, or sustainability issues, and a systematic understanding of campervan users as a differentiated social population remains lacking. This article addresses that gap through the largest empirical study of campervan users currently available in the academic literature (N = 2845). title: Un émulo de La Fontaine en Inglaterra: John Gay, el primer escritor inglés de fábulas en verso
abstract: El presente artículo versa sobre el escritor inglés John Gay, considerado en su país como uno de los mejores poetas burlescos y satíricos de su época; más concretamente de su obra The Fables, que consta de sesenta y ocho fábulas: cincuenta publicadas en 1727, a las que se añadieron dieciocho en 1738. abstract: During 2013 (Gulf of Aqaba) and 2020/2022 (Oman), extensive sampling efforts were conducted, covering two areas of the northwestern Indian ocean. title: When Alexander Did Not Visit Jerusalem in 332-331 BCE
abstract: The famous legend of Alexander the Great’s respectful visit to Jerusalem represents the positive relationship between Hellenistic kings and the Jewish people. We can prove that this event never happened. The question becomes how and why the story developed. The tale concludes with the invitation to the Jews to enlist in his army, and their acceptance illustrates the loyalty of Jewish soldiers in Alexander’s armies and those of his successors, the Seleukids and the Ptolemies, for over a century and a half.

abstract: Abstract Pathogenic spillovers from animals into humans have catalyzed epidemics throughout history. They result from multiple factors. title: A multidimensional assessment of household vulnerability to coastal hazards and its determinants in Odisha’s coastal districts
abstract: Abstract Coastal households in eastern India are increasingly affected by recurrent cyclones, flooding, storm surges, salinity intrusion, and coastal erosion, yet household-level evidence on multidimensional vulnerability remains limited. This study assesses household vulnerability to coastal hazards in Puri and Kendrapara districts of Odisha, India, and identifies the major socio-economic and preparedness-related determinants of vulnerability. abstract: Sacrifice zones – territories marked by environmental contamination and socio-economic marginalisation – embody inequalities produced by uneven capitalist development. These socio-spatial formations are produced through the uneven distribution of environmental burdens and through spatial imaginaries that render certain places and populations expendable, normalise degradation, and constrain alternative possibilities. abstract: In the present paper we report the results of taxonomic analysis through morphological and molecular tools of Ianiropsis (Isopoda) specimens collected in the lagoon of Venice in Italy within Marine Strategy Framework Directive monitoring campaigns. Six specimens previously identified as Ianiropsis serricaudis by morphological analysis were assigned with high confidence to Ianiropsis epilittoralis through barcode sequence analysis of the partial COI gene. title: Prevalencia de enfermedades coralinas y blanqueamiento en 2019 en Akumal, un sistema arrecifal bajo presión antropogénica
abstract: Introduction: Globally, coral reefs are undergoing an unprecedented crisis characterized by rapid structural and functional degradation associated with cumulative local pressures and climate change. In the Mexican Caribbean, conservation efforts implemented since the 1990s were associated with a relatively stable trend in reef condition between the mid-1990s and the mid-2010s; however, since 2018, an intensification of disturbances has been observed, marked by disease outbreaks and mass bleaching associated with high mortality rates. title: ‘You Will Die at Sea’: dying with poetry in Mediterranean borderscapes
abstract: This essay examines the role of poetry as a medium of survival, testimony and ethical witness in the context of Mediterranean migration crises, focusing on the works of Eritrean poet Segen Tesfalidet and Sudanese poet Abdel Wahab Yousif (Latino). Through their verses and prophetic compositions, these poets navigate the liminality of borderised zones, transforming sites of disposability and necropolitics into spaces of self-documentation, communal memory and resilience. title: Instability is not the only driver of rubble impacts on coral settlement and recruitment
abstract: Abstract Beds of dead coral rubble are widely reported to impede coral recovery, and causation has been linked to rubble instability. However, additional environmental factors, including flow and sedimentation, may also impact coral recruitment in this habitat. Indeed, the drivers of coral recruitment likely differ with the type of rubble. title: Severe environmental disturbances compromise ecological thresholds in aquatic environments
abstract: Large-scale disturbances can profoundly alter aquatic ecosystems by modifying water chemistry, sediment dynamics, and biodiversity across connected freshwater and marine environments. The 2015 Fundão Dam collapse in Brazil provides an unprecedented context to evaluate how multiple aquatic communities respond to intense and prolonged contamination, revealing key mechanisms of community reorganization under chronic anthropogenic impacts. title: Logistical competition and risk in wheat trade and impacts of changes in Black Sea shipping
abstract: Abstract Geopolitical disruptions in the Black Sea have increased maritime shipping risks, constrained port capacity, and accelerated the development of alternative Russian grain-export routes through the Baltic and Caspian Seas. This study examines how these changes affect maritime logistics, port competition, and global wheat trade. We develop a monthly stochastic minimum-cost network-flow model using Optimized Monte Carlo Simulation (OMCS) that incorporates uncertainty in export prices, ocean freight rates, export supply, import demand, and port capacity. title: Distribution of hydrocarbons, trace metals, and physico-chemical properties of sediments in an Estuarine Ecosystem in Rivers State (Nigeria): Ecological risk assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT This research quantified the spatiotemporal distribution of hydrocarbons, trace metals and sediment characteristics in a Niger Delta estuarine creek (Rivers State, Nigeria). Monthly grab samples (0-5 cm) were obtained over a one-year period (January-December 2025) from three stations; compositing (nine samples/station-month) provided 36 samples. Sediments were extracted and analysed for TPH, 16PAHs, Zn, Ni, Cd, Fe, Cr and Co, in addition to pH, EC, TOC, TON and P. title: Microplastic Contamination of Marine and Freshwater Fish in Nigeria: Occurrence, Particle Characteristics, Distribution, Ecological Implications and Human-health Concerns
abstract: Nigeria combines a large burden of mismanaged plastic waste with strong dietary reliance on fish, which makes the contamination of fish by microplastics a question of ecological and public-health relevance. Field studies on Nigerian fish have multiplied since the first report from a municipal water-supply lake, yet earlier syntheses either predate most of this evidence or pool fish with water, sediment, salt and other matrices. abstract: ABSTRACT To avoid competition, species partition resource‐use along various niche axes. However, variable resource availability, especially within dynamic environments, may influence this partitioning. Theory predicts that species will contract their ecological niche to limit competition during times of resource scarcity. We analysed blood δ 13 C and δ 15 N composition in four albatrosses, four penguin, two giant petrel and two fur seal species breeding on sub‐Antarctic Marion Island, during two seasons (autumn and summer) over 3 years. This study integrates whole‑rock major–trace element data from Rajang–Crocker and Neogene successions in Sabah with detrital zircon U–Pb age spectra to reconstruct source‑to‑sink evolution and to evaluate the relative contribution of first‑cycle and recycled sediment sources. title: Satellite-observed characteristics and prediction of internal solitary waves in the Maluku Sea
abstract: Internal solitary waves (ISWs) are frequently observed in the Indonesian seas, where strong tides, complex topography, and stratified water masses generate energetic internal wave activity. The Maluku Sea is a key passage linking the western Pacific, Celebes Sea, and Banda Sea, yet the long-term characteristics and predictability of satellite-visible ISW signatures remain insufficiently documented. title: Seasonal Changes in Aquatic Fungal Communities of a Coastal Lagoon (Ria de Aveiro, Portugal)
abstract: Despite the ecological and economic importance of Ria de Aveiro, Portugal, little is known about the diversity and seasonal dynamics of fungal communities. We analysed fungal communities in water samples from eight sites, during four seasonal campaigns, using DNA metabarcoding of the ITS1 region. A total of 12,929 ASVs (1,871,816 reads) were obtained, affiliated with 16 fungal phyla, though 33.9% of the reads could not be assigned at phylum level. abstract: ABSTRACT The study examines the 6‐year corrosion of carbon‐steel casing in Andra's deep geological repository (Bure, France), where steel pipes are embedded in cementitious filling grout (CFG) within Callovo‐Oxfordian claystone. abstract: The cone penetration test (CPT) is widely used in offshore geotechnical engineering, with growing interest in directly deriving soil responses such as p–y curves for monopiles, to reduce the need for advanced laboratory testing. This requires reliable relationships between the CPT response and the underlying soil stress–strain behaviour. title: Using 3D modelling to identify cliff erosion processes and their controls and to map and predict geohazards: a case study of Pakri Cliff, Estonia
abstract: Coastal zones, particularly those with low-lying areas, are increasingly affected by anthropogenic pressures and climate change. Rocky and cliffed coasts, slow-evolving geomorphic systems, experience erosional processes that pose significant geohazards. Understanding the controls on cliff retreat is critical for predicting coastal evolution, assessing geological risk, and supporting land-use and heritage management. Effectiveness of Educational Videos on Health Literacy and Contact Dermatitis Prevention among Seaweed Farmers in Tarakan
abstract: Contact dermatitis is an occupational skin disease that may affect seaweed farmers because of repeated exposure to seawater, humidity, marine organisms, and irritants. Limited health literacy and inadequate preventive behavior may increase workers’ vulnerability to skin disorders. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of an educational video in improving health literacy and contact dermatitis prevention behavior among seaweed farmers in RT 05 Pantai Amal, Tarakan City. title: Metals and Metalloids in the Carapace of Hawksbill (Eretmochelys imbricata) and Green Turtles (Chelonia mydas) Nesting in the Southern Gulf of Mexico
abstract: Keratin matrixes are a highly relevant tissue for measuring and evaluating the accumulation of endogenous and exogenous substances across a wide variety of species. In this context, the carapace of marine turtles is a valuable source of information. In this study, we collected carapace samples from two species of marine turtles to analyze metals and metalloids. title: Baltic: A benchmark and cross-domain strategy for 3D reconstruction across air and underwater domains under varying illumination
abstract: Robust 3D reconstruction across varying environmental conditions remains a critical challenge for robotic perception, particularly when transitioning between air and water. To address this, we introduce BALTIC, a controlled benchmark designed to systematically evaluate modern 3D reconstruction methods under variations in medium and lighting. abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) increasingly face governance challenges associated with wildlife-based tourism. In the Archipelago of Fernando de Noronha (Brazil), four non-fatal incidents involving the Atlantic nurse shark, Ginglymostoma cirratum (Bonnaterre, 1788) were recorded between 2025 and 2026 at the same site on the island. title: Selection of the bow for tuna purse seiners
abstract: The paper is devoted to the issue of designing the hull shape of mo-dern tuna seiners for ocean fishing. The applicability of modern non-standard shapes of bow tips to tuna fishing vessels is considered. The expediency of preserving the classical hull shape for a tuna seiner has been substantiated – an inclined stem with a bulbous bow in the underwater part. title: Oceanographic Variability Constrains Recovery of Overexploited Cod and Haddock on the Faroe Bank: Evidence for Environmental Recovery Windows at Low Stock Size
abstract: ABSTRACT In a changing global ocean certain fish populations are approaching the upper limits of their thermal tolerance. Understanding how a warming climate and plankton dynamics affect stock recovery is thus a central challenge for fisheries management. Here we use the Faroe Bank ecosystem in the northeast Atlantic as a climate‐sensitive case study to investigate how environmental variability influences recovery of demersal fish stocks following overexploitation. title: Essential habitats are context-dependent for the cosmopolitan scalloped hammerhead shark (Sphyrna lewini)
abstract: Abstract Essential habitats often shift throughout ontogeny as different life stages have distinct life history requirements. The scalloped hammerhead shark (Sphyrna lewini) is a cosmopolitan species known to undergo ontogenetic habitat shifts. However, the characteristics of habitats considered important for the species varies among and within geographic regions. abstract: The southern Levant extends between the hyperarid Sahara–Arabia Desert belt in the south and the temperate Mediterranean climate zone in the north, making the regional hydroclimate extremely sensitive to even small perturbations of global climate. The region further served as a major pathway for the “out-of-Africa” dispersal of fauna, flora, and hominins throughout the Quaternary, as well as for human cultural development from the Paleolithic to the Neolithic. abstract: The article presents data on the first report for the Black Sea of the non-indigenous red alga Ahnfeltia plicata, first registered in Odesa Bay (Ukraine) in 2023. The finding is confirmed by morphological observations, photographs, and DNA barcoding data. All recorded localities of A. plicata are confined to the shallow waters (0.5–1.5 m) characterized by high hydrodynamic activity. abstract: Vibrio and Shewanella infections are climate-sensitive marine bacterial infections of increasing public health relevance in northern Europe, particularly in areas with brackish or low-salinity waters. Previous nationwide Danish data described infection patterns through 2018, but registry-linked severity outcomes and a standardised episode-based baseline for routine surveillance have not been described. title: Study on the Applicability of Vertical Bearing Capacity Calculation Methods for Large-Diameter Pipe Piles Based on a Static Load Test Database
abstract: Large-diameter steel pipe piles (LDSPPs) are increasingly used for offshore wind turbines, marine terminals, long-span bridges, and other heavily loaded infrastructure. Their axial capacity is commonly estimated using design methods developed or calibrated mainly for smaller driven piles, and the extent to which those methods remain reliable at large diameters is not yet well established. abstract: The escalating resistance of agricultural pests to conventional chemical insecticides has created an urgent need for eco-friendly biological alternatives with novel modes of action. Sea anemone venoms are rich in structurally stable and target-specific ion channel-modulating peptides, representing a promising source of new insecticidal molecules. abstract: Forecasts of whether marine species can evolve fast enough to survive climate change rely largely on single-stage tolerance assays, tacitly assuming that tolerance measured at one developmental stage reflects adaptive capacity across the organism's life cycle. title: Germination behaviour and desiccation tolerance of Coprosma (Rubiaceae) seeds from a remote oceanic island
abstract: Abstract Seed banking can be an efficient approach to conserve plant species ex situ . Research into the suitability of long-term seed banking for (sub)tropical species is limited and urgent, especially for taxa with limited distributions such as those endemic to oceanic islands. Here, we combine a stepwise experimental methodology with non-parametric and survival analyses to assess the germination requirements and desiccation tolerance of three species of Currant Bush Coprosma (Rubiaceae) from Lord Howe Island, a remote island in the South Pacific.
