title: Translating Place Identity into Textile Motif Design
abstract: Place identity is expressed through symbols, practices, and visual representations. Translating regional identity into textile motifs requires a systematic approach that connects local visual sources with meaningful design decisions. This study aims to identify Pangandaran's visual identity sources, translate them into textile motif compositions, and evaluate the resulting prototype. title: A new species of the genus Dysommina from the Lakshadweep Sea, India (Anguilliformes: Synaphobranchidae: Ilyophinae)
abstract: This study describes a new Dysommina species, based on two specimens collected at a depth of ca. 600 m in the Lakshadweep Sea off south-western India. The new species differs from its congeners in having fewer total vertebrae (120-127 vs. 134 in D. castanea, 133-134 in D. brevis, and 137-141 in D. orientalis), fewer predorsal vertebrae (14-15 vs. 16 in D. pygmaea), fewer preanal vertebrae (24-27 vs. 28-31 in D. rugosa), and in a combination of morphometric, meristic, dentition and colouration characters. title: Computational identification of potential GLP-1 receptor agonists from marine natural products for nutraceutical applications in diabetes and obesity management
abstract: The Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor (GLP-1R) is a validated diabetes and obesity target, yet challenges with current peptide agonists necessitate orally bioavailable small-molecule alternatives. Marine natural products (MNPs) offer a structurally diverse reservoir for discovering such compounds for nutraceutical use. This study employed a multi-stage computational workflow to identify potential non-peptide GLP-1R agonists from the Comprehensive Marine Natural Products Database (CMNPD). title: Beyond the North Sea: The Royal Navy’s Experience of the Macedonian Front, 1915–1918
abstract: Little attention has been devoted to exploring the personal experiences of those who served with the Royal Navy during the First World War. The cultural dominance of the British ‘Tommy’ in the trenches of the Western Front and the focus of maritime historians on operations and technology have left the wartime lives of sailors marginalised by studies of the conflict. This article contributes to a fuller understanding of the Navy’s war by reconstructing the diverse experiences of the personnel who served at sea, on land, and in the air during the campaign in Macedonia between 1915 and 1918. abstract: Abstract Purpose Coastal vegetated soils play a critical role in global carbon storage and biogeochemical cycling, yet methods for characterising soil organic matter (OM) composition remain limited. This study used mid-infrared attenuated total reflectance (MIR-ATR) in the field for characterization of OM in coastal vegetated sites. Methods The study area comprised three vegetation zones (mangrove, MG; saltmarsh, SM; and paperbark, PB) from Wilsons Promontory National Park, Victoria, Australia. title: An improved polarization-sensitive semi-analytic monte carlo simulation method for bathymetric lidar considering complex water-column stratification
abstract: Bathymetric lidar simulation has long treated seawater as an optically uniform medium, so existing models cannot reproduce how a thermocline, a turbidity layer, or a subsurface chlorophyll maximum reshapes the polarized echo. This paper develops an improved polarization-sensitive semi-analytic Monte Carlo (SMC) method for vertically stratified water. title: Cooperative Cable-Suspended Maritime Salvage Using Multiple Unmanned Helicopters with Prescribed-Performance Position Tracking
abstract: Cooperative maritime salvage using multiple unmanned helicopters involves coupled cable forces and changes in seabed suction, hydrodynamic drag, and buoyancy. This paper studies helicopter position tracking during seabed release, underwater lifting, partial emergence, and aerial transport. title: Synchronous end-Permian mass extinction zenith in marine and low–middle latitude terrestrial North China
abstract: The end-Permian mass extinction was the most severe biotic crisis of the Phanerozoic, yet temporal synchrony between marine and terrestrial extinctions remains debated due to correlation uncertainties. title: Papering over the cracks: How residents and professionals experience market-led regeneration in four English coastal towns
abstract: English coastal towns were once celebrated for their salutogenic qualities; today, however, many experience persistent deprivation and poor health. Successive governments have responded with market-led regeneration programmes focused on physical infrastructure, yet health inequalities remain entrenched. This paper draws on interviews and focus groups with 140 residents and local professionals in Hartlepool, Blackpool, Hastings, and Torbay, conducted in 2023 as part of a wider study of the north-south health divide. title: Microbiome plasticity during the early life-stage of the angelshark (Squatina squatina) in Las Teresitas (Canary Islands)
abstract: Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. title: COMPARATIVE BIODIVERSITY OF VERTEBRATES IN MAHARASHTRA ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: This study, Comparative Biodiversity of Vertebrates in Maharashtra Ecosystems, examines vertebrate diversity, distribution, and ecological roles across Maharashtra’s varied landscapes, including forests, wetlands, rivers, reservoirs, grasslands, coastal zones, and arid regions. Maharashtra is recognised as one of India’s ecological hotspots, supporting a wide range of mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes. abstract: The article analyzes the measures taken to suppress the popular uprising that took place in 1916 in the Amu Darya Division of the Turkestan region, as well as the arrest, investigation, and trial of uprising participants by military courts. Based on archival information, memoirs, and collections of documents cited in the dissertation, it examines resistance movements in Chimbay, Davkara, Terbenbes, and the Aral Sea region, the activities of punitive detachments, and inequalities in labor conscription. abstract: Abstract To address the severe environmental pollution caused by conventional chemical hydrate inhibitors in deep‐sea oil and gas pipelines, this study developed a biodegradable green kinetic hydrate inhibitor (KHI) based on silk protein hydrolyzates (PHs). Ocean Centra Furnindo Medan during the 2023–2025 period, accompanied by increasing absenteeism, indicates performance issues potentially related to organizational communication, the physical work environment, and work discipline. title: ‘Privateering and piracy’: Australian responses to commerce warfare fears from German naval planning to 1914
abstract: Despite the extensive German archival evidence, there is still some historical opinion that Germany did not constitute a threat to Australia in 1914. It was clear to both British and German military planners that an effective way to fight an enemy was to disrupt its trade and food supplies. abstract: Background: Sofifi Port is an important logistics distribution hub for the capital of North Maluku Province, but its service performance has not fully kept pace with increasing vessel traffic and cargo volumes. Objective: This study evaluates the optimization of cargo-handling services at Sofifi Port and formulates a phased development strategy through 2030. title: Reflections, perceptions and practices of spearfishing among Ulithian communities
abstract: Abstract Spearfishing is a common and effective subsistence fishing method in coral reef‐dependent communities. Although its ecological impacts have been widely studied, spearfishing's sociocultural dimensions have received less attention despite its direct impacts on both reef and reef‐dependent communities. title: Differentially Expressed Infection-Associated Genes in a Shewanella algae isolate From a Deceased Northern Bottlenose Whale
abstract: Diseases are an important but poorly understood influence on marine ecosystems. However, many pathogens of wild marine organisms remain poorly characterized, limiting our understanding of their ecology and potential impacts. abstract: Abstract Background: Nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) is the most common malignancy worldwide, yet comprehensive national mortality surveillance remains limited in the United States (U.S.). title: Bioassay Evaluation Antioxidant Activity, Total Phenolic Content, and Total Flavonoid Content in Blumea balsamifera Leaves under Different Environmental Conditions
abstract: Blumea balsamifera is a medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine and known for its bioactive compounds with antioxidant potential. abstract: The people of Mwoakilloa (population < 200) and the Mwoakilloan diaspora (ca. 2000) represent a resilient Oceanic culture that has adapted to both island life and migration across the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) and to the United States. We describe collaborative work by Mwoakilloan speakers with linguists documenting their language and culture through oral environmental narratives recorded in both English and Mwoakilloan. abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. abstract: Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude is an archive about the dusk and dawn of seven generations of the Buendia family through the lens of magical realism. abstract: Iron is required for photosynthesis and thus affects carbon fixation rates in widespread aquatic regions where availability is limited. abstract: Post-baking operations in bakery processing environments create opportunities for microbial recontamination through food-contact surfaces that may remain contaminated after routine sanitation. Challenging the Renders of Urban-Real Estate Extractivism: Listening Practices in Anguilas Stream in the Paraná Delta, Argentina
abstract: Abstract This article examines two documentaries about the Colony Park real estate conflict in the Low Paraná River Delta archipelago: a documentary in which a photographer has gradually been received into an island community, and a found-footage film that redirects Colony Park’s own promotional archive against itself. Presenting the concept of hospitable listening, the article argues that both films enact diplomatic postures to address this river island conflict.

title: Urban Wastewater and River Health in Bangladesh: A Systematic Evidence Map Revealing a Dhaka Bias and a Neglected Barnoi River
abstract: Background: Urban and industrial wastewater discharge has contributed to river pollution in Bangladesh, raising concerns about water quality and ecosystem health. However, existing research remains unevenly distributed across geographical regions and environmental compartments, particularly in rivers associated with secondary cities. Objective: To map primary field studies of effluent-affected rivers by region, sampled compartment and pollutant group, with particular attention to the Barnoi River near Rajshahi. abstract: The aim of the present study was to evaluate the in vitro antimicrobial efficacy of an experimentally developed chlorhexidine-free children’s mouthwash against selected beneficial and pathogenic oral microorganisms. abstract: In Indonesia, microplastics (MPs) have become a significant environmental and public health threat due to the rising levels of plastic waste. The issue of microplastic pollution represents a pervasive transnational public health challenge. Whilst global studies have established general toxicity mechanisms, it is crucial to understand region-specific exposure pathways. The research method employs normative legal research through statutory and conceptual approaches, focusing the analysis on the harmonization of regulatory texts. abstract: Light is a fundamental environmental cue influencing movement, habitat selection, and aggregation in aquatic organisms. While phototaxis has traditionally been studied at the level of individual responses, how social context and density modulate light-driven behavior in non-marine microcrustaceans remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the phototactic response of the ostracod Heterocypris incongruens across three density regimes (single individuals, pairs, and groups of ≥30 individuals). abstract: This article reflects on the long-running transdisciplinary collaboration between ceramicist Diana Butucariu and musician Erik Lindeborg, tracing their evolving practice from pop-up events to situated works that engage with sustainability, heritage, and place. Collaboration emerges as a process of mutual orientation, developed under conditions of precarity. abstract: The purpose of the research was to identify Chrysolina americana (Linnaeus, 1758) on the Black Sea coast of Sochi and select effective modern insecticides against the rosemary leaf beetle ( C. americana L.). abstract: Aims: Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1895) (Diptera: Culicidae) is a highly invasive vector responsible for the transmission of several arboviruses worldwide. abstract: Sida cordata (Burm.f.) Borss.Waalk. is a widely distributed member of the genus Sida (Malvaceae), yet its modern occurrence and distribution on the mainland of Indonesia remain poorly documented following historical records from the Seribu Islands in 1948. Utilizing virtual herbarium networks and digital specimen examinations from major international repositories (such as Naturalis Biodiversity Center), this study updates the distribution of S. cordata in the region. title: Aeolian sedimentary heterogeneity in the Triassic Sherwood Sandstone Group, UK: implications for CO 2 storage
abstract: Understanding lithologic and stratigraphic heterogeneity is useful for planning carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects. In the UK East Irish Sea Basin, depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs of the Triassic Sherwood Sandstone Group (SSG) are targets for large-scale geological storage of CO 2 . abstract: Multiple agencies independently produce tropical cyclone best-track datasets for the western North Pacific, and these datasets are often regarded as interchangeable in coastal hazard applications. This study examined when this assumption holds. KMA, JMA, and JTWC data for 1977–2024 were matched by cyclone and observation time, and inter-agency differences were analyzed on a response surface defined by intensity and proximity to the Korean Peninsula. title: Ecological and biological determinants of fecal bacterial diversity in bats across four continents and phylogenetic screening for pathogen.affiliated bacterial lineages
abstract: Objective: To characterize the diversity and composition of bacterial communities in bat fecal samples under distinct ecological and biological conditions and to investigate the phylogenetic relationships of selected bacterial lineages with clinically relevant taxa. title: An Invasive Crab Species Exhibits Greater Daily Behaviour Plasticity Than a Naïve Native Crab Species
abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioural plasticity is considered highly relevant for biological invasions. As daily behavioural rhythmicity is plastic in response to environmental factors, we suggest that it may also be worth considering in the context of invasion success. abstract: Trilobites exhibiting injuries are ideal palaeontological archives for Palaeozoic predator-prey interactions. However, the current methods for diagnosing trilobite injuries primarily depend on the various morphological features at the edges of the injured exoskeleton, without evaluating the process and timing of morphological changes. abstract: The employment of sustainable liquid fuels in different power plants, including those which integrate Diesel engines into propulsive systems of land non-road or marine vehicles, results in a transient but interesting option to reach sustainability of tourist transportation. The goal was to compare the effect of a renewable Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) and a fossil Diesel fuel on regulated pollutant emissions in the surroundings of the Atlantic Islands National Park. title: Microbial profiling of Drosophila in French Guiana reveals candidate microbial taxa associated with native and invasive host
abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) threaten biodiversity, human health, and economies, yet host-associated microbiome differences between invasive and native species remain poorly understood in natural systems. We investigated bacterial and fungal microbiomes of IAS and native Drosophila species collected along an anthropisation gradient in French Guiana. abstract: To reasonably predict the chloride concentration in the interface zone of existing precast and cast-in-place concrete structures, this study establishes quantitative relationships between interfacial chloride concentration and governing factors, based on the rational Taylor model. abstract: This essay analyzes the film Color perro que huye (2011) by Venezuelan filmmaker Andrés Duque, focusing on the chapter COLOR (20:48-40:33) to examine how the director articulates his migratory experience by recovering his personal archive of digital images. title: Introduction: Russia, the West and economic statecraft
abstract: When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the West responded with the most sweeping restrictions imposed on a major economy since 1945. title: Phosphogypsum valorization through circular economy processes: review of the state of the art and perspectives from the FIC-FIGHTERS project
abstract: Abstract Phosphogypsum is a by-product of the wet production process of phosphoric acid from phosphate minerals. Since the 1950s, many industries in Europe used this process to produce fertilizers and detergents. Processing residues and waste were often dumped near production facilities or dispersed in sensitive areas such as river estuaries or coastal lagoons, resulting in the release of toxic substances into the environment and damage to the ecosystem. abstract: This study aims to explore the physical-acoustic characteristics of talilo huidu bamboo from Bone Bolango, Tomini Bay area, in the production of Polopalo, while formulating geometric standards to preserve local ecology and cultural heritage. Utilizing a qualitative method as the primary approach, this research integrates oral ethnoorganological studies with sound analysis via Fast Fourier Transform in Audacity as supporting data, alongside the sound philosophy concepts of the Gorontalo community. title: Embroidering a New Constitution for Chile: The Textile Artists of the Salvador Allende Solidarity Museum
abstract: This article examines the collective work of the textile artists of the Salvador Allende Solidarity Museum after Chile’s 2019 social outburst, reflecting on the relationship between art, human rights, and political resistance in transitional societies. We focus on their 2020 virtual workshop, Dreaming a New Constitution, conceived during the COVID-19 pandemic to foster collective dialogue and challenge the 1980 Constitution. abstract: For the Jesuits, libraries constituted one of their most valuable assets, as they housed a significant proportion of works linked to Classical Antiquity. title: PRIVATE LANDHOLDINGS AND PLANTATION CAPITAL: MICHIELS–ARNOLD LANDEN IN EASTERN BUITENZORG (1887–1942)
abstract: This study examines the role of private landholdings (tanah partikelir) as a key foundation for plantation capital accumulation through a case study of the Michiels–Arnold Landen company in Eastern Buitenzorg from 1887 to 1942. It highlights the importance of private land in shaping Java’s colonial agrarian structure, where land functioned not only as an economic asset but also as an instrument of juridical, fiscal, and administrative power. abstract: Caulerpa seaweed has the potential to be developed as a nutritious food source and a raw material for value-added bioproducts. However, its utilization in Indonesia is still dominated by fresh consumption, while information regarding its nutritional composition, bioactive compounds, food safety, and product development opportunities remains scattered across various studies. abstract: We report the first Georgia, USA, records for the relapsing fever tick, Ornithodoros turicata americanus Marx, a gopher tortoise (Gopherus polyphemus Daudin) burrow commensal and proven vector for human relapsing fever spirochetes and African Swine Fever Virus. title: Fernando Herrero Tejedor, una trayectoria falangista al servicio del régimen franquista (1920-1975)
abstract: Fernando Herrero Tejedor (1920-1975) was a key figure in the political class of the Franco dictatorship. title: The Volumetric Potentials of Rain-Harvesting Cisterns to Shape Hydrosociality in the Semiarid Region of Ceará, Northeast Brazil
abstract: This article uses a volumetric lens to explore how household rain-harvesting cisterns help (re)shape hydrosocial relations across the semiarid region of Ceará, Northeast Brazil, where vulnerability to climate variability remains high among the rural poor. title: Multivariate assessment of genetic variability in Mundu chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) accessions for yield and quality traits
abstract: Mundu chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) is an important rainfed spice cum vegetable crop cultivated in the coastal regions of Tamil Nadu, valued for its yield stability and quality attributes. The present study evaluated 27 purified Mundu chilli genotypes collected from Ramanathapuram district to assess variability for yield and quality traits using multivariate approaches. abstract: Mafic granulites from the Balaram area, South Delhi Terrane, Aravalli–Delhi Mobile Belt (ADMB), provide important insights into the petrogenesis and tectonometamorphic evolution of the lower continental crust. title: The Mednyi Arctic Fox (Vulpes lagopus semenovi (Ognev, 1931)): A Disappearing Island Endemic
abstract: Abstract The biology and history of the decline of the Arctic fox population on the Mednyi Island, Commander Islands, North Pacific, are considered. title: Between Helsinki and Brussels: The 1995 EU Commission Strategy for the South Caucasus and the Emergence of an EU Strategy on Russia
abstract: This article examines the European Union’s (EU) unsuccessful effort to develop a common strategy toward the South Caucasus and argues that the process nevertheless played a significant role in the evolution of the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) and emerging debates on a common strategy toward Russia. title: The Architecture of Intoxication: Opium Dens, Use of Bodies and New World Orders
abstract: Abstract What is the relationship between the experience of intoxication and the built environment in which it occurs? This article reflects on how the materiality of spaces of intoxication offers a lens for exploring the interplay between bodily and psychic experiences and their connection to the emerging world orders. abstract: The Youjiang Basin in South China hosts giant karstic bauxite deposits (>1 billion tons) formed in a short time interval during the Late Permian, which has attracted significant research interest due to its implications for understanding super-enrichment mechanisms of aluminum and associated critical metals (such as rare earth elements, gallium, and lithium). title: Setting time of alkali-activated materials: Mechanisms, controlling factors, and retardation strategies
abstract: Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are emerging sustainable binders with low carbon emissions and promising performance, but their practical application is limited by highly variable and system-dependent setting behaviour. abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, we ‘think with care’ about gender in Scotland in the early twentieth century, undertaking an ethnographic approach to the archive of OneKind, formerly the Scottish Society for the Prevention of Vivisection (SSPV), which has only recently been catalogued. In exploring the development of the SSPV from its beginnings in 1911 to 1930, we draw on Joan Tronto's definition of care and Puig de la Bellacasa's three dimensions of care: labour/work, affect/affections and ethics/politics. abstract: The reviewed book by Paul Carter, a renowned specialist in Australian cultural geography, addresses an intriguing applied problem: the creation of names for new geographical features in the Perth metropolitan area in the Noongar language, the language of the largest Indigenous group that once inhabited south-western Australia. abstract: ABSTRACT This qualitative case study examined how the Center for Science and the Schools (CSATS), a university‐based intermediary organization, sustained partnerships between STEM researchers and K‐12 educators over 20 years (2004–2024). abstract: The study assessed the vulnerability of non-target species in Rastrineobola argentea fishery in Uganda’s artisanal capture fisheries in Lake Victoria. title: “Don’t Throw Money Away”: Reynolds, Alcoa, and Aluminum Beverage Can Recycling in the United States, 1958–1990
abstract: This article uses oral histories and archival evidence from two major aluminum firms, Alcoa and Reynolds, to reevaluate the interlinked histories of the aluminum beverage can and recycling in the United States. abstract: Roadsides represent one of the most extensive anthropogenic networks globally, yet no integrative framework currently supports their systemic ecological characterisation and condition assessment. abstract: This dissertation examines how Western-style confectionery such as caramel, chocolate, chewing gum, and other sweets became intertwined with Japan’s empire-building from the Meiji period (1868–1912) to the early postwar years. title: Mobilizing the seafood industry for climate action
abstract: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies providing no climate-related disclosures. Reporting, which can be an indicator of action and priorities, has focused primarily on mitigation, with little attention to adaptation. We consider these gaps and propose four priorities to support capacity and pathways for climate-resilient seafood operations.

title: Cigarrillos electrónicos en jóvenes: ¿Cuáles son los verdaderos efectos en la salud?
abstract: Electronic cigarettes emerged as an alternative for conventional cigarette consumers, given that smoking accounts for 9% of deaths worldwide. Their initial goal was to facilitate smoking cessation through a progressive reduction in nicotine intake. However, electronic cigarettes have fostered nicotine addiction in young people without prior exposure to tobacco. This situation is a public health concern, as it compromises the respiratory and systemic health of users. abstract: Scholarship on the Anthropocene remains divided between Earth-system analyses of material change and environmental-humanities readings of crisis narrative, a split that leaves each side under-equipped to explain how industrial power, ecological rupture, and cultural meaning shape one another. Integrative models already exist. The most established is the Driver-Pressure-State-Impact-Response (DPSIR) framework, adopted by the European Environment Agency to organise environmental indicators for policy. abstract: Aquatic mites have successfully colonized freshwater habitats, providing an excellent model for investigating the molecular basis of adaptive evolution. Because mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is essential for cellular energy production, adaptive changes in mitochondrial protein-coding genes may reflect evolutionary responses to environmental pressures. abstract: Abstract Background Dental caries disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to fluoride toothpaste is often limited by poor affordability. This study aimed to assess the affordability of ≥ 950 parts per million of fluoride (ppm F) toothpaste for the general population in LMICs and its association with the prevalence of untreated dental caries. title: Genetic Diversity of Hepatitis B Virus and Drug Resistance among Pregnant Women in Tharaka-Nithi County, Kenya: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: With an estimated 360 million people chronically infected, hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has become one of the major global public health concerns, yet little is known about the genetic diversity and drug resistance among pregnant women in Kenya. Therefore, this study investigated the genetic diversity and drug resistance of hepatitis B virus among pregnant women in Tharaka-Nithi County, Kenya. title: Work, job satisfaction and role performance among ASHA workers in Karnataka: an overview of existing evidence
abstract: Accredited social health activists (ASHAs) are an important component of community-based health service delivery in India. Their responsibilities have expanded considerably and include maternal and child health, health education, community mobilisation, referral services, disease prevention and support for national health programmes. The conditions under which ASHAs work may influence their job satisfaction and role performance. abstract: This study investigated the applicability of the EurOtop mean wave overtopping formula using the results of 270 hydraulic model tests conducted on rubble-mound structures with two-layer regular tetrapod armor and crown structures of vertical and return-wall types. title: Scale‐dependent pathways from land use to fish diversity: eDNA analysis reveals water quality as key mediator in the Nanliu River Basin
abstract: Abstract Human‐induced land‐use change poses substantial risks to aquatic biodiversity; however, the multi‐scale pathways linking land‐use patterns to fish diversity remain insufficiently resolved. Focusing on the Nanliu River Basin (Guangxi, China), we integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) detection with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) across three spatial scales—1000 m circular buffers, 2000 m river (riparian) buffers, and sub‐watersheds—to quantify the effects on species richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson diversity. abstract: The aquatic biome is exposed to a significant threat of persistent contamination by polyethylene (PE) in the ecosystem. A critical research gap exists in PE-induced tissue-specific bioaccumulation, associated immune and stress responses in fish, followed by potential bioremediation solutions. The present study investigated the bioaccumulation of PE particles and subsequent oxidative stress in Labeo rohita induced by two different doses (0.1 and 0.5 mg/L) over 2 weeks. title: Evaluating environmental DNA metabarcoding for describing freshwater fish and shellfish occurrence in an Eastern Cascades watershed
abstract: Abstract Objective Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding offers a promising, cost-effective tool to collect data across a large spatial scale, but analyzing these data poses several critical decisions that are uncommon to traditional field sampling. The objective of our study was to evaluate data collection, filtering, and analytical components of occurrence data generated using an eDNA metabarcoding approach. title: Length-based stock assessment of largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides Lacepède, 1802) in Al Massira Reservoir, Morocco
abstract: The largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) represents one of the most economically important freshwater fish species exploited by artisanal fisheries in Moroccan reservoirs. However, information regarding its stock status and exploitation level remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the population dynamics and exploitation status of M. salmoides in Al Massira Reservoir using length-frequency data and length-based stock assessment models. title: Integrative approach reveals hidden diversity in the Brachionus (Rotifera, Monogononta)
abstract: The phylum Rotifera has many species complexes that require integrative analyses to resolve their taxonomic identity. Brachionus angularis comprises different morphotypes. In Aguascalientes, Mexico, we observed two of these morphotypes coexisting. To explore their species identity, we applied an integrative approach that combined taxonomical, ecological, and molecular data. title: Integrated geothermal applications in Türkiye for energy carbon management and resource recovery
abstract: Abstract Türkiye is important for geothermal energy not only because it produces electricity from high-temperature fields, but also because it uses geothermal resources for other innovative direct-use applications. A large part of the resource value comes from direct heat use, chemically complex fluids, separated gases, and the way these systems are operated at the surface. This review examines geothermal systems in Türkiye from this broader perspective. title: Actualización taxonómica de cianoprocariontes marinos de México
abstract: Antecedentes y Objetivos: Los cianoprocariontes son los primeros organismos capaces de realizar fotosíntesis oxigénica, con gran diversidad morfológica y amplia distribución geográfica, tanto en ambientes acuáticos como extremófilos. title: Blue Economy: Sustainable Development Factor in the Regions Adjacent to the Danube
abstract: The blue economy is an essential pillar for the sustainable development of the Danube regions, capitalizing on the economic potential of the waters and associated ecosystems through practices that protect the environment. It stimulates the creation of green jobs, innovation and regional connectivity. The Danube Region integrates the principles of the blue economy through several strategic directions and concrete initiatives that will be analyzed in this research. title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
abstract: Abstract When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. abstract: Protected Area (PA) management faces multiple challenges, making Protected Area management effectiveness (PAME) assessment essential for promoting continuous improvements in biodiversity conservation. In this context, this study aims to map the global distribution of PAME assessment tools developed in Brazil and internationally, and to analyze how their indicators address society-nature interactions. title: Increasing fire severity changes the assembly and coupling between plant taxonomic and functional diversity in a dry conifer forest understory
abstract: Disturbance regimes are changing globally with uncertain consequences for the assembly and functioning of ecosystems. In western North America, wildfires are increasing in frequency and severity relative to historic fire regimes. How plant community assembly and function will respond as disturbance intensifies is poorly understood. Ecosystem functions rely on the functional traits of species within a community. title: Opportunities for standardizing resilience, adaptation, and sustainability planning elements: a structured comparison of community-oriented planning guidance
abstract: Abstract Communities in the United States increasingly undertake distinct planning processes to build resilience to reduce natural hazard impacts, adapt to changing conditions, enhance sustainability to reduce energy and resource use and consumption, and promote economic prosperity. Planning efforts addressing these multifaceted goals result in community-based resilience, adaptation, and sustainability plans. title: Deforestation and monoculture expansion restructure zooplankton communities in neotropical reservoirs
abstract: Abstract Deforestation and monoculture expansion in tropical watersheds represent important pressures on aquatic ecosystems, yet their associations with zooplankton communities in Neotropical reservoirs remain poorly understood. We evaluated how land use and land cover are associated with the distribution, diversity, composition, and structure of zooplankton communities in six tropical reservoirs with contrasting landscape configurations and trophic conditions. abstract: El pueblo aymara forma parte de los territorios y comunidades andinas del norte de Chile, y su lengua, perteneciente a la familia lingüística jaqi, se ha sostenido a través de generaciones en el ámbito escolar y comunitario. title: Comparative Physiological and Ecological Characterization of the Photosymbiotic Amoeba Mayorella viridis Across Symbiotic and Aposymbiotic States
abstract: Symbiosis is a fundamental biological strategy that enables metabolic complementation between distinct organisms. The amoeba Mayorella viridis establishes a photosymbiotic relationship with the green alga Chlorella, yet the physiological basis of this association remains poorly understood. Here, we compared symbiotic (green) and aposymbiotic (white) strains to quantify phenotypic effects of the symbiotic state. abstract: Abstract As a sensitive region of global climate change, the Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau is experiencing permafrost degradation, leading to the release of sequestered carbon and nitrogen into aquatic ecosystems. However, the spatial heterogeneity and underlying drivers of greenhouse gas concentrations across diverse water body types remain unclear. abstract: Intensive captive breeding, head starting, reintroduction, individual and population health monitoring, and habitat protection for the past 20 years are credited for the ongoing recovery of the endangered Grand Cayman blue iguana (Cyclura lewisi). abstract: Abstract The impact of oil and gas activities on the social, economic, and environmental aspects is threatening, regardless of the varying degrees. abstract: Abstract. Traditionally Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment (PSHA) is mainly based on historical and instrumental catalogues. abstract: ABSTRACT Rising global soil salinity has increased freshwater scarcity, driving widespread use of reverse osmosis (RO) systems that generate high total dissolved solids (TDS) wastewater. abstract: Accurate quantification of serpentinization extent is essential for determining reaction kinetics and understanding water-rock interactions in hydrothermal systems. abstract: Abstract Lake littoral sediments are critical carbon cycle hotspots that bridge terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. The chemodiversity of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in these sediments reflects ecosystem multifunctionality, particularly regarding carbon storage. The Greater Caribbean manatee ( Trichechus manatus manatus ) population in Puerto Rico is classified as endangered and has previously shown limited mitochondrial haplotype diversity. abstract: Tuntong laut (Batagur borneoensis) merupakan spesies kura-kura berstatus sangat terancam punah (Critically Endangered) akibat degradasi ekosistem dan aktivitas manusia. abstract: Species turnover, the spatial dissimilarity in species composition, is a central concept in island biogeography and community ecology. abstract: Abstract Erosion from ice‐rich permafrost thaw (“thermokarst”) alters tundra vegetation cover and soil moisture, and laterally transports organic material into lakes, altering net fluxes of carbon dioxide (F CO2 ), methane (F CH4 ), and nitrous oxide (F N2O ). abstract: The main purpose of this study was to determine the extent to which records management strategies influence accountability of the table water business in Akwa Ibom State. title: Checklist of threatened plants of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
abstract: Covering approximately 10% of Borneo’s land area, Sabah is one of the global hotspots for plant biodiversity, yet it faces increasing threats to its flora due to habitat loss and exploitation. This paper aims to compile a comprehensive checklist of threatened plant species in Sabah based on assessments published in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. title: Roost site characteristics and habitat associations of bats (Mammalia: Chiroptera) in Kamrup District, Assam, India
abstract: Chiroptera play vital ecological roles as pollinators, seed dispersers, and insect population regulators; however, information on their roost site requirements remains limited in many parts of northeastern India. The present study examined roost site characteristics and habitat associations of Chiroptera in Kamrup District, Assam, India. abstract: Olfactory signalling among mammals remains understudied, particularly in ungulates. This study documents “preaching,” an olfactory communication behaviour exhibited by male Sambar Deer Rusa unicolor, that involves an upright posture, rubbing of the pre-orbital gland, and sniffing tree bases. abstract: The professionalisation of emergency management in Australia is ongoing. Supporting that process is the development of a body of knowledge to support the new profession. The body of knowledge for emergency management requires that emergency events are recorded in a manner and format that supports ongoing learning and research. abstract: Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. title: Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: 2026 Expert Consensus
abstract: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Spasticity is one of the most frequent and highly disabling features of MS, often accompanied by cramps, pain, bladder dysfunction, sleep disturbances, fatigue, and tremor. abstract: Despite abundant copper deposits, the deep history of copper mining in Iberia has not been as extensively studied as in other European ore-rich areas. Here, the authors present new radiocarbon dates that demonstrate Late Bronze Age copper mining at Las Minillas, near Granja de Torrehermosa (southern Spain). abstract: Driven by the global demand for public health security, ultraviolet C light-emitting diode (UVC-LED) disinfection technology has emerged as a promising mercury-free alternative to conventional methods. abstract: Abstract The impacts of non-native Emerald Ash Borer (EAB) are likely to be most severe in black ash wetlands, possibly requiring preemptive forest management to maintain ecosystem functions such as carbon storage. abstract: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate the “SCSCE Model” (Sala Noi Model), an interdisciplinary local learning management framework using Lanna traditional crafts to foster community innovators. abstract: This paper considers the dilemma of wastewater reuse through the lens of Australian economic regulation. abstract: This study investigates the effects of contract duration, internet connectivity, and workload on Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) and employee performance among Indonesian seafarers employed by foreign shipping companies operating on international routes. abstract: This article examines the source of a counternarrative on Latin American and Ecuadorian historiography, by reinterpreting the seventh story of Herman Melville's The Encantadas (1856). abstract: Abstract Elucidating the drivers of evolution in dry environments is central to understanding how organisms respond to climate change. abstract: Current theories of action control assume that the binding and retrieval of features into and from common memory representations (i.e., event files) constitute core mechanisms supporting goal-directed behavior. abstract: Rice husk biochar was applied at 0, 10, 20, and 30 Mg ha⁻¹ to three soil textures (loamy sand, loam, and clay loam) to evaluate its effects on nitrate (NO₃⁻) and potassium (K⁺) leaching under saturated column conditions. title: Do Protected Areas Affect the Income Levels in Remote Regions? Evidence from Italian Inner Areas
abstract: Abstract The economic impact of protected areas (PAs) on local development remains a debated topic in regional economics, particularly in peripheral regions facing demographic and economic decline. While protected areas provide essential ecological benefits, their effects on local economies remain debated, with concerns about land-use restrictions potentially limiting economic opportunities alongside potential gains from tourism and ecosystem services. abstract: This study examined the reading skills of Grade 3 learners and their relationship with academic performance in English in selected public elementary schools in the Bantayan District, Schools Division of Cebu Province, during School Year 2026–2027. abstract: This review explores the nutritional implications of plant-based diets, including veganism and vegetarianism. However, exclusive plant-based diets may lead to potential deficiencies in protein, calcium, vitamin D, vitamin B12, zinc, and iron. title: Finding Third ways? The dynamics of settlement on customary land conflict In Papua, Indonesia
abstract: This article examines alternative approaches to the resolution of customary land conflicts in Papua, which emerge as both private and communal disputes and are continually shaped by competing narratives of development. The study employs a constructivist approach, which views customary land not merely as a legal or economic asset but as a socially constructed space whose meaning is negotiated through interaction, authority relations, and historical experience. abstract: Post-operative pain after single visit root canal treatment remains a common clinical challenge and the optimal irrigant for balancing pain control with antimicrobial efficacy is uncertain. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the post-operative pain and antibacterial efficacy of 3% sodium hypochlorite and 2% chlorhexidine in 80 patients undergoing single-visit endodontic treatment. abstract: El presente escrito es un repaso por los principales métodos de medición de altura de las montañas a lo largo de la historia llegando hasta nuestros días, donde un equipo de ingenieros en geomática y topografía llamados Sostremetries, está actualizando las cotas de toda la cordillera del Pirineo con la tecnología y los métodos más precisos del momento, elaborando así una nueva la lista de los tres miles basada en criterios objetivos y mediciones precisas.

abstract: Literacy is fundamentally an act of meaning-making that requires bridging micro-level linguistic choices with macro-level text structures across genres. Current literacy policies dominated by Science of Reading (SoR) mandates often overemphasize isolated, word-level foundational skills. title: Diet of Drymarchon corais (Squamata: Colubridae) and a new prey record
abstract: Drymarchon corais is a generalist species, with a diet that includes amphibians, lizards, amphisbaenians, other snakes, eggs, birds, and small mammals. On 9 August 2025 we recorded an adult D. corais preying on a juvenile Boa constrictor. abstract: E-commerce has become a major force driving industrial upgrading, urban expansion, and urban–rural integration. Yet it remains unclear whether classical theories of urban land expansion can adequately explain the digital era, particularly in terms of when and at what scale E-commerce begins to reshape urban space in traditional manufacturing cities. abstract: Abstract Scholarship on Islam in Ethiopia has examined religious authority, scholarly networks, and Muslim communities, but has paid less attention to how local centres of Islamic learning were established and sustained. This article examines Gata Majlis in nineteenth-century South Wollo, focusing on how Haji Bushra’s scholarly authority shaped its formation, how learning continued after his death, and how later generations remembered his role. abstract: Abstract The efficient conversion of CO2 and industrial waste streams into value-added products remains a critical challenge for sustainable microbial processes. Here, we present the first systematic demonstration of purple phototrophic bacteria (PPB) as platforms for the autotrophic valorization of CO2 and industrial off-gases or sulfur byproducts into valuable metabolites. abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, with hypertension as a key modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Nutritional status is considered an important determinant of hypertension due to its association with energy balance, dietary patterns, and metabolic conditions. abstract: After a recollection of some of my encounters with Gilles Brassard, on the occasion of his 70th birthday I present, first, a new idea on the creation of new information at a limited rate. abstract: Gender disparity in higher education is primarily rooted in unequal access to power, which is often a result of limited education and low income. This study explores gender inequality in higher education through a case study of Bagmati Municipality in the Sarlahi District of Nepal. abstract: Flooding affects an estimated 70% of the global poor, highlighting the need to understand how disaster risk reduction investments may contribute to poverty and inequality reduction. abstract: Abstract Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. abstract: Temperature determines butterflies' physiological processes and performance. abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Invasive Aedes species are continuously spreading in Europe and have been increasingly reported from urban settlements. abstract: Climate change-induced abiotic stresses, particularly drought and salinity, severely constrain global agricultural productivity. While natural plant-microbe interactions enhance stress tolerance, their efficacy is often inconsistent under extreme conditions. abstract: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. title: Factors Affecting the Choice of Marketing Channels among Smallholder Mango Farmers in Elgeyo-Marakwet County
abstract: Mango is the main occupation of most of the small-scale farmers residing in the lowlands in Elgeyo-Marakwet County. Currently, its production in the County has been declining due to marketing inefficiency. The following objectives guided the study: to map the mango marketing channels and to determine the factors affecting mango marketing channels among smallholder mango farmers in Elgeyo-Marakwet County. The study was guided by the theory of the firm and the theory of planned behaviour. Descriptive survey and analytical research designs were applied in the study. A closed- and open-ended quest

title: The Resource-Rich Region Paradox: Education Gaps and Local Employment Opportunities in Teluk Bintuni Regency
abstract: Teluk Bintuni Regency in West Papua ranks among Indonesia’s richest regions by gross regional domestic product (GRDP) per capita, yet a quarter of its population is poor. This study examines how education gaps shape local people’s access to employment in an economy dominated by the Tangguh liquefied natural gas (LNG) project. It uses a qualitative case study based on document analysis of official statistics for 2023–2025, regional government documents, an independent panel report on Tangguh, special autonomy regulations, and published field studies, cross-checked through source triangulation.

title: Association of KCNJ11 and TCF7L2 genetic variants with type 2 diabetes in a Mexican region with high disease prevalence and strong Mayan cultural heritage
abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes (T2D) affects up to 18.3% of Mexicans, surpassing the global prevalence of 11.1%. Among Amerindian groups, Mayan ancestry has been linked to a higher risk of T2D. Sisal, a southeastern Mexican town with strong Mayan heritage, reports a prevalence of 22%, providing a unique setting to study genetic factors in an underrepresented population. We examined associations of KCNJ11 (rs5215, rs5219) and TCF7L2 (rs7901695, rs11196205) genetic variants with T2D in 232 individuals, including 99 participants diagnosed with T2D and 132 metabolically healthy individuals. title: Mythopoetics as Epistemic Revolt: Decolonial Reading and Fragmented Perception in Ben Okri’s The Famished Road
abstract: This article argues that the kind of mythopoetics employed in Ben Okri’s The Famished Road is a species of epistemic defiance and resistance against the perceptual and narrative frames by means of which colonial modernity claims to achieve comprehensibility, coherence, linear progression, and political control of its social world. title: Assessing genetic variability and Agronomic Performance of turmeric (Curcuma Longa l.) Genotypes for Yield improvement
abstract: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) germplasm evaluation is essential for identifying valuable genetic resources and understanding agronomic performance to enhance productivity. During 2022- 23 growing season, a field experiment was carried out at Spices Research Centre, Shibganj, Bogura to evaluate ten turmeric genotypes using a randomized complete block design with three replications. title: New Record of Raillietiella furcocerca (Pentastomida: Raillietiellidae) in Bothrops atrox from the Brazilian Amazon: Morphological Characterization and Infection Sites
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to document the occurrence of Raillietiella furcocerca infecting Bothrops atrox in the Lower Amazon region, State of Pará, Brazil, providing morphometric characterization, infection descriptors, and new insights into extrapulmonary infection sites. METHODS: A total of 48 B. atrox specimens were examined between 2009 and 2011 (Tapajós National Forest) and 2023-2024 (Santarém and Belterra). abstract: El ensayo analiza los desafíos jurídicos, técnicos e institucionales que enfrenta el Instituto de MedicinaLegal y Ciencias Forenses para preservar datos volátiles dentro de la cadena de custodia de laevidencia digital en Panamá. title: The litter decomposition dynamics under land-type conversion by microbial communities in the Yellow River floodplain
abstract: Land-type conversion contributes significantly to litter decomposition, yet microbial feedback mechanisms remain unclear in river-floodplain areas. The distinct roles of bacteria versus fungi in wetland litter decomposition remain a key unresolved issue requiring further investigation. Litter decomposition dynamics and microecological mechanisms of three diverse land-types (riparian higher-beach wetland (RHW), cultivated wetland (CW), mesophytic wetland (MW)) within the Yellow River tidal flat were studied via litter bag method and high-throughput sequencing method for 2 years. title: Faktor Risiko Kejadian Tuberkulosis di Wilayah Perdesaan: Studi Kasus
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a high-burden public health problem, including in rural areas such as the working area of Puskesmas Wanareja I, Cilacap Regency, which recorded 96 active cases in 2025. Objective: This study aimed to analyze environmental, individual, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors associated with TB incidence and to determine the most dominant factor. Methods: A case-control design was applied to 158 respondents (79 cases, 79 controls) in the working area of Puskesmas Wanareja I. title: Heat‐responsive genes in Bemisia tabaci : roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance
abstract: BACKGROUND: Temperature strongly influences insect physiology and can affect responses to chemical stress. However, the molecular basis underlying the relationship between thermal responses and insecticide resistance in the whitefly Bemisia tabaci remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify conserved temperature-responsive genes and determine their functional roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance. title: International heritage law as resistance to occupation
abstract: Abstract International law posits that occupation is a temporary state that does not transfer an atom of sovereignty to the occupying power. Nevertheless, in situations of prolonged occupation driven by the political goal of (unlawful) annexation, the occupying power might try to enforce its presence by claiming historic title to territory and denying the ties of the present population to their homeland. title: Los principios de una sociedad igualitaria, según el poder de la acción colectiva defendida por Noam Chomsky
abstract: Este artículo analiza la propuesta de Noam Chomsky para alcanzar una sociedad igualitaria, fundamentada en el poder de la acción colectiva y una interpretación específica de la naturaleza humana. Partiendo de la crítica a los modelos socioeconómicos dominantes, se examinan las limitaciones de las posturas liberales, autoritarias y socialistas-leninistas para realizar el potencial humano. title: Multidimensional Poverty Reduction Under the National Target Programme on Sustainable Poverty Reduction in Viet Nam: Evidence from the 2021-2025 Cycle and Implications for 2026-2030
abstract: The National Target Programme on Sustainable Poverty Reduction for 2021-2025 closed at a moment of fundamental institutional change: Viet Nam’s national target programmes were consolidated from 2026, and the multidimensional poverty standard will be raised from 2027. This study evaluates the full implementation cycle of the programme, measures the degree of disparity across regions, and identifies the bottlenecks facing the new period. title: Sous l’ordre colonial, le genre
abstract: À partir des données relatives à l’indemnité coloniale versée par la France aux anciens propriétaires d’esclaves après l’abolition de l’esclavage le 27 avril 1848, cet article analyse des trajectoires d’hommes blancs et de femmes de couleur de la Martinique de la première moitié du xix e siècle dont les parcours de propriétaires furent marqués par les représentations, les discours et les normes entourant les relations intimes et sous surveillance qui les unissent. journal: Revue des politiques sociales et familiales

title: Aupasargika Nidana of Kushtha: Bridging Classical Ayurvedic Concepts of Disease Transmission with Contemporary Medical Evidence and Emerging Insights
abstract: Introduction: Skin diseases constitute a substantial global health burden, with communicable dermatoses such as scabies and superficial bacterial and fungal infections remaining important public-health concerns. The occurrence and transmission of these diseases are associated with factors such as close physical contact, household exposure, sharing of personal articles, overcrowding, and environmental conditions. title: Phytochemical analyses, antimicrobial, antioxidant and anticancer activities of endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa
abstract: Fungal endophytes considered one of the major sources of promising bioactive compounds. This study aimed to isolate endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa for the first time, and to evaluate their biological activities. Results illustrated that, two fungal endophytes isolates were isolated, identified as Alternaria sp. and Alternaria alternata morphologically and genetically. title: RETRACING CULTURE OF RAINWATER HARVESTING IN PONTIANAK RIVER CITY
abstract: This paper investigates the origins and ongoing practices of rainwater conservation in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, asking how residential environments have adapted to the city’s distinctive climatic and hydrological conditions through culturally embedded water practices. Situated on the equator within a tropical wetland environment, Pontianak is shaped by abundant rainfall, rivers, and peatlands. title: Statins promote bone anabolism in estrogen deficiency by inducing osteogenic differentiation of skeletal stem/progenitor cells
abstract: Abstract Menopause-associated estrogen deficiency drives age-related bone loss in women. Statin use has been associated with higher bone mineral density in postmenopausal women, but whether menopause alters skeletal responses to statins remains unclear. title: Phylogenomic coupling of F1 chemosensory and archaellum systems across archaea and monoderm bacteria
abstract: Abstract Archaellum-associated motility has been viewed as solely archaeal, yet new findings in Chloroflexota prompt a broader perspective. By analysing a curated ∼22,000 NCBI reference genomes alongside 2,397 archaeal and 226 archaellum-encoding Chloroflexota genomes, this study systematically characterises the co-distribution of archaellum loci with chemosensory system (CSS) classes. title: Functional systems integration: a framework for reconciling livestock production and wild herbivore conservation in nature-positive rangelands
abstract: Reconciling livestock production, wild herbivore conservation and human well-being remains a persistent challenge in rangeland management. Conventional approaches have largely pursued these objectives through separate production and conservation strategies, reinforcing a production–conservation trade-off while overlooking the ecological and institutional processes linking them. abstract: Diare akut masih menjadi salah satu penyebab utama morbiditas dan mortalitas yang dapat memicu terjadinya dehidrasi serta ketidakseimbangan elektrolit pada bayi, secara khusus pada usia dibawah 12 bulan. title: Current State of Knowledge on Groundwater Quality in Moundou, Southwestern Chad: Hydrochemical Processes, Contamination Pathways and Implications for Public Health
abstract: Groundwater is the main source of domestic water supply in Moundou, the second-largest city in Chad, located in the Western Logone basin and within the Chari-Logone hydrological system. The literature published specifically on groundwater quality in Moundou remains sparse, originating from a small number of research teams and often based on one-off sampling campaigns. title: Thermal Performance and Cooling Mechanisms of Thatch Roofs in Nigerian Traditional Architecture
abstract: Contemporary architecture in Nigeria has largely abandoned indigenous building typologies in favor of Western-derived, energy-intensive designs reliant on reinforced concrete and corrugated metal sheets. This shift has resulted in severe indoor thermal discomfort, necessitating massive energy consumption for mechanical cooling. This paper provides a comprehensive thermodynamic and architectural analysis of the cooling efficacy of thatch roofs combined with mud walls in Nigerian traditional architecture. abstract: BACKGROUND: The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) includes a large workforce with a diverse spectrum of military occupations and potentially related exposures. The objective was to examine associations between service in distinct military occupations and the subsequent development of cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used CAF administrative data linked to national cancer registry data. abstract: This study aims to develop a framework for the Carbon Credit Market. Assessment of credit risk in financing environmental performance and the voluntary market. A total of 5,432 peer-reviewed journal articles published during the years 2001 to 2026 were reviewed to map out the academic structure and evolution of this field. abstract: The bond behavior of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) and steel rebars in advanced cementitious composites is governed by a complex interplay of rebar type, concrete matrix, confinement, embedment length, and geometric parameters, yet it remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Objetivou-se avaliar alterações na qualidade de vida e na funcionalidade de pessoas idosas comunitárias após um protocolo fisioterapêutico multicomponente domiciliar. abstract: Abstract In the US Midwest, liquid manure is most commonly applied on bare soil after fall crop harvest, increasing the risk of nutrient loss during winter and early spring. Applying manure as a side‐dress into standing corn ( Zea mays L.) using tankers or soft drag hose systems can better match seasonal plant N uptake, but producers need evidence that this practice maintains crop yields and reduces excess nitrogen (N) in the soil after harvest. abstract: Abstract Plastic waste, particularly from microplastics (MPs), has become a pervasive pollutant in aquatic environments, while conventional wastewater treatment plants remain largely ineffective at removing these persistent contaminants. Bioelectrochemical systems (BESs) have emerged as promising platforms for sustainable environmental mitigation, integrating microbial metabolism with electrochemical processes for the concomitant removal of contaminants and resource recovery. abstract: Heatwaves are increasing in intensity, frequency, and duration and may drive the responses of organisms to climate change more strongly than gradual increases in mean temperature. The effects of heatwave events on wildlife remain poorly understood because the magnitude of these effects often depends on environmental the context: additional environmental stressors can exacerbate the impact of extreme temperatures. title: Perceived benefits and challenges of the use of immersive virtual reality Tai Chi by older Chinese and Korean immigrants
abstract: BACKGROUND: Older Asian immigrants encounter challenges that limit access to healthcare services and experience physical inactivity that can exacerbate psychological distress. Virtual reality offers a promising technology for delivering mindfulness and physical activity interventions that promote body awareness and physical fitness. title: Placental Interdigitation Is Associated with Reproductive Pace across Mammals
abstract: The placenta is a transient organ mainly derived from fetal tissue that is essential for establishing metabolic and immune interactions that support healthy pregnancies in eutherian mammals. Across mammals, placentas show high morphological diversity in both the degree of tissue invasiveness and in the complexity of tissue integration between maternal and fetal tissues. abstract: Abstract High-temperatures significantly constrain the growth and resilience of day-neutral strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa ) varieties, affecting their morphological, physiological, and biochemical characteristics. abstract: Pedobacter lusitanus NL19 is a Gram-negative bacterium recognized for its potential to produce various antimicrobial metabolites, including lipids. However, how growth conditions regulate this production capability remains poorly understood. Like other bacteria, P. lusitanus NL19 adapts its membrane fatty acid (FA) composition in response to environmental conditions, a process that appears closely linked to its antimicrobial activity. abstract: Economic growth and income inequality are two important indicators of a country's economic development. China and India have experienced substantial economic transformation since 2000. China has become a major manufacturing and export centre, while India has expanded in services, information technology, manufacturing and domestic consumption. abstract: Geomorphology provides essential information on landscape evolution through the analysis of landforms, surface processes, and their controlling factors. abstract: Este artículo analiza la serie fotográfica Ravens (1986) del fotógrafo japonés Fukase Masahisa, centrándose en la construcción de la escena fantasmática y su capacidad para generar conexiones emocionales profundas con el espectador. abstract: Abstract Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO 2 ), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15 O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. abstract: BACKGROUND: Massive bee stings can cause systemic manifestations and life-threatening complications. In French Guiana, data on such envenomations are scarce. Vibrio alginolyticus produces lateral flagella for surface-associated motility in viscous environments, with LafA forming its filament as flagellin. A maf homolog encoding a putative flagellin glycosylation factor is located immediately downstream of lafA , suggesting that the lateral filament is glycosylated. title: Radiocarbon-based models of earliest Iron Age village community (Køge Bay region, East Zealand)
abstract: This paper explores the dynamics of village community formation and change during the earliest Iron Age (c. 500–1 BC) using radiocarbon-based models. title: Comparative effects of endemic plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria on morphological and nutritional characteristics of Hordeum vulgare and Avena sativa forages
abstract: Plant–microbe interactions play a fundamental role in regulating plant growth and nutrient accumulation, thereby influencing forage yield and chemical composition. This study evaluated the effects of three PGPR strains on the growth and nutritional composition of two forage cereals, Hordeum vulgare and Avena sativa, cultivated under non-controlled field conditions. abstract: Vanaf de jaren zestig had de cultuurkritische antipsychiatrische beweging een grote invloed. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. abstract: The article aims to analyze the epistemological construction and consolidation of the concept of the historic center as a fundamental category within cultural heritage studies and urban planning. A documentary-analytical study was conducted, based on a systematic review of specialized literature, documents issued by international organizations, and heritage charters. The Kosovo analogy in Putin’s foreign policy discourse
abstract: Historical analogies can inform policy debate and justify action, but public references alone cannot establish learning. This article examines how Vladimir Putin invoked Kosovo in official discourse between 2000 and 2023. A longitudinal qualitative analysis of 24 executive records distinguishes the analogy’s source referent, target, public timing and argumentative function. The records show overlapping uses. abstract: Using a double-voiced narration as self-ethnography, the paper draws on our individual practices across the fields of performance, craft, and ethnology, as well as on territories where they overlap: on one side, mask-making, and on the other, mask-wearing. We reflect on how masks (face-masks and mask-costumes) have found their way into our work as the duo behind “Plastic Art Performance collective”, an (eco)art group that emerged in 2020 within the Bucharest performance art scene which works to connect body practices to ecological consciousness. title: Proxy warfare and regional instability: The role of non-state actors in the Pakistan-India-Afghanistan triangle (2015-2025)
abstract: Proxy warfare has become a prominent feature of modern warfare and conflicts as both large and small states alike are pursuing these tactics to attain greater strategic leverage with minimal financial and political costs. South Asia has long been suffering from regional rivalries and disputes marked by tacit pitching of non-state actors or proxies having ramifications for the region and beyond. title: El descenso de la migración interna en México
abstract: Este estudio analiza el descenso de la migración interna en México utilizando información censal de 2000, 2010 y 2020. Los resultados muestran una disminución de la intensidad migratoria reciente, asociada principalmente a los cambios en la estructura por edad derivados de la transición demográfica. La reducción de la población joven ha contribuido al debilitamiento de los flujos migratorios y a una reconfiguración territorial de los movimientos internos del país.

abstract: La gestión hospitalaria ha mostrado una gran transformación en las últimas décadas, impulsada por las necesidades de los pacientes, los avances tecnológicos, y la perspectiva actual sobre la atención sanitaria. abstract: The intraspecific variation in elytral maculation of Cylindera (Cylindera) sauteri (Horn, 1912) and Cylindera (Cylindera) pseudocylindriformis (Horn, 1913) (Coleoptera: Cicindelidae) has not previously been studied in detail. abstract: Abstract Amid growing calls for Australian universities to engage meaningfully with Indigenous knowledges, this article examines how Indigenous-led, place-based inquiry can reorient academic practice toward culturally regenerative possibilities. Drawing on a Cooperative Inquiry conducted with Whadjuk Noongar Boodjar, we follow six Noongar-led experiences involving Country, language, ceremony, deep time, embodiment and more-than-human relations. title: Awareness without actionable knowledge: understanding physical activity recommendations among people with COPD
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Physical activity (PA) promotion is a cornerstone of non-pharmacological Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management. Recognising the benefits of PA may not be sufficient to guide behaviour if people with COPD do not know the specific PA recommendations. This actionable knowledge may support PA engagement. This study aimed to characterise awareness of PA benefits, inactivity risks and knowledge of the WHO recommendations among people with COPD, exploring associations with participants' characteristics. abstract: This paper explores the epistemology of mourning through the lens of two Asian American scholars pursuing doctoral degrees at a Midwestern university. We examine how racialization in Midwestern educational institutions reflects a broader historical and cultural distancing from Vietnamese immigrants and refugees, despite a shared geopolitical past. title: Logística e innovación bajo fuego: Acelerar la experiencia militar
abstract: El empirismo de Clausewitz sostiene que el conocimiento práctico del campo de batalla supera cualquier modelo teórico, no existen fórmulas universales y el mando debe adaptarse a las circunstancias reales. El conflicto en Ucrania ha redefinido el diseño de la guerra, obligando a los ejércitos a innovar en terreno y fortalecer el apoyo logístico. Ante futuros escenarios volátiles y complejos, se vuelve urgente agilizar la toma de decisiones en el frente, donde la adaptación táctica es decisiva para la supervivencia.

Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. abstract: Hoy en día, el diseño de consorcios microalga-bacteria, así como el suministro de gases industriales como fuente de carbono son estrategias implementadas para maximizar la relación costo-beneficio de la producción de compuestos bioactivos – es decir, sutancias naturales beneficas para la sociedad – como pigmentos, polisacáridos, proteínas, vitaminas, hormonas, antioxidantes, entre otros. abstract: Moisture deficit heavily constrains common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L .) production in Ethiopia, serving as a critical limitation in areas characterized by erratic rainfall. To address this challenge, forty-three common bean genotypes were evaluated in a greenhouse experiment at Hawassa University in 2022 to identify drought-tolerant materials. abstract: This study examines the role of agricultural land sustainability in Türkiye’s decarbonization pathway by analyzing the impact of the Cropland Load Capacity Factor (CROPLCF) on greenhouse gas (GHG) and CO₂ emissions. abstract: Canyons are geographical structures consisting of deep valleys formed by a deep cleft and rivers on the earth’s surface, and are areas where many tourism activities can be carried out. Canyons have emerged as alternative tourist areas preferred in tourism in recent years, and canyon tourism has come to the fore as canyons have started to come to the fore in tourism activities. abstract: The philosophy of "Satu Tungku Tiga Batu" (One Stove Three Stones) in Fakfak Regency, West Papua, is a model of local wisdom proven effective in maintaining harmony among religious communities (Islam, Protestantism, and Catholicism). This study aims to deeply analyze the phenomenological meaning of the philosophy based on the lived experiences and intersubjective consciousness of the local community. abstract: Biomonitoring is an organism monitoring activity aimed at obtaining baseline data on species occurrence and composition within a particular area. This study was conducted at Sato Loka Wildlife and Livestock Park, Kaliurang, Sleman Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta. abstract: This article investigates the construction, demolition, and subsequent reconstruction efforts surrounding the bell tower commissioned by Kaptan Yorgi Pasha, who served as Giresun’s mayor from 1885 to 1904. title: Association between plasma docosahexaenoic acid levels and the incidence of frailty: A prospective analysis of the UK Biobank
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The blood level of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) has been associated cross-sectionally with frailty, but its relationship with incident frailty remains unclear. abstract: Abstract The emerald ash borer ( Agrilus planipennis ) is an invasive insect in the United States that preferentially feeds on ash ( Fraxinus spp.) trees, causing widespread ash decline. Resulting canopy gaps may facilitate understory invasion by non-native plants, such as Amur honeysuckle ( Lonicera maackii ). We investigated whether ash decline and invasive shrub management, which opens the shrub layer, interact to influence understory plant communities.
