title: Fibrilación ventricular autolimitada: un caso clínico inusual que resalta el rol estratégico de la enfermería en monitorización Holter
abstract: La monitorización electrocardiográfica ambulatoria mediante Holter de 24 horas constituye una herramienta fundamental para correlacionar síntomas como síncope o mareos con arritmias transitorias. El objetivo del presente trabajo fue desarrollar un plan de cuidados de enfermería estructurado en dos fases —previa a la implantación del dispositivo y durante la monitorización—, basado en los patrones funcionales de Marjory Gordon y las taxonomías NANDA-I, NOC y NIC, así como destacar el papel estratégico de la enfermería en la detección precoz de arritmias y eventos cardíacos.

abstract: Colombian schools are required to state a pedagogical model in their Institutional Educational Project (PEI); however, the way teachers understand and enact it does not always match what is declared. This article interprets the experiences of teachers at a private school in Popayán, Colombia, with the pedagogical models they apply, and analyzes their relationship with the socio-constructivist model stated in the institutional educational project (PEI, for its Spanish acronym). title: The Climate Impasse: Disavowal, Exhaustion and Everyday Life in the Climate Crisis
abstract: ABSTRACT The consequences of climate‐related disasters and emergencies are becoming increasingly stark. And yet in many places, consensus on climate action appears unattainable. I call this problem the climate impasse. In this paper, I draw on emerging theory on affect and negativity to characterise this impasse in three ways. title: Populism and normative resistance under EU conditionality: ethnic cleavages and party strategies in the Western Balkans
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how political parties in EU-aspiring countries navigate the tension between domestic cleavages and external pressures discursively. abstract: This study evaluates the market reaction to the official announcement of the Green Equity Designation policy by the Indonesia Stock Exchange. title: Tecnología y conservación del idioma Ngäbere en comunidades indígenas de Costa Rica
abstract: El ngäbere, lengua hablada en cinco territorios indígenas de Costa Rica, enfrenta un proceso de desplazamiento que amenaza la continuidad del patrimonio lingüístico y cultural del pueblo Ngäbe-Buglé. abstract: This paper is based on interviews with respondents who have lived in the city of Craiova for at least part of their lives. Some were born in Bulgaria and later continued their careers in Craiova, while others were born across the Danube but were attracted to Bulgaria in various ways. abstract: This article examines whether the diffusion of populist rhetoric from populist to mainstream parties reduces public support for international organisations (IOs) and multilateral aid. abstract: Este artigo analisa como a mídia britânica contribui para a estigmatização e criminalização de refugiados, requerentes de asilo e imigrantes islâmicos. abstract: While empathy training has long been considered a cornerstone of clinical interventions for intimate partner violence (IPV), emerging evidence on the link between empathy and IPV perpetration suggests an inconsistent association. abstract: Baseball arrived on Prince Edward Island through the same networks of travel, trade, and migration that connected the Island to the wider world. First introduced through visiting fishermen and strengthened by growing ties between Island communities, the game gradually moved from informal contests in fields and public spaces into organized clubs, interprovincial competition, and established leagues. abstract: Abstract Children's interactions with animals shape their understanding of the biological world and humans' place in it. Understanding where children report they encounter and gain their knowledge of animals can provide insight into the early experiences that help shape human attitudes and connections to nature. abstract: Abstract. Urban secondary organic aerosol (SOA) contributes to degraded air quality which can affect human health. Improvements in Los Angeles (LA), CA air quality have mainly plateaued since 2010. In summer 2022, measurements were made to quantify the SOA formation potential (SOA-FP) in ambient LA air. Two oxidation flow reactors (OFRs) ingested ambient air: one was equipped with an electrically conductive polymer inlet that denuded lower volatility species, and the other was run without an inlet. abstract: Sorption of Cu(II) by different horizons of a podzolic soil (A(O)EL, EL, and IIBD) was studied in model laboratory experiments and described using surface complexation models. abstract: Mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) is an integral part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and plays a pivotal role in maintaining mitochondrial function. abstract: Abstract Disputes over land and other resources are common in poor areas of Asia and the Pacific, where common pool resources matter for livelihoods, property rights are poorly defined, and state capacity for dispute resolution is low. For example, in Papua New Guinea (PNG), the subject of the current study, one‐quarter of households experience land disputes within a year and tribal fighting also happens frequently. abstract: Parent–child early interaction is crucial for promoting children’s development. This study explored associations of self-reported and observed parental playfulness with young children’s social, emotional, and behavioral development. title: Elevated CO2 primes drought resistance in mulberry via multi-omics reprogramming of carbon and redox metabolism
abstract: Abstract Drought stress severely constrains the growth and productivity of woody perennials. abstract: How administrative-division adjustments influence agricultural production constitutes a vital issue to unpack the linkage between county-level urbanization and food security across China. abstract: The fundamental biochemical and stereochemical difference in how cell membrane lipids are built between Archaea on one side, and Bacteria and Eukarya on the other is known as the lipid divide. title: FILICIDIO Y HOMICIDIO INFANTIL: UN ANÁLISIS CUANTITATIVO DE LAS SENTENCIAS DICTADAS EN ESPAÑA
abstract: Este estudio ha examinado los casos de filicidio enjuiciados por los tribunales españoles, comparándolos con otros casos de homicidio de personas menores de edad, al objeto de analizar los resultados del proceso judicial y determinar los factores que influyen en los mismos. Mediante el análisis de 128 casos de filicidio enjuiciados entre 2016 y 2025 y otros 82 de homicidio infantil, se ha encontrado que aquellos terminan en sentencia condenatoria en menor medida que los del grupo de comparación, lo cual se explica en buena parte por la aplicación de la causa eximente de responsabilidad de anom
journal: Revista de Derecho Penal y Criminología

title: Becoming-weather: posthuman pedagogy in times of climate and nature emergency in Ireland
abstract: In Ireland, weather has long shaped people’s understandings of place and numerous myths and folktales highlight embodied experiences of the land. Yet, many of these traditional relationships with weather and the environment seem increasingly disconnected from contemporary life and education. In response to the escalating climate and nature emergency, this paper argues that embodied encounters with weather offer valuable possibilities for rethinking education for sustainable development (ESD) in Irish secondary education, going beyond human-centred approaches. title: Certezas fragmentadas. La procelosa vida del “comandante Morales”
abstract: Hidden among inaccuracies, the life of Commander Morales allows for debate about the use of document as providers of certainty. Sources are always partial in several senses and their fragmentary contribution requires conceiving them as imperfect pieces of a puzzle in permanent construction, ultimately incomplete and distorted, where there is no room for shortcuts. Several interesting lives come together in a village near the front to compose a portrait of the Republican rearguard that calls into question the usual narrative and leads us to reflect on the limits of historical knowledge.

title: “Nutritional and Structural Characterization of Mango and Potato Peel Powders and Foxtail Millet for Sustainable Functional Food Development”
abstract: Background and Aim: The increasing demand for sustainable and nutrient-dense functional foods has driven interest in the valorization of agro-industrial by-products. Mango peel, potato peel, and foxtail millet are underutilized resources with considerable nutritional and functional potential. This study aimed to evaluate the nutritional composition, microstructural features, and crystalline properties of mango peel powder (MPP), potato peel powder (PPP), and foxtail millet flour (FMF) to assess their suitability for functional food applications. title: Local Wisdom Integration and Community-Based Environmental Conservation in Bali Starling Conservation for The Development of Tengkudak Tourism Village
abstract: The development of tourism villages is no longer solely oriented toward increasing tourist arrivals but is also expected to maintain environmental sustainability, strengthen local identity, and provide tangible benefits to local communities. Tengkudak Village, Penebel District, Tabanan Regency, Bali, possesses unique potential through the presence of the Bali Starling (Leucopsar rothschildi), agricultural landscapes, rural community life, culture, and local wisdom that has developed within the community's social life. title: Preparation and Study of the Mechanical Properties of CTBN /n‐ CeO 2 Synergistically Modified With Epoxy‐Based Glass Fiber Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Glass fiber‐reinforced polymer (GFRP) composites are widely utilized across various industries due to their high specific strength and cost‐effectiveness. However, their structural reliability under complex loading is fundamentally limited by the inherent brittleness of the epoxy resin matrix and weak interfacial bonding, which often precipitate premature interlaminar delamination. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a multi‐scale synergistic toughening strategy using carboxyl‐terminated butadiene‐acrylonitrile (CTBN) rubber and nano‐cerium dioxide (n‐CeO 2 ). title: The train and the abyss: Israeli Hebrew and the dialectic of old, new, and in-between
abstract: This paper examines the pseudo-restoration of Hebrew and its status in modern Israel as a case study in how an ‘ancient’ language is mobilised for national identity and political myth-making. Originally a regional variant of Canaanite, Hebrew was superseded as a vernacular by Aramaic and ceased to be spoken in late antiquity. However, it survived in written texts and is perhaps best understood not as a language but as a set of linguistic repertoires built around an abstract matrix known as leshon ha-qodesh (the holy tongue). title: Adaptive Lubrication and Antiwear Enabled by Synergy Between Friction‐Induced In Situ Tribo‐Click Reaction and Gel Confinement of Reaction Products
abstract: ABSTRACT Friction and wear cause massive energy dissipation and mechanical failure, driving the demand for advanced lubrication. Here, we report a facile gel‐confined in situ tribo‐click platform triggered by interfacial friction. Azide and alkyne precursors are incorporated into supramolecular gel lubricants; reciprocal sliding on copper releases catalytic Cu(I) ions to initiate on‐site Cu(I)‐catalyzed azide‐alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reactions, producing lubricious triazole adducts. title: Agricultural chemical intensification and ecological footprint comparative analysis of pesticide and insecticide consumption
abstract: This study examines how agricultural chemical intensification affects environmental sustainability in Nigeria by comparing the ecological footprint impacts of pesticide and insecticide consumption from 1990 to 2024. The analysis incorporates economic growth, renewable energy consumption, financial development, and energy use as control variables, and tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. abstract: Objective: This study investigates the morphology and elemental composition of particles deposited on Tillandsia usneoides leaves, focusing on trace element identification and potential interference from foliar fertilizer in air pollution biomonitoring Theoretical Framework: Plant-based biomonitoring is a cost-effective alternative for assessing atmospheric pollution, particularly in remote areas with limited access to conventional monitoring systems. title: El trabajo docente en tiempos de la Nueva Escuela Mexicana: extensión, subordinación y efectos
abstract: This communication presents the results of a research study whose objective was to analyze the effects of extending the teaching workday during the 2023-2024 school year. From a qualitative perspective, the idea of teaching work by González (2012), the concept of workday extension by González, Rivera, and Guerra (2024), and the subordination of life to work by Sánchez (2018) and Pagura (2008) are revisited. title: Charlie White, Leon Day, and a Groundbreaking Summer in Toronto: The Integration Story of the International League Maple Leafs
abstract: For much of their existence, the International League Toronto Maple Leafs adhered to the same segregationist colour barrier that was in place across all of white organized baseball. For myriad reasons, it wasn't until 1951 that the team began an earnest pursuit of Black ballplayers. A young catcher and infielder named Charlie White, and the legendary Negro League veteran, Leon Day, were the first Black players to suit up for the Maple Leafs in July 1951. title: Linking reproduction and recruitment: Identifying demographic bottlenecks limiting the spread of Bighead Carp and Silver Carp in the Ohio River
abstract: Abstract Objective Reproduction and recruitment represent distinct demographic processes that may independently limit establishment and spread of an invasive species. We evaluated reproduction and recruitment success of Bighead Carp Hypophthalmichthys nobilis and Silver Carp H. molitrix in the Ohio River basin across multiple spatial and temporal scales to identify potential demographic bottlenecks. title: CLIMATE CHANGE AND FOOD SECURITY AS A HUMAN RIGHT: INTERNATIONAL LEGAL OBLIGATIONS OF STATES AND THE EXPERIENCE OF UZBEKISTAN
abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognised not only as an environmental challenge but as a direct threat to the human right to adequate food protected under Article 11 of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR). This article examines how the warming climate reshapes the content and the reach of States' international legal obligations to respect, protect and fulfil the right to food, and tests that framework against the experience of Uzbekistan, a doubly land-locked, water-stressed Central Asian State pursuing rapid legal reform. title: Cambios, tendencias e implicaciones socioeconómicas del uso y cobertura del suelo hacia 2050 en territorios de montaña: La Araucanía (Chile)
abstract: Este artículo analiza los cambios de uso y cobertura del suelo ocurridos entre 1994 y 2017 en ocho comunas de montaña de La Araucanía, sur de Chile, y desarrolla una proyección tendencial hacia 2050. Se utilizaron catastros de uso del suelo y vegetación de la Corporación Nacional Forestal, procesados en QGIS 3.36 y armonizados en diez categorías. La proyección se realizó mediante Land Change Modeler de TerrSet 2020 y cadenas de Markov. Las dinámicas demográficas y urbano-rurales se examinaron a partir de los censos de 1982, 1992 y 2017. title: In Their Own Words: Qualitative and Quantitative Analyses of What Students, Staff, and Faculty Say About Vertical Transfer
abstract: This research analyzed higher education constituencies’ statements about vertical transfer (student transfer from community to bachelor’s colleges). Data consisted of both focus group excerpts involving dozens of students, staff, and faculty, and of answers to open-ended survey questions completed by thousands of students and faculty. Results were generally consistent using both qualitative (topic identification) and quantitative (bigram frequency and sentiment analysis) analyses. title: Optimized production and application-oriented characterization of a low-molecular-weight levan-type EPS from Bacillus licheniformis CPS3–3 for the recovery of UV-impaired keratinocytes
abstract: Microbial exopolysaccharides (EPS) are promising sustainable carbohydrate polymers for aqueous biomaterial and skincare-related formulations; however, achieving high production efficiency together with favorable physicochemical and functional properties remains challenging. In this study, an EPS-producing Bacillus licheniformis strain, CPS3, was isolated from peony flowers and improved by N-methyl-N′-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine mutagenesis to obtain the high-yield mutant CPS3-3. Subsequent sucrose-centered medium optimization using response surface methodology increased EPS production to 34.2 g/L

title: Scenes of feminist listening as act: a psychosocial ethnography of feminist desire in Argentinean psychoanalysis
abstract: Abstract When researching a specific field of practice, or a situated phenomenon, we may wonder what is it that keeps this very field alive, lending it vitality as well as attunement to times, necessities and possibilities. Here I propose a psychosocial ethnography in which I knit together historical and contemporary threads that compose what we can hold on to as scenes of feminist desire in Argentinean psychoanalysis. title: Marketing de Influencers y Comportamiento de Compra Impulsiva Gastronómica en Ecuador
abstract: El presente estudio analiza la relación entre el marketing de influencers y el comportamiento de compra impulsiva gastronómica en Guayaquil, Ecuador. La investigación tuvo como objetivo determinar la relación entre ambos constructos y examinar adicionalmente la asociación del rango de edad con el comportamiento de compra impulsiva. Se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cuantitativo, con diseño no experimental y corte transversal. title: Entre La Norma y su Aplicación: Análisis de la Implementación de la Regulación Ambiental Municipal
abstract: La existencia de un amplio marco jurídico ambiental no garantiza su aplicación en el territorio. En municipios con crecimiento urbano y turístico, la capacidad institucional para implementar, supervisar y evaluar la regulación ambiental es fundamental. Este artículo analiza el grado de implementación documentalmente acreditado de la regulación ambiental aplicable al municipio de Bahía de Banderas, Nayarit, mediante la contrastación entre obligaciones jurídicas y evidencia sobre su aplicación en competencias normativas, ambientales, de planeación, participación y transparencia ambiental. title: What’s on the menu? Quantifying the greenhouse gas emissions and water footprint of the food service procurement within elite male & female football teams
abstract: Abstract Background: The global food system contributes approximately 34% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) and exerts substantial pressure on freshwater resources, yet the environmental impact of food provision within professional sport remains unexplored. Addressing this evidence gap, this study quantified the environmental footprint of food service provision across four professional football clubs in England, representing the English Premier League (EPL), English Football League Championship (EFL Champ), English Football League One (EFL L1), and Women’s Super League (WSL). title: Supporting circular economy decisions in hospitality SMEs: A multi-criteria approach to strategy prioritization
abstract: Circular economy (CE) research has mainly focused on manufacturing and product-based sectors, while its application to service industries remains less understood. In services, circularity cannot be reduced to material loops, as it involves customer participation, organizational capabilities, service routines, and stakeholder coordination. title: From Knowledge Organisation to Knowledge Application: Designing Mind-Mapping Instruction for Senior High School Regional Geography in China
abstract: Senior high school regional geography in China requires students to compare regions, explain relationships and consider development problems. Mind mapping can organise knowledge, but a complete diagram does not demonstrate independent knowledge application. This conceptual article develops a four-stage instructional framework through a purposive synthesis of curriculum and geographical education research, mapping literature, and theories of engagement, transfer, scaffolding and formative assessment. abstract: ABSTRACT As the world navigates intertwined environmental and economic crises, the challenge of sustainable energy provision has grown more pressing than ever. These interconnected imperatives emphasize the need for sustainable energy solutions that protect the environment. Therefore, the renewable energy transition is strategically important for achieving environmental, economic, and sustainable development goals. title: La categoría “acumulación por desposesión”. Una reflexión sobre su uso en los estudios rurales argentinos
abstract: La categoría “acumulación por desposesión”, asociada a la obra de David Harvey, es muy utilizada en programas de investigación en ciencias sociales –y en particular en los que se centran en el sector rural– para explicar la instalación o el crecimiento de capitales dedicados a la producción de materias primas. Este artículo, escrito en clave de ensayo, se propone discutir el concepto (considerando los trabajos de Harvey y sus antecedentes) y, en particular, ponderar la virtud que tiene su aplicación en los estudios agrarios argentinos. title: Minor moments of more-than-human encounters: Rethinking climate change education in early childhood
abstract: In the context of intensifying climate crises, early childhood education is increasingly positioned as a site for cultivating the capacities, sensitivities, and solidarities needed for more sustainable futures (Spiteri & Pace, 2023; UNESCO & MECCE, 2024). Yet dominant approaches to climate change education continue to privilege cognitive, anthropocentric, and developmental framings, emphasizing knowledge transmission and individual responsibility while overlooking children’s relational and ecological entanglements. title: Indicator-based diagnosis of carbon metabolism in production–living–ecological spaces: Land-use transitions, ecological network relationships, and terrain-constrained carbon flows in the Nanling Mountains, China
abstract: Land-use changes among production–living–ecological (PLE) spaces are critical drivers of regional carbon metabolism. Although these changes have been extensively examined in urban agglomerations and plains, their carbon metabolic mechanisms in mountainous areas remain inadequately explored. In this study, ecological network analysis (ENA) was used to identify ecological interactions among PLE spatial categories and evaluate the utility of the carbon metabolism network. title: La prevención del sedentarismo en niños y adolescentes
abstract: La prevención del sedentarismo durante la infancia y la adolescencia requiere diferenciar el tiempo sedentario, la actividad física insuficiente y el uso recreativo de pantallas. Este artículo analiza estrategias educativas y familiares mediante una revisión bibliográfica narrativa crítica de seis publicaciones comprendidas en el periodo de elegibilidad 2021–2026. Se efectuaron búsquedas dirigidas y se verificaron las referencias en páginas editoriales, registros académicos y organismos oficiales. title: An evolutionary perspective on the conservation of endogenous Ah receptor activation
abstract: ABSTRACT The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) senses environmental and physiological cues by responding to a wide range of chemicals, thereby mediating diverse physiological functions. There are four sources of AHR agonists: anthropogenic, microbial, dietary, and host origin. The structural diversity and potency of the chemicals that activate the AHR makes it difficult to discern key ligands that facilitate various activities. abstract: Purpose is to evaluate the impact of the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic on selected temporal and organizational parameters of prehospital emergency care for patients with suspected stroke in the Ústí nad Labem Region by comparing system performance before and during the pandemic. Materials and Methods. A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the Electronic Patient Record system of the Ústí nad Labem Region Emergency Medical Service. title: Pengaruh Segmentasi Pasar terhadap Minat Pembelian Perlengkapan Sekolah di UD. Harapan Kota Gunungsitoli
abstract: Persaingan usaha ritel perlengkapan sekolah di Kota Gunungsitoli semakin ketat seiring bertambahnya pelaku usaha, sementara data penjualan UD. Harapan tahun 2025 menunjukkan fluktuasi yang signifikan antara periode puncak dan periode normal, sehingga ketepatan segmentasi pasar dalam memahami minat pembelian konsumen menjadi penting untuk dikaji. title: Mecanismos Inmunometabólicos de la Resistencia a la Insulina y sus Implicaciones en el Síndrome pos-COVID-19
abstract: La infección por SARS-CoV-2 desencadena una respuesta inflamatoria sistémica que trasciende el compromiso respiratorio y afecta de manera significativa al sistema endocrino-metabólico. El objetivo de este artículo de revisión fue analizar los mecanismos inmunometabólicos de la resistencia a la insulina y sus implicaciones en el síndrome pos-COVID-19. title: Harnessing benefits of vermicompost for sustainable agriculture: improving soil health, crop productivity and environmental sustainability
abstract: Vermicompost (VC) is an effective organic amendment of soil that is produced through the non-thermophilic biodegradation of organic waste by earthworms and microbes. This study focuses on identifying influence of VC on soil physical properties and biological functions such as soil structure, bulk density, and water-holding capacity, as well as its contribution to nutrient availability and microbial activity. title: A Numerical Study of the Equatorial Wind Jet Response to the X2.2 Solar Flare on 6 September 2017
abstract: Abstract Using paired Thermosphere–Ionosphere–Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM) simulations, we investigated the response of the equatorial thermospheric zonal wind jet to the X2.2 solar flare that peaked at 09:10 UT on 6 September 2017. title: How sustainable finance initiatives and forums address environmental issues, including climate change, and the challenges they face
abstract: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles and effects, including how they overlap and synergize. This study examined how transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums contribute to scaling up private finance and investment and encourage private sector participation. title: Extreme Heat and Food Price Inflation in The United Arab Emirates
abstract: The UAE is one of the world's hottest countries and imports more than 90% of the food consumed by its population. This study asks a simple question: when UAE summers become more extreme, do food prices increase? To answer this, annual temperature records and annual food price inflation data for the UAE from 2013 to 2025 were collected and compared using straightforward statistical tools - averages, percentage changes, year-on-year comparisons, and the Pearson correlation coefficient. abstract: In this paper, we reflect on the central role of teachers’ actions in the initial construction of algebraic practice in the classroom, as well as on the value of the collective space as a condition that enhances this process. We emphasize how this practice can foster the development of habits for interpreting information in numerical expressions and transforming them in ways that enable new interpretations. title: Reconstructing the Truth: Anti‐Immigrant Discourses of Right‐Wing Populist Parties in Türkiye
abstract: This study examines the ways in which anti‐immigrant right‐wing populist discourse is produced in Türkiye within the framework of population politics. The discourses of the Victory Party and the Good Party were analyzed within the framework of Wodak’s (2015a) discourse‐historical approach; a dataset consisting of parliamentary group speeches and press releases covering the periods of the 2023 general elections and the 2024 local elections was used. title: What Predicts Entrepreneurship? The Quagmire of Entrepreneurial Desirability
abstract: Entrepreneurial action begins with the availability of an opportunity and with an individual's perception that entrepreneurship represents a desirable and feasible course of action. Building on the entrepreneurial event model, this study examines the factors associated with the entrepreneurial desirability among individuals who received exposure to entrepreneurship training and activities in Pokhara Metropolitan City, Nepal. title: The Impact of Executives’ Overseas Background on Corporate ESG: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
abstract: Within the dual background of the “dual carbon” strategy and the standardized development of ESG in capital markets, exploring the driving mechanisms of corporate ESG performance is crucial, for promoting the sustainable operation of listed companies. This research takes Chinese A-share listed companies, from 2009 to 2023, as the research sample and, empirically analyzes the impact of executives’ overseas background on corporate ESG performance, based on upper echelons theory. title: Effect of Weed Control Methods on the Performance of Maize (Zea mays L.) Varieties in the Northern Guinea and Sudan Savanna Zones of Kebbi State
abstract: Effective weed control and varietal selection are important for maize productivity in savanna agroecological zones. This study evaluated the responses of three maize varieties to five weed control treatments in two field trials conducted during the 2025 wet season in Aliero and Yauri, Kebbi State, Nigeria. abstract: This article aims to situate itself within religious anthropological scholarship through a comparative study of Indigenous religious transformation in Malaysia and Bangladesh. title: Segundo consenso de postura sobre los aneurismas de aorta abdominal en México
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive and life-threatening disease, with rupture-related mortality reaching up to 80% in Mexico. Limited national epidemiological data and the need to standardize diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up strategies prompted the development of the Second National Consensus on AAA in Mexico, coordinated by the Mexican Society of Angiology, Vascular and Endovascular Surgery (SMACVE), based on the Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines and adapted to local practice. METHODS: The consensus was developed using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method
institutions: Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubirán

title: Chronic non-24-h light–dark cycles alter healthspan measures but not overall survival in male C57BL/6 J mice
abstract: Circadian biology is recognized for its importance to physiology and metabolism, with implications for healthy aging and disease risk. abstract: El concepto de algoritmo suele asociarse en la actualidad al concepto de programa o a desarrollos tecnológicos contemporáneos. title: Climate effects on flowering cues of ornithophilous plants in a Costa Rican cloud forest
abstract: ABSTRACT The influence of a changing climate on the phenology of organisms in a region is dependent on how regional climate cues or modifies the timing of local life history events and how those cues are changing over time. There is extensive evidence of phenolological shifts in flowering time over the past 50 years in response to increasing temperatures in temperate regions, but far less is known about tropical regions where seasonality is less temperature driven. title: Diversity of woody species in homestead agroforestry practices in Amhara National Regional State, Ethiopia
abstract: Homestead agroforestry is a cornerstone of traditional farming systems in Ethiopia, significantly contributing to both livelihoods and biodiversity. While similar practices have been studied elsewhere, findings are often context-dependent. Therefore, this study was initiated to reveal the contribution of homestead agroforestry practices to woody species conservation in the Amhara Regional State. A multistage random sampling design was employed, in which 300 smallholder farmers were randomly selected from six Kebeles. title: Book Publishing Activities of the Union for the Liberation of Ukraine in Europe (1914–1918)
abstract: The article analyzes the distinctive features of the book publishing activities of the Union for the Liberation of Ukraine (ULU) during the First World War. These activities became possible due to financial support from Germany and Austria-Hungary, part of which was directed towards information and propaganda campaigns serving both the interests of the Central Powers and the promotion of the Ukrainian question in Europe. The quantitative investigation employed microdata provided by the Indonesian Central Statistics Agency (BPS). title: Living with the Stones: Intangible Heritage, Storytelling, and Contemporary Engagements with Megalithic Landscapes
abstract: This article explores how contemporary intangible cultural heritage (ICH) is produced and negotiated through lived engagements with megalithic sites in Portugal and Scotland. While prehistoric stone circles are commonly interpreted through archaeological and expert-led frameworks, the present study foregrounds personal narratives, sensory encounters, and imaginative practices as forms of ICH which are central to how these sites acquire meaning in the present. title: Protecting birds in protected areas: a multi-scale analysis of forest structure and species occurrence
abstract: Protected areas are cornerstones of avian conservation, yet forest-associated bird communities continue to decline even within protected lands. The capacity of a protected area to sustain bird populations depends on both internal habitat quality and the surrounding landscape context, yet the relative importance of these scales remains poorly understood. We evaluate how forest structure at three nested spatial scales (local, park, and county) influences the occurrence of forest-associated birds within protected areas. title: The Humanitarian Principles: Relativity Revisited
abstract: Abstract The principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and independence are widely viewed as integral to humanitarian assistance. Yet, despite shaping the work of many humanitarians, the international legal status of these principles is unclear. title: Traumatismo craneoencefálico en motociclistas: Síntesis de la evidencia con contextualización para Paraguay
abstract: Introducción: en Paraguay, los motociclistas fueron el 58 % de las muertes viales en 2024; en una serie hospitalaria de motociclistas fallecidos, el 86,9 % presentaba lesión craneoencefálica. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia sobre mecanismos, factores modificables y prevención del traumatismo craneoencefálico (TCE) en motociclistas, distinguiendo evidencia directa e indirecta, y contextualizarla para Paraguay.Materiales y métodos: revisión narrativa (selección intencionada, no exhaustiva) con búsquedas documentadas en PubMed/MEDLINE, LILACS, SciELO y fuentes oficiales (octubre de 2026).

abstract: Abstract Given the existing gap in biodiversity funding, mobilizing private finance will be essential to achieving global biodiversity conservation goals, especially across lower- and middle-income countries with limited capacity and public finance. The emerging voluntary biodiversity market (VBM) holds promise to leverage private finance for biodiversity, but credit-generating protocols must be robust to prevent greenwashing and maximize effectiveness. abstract: Introduction. The choice of construction technology affects not only the organization of the construction process but also its duration and, consequently, the project’s payback period. The growing trend towards construction in dense urban environments necessitates the active development of underground space. abstract: During pediatric hospitalization, invasive and painful procedures are frequently performed and may cause anxiety and fear, particularly among children who, due to their age, may not fully understand the situation. If pain is not adequately managed, it may be associated with negative consequences, such as sleep disturbances, needle phobia, and reluctance or refusal to seek or receive healthcare. title: Assessment of phytochemicals and developmental toxicity of Litsea cubeba (Lours.) Pers. fruit extract using zebrafish embryo as a model
abstract: Litsea cubeba (Lours.) Pers. is an aromatic plant whose fruits are extensively used in traditional medicine and as flavouring ingredients. Although widely used, the information regarding its phytochemical constituents and toxicity remains scarce. This study focused on identifying the phytochemicals present in the methanolic fruit extract of L. cubeba, as well as evaluating the embryotoxicity and developmental toxicity using zebrafish embryos as a model. abstract: L’article analyse la transformation profonde du paysage sécuritaire sahélien depuis 2023, marquée par le retrait des forces internationales et l’affaiblissement des États de la région du Liptako-Gourma. abstract: The paleobiology of sauropodomorph dinosaurs has historically garnered considerable interest, primarily because this clade includes the largest terrestrial vertebrates. Bone and tooth microstructures are crucial sources of paleobiological data, and many paleohistological studies have focused on this group. Here we review and synthesize the main advances in an understanding of sauropodomorph paleobiology derived from osteological and dental histology. title: Bancarización, autonomía y poder en la vejez rural mexicana
abstract: Este artículo revisa cómo el pago bancario de la Pensión para el Bienestar incide en la autonomía económica de las personas adultas mayores del campo mexicano. El padrón ya no es el vacío principal. Lo que queda abierto es quién controla el dinero después de que el gobierno lo deposita. El análisis se sostiene en el Estado ampliado de Antonio Gramsci: el gobierno pone la tarjeta, el cajero y las reglas del Banco del Bienestar; en las familias y comunidades puede volverse habitual que un hijo, una nuera o un vecino cobre «por ayuda». title: Morphological and molecular identification of Magnaporthe oryzae causing finger millet blast disease in Kenya
abstract: Finger millet { Eleusine coracana (L.) Gaertn.} is an underutilized climate-resilient cereal crop with excellent nutraceutical properties. It is an important subsistence crop to the majority smallholder women farmers in western and eastern parts of Kenya, where it is grown under low input mixed cropping systems. One of the challenges limiting its production is blast disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (syn. Pyricularia oryzae ). abstract: Date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) cultivation in the Arabian Peninsula represents a six- millennium agronomic tradition now undergoing rapid genomic and phytochemical reappraisal. abstract: Random walks are commonly used to model movement throughout the sciences, from the motion of particles and molecules to the observed behaviour of animals and crowds. title: Juridical Intelligibility: The Limits of Anti-Discrimination Law in Family Relations
abstract: Anti-discrimination law addresses unjustified differential treatment but assumes that the subjects and relationships under review are already legally intelligible. This article argues that the framework cannot fully address forms of inequality produced by the legal conditions that determine which family relationships are recognized in the first place. It distinguishes downstream discrimination from upstream inequality and shows how dominant family norms, binary registration systems, and discretionary decision-making can sustain exclusion within formally non-discriminatory frameworks. abstract: This article explores how creative writing can accommodate non-binary gender experiences that exceed the normative intelligibility of language. Drawing on a free six-session workshop held in Viña del Mar (Chile) in 2024, it proposes an atmospheric reading of four texts produced by non-binary participants. abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), which is a bacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, still remains a prominent global public health challenge though it is both preventable and curable. The disease was historically managed through supportive care like the sanatorium care and collapse therapy. The treatment of TB was transformed in the antibiotic era. This was brought about by the introduction of streptomycin and the subsequent multidrug regimens. abstract: This paper undertakes an in-depth exploration of Frida Kahlo’s iconic self-portraits, reinterpreting them as profound visual narratives of her experience living with lingering pain, illness, and trauma. abstract: Financial disruption can intensify market uncertainty and increase the importance of credible corporate communication. This study aims to analyze the role of corporate storytelling in shaping market reactions during periods of financial disruption. title: Urban Spatial Structure and the Skill Earnings Gap: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how urban spatial structure affects the earnings gap between high‐ and low‐skilled workers in China. title: Comparative mobilization and bioaccumulation of cadmium and lead in apple orchards and associated screening level ecological and human health risks
abstract: Abstract Lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd) accumulate in agricultural soils through long-term agrochemical use, posing ecosystem and food-safety risks; whether these inputs elevate Pb and Cd in edible fruit had not previously been quantified for Iranian apple orchards. This screening-level, multi-index study assessed Pb and Cd across the fertilizer/pesticide–soil–fruit continuum in Padena, Semirom, combining paired soil and root-stem-fruit tissue analysis ( n = 36) with ecological and deterministic human health risk indices for adults and children. title: City birds are smaller but noisier: morphology, body condition, and song variation between Rufous-collared Sparrows (Zonotrichia capensis) from urban and wild environments in Central Chile
abstract: Abstract Urban environments impose challenges for wildlife survival, yet some populations show morphological and behavioral adaptations to these novel conditions. The Rufous-collared Sparrow, Zonotrichia capensis, is a neotropical bird that successfully inhabits both urban and wild environments. This study evaluated morphological and song variations of populations in Central Chile and their association with food availability and anthropogenic noise. title: Wild bee diversity in the village of Peyresq and the surrounding areas in the southern French Alps
abstract: Background Wild bees are essential pollinators, yet the populations of an increasing number of species are declining across Europe, with knowledge gaps particularly acute in mountain regions. The southern French Alps represent a biogeographically exceptional area, situated at the interface of Alpine and Mediterranean influences, but their bee fauna remains poorly documented. title: Plant–soil compartments predominantly shape microbiome structure and function across juvenile and mature moso bamboo
abstract: Plant-associated microbes are essential for host resistance and productivity, but their host age-related dynamics remain poorly explored in long-lived species such as bamboo. In this study, we investigated the microbiomes of various bamboo compartments (i.e., bulk and rhizosphere soils, roots, stems, branches, and leaves) in juvenile and mature moso bamboo ( Phyllostachys edulis ), to explore age-dependent microbial patterns in various compartments. title: An Interface to the World: Evoking Environmental Responsibility in Responsive Environments
abstract: The late twentieth-century art form Responsive Environments (REs) comprised interrelations between artist, artwork, and audience, wherein response-ability and responsibility to the social and/or physical environment of the artwork could be tangibly evoked. Wherein participants’ collective behavior within an artwork-as-environment serves as a proxy for the cumulative effect of human behavior on the more-than-human environment. title: Household Water Sources, Accessibility and Consumption Patterns in Selected Rural Communities of Taraba State, Nigeria
abstract: Rural water insecurity remains a persistent development challenge in Nigeria, particularly in communities with limited access to reliable water infrastructure. This study assessed water supply, household water consumption patterns, and factors influencing water use in ten rural communities of Taraba State, northeastern Nigeria. The communities were purposively selected based on their rural characteristics and varying access to functional water infrastructure, after which households were sampled systematically. title: Acoustic cavitation-mediated ultrasound-assisted extraction enhances recovery of antioxidant and antidiabetic phytochemicals from Tanacetum gracile: Stabilization through alginate–whey protein microencapsulation
abstract: Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) offers a rapid process-intensification approach for recovering plant-derived bioactive compounds, while subsequent microencapsulation may improve their post-extraction stability. This study investigated the recovery and stabilization of antioxidant and antidiabetic phytochemicals from Tanacetum gracile using UAE followed by alginate–whey protein microencapsulation. title: Botanical diversity and seasonal dynamics of the Asian elephant (Elephas maximus) diet in Sri Lanka: Insights from frontline rangers
abstract: Dietary knowledge of Asian elephants ( Elephas maximus ) in Sri Lanka remains limited, and earlier inventories underestimate the range of plants they consumed. This constrains evidence-based conservation and the mitigation of human–elephant conflict (HEC). We compiled an expanded dietary inventory using a ranger-based assessment and tested for seasonal variation in diet composition. title: Implementación de la auto-toma para VPH en programas de tamizaje
abstract: El automuestreo cervicovaginal para la detección del virus del papiloma humano (VPH) constituye una alternativa para fortalecer los programas de tamizaje del cáncer cervicouterino, especialmente en poblaciones con barreras de acceso sanitario. El objetivo fue evaluar la evidencia científica sobre su implementación en programas de tamizaje, considerando las características metodológicas y poblacionales de los estudios, el desempeño diagnóstico, la aceptación y la factibilidad. title: Comparative Study of the Performance of Black-Coated and Reflecting-Surface Solar Box Cookers and a Parabolic Dish Solar Cooker
abstract: The thermal performance of a two-compartment solar box cooker and a parabolic dish solar cooker were experimented and compared under same environmental conditions at [name of laboratory/workshop], Bali Town, Taraba State, Nigeria. The identical box compartments (aperture 0.334 m² each) shared one glazing and two booster mirrors; one had black-coated inner surfaces (SC.B) and the other reflecting walls with a black floor (SC.RB). title: Entre lo instrumental y lo pedagógico: percepciones y competencias digitales de docentes universitarios de inglés
abstract: Este artículo presenta los resultados de un estudio de enfoque mixto, descriptivo-exploratorio, que analizó la percepción de doce docentes universitarios sobre la integración de tecnologías digitales en la enseñanza del inglés como lengua extranjera (ILE), en una institución privada de educación superior en Chile. journal: Autoctonia Revista de Ciencias Sociales e Historia

title: Victimización digital y derecho penal: respuestas jurídicas frente al acoso, sextorsión y violencia tecnológica contemporánea
abstract: The expansion of digital technologies has reshaped intimidation, sexual coercion, and violations of privacy, challenging traditional categories of criminal law. This study examines contemporary criminal law responses to digital harassment, sextortion, and image-based sexual abuse, identifying regulatory, evidentiary, jurisdictional, and victimological limitations documented between 2021 and 2026. title: Determinants of soil aggregate stability in a long-term experiment under different tillage intensity and crop management systems
abstract: Soil aggregate stability (AS) is a critical indicator of soil physical quality, yet its long-term drivers in vulnerable silty soils remain inadequately quantified. This study analyzed the determinants of AS over 25 years (1999–2023) in a long-term field experiment on a temperate silty Luvisol, comparing four cropping systems: conventional (CON), low-input (LI), organic (ORG), and conservation agriculture (CA). abstract: Anonim ortaklıklarda akdedilen pay sahipleri sözleşmelerinin aleniyeti, hukuk alanında hem teorik hem de pratik açıdan önem taşımaktadır. title: Convergencia de procesos en la institucionalización académica del trabajo social: Universidad del Valle
abstract: Introducción La institucionalización académica del trabajo social en Cali, iniciada en 1953 con la creación de la Facultad de Servicio Social de Cali y que en la década de 1960 muestra una relación intensa con la Universidad del Valle, experimentó durante los primeros años de 1970 una fase particular del proceso que deriva en la anexión de la facultad a la Universidad del Valle como unidad académica de la División de Humanidades. title: An Argument for Minimalism about Action
abstract: Abstract Minimalism is the view that the mark of action is object‐causation, rather than intentionality, voluntariness or goal‐directedness. Actions, on this view, are instances of objects causing change. Despite a recent surge of interest in the view, it is still seldom regarded as a serious alternative to orthodox theories of action, according to which action is, by its nature, intentional, voluntary, or, more broadly, a psychological phenomenon. This paper argues that it should. It provides a simple argument for regarding minimalism as the default view of the nature of action.

title: Invariantes frente al contexto en la obra de Fernando Higueras en Oriente Medio
abstract: El nuevo protagonismo de los países productores de petróleo a partir de la década de los 1970 empujóa muchos arquitectos occidentales a buscar encargos en países de Oriente Medio que, liberados ya de atadurascoloniales y con unos ingresos sin precedentes, promovían proyectos de gran escala. Los profesionales españoles nofueron ajenos a este fenómeno. Entre ellos destacó Fernando Higueras, quien apeló a la tradición de la arquitecturahispano-musulmana para adaptar soluciones tipológicas ya ensayadas en España al contexto geográfico y culturalde estos países. title: Understanding the impact of air pollution on young children in Delhi through the voices of parents, teachers, and children
abstract: Climate change is increasingly considered as one of the greatest threats to the health, development and well-being of children. New Delhi's winter smog has raised concerns about the immediate and long-term effects of air pollution on children. Young children are physiologically more vulnerable to air pollutants. The current New Delhi Air Quality Index is 302, indicating a hazardous level of real-time air pollution, with PM2.5 levels. title: EXTREMOS DE PRECIPITAÇÃO E SISTEMA DE ALERTA DE DESASTRES: UMA ANÁLISE DA COMUNICAÇÃO E DA RESPOSTA DA POPULAÇÃO EM ANGRA DOS REIS – RJ
abstract: Este trabalho analisa a adesão da população aos alertas hidrometeorológicos emitidos pela Defesa Civil do município de Angra dos Reis (RJ), região marcada pela recorrência de chuvas intensas e deslizamentos de encostas. A pesquisa buscou compreender o processo de transformação dos dados hidrometeorológicos em alertas operacionais e avaliar como essas mensagens são percebidas, interpretadas e utilizadas pela população residente em áreas de risco. title: Small-state strategic resilience in NATO’s southeastern flank: A conceptual and comparative analysis of Albania and Kosovo
abstract: Abstract Hybrid threats, cyberattacks and geopolitical interference are increasingly challenging NATO’s southeastern flank. Despite this, resilience research tends to focus more on the alliance’s northern and eastern areas. The Western Balkans, which are highly vulnerable to hybrid pressure and strategically located along the Mediterranean–Central Europe corridor, often receive insufficient attention. title: Educación financiera y bienestar integral en familias de La Libertad, Perú: Un enfoque multidimensional
abstract: En América Latina, amplios sectores de la población continúan enfrentando escenarios de informalidad laboral, vulnerabilidad económica y limitadas capacidades de planificación financiera, situación que no solo repercute en la administración de los ingresos, sino también en el bienestar emocional, familiar y social. El objetivo de esta investigación fue determinar la relación entre la educación financiera y el bienestar integral en una muestra de 497 familias de la región La Libertad, Perú, desde una perspectiva multidimensional. title: Der Tiger, A German War Film: An Anti-War Movie or An Act of National Atonement?
abstract: This article examines Dennis Gansel's 2025 film Der Tiger through the historical, psychological, and moral dimensions of Germany's war against the Soviet Union during World War II. Set against the collapse of German military operations on the Eastern Front, the film follows a Tiger tank crew assigned a mysterious mission that gradually exposes the consequences of ideological warfare and unquestioning obedience to military orders. title: Efectos del contexto consonántico y del acento léxico en las vocales del español en la ciudad de Mar del Plata (Buenos Aires, Argentina)
abstract: Based on data from speakers in Mar del Plata (Buenos Aires, Argentina), this study analyzes the influence of consonantal context and lexical stress on the F1 and F2 trajectories of the Spanish vowels /a e o/. abstract: Isoflavonoids are a specialized subclass of flavonoids predominantly distributed in the Fabaceae, where they fulfill essential ecophysiological roles as antimicrobial phytoalexins and symbiotic signal molecules. abstract: Hospitalization contributes to worsening of the nutritional status and malnutrition is associate to increase in morbidity and mortality. abstract: This study clarifies the meaning and role of the concept of “ruins” within Arata Isozaki's apocalyptic view of cities. Focusing on his discourse, it examines this concept from four perspectives: 1) historical relativization, 2) diachronic transformation accompanying social conditions, 3) the sublation of self-discourse and external criticism, and 4) contrast with Metabolism. title: Folic acid intake by pregnant women from Vale do Jequitinhonha, Brazil, and the contribution of fortified foods
abstract: The folate deficiency can result in irreversible health damage, such as the neural tube defects. The aim of this article is to determine the folate intake of pregnant women in Vale do Jequitinhonha, Minas Gerais state, Brazil, one of the poorest regions in the world. A descriptive, cross-sectional study was done in 2013 with 492 pregnant women attending the basic health units run by the public health service (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) in 15 municipalities. abstract: Salinization is a major constraint to agricultural sustainability in arid and semi-arid regions worldwide. The ameliorative effects of grass clipping mulching on alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) growth and forage quality in soda saline–alkali land in Northeast China and its regulatory mechanisms were studied. abstract: Healthy eating habits promote wellness and prevent disease, however, despite the intention to change a bad habit, people often fail in theirattempts. This is due, since the performance of a change requires self-regulation skills that allow to observe, to evaluate and to take an action, in a constant motivation during the all the process; not only theknowledge about proper nutrition. abstract: Abstract Economic development is inherently uneven, proceeding through sequenced imbalances across sectors, skill groups, and regions. Following Ray (2010), this paper adopts an imbalance framework as its organizing lens, arguing that “balanced growth" is an inadequate abstraction for economies undergoing processes of structural transformation. We show that development strategies — from dual-economy transitions to modern industrial policy — rely on steering these productive disequilibria. title: Development and preliminary validation of the Arabic Quality of Life During War Scale (AQOL-War)
abstract: BACKGROUND: War profoundly affects quality of life (QOL) by disrupting daily routines, damaging infrastructure, and creating fear and uncertainty. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate the Arabic Quality of Life During War Scale (AQOL-War). METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Sudan during wartime from June 11 to September 10, 2024. Data were collected through an anonymous online survey and face-to-face interviews. title: Sodio en panes y snacks de mayor consumo en Costa Rica. Contenido basal y verificación del etiquetado nutricional
abstract: Bread is highly consumed by population, making it one of the main sources of sodium in the diet, despite being moderate in salt. Mean while, snacks have high sodium content, but are less consumed by the general population. The aim of this study was to determine by direct analysis the baseline of sodium in breads and snacks most consumed in Costa Rica and verify compliance with the Central American Technical Regulation on Nutritional Labeling. title: El Mundo naval Ilustrado (1897-1901): Colaboraciones y contenidos en una revista especializada en la prensa naval española
abstract: This article examines El Mundo Naval Ilustrado (1897–1901) through its tables of contents to characterize its subject matter, contributors, editorial structure, and thematic evolution. Documentary research and descriptive analysis were conducted on a chronological sample of 23 of the 135 published issues, yielding 321 entries classified by subject, type, authorship, and geographical scope. title: Consideraciones sobre la elaboración de las directrices de nutrición de la Organización Mundial de la Salud y su implementación
abstract: La Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) sigue un proceso complejo y riguroso para la elaboración de directrices mundiales. En el caso de las directrices relacionadas con nutrición, la participación conjunta de las autoridades de los Estados Miembros de la OMS y sus aliados, incluidos aquellos de la economía social y solidaria, es clave para fortalecer el proceso de elaboración de directrices informadas por las pruebas científicas y su posterior implementación, como parte de las estrategias nacionales de salud pública. abstract: Este artículo analiza la relación entre la memoria democrática y la gestión museística a partir del caso del Museo Arrese de Corella, una institución cuyo origen y finalidad están vinculados a la figura del dirigente franquista José Luis Arrese. abstract: Antarctic ice shelves play a key role in controlling the mass loss of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Increasing evidence from regional studies suggests the possibility of abrupt transitions from low to high basal melt regimes under future climate forcing. The computational cost and complexity of these realistic simulations yet limit their ability to systematically investigate the steady-state response of ice shelves to incremental forcing, the reversibility of abrupt transitions and the underlying positive feedback loops. title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
abstract: Agents powered by large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in solving complex reasoning tasks. However, LLM agents often falter on long-horizon tasks due to cognitive overload, as their working memory becomes cluttered with expanding and irrelevant information, which dilutes their attention and hinders effective planning and reasoning. title: Multilingual Agent System for Inclusive Wildfire Evacuation Guidance
abstract: Wildfire seasons have become 84 days longer in the current days than in the 1970s, causing enormous threats to one's financial status and short- and long-term health. During the fire, public agencies send out emergency messages to provide warnings and orders. Although 26 million people in the US have limited English proficiency, over 80% of those messages are only delivered in English, which can cause disproportionate information distribution and awareness. title: Two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures with ECMC
abstract: We discuss reversible and non-reversible local Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures. We illustrate how the factorized Metropolis filter efficiently handles long-range interactions even for binary mixtures, using an adapted cell-veto strategy. We then benchmark the non-reversible event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) algorithm against the factorized Metropolis algorithm. title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
abstract: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs), such as Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), and Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs) are increasingly deployed in power transmission grids to address congestion and improve grid utilization. abstract: We study the effect of constant vorticity on the Benjamin-Feir instability of small-amplitude Stokes waves in infinite depth. title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe$_2$S$_3$: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables teams of agents, such as robots and autonomous vehicles, to learn coordinated behavior, but what such teams learn is largely determined by their reward function. Because task success alone provides too little guidance for learning, intermediate rewards are usually designed by hand, and this effort must often be repeated whenever the environment or the team changes. Large language models (LLMs) can automate the effort by writing reward functions as code, yet the resulting rewards are typically designed and tested in a single setting.

abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid channel simulation framework that combines site-specific ray tracing (RT) with 3GPP-compliant statistical channel simulation for non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The proposed approach uses RT to generate dominant propagation paths and augments them with statistically generated paths and subpaths to provide richer multipath realizations under practical simulation complexity. abstract: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) in Earth's atmosphere is a known source of systematic error in ground-based astronomical measurements, particularly at wavelengths greater than 7,000 angstroms. abstract: The observed bimodal radius distribution of close-in small planets provides important constraints on their formation and evolution. abstract: The evolution of long wavelength perturbations of traveling wave 2-soliton solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP) equation are investigated using modulation theory. abstract: Abstract Ocean turbulence plays a key role in shaping large-scale circulation, heat uptake, and biogeochemical processes. abstract: Abstract Sulfur (S) is thought to degas at higher pressures from hydrous magmas (e.g., arc and some ocean island basalts) relative to water-poor magmas, from which S degasses at lower pressures (e.g., Kīlauea, mid-ocean ridge basalts). abstract: Abstract Age and growth-related data provide key insights into life-history strategies, yet remain scarce for neotropical amphibians, particularly arboreal species inhabiting highly seasonal environments. abstract: Se documenta la fabricación y puesta a punto de un prototipo de mesa vibratoria uniaxial de bajo costo para el laboratorio del TESVB, como continuación del diseño esquemático previo. La metodología incluyó la adquisición de materiales, la fabricación de componentes estructurales, la integración electromecánica y las pruebas funcionales. El prototipo se construyó con perfil PTR de acero, placa galvanizada, correderas de extensión y un mecanismo de biela-manivela de madera de pino de 40 mm, accionado por un motor universal de CA de 375 W y 2000 rpm, con controlador TRIAC. title: Del error a la adaptación: la cultura de gestión del error como una Capacidad Dinámica
abstract: This essay examines error management culture as a higher-order dynamic capability that fosters organizational learning, innovation, psychological safety, and strategic renewal. Drawing upon the rationalist deductive method of René Descartes and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, a rationalist paradigm, and an objectivist critical realist perspective, it argues that error should not be understood as an accidental deviation from organizational functioning, but rather as a constitutive mechanism of knowledge creation, adaptation, and the evolution of social systems. title: Effects of tree size and competition on the growth of Norway spruce and silver birch trees in monocultures and mixed planted stand during mid-rotation
abstract: In Northern Europe, growing a mixture of shade-tolerant spruce and light-demanding birch instead of monocultures of either species is a potential way to improve forest resilience and adaptation to climate change. Planting both species at the establishment phase is a rare practice in silviculture, but it can be a viable approach for success in designing the mixture. Currently, there is a lack of knowledge on how these two species respond in size-growth relationships under intra- and interspecific competition when nursery-grown seedlings are used for establishing mixtures of both species. title: Silage yield and quality of maize cultivars in central Gujarat conditions
abstract: A field experiment was conducted during kharif 2020 at the Fodder Demonstration Unit, National Dairy Development Board, Anand, Gujarat, to evaluate ten maize cultivars for fodder yield and silage quality using a randomized block design with three replications. Significant differences were observed among the cultivars for fodder yield, silage yield, and quality traits. title: Extending the Martian landslide inventory southward: distribution, landslide types, and latitudinal extent
abstract: Martian landslide inventories remain concentrated near the equator, particularly in Valles Marineris. We present 411 previously uncatalogued landslides spanning 63°S–34°N, extending coverage of the southern mid-latitudes and increasing the existing global catalogue by approximately 13%. Most events (73.7%) occur between 20°S and 50°S, and 84.9% originate within Early and Middle Noachian highland units. title: Effects of packing density and homofermentative microbial inoculant on the physical quality, chemical composition, and estimated nutritive value of maize silage
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of packing density (500, 650, and 800 g/L fresh weight) and a homofermentative microbial inoculant (containing Lactobacillus plantarum and Enterococcus faecium; 0 or 500 mg/kg) on the physical quality, chemical composition, and estimated nutritive value of maize (Zea mays L.) silage. A completely randomised design with a 3 × 2 factorial arrangement was used, with each of the six treatment combinations replicated four times (n = 24). title: Borders and boundaries in words: The linguistic construction of Mediterranean migration in EU/UN and MSF texts
abstract: Every year, thousands of people flee war, persecution, and poverty in their home countries and make the dangerous journey across the Mediterranean in search of a safer future. title: Reduction of resource use and waste generation in nucleophilic substitutions: Low-waste alkyl halide synthesis
abstract: Nucleophilic substitution reactions are among the most commonly executed reactions employed in the synthesis of pharmaceutical compounds. Alkyl halides or pseudohalides are typically employed as the electrophilic reagents in these reactions, but both the reactions in which these electrophilic species are formed and the processes used to generate the precursors required for these reactions are highly resource intensive and result in very significant waste generation. title: Molecular and elemental compositions of humic acids of arable soils in north forest-steppe zone of Russia
abstract: The degradation of arable lands is becoming widespread and leads to significant loss of soil organic matter (SOM), expressed both in quantitative losses and in qualitative changes in the molecular and elemental composition of SOM. In this regard, a study of soils in the forest-steppe zone of Russia was conducted on the territory of the proposed Carbon Polygon in the Tambov Region and its humus state was characterised. title: Linking Corrosion Product Morphology to Impedance Response Across Immersion and Salt Spray Testing of Coated Steel
abstract: ABSTRACT Neutral salt spray and immersion testing are both routinely used to assess coated‐steel corrosion, yet rarely compared at the level of the corrosion product itself. This work examines whether electrochemical impedance spectroscopy differences between natural immersion, artificially aerated immersion, and neutral salt spray trace back to corrosion product architecture rather than to the test method. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how infection‐related traits vary across parasite populations and host stages is key to predicting host–parasite dynamics in complex life cycles. We tested whether the geographic origin of the acanthocephalan parasite Pomphorhynchus laevis influences infection success in both its intermediate ( Gammarus pulex ) and definitive ( Squalius cephalus ) hosts. title: In vitro Cytotoxicity and In silico Screening Evaluation of Clitoria ternatea L. Flower Methanolic Extract against Cancer Cell Lines
abstract: Clitoria ternatea L. (Fabaceae) flowers are used widely in traditional medicine and are rich in anthocyanins. The methanolic extract of this flower was screened for phytochemical classes, profiled by GC-MS, and tested by MTT assay against HeLa, MCF-7, and A549 cells. Ten GC-MS-identified compounds were carried forward for ADMET prediction (ADMETlab 3.0) and molecular docking (AutoDock Vina) against six targets: EGFR (1M17), estrogen receptor α (3ERT), MDM2 (4HFZ), a Bcl-2/Bcl-xL chimera (2W3L), tubulin at the colchicine site (1SA0), and KRAS G12S (7TLG). title: Effect of Water Content on the Tribological Properties of Grease
abstract: ABSTRACT In mechanical lubrication systems, grease can become contaminated with water due to seal failure and high ambient humidity. Water can alter the fibrous network of the thickener in grease, leading to base‐oil separation, reduced consistency and abnormal oil bleeding. In this study, experiments were combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the tribological behaviour of lubricating systems with different water contents, together with changes in parameters such as density distribution and system height. title: Screech in rocket nozzles undergoing free shock separation
abstract: Flow separation in rocket nozzles generates intense side loads that can lead to structural damage affecting space flight safety. Recent studies have hypothesised that a screech-like resonance loop may be responsible for such oscillations in the free shock separation (FSS) regime. In this work, we aim to confirm if screech is indeed present in this flow. title: Perancangan Film Pendek Animasi 2D Mengenai Dampak Polusi Cahaya Terhadap Lingkungan dan Ekosistem
abstract: Polusi cahaya merupakan salah satu bentuk pencemaran lingkungan yang jarang disadari, namun memiliki dampak signifikan terhadap kehidupan manusia, hewan, dan proses ilmiah seperti observasi astronomi. Di Indonesia, penyebaran informasi mengenai dampak polusi cahaya masih terbatas, terutama melalui media yang menarik dan mudah dipahami oleh masyarakat usia muda. title: Revision of Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier (Asparagaceae) from Madagascar, with the description of five new species and two new varieties
abstract: Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier, which includes the members of the genus with phylloclades, is defined and revised for Madagascar and the Comoro Islands based primarily on morphological evidence. This builds on earlier treatments of the group, taking into account the wealth of new material now available. title: The MASSIMAL Dataset: UAV Hyperspectral Images and Ground Truth Observations for Coastal Habitat Mapping in Norway
abstract: The MASSIMAL dataset was collected in an effort to develop new remote sensing methods for mapping shallow water coastal habitats, such as kelp forests, seagrass meadows and maerl beds. The main component of the dataset is a set of hyperspectral images collected using a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Images were collected during 45 UAV flights performed at 4 main areas along the Norwegian coast, spanning across a wide latitude range, from 59 to 67 degrees north. title: Smooth Threshold GARCH: Quasi Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Empirical Evidence
abstract: It is well established that the volatility of daily stock returns responds asymmetrically to news, as described by the news impact curve (NIC), which relates volatility to the previous return. Empirical studies suggest that (i) volatility reacts more strongly to negative returns than to positive returns of the same magnitude, (ii) the point of asymmetry, where the NIC attains its minimum, is positive, and (iii) returns above this point often do not increase volatility at all. title: Advance identification of where the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake would begin
abstract: Long-term forecasts say how likely a fault segment is to rupture, not where the rupture will begin. The b-value, the slope of the earthquake size distribution, falls as stress rises. After the 2016 Kumamoto sequence in Japan, b-values rose along the ruptured faults but fell in the unruptured central part of the Hinagu fault zone, which we identified in 2019 as where the next rupture was most likely to begin. title: The Generalised Kessler Syndrome and the Persian Gulf
abstract: The term Kessler syndrome was coined for a runaway orbital cascade creating a high-density debris field. The idea is generalised and applied to supply chains. An additive channel enables failures to generate further failures; a subtractive channel erodes the capacity to contain and restore. When damage outpaces repair, failure becomes irreversible and the system settles into a new state. Supplies connect the theory to its application. title: Propulsion Systems for a Starshade Rendezvous Mission with the Habitable World Observatory
abstract: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints affect exo-Earth characterization with a starshade rendezvous mission for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)-like telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with EXOSIMS, we model a 60 m starshade for visible-band spectroscopy (500-1000 nm) and a 35 m starshade for near-ultraviolet characterization (250-550 nm). title: X-Dubbing: Speech-to-Speech Translation under Temporal and Visual Constraints
abstract: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video. The key to this task is to produce a faithful translation that is naturally speakable within the source timing, which is non-trivial because languages differ in duration, rhythm, and articulation.
